1:10:1.text: This is the account of Noah’s sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth, who also had sons after the flood.

1:10:10.text: His kingdom began in Babylon, Erech, Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.

1:10:11.text: From that land he went forth into Assyria, where he built Nineveh, Rehoboth-Ir, Calah,

1:10:12.text: and Resen, which is between Nineveh and the great city of Calah.

1:10:13.text: Mizraim was the father of the Ludites, the Anamites, the Lehabites, the Naphtuhites,

1:10:14.text: the Pathrusites, the Casluhites (from whom the Philistines came), and the Caphtorites.

1:10:15.text: And Canaan was the father of Sidon his firstborn, and of the Hittites,

1:10:16.text: the Jebusites, the Amorites, the Girgashites,

1:10:17.text: the Hivites, the Arkites, the Sinites,

1:10:18.text: the Arvadites, the Zemarites, and the Hamathites. Later the Canaanite clans were scattered,

1:10:19.text: and the borders of Canaan extended from Sidon toward Gerar as far as Gaza, and then toward Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, as far as Lasha.

1:10:2.text: The sons of Japheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.

1:10:20.text: These are the sons of Ham according to their clans, languages, lands, and nations.

1:10:21.text: And sons were also born to Shem, the older brother of Japheth; Shem was the forefather of all the sons of Eber.

1:10:22.text: The sons of Shem: Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, and Aram.

1:10:23.text: The sons of Aram: Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash.

1:10:24.text: Arphaxad was the father of Shelah, and Shelah was the father of Eber.

1:10:25.text: Two sons were born to Eber: One was named Peleg, because in his days the earth was divided, and his brother was named Joktan.

1:10:26.text: And Joktan was the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,

1:10:29.text: Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these were sons of Joktan.

1:10:3.text: The sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.

1:10:30.text: Their territory extended from Mesha to Sephar, in the eastern hill country.

1:10:31.text: These are the sons of Shem, according to their clans, languages, lands, and nations.

1:10:32.text: All these are the clans of Noah’s sons, according to their generations and nations. From these the nations of the earth spread out after the flood.

1:10:4.text: And the sons of Javan: Elishah, Tarshish, the Kittites, and the Rodanites.

1:10:5.text: From these, the maritime peoples separated into their territories, according to their languages, by clans within their nations.

1:10:6.text: The sons of Ham: Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.

1:10:7.text: The sons of Cush: Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. And the sons of Raamah: Sheba and Dedan.

1:10:8.text: Cush was the father of Nimrod, who began to be a mighty one on the earth.

1:10:9.text: He was a mighty hunter before the Lord ; so it is said, “Like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before the Lord.”

1:11:1.text: Now the whole world had one language and a common form of speech.

1:11:10.text: This is the account of Shem. Two years after the flood, when Shem was 100 years old, he became the father of Arphaxad.

1:11:11.text: And after he had become the father of Arphaxad, Shem lived 500 years and had other sons and daughters.

1:11:12.text: When Arphaxad was 35 years old, he became the father of Shelah.

1:11:13.text: And after he had become the father of Shelah, Arphaxad lived 403 years and had other sons and daughters.

1:11:14.text: When Shelah was 30 years old, he became the father of Eber.

1:11:15.text: And after he had become the father of Eber, Shelah lived 403 years and had other sons and daughters.

1:11:16.text: When Eber was 34 years old, he became the father of Peleg.

1:11:17.text: And after he had become the father of Peleg, Eber lived 430 years and had other sons and daughters.

1:11:18.text: When Peleg was 30 years old, he became the father of Reu.

1:11:19.text: And after he had become the father of Reu, Peleg lived 209 years and had other sons and daughters.

1:11:2.text: And as people journeyed eastward, they found a plain in the land of Shinar and settled there.

1:11:20.text: When Reu was 32 years old, he became the father of Serug.

1:11:21.text: And after he had become the father of Serug, Reu lived 207 years and had other sons and daughters.

1:11:22.text: When Serug was 30 years old, he became the father of Nahor.

1:11:23.text: And after he had become the father of Nahor, Serug lived 200 years and had other sons and daughters.

1:11:24.text: When Nahor was 29 years old, he became the father of Terah.

1:11:25.text: And after he had become the father of Terah, Nahor lived 119 years and had other sons and daughters.

1:11:26.text: When Terah was 70 years old, he became the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran.

1:11:27.text: This is the account of Terah. Terah became the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran. And Haran became the father of Lot.

1:11:28.text: During his father Terah’s lifetime, Haran died in his native land, in Ur of the Chaldeans.

1:11:29.text: And Abram and Nahor took wives for themselves. Abram’s wife was named Sarai, and Nahor’s wife was named Milcah; she was the daughter of Haran, who was the father of both Milcah and Iscah.

1:11:3.text: And they said to one another, “Come, let us make bricks and bake them thoroughly.” So they used brick instead of stone, and tar instead of mortar.

1:11:30.text: But Sarai was barren; she had no children.

1:11:31.text: And Terah took his son Abram, his grandson Lot son of Haran, and his daughter-in-law Sarai the wife of Abram, and they set out from Ur of the Chaldeans for the land of Canaan. But when they arrived in Haran, they settled there.

1:11:32.text: Terah lived 205 years, and he died in Haran.

1:11:4.text: “Come,” they said, “let us build for ourselves a city with a tower that reaches to the heavens, that we may make a name for ourselves and not be scattered over the face of all the earth.”

1:11:5.text: Then the Lord came down to see the city and the tower that the sons of men were building.

1:11:6.text: And the Lord said, “If they have begun to do this as one people speaking the same language, then nothing they devise will be beyond them.

1:11:7.text: Come, let Us go down and confuse their language, so that they will not understand one another’s speech.”

1:11:8.text: So the Lord scattered them from there over the face of all the earth, and they stopped building the city.

1:11:9.text: That is why it is called Babel, for there the Lord confused the language of the whole world, and from that place the Lord scattered them over the face of all the earth.

1:12:1.text: Then the Lord said to Abram, “Leave your country, your kindred, and your father’s household, and go to the land I will show you.

1:12:10.text: Now there was a famine in the land. So Abram went down to Egypt to live there for a while because the famine was severe.

1:12:11.text: As he was about to enter Egypt, he said to his wife Sarai, “Look, I know that you are a beautiful woman,

1:12:12.text: and when the Egyptians see you, they will say, ‘This is his wife.’ Then they will kill me but will let you live.

1:12:13.text: Please say you are my sister, so that I will be treated well for your sake, and on account of you my life will be spared.”

1:12:14.text: So when Abram entered Egypt, the Egyptians saw that the woman was very beautiful.

1:12:15.text: When Pharaoh’s officials saw Sarai, they commended her to him, and she was taken into the palace of Pharaoh.

1:12:16.text: He treated Abram well on her account, and Abram acquired sheep and cattle, male and female donkeys, menservants and maidservants, and camels.

1:12:17.text: The Lord, however, afflicted Pharaoh and his household with severe plagues because of Abram’s wife Sarai.

1:12:18.text: So Pharaoh summoned Abram and asked, “What have you done to me? Why didn’t you tell me she was your wife?

1:12:19.text: Why did you say, ‘She is my sister,’ so that I took her as my wife? Now then, here is your wife. Take her and go!”

1:12:2.text: I will make you into a great nation, and I will bless you; I will make your name great, so that you will be a blessing.

1:12:20.text: Then Pharaoh gave his men orders concerning Abram, and they sent him away with his wife and all his possessions.

1:12:3.text: I will bless those who bless you and curse those who curse you; and all the families of the earth will be blessed through you. ”

1:12:4.text: So Abram departed, as the Lord had directed him, and Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran.

1:12:5.text: And Abram took his wife Sarai, his nephew Lot, and all the possessions and people they had acquired in Haran, and set out for the land of Canaan. When they came to the land of Canaan,

1:12:6.text: Abram traveled through the land as far as the site of the Oak of Moreh at Shechem. And at that time the Canaanites were in the land.

1:12:7.text: Then the Lord appeared to Abram and said, “I will give this land to your offspring. ” So Abram built an altar there to the Lord, who had appeared to him.

1:12:8.text: From there Abram moved on to the hill country east of Bethel and pitched his tent, with Bethel to the west and Ai to the east. There he built an altar to the Lord, and he called on the name of the Lord.

1:12:9.text: And Abram journeyed on toward the Negev.

1:13:1.text: So Abram went up out of Egypt into the Negev — he and his wife and all his possessions — and Lot was with him.

1:13:10.text: And Lot looked out and saw that the whole plain of the Jordan, all the way to Zoar, was well watered like the garden of the Lord, like the land of Egypt. (This was before the Lord destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.)

1:13:11.text: So Lot chose the whole plain of the Jordan for himself and set out toward the east. And Abram and Lot parted company.

1:13:12.text: Abram lived in the land of Canaan, but Lot settled in the cities of the plain and pitched his tent toward Sodom.

1:13:13.text: But the men of Sodom were wicked, sinning greatly against the Lord.

1:13:14.text: After Lot had departed, the Lord said to Abram, “Now lift up your eyes from the place where you are, and look to the north and south and east and west,

1:13:15.text: for all the land that you see, I will give to you and your offspring forever.

1:13:16.text: I will make your offspring like the dust of the earth, so that if one could count the dust of the earth, then your offspring could be counted.

1:13:17.text: Get up and walk around the land, through its length and breadth, for I will give it to you.”

1:13:18.text: So Abram moved his tent and went to live near the Oaks of Mamre at Hebron, where he built an altar to the Lord.

1:13:2.text: And Abram had become extremely wealthy in livestock and silver and gold.

1:13:3.text: From the Negev he journeyed from place to place toward Bethel, until he came to the place between Bethel and Ai where his tent had formerly been pitched,

1:13:4.text: to the site where he had built the altar. And there Abram called on the name of the Lord.

1:13:5.text: Now Lot, who was traveling with Abram, also had flocks and herds and tents.

1:13:6.text: But the land was unable to support both of them while they stayed together, for they had so many possessions that they were unable to coexist.

1:13:7.text: And there was discord between the herdsmen of Abram and the herdsmen of Lot. At that time the Canaanites and the Perizzites were also living in the land.

1:13:8.text: So Abram said to Lot, “Please let there be no contention between you and me, or between your herdsmen and my herdsmen. After all, we are brothers.

1:13:9.text: Is not the whole land before you? Now separate yourself from me. If you go to the left, I will go to the right; if you go to the right, I will go to the left.”

1:15:1.text: After these events, the word of the Lord came to Abram in a vision: “Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your very great reward.”

1:15:10.text: So Abram brought all these to Him, split each of them down the middle, and laid the halves opposite each other. The birds, however, he did not cut in half.

1:15:11.text: And the birds of prey descended on the carcasses, but Abram drove them away.

1:15:12.text: As the sun was setting, Abram fell into a deep sleep, and suddenly great terror and darkness overwhelmed him.

1:15:13.text: Then the Lord said to Abram, “Know for certain that your descendants will be strangers in a land that is not their own, and they will be enslaved and mistreated four hundred years.

1:15:14.text: But I will judge the nation they serve as slaves, and afterward they will depart with many possessions.

1:15:15.text: You, however, will go to your fathers in peace and be buried at a ripe old age.

1:15:16.text: In the fourth generation your descendants will return here, for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet complete.”

1:15:17.text: When the sun had set and darkness had fallen, behold, a smoking firepot and a flaming torch appeared and passed between the halves of the carcasses.

1:15:18.text: On that day the Lord made a covenant with Abram, saying, “To your descendants I have given this land — from the river of Egypt to the great River Euphrates —

1:15:19.text: the land of the Kenites, Kenizzites, Kadmonites,

1:15:2.text: But Abram replied, “O Lord GOD, what can You give me, since I remain childless, and the heir of my house is Eliezer of Damascus?”

1:15:3.text: Abram continued, “Behold, You have given me no offspring, so a servant in my household will be my heir.”

1:15:4.text: Then the word of the Lord came to Abram, saying, “This one will not be your heir, but one who comes from your own body will be your heir.”

1:15:5.text: And the Lord took him outside and said, “Now look to the heavens and count the stars, if you are able.” Then He told him, “So shall your offspring be.”

1:15:6.text: Abram believed the Lord, and it was credited to him as righteousness.

1:15:7.text: The Lord also told him, “I am the Lord, who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans to give you this land to possess.”

1:15:8.text: But Abram replied, “Lord GOD, how can I know that I will possess it?”

1:15:9.text: And the Lord said to him, “Bring Me a heifer, a goat, and a ram, each three years old, along with a turtledove and a young pigeon.”

1:17:1.text: When Abram was ninety-nine years old, the Lord appeared to him and said, “I am God Almighty. Walk before Me and be blameless.

1:17:10.text: This is My covenant with you and your descendants after you, which you are to keep: Every male among you must be circumcised.

1:17:11.text: You are to circumcise the flesh of your foreskin, and this will be a sign of the covenant between Me and you.

1:17:12.text: Generation after generation, every male must be circumcised when he is eight days old, including those born in your household and those purchased from a foreigner — even those who are not your offspring.

1:17:13.text: Whether they are born in your household or purchased, they must be circumcised. My covenant in your flesh will be an everlasting covenant.

1:17:14.text: But if any male is not circumcised, he will be cut off from his people; he has broken My covenant.”

1:17:15.text: Then God said to Abraham, “As for Sarai your wife, do not call her Sarai, for her name is to be Sarah.

1:17:16.text: And I will bless her and will surely give you a son by her. I will bless her, and she will be the mother of nations; kings of peoples will descend from her.”

1:17:17.text: Abraham fell facedown. Then he laughed and said to himself, “Can a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old? Can Sarah give birth at the age of ninety?”

1:17:18.text: And Abraham said to God, “O that Ishmael might live under Your blessing!”

1:17:19.text: But God replied, “Your wife Sarah will indeed bear you a son, and you are to name him Isaac. I will establish My covenant with him as an everlasting covenant for his descendants after him.

1:17:2.text: I will establish My covenant between Me and you, and I will multiply you exceedingly.”

1:17:20.text: As for Ishmael, I have heard you, and I will surely bless him; I will make him fruitful and multiply him greatly. He will become the father of twelve rulers, and I will make him into a great nation.

1:17:21.text: But I will establish My covenant with Isaac, whom Sarah will bear to you at this time next year.”

1:17:22.text: When He had finished speaking with Abraham, God went up from him.

1:17:23.text: On that very day Abraham took his son Ishmael and all those born in his household or purchased with his money — every male among the members of Abraham’s household — and he circumcised them, just as God had told him.

1:17:24.text: So Abraham was ninety-nine years old when he was circumcised,

1:17:25.text: and his son Ishmael was thirteen;

1:17:26.text: Abraham and his son Ishmael were circumcised on the same day.

1:17:27.text: And all the men of Abraham’s household — both servants born in his household and those purchased from foreigners — were circumcised with him.

1:17:3.text: Then Abram fell facedown, and God said to him,

1:17:4.text: “As for Me, this is My covenant with you: You will be the father of many nations.

1:17:5.text: No longer will you be called Abram, but your name will be Abraham, for I have made you a father of many nations.

1:17:6.text: I will make you exceedingly fruitful; I will make nations of you, and kings will descend from you.

1:17:7.text: I will establish My covenant as an everlasting covenant between Me and you and your descendants after you, to be your God and the God of your descendants after you.

1:17:8.text: And to you and your descendants I will give the land where you are residing — all the land of Canaan — as an eternal possession; and I will be their God.”

1:17:9.text: God also said to Abraham, “You must keep My covenant — you and your descendants in the generations after you.

1:18:1.text: Then the Lord appeared to Abraham by the Oaks of Mamre in the heat of the day, while he was sitting at the entrance of his tent.

1:18:10.text: Then the Lord said, “I will surely return to you at this time next year, and your wife Sarah will have a son!” Now Sarah was behind him, listening at the entrance to the tent.

1:18:11.text: And Abraham and Sarah were already old and well along in years; Sarah had passed the age of childbearing.

1:18:12.text: So she laughed to herself, saying, “After I am worn out and my master is old, will I now have this pleasure?”

1:18:13.text: And the Lord asked Abraham, “Why did Sarah laugh and say, ‘Can I really bear a child when I am old?’

1:18:14.text: Is anything too difficult for the Lord? At the appointed time I will return to you — in about a year — and Sarah will have a son.”

1:18:15.text: But Sarah was afraid, so she denied it and said, “I did not laugh.” “No,” replied the Lord, “but you did laugh.”

1:18:16.text: When the men got up to leave, they looked out over Sodom, and Abraham walked along with them to see them off.

1:18:17.text: And the Lord said, “Shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do?

1:18:18.text: Abraham will surely become a great and powerful nation, and through him all the nations of the earth will be blessed.

1:18:19.text: For I have chosen him, so that he will command his children and his household after him to keep the way of the Lord by doing what is right and just, in order that the Lord may bring upon Abraham what He has promised.”

1:18:2.text: And Abraham looked up and saw three men standing nearby. When he saw them, he ran from the entrance of his tent to meet them and bowed low to the ground.

1:18:20.text: Then the Lord said, “The outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah is great. Because their sin is so grievous,

1:18:21.text: I will go down to see if their actions fully justify the outcry that has reached Me. If not, I will find out.”

1:18:22.text: And the two men turned away and went toward Sodom, but Abraham remained standing before the Lord.

1:18:23.text: Abraham stepped forward and said, “Will You really sweep away the righteous with the wicked?

1:18:24.text: What if there are fifty righteous ones in the city? Will You really sweep it away and not spare the place for the sake of the fifty righteous ones who are there?

1:18:25.text: Far be it from You to do such a thing — to kill the righteous with the wicked, so that the righteous and the wicked are treated alike. Far be it from You! Will not the Judge of all the earth do what is right?”

1:18:26.text: So the Lord replied, “If I find fifty righteous ones within the city of Sodom, on their account I will spare the whole place.”

1:18:27.text: Then Abraham answered, “Now that I have ventured to speak to the Lord — though I am but dust and ashes —

1:18:28.text: suppose the fifty righteous ones lack five. Will You destroy the whole city for the lack of five?” He replied, “If I find forty-five there, I will not destroy it.”

1:18:29.text: Once again Abraham spoke to the Lord, “Suppose forty are found there?” He answered, “On account of the forty, I will not do it.”

1:18:3.text: “My lord,” said Abraham, “if I have found favor in your sight, please do not pass your servant by.

1:18:30.text: Then Abraham said, “May the Lord not be angry, but let me speak further. Suppose thirty are found there?” He replied, “If I find thirty there, I will not do it.”

1:18:31.text: And Abraham said, “Now that I have ventured to speak to the Lord, suppose twenty are found there?” He answered, “On account of the twenty, I will not destroy it.”

1:18:32.text: Finally, Abraham said, “May the Lord not be angry, but let me speak once more. Suppose ten are found there?” And He answered, “On account of the ten, I will not destroy it.”

1:18:33.text: When the Lord had finished speaking with Abraham, He departed, and Abraham returned home.

1:18:4.text: Let a little water be brought, that you may wash your feet and rest yourselves under the tree.

1:18:5.text: And I will bring a bit of bread so that you may refresh yourselves. This is why you have passed your servant’s way. After that, you may continue on your way.” “Yes,” they replied, “you may do as you have said.”

1:18:6.text: So Abraham hurried into the tent and said to Sarah, “Quick! Prepare three seahs of fine flour, knead it, and bake some bread.”

1:18:7.text: Meanwhile, Abraham ran to the herd, selected a tender and choice calf, and gave it to a servant, who hurried to prepare it.

1:18:8.text: Then Abraham brought curds and milk and the calf that had been prepared, and he set them before the men and stood by them under the tree as they ate.

1:18:9.text: “Where is your wife Sarah?” they asked. “There, in the tent,” he replied.

1:1:1.text: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.

1:1:10.text: God called the dry land “earth,” and the gathering of waters He called “seas.” And God saw that it was good.

1:1:11.text: Then God said, “Let the earth bring forth vegetation: seed-bearing plants and fruit trees, each bearing fruit with seed according to its kind.” And it was so.

1:1:12.text: The earth produced vegetation: seed-bearing plants according to their kinds and trees bearing fruit with seed according to their kinds. And God saw that it was good.

1:1:13.text: And there was evening, and there was morning — the third day.

1:1:14.text: And God said, “Let there be lights in the expanse of the sky to distinguish between the day and the night, and let them be signs to mark the seasons and days and years.

1:1:15.text: And let them serve as lights in the expanse of the sky to shine upon the earth.” And it was so.

1:1:16.text: God made two great lights: the greater light to rule the day and the lesser light to rule the night. And He made the stars as well.

1:1:17.text: God set these lights in the expanse of the sky to shine upon the earth,

1:1:18.text: to preside over the day and the night, and to separate the light from the darkness. And God saw that it was good.

1:1:19.text: And there was evening, and there was morning — the fourth day.

1:1:2.text: Now the earth was formless and void, and darkness was over the surface of the deep. And the Spirit of God was hovering over the surface of the waters.

1:1:20.text: And God said, “Let the waters teem with living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth in the open expanse of the sky.”

1:1:21.text: So God created the great sea creatures and every living thing that moves, with which the waters teemed according to their kinds, and every bird of flight after its kind. And God saw that it was good.

1:1:22.text: Then God blessed them and said, “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the waters of the seas, and let birds multiply on the earth.”

1:1:23.text: And there was evening, and there was morning — the fifth day.

1:1:24.text: And God said, “Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kinds: livestock, land crawlers, and beasts of the earth according to their kinds.” And it was so.

1:1:25.text: God made the beasts of the earth according to their kinds, the livestock according to their kinds, and everything that crawls upon the earth according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.

1:1:26.text: Then God said, “Let Us make man in Our image, after Our likeness, to rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air, over the livestock, and over all the earth itself and every creature that crawls upon it.”

1:1:27.text: So God created man in His own image; in the image of God He created him; male and female He created them.

1:1:28.text: God blessed them and said to them, “Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth and subdue it; rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air and every creature that crawls upon the earth.”

1:1:29.text: Then God said, “Behold, I have given you every seed-bearing plant on the face of all the earth, and every tree whose fruit contains seed. They will be yours for food.

1:1:3.text: And God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light.

1:1:30.text: And to every beast of the earth and every bird of the air and every creature that crawls upon the earth — everything that has the breath of life in it — I have given every green plant for food.” And it was so.

1:1:31.text: And God looked upon all that He had made, and indeed, it was very good. And there was evening, and there was morning — the sixth day.

1:1:4.text: And God saw that the light was good, and He separated the light from the darkness.

1:1:5.text: God called the light “day,” and the darkness He called “night.” And there was evening, and there was morning — the first day.

1:1:6.text: And God said, “Let there be an expanse between the waters, to separate the waters from the waters.”

1:1:7.text: So God made the expanse and separated the waters beneath it from the waters above. And it was so.

1:1:8.text: God called the expanse “sky.” And there was evening, and there was morning — the second day.

1:1:9.text: And God said, “Let the waters under the sky be gathered into one place, so that the dry land may appear.” And it was so.

1:22:1.text: Some time later God tested Abraham and said to him, “Abraham!” “Here I am,” he answered.

1:22:10.text: Then Abraham reached out his hand and took the knife to slaughter his son.

1:22:11.text: Just then the angel of the Lord called out to him from heaven, “Abraham, Abraham!” “Here I am,” he replied.

1:22:12.text: “Do not lay a hand on the boy or do anything to him,” said the angel, “for now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld your only son from me. ”

1:22:13.text: Then Abraham looked up and saw behind him a ram in a thicket, caught by its horns. So he went and took the ram and offered it as a burnt offering in place of his son.

1:22:14.text: And Abraham called that place The Lord Will Provide. So to this day it is said, “On the mountain of the Lord it will be provided.”

1:22:15.text: And the angel of the Lord called to Abraham from heaven a second time,

1:22:16.text: saying, “By Myself I have sworn, declares the Lord, that because you have done this and have not withheld your only son,

1:22:17.text: I will surely bless you, and I will multiply your descendants like the stars in the sky and the sand on the seashore. Your descendants will possess the gates of their enemies.

1:22:18.text: And through your offspring all nations of the earth will be blessed, because you have obeyed My voice.”

1:22:19.text: Abraham went back to his servants, and they got up and set out together for Beersheba. And Abraham settled in Beersheba.

1:22:2.text: “Take your son,” God said, “your only son Isaac, whom you love, and go to the land of Moriah. Offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains, which I will show you.”

1:22:20.text: Some time later, Abraham was told, “Milcah has also borne sons to your brother Nahor:

1:22:21.text: Uz the firstborn, his brother Buz, Kemuel (the father of Aram),

1:22:22.text: Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel.”

1:22:23.text: And Bethuel became the father of Rebekah. Milcah bore these eight sons to Abraham’s brother Nahor.

1:22:24.text: Moreover, Nahor’s concubine, whose name was Reumah, bore Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.

1:22:3.text: So Abraham got up early the next morning, saddled his donkey, and took along two of his servants and his son Isaac. He split the wood for a burnt offering and set out for the place God had designated.

1:22:4.text: On the third day Abraham looked up and saw the place in the distance.

1:22:5.text: “Stay here with the donkey,” Abraham told his servants. “The boy and I will go over there to worship, and then we will return to you.”

1:22:6.text: Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering and placed it on his son Isaac. He himself carried the fire and the sacrificial knife, and the two of them walked on together.

1:22:7.text: Then Isaac said to his father Abraham, “My father!” “Here I am, my son,” he replied. “The fire and the wood are here,” said Isaac, “but where is the lamb for the burnt offering?”

1:22:8.text: Abraham answered, “God Himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son.” And the two walked on together.

1:22:9.text: When they arrived at the place God had designated, Abraham built the altar there and arranged the wood. He bound his son Isaac and placed him on the altar, atop the wood.

1:27:10.text: Then take it to your father to eat, so that he may bless you before he dies.”

1:27:11.text: Jacob answered his mother Rebekah, “Look, my brother Esau is a hairy man, but I am smooth-skinned.

1:27:12.text: What if my father touches me? Then I would be revealed to him as a deceiver, and I would bring upon myself a curse rather than a blessing.”

1:27:13.text: His mother replied, “Your curse be on me, my son. Just obey my voice and go get them for me.”

1:27:14.text: So Jacob went and got two goats and brought them to his mother, who made the tasty food his father loved.

1:27:15.text: And Rebekah took the finest clothes in the house that belonged to her older son Esau, and she put them on her younger son Jacob.

1:27:16.text: She also put the skins of the young goats on his hands and on the smooth part of his neck.

1:27:17.text: Then she handed her son Jacob the tasty food and bread she had made.

1:27:18.text: So Jacob went to his father and said, “My father.” “Here I am!” he answered. “Which one are you, my son?”

1:27:19.text: Jacob said to his father, “I am Esau, your firstborn. I have done as you told me. Please sit up and eat some of my game, so that you may bless me.”

1:27:2.text: “Look,” said Isaac, “I am now old, and I do not know the day of my death.

1:27:20.text: But Isaac asked his son, “How did you ever find it so quickly, my son?” “Because the Lord your God brought it to me,” he replied.

1:27:21.text: Then Isaac said to Jacob, “Please come closer so I can touch you, my son. Are you really my son Esau, or not?”

1:27:22.text: So Jacob came close to his father Isaac, who touched him and said, “The voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau.”

1:27:23.text: Isaac did not recognize him, because his hands were hairy like those of his brother Esau; so he blessed him.

1:27:24.text: Again he asked, “Are you really my son Esau?” And he replied, “I am.”

1:27:25.text: “Serve me,” said Isaac, “and let me eat some of my son’s game, so that I may bless you.” Jacob brought it to him, and he ate; then he brought him wine, and he drank.

1:27:26.text: Then his father Isaac said to him, “Please come near and kiss me, my son.”

1:27:27.text: So he came near and kissed him. When Isaac smelled his clothing, he blessed him and said: “Ah, the smell of my son is like the smell of a field that the Lord has blessed.

1:27:29.text: May peoples serve you and nations bow down to you. May you be the master of your brothers, and may the sons of your mother bow down to you. May those who curse you be cursed, and those who bless you be blessed.”

1:27:30.text: As soon as Isaac had finished blessing him and Jacob had left his father’s presence, his brother Esau returned from the hunt.

1:27:31.text: He too made some tasty food, brought it to his father, and said to him, “My father, sit up and eat of your son’s game, so that you may bless me.”

1:27:32.text: But his father Isaac replied, “Who are you?” “I am Esau, your firstborn son,” he answered.

1:27:33.text: Isaac began to tremble violently and said, “Who was it, then, who hunted the game and brought it to me? Before you came in, I ate it all and blessed him — and indeed, he will be blessed!”

1:27:34.text: When Esau heard his father’s words, he let out a loud and bitter cry and said to his father, “Bless me too, O my father!”

1:27:35.text: But Isaac replied, “Your brother came deceitfully and took your blessing.”

1:27:36.text: So Esau declared, “Is he not rightly named Jacob? For he has cheated me twice. He took my birthright, and now he has taken my blessing.” Then he asked, “Haven’t you saved a blessing for me?”

1:27:37.text: But Isaac answered Esau: “Look, I have made him your master and given him all his relatives as servants; I have sustained him with grain and new wine. What is left that I can do for you, my son?”

1:27:38.text: Esau said to his father, “Do you have only one blessing, my father? Bless me too, O my father!” Then Esau wept aloud.

1:27:39.text: His father Isaac answered him: “Behold, your dwelling place shall be away from the richness of the land, away from the dew of heaven above.

1:27:41.text: Esau held a grudge against Jacob because of the blessing his father had given him. And Esau said in his heart, “The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then I will kill my brother Jacob.”

1:27:42.text: When the words of her older son Esau were relayed to Rebekah, she sent for her younger son Jacob and told him, “Look, your brother Esau is consoling himself by plotting to kill you.

1:27:43.text: So now, my son, obey my voice and flee at once to my brother Laban in Haran.

1:27:44.text: Stay with him for a while, until your brother’s fury subsides —

1:27:45.text: until your brother’s rage against you wanes and he forgets what you have done to him. Then I will send for you and bring you back from there. Why should I lose both of you in one day?”

1:27:46.text: Then Rebekah said to Isaac, “I am weary of my life because of these Hittite women. If Jacob takes a Hittite wife from among them, what good is my life?”

1:27:7.text: ‘Bring me some game and prepare me a tasty dish to eat, so that I may bless you in the presence of the Lord before I die.’

1:27:8.text: Now, my son, listen to my voice and do exactly as I tell you.

1:27:9.text: Go out to the flock and bring me two choice young goats, so that I can make them into a tasty dish for your father — the kind he loves.

1:2:1.text: Thus the heavens and the earth were completed in all their vast array.

1:2:10.text: Now a river flowed out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it branched into four headwaters:

1:2:11.text: The name of the first river is Pishon; it winds through the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold.

1:2:12.text: And the gold of that land is pure, and bdellium and onyx are found there.

1:2:13.text: The name of the second river is Gihon; it winds through the whole land of Cush.

1:2:14.text: The name of the third river is Hiddekel; it runs along the east side of Assyria. And the fourth river is the Euphrates.

1:2:15.text: Then the Lord God took the man and placed him in the Garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it.

1:2:16.text: And the Lord God commanded him, “You may eat freely from every tree of the garden,

1:2:17.text: but you must not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil; for in the day that you eat of it, you will surely die.”

1:2:18.text: The Lord God also said, “It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make for him a suitable helper.”

1:2:19.text: And out of the ground the Lord God formed every beast of the field and every bird of the air, and He brought them to the man to see what he would name each one. And whatever the man called each living creature, that was its name.

1:2:2.text: And by the seventh day God had finished the work He had been doing; so on that day He rested from all His work.

1:2:20.text: The man gave names to all the livestock, to the birds of the air, and to every beast of the field. But for Adam no suitable helper was found.

1:2:21.text: So the Lord God caused the man to fall into a deep sleep, and while he slept, He took one of the man’s ribs and closed up the area with flesh.

1:2:22.text: And from the rib that the Lord God had taken from the man, He made a woman and brought her to him.

1:2:23.text: And the man said: “This is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called ‘woman,’ for out of man she was taken.”

1:2:24.text: For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife, and they will become one flesh.

1:2:25.text: And the man and his wife were both naked, and they were not ashamed.

1:2:3.text: Then God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, because on that day He rested from all the work of creation that He had accomplished.

1:2:4.text: This is the account of the heavens and the earth when they were created, in the day that the Lord God made them.

1:2:5.text: Now no shrub of the field had yet appeared on the earth, nor had any plant of the field sprouted; for the Lord God had not yet sent rain upon the earth, and there was no man to cultivate the ground.

1:2:6.text: But springs welled up from the earth and watered the whole surface of the ground.

1:2:7.text: Then the Lord God formed man from the dust of the ground and breathed the breath of life into his nostrils, and the man became a living being.

1:2:8.text: And the Lord God planted a garden in Eden, in the east, where He placed the man He had formed.

1:2:9.text: Out of the ground the Lord God gave growth to every tree that is pleasing to the eye and good for food. And in the middle of the garden were the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.

1:31:1.text: Now Jacob heard that Laban’s sons were saying, “Jacob has taken away all that belonged to our father and built all this wealth at our father’s expense.”

1:31:10.text: When the flocks were breeding, I saw in a dream that the streaked, spotted, and speckled males were mating with the females.

1:31:11.text: In that dream the angel of God said to me, ‘Jacob!’ And I replied, ‘Here I am.’

1:31:12.text: ‘Look up,’ he said, ‘and see that all the males that are mating with the flock are streaked, spotted, or speckled; for I have seen all that Laban has done to you.

1:31:13.text: I am the God of Bethel, where you anointed the pillar and made a solemn vow to Me. Now get up and leave this land at once, and return to your native land.’ ”

1:31:14.text: And Rachel and Leah replied, “Do we have any portion or inheritance left in our father’s house?

1:31:15.text: Are we not regarded by him as outsiders? Not only has he sold us, but he has certainly squandered what was paid for us.

1:31:16.text: Surely all the wealth that God has taken away from our father belongs to us and to our children. So do whatever God has told you.”

1:31:17.text: Then Jacob got up and put his children and his wives on camels,

1:31:18.text: and he drove all his livestock before him, along with all the possessions he had acquired in Paddan-aram, to go to his father Isaac in the land in Canaan.

1:31:19.text: Now while Laban was out shearing his sheep, Rachel stole her father’s household idols.

1:31:2.text: And Jacob saw from the countenance of Laban that his attitude toward him had changed.

1:31:20.text: Moreover, Jacob deceived Laban the Aramean by not telling him that he was running away.

1:31:21.text: So he fled with all his possessions, crossed the Euphrates, and headed for the hill country of Gilead.

1:31:22.text: On the third day Laban was informed that Jacob had fled.

1:31:23.text: So he took his relatives with him, pursued Jacob for seven days, and overtook him in the hill country of Gilead.

1:31:24.text: But that night God came to Laban the Aramean in a dream and warned him, “Be careful not to say anything to Jacob, either good or bad.”

1:31:25.text: Now Jacob had pitched his tent in the hill country of Gilead when Laban overtook him, and Laban and his relatives camped there as well.

1:31:26.text: Then Laban said to Jacob, “What have you done? You have deceived me and carried off my daughters like captives of war!

1:31:27.text: Why did you run away secretly and deceive me, without even telling me? I would have sent you away with joy and singing, with tambourines and harps.

1:31:28.text: But you did not even let me kiss my grandchildren and my daughters goodbye. Now you have done a foolish thing.

1:31:29.text: I have power to do you great harm, but last night the God of your father said to me, ‘Be careful not to say anything to Jacob, either good or bad.’

1:31:3.text: Then the Lord said to Jacob, “Go back to the land of your fathers and to your kindred, and I will be with you.”

1:31:30.text: Now you have gone off because you long for your father’s house. But why have you stolen my gods?”

1:31:31.text: “I was afraid,” Jacob answered, “for I thought you would take your daughters from me by force.

1:31:32.text: If you find your gods with anyone here, he shall not live! In the presence of our relatives, see for yourself if anything is yours, and take it back.” For Jacob did not know that Rachel had stolen the idols.

1:31:33.text: So Laban went into Jacob’s tent, then Leah’s tent, and then the tents of the two maidservants, but he found nothing. Then he left Leah’s tent and entered Rachel’s tent.

1:31:34.text: Now Rachel had taken Laban’s household idols, put them in the saddlebag of her camel, and was sitting on them. And Laban searched everything in the tent but found nothing.

1:31:35.text: Rachel said to her father, “Sir, do not be angry that I cannot stand up before you; for I am having my period.” So Laban searched, but could not find the household idols.

1:31:36.text: Then Jacob became incensed and challenged Laban. “What is my crime?” he said. “For what sin of mine have you so hotly pursued me?

1:31:37.text: You have searched all my goods! Have you found anything that belongs to you? Put it here before my brothers and yours, that they may judge between the two of us.

1:31:38.text: I have been with you for twenty years now. Your sheep and goats have not miscarried, nor have I eaten the rams of your flock.

1:31:39.text: I did not bring you anything torn by wild beasts; I bore the loss myself. And you demanded payment from me for what was stolen by day or night.

1:31:4.text: So Jacob sent word and called Rachel and Leah to the field where his flocks were,

1:31:40.text: As it was, the heat consumed me by day and the frost by night, and sleep fled from my eyes.

1:31:41.text: Thus for twenty years I have served in your household — fourteen years for your two daughters and six years for your flocks — and you have changed my wages ten times!

1:31:42.text: If the God of my father, the God of Abraham and the Fear of Isaac, had not been with me, surely by now you would have sent me away empty-handed. But God has seen my affliction and the toil of my hands, and last night He rendered judgment.”

1:31:43.text: But Laban answered Jacob, “These daughters are my daughters, these sons are my sons, and these flocks are my flocks! Everything you see is mine! Yet what can I do today about these daughters of mine or the children they have borne?

1:31:44.text: Come now, let us make a covenant, you and I, and let it serve as a witness between you and me.”

1:31:45.text: So Jacob picked out a stone and set it up as a pillar,

1:31:46.text: and he said to his relatives, “Gather some stones.” So they took stones and made a mound, and there by the mound they ate.

1:31:47.text: Laban called it Jegar-sahadutha, and Jacob called it Galeed.

1:31:48.text: Then Laban declared, “This mound is a witness between you and me this day.” Therefore the place was called Galeed.

1:31:49.text: It was also called Mizpah, because Laban said, “May the Lord keep watch between you and me when we are absent from each other.

1:31:5.text: and he told them, “I can see from your father’s countenance that his attitude toward me has changed; but the God of my father has been with me.

1:31:50.text: If you mistreat my daughters or take other wives, although no one is with us, remember that God is a witness between you and me.”

1:31:51.text: Laban also said to Jacob, “Here is the mound, and here is the pillar I have set up between you and me.

1:31:52.text: This mound is a witness, and this pillar is a witness, that I will not go past this mound to harm you, and you will not go past this mound and pillar to harm me.

1:31:53.text: May the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge between us.” So Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac.

1:31:54.text: Then Jacob offered a sacrifice on the mountain and invited his relatives to eat a meal. And after they had eaten, they spent the night on the mountain.

1:31:55.text: Early the next morning, Laban got up and kissed his grandchildren and daughters and blessed them. Then he left to return home.

1:3:1.text: Now the serpent was more crafty than any beast of the field that the Lord God had made. And he said to the woman, “Did God really say, ‘You must not eat from any tree in the garden?’ ”

1:3:10.text: “I heard Your voice in the garden,” he replied, “and I was afraid because I was naked; so I hid myself.”

1:3:11.text: “Who told you that you were naked?” asked the Lord God. “Have you eaten from the tree of which I commanded you not to eat?”

1:3:12.text: And the man answered, “The woman whom You gave me, she gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate it.”

1:3:13.text: Then the Lord God said to the woman, “What is this you have done?” “The serpent deceived me,” she replied, “and I ate.”

1:3:14.text: So the Lord God said to the serpent: “Because you have done this, cursed are you above all livestock and every beast of the field! On your belly will you go, and dust you will eat, all the days of your life.

1:3:15.text: And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed. He will crush your head, and you will strike his heel. ”

1:3:16.text: To the woman He said: “I will sharply increase your pain in childbirth; in pain you will bring forth children. Your desire will be for your husband, and he will rule over you.”

1:3:17.text: And to Adam He said: “Because you have listened to the voice of your wife and have eaten from the tree of which I commanded you not to eat, cursed is the ground because of you; through toil you will eat of it all the days of your life.

1:3:18.text: Both thorns and thistles it will yield for you, and you will eat the plants of the field.

1:3:19.text: By the sweat of your brow you will eat your bread, until you return to the ground — because out of it were you taken. For dust you are, and to dust you shall return.”

1:3:20.text: And Adam named his wife Eve, because she would be the mother of all the living.

1:3:6.text: When the woman saw that the tree was good for food and pleasing to the eyes, and that it was desirable for obtaining wisdom, she took the fruit and ate it. She also gave some to her husband who was with her, and he ate it.

1:43:1.text: Now the famine was still severe in the land.

1:43:10.text: If we had not delayed, we could have come and gone twice by now.”

1:43:11.text: Then their father Israel said to them, “If it must be so, then do this: Put some of the best products of the land in your packs and carry them down as a gift for the man — a little balm and a little honey, spices and myrrh, pistachios and almonds.

1:43:12.text: Take double the silver with you so that you may return the silver that was put back into the mouths of your sacks. Perhaps it was a mistake.

1:43:13.text: Take your brother as well, and return to the man at once.

1:43:14.text: May God Almighty grant you mercy before the man, that he may release your other brother along with Benjamin. As for me, if I am bereaved, I am bereaved.”

1:43:15.text: So the men took these gifts, along with double the amount of silver, and Benjamin as well. Then they hurried down to Egypt and stood before Joseph.

1:43:16.text: When Joseph saw Benjamin with his brothers, he said to the steward of his house, “Take these men to my house. Slaughter an animal and prepare it, for they shall dine with me at noon.”

1:43:17.text: The man did as Joseph had commanded and took the brothers to Joseph’s house.

1:43:18.text: But the brothers were frightened that they had been taken to Joseph’s house. “We have been brought here because of the silver that was returned in our bags the first time,” they said. “They intend to overpower us and take us as slaves, along with our donkeys.”

1:43:19.text: So they approached Joseph’s steward and spoke to him at the entrance to the house.

1:43:2.text: So when Jacob’s sons had eaten all the grain they had brought from Egypt, their father said to them, “Go back and buy us a little more food.”

1:43:20.text: “Please, sir,” they said, “we really did come down here the first time to buy food.

1:43:21.text: But when we came to the place we lodged for the night, we opened our sacks and, behold, each of us found his silver in the mouth of his sack! It was the full amount of our silver, and we have brought it back with us.

1:43:22.text: We have brought additional silver with us to buy food. We do not know who put our silver in our sacks.”

1:43:23.text: “It is fine,” said the steward. “Do not be afraid. Your God, the God of your father, gave you the treasure that was in your sacks. I received your silver.” Then he brought Simeon out to them.

1:43:24.text: And the steward took the men into Joseph’s house, gave them water to wash their feet, and provided food for their donkeys.

1:43:25.text: Since the brothers had been told that they were going to eat a meal there, they prepared their gift for Joseph’s arrival at noon.

1:43:26.text: When Joseph came home, they presented him with the gifts they had brought, and they bowed to the ground before him.

1:43:27.text: He asked if they were well, and then he asked, “How is your elderly father you told me about? Is he still alive?”

1:43:28.text: “Your servant our father is well,” they answered. “He is still alive.” And they bowed down to honor him.

1:43:29.text: When Joseph looked up and saw his brother Benjamin, his own mother’s son, he asked, “Is this your youngest brother, the one you told me about?” Then he declared, “May God be gracious to you, my son.”

1:43:3.text: But Judah replied, “The man solemnly warned us, ‘You will not see my face again unless your brother is with you.’

1:43:30.text: Joseph hurried out because he was moved to tears for his brother, and he went to a private room to weep.

1:43:31.text: Then he washed his face and came back out. Regaining his composure, he said, “Serve the meal.”

1:43:32.text: They separately served Joseph, his brothers, and the Egyptians. They ate separately because the Egyptians would not eat with the Hebrews, since that was detestable to them.

1:43:33.text: They were seated before Joseph in order by age, from the firstborn to the youngest, and the men looked at one another in astonishment.

1:43:34.text: When the portions were served to them from Joseph’s table, Benjamin’s portion was five times larger than any of the others. So they feasted and drank freely with Joseph.

1:43:4.text: If you will send our brother with us, we will go down and buy food for you.

1:43:5.text: But if you will not send him, we will not go; for the man told us, ‘You will not see my face again unless your brother is with you.’ ”

1:43:6.text: “Why did you bring this trouble upon me?” Israel asked. “Why did you tell the man you had another brother?”

1:43:7.text: They replied, “The man questioned us in detail about ourselves and our family: ‘Is your father still alive? Do you have another brother?’ And we answered him accordingly. How could we possibly know that he would say, ‘Bring your brother here’ ?”

1:43:8.text: And Judah said to his father Israel, “Send the boy with me, and we will go at once, so that we may live and not die — neither we, nor you, nor our children.

1:43:9.text: I will guarantee his safety. You may hold me personally responsible. If I do not bring him back and set him before you, then may I bear the guilt before you all my life.

1:45:1.text: Then Joseph could no longer control himself before all his attendants, and he cried out, “Send everyone away from me!” So none of them were with Joseph when he made himself known to his brothers.

1:45:10.text: You shall settle in the land of Goshen and be near me — you and your children and grandchildren, your flocks and herds, and everything you own.

1:45:11.text: And there I will provide for you, because there will be five more years of famine. Otherwise, you and your household and everything you own will come to destitution.’

1:45:12.text: Behold! You and my brother Benjamin can see that I, Joseph, am the one speaking with you.

1:45:13.text: Tell my father about all my splendor in Egypt and everything you have seen. And bring my father down here quickly.”

1:45:14.text: Then Joseph threw his arms around his brother Benjamin and wept, and Benjamin wept as they embraced.

1:45:15.text: Joseph kissed each of his brothers as he wept over them. And afterward his brothers talked with him.

1:45:16.text: When the news reached Pharaoh’s house that Joseph’s brothers had come, Pharaoh and his servants were pleased.

1:45:17.text: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Tell your brothers, ‘Do as follows: Load your animals and return to the land of Canaan.

1:45:18.text: Then bring your father and your families and return to me. I will give you the best of the land of Egypt, and you shall eat from the fat of the land.’

1:45:19.text: You are also directed to tell them: ‘Take wagons from the land of Egypt for your young children and your wives, and bring your father and come back.

1:45:2.text: But he wept so loudly that the Egyptians heard him, and Pharaoh’s household soon heard of it.

1:45:20.text: But pay no regard to your belongings, for the best of all the land of Egypt is yours.’ ”

1:45:21.text: So the sons of Israel did as they were told. Joseph gave them wagons as Pharaoh had instructed, and he also gave them provisions for their journey.

1:45:22.text: He gave new garments to each of them, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred shekels of silver and five sets of clothes.

1:45:23.text: And he sent to his father the following: ten donkeys loaded with the best of Egypt, and ten female donkeys loaded with grain and bread and provisions for his father’s journey.

1:45:24.text: Then Joseph sent his brothers on their way, and as they were leaving, he said to them, “Do not quarrel on the way!”

1:45:25.text: So the brothers went up out of Egypt and came to their father Jacob in the land of Canaan.

1:45:26.text: “Joseph is still alive,” they said, “and he is ruler over all the land of Egypt!” But Jacob was stunned, for he did not believe them.

1:45:27.text: However, when they relayed all that Joseph had told them, and when he saw the wagons that Joseph had sent to carry him back, the spirit of their father Jacob was revived.

1:45:28.text: “Enough!” declared Israel. “My son Joseph is still alive! I will go to see him before I die.”

1:45:3.text: Joseph said to his brothers, “I am Joseph! Is my father still alive?” But they were unable to answer him, because they were terrified in his presence.

1:45:4.text: Then Joseph said to his brothers, “Please come near me.” And they did so. “I am Joseph, your brother,” he said, “the one you sold into Egypt!

1:45:5.text: And now, do not be distressed or angry with yourselves that you sold me into this place, because it was to save lives that God sent me before you.

1:45:6.text: For the famine has covered the land these two years, and there will be five more years without plowing or harvesting.

1:45:7.text: God sent me before you to preserve you as a remnant on the earth and to save your lives by a great deliverance.

1:45:8.text: Therefore it was not you who sent me here, but God, who has made me a father to Pharaoh — lord of all his household and ruler over all the land of Egypt.

1:45:9.text: Now return quickly to my father and tell him, ‘This is what your son Joseph says: God has made me lord of all Egypt. Come down to me without delay.

1:46:29.text: Joseph prepared his chariot and went there to meet his father Israel. Joseph presented himself to him, embraced him, and wept profusely.

1:46:30.text: Then Israel said to Joseph, “Finally I can die, now that I have seen your face and know that you are still alive!”

1:46:31.text: Joseph said to his brothers and to his father’s household, “I will go up and inform Pharaoh: ‘My brothers and my father’s household from the land of Canaan have come to me.

1:46:33.text: When Pharaoh summons you and asks, ‘What is your occupation?’

1:46:4.text: I will go down with you to Egypt, and I will surely bring you back. And Joseph’s own hands will close your eyes.”

1:46:5.text: Then Jacob departed from Beersheba, and the sons of Israel took their father Jacob in the wagons Pharaoh had sent to carry him, along with their children and wives.

1:46:6.text: They also took the livestock and possessions they had acquired in the land of Canaan, and Jacob and all his offspring went to Egypt.

1:46:7.text: Jacob took with him to Egypt his sons and grandsons, and his daughters and granddaughters — all his offspring.

1:46:8.text: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel (Jacob and his descendants) who went to Egypt: Reuben, Jacob’s firstborn.

1:46:9.text: The sons of Reuben: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.

1:4:1.text: And Adam had relations with his wife Eve, and she conceived and gave birth to Cain. “With the help of the Lord I have brought forth a man,” she said.

1:4:10.text: “What have you done?” replied the Lord. “The voice of your brother’s blood cries out to Me from the ground.

1:4:11.text: Now you are cursed and banished from the ground, which has opened its mouth to receive your brother’s blood from your hand.

1:4:12.text: When you till the ground, it will no longer yield its produce to you. You will be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth.”

1:4:13.text: But Cain said to the Lord, “My punishment is greater than I can bear.

1:4:14.text: Behold, this day You have driven me from the face of the earth, and from Your face I will be hidden; I will be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth, and whoever finds me will kill me.”

1:4:15.text: “Not so!” replied the Lord. “If anyone slays Cain, then Cain will be avenged sevenfold.” And the Lord placed a mark on Cain, so that no one who found him would kill him.

1:4:16.text: So Cain went out from the presence of the Lord and settled in the land of Nod, east of Eden.

1:4:17.text: And Cain had relations with his wife, and she conceived and gave birth to Enoch. Then Cain built a city and named it after his son Enoch.

1:4:18.text: Now to Enoch was born Irad, and Irad was the father of Mehujael, and Mehujael was the father of Methusael, and Methusael was the father of Lamech.

1:4:19.text: And Lamech married two women, one named Adah and the other Zillah.

1:4:2.text: Later she gave birth to Cain’s brother Abel. Now Abel was a keeper of sheep, while Cain was a tiller of the soil.

1:4:20.text: Adah gave birth to Jabal; he was the father of those who dwell in tents and raise livestock.

1:4:21.text: And his brother’s name was Jubal; he was the father of all who play the harp and flute.

1:4:22.text: And Zillah gave birth to Tubal-cain, a forger of every implement of bronze and iron. And the sister of Tubal-cain was Naamah.

1:4:23.text: Then Lamech said to his wives: “Adah and Zillah, hear my voice; wives of Lamech, listen to my speech. For I have slain a man for wounding me, a young man for striking me.

1:4:24.text: If Cain is avenged sevenfold, then Lamech seventy-sevenfold.”

1:4:25.text: And Adam again had relations with his wife, and she gave birth to a son and named him Seth, saying, “God has granted me another seed in place of Abel, since Cain killed him.”

1:4:26.text: And to Seth also a son was born, and he called him Enosh. At that time men began to call upon the name of the Lord.

1:4:3.text: So in the course of time, Cain brought some of the fruit of the soil as an offering to the Lord,

1:4:4.text: while Abel brought the best portions of the firstborn of his flock. And the Lord looked with favor on Abel and his offering,

1:4:5.text: but He had no regard for Cain and his offering. So Cain became very angry, and his countenance fell.

1:4:6.text: “Why are you angry,” said the Lord to Cain, “and why has your countenance fallen?

1:4:7.text: If you do what is right, will you not be accepted? But if you refuse to do what is right, sin is crouching at your door; it desires you, but you must master it.”

1:4:8.text: Then Cain said to his brother Abel, “Let us go out to the field.” And while they were in the field, Cain rose up against his brother Abel and killed him.

1:4:9.text: And the Lord said to Cain, “Where is your brother Abel?” “I do not know!” he answered. “Am I my brother’s keeper?”

1:50:1.text: Then Joseph fell upon his father’s face, wept over him, and kissed him.

1:50:10.text: When they reached the threshing floor of Atad, which is across the Jordan, they lamented and wailed loudly, and Joseph mourned for his father seven days.

1:50:11.text: When the Canaanites of the land saw the mourning at the threshing floor of Atad, they said, “This is a solemn ceremony of mourning by the Egyptians.” Thus the place across the Jordan is called Abel-mizraim.

1:50:12.text: So Jacob’s sons did as he had charged them.

1:50:13.text: They carried him to the land of Canaan and buried him in the cave at Machpelah in the field near Mamre, which Abraham had purchased from Ephron the Hittite as a burial site.

1:50:14.text: After Joseph had buried his father, he returned to Egypt with his brothers and all who had gone with him to bury his father.

1:50:15.text: When Joseph’s brothers saw that their father was dead, they said, “What if Joseph bears a grudge? Then he will surely repay us for all the evil that we did to him.”

1:50:16.text: So they sent word to Joseph, saying, “Before he died, your father commanded,

1:50:17.text: ‘This is what you are to say to Joseph: I beg you, please forgive the transgression and sin of your brothers, for they did you wrong.’ So now, Joseph, please forgive the transgression of the servants of the God of your father.” When their message came to him, Joseph wept.

1:50:18.text: His brothers also came to him, bowed down before him, and said, “We are your slaves!”

1:50:19.text: But Joseph replied, “Do not be afraid. Am I in the place of God?

1:50:2.text: And Joseph directed the physicians in his service to embalm his father Israel. So they embalmed him,

1:50:20.text: As for you, what you intended against me for evil, God intended for good, in order to accomplish a day like this — to preserve the lives of many people.

1:50:21.text: Therefore do not be afraid. I will provide for you and your little ones.” So Joseph reassured his brothers and spoke kindly to them.

1:50:22.text: Now Joseph and his father’s household remained in Egypt, and Joseph lived to the age of 110.

1:50:23.text: He saw Ephraim’s sons to the third generation, and indeed the sons of Machir son of Manasseh were brought up on Joseph’s knees.

1:50:24.text: Then Joseph said to his brothers, “I am about to die, but God will surely visit you and bring you up from this land to the land He promised on oath to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”

1:50:25.text: And Joseph made the sons of Israel take an oath and said, “God will surely attend to you, and then you must carry my bones up from this place.”

1:50:26.text: So Joseph died at the age of 110. And they embalmed his body and placed it in a coffin in Egypt.

1:50:6.text: Pharaoh replied, “Go up and bury your father, as he made you swear to do.”

1:6:10.text: And Noah had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

1:6:11.text: Now the earth was corrupt in the sight of God, and full of violence.

1:6:12.text: And God looked upon the earth and saw that it was corrupt; for all living creatures on the earth had corrupted their ways.

1:6:13.text: Then God said to Noah, “The end of all living creatures has come before Me, because through them the earth is full of violence. Now behold, I will destroy both them and the earth.

1:6:14.text: Make for yourself an ark of gopher wood; make rooms in the ark and coat it with pitch inside and out.

1:6:15.text: And this is how you are to build it: The ark is to be 300 cubits long, 50 cubits wide, and 30 cubits high.

1:6:16.text: You are to make a roof for the ark, finish its walls a cubit from the top, place a door in the side of the ark, and build lower, middle, and upper decks.

1:6:17.text: And behold, I will bring floodwaters upon the earth to destroy every creature under the heavens that has the breath of life. Everything on the earth will perish.

1:6:18.text: But I will establish My covenant with you, and you will enter the ark — you and your sons and your wife and your sons’ wives with you.

1:6:19.text: And you are to bring two of every living creature into the ark — male and female — to keep them alive with you.

1:6:20.text: Two of every kind of bird and animal and crawling creature will come to you to be kept alive.

1:6:22.text: So Noah did everything precisely as God had commanded him.

1:6:3.text: So the Lord said, “My Spirit will not contend with man forever, for he is mortal; his days shall be 120 years.”
