23:13:20.text: She will never be inhabited or settled from generation to generation; no nomad will pitch his tent there, no shepherd will rest his flock there.

23:13:21.text: But desert creatures will lie down there, and howling creatures will fill her houses. Ostriches will dwell there, and wild goats will leap about.

23:13:22.text: Hyenas will howl in her fortresses and jackals in her luxurious palaces. Babylon’s time is at hand, and her days will not be prolonged.

23:13:3.text: I have commanded My sanctified ones; I have even summoned My warriors to execute My wrath and exult in My triumph.

23:13:4.text: Listen, a tumult on the mountains, like that of a great multitude! Listen, an uproar among the kingdoms, like nations gathered together! The Lord of Hosts is mobilizing an army for war.

23:13:5.text: They are coming from faraway lands, from the ends of the heavens — the Lord and the weapons of His wrath — to destroy the whole country.

23:13:6.text: Wail, for the Day of the Lord is near; it will come as destruction from the Almighty.

23:13:7.text: Therefore all hands will fall limp, and every man’s heart will melt.

23:13:8.text: Terror, pain, and anguish will seize them; they will writhe like a woman in labor. They will look at one another, their faces flushed with fear.

23:13:9.text: Behold, the Day of the Lord is coming — cruel, with fury and burning anger — to make the earth a desolation and to destroy the sinners within it.

23:14:1.text: For the Lord will have compassion on Jacob; once again He will choose Israel and settle them in their own land. The foreigner will join them and unite with the house of Jacob.

23:14:10.text: They will all respond to you, saying, “You too have become weak, as we are; you have become like us!”

23:14:11.text: Your pomp has been brought down to Sheol, along with the music of your harps. Maggots are your bed and worms your blanket.

23:14:12.text: How you have fallen from heaven, O day star, son of the dawn! You have been cut down to the ground, O destroyer of nations.

23:14:13.text: You said in your heart: “I will ascend to the heavens; I will raise my throne above the stars of God. I will sit on the mount of assembly, in the far reaches of the north.

23:14:14.text: I will ascend above the tops of the clouds; I will make myself like the Most High.”

23:14:15.text: But you will be brought down to Sheol, to the lowest depths of the Pit.

23:14:16.text: Those who see you will stare; they will ponder your fate: “Is this the man who shook the earth and made the kingdoms tremble,

23:14:17.text: who turned the world into a desert and destroyed its cities, who refused to let the captives return to their homes?”

23:14:18.text: All the kings of the nations lie in state, each in his own tomb.

23:14:19.text: But you are cast out of your grave like a rejected branch, covered by those slain with the sword, and dumped into a rocky pit like a carcass trampled underfoot.

23:14:2.text: The nations will escort Israel and bring it to its homeland. Then the house of Israel will possess the nations as menservants and maidservants in the Lord’s land. They will make captives of their captors and rule over their oppressors.

23:14:20.text: You will not join them in burial, since you have destroyed your land and slaughtered your own people. The offspring of the wicked will never again be mentioned.

23:14:21.text: Prepare a place to slaughter his sons for the iniquities of their forefathers. They will never rise up to possess a land or cover the earth with their cities.

23:14:22.text: “I will rise up against them,” declares the Lord of Hosts. “I will cut off from Babylon her name and her remnant, her offspring and her posterity,” declares the Lord.

23:14:23.text: “I will make her a place for owls and for swamplands; I will sweep her away with the broom of destruction,” declares the Lord of Hosts.

23:14:24.text: The Lord of Hosts has sworn: “Surely, as I have planned, so will it be; as I have purposed, so will it stand.

23:14:25.text: I will break Assyria in My land; I will trample him on My mountain. His yoke will be taken off My people, and his burden removed from their shoulders.”

23:14:26.text: This is the plan devised for the whole earth, and this is the hand stretched out over all the nations.

23:14:27.text: The Lord of Hosts has purposed, and who can thwart Him? His hand is outstretched, so who can turn it back?

23:14:28.text: In the year that King Ahaz died, this burden was received:

23:14:29.text: Do not rejoice, all you Philistines, that the rod that struck you is broken. For a viper will spring from the root of the snake, and a flying serpent from its egg.

23:14:3.text: On the day that the Lord gives you rest from your pain and torment, and from the hard labor into which you were forced,

23:14:30.text: Then the firstborn of the poor will find pasture, and the needy will lie down in safety, but I will kill your root by famine, and your remnant will be slain.

23:14:31.text: Wail, O gate! Cry out, O city! Melt away, all you Philistines! For a cloud of smoke comes from the north, and there are no stragglers in its ranks.

23:14:32.text: What answer will be given to the envoys of that nation? “The Lord has founded Zion, where His afflicted people will find refuge.”

23:14:4.text: you will sing this song of contempt against the king of Babylon: How the oppressor has ceased, and how his fury has ended!

23:14:5.text: The Lord has broken the staff of the wicked, the scepter of the rulers.

23:14:6.text: It struck the peoples in anger with unceasing blows; it subdued the nations in rage with relentless persecution.

23:14:7.text: All the earth is at peace and at rest; they break out in song.

23:14:8.text: Even the cypresses and cedars of Lebanon exult over you: “Since you have been laid low, no woodcutter comes against us.”

23:14:9.text: Sheol beneath is eager to meet you upon your arrival. It stirs the spirits of the dead to greet you — all the rulers of the earth. It makes all the kings of the nations rise from their thrones.

23:1:1.text: This is the vision concerning Judah and Jerusalem that Isaiah son of Amoz saw during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.

23:1:10.text: Hear the word of the Lord, you rulers of Sodom; listen to the instruction of our God, you people of Gomorrah!

23:1:11.text: “What good to Me is your multitude of sacrifices?” says the Lord. “I am full from the burnt offerings of rams and the fat of well-fed cattle; I take no delight in the blood of bulls and lambs and goats.

23:1:12.text: When you come to appear before Me, who has required this of you — this trampling of My courts?

23:1:13.text: Bring your worthless offerings no more; your incense is detestable to Me — your New Moons, Sabbaths, and convocations. I cannot endure iniquity in a solemn assembly.

23:1:14.text: I hate your New Moons and your appointed feasts. They have become a burden to Me; I am weary of bearing them.

23:1:15.text: When you spread out your hands in prayer, I will hide My eyes from you; even though you multiply your prayers, I will not listen. Your hands are covered with blood.

23:1:16.text: Wash and cleanse yourselves. Remove your evil deeds from My sight. Stop doing evil!

23:1:17.text: Learn to do right; seek justice and correct the oppressor. Defend the fatherless and plead the case of the widow.”

23:1:18.text: “Come now, let us reason together,” says the Lord. “Though your sins are like scarlet, they will be as white as snow; though they are as red as crimson, they will become like wool.

23:1:19.text: If you are willing and obedient, you will eat the best of the land.

23:1:2.text: Listen, O heavens, and give ear, O earth, for the Lord has spoken: “I have raised children and brought them up, but they have rebelled against Me.

23:1:20.text: But if you resist and rebel, you will be devoured by the sword.” For the mouth of the Lord has spoken.

23:1:21.text: See how the faithful city has become a harlot! She once was full of justice; righteousness resided within her, but now only murderers!

23:1:22.text: Your silver has become dross; your fine wine is diluted with water.

23:1:23.text: Your rulers are rebels, friends of thieves. They all love bribes and chasing after rewards. They do not defend the fatherless, and the plea of the widow never comes before them.

23:1:24.text: Therefore the Lord GOD of Hosts, the Mighty One of Israel, declares: “Ah, I will be relieved of My foes and avenge Myself on My enemies.

23:1:25.text: I will turn My hand against you; I will thoroughly purge your dross; I will remove all your impurities.

23:1:26.text: I will restore your judges as at first, and your counselors as at the beginning. After that you will be called the City of Righteousness, the Faithful City.”

23:1:27.text: Zion will be redeemed with justice, her repentant ones with righteousness.

23:1:28.text: But rebels and sinners will together be shattered, and those who forsake the Lord will perish.

23:1:29.text: Surely you will be ashamed of the sacred oaks in which you have delighted; you will be embarrassed by the gardens that you have chosen.

23:1:3.text: The ox knows its owner, and the donkey its master’s manger, but Israel does not know; My people do not understand.”

23:1:30.text: For you will become like an oak whose leaves are withered, like a garden without water.

23:1:31.text: The strong man will become tinder and his work will be a spark; both will burn together, with no one to quench the flames.

23:1:4.text: Alas, O sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a brood of evildoers, children of depravity! They have forsaken the Lord ; they have despised the Holy One of Israel and turned their backs on Him.

23:1:5.text: Why do you want more beatings? Why do you keep rebelling? Your head has a massive wound, and your whole heart is afflicted.

23:1:6.text: From the sole of your foot to the top of your head, there is no soundness — only wounds and welts and festering sores neither cleansed nor bandaged nor soothed with oil.

23:1:7.text: Your land is desolate; your cities are burned with fire. Foreigners devour your fields before you — a desolation demolished by strangers.

23:1:8.text: And the Daughter of Zion is abandoned like a shelter in a vineyard, like a shack in a cucumber field, like a city besieged.

23:1:9.text: Unless the Lord of Hosts had left us a few survivors, we would have become like Sodom, we would have resembled Gomorrah.

23:25:1.text: O Lord, You are my God! I will exalt You; I will praise Your name. For You have worked wonders — plans formed long ago — in perfect faithfulness.

23:25:10.text: For the hand of the Lord will rest on this mountain. But Moab will be trampled in his place as straw is trodden into the dung pile.

23:25:11.text: He will spread out his hands within it, as a swimmer spreads his arms to swim. His pride will be brought low, despite the skill of his hands.

23:25:12.text: The high-walled fortress will be brought down, cast to the ground, into the dust.

23:25:2.text: Indeed, You have made the city a heap of rubble, the fortified town a ruin. The fortress of strangers is a city no more; it will never be rebuilt.

23:25:3.text: Therefore, a strong people will honor You. The cities of ruthless nations will revere You.

23:25:4.text: For You have been a refuge for the poor, a stronghold for the needy in distress, a refuge from the storm, a shade from the heat. For the breath of the ruthless is like rain against a wall,

23:25:5.text: like heat in a dry land. You subdue the uproar of foreigners. As the shade of a cloud cools the heat, so the song of the ruthless is silenced.

23:25:6.text: On this mountain the Lord of Hosts will prepare a banquet for all the peoples, a feast of aged wine, of choice meat, of finely aged wine.

23:25:7.text: On this mountain He will swallow up the shroud that enfolds all peoples, the sheet that covers all nations;

23:25:8.text: He will swallow up death forever. The Lord GOD will wipe away the tears from every face and remove the disgrace of His people from the whole earth. For the Lord has spoken.

23:25:9.text: And in that day it will be said, “Surely this is our God; we have waited for Him, and He has saved us. This is the Lord for whom we have waited. Let us rejoice and be glad in His salvation.”

23:26:1.text: In that day this song will be sung in the land of Judah: We have a strong city; salvation is established as its walls and ramparts.

23:26:10.text: Though grace is shown to the wicked man, he does not learn righteousness. In the land of righteousness he acts unjustly and fails to see the majesty of the Lord.

23:26:11.text: O Lord, Your hand is upraised, but they do not see it. They will see Your zeal for Your people and be put to shame. The fire set for Your enemies will consume them!

23:26:12.text: O Lord, You will establish peace for us. For all that we have accomplished, You have done for us.

23:26:13.text: O Lord our God, other lords besides You have had dominion, but Your name alone do we confess.

23:26:14.text: The dead will not live; the departed spirits will not rise. Therefore You have punished and destroyed them; You have wiped out all memory of them.

23:26:15.text: You have enlarged the nation, O Lord ; You have enlarged the nation. You have gained glory for Yourself; You have extended all the borders of the land.

23:26:16.text: O Lord, they sought You in their distress; when You disciplined them, they poured out a quiet prayer.

23:26:17.text: As a woman with child about to give birth writhes and cries out in pain, so were we in Your presence, O Lord.

23:26:18.text: We were with child; we writhed in pain; but we gave birth to wind. We have given no salvation to the earth, nor brought any life into the world.

23:26:19.text: Your dead will live; their bodies will rise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust! For your dew is like the dew of the morning, and the earth will bring forth her dead.

23:26:2.text: Open the gates so a righteous nation may enter — one that remains faithful.

23:26:20.text: Go, my people, enter your rooms and shut your doors behind you. Hide yourselves a little while until the wrath has passed.

23:26:21.text: For behold, the Lord is coming out of His dwelling to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity. The earth will reveal her bloodshed and will no longer conceal her slain.

23:26:3.text: You will keep in perfect peace the steadfast of mind, because he trusts in You.

23:26:4.text: Trust in the Lord forever, because GOD the Lord is the Rock eternal.

23:26:5.text: For He has humbled those who dwell on high; He lays the lofty city low. He brings it down to the ground; He casts it into the dust.

23:26:6.text: Feet trample it down — the feet of the oppressed, the steps of the poor.

23:26:7.text: The path of the righteous is level; You clear a straight path for the upright.

23:26:8.text: Yes, we wait for You, O Lord ; we walk in the path of Your judgments. Your name and renown are the desire of our souls.

23:26:9.text: My soul longs for You in the night; indeed, my spirit seeks You at dawn. For when Your judgments come upon the earth, the people of the world learn righteousness.

23:27:1.text: In that day the Lord will take His sharp, great, and mighty sword, and bring judgment on Leviathan the fleeing serpent — Leviathan the coiling serpent — and He will slay the dragon of the sea.

23:27:10.text: For the fortified city lies deserted — a homestead abandoned, a wilderness forsaken. There the calves graze, and there they lie down; they strip its branches bare.

23:27:11.text: When its limbs are dry, they are broken off. Women come and use them for kindling; for this is a people without understanding. Therefore their Maker has no compassion on them, and their Creator shows them no favor.

23:27:12.text: In that day the Lord will thresh from the flowing Euphrates to the Wadi of Egypt, and you, O Israelites, will be gathered one by one.

23:27:13.text: And in that day a great ram’s horn will sound, and those who were perishing in Assyria will come forth with those who were exiles in Egypt. And they will worship the Lord on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.

23:27:2.text: In that day: “Sing about a fruitful vineyard.

23:27:3.text: I, the Lord, am its keeper; I water it continually. I guard it night and day so no one can disturb it;

23:27:4.text: I am not angry. If only thorns and briers confronted Me, I would march and trample them, I would burn them to the ground.

23:27:5.text: Or let them lay claim to My protection; let them make peace with Me — yes, let them make peace with Me.”

23:27:6.text: In the days to come, Jacob will take root. Israel will bud and blossom and fill the whole world with fruit.

23:27:7.text: Has the Lord struck Israel as He struck her oppressors? Was she killed like those who slayed her?

23:27:8.text: By warfare and exile You contended with her and removed her with a fierce wind, as on the day the east wind blows.

23:27:9.text: Therefore Jacob’s guilt will be atoned for, and the full fruit of the removal of his sin will be this: When he makes all the altar stones like crushed bits of chalk, no Asherah poles or incense altars will remain standing.

23:28:1.text: Woe to the majestic crown of Ephraim’s drunkards, to the fading flower of his glorious splendor, set on the summit above the fertile valley, the pride of those overcome by wine.

23:28:10.text: For they hear: “Order on order, order on order, line on line, line on line; a little here, a little there.”

23:28:11.text: Indeed, with mocking lips and foreign tongues, He will speak to this people

23:28:12.text: to whom He has said: “This is the place of rest, let the weary rest; this is the place of repose.” But they would not listen.

23:28:13.text: Then the word of the Lord to them will become: “Order on order, order on order, line on line, line on line; a little here, a little there,” so that they will go stumbling backward and will be injured, ensnared, and captured.

23:28:14.text: Therefore hear the word of the Lord, O scoffers who rule this people in Jerusalem.

23:28:15.text: For you said, “We have made a covenant with death; we have fashioned an agreement with Sheol. When the overwhelming scourge passes through it will not touch us, because we have made lies our refuge and falsehood our hiding place.”

23:28:16.text: So this is what the Lord GOD says: “See, I lay a stone in Zion, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation; the one who believes will never be shaken.

23:28:17.text: I will make justice the measuring line and righteousness the level. Hail will sweep away your refuge of lies, and water will flood your hiding place.

23:28:18.text: Your covenant with death will be dissolved, and your agreement with Sheol will not stand. When the overwhelming scourge passes through, you will be trampled by it.

23:28:19.text: As often as it passes through, it will carry you away; it will sweep through morning after morning, by day and by night.” The understanding of this message will bring sheer terror.

23:28:2.text: Behold, the Lord has one who is strong and mighty. Like a hailstorm or destructive tempest, like a driving rain or flooding downpour, he will smash that crown to the ground.

23:28:20.text: Indeed, the bed is too short to stretch out on, and the blanket too small to wrap around you.

23:28:21.text: For the Lord will rise up as at Mount Perazim. He will rouse Himself as in the Valley of Gibeon, to do His work, His strange work, and to perform His task, His disturbing task.

23:28:22.text: So now, do not mock, or your shackles will become heavier. Indeed, I have heard from the Lord GOD of Hosts a decree of destruction against the whole land.

23:28:23.text: Listen and hear my voice. Pay attention and hear what I say.

23:28:24.text: Does the plowman plow for planting every day? Does he continuously loosen and harrow the soil?

23:28:25.text: When he has leveled its surface, does he not sow caraway and scatter cumin? He plants wheat in rows and barley in plots, and rye within its border.

23:28:26.text: For his God instructs and teaches him properly.

23:28:27.text: Surely caraway is not threshed with a sledge, and the wheel of a cart is not rolled over the cumin. But caraway is beaten out with a stick, and cumin with a rod.

23:28:28.text: Grain for bread must be ground, but it is not endlessly threshed. Though the wheels of the cart roll over it, the horses do not crush it.

23:28:29.text: This also comes from the Lord of Hosts, who is wonderful in counsel and excellent in wisdom.

23:28:3.text: The majestic crown of Ephraim’s drunkards will be trampled underfoot.

23:28:4.text: The fading flower of his beautiful splendor, set on the summit above the fertile valley, will be like a ripe fig before the summer harvest: Whoever sees it will take it in his hand and swallow it.

23:28:5.text: On that day the Lord of Hosts will be a crown of glory, a diadem of splendor to the remnant of His people,

23:28:6.text: a spirit of justice to him who sits in judgment, and a strength to those who repel the onslaught at the gate.

23:28:7.text: These also stagger from wine and stumble from strong drink: Priests and prophets reel from strong drink and are befuddled by wine. They stumble because of strong drink, muddled in their visions and stumbling in their judgments.

23:28:8.text: For all their tables are covered with vomit; there is not a place without filth.

23:28:9.text: Whom is He trying to teach? To whom is He explaining His message? To infants just weaned from milk? To babies removed from the breast?

23:29:1.text: Woe to you, O Ariel, the city of Ariel where David camped! Year upon year let your festivals recur.

23:29:10.text: For the Lord has poured out on you a spirit of deep sleep. He has shut your eyes, O prophets; He has covered your heads, O seers.

23:29:11.text: And the entire vision will be to you like the words sealed in a scroll. If it is handed to someone to read, he will say, “I cannot, because it is sealed.”

23:29:12.text: Or if the scroll is handed to one unable to read, he will say, “I cannot read.”

23:29:13.text: Therefore the Lord said: “These people draw near to Me with their mouths and honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me. Their worship of Me is but rules taught by men.

23:29:14.text: Therefore I will again confound these people with wonder upon wonder. The wisdom of the wise will vanish, and the intelligence of the intelligent will be hidden. ”

23:29:15.text: Woe to those who dig deep to hide their plans from the Lord. In darkness they do their works and say, “Who sees us, and who will know?”

23:29:16.text: You have turned things upside down, as if the potter were regarded as clay. Shall what is formed say to him who formed it, “He did not make me”? Can the pottery say of the potter, “He has no understanding”?

23:29:17.text: In a very short time, will not Lebanon become an orchard, and the orchard seem like a forest?

23:29:18.text: On that day the deaf will hear the words of the scroll, and out of the deep darkness the eyes of the blind will see.

23:29:19.text: The humble will increase their joy in the Lord, and the poor among men will rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.

23:29:2.text: And I will constrain Ariel, and there will be mourning and lamentation; she will be like an altar hearth before Me.

23:29:20.text: For the ruthless will vanish, the mockers will disappear, and all who look for evil will be cut down —

23:29:21.text: those who indict a man with a word, who ensnare the mediator at the gate, and who with false charges deprive the innocent of justice.

23:29:22.text: Therefore the Lord who redeemed Abraham says of the house of Jacob: “No longer will Jacob be ashamed and no more will his face grow pale.

23:29:23.text: For when he sees his children around him, the work of My hands, they will honor My name, they will sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and they will stand in awe of the God of Israel.

23:29:24.text: Then the wayward in spirit will come to understanding, and those who grumble will accept instruction.”

23:29:3.text: I will camp in a circle around you; I will besiege you with towers and set up siege works against you.

23:29:4.text: You will be brought low, you will speak from the ground, and out of the dust your words will be muffled. Your voice will be like a spirit from the ground; your speech will whisper out of the dust.

23:29:5.text: But your many foes will be like fine dust, the multitude of the ruthless like blowing chaff. Then suddenly, in an instant,

23:29:6.text: you will be visited by the Lord of Hosts with thunder and earthquake and loud noise, with windstorm and tempest and consuming flame of fire.

23:29:7.text: All the many nations going out to battle against Ariel — even all who war against her, laying siege and attacking her — will be like a dream, like a vision in the night,

23:29:8.text: as when a hungry man dreams he is eating, then awakens still hungry; as when a thirsty man dreams he is drinking, then awakens faint and parched. So will it be for all the many nations who go to battle against Mount Zion.

23:29:9.text: Stop and be astonished; blind yourselves and be sightless; be drunk, but not with wine; stagger, but not from strong drink.

23:2:1.text: This is the message that was revealed to Isaiah son of Amoz concerning Judah and Jerusalem:

23:2:10.text: Go into the rocks and hide in the dust from the terror of the Lord and the splendor of His majesty.

23:2:11.text: The proud look of man will be humbled, and the loftiness of men brought low; the Lord alone will be exalted in that day.

23:2:12.text: For the Day of the Lord of Hosts will come against all the proud and lofty, against all that is exalted — it will be humbled —

23:2:13.text: against all the cedars of Lebanon, lofty and lifted up, against all the oaks of Bashan,

23:2:14.text: against all the tall mountains, against all the high hills,

23:2:15.text: against every high tower, against every fortified wall,

23:2:16.text: against every ship of Tarshish, and against every stately vessel.

23:2:17.text: So the pride of man will be brought low, and the loftiness of men will be humbled; the Lord alone will be exalted in that day,

23:2:18.text: and the idols will vanish completely.

23:2:19.text: Men will flee to caves in the rocks and holes in the ground, away from the terror of the Lord and from the splendor of His majesty, when He rises to shake the earth.

23:2:2.text: In the last days the mountain of the house of the Lord will be established as the chief of the mountains; it will be raised above the hills, and all nations will stream to it.

23:2:20.text: In that day men will cast away to the moles and bats their idols of silver and gold — the idols they made to worship.

23:2:21.text: They will flee to caverns in the rocks and crevices in the cliffs, away from the terror of the Lord and from the splendor of His majesty, when He rises to shake the earth.

23:2:22.text: Put no more trust in man, who has only the breath in his nostrils. Of what account is he?

23:2:3.text: And many peoples will come and say: “Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Jacob. He will teach us His ways so that we may walk in His paths.” For the law will go forth from Zion, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.

23:2:4.text: Then He will judge between the nations and arbitrate for many peoples. They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation will no longer take up the sword against nation, nor train anymore for war.

23:2:5.text: Come, O house of Jacob, let us walk in the light of the Lord.

23:2:6.text: For You have abandoned Your people, the house of Jacob, because they are filled with influences from the east; they are soothsayers like the Philistines; they strike hands with the children of foreigners.

23:2:7.text: Their land is full of silver and gold, with no limit to their treasures; their land is full of horses, with no limit to their chariots.

23:2:8.text: Their land is full of idols; they bow down to the work of their hands, to what their fingers have made.

23:2:9.text: So mankind is brought low, and man is humbled — do not forgive them!

23:37:1.text: On hearing this report, King Hezekiah tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and entered the house of the Lord.

23:37:10.text: “Give this message to Hezekiah king of Judah: ‘Do not let your God, in whom you trust, deceive you by saying that Jerusalem will not be delivered into the hand of the king of Assyria.

23:37:11.text: Surely you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the other countries, devoting them to destruction. Will you then be spared?

23:37:12.text: Did the gods of the nations destroyed by my fathers rescue those nations — the gods of Gozan, Haran, and Rezeph, and of the people of Eden in Telassar?

23:37:13.text: Where are the kings of Hamath, Arpad, Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah?’ ”

23:37:14.text: So Hezekiah received the letter from the messengers, read it, and went up to the house of the Lord and spread it out before the Lord.

23:37:15.text: And Hezekiah prayed to the Lord :

23:37:16.text: “O Lord of Hosts, God of Israel, enthroned above the cherubim, You alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made the heavens and the earth.

23:37:17.text: Incline Your ear, O Lord, and hear; open Your eyes, O Lord, and see. Listen to all the words that Sennacherib has sent to defy the living God.

23:37:18.text: Truly, O Lord, the kings of Assyria have laid waste all these countries and their lands.

23:37:19.text: They have cast their gods into the fire and destroyed them, for they were not gods, but only wood and stone — the work of human hands.

23:37:2.text: And he sent Eliakim the palace administrator, Shebna the scribe, and the leading priests, all wearing sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz

23:37:20.text: And now, O Lord our God, save us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that You alone, O Lord, are God. ”

23:37:21.text: Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent a message to Hezekiah: “This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: Because you have prayed to Me concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria,

23:37:22.text: this is the word that the Lord has spoken against him: ‘The Virgin Daughter of Zion despises you and mocks you; the Daughter of Jerusalem shakes her head behind you.

23:37:23.text: Whom have you taunted and blasphemed? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted your eyes in pride? Against the Holy One of Israel!

23:37:24.text: Through your servants you have taunted the Lord, and you have said: “With my many chariots I have ascended to the heights of the mountains, to the remote peaks of Lebanon. I have cut down its tallest cedars, the finest of its cypresses. I have reached its farthest heights, the densest of its forests.

23:37:25.text: I have dug wells and drunk foreign waters. With the soles of my feet I have dried up all the streams of Egypt.”

23:37:26.text: Have you not heard? Long ago I ordained it; in days of old I planned it. Now I have brought it to pass, that you should crush fortified cities into piles of rubble.

23:37:27.text: Therefore their inhabitants, devoid of power, are dismayed and ashamed. They are like plants in the field, tender green shoots, grass on the rooftops, scorched before it is grown.

23:37:28.text: But I know your sitting down, your going out and coming in, and your raging against Me.

23:37:29.text: Because your rage and arrogance against Me have reached My ears, I will put My hook in your nose and My bit in your mouth; I will send you back the way you came.’

23:37:3.text: to tell him, “This is what Hezekiah says: Today is a day of distress, rebuke, and disgrace; for children have come to the point of birth, but there is no strength to deliver them.

23:37:30.text: And this will be a sign to you, O Hezekiah: This year you will eat what grows on its own, and in the second year what springs from the same. But in the third year you will sow and reap; you will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.

23:37:31.text: And the surviving remnant of the house of Judah will again take root below and bear fruit above.

23:37:32.text: For a remnant will go forth from Jerusalem, and survivors from Mount Zion. The zeal of the Lord of Hosts will accomplish this.

23:37:33.text: So this is what the Lord says about the king of Assyria: ‘He will not enter this city or shoot an arrow into it. He will not come before it with a shield or build up a siege ramp against it.

23:37:34.text: He will go back the way he came, and he will not enter this city,’declares the Lord.

23:37:35.text: ‘I will defend this city and save it for My own sake and for the sake of My servant David.’ ”

23:37:36.text: Then the angel of the Lord went out and struck down 185,000 men in the camp of the Assyrians. When the people got up the next morning, there were all the dead bodies!

23:37:37.text: So Sennacherib king of Assyria broke camp and withdrew. He returned to Nineveh and stayed there.

23:37:38.text: One day, while he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer put him to the sword and escaped to the land of Ararat. And his son Esar-haddon reigned in his place.

23:37:4.text: Perhaps the Lord your God will hear the words of the Rabshakeh, whom his master the king of Assyria has sent to defy the living God, and He will rebuke him for the words that the Lord your God has heard. Therefore lift up a prayer for the remnant that still survives.”

23:37:5.text: So the servants of King Hezekiah went to Isaiah,

23:37:6.text: who replied, “Tell your master that this is what the Lord says: ‘Do not be afraid of the words you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed Me.

23:37:7.text: Behold, I will put a spirit in him so that he will hear a rumor and return to his own land, where I will cause him to fall by the sword.’ ”

23:37:8.text: When the Rabshakeh heard that the king of Assyria had left Lachish, he withdrew and found the king fighting against Libnah.

23:37:9.text: Now Sennacherib had been warned about Tirhakah king of Cush: “He has set out to fight against you.” On hearing this, Sennacherib sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying,

23:38:1.text: In those days Hezekiah became mortally ill. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz came to him and said, “This is what the Lord says: ‘Put your house in order, for you are about to die; you will not recover.’ ”

23:38:10.text: I said, “In the prime of my life I must go through the gates of Sheol and be deprived of the remainder of my years.”

23:38:11.text: I said, “I will never again see the Lord, even the Lord, in the land of the living; I will no longer look on mankind with those who dwell in this world.

23:38:12.text: My dwelling has been picked up and removed from me like a shepherd’s tent. I have rolled up my life like a weaver; He cuts me off from the loom; from day until night You make an end of me.

23:38:13.text: I composed myself until the morning. Like a lion He breaks all my bones; from day until night You make an end of me.

23:38:14.text: I chirp like a swallow or crane; I moan like a dove. My eyes grow weak as I look upward. O Lord, I am oppressed; be my security.”

23:38:15.text: What can I say? He has spoken to me, and He Himself has done this. I will walk slowly all my years because of the anguish of my soul.

23:38:16.text: O Lord, by such things men live, and in all of them my spirit finds life. You have restored me to health and have let me live.

23:38:17.text: Surely for my own welfare I had such great anguish; but Your love has delivered me from the pit of oblivion, for You have cast all my sins behind Your back.

23:38:18.text: For Sheol cannot thank You; Death cannot praise You. Those who descend to the Pit cannot hope for Your faithfulness.

23:38:19.text: The living, only the living, can thank You, as I do today; fathers will tell their children about Your faithfulness.

23:38:2.text: Then Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the Lord,

23:38:20.text: The Lord will save me; we will play songs on stringed instruments all the days of our lives in the house of the Lord.

23:38:21.text: Now Isaiah had said, “Prepare a lump of pressed figs and apply it to the boil, and he will recover.”

23:38:22.text: And Hezekiah had asked, “What will be the sign that I will go up to the house of the Lord?”

23:38:3.text: saying, “Please, O Lord, remember how I have walked before You faithfully and with wholehearted devotion; I have done what was good in Your sight.” And Hezekiah wept bitterly.

23:38:4.text: And the word of the Lord came to Isaiah, saying,

23:38:5.text: “Go and tell Hezekiah that this is what the Lord, the God of your father David, says: ‘I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears. Behold, I will add fifteen years to your life.

23:38:6.text: And I will deliver you and this city from the hand of the king of Assyria. I will defend this city.

23:38:7.text: This will be a sign to you from the Lord that He will do what He has promised:

23:38:8.text: I will make the sun’s shadow that falls on the stairway of Ahaz go back ten steps.’ ” So the sunlight went back the ten steps it had descended.

23:38:9.text: This is a writing by Hezekiah king of Judah after his illness and recovery:

23:3:1.text: For behold, the Lord GOD of Hosts is about to remove from Jerusalem and Judah both supply and support: the whole supply of food and water,

23:3:10.text: Tell the righteous it will be well with them, for they will enjoy the fruit of their labor.

23:3:11.text: Woe to the wicked; disaster is upon them! For they will be repaid with what their hands have done.

23:3:12.text: Youths oppress My people, and women rule over them. O My people, your guides mislead you; they turn you from your paths.

23:3:13.text: The Lord arises to contend; He stands to judge the people.

23:3:14.text: The Lord brings this charge against the elders and leaders of His people: “You have devoured the vineyard; the plunder of the poor is in your houses.

23:3:15.text: Why do you crush My people and grind the faces of the poor?” declares the Lord GOD of Hosts.

23:3:16.text: The Lord also says: “Because the daughters of Zion are haughty — walking with heads held high and wanton eyes, prancing and skipping as they go, jingling the bracelets on their ankles —

23:3:17.text: the Lord will bring sores on the heads of the daughters of Zion, and the Lord will make their foreheads bare. ”

23:3:18.text: In that day the Lord will take away their finery: their anklets and headbands and crescents;

23:3:2.text: the mighty man and the warrior, the judge and the prophet, the soothsayer and the elder,

23:3:20.text: their headdresses, ankle chains, and sashes; their perfume bottles and charms;

23:3:21.text: their signet rings and nose rings;

23:3:22.text: their festive robes, capes, cloaks, and purses;

23:3:23.text: and their mirrors, linen garments, tiaras, and shawls.

23:3:24.text: Instead of fragrance there will be a stench; instead of a belt, a rope; instead of styled hair, baldness; instead of fine clothing, sackcloth; instead of beauty, shame.

23:3:25.text: Your men will fall by the sword, and your warriors in battle.

23:3:26.text: And the gates of Zion will lament and mourn; destitute, she will sit on the ground.

23:3:3.text: the commander of fifty and the dignitary, the counselor, the cunning magician, and the clever enchanter.

23:3:4.text: “I will make mere lads their leaders, and children will rule over them.”

23:3:5.text: The people will oppress one another, man against man, neighbor against neighbor; the young will rise up against the old, and the base against the honorable.

23:3:6.text: A man will seize his brother within his father’s house: “You have a cloak — you be our leader! Take charge of this heap of rubble.”

23:3:7.text: On that day he will cry aloud: “I am not a healer. I have no food or clothing in my house. Do not make me leader of the people!”

23:3:8.text: For Jerusalem has stumbled and Judah has fallen because they spoke and acted against the Lord, defying His glorious presence.

23:3:9.text: The expression on their faces testifies against them, and like Sodom they flaunt their sin; they do not conceal it. Woe to them, for they have brought disaster upon themselves.

23:40:1.text: “Comfort, comfort My people,” says your God.

23:40:10.text: Behold, the Lord GOD comes with might, and His arm establishes His rule. His reward is with Him, and His recompense accompanies Him.

23:40:11.text: He tends His flock like a shepherd; He gathers the lambs in His arms and carries them close to His heart. He gently leads the nursing ewes.

23:40:12.text: Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, or marked off the heavens with the span of his hand? Who has held the dust of the earth in a basket, or weighed the mountains on a scale and the hills with a balance?

23:40:13.text: Who has directed the Spirit of the Lord, or informed Him as His counselor?

23:40:14.text: Whom did He consult to enlighten Him, and who taught Him the paths of justice? Who imparted knowledge to Him and showed Him the way of understanding?

23:40:15.text: Surely the nations are like a drop in a bucket; they are considered a speck of dust on the scales; He lifts up the islands like fine dust.

23:40:16.text: Lebanon is not sufficient for fuel, nor its animals enough for a burnt offering.

23:40:17.text: All the nations are as nothing before Him; He regards them as nothingness and emptiness.

23:40:18.text: To whom will you liken God? To what image will you compare Him?

23:40:19.text: To an idol that a craftsman casts and a metalworker overlays with gold and fits with silver chains?

23:40:2.text: “Speak tenderly to Jerusalem, and proclaim to her that her forced labor has been completed; her iniquity has been pardoned. For she has received from the hand of the Lord double for all her sins.”

23:40:20.text: To one bereft of an offering who chooses wood that will not rot, who seeks a skilled craftsman to set up an idol that will not topple?

23:40:21.text: Do you not know? Have you not heard? Has it not been declared to you from the beginning? Have you not understood since the foundation of the earth?

23:40:22.text: He sits enthroned above the circle of the earth; its dwellers are like grasshoppers. He stretches out the heavens like a curtain, and spreads them out like a tent to dwell in.

23:40:23.text: He brings the princes to nothing and makes the rulers of the earth meaningless.

23:40:24.text: No sooner are they planted, no sooner are they sown, no sooner have their stems taken root in the ground, than He blows on them and they wither, and a whirlwind sweeps them away like stubble.

23:40:25.text: “To whom will you liken Me, or who is My equal?” asks the Holy One.

23:40:26.text: Lift up your eyes on high: Who created all these? He leads forth the starry host by number; He calls each one by name. Because of His great power and mighty strength, not one of them is missing.

23:40:27.text: Why do you say, O Jacob, and why do you assert, O Israel, “My way is hidden from the Lord, and my claim is ignored by my God”?

23:40:28.text: Do you not know? Have you not heard? The Lord is the everlasting God, the Creator of the ends of the earth. He will not grow tired or weary; His understanding is beyond searching out.

23:40:29.text: He gives power to the faint and increases the strength of the weak.

23:40:3.text: A voice of one calling: “Prepare the way for the Lord in the wilderness; make a straight highway for our God in the desert.

23:40:30.text: Even youths grow tired and weary, and young men stumble and fall.

23:40:31.text: But those who wait upon the Lord will renew their strength; they will mount up with wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary, they will walk and not faint.

23:40:4.text: Every valley shall be lifted up, and every mountain and hill made low; the uneven ground will become smooth, and the rugged land a plain.

23:40:5.text: And the glory of the Lord will be revealed, and all humanity together will see it. For the mouth of the Lord has spoken.”

23:40:6.text: A voice says, “Cry out!” And I asked, “What should I cry out?” “All flesh is like grass, and all its glory like the flowers of the field.

23:40:7.text: The grass withers and the flowers fall when the breath of the Lord blows on them; indeed, the people are grass.

23:40:8.text: The grass withers and the flowers fall, but the word of our God stands forever.”

23:40:9.text: Go up on a high mountain, O Zion, herald of good news. Raise your voice loudly, O Jerusalem, herald of good news. Lift it up, do not be afraid! Say to the cities of Judah, “Here is your God!”

23:41:1.text: “Be silent before Me, O islands, and let the peoples renew their strength. Let them come forward and testify; let us together draw near for judgment.

23:41:10.text: Do not fear, for I am with you; do not be afraid, for I am your God. I will strengthen you; I will surely help you; I will uphold you with My right hand of righteousness.

23:41:11.text: Behold, all who rage against you will be ashamed and disgraced; those who contend with you will be reduced to nothing and will perish.

23:41:12.text: You will seek them but will not find them. Those who wage war against you will come to nothing.

23:41:13.text: For I am the Lord your God, who takes hold of your right hand and tells you: Do not fear, I will help you.

23:41:14.text: Do not fear, O worm of Jacob, O few men of Israel. I will help you,” declares the Lord. “Your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel.

23:41:15.text: Behold, I will make you into a threshing sledge, new and sharp, with many teeth. You will thresh the mountains and crush them, and reduce the hills to chaff.

23:41:16.text: You will winnow them, and a wind will carry them away; a gale will scatter them. But you will rejoice in the Lord ; you will glory in the Holy One of Israel.

23:41:17.text: The poor and needy seek water, but there is none; their tongues are parched with thirst. I, the Lord, will answer them; I, the God of Israel, will not forsake them.

23:41:18.text: I will open rivers on the barren heights, and fountains in the middle of the valleys. I will turn the desert into a pool of water, and the dry land into flowing springs.

23:41:19.text: I will plant cedars in the wilderness, acacias, myrtles, and olive trees. I will set cypresses in the desert, elms and boxwood together,

23:41:2.text: Who has aroused one from the east and called him to his feet in righteousness? He hands nations over to him and subdues kings before him. He turns them to dust with his sword, to windblown chaff with his bow.

23:41:20.text: so that all may see and know, may consider and understand, that the hand of the Lord has done this and the Holy One of Israel has created it.”

23:41:21.text: “Present your case,” says the Lord. “Submit your arguments,” says the King of Jacob.

23:41:22.text: “Let them come and tell us what will happen. Tell the former things, so that we may reflect on them and know the outcome. Or announce to us what is coming.

23:41:23.text: Tell us the things that are to come, so that we may know that you are gods. Yes, do something good or evil, that we may look on together in dismay.

23:41:24.text: Behold, you are nothing and your work is of no value. Anyone who chooses you is detestable.

23:41:25.text: I have raised up one from the north, and he has come — one from the east who calls on My name. He will march over rulers as if they were mortar, like a potter who treads the clay.

23:41:26.text: Who has declared this from the beginning, so that we may know, and from times past, so that we may say: ‘He was right’ ? No one announced it, no one foretold it, no one heard your words.

23:41:27.text: I was the first to tell Zion: ‘Look, here they are!’ And I gave to Jerusalem a herald of good news.

23:41:28.text: When I look, there is no one; there is no counselor among them; when I ask them, they have nothing to say.

23:41:29.text: See, they are all a delusion; their works amount to nothing; their images are as empty as the wind.

23:41:3.text: He pursues them, going on safely, hardly touching the path with his feet.

23:41:4.text: Who has performed this and carried it out, calling forth the generations from the beginning? I, the Lord — the first and the last — I am He.”

23:41:5.text: The islands see and fear; the ends of the earth tremble. They approach and come forward.

23:41:6.text: Each one helps the other and says to his brother, “Be strong!”

23:41:7.text: The craftsman encourages the goldsmith, and he who wields the hammer cheers him who strikes the anvil, saying of the welding, “It is good.” He nails it down so it will not be toppled.

23:41:8.text: “But you, O Israel, My servant, Jacob, whom I have chosen, descendant of Abraham My friend —

23:41:9.text: I brought you from the ends of the earth and called you from its farthest corners. I said, ‘You are My servant.’ I have chosen and not rejected you.

23:42:1.text: “Here is My Servant, whom I uphold, My Chosen One, in whom My soul delights. I will put My Spirit on Him, and He will bring justice to the nations.

23:42:10.text: Sing to the Lord a new song — His praise from the ends of the earth — you who go down to the sea, and all that is in it, you islands, and all who dwell in them.

23:42:11.text: Let the desert and its cities raise their voices; let the villages of Kedar cry aloud. Let the people of Sela sing for joy; let them cry out from the mountaintops.

23:42:12.text: Let them give glory to the Lord and declare His praise in the islands.

23:42:13.text: The Lord goes forth like a mighty one; He stirs up His zeal like a warrior. He shouts; yes, He roars in triumph over His enemies:

23:42:14.text: “I have kept silent from ages past; I have remained quiet and restrained. But now I will groan like a woman in labor; I will at once gasp and pant.

23:42:15.text: I will lay waste the mountains and hills and dry up all their vegetation. I will turn the rivers into dry land and drain the marshes.

23:42:16.text: I will lead the blind by a way they did not know; I will guide them on unfamiliar paths. I will turn darkness into light before them and rough places into level ground. These things I will do for them, and I will not forsake them.

23:42:17.text: But those who trust in idols and say to molten images, ‘You are our gods!’ will be turned back in utter shame.

23:42:18.text: Listen, you deaf ones; look, you blind ones, that you may see!

23:42:19.text: Who is blind but My servant, or deaf like the messenger I am sending? Who is blind like My covenant partner, or blind like the servant of the Lord?

23:42:2.text: He will not cry out or raise His voice, nor make His voice heard in the streets.

23:42:20.text: Though seeing many things, you do not keep watch. Though your ears are open, you do not hear.”

23:42:21.text: The Lord was pleased, for the sake of His righteousness, to magnify His law and make it glorious.

23:42:22.text: But this is a people plundered and looted, all trapped in caves or imprisoned in dungeons. They have become plunder with no one to rescue them, and loot with no one to say, “Send them back!”

23:42:23.text: Who among you will pay attention to this? Who will listen and obey hereafter?

23:42:24.text: Who gave Jacob up for spoil, and Israel to the plunderers? Was it not the Lord, against whom we have sinned? They were unwilling to walk in His ways, and they would not obey His law.

23:42:25.text: So He poured out on them His furious anger and the fierceness of battle. It enveloped them in flames, but they did not understand; it consumed them, but they did not take it to heart.

23:42:3.text: A bruised reed He will not break and a smoldering wick He will not extinguish; He will faithfully bring forth justice.

23:42:4.text: He will not grow weak or discouraged before He has established justice on the earth. In His law the islands will put their hope.”

23:42:5.text: This is what God the Lord says — He who created the heavens and stretched them out, who spread out the earth and its offspring, who gives breath to the people on it and life to those who walk in it:

23:42:6.text: “I, the Lord, have called you for a righteous purpose, and I will take hold of your hand. I will keep you and appoint you to be a covenant for the people and a light to the nations,

23:42:7.text: to open the eyes of the blind, to bring prisoners out of the dungeon and those sitting in darkness out from the prison house.

23:42:8.text: I am the Lord ; that is My name! I will not yield My glory to another or My praise to idols.

23:42:9.text: Behold, the former things have happened, and now I declare new things. Before they spring forth I proclaim them to you.”

23:45:1.text: This is what the Lord says to Cyrus His anointed, whose right hand I have grasped to subdue nations before him, to disarm kings, to open the doors before him, so that the gates will not be shut:

23:45:10.text: Woe to him who says to his father, ‘What have you begotten?’ or to his mother, ‘What have you brought forth?’ ”

23:45:11.text: Thus says the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, and its Maker: “How dare you question Me about My sons, or instruct Me in the work of My hands?

23:45:12.text: It is I who made the earth and created man upon it. It was My hands that stretched out the heavens, and I ordained all their host.

23:45:13.text: I will raise up Cyrus in righteousness, and I will make all his ways straight. He will rebuild My city and set My exiles free, but not for payment or reward, says the Lord of Hosts.”

23:45:14.text: This is what the Lord says: “The products of Egypt and the merchandise of Cush, along with the Sabeans, men of stature, will come over to you and will be yours; they will trudge behind you; they will come over in chains and bow down to you. They will confess to you: ‘God is indeed with you, and there is no other; there is no other God.’ ”

23:45:15.text: Truly You are a God who hides Himself, O God of Israel, the Savior.

23:45:16.text: They will all be put to shame and humiliated; the makers of idols will depart together in disgrace.

23:45:17.text: But Israel will be saved by the Lord with an everlasting salvation; you will not be put to shame or humiliated, to ages everlasting.

23:45:18.text: For thus says the Lord, who created the heavens — He is God; He formed the earth and fashioned it; He established it; He did not create it to be empty, but formed it to be inhabited: “I am the Lord, and there is no other.

23:45:19.text: I have not spoken in secret, from a place in a land of darkness. I did not say to the descendants of Jacob, ‘Seek Me in a wasteland.’ I, the Lord, speak the truth; I say what is right.

23:45:2.text: “I will go before you and level the mountains; I will break down the gates of bronze and cut through the bars of iron.

23:45:20.text: Come, gather together, and draw near, you fugitives from the nations. Ignorant are those who carry idols of wood and pray to a god that cannot save.

23:45:21.text: Speak up and present your case — yes, let them take counsel together. Who foretold this long ago? Who announced it from ancient times? Was it not I, the Lord? There is no other God but Me, a righteous God and Savior; there is none but Me.

23:45:22.text: Turn to Me and be saved, all the ends of the earth; for I am God, and there is no other.

23:45:23.text: By Myself I have sworn; truth has gone out from My mouth, a word that will not be revoked: Every knee will bow before Me, every tongue will swear allegiance.

23:45:24.text: Surely they will say of Me, ‘In the Lord alone are righteousness and strength.’ ” All who rage against Him will come to Him and be put to shame.

23:45:25.text: In the Lord all descendants of Israel will be justified and will exult.

23:45:3.text: I will give you the treasures of darkness and the riches hidden in secret places, so that you may know that I am the Lord, the God of Israel, who calls you by name.

23:45:4.text: For the sake of Jacob My servant and Israel My chosen one, I call you by name; I have given you a title of honor, though you have not known Me.

23:45:5.text: I am the Lord, and there is no other; there is no God but Me. I will equip you for battle, though you have not known Me,

23:45:6.text: so that all may know, from where the sun rises to where it sets, that there is none but Me; I am the Lord, and there is no other.

23:45:7.text: I form the light and create the darkness; I bring prosperity and create calamity. I, the Lord, do all these things.

23:45:8.text: Drip down, O heavens, from above, and let the skies pour down righteousness. Let the earth open up that salvation may sprout and righteousness spring up with it; I, the Lord, have created it.

23:45:9.text: Woe to him who quarrels with his Maker — one clay pot among many. Does the clay ask the potter, ‘What are you making?’ Does your work say, ‘He has no hands’ ?

23:48:1.text: “Listen to this, O house of Jacob, you who are called by the name of Israel, who have descended from the line of Judah, who swear by the name of the Lord, who invoke the God of Israel — but not in truth or righteousness —

23:48:10.text: See, I have refined you, but not as silver; I have tested you in the furnace of affliction.

23:48:11.text: For My own sake, My very own sake, I will act; for how can I let Myself be defamed? I will not yield My glory to another.

23:48:12.text: Listen to Me, O Jacob, and Israel, whom I have called: I am He; I am the first, and I am the last.

23:48:13.text: Surely My own hand founded the earth, and My right hand spread out the heavens; when I summon them, they stand up together.

23:48:14.text: Come together, all of you, and listen: Which of the idols has foretold these things? The Lord’s chosen ally will carry out His desire against Babylon, and His arm will be against the Chaldeans.

23:48:15.text: I, even I, have spoken; yes, I have called him. I have brought him, and he will succeed in his mission.

23:48:16.text: Come near to Me and listen to this: From the beginning I have not spoken in secret; from the time it happened, I was there.” And now the Lord GOD has sent me, accompanied by His Spirit.

23:48:17.text: Thus says the Lord your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: “I am the Lord your God, who teaches you for your benefit, who directs you in the way you should go.

23:48:18.text: If only you had paid attention to My commandments, your peace would have been like a river, and your righteousness like waves of the sea.

23:48:19.text: Your descendants would have been as countless as the sand, and your offspring as numerous as its grains; their name would never be cut off or eliminated from My presence.”

23:48:2.text: who indeed call yourselves after the holy city and lean on the God of Israel; the Lord of Hosts is His name.

23:48:20.text: Leave Babylon! Flee from the Chaldeans! Declare it with a shout of joy, proclaim it, let it go out to the ends of the earth, saying, “The Lord has redeemed His servant Jacob!”

23:48:21.text: They did not thirst when He led them through the deserts; He made water flow for them from the rock; He split the rock, and water gushed out.

23:48:22.text: “There is no peace,” says the Lord, “for the wicked.”

23:48:3.text: I foretold the former things long ago; they came out of My mouth and I proclaimed them. Suddenly I acted, and they came to pass.

23:48:4.text: For I knew that you are stubborn; your neck is iron and your forehead is bronze.

23:48:5.text: Therefore I declared it to you long ago; I announced it before it came to pass, so that you could not claim, ‘My idol has done this; my carved image and molten god has ordained it.’

23:48:6.text: You have heard these things; look at them all. Will you not acknowledge them? From now on I will tell you of new things, hidden things unknown to you.

23:48:7.text: They are created now, and not long ago; you have not heard of them before today. So you cannot claim, ‘I already knew them!’

23:48:8.text: You have never heard; you have never understood; for a long time your ears have not been open. For I knew how deceitful you are; you have been called a rebel from birth.

23:48:9.text: For the sake of My name I will delay My wrath; for the sake of My praise I will restrain it, so that you will not be cut off.

23:49:1.text: Listen to Me, O islands; pay attention, O distant peoples: The Lord called Me from the womb; from the body of My mother He named Me.

23:49:10.text: They will not hunger or thirst, nor will scorching heat or sun beat down on them. For He who has compassion on them will guide them and lead them beside springs of water.

23:49:11.text: I will turn all My mountains into roads, and My highways will be raised up.

23:49:12.text: Behold, they will come from far away, from the north and from the west, and from the land of Aswan. ”

23:49:13.text: Shout for joy, O heavens; rejoice, O earth; break forth in song, O mountains! For the Lord has comforted His people, and He will have compassion on His afflicted ones.

23:49:14.text: But Zion said, “The Lord has forsaken me; the Lord has forgotten me!”

23:49:15.text: “Can a woman forget her nursing child, or lack compassion for the son of her womb? Even if she could forget, I will not forget you!

23:49:16.text: Behold, I have inscribed you on the palms of My hands; your walls are ever before Me.

23:49:17.text: Your builders hasten back; your destroyers and wreckers depart from you.

23:49:18.text: Lift up your eyes and look around. They all gather together; they come to you. As surely as I live,” declares the Lord, “you will wear them all as jewelry and put them on like a bride.

23:49:19.text: For your ruined and desolate places and your ravaged land will now indeed be too small for your people, and those who devoured you will be far away.

23:49:2.text: He made My mouth like a sharp sword; He hid Me in the shadow of His hand. He made Me like a polished arrow; He hid Me in His quiver.

23:49:20.text: Yet the children of your bereavement will say in your hearing, ‘This place is too small for us; make room for us to live here.’

23:49:21.text: Then you will say in your heart, ‘Who has begotten these for me? I was bereaved and barren; I was exiled and rejected. So who has reared them? Look, I was left all alone, so where did they come from?’ ”

23:49:22.text: This is what the Lord GOD says: “Behold, I will lift up My hand to the nations, and raise My banner to the peoples. They will bring your sons in their arms and carry your daughters on their shoulders.

23:49:23.text: Kings will be your foster fathers, and their queens your nursing mothers. They will bow to you facedown and lick the dust at your feet. Then you will know that I am the Lord ; those who hope in Me will never be put to shame.”

23:49:24.text: Can the plunder be snatched from the mighty, or the captives of a tyrant be delivered?

23:49:25.text: Indeed, this is what the Lord says: “Even the captives of the mighty will be taken away, and the plunder of the tyrant will be retrieved; I will contend with those who contend with you, and I will save your children.

23:49:26.text: I will make your oppressors eat their own flesh; they will be drunk on their own blood, as with wine. Then all mankind will know that I, the Lord, am your Savior and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.”

23:49:3.text: He said to Me, “You are My Servant, Israel, in whom I will display My glory.”

23:49:4.text: But I said, “I have labored in vain, I have spent My strength in futility and vanity; yet My vindication is with the Lord, and My reward is with My God.”

23:49:5.text: And now says the Lord, who formed Me from the womb to be His Servant, to bring Jacob back to Him, that Israel might be gathered to Him — for I am honored in the sight of the Lord, and My God is My strength —

23:49:6.text: He says: “It is not enough for You to be My Servant, to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the protected ones of Israel. I will also make You a light for the nations, to bring My salvation to the ends of the earth.”

23:49:7.text: Thus says the Lord, the Redeemer and Holy One of Israel, to Him who was despised and abhorred by the nation, to the Servant of rulers: “Kings will see You and rise, and princes will bow down, because of the Lord, who is faithful, the Holy One of Israel, who has chosen You.”

23:49:8.text: This is what the Lord says: “In the time of favor I will answer You, and in the day of salvation I will help You; I will keep You and appoint You to be a covenant for the people, to restore the land, to apportion its desolate inheritances,

23:49:9.text: to say to the prisoners, ‘Come out,’ and to those in darkness, ‘Show yourselves.’ They will feed along the pathways, and find pasture on every barren hill.

23:4:1.text: In that day seven women will take hold of one man and say, “We will eat our own bread and provide our own clothes. Just let us be called by your name. Take away our disgrace!”

23:4:2.text: On that day the Branch of the Lord will be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the land will be the pride and glory of Israel’s survivors.

23:4:3.text: Whoever remains in Zion and whoever is left in Jerusalem will be called holy — all in Jerusalem who are recorded among the living —

23:4:4.text: when the Lord has washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion and cleansed the bloodstains from the heart of Jerusalem by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of fire.

23:4:5.text: Then the Lord will create over all of Mount Zion and over her assemblies a cloud of smoke by day and a glowing flame of fire by night. For over all the glory there will be a canopy,

23:4:6.text: a shelter to give shade from the heat by day, and a refuge and hiding place from the storm and the rain.

23:58:1.text: “Cry aloud, do not hold back! Raise your voice like a ram’s horn. Declare to My people their transgression and to the house of Jacob their sins.

23:58:10.text: and if you give yourself to the hungry and satisfy the afflicted soul, then your light will go forth in the darkness, and your night will be like noonday.

23:58:11.text: The Lord will always guide you; He will satisfy you in a sun-scorched land and strengthen your frame. You will be like a well-watered garden, like a spring whose waters never fail.

23:58:12.text: Your people will rebuild the ancient ruins; you will restore the age-old foundations; you will be called Repairer of the Breach, Restorer of the Streets of Dwelling.

23:58:13.text: If you turn your foot from breaking the Sabbath, from doing as you please on My holy day, if you call the Sabbath a delight, and the Lord’s holy day honorable, if you honor it by not going your own way or seeking your own pleasure or speaking idle words,

23:58:14.text: then you will delight yourself in the Lord, and I will make you ride on the heights of the land and feed you with the heritage of your father Jacob.” For the mouth of the Lord has spoken.

23:58:2.text: For day after day they seek Me and delight to know My ways, like a nation that does what is right and does not forsake the justice of their God. They ask Me for righteous judgments; they delight in the nearness of God.”

23:58:3.text: “Why have we fasted, and You have not seen? Why have we humbled ourselves, and You have not noticed?” “Behold, on the day of your fast, you do as you please, and you oppress all your workers.

23:58:4.text: You fast with contention and strife to strike viciously with your fist. You cannot fast as you do today and have your voice be heard on high.

23:58:5.text: Is this the fast I have chosen: a day for a man to deny himself, to bow his head like a reed, and to spread out sackcloth and ashes? Will you call this a fast and a day acceptable to the Lord?

23:58:6.text: Isn’t this the fast that I have chosen: to break the chains of wickedness, to untie the cords of the yoke, to set the oppressed free and tear off every yoke?

23:58:7.text: Isn’t it to share your bread with the hungry, to bring the poor and homeless into your home, to clothe the naked when you see him, and not to turn away from your own flesh and blood?

23:58:8.text: Then your light will break forth like the dawn, and your healing will come quickly. Your righteousness will go before you, and the glory of the Lord will be your rear guard.

23:58:9.text: Then you will call, and the Lord will answer; you will cry out, and He will say, ‘Here I am.’ If you remove the yoke from your midst, the pointing of the finger and malicious talk,

23:5:1.text: I will sing for my beloved a song of his vineyard: My beloved had a vineyard on a very fertile hill.

23:5:10.text: For ten acres of vineyard will yield but a bath of wine, and a homer of seed only an ephah of grain. ”

23:5:11.text: Woe to those who rise early in the morning in pursuit of strong drink, who linger into the evening, to be inflamed by wine.

23:5:12.text: At their feasts are the lyre and harp, tambourines and flutes and wine. They disregard the actions of the Lord and fail to see the work of His hands.

23:5:13.text: Therefore My people will go into exile for their lack of understanding; their dignitaries are starving and their masses are parched with thirst.

23:5:14.text: Therefore Sheol enlarges its throat and opens wide its enormous jaws, and down go Zion’s nobles and masses, her revelers and carousers!

23:5:15.text: So mankind will be brought low, and each man humbled; the arrogant will lower their eyes.

23:5:16.text: But the Lord of Hosts will be exalted by His justice, and the holy God will show Himself holy in righteousness.

23:5:17.text: Lambs will graze as in their own pastures, and strangers will feed in the ruins of the wealthy.

23:5:18.text: Woe to those who draw iniquity with cords of deceit and pull sin along with cart ropes,

23:5:19.text: to those who say, “Let Him hurry and hasten His work so that we may see it! Let the plan of the Holy One of Israel come so that we may know it!”

23:5:2.text: He dug it up and cleared the stones and planted the finest vines. He built a watchtower in the middle and dug out a winepress as well. He waited for the vineyard to yield good grapes, but the fruit it produced was sour!

23:5:20.text: Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who turn darkness to light and light to darkness, who replace bitter with sweet and sweet with bitter.

23:5:21.text: Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes and clever in their own sight.

23:5:22.text: Woe to those who are heroes in drinking wine and champions in mixing beer,

23:5:23.text: who acquit the guilty for a bribe and deprive the innocent of justice.

23:5:24.text: Therefore, as a tongue of fire consumes the straw, and as dry grass shrivels in the flame, so their roots will decay and their blossoms will blow away like dust; for they have rejected the instruction of the Lord of Hosts and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.

23:5:25.text: Therefore the anger of the Lord burns against His people; His hand is raised against them to strike them down. The mountains quake, and the corpses lay like refuse in the streets. Despite all this, His anger is not turned away; His hand is still upraised.

23:5:26.text: He lifts a banner for the distant nations and whistles for those at the ends of the earth. Behold — how speedily and swiftly they come!

23:5:27.text: None of them grows weary or stumbles; no one slumbers or sleeps. No belt is loose and no sandal strap is broken.

23:5:28.text: Their arrows are sharpened, and all their bows are strung. The hooves of their horses are like flint; their chariot wheels are like a whirlwind.

23:5:29.text: Their roaring is like that of a lion; they roar like young lions. They growl and seize their prey; they carry it away from deliverance.

23:5:3.text: “And now, O dwellers of Jerusalem and men of Judah, I exhort you to judge between Me and My vineyard.

23:5:30.text: In that day they will roar over it, like the roaring of the sea. If one looks over the land, he will see darkness and distress; even the light will be obscured by clouds.

23:5:4.text: What more could I have done for My vineyard than I already did for it? Why, when I expected sweet grapes, did it bring forth sour fruit?

23:5:5.text: Now I will tell you what I am about to do to My vineyard: I will take away its hedge, and it will be consumed; I will tear down its wall, and it will be trampled.

23:5:6.text: I will make it a wasteland, neither pruned nor cultivated, and thorns and briers will grow up. I will command the clouds that rain shall not fall on it.”

23:5:7.text: For the vineyard of the Lord of Hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah are the plant of His delight. He looked for justice, but saw bloodshed; for righteousness, but heard a cry of distress.

23:5:8.text: Woe to you who add house to house and join field to field until no place is left and you live alone in the land.

23:5:9.text: I heard the Lord of Hosts declare: “Surely many houses will become desolate, great mansions left unoccupied.

23:65:1.text: “I revealed Myself to those who did not ask for Me; I was found by those who did not seek Me. To a nation that did not call My name, I said, ‘Here I am! Here I am!’

23:65:10.text: Sharon will become a pasture for flocks, and the Valley of Achor a resting place for herds, for My people who seek Me.

23:65:11.text: But you who forsake the Lord, who forget My holy mountain, who set a table for Fortune and fill bowls of mixed wine for Destiny,

23:65:12.text: I will destine you for the sword, and you will all kneel down to be slaughtered, because I called and you did not answer, I spoke and you did not listen; you did evil in My sight and chose that in which I did not delight.”

23:65:13.text: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: “My servants will eat, but you will go hungry; My servants will drink, but you will go thirsty; My servants will rejoice, but you will be put to shame.

23:65:14.text: My servants will shout for joy with a glad heart, but you will cry out with a heavy heart and wail with a broken spirit.

23:65:15.text: You will leave behind your name as a curse for My chosen ones, and the Lord GOD will slay you; but to His servants He will give another name.

23:65:16.text: Whoever invokes a blessing in the land will do so by the God of truth, and whoever takes an oath in the land will swear by the God of truth. For the former troubles will be forgotten and hidden from My sight.

23:65:17.text: For behold, I will create new heavens and a new earth. The former things will not be remembered, nor will they come to mind.

23:65:18.text: But be glad and rejoice forever in what I create; for I will create Jerusalem to be a joy and its people to be a delight.

23:65:19.text: I will rejoice in Jerusalem and take delight in My people. The sounds of weeping and crying will no longer be heard in her.

23:65:2.text: All day long I have held out My hands to an obstinate people who walk in the wrong path, who follow their own imaginations,

23:65:20.text: No longer will a nursing infant live but a few days, or an old man fail to live out his years. For the youth will die at a hundred years, and he who fails to reach a hundred will be considered accursed.

23:65:21.text: They will build houses and dwell in them; they will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.

23:65:22.text: No longer will they build houses for others to inhabit, nor plant for others to eat. For as is the lifetime of a tree, so will be the days of My people, and My chosen ones will fully enjoy the work of their hands.

23:65:23.text: They will not labor in vain or bear children doomed to disaster; for they will be a people blessed by the Lord — they and their descendants with them.

23:65:24.text: Even before they call, I will answer, and while they are still speaking, I will hear.

23:65:25.text: The wolf and the lamb will feed together, and the lion will eat straw like the ox, but the food of the serpent will be dust. They will neither harm nor destroy on all My holy mountain,” says the Lord.

23:65:3.text: to a people who continually provoke Me to My face, sacrificing in the gardens and burning incense on altars of brick,

23:65:4.text: sitting among the graves, spending nights in secret places, eating the meat of pigs and polluted broth from their bowls.

23:65:5.text: They say, ‘Keep to yourself; do not come near me, for I am holier than you!’ Such people are smoke in My nostrils, a fire that burns all day long.

23:65:6.text: Behold, it is written before Me: I will not keep silent, but I will repay; I will pay it back into their laps,

23:65:7.text: both for your iniquities and for those of your fathers,” says the Lord. “Because they burned incense on the mountains and scorned Me on the hills, I will measure into their laps full payment for their former deeds.”

23:65:8.text: This is what the Lord says: “As the new wine is found in a cluster of grapes, and men say, ‘Do not destroy it, for it contains a blessing,’so I will act on behalf of My servants; I will not destroy them all.

23:65:9.text: And I will bring forth descendants from Jacob, and heirs from Judah; My elect will possess My mountains, and My servants will dwell there.

23:66:1.text: This is what the Lord says: “Heaven is My throne, and earth is My footstool. What kind of house will you build for Me? Or where will My place of repose be?

23:66:10.text: Be glad for Jerusalem and rejoice over her, all who love her. Rejoice greatly with her, all who mourn over her,

23:66:11.text: so that you may nurse and be satisfied at her comforting breasts; you may drink deeply and delight yourselves in her glorious abundance.

23:66:12.text: For this is what the Lord says: “I will extend peace to her like a river, and the wealth of nations like a flowing stream; you will nurse and be carried on her arm, and bounced upon her knees.

23:66:13.text: As a mother comforts her son, so will I comfort you, and you will be consoled over Jerusalem.”

23:66:14.text: When you see, you will rejoice, and you will flourish like grass; then the hand of the Lord will be revealed to His servants, but His wrath will be shown to His enemies.

23:66:15.text: For behold, the Lord will come with fire — His chariots are like a whirlwind — to execute His anger with fury and His rebuke with flames of fire.

23:66:16.text: For by fire and by His sword, the Lord will execute judgment on all flesh, and many will be slain by the Lord.

23:66:17.text: “Those who consecrate and purify themselves to enter the groves — to follow one in the center of those who eat the flesh of swine and vermin and rats — will perish together,” declares the Lord.

23:66:18.text: “And I, knowing their deeds and thoughts, am coming to gather all nations and tongues, and they will come and see My glory.

23:66:19.text: I will establish a sign among them, and I will send survivors from among them to the nations — to Tarshish, Put, and the archers of Lud; to Tubal, Javan, and the islands far away who have not heard of My fame or seen My glory. So they will proclaim My glory among the nations.

23:66:2.text: Has not My hand made all these things? And so they came into being,” declares the Lord. “This is the one I will esteem: he who is humble and contrite in spirit, who trembles at My word.
