23:66:20.text: And they will bring all your brothers from all the nations as a gift to the Lord on horses and chariots and wagons, on mules and camels, to My holy mountain Jerusalem,” says the Lord, “just as the Israelites bring an offering in a clean vessel to the house of the Lord.”

23:66:21.text: “And I will select some of them as priests and Levites,” says the Lord.

23:66:22.text: “For just as the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, will endure before Me,” declares the Lord, “so your descendants and your name will endure.

23:66:23.text: From one New Moon to another and from one Sabbath to another, all mankind will come to worship before Me,” says the Lord.

23:66:24.text: “As they go forth, they will see the corpses of the men who have rebelled against Me; for their worm will never die, their fire will never be quenched, and they will be a horror to all mankind.”

23:66:3.text: Whoever slaughters an ox is like one who slays a man; whoever sacrifices a lamb is like one who breaks a dog’s neck; whoever presents a grain offering is like one who offers pig’s blood; whoever offers frankincense is like one who blesses an idol. Indeed, they have chosen their own ways and delighted in their abominations.

23:66:4.text: So I will choose their punishment and I will bring terror upon them, because I called and no one answered, I spoke and no one listened. But they did evil in My sight and chose that in which I did not delight.”

23:66:5.text: You who tremble at His word, hear the word of the Lord : “Your brothers who hate you and exclude you because of My name have said, ‘Let the Lord be glorified that we may see your joy!’ But they will be put to shame.”

23:66:6.text: Hear the uproar from the city; listen to the voice from the temple! It is the voice of the Lord, repaying His enemies what they deserve!

23:66:7.text: “Before she was in labor, she gave birth; before she was in pain, she delivered a boy.

23:66:8.text: Who has heard of such as this? Who has seen such things? Can a country be born in a day or a nation be delivered in an instant? Yet as soon as Zion was in labor, she gave birth to her children.

23:66:9.text: Shall I bring a baby to the point of birth and not deliver it?” says the Lord. “Or will I who deliver close the womb?” says your God.

23:6:1.text: In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord seated on a throne, high and exalted; and the train of His robe filled the temple.

23:6:10.text: Make the hearts of this people calloused; deafen their ears and close their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn and be healed. ”

23:6:11.text: Then I asked: “How long, O Lord?” And He replied: “Until the cities lie ruined and without inhabitant, until the houses are left unoccupied and the land is desolate and ravaged,

23:6:12.text: until the Lord has driven men far away and the land is utterly forsaken.

23:6:13.text: And though a tenth remains in the land, it will be burned again. As the terebinth and oak leave stumps when felled, so the holy seed will be a stump in the land.”

23:6:2.text: Above Him stood seraphim, each having six wings: With two wings they covered their faces, with two they covered their feet, and with two they were flying.

23:6:3.text: And they were calling out to one another: “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Hosts; all the earth is full of His glory.”

23:6:4.text: At the sound of their voices the doorposts and thresholds shook, and the temple was filled with smoke.

23:6:5.text: Then I said: “Woe is me, for I am ruined, because I am a man of unclean lips dwelling among a people of unclean lips; for my eyes have seen the King, the Lord of Hosts.”

23:6:6.text: Then one of the seraphim flew to me, and in his hand was a glowing coal that he had taken with tongs from the altar.

23:6:7.text: And with it he touched my mouth and said: “Now that this has touched your lips, your iniquity is removed and your sin is atoned for.”

23:6:8.text: Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying: “Whom shall I send? Who will go for Us?” And I said: “Here am I. Send me!”

23:6:9.text: And He replied: “Go and tell this people, ‘Be ever hearing, but never understanding; be ever seeing, but never perceiving.’

23:7:1.text: Now in the days that Ahaz son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, was king of Judah, Rezin king of Aram marched up to wage war against Jerusalem. He was accompanied by Pekah son of Remaliah the king of Israel, but he could not overpower the city.

23:7:10.text: Again the Lord spoke to Ahaz, saying,

23:7:11.text: “Ask for a sign from the Lord your God, whether from the depths of Sheol or the heights of heaven.”

23:7:12.text: But Ahaz replied, “I will not ask; I will not test the Lord.”

23:7:13.text: Then Isaiah said, “Hear now, O house of David! Is it not enough to try the patience of men? Will you try the patience of my God as well?

23:7:14.text: Therefore the Lord Himself will give you a sign: Behold, the virgin will be with child and will give birth to a son, and will call Him Immanuel.

23:7:15.text: By the time He knows enough to reject evil and choose good, He will be eating curds and honey.

23:7:16.text: For before the boy knows enough to reject evil and choose good, the land of the two kings you dread will be laid waste.

23:7:17.text: The Lord will bring on you and on your people and on the house of your father a time unlike any since the day Ephraim separated from Judah — He will bring the king of Assyria.”

23:7:18.text: On that day the Lord will whistle to the flies at the farthest streams of the Nile and to the bees in the land of Assyria.

23:7:19.text: And they will all come and settle in the steep ravines and clefts of the rocks, in all the thornbushes and watering holes.

23:7:2.text: When it was reported to the house of David that Aram was in league with Ephraim, the hearts of Ahaz and his people trembled like trees in the forest shaken by the wind.

23:7:20.text: On that day the Lord will use a razor hired from beyond the Euphrates — the king of Assyria — to shave your head and the hair of your legs, and to remove your beard as well.

23:7:21.text: On that day a man will raise a young cow and two sheep,

23:7:22.text: and from the abundance of milk they give, he will eat curds; for all who remain in the land will eat curds and honey.

23:7:23.text: And on that day, in every place that had a thousand vines worth a thousand shekels of silver, only briers and thorns will be found.

23:7:24.text: Men will go there with bow and arrow, for the land will be covered with briers and thorns.

23:7:25.text: For fear of the briers and thorns, you will no longer traverse the hills once tilled by the hoe; they will become places for oxen to graze and sheep to trample.

23:7:3.text: Then the Lord said to Isaiah, “Go out with your son Shear-jashub to meet Ahaz at the end of the aqueduct that feeds the upper pool, on the road to the Launderer’s Field,

23:7:4.text: and say to him: Calm down and be quiet. Do not be afraid or disheartened over these two smoldering stubs of firewood — over the fierce anger of Rezin and Aram and of the son of Remaliah.

23:7:5.text: For Aram, along with Ephraim and the son of Remaliah, has plotted your ruin, saying:

23:7:6.text: ‘Let us invade Judah, terrorize it, and divide it among ourselves. Then we can install the son of Tabeal over it as king.’

23:7:7.text: But this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘It will not arise; it will not happen.

23:7:8.text: For the head of Aram is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin. Within sixty-five years Ephraim will be shattered as a people.

23:7:9.text: The head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah. If you do not stand firm in your faith, then you will not stand at all.’ ”

23:8:1.text: Then the Lord said to me, “Take a large scroll and write on it with an ordinary stylus: Maher-shalal-hash-baz.

23:8:10.text: Devise a plan, but it will be thwarted; state a proposal, but it will not happen. For God is with us. ”

23:8:11.text: For this is what the Lord has spoken to me with a strong hand, instructing me not to walk in the way of this people:

23:8:12.text: “Do not call conspiracy everything these people regard as conspiracy. Do not fear what they fear; do not live in dread.

23:8:13.text: The Lord of Hosts is the One you shall regard as holy. Only He should be feared; only He should be dreaded.

23:8:14.text: And He will be a sanctuary — but to both houses of Israel a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense, to the dwellers of Jerusalem a trap and a snare.

23:8:15.text: Many will stumble over these; they will fall and be broken; they will be ensnared and captured.”

23:8:16.text: Bind up the testimony and seal the law among my disciples.

23:8:17.text: I will wait for the Lord, who is hiding His face from the house of Jacob. I will put my trust in Him.

23:8:18.text: Here am I, and the children the Lord has given me as signs and symbols in Israel from the Lord of Hosts, who dwells on Mount Zion.

23:8:19.text: When men tell you to consult the spirits of the dead and the spiritists who whisper and mutter, shouldn’t a people consult their God instead? Why consult the dead on behalf of the living?

23:8:2.text: And I will appoint for Myself trustworthy witnesses — Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Jeberekiah.”

23:8:20.text: To the law and to the testimony! If they do not speak according to this word, they have no light of dawn.

23:8:21.text: They will roam the land, dejected and hungry. When they are famished, they will become enraged; and looking upward, they will curse their king and their God.

23:8:22.text: Then they will look to the earth and see only distress and darkness and the gloom of anguish. And they will be driven into utter darkness.

23:8:3.text: And I had relations with the prophetess, and she conceived and gave birth to a son. The Lord said to me, “Name him Maher-shalal-hash-baz.

23:8:4.text: For before the boy knows how to cry ‘Father’ or ‘Mother,’ the wealth of Damascus and the plunder of Samaria will be carried off by the king of Assyria.”

23:8:5.text: And the Lord spoke to me further:

23:8:6.text: “Because this people has rejected the gently flowing waters of Shiloah and rejoiced in Rezin and the son of Remaliah,

23:8:7.text: the Lord will surely bring against them the mighty floodwaters of the Euphrates — the king of Assyria and all his pomp. It will overflow its channels and overrun its banks.

23:8:8.text: It will pour into Judah, swirling and sweeping over it, reaching up to the neck; its spreading streams will cover your entire land, O Immanuel!

23:8:9.text: Huddle together, O peoples, and be shattered; pay attention, all you distant lands; prepare for battle, and be shattered; prepare for battle, and be shattered!

23:9:1.text: Nevertheless, there will be no more gloom for those in distress. In the past He humbled the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, but in the future He will honor the Way of the Sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations:

23:9:10.text: “The bricks have fallen, but we will rebuild with finished stone; the sycamores have been felled, but we will replace them with cedars.”

23:9:11.text: The Lord has raised up the foes of Rezin against him and joined his enemies together.

23:9:12.text: Aram from the east and Philistia from the west have devoured Israel with open mouths. Despite all this, His anger is not turned away; His hand is still upraised.

23:9:13.text: But the people did not return to Him who struck them; they did not seek the Lord of Hosts.

23:9:14.text: So the Lord will cut off Israel’s head and tail, both palm branch and reed in a single day.

23:9:15.text: The head is the elder and honorable man, and the tail is the prophet who teaches lies.

23:9:16.text: For those who guide this people mislead them, and those they mislead are swallowed up.

23:9:17.text: Therefore the Lord takes no pleasure in their young men; He has no compassion on their fatherless and widows. For every one of them is godless and wicked, and every mouth speaks folly. Despite all this, His anger is not turned away; His hand is still upraised.

23:9:18.text: For wickedness burns like a fire that consumes the thorns and briers and kindles the forest thickets which roll upward in billows of smoke.

23:9:19.text: By the wrath of the Lord of Hosts the land is scorched, and the people are fuel for the fire. No man even spares his brother.

23:9:2.text: The people walking in darkness have seen a great light; on those living in the land of the shadow of death, a light has dawned.

23:9:20.text: They carve out what is on the right, but they are still hungry; they eat what is on the left, but they are still not satisfied. Each one devours the flesh of his own offspring.

23:9:21.text: Manasseh devours Ephraim, and Ephraim Manasseh; together they turn against Judah. Despite all this, His anger is not turned away; His hand is still upraised.

23:9:3.text: You have enlarged the nation and increased its joy. The people rejoice before You as they rejoice at harvest time, as men rejoice in dividing the plunder.

23:9:4.text: For as in the day of Midian You have shattered the yoke of their burden, the bar across their shoulders, and the rod of their oppressor.

23:9:5.text: For every trampling boot of battle and every garment rolled in blood will be burned as fuel for the fire.

23:9:6.text: For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given, and the government will be upon His shoulders. And He will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

23:9:7.text: Of the increase of His government and peace there will be no end. He will reign on the throne of David and over his kingdom, to establish and sustain it with justice and righteousness from that time and forevermore. The zeal of the Lord of Hosts will accomplish this.

23:9:8.text: The Lord has sent a message against Jacob, and it has fallen upon Israel.

23:9:9.text: All the people will know it — Ephraim and the dwellers of Samaria. With pride and arrogance of heart they will say:

29:2:1.text: Blow the ram’s horn in Zion; sound the alarm on My holy mountain! Let all who dwell in the land tremble, for the Day of the Lord is coming; indeed, it is near —

29:2:10.text: Before them the earth quakes; the heavens tremble. The sun and moon grow dark, and the stars lose their brightness.

29:2:11.text: The Lord raises His voice in the presence of His army. Indeed, His camp is very large, for mighty are those who obey His command. For the Day of the Lord is great and very dreadful. Who can endure it?

29:2:12.text: “Yet even now,” declares the Lord, “return to Me with all your heart, with fasting, weeping, and mourning.”

29:2:13.text: So rend your hearts and not your garments, and return to the Lord your God. For He is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion. And He relents from sending disaster.

29:2:14.text: Who knows? He may turn and relent and leave a blessing behind Him — grain and drink offerings for the Lord your God.

29:2:15.text: Blow the ram’s horn in Zion, consecrate a fast, proclaim a sacred assembly.

29:2:16.text: Gather the people, sanctify the congregation, assemble the aged, gather the children, even those nursing at the breast. Let the bridegroom leave his room, and the bride her chamber.

29:2:17.text: Let the priests who minister before the Lord weep between the portico and the altar, saying, “Spare Your people, O Lord, and do not make Your heritage a reproach, an object of scorn among the nations. Why should they say among the peoples, ‘Where is their God?’ ”

29:2:18.text: Then the Lord became jealous for His land, and He spared His people.

29:2:19.text: And the Lord answered His people: “Behold, I will send you grain, new wine, and oil, and by them you will be satisfied. I will never again make you a reproach among the nations.

29:2:2.text: a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and blackness. Like the dawn overspreading the mountains a great and strong army appears, such as never was of old, nor will ever be in ages to come.

29:2:20.text: The northern army I will drive away from you, banishing it to a barren and desolate land, its front ranks into the Eastern Sea, and its rear guard into the Western Sea. And its stench will rise; its foul odor will ascend. For He has done great things.

29:2:21.text: Do not be afraid, O land; rejoice and be glad, for the Lord has done great things.

29:2:22.text: Do not be afraid, O beasts of the field, for the open pastures have turned green, the trees bear their fruit, and the fig tree and vine yield their best.

29:2:23.text: Be glad, O children of Zion, and rejoice in the Lord your God, for He has given you the autumn rains for your vindication. He sends you showers, both autumn and spring rains, as before.

29:2:24.text: The threshing floors will be full of grain, and the vats will overflow with new wine and oil.

29:2:25.text: I will repay you for the years eaten by locusts — the swarming locust, the young locust, the destroying locust, and the devouring locust — My great army that I sent against you.

29:2:26.text: You will have plenty to eat, until you are satisfied. You will praise the name of the Lord your God, who has worked wonders for you. My people will never again be put to shame.

29:2:27.text: Then you will know that I am present in Israel and that I am the Lord your God, and there is no other. My people will never again be put to shame.

29:2:28.text: And afterward, I will pour out My Spirit on all people. Your sons and daughters will prophesy, your old men will dream dreams, your young men will see visions.

29:2:29.text: Even on My menservants and maidservants, I will pour out My Spirit in those days.

29:2:3.text: Before them a fire devours, and behind them a flame scorches. The land before them is like the Garden of Eden, but behind them, it is like a desert wasteland — surely nothing will escape them.

29:2:30.text: I will show wonders in the heavens and on the earth, blood and fire and columns of smoke.

29:2:31.text: The sun will be turned to darkness and the moon to blood before the coming of the great and awesome Day of the Lord.

29:2:32.text: And everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved; for on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be deliverance, as the Lord has promised, among the remnant called by the Lord.

29:2:4.text: Their appearance is like that of horses, and they gallop like swift steeds.

29:2:5.text: With a sound like that of chariots they bound over the mountaintops, like the crackling of fire consuming stubble, like a mighty army deployed for battle.

29:2:6.text: Nations writhe in horror before them; every face turns pale.

29:2:7.text: They charge like mighty men; they scale the walls like men of war. Each one marches in formation, not swerving from the course.

29:2:8.text: They do not jostle one another; each proceeds in his path. They burst through the defenses, never breaking ranks.

29:2:9.text: They storm the city; they run along the wall; they climb into houses, entering through windows like thieves.

29:3:1.text: “Yes, in those days and at that time, when I restore Judah and Jerusalem from captivity,

29:3:10.text: Beat your plowshares into swords and your pruning hooks into spears. Let the weak say, ‘I am strong!’

29:3:11.text: Come quickly, all you surrounding nations, and gather yourselves. Bring down Your mighty ones, O LORD.

29:3:12.text: Let the nations be roused and advance to the Valley of Jehoshaphat, for there I will sit down to judge all the nations on every side.

29:3:13.text: Swing the sickle, for the harvest is ripe. Come, trample the grapes, for the winepress is full; the wine vats overflow because their wickedness is great.

29:3:14.text: Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision! For the Day of the Lord is near in the valley of decision.

29:3:15.text: The sun and moon will grow dark, and the stars will no longer shine.

29:3:16.text: The Lord will roar from Zion and raise His voice from Jerusalem; heaven and earth will tremble. But the Lord will be a refuge for His people, a stronghold for the people of Israel.

29:3:17.text: Then you will know that I am the Lord your God, who dwells in Zion, My holy mountain. Jerusalem will be holy, never again to be overrun by foreigners.

29:3:18.text: And in that day the mountains will drip with sweet wine, and the hills will flow with milk. All the streams of Judah will run with water, and a spring will flow from the house of the Lord to water the Valley of Acacias.

29:3:19.text: Egypt will become desolate, and Edom a desert wasteland, because of the violence done to the people of Judah, in whose land they shed innocent blood.

29:3:2.text: I will gather all the nations and bring them down to the Valley of Jehoshaphat. There I will enter into judgment against them concerning My people, My inheritance, Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations as they divided up My land.

29:3:20.text: But Judah will be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.

29:3:21.text: For I will avenge their blood, which I have not yet avenged. ” For the Lord dwells in Zion.

29:3:3.text: They cast lots for My people; they bartered a boy for a prostitute and sold a girl for wine to drink.

29:3:4.text: Now what do you have against Me, O Tyre, Sidon, and all the regions of Philistia? Are you rendering against Me a recompense? If you retaliate against Me, I will swiftly and speedily return your recompense upon your heads.

29:3:5.text: For you took My silver and gold and carried off My finest treasures to your temples.

29:3:6.text: You sold the people of Judah and Jerusalem to the Greeks, to send them far from their homeland.

29:3:7.text: Behold, I will rouse them from the places to which you sold them; I will return your recompense upon your heads.

29:3:8.text: I will sell your sons and daughters into the hands of the people of Judah, and they will sell them to the Sabeans — to a distant nation.” Indeed, the Lord has spoken.

29:3:9.text: Proclaim this among the nations: “Prepare for war; rouse the mighty men; let all the men of war advance and attack!

38:8:1.text: Again the word of the Lord of Hosts came to me, saying:

38:8:10.text: For before those days neither man nor beast received wages, nor was there safety from the enemy for anyone who came or went, for I had turned every man against his neighbor.

38:8:11.text: But now I will not treat the remnant of this people as I did in the past,” declares the Lord of Hosts.

38:8:12.text: “For the seed will be prosperous, the vine will yield its fruit, the ground will yield its produce, and the skies will give their dew. To the remnant of this people I will give all these things as an inheritance.

38:8:13.text: As you have been a curse among the nations, O house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will save you, and you will be a blessing. Do not be afraid; let your hands be strong.”

38:8:14.text: For this is what the Lord of Hosts says: “Just as I resolved to bring disaster upon you when your fathers provoked Me to anger, and I did not relent,” says the Lord of Hosts,

38:8:15.text: “so now I have resolved to do good again to Jerusalem and Judah. Do not be afraid.

38:8:16.text: These are the things you must do: Speak truth to one another, render true and sound judgments in your gates,

38:8:17.text: do not plot evil in your hearts against your neighbor, and do not love to swear falsely, for I hate all these things,” declares the Lord.

38:8:18.text: Then the word of the Lord of Hosts came to me, saying,

38:8:19.text: “This is what the Lord of Hosts says: The fasts of the fourth, the fifth, the seventh, and the tenth months will become times of joy and gladness, cheerful feasts for the house of Judah. Therefore you are to love both truth and peace.”

38:8:2.text: This is what the Lord of Hosts says: “I am jealous for Zion with great zeal; I am jealous for her with great fervor.”

38:8:20.text: This is what the Lord of Hosts says: “Peoples will yet come — the residents of many cities —

38:8:21.text: and the residents of one city will go to another, saying: ‘Let us go at once to plead before the Lord and to seek the Lord of Hosts. I myself am going.’

38:8:22.text: And many peoples and strong nations will come to seek the Lord of Hosts in Jerusalem and to plead before the Lord.”

38:8:23.text: This is what the Lord of Hosts says: “In those days ten men from the nations of every tongue will tightly grasp the robe of a Jew, saying, ‘Let us go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.’ ”

38:8:3.text: This is what the Lord says: “I will return to Zion and dwell in Jerusalem. Then Jerusalem will be called the City of Truth, and the mountain of the Lord of Hosts will be called the Holy Mountain.”

38:8:4.text: This is what the Lord of Hosts says: “Old men and old women will again sit along the streets of Jerusalem, each with a staff in hand because of great age.

38:8:5.text: And the streets of the city will be filled with boys and girls playing there.”

38:8:6.text: This is what the Lord of Hosts says: “If this is impossible in the eyes of the remnant of this people in these days, should it also be impossible in My eyes?” declares the Lord of Hosts.

38:8:7.text: This is what the Lord of Hosts says: “I will save My people from the land of the east and from the land of the west.

38:8:8.text: I will bring them back to dwell in Jerusalem, where they will be My people, and I will be their faithful and righteous God.”

38:8:9.text: This is what the Lord of Hosts says: “Let your hands be strong, you who now hear these words spoken by the prophets who were present when the foundations were laid to rebuild the temple, the house of the Lord of Hosts.

40:10:1.text: And calling His twelve disciples to Him, Jesus gave them authority over unclean spirits, so that they could drive them out and heal every disease and sickness.

40:10:10.text: Take no bag for the road, or second tunic, or sandals, or staff; for the worker is worthy of his provisions.

40:10:11.text: Whatever town or village you enter, find out who is worthy there and stay at his house until you move on.

40:10:12.text: As you enter the home, greet its occupants.

40:10:13.text: If the home is worthy, let your peace rest on it; but if it is not, let your peace return to you.

40:10:14.text: And if anyone will not welcome you or heed your words, shake the dust off your feet when you leave that home or town.

40:10:15.text: Truly I tell you, it will be more bearable for Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that town.

40:10:16.text: Behold, I am sending you out like sheep among wolves; therefore be as shrewd as snakes and as innocent as doves.

40:10:17.text: But beware of men; for they will hand you over to their councils and flog you in their synagogues.

40:10:18.text: On My account, you will be brought before governors and kings as witnesses to them and to the Gentiles.

40:10:19.text: But when they hand you over, do not worry about how to respond or what to say. In that hour you will be given what to say.

40:10:2.text: These are the names of the twelve apostles: first Simon, called Peter, and his brother Andrew; James son of Zebedee, and his brother John;

40:10:20.text: For it will not be you speaking, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you.

40:10:21.text: Brother will betray brother to death, and a father his child; children will rise against their parents and have them put to death.

40:10:22.text: You will be hated by everyone because of My name, but the one who perseveres to the end will be saved.

40:10:23.text: When they persecute you in one town, flee to the next. Truly I tell you, you will not reach all the towns of Israel before the Son of Man comes.

40:10:24.text: A disciple is not above his teacher, nor a servant above his master.

40:10:25.text: It is enough for a disciple to be like his teacher, and a servant like his master. If the head of the house has been called Beelzebul, how much more the members of his household!

40:10:26.text: So do not be afraid of them. For there is nothing concealed that will not be disclosed, and nothing hidden that will not be made known.

40:10:27.text: What I tell you in the dark, speak in the daylight; what is whispered in your ear, proclaim from the housetops.

40:10:28.text: Do not be afraid of those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Instead, fear the One who can destroy both soul and body in hell.

40:10:29.text: Are not two sparrows sold for a penny? Yet not one of them will fall to the ground apart from the will of your Father.

40:10:3.text: Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax collector; James son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus;

40:10:30.text: And even the very hairs of your head are all numbered.

40:10:31.text: So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.

40:10:32.text: Therefore everyone who confesses Me before men, I will also confess him before My Father in heaven.

40:10:33.text: But whoever denies Me before men, I will also deny him before My Father in heaven.

40:10:34.text: Do not assume that I have come to bring peace to the earth; I have not come to bring peace, but a sword.

40:10:35.text: For I have come to turn‘ a man against his father, a daughter against her mother, a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.

40:10:36.text: A man’s enemies will be the members of his own household.’

40:10:37.text: Anyone who loves his father or mother more than Me is not worthy of Me; anyone who loves his son or daughter more than Me is not worthy of Me;

40:10:38.text: and anyone who does not take up his cross and follow Me is not worthy of Me.

40:10:39.text: Whoever finds his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life for My sake will find it.

40:10:4.text: Simon the Zealot, and Judas Iscariot, who betrayed Jesus.

40:10:40.text: He who receives you receives Me, and he who receives Me receives the One who sent Me.

40:10:41.text: Whoever receives a prophet because he is a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward, and whoever receives a righteous man because he is a righteous man will receive a righteous man’s reward.

40:10:42.text: And if anyone gives even a cup of cold water to one of these little ones because he is My disciple, truly I tell you, he will never lose his reward.”

40:10:5.text: These twelve Jesus sent out with the following instructions: “Do not go onto the road of the Gentiles or enter any town of the Samaritans.

40:10:6.text: Go rather to the lost sheep of Israel.

40:10:7.text: As you go, preach this message: ‘The kingdom of heaven is near.’

40:10:8.text: Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse the lepers, drive out demons. Freely you have received; freely give.

40:10:9.text: Do not carry any gold or silver or copper in your belts.

40:11:1.text: After Jesus had finished instructing His twelve disciples, He went on from there to teach and preach in their cities.

40:11:10.text: This is the one about whom it is written: ‘Behold, I will send My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way before You.’

40:11:11.text: Truly I tell you, among those born of women there has risen no one greater than John the Baptist. Yet even the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.

40:16:27.text: For the Son of Man will come in His Father’s glory with His angels, and then He will repay each one according to what he has done.

40:16:28.text: Truly I tell you, some who are standing here will not taste death before they see the Son of Man coming in His kingdom.”

40:16:3.text: and in the morning, ‘Today it will be stormy, for the sky is red and overcast.’ You know how to interpret the appearance of the sky, but not the signs of the times.

40:16:4.text: A wicked and adulterous generation demands a sign, but none will be given it except the sign of Jonah.” Then He left them and went away.

40:16:5.text: When they crossed to the other side, the disciples forgot to take bread.

40:16:6.text: “Watch out!” Jesus told them. “Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”

40:16:7.text: They discussed this among themselves and concluded, “It is because we did not bring any bread.”

40:16:8.text: Aware of their conversation, Jesus said, “You of little faith, why are you debating among yourselves about having no bread?

40:16:9.text: Do you still not understand? Do you not remember the five loaves for the five thousand, and how many basketfuls you gathered?

40:17:1.text: After six days Jesus took with Him Peter, James, and John the brother of James, and led them up a high mountain by themselves.

40:17:10.text: The disciples asked Him, “Why then do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”

40:17:11.text: Jesus replied, “Elijah does indeed come, and he will restore all things.

40:17:12.text: But I tell you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but have done to him whatever they wished. In the same way, the Son of Man will suffer at their hands.”

40:17:13.text: Then the disciples understood that He was speaking to them about John the Baptist.

40:17:14.text: When they came to the crowd, a man came up to Jesus and knelt before Him.

40:17:15.text: “Lord, have mercy on my son,” he said. “He has seizures and is suffering terribly. He often falls into the fire or into the water.

40:17:16.text: I brought him to Your disciples, but they could not heal him.”

40:17:17.text: “O unbelieving and perverse generation!” Jesus replied. “How long must I remain with you? How long must I put up with you? Bring the boy here to Me.”

40:17:18.text: Then Jesus rebuked the demon, and it came out of the boy, and he was healed from that moment.

40:17:19.text: Afterward the disciples came to Jesus privately and asked, “Why couldn’t we drive it out?”

40:17:2.text: There He was transfigured before them. His face shone like the sun, and His clothes became as white as the light.

40:17:20.text: “Because you have so little faith,” He answered. “For truly I tell you, if you have faith the size of a mustard seed, you can say to this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move. Nothing will be impossible for you.”

40:17:22.text: When they gathered together in Galilee, Jesus told them, “The Son of Man is about to be delivered into the hands of men.

40:17:23.text: They will kill Him, and on the third day He will be raised to life.” And the disciples were deeply grieved.

40:17:24.text: After they had arrived in Capernaum, the collectors of the two-drachma tax came to Peter and asked, “Does your Teacher pay the two drachmas?”

40:17:25.text: “Yes,” he answered. When Peter entered the house, Jesus preempted him. “What do you think, Simon?” He asked. “From whom do the kings of the earth collect customs and taxes: from their own sons, or from others?”

40:17:26.text: “From others,” Peter answered. “Then the sons are exempt,” Jesus declared.

40:17:27.text: “But so that we may not offend them, go to the sea, cast a hook, and take the first fish you catch. When you open its mouth, you will find a four-drachma coin. Take it and give it to them for My tax and yours.”

40:17:3.text: Suddenly Moses and Elijah appeared before them, talking with Jesus.

40:17:4.text: Peter said to Jesus, “Lord, it is good for us to be here. If You wish, I will put up three shelters — one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”

40:17:5.text: While Peter was still speaking, a bright cloud enveloped them, and a voice from the cloud said, “This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Listen to Him!”

40:17:6.text: When the disciples heard this, they fell facedown in terror.

40:17:7.text: Then Jesus came over and touched them. “Get up,” He said. “Do not be afraid.”

40:17:8.text: And when they looked up, they saw no one except Jesus.

40:17:9.text: As they were coming down the mountain, Jesus commanded them, “Do not tell anyone about this vision until the Son of Man has been raised from the dead.”

40:18:1.text: At that time the disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Who then is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?”

40:18:10.text: See that you do not look down on any of these little ones. For I tell you that their angels in heaven always see the face of My Father in heaven.

40:18:12.text: What do you think? If a man has a hundred sheep and one of them goes astray, will he not leave the ninety-nine on the hills and go out to search for the one that is lost?

40:18:13.text: And if he finds it, truly I tell you, he rejoices more over that one sheep than over the ninety-nine that did not go astray.

40:18:14.text: In the same way, your Father in heaven is not willing that any of these little ones should perish.

40:18:15.text: If your brother sins against you, go and confront him privately. If he listens to you, you have won your brother over.

40:18:16.text: But if he will not listen, take one or two others along, so that ‘every matter may be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.’

40:18:17.text: If he refuses to listen to them, tell it to the church. And if he refuses to listen even to the church, regard him as you would a pagan or a tax collector.

40:18:18.text: Truly I tell you, whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven.

40:18:19.text: Again, I tell you truly that if two of you on the earth agree about anything you ask for, it will be done for you by My Father in heaven.

40:18:2.text: Jesus invited a little child to stand among them.

40:18:20.text: For where two or three gather together in My name, there am I with them.”

40:18:21.text: Then Peter came to Jesus and asked, “Lord, how many times shall I forgive my brother who sins against me? Up to seven times?”

40:18:22.text: Jesus answered, “I tell you, not just seven times, but seventy-seven times!

40:18:23.text: Because of this, the kingdom of heaven is like a king who wanted to settle accounts with his servants.

40:18:24.text: As he began the settlements, a debtor was brought to him owing ten thousand talents.

40:18:25.text: Since the man was unable to pay, the master ordered that he be sold to pay his debt, along with his wife and children and everything he owned.

40:18:26.text: Then the servant fell on his knees before him. ‘Have patience with me,’ he begged, ‘and I will pay back everything.’

40:18:27.text: His master had compassion on him, forgave his debt, and released him.

40:18:28.text: But when that servant went out, he found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred denarii. He grabbed him and began to choke him, saying, ‘Pay back what you owe me!’

40:18:29.text: So his fellow servant fell down and begged him, ‘Have patience with me, and I will pay you back.’

40:18:3.text: “Truly I tell you,” He said, “unless you change and become like little children, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.

40:18:30.text: But he refused. Instead, he went and had the man thrown into prison until he could pay his debt.

40:18:31.text: When his fellow servants saw what had happened, they were greatly distressed, and they went and recounted all of this to their master.

40:18:32.text: Then the master summoned him and declared, ‘You wicked servant! I forgave all your debt because you begged me.

40:18:33.text: Shouldn’t you have had mercy on your fellow servant, just as I had on you?’

40:18:34.text: In anger his master turned him over to the jailers to be tortured, until he should repay all that he owed.

40:18:35.text: That is how My heavenly Father will treat each of you unless you forgive your brother from your heart.”

40:18:4.text: Therefore, whoever humbles himself like this little child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.

40:18:5.text: And whoever welcomes a little child like this in My name welcomes Me.

40:18:6.text: But if anyone causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to stumble, it would be better for him to have a large millstone hung around his neck and to be drowned in the depths of the sea.

40:18:7.text: Woe to the world for the causes of sin. These stumbling blocks must come, but woe to the man through whom they come!

40:18:8.text: If your hand or your foot causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away. It is better for you to enter life crippled or lame than to have two hands and two feet and be thrown into the eternal fire.

40:18:9.text: And if your eye causes you to sin, gouge it out and throw it away. It is better for you to enter life with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into the fire of hell.

40:19:1.text: When Jesus had finished saying these things, He left Galilee and went into the region of Judea beyond the Jordan.

40:19:10.text: His disciples said to Him, “If this is the case between a man and his wife, it is better not to marry.”

40:19:11.text: “Not everyone can accept this word,” He replied, “but only those to whom it has been given.

40:19:12.text: For there are eunuchs who were born that way; others were made that way by men; and still others live like eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. The one who can accept this should accept it.”

40:19:13.text: Then the little children were brought to Jesus for Him to place His hands on them and pray for them. And the disciples rebuked those who brought them.

40:19:14.text: But Jesus said, “Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them! For the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these.”

40:19:15.text: And after He had placed His hands on them, He went on from there.

40:19:16.text: Just then a man came up to Jesus and inquired, “Teacher, what good thing must I do to obtain eternal life?”

40:19:17.text: “Why do you ask Me about what is good?” Jesus replied. “There is only One who is good. If you want to enter life, keep the commandments.”

40:19:18.text: “Which ones?” the man asked. Jesus answered, “‘Do not murder, do not commit adultery, do not steal, do not bear false witness,

40:19:19.text: honor your father and mother, and love your neighbor as yourself.’ ”

40:19:2.text: Large crowds followed Him, and He healed them there.

40:19:20.text: “All these I have kept,” said the young man. “What do I still lack?”

40:19:21.text: Jesus told him, “If you want to be perfect, go, sell your possessions and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow Me.”

40:19:22.text: When the young man heard this, he went away in sorrow, because he had great wealth.

40:19:23.text: Then Jesus said to His disciples, “Truly I tell you, it is hard for a rich man to enter the kingdom of heaven.

40:19:24.text: Again I tell you, it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.”

40:19:25.text: When the disciples heard this, they were greatly astonished and asked, “Who then can be saved?”

40:19:26.text: Jesus looked at them and said, “With man this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.”

40:19:27.text: “Look,” Peter replied, “we have left everything to follow You. What then will there be for us?”

40:19:28.text: Jesus said to them, “Truly I tell you, in the renewal of all things, when the Son of Man sits on His glorious throne, you who have followed Me will also sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

40:19:29.text: And everyone who has left houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or wife or children or fields for the sake of My name will receive a hundredfold and will inherit eternal life.

40:19:3.text: Then some Pharisees came and tested Him by asking, “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any reason?”

40:19:30.text: But many who are first will be last, and the last will be first.

40:19:4.text: Jesus answered, “Have you not read that from the beginning the Creator ‘made them male and female,’

40:19:5.text: and said, ‘For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife, and the two will become one flesh’ ?

40:19:6.text: So they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore what God has joined together, let man not separate.”

40:19:7.text: “Why then,” they asked, “did Moses order a man to give his wife a certificate of divorce and send her away? ”

40:19:8.text: Jesus replied, “Moses permitted you to divorce your wives because of your hardness of heart; but it was not this way from the beginning.

40:19:9.text: Now I tell you that whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, and marries another woman, commits adultery. ”

40:1:1.text: This is the record of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham:

40:1:10.text: Hezekiah was the father of Manasseh, Manasseh the father of Amon, Amon the father of Josiah,

40:1:11.text: and Josiah the father of Jeconiah and his brothers at the time of the exile to Babylon.

40:1:12.text: After the exile to Babylon: Jeconiah was the father of Shealtiel, Shealtiel the father of Zerubbabel,

40:1:13.text: Zerubbabel the father of Abiud, Abiud the father of Eliakim, and Eliakim the father of Azor.

40:1:14.text: Azor was the father of Zadok, Zadok the father of Achim, and Achim the father of Eliud.

40:1:15.text: Eliud was the father of Eleazar, Eleazar the father of Matthan, Matthan the father of Jacob,

40:1:16.text: and Jacob the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.

40:1:17.text: In all, then, there were fourteen generations from Abraham to David, fourteen from David to the exile to Babylon, and fourteen from the exile to the Christ.

40:1:18.text: This is how the birth of Jesus Christ came about: His mother Mary was pledged in marriage to Joseph, but before they came together, she was found to be with child through the Holy Spirit.

40:1:19.text: Because Joseph her husband was a righteous man and was unwilling to disgrace her publicly, he resolved to divorce her quietly.

40:1:2.text: Abraham was the father of Isaac, Isaac the father of Jacob, and Jacob the father of Judah and his brothers.

40:1:20.text: But after he had pondered these things, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, “Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to embrace Mary as your wife, for the One conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.

40:1:21.text: She will give birth to a Son, and you are to give Him the name Jesus, because He will save His people from their sins.”

40:1:22.text: All this took place to fulfill what the Lord had said through the prophet:

40:1:23.text: “Behold, the virgin will be with child and will give birth to a son, and they will call Him Immanuel” (which means, “God with us” ).

40:1:24.text: When Joseph woke up, he did as the angel of the Lord had commanded him, and embraced Mary as his wife.

40:1:25.text: But he had no union with her until she gave birth to a Son. And he gave Him the name Jesus.

40:1:3.text: Judah was the father of Perez and Zerah by Tamar, Perez the father of Hezron, and Hezron the father of Ram.

40:1:4.text: Ram was the father of Amminadab, Amminadab the father of Nahshon, and Nahshon the father of Salmon.

40:1:5.text: Salmon was the father of Boaz by Rahab, Boaz the father of Obed by Ruth, Obed the father of Jesse,

40:1:6.text: and Jesse the father of David the king. Next: David was the father of Solomon by Uriah’s wife,

40:1:7.text: Solomon the father of Rehoboam, Rehoboam the father of Abijah, and Abijah the father of Asa.

40:1:8.text: Asa was the father of Jehoshaphat, Jehoshaphat the father of Joram, and Joram the father of Uzziah.

40:1:9.text: Uzziah was the father of Jotham, Jotham the father of Ahaz, and Ahaz the father of Hezekiah.

40:20:1.text: “For the kingdom of heaven is like a landowner who went out early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard.

40:20:10.text: So when the original workers came, they assumed they would receive more. But each of them also received a denarius.

40:20:11.text: On receiving their pay, they began to grumble against the landowner.

40:20:12.text: ‘These men who were hired last worked only one hour,’ they said, ‘and you have made them equal to us who have borne the burden and the scorching heat of the day.’

40:20:13.text: But he answered one of them, ‘Friend, I am not being unfair to you. Did you not agree with me on one denarius?

40:20:14.text: Take your pay and go. I want to give this last man the same as I gave you.

40:20:15.text: Do I not have the right to do as I please with what is mine? Or are you envious because I am generous?’

40:20:16.text: So the last will be first, and the first will be last.”

40:20:17.text: As Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, He took the twelve disciples aside and said,

40:20:18.text: “Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be delivered over to the chief priests and scribes. They will condemn Him to death

40:20:19.text: and will deliver Him over to the Gentiles to be mocked and flogged and crucified. And on the third day He will be raised to life.”

40:20:2.text: He agreed to pay them a denarius for the day and sent them into his vineyard.

40:20:20.text: Then the mother of Zebedee’s sons came to Jesus with her sons and knelt down to make a request of Him.

40:20:21.text: “What do you want?” He inquired. She answered, “Declare that in Your kingdom one of these two sons of mine may sit at Your right hand, and the other at Your left.”

40:20:22.text: “You do not know what you are asking,” Jesus replied. “Can you drink the cup I am going to drink?” “We can,” the brothers answered.

40:20:23.text: “You will indeed drink My cup,” Jesus said. “But to sit at My right or left is not Mine to grant. These seats belong to those for whom My Father has prepared them.”

40:20:24.text: When the ten heard about this, they were indignant with the two brothers.

40:20:25.text: But Jesus called them aside and said, “You know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their superiors exercise authority over them.

40:20:26.text: It shall not be this way among you. Instead, whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant,

40:20:27.text: and whoever wants to be first among you must be your slave —

40:20:28.text: just as the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many.”

40:20:29.text: As they were leaving Jericho, a large crowd followed Him.

40:20:3.text: About the third hour he went out and saw others standing in the marketplace doing nothing.

40:20:30.text: And there were two blind men sitting beside the road. When they heard that Jesus was passing by, they cried out, “Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!”

40:20:31.text: The crowd admonished them to be silent, but they cried out all the louder, “Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!”

40:20:32.text: Jesus stopped and called them. “What do you want Me to do for you?” He asked.

40:20:33.text: “Lord,” they answered, “let our eyes be opened.”

40:20:34.text: Moved with compassion, Jesus touched their eyes, and at once they received their sight and followed Him.

40:20:4.text: ‘You also go into my vineyard,’ he said, ‘and I will pay you whatever is right.’

40:20:5.text: So they went. He went out again about the sixth hour and the ninth hour and did the same thing.

40:20:6.text: About the eleventh hour he went out and found still others standing around. ‘Why have you been standing here all day long doing nothing?’ he asked.

40:20:7.text: ‘Because no one has hired us,’ they answered. So he told them, ‘You also go into my vineyard.’

40:20:8.text: When evening came, the owner of the vineyard said to his foreman, ‘Call the workers and pay them their wages, starting with the last ones hired and moving on to the first.’

40:20:9.text: The workers who were hired about the eleventh hour came and each received a denarius.

40:21:1.text: As they approached Jerusalem and came to Bethphage on the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent out two disciples,

40:21:10.text: When Jesus had entered Jerusalem, the whole city was stirred and asked, “Who is this?”

40:21:11.text: The crowds replied, “This is Jesus, the prophet from Nazareth in Galilee.”

40:21:12.text: Then Jesus entered the temple courts and drove out all who were buying and selling there. He overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling doves.

40:21:13.text: And He declared to them, “It is written: ‘My house will be called a house of prayer.’ But you are making it ‘a den of robbers.’ ”

40:21:14.text: The blind and the lame came to Him at the temple, and He healed them.

40:21:15.text: But the chief priests and scribes were indignant when they saw the wonders He performed and the children shouting in the temple courts, “Hosanna to the Son of David!”

40:21:16.text: “Do you hear what these children are saying?” they asked. “Yes,” Jesus answered. “Have you never read: ‘From the mouths of children and infants You have ordained praise’ ?”

40:21:17.text: Then He left them and went out of the city to Bethany, where He spent the night.

40:21:18.text: In the morning, as Jesus was returning to the city, He was hungry.

40:21:19.text: Seeing a fig tree by the road, He went up to it but found nothing on it except leaves. “May you never bear fruit again!” He said. And immediately the tree withered.

40:21:2.text: saying to them, “Go into the village ahead of you, and at once you will find a donkey tied there, with her colt beside her. Untie them and bring them to Me.

40:21:20.text: When the disciples saw this, they marveled and asked, “How did the fig tree wither so quickly?”

40:21:21.text: “Truly I tell you,” Jesus replied, “if you have faith and do not doubt, not only will you do what was done to the fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,’ it will happen.

40:21:22.text: If you believe, you will receive whatever you ask for in prayer.”

40:21:23.text: When Jesus returned to the temple courts and began to teach, the chief priests and elders of the people came up to Him. “By what authority are You doing these things?” they asked. “And who gave You this authority?”

40:21:24.text: “I will also ask you one question,” Jesus replied, “and if you answer Me, I will tell you by what authority I am doing these things.

40:21:25.text: What was the source of John’s baptism? Was it from heaven or from men?” They deliberated among themselves and said, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ He will ask, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’

40:21:26.text: But if we say, ‘From men,’ we are afraid of the people, for they all regard John as a prophet.”

40:21:27.text: So they answered, “We do not know.” And Jesus replied, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things.

40:21:28.text: But what do you think? There was a man who had two sons. He went to the first one and said, ‘Son, go and work today in the vineyard.’

40:21:29.text: ‘I will not,’ he replied. But later he changed his mind and went.

40:21:3.text: If anyone questions you, tell him that the Lord needs them, and he will send them right away.”

40:21:30.text: Then the man went to the second son and told him the same thing. ‘I will, sir,’ he said. But he did not go.

40:21:31.text: Which of the two did the will of his father?” “The first, ” they answered. Jesus said to them, “Truly I tell you, the tax collectors and prostitutes are entering the kingdom of God before you.

40:21:32.text: For John came to you in a righteous way and you did not believe him, but the tax collectors and prostitutes did. And even after you saw this, you did not repent and believe him.

40:21:33.text: Listen to another parable: There was a landowner who planted a vineyard. He put a wall around it, dug a winepress in it, and built a tower. Then he rented it out to some tenants and went away on a journey.

40:21:34.text: When the harvest time drew near, he sent his servants to the tenants to collect his share of the fruit.

40:21:35.text: But the tenants seized his servants. They beat one, killed another, and stoned a third.

40:21:36.text: Again, he sent other servants, more than the first group. But the tenants did the same to them.

40:21:37.text: Finally, he sent his son to them. ‘They will respect my son,’ he said.

40:21:38.text: But when the tenants saw the son, they said to one another, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him and take his inheritance.’

40:21:39.text: So they seized him and threw him out of the vineyard and killed him.

40:21:4.text: This took place to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet:

40:21:40.text: Therefore, when the owner of the vineyard returns, what will he do to those tenants?”

40:21:41.text: “He will bring those wretches to a wretched end,” they replied, “and will rent out the vineyard to other tenants who will give him his share of the fruit at harvest time.”

40:21:42.text: Jesus said to them, “Have you never read in the Scriptures: ‘The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone. This is from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes’ ?

40:21:43.text: Therefore I tell you that the kingdom of God will be taken away from you and given to a people who will produce its fruit.

40:21:44.text: He who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces, but he on whom it falls will be crushed. ”

40:21:45.text: When the chief priests and Pharisees heard His parables, they knew that Jesus was speaking about them.

40:21:46.text: Although they wanted to arrest Him, they were afraid of the crowds, because the people regarded Him as a prophet.

40:21:5.text: “Say to the Daughter of Zion, ‘See, your King comes to you, gentle and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.’ ”

40:21:6.text: So the disciples went and did as Jesus had directed them.

40:21:7.text: They brought the donkey and the colt and laid their cloaks on them, and Jesus sat on them.

40:21:8.text: A massive crowd spread their cloaks on the road, while others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road.

40:21:9.text: The crowds that went ahead of Him and those that followed were shouting: “Hosanna to the Son of David!” “Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!” “Hosanna in the highest!”
