40:22:10.text: So the servants went out into the streets and gathered everyone they could find, both evil and good, and the wedding hall was filled with guests.

40:22:11.text: But when the king came in to see the guests, he spotted a man who was not dressed in wedding clothes.

40:22:12.text: ‘Friend,’ he asked, ‘how did you get in here without wedding clothes?’ But the man was speechless.

40:22:13.text: Then the king told the servants, ‘Tie him hand and foot, and throw him into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.’

40:22:14.text: For many are called, but few are chosen.”

40:22:15.text: Then the Pharisees went out and conspired to trap Jesus in His words.

40:22:16.text: They sent their disciples to Him along with the Herodians. “Teacher,” they said, “we know that You are honest and that You teach the way of God in accordance with the truth. You seek favor from no one, because You pay no attention to external appearance.

40:22:17.text: So tell us what You think: Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar or not?”

40:22:18.text: But Jesus knew their evil intent and said, “You hypocrites, why are you testing Me?

40:22:19.text: Show Me the coin used for the tax.” And they brought Him a denarius.

40:22:2.text: “The kingdom of heaven is like a king who prepared a wedding banquet for his son.

40:22:20.text: “Whose image is this,” He asked, “and whose inscription?”

40:22:21.text: “Caesar’s,” they answered. So Jesus told them, “Give to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s.”

40:22:22.text: And when they heard this, they were amazed. So they left Him and went away.

40:22:23.text: That same day the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to Jesus and questioned Him.

40:22:24.text: “Teacher,” they said, “Moses declared that if a man dies without having children, his brother is to marry the widow and raise up offspring for him.

40:22:25.text: Now there were seven brothers among us. The first one married and died without having children. So he left his wife to his brother.

40:22:26.text: The same thing happened to the second and third brothers, down to the seventh.

40:22:27.text: And last of all, the woman died.

40:22:28.text: In the resurrection, then, whose wife will she be of the seven? For all of them were married to her.”

40:22:29.text: Jesus answered, “You are mistaken because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God.

40:22:3.text: He sent his servants to call those he had invited to the banquet, but they refused to come.

40:22:30.text: In the resurrection, people will neither marry nor be given in marriage. Instead, they will be like the angels in heaven.

40:22:31.text: But concerning the resurrection of the dead, have you not read what God said to you:

40:22:32.text: ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’ ? He is not the God of the dead, but of the living.”

40:22:33.text: When the crowds heard this, they were astonished at His teaching.

40:22:34.text: And when the Pharisees heard that Jesus had silenced the Sadducees, they themselves gathered together.

40:22:35.text: One of them, an expert in the law, tested Him with a question:

40:22:36.text: “Teacher, which commandment is the greatest in the Law?”

40:22:37.text: Jesus declared, “‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.’

40:22:38.text: This is the first and greatest commandment.

40:22:39.text: And the second is like it: ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’

40:22:4.text: Again, he sent other servants and said, ‘Tell those who have been invited that I have prepared my dinner. My oxen and fattened cattle have been killed, and everything is ready. Come to the wedding banquet.’

40:22:40.text: All the Law and the Prophets hang on these two commandments.”

40:22:41.text: While the Pharisees were assembled, Jesus questioned them:

40:22:42.text: “What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is He?” “David’s,” they answered.

40:22:43.text: Jesus said to them, “How then does David in the Spirit call Him ‘Lord’ ? For he says:

40:22:44.text: ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand until I put Your enemies under Your feet.”’

40:22:45.text: So if David calls Him ‘Lord,’ how can He be David’s son?”

40:22:46.text: No one was able to answer a word, and from that day on no one dared to question Him any further.

40:22:5.text: But they paid no attention and went away, one to his field, another to his business.

40:22:6.text: The rest seized his servants, mistreated them, and killed them.

40:22:7.text: The king was enraged, and he sent his troops to destroy those murderers and burn their city.

40:22:8.text: Then he said to his servants, ‘The wedding banquet is ready, but those I invited were not worthy.

40:22:9.text: Go therefore to the crossroads and invite to the banquet as many as you can find.’

40:23:1.text: Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and to His disciples:

40:23:10.text: Nor are you to be called instructors, for you have one Instructor, the Christ.

40:23:11.text: The greatest among you shall be your servant.

40:23:12.text: For whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.

40:23:13.text: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You shut the kingdom of heaven in men’s faces. You yourselves do not enter, nor will you let in those who wish to enter.

40:23:15.text: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You traverse land and sea to win a single convert, and when he becomes one, you make him twice as much a son of hell as you are.

40:23:16.text: Woe to you, blind guides! You say, ‘If anyone swears by the temple, it means nothing; but if anyone swears by the gold of the temple, he is bound by his oath.’

40:23:17.text: You blind fools! Which is greater: the gold, or the temple that makes it sacred?

40:23:18.text: And you say, ‘If anyone swears by the altar, it means nothing; but if anyone swears by the gift on it, he is bound by his oath.’

40:23:19.text: You blind men! Which is greater: the gift, or the altar that makes it sacred?

40:23:2.text: “The scribes and Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat.

40:23:20.text: So then, he who swears by the altar swears by it and by everything on it.

40:23:21.text: And he who swears by the temple swears by it and by the One who dwells in it.

40:23:22.text: And he who swears by heaven swears by God’s throne and by the One who sits on it.

40:23:23.text: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You pay tithes of mint, dill, and cumin. But you have disregarded the weightier matters of the law: justice, mercy, and faithfulness. You should have practiced the latter, without neglecting the former.

40:23:24.text: You blind guides! You strain out a gnat but swallow a camel.

40:23:25.text: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You clean the outside of the cup and dish, but inside they are full of greed and self-indulgence.

40:23:26.text: Blind Pharisee! First clean the inside of the cup and dish, so that the outside may become clean as well.

40:23:27.text: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You are like whitewashed tombs, which look beautiful on the outside, but on the inside are full of dead men’s bones and every kind of impurity.

40:23:28.text: In the same way, on the outside you appear to be righteous, but on the inside you are full of hypocrisy and wickedness.

40:23:29.text: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You build tombs for the prophets and decorate the monuments of the righteous.

40:23:3.text: So practice and observe everything they tell you. But do not do what they do, for they do not practice what they preach.

40:23:30.text: And you say, ‘If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partners with them in shedding the blood of the prophets.’

40:23:31.text: So you testify against yourselves that you are the sons of those who murdered the prophets.

40:23:32.text: Fill up, then, the measure of the sin of your fathers.

40:23:33.text: You snakes! You brood of vipers! How will you escape the sentence of hell?

40:23:34.text: Because of this, I am sending you prophets and wise men and teachers. Some of them you will kill and crucify, and others you will flog in your synagogues and persecute in town after town.

40:23:35.text: And so upon you will come all the righteous blood shed on earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Berechiah, whom you murdered between the temple and the altar.

40:23:36.text: Truly I tell you, all these things will come upon this generation.

40:23:37.text: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her, how often I have longed to gather your children together, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you were unwilling!

40:23:38.text: Look, your house is left to you desolate.

40:23:39.text: For I tell you that you will not see Me again until you say, ‘Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord.’ ”

40:23:4.text: They tie up heavy, burdensome loads and lay them on men’s shoulders, but they themselves are not willing to lift a finger to move them.

40:23:5.text: All their deeds are done for men to see. They broaden their phylacteries and lengthen their tassels.

40:23:6.text: They love the places of honor at banquets, the chief seats in the synagogues,

40:23:7.text: the greetings in the marketplaces, and the title of ‘Rabbi’ by which they are addressed.

40:23:8.text: But you are not to be called ‘Rabbi,’ for you have one Teacher, and you are all brothers.

40:23:9.text: And do not call anyone on earth your father, for you have one Father, who is in heaven.

40:24:1.text: As Jesus left the temple and was walking away, His disciples came up to Him to point out its buildings.

40:24:10.text: At that time many will fall away and will betray and hate one another,

40:24:11.text: and many false prophets will arise and mislead many.

40:24:12.text: Because of the multiplication of wickedness, the love of most will grow cold.

40:24:13.text: But the one who perseveres to the end will be saved.

40:24:14.text: And this gospel of the kingdom will be preached in all the world as a testimony to all nations, and then the end will come.

40:24:15.text: So when you see standing in the holy place ‘the abomination of desolation,’described by the prophet Daniel (let the reader understand),

40:24:16.text: then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains.

40:24:17.text: Let no one on the housetop come down to retrieve anything from his house.

40:24:18.text: And let no one in the field return for his cloak.

40:24:19.text: How miserable those days will be for pregnant and nursing mothers!

40:24:2.text: “Do you see all these things?” He replied. “Truly I tell you, not one stone here will be left on another; every one will be thrown down.”

40:24:20.text: Pray that your flight will not occur in the winter or on the Sabbath.

40:24:21.text: For at that time there will be great tribulation, unmatched from the beginning of the world until now, and never to be seen again.

40:24:22.text: If those days had not been cut short, nobody would be saved. But for the sake of the elect, those days will be cut short.

40:24:23.text: At that time, if anyone says to you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or ‘There He is!’ do not believe it.

40:24:24.text: For false Christs and false prophets will appear and perform great signs and wonders that would deceive even the elect, if that were possible.

40:24:25.text: See, I have told you in advance.

40:24:26.text: So if they tell you, ‘There He is in the wilderness,’ do not go out; or, ‘Here He is in the inner rooms,’ do not believe it.

40:24:27.text: For just as the lightning comes from the east and flashes as far as the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.

40:24:28.text: Wherever there is a carcass, there the vultures will gather.

40:24:29.text: Immediately after the tribulation of those days: ‘The sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light; the stars will fall from the sky, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.’

40:24:3.text: While Jesus was sitting on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to Him privately. “Tell us,” they said, “when will these things happen, and what will be the sign of Your coming and of the end of the age?”

40:24:30.text: At that time the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven, and all the tribes of the earth will mourn. They will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven, with power and great glory.

40:24:31.text: And He will send out His angels with a loud trumpet call, and they will gather His elect from the four winds, from one end of the heavens to the other.

40:24:32.text: Now learn this lesson from the fig tree: As soon as its branches become tender and sprout leaves, you know that summer is near.

40:24:33.text: So also, when you see all these things, you will know that He is near, right at the door.

40:24:34.text: Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things have happened.

40:24:35.text: Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away.

40:24:36.text: No one knows about that day or hour, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.

40:24:37.text: As it was in the days of Noah, so will it be at the coming of the Son of Man.

40:24:38.text: For in the days before the flood, people were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, up to the day Noah entered the ark.

40:24:39.text: And they were oblivious, until the flood came and swept them all away. So will it be at the coming of the Son of Man.

40:24:4.text: Jesus answered, “See to it that no one deceives you.

40:24:40.text: Two men will be in the field: one will be taken and the other left.

40:24:41.text: Two women will be grinding at the mill: one will be taken and the other left.

40:24:42.text: Therefore keep watch, because you do not know the day on which your Lord will come.

40:24:43.text: But understand this: If the homeowner had known in which watch of the night the thief was coming, he would have kept watch and would not have let his house be broken into.

40:24:44.text: For this reason, you also must be ready, because the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not expect.

40:24:45.text: Who then is the faithful and wise servant, whom the master has put in charge of his household, to give the others their food at the proper time?

40:24:46.text: Blessed is that servant whose master finds him doing so when he returns.

40:24:47.text: Truly I tell you, he will put him in charge of all his possessions.

40:24:48.text: But suppose that servant is wicked and says in his heart, ‘My master will be away a long time.’

40:24:49.text: And he begins to beat his fellow servants and to eat and drink with drunkards.

40:24:5.text: For many will come in My name, claiming, ‘I am the Christ,’ and will deceive many.

40:24:50.text: The master of that servant will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not anticipate.

40:24:51.text: Then he will cut him to pieces and assign him a place with the hypocrites, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

40:24:6.text: You will hear of wars and rumors of wars, but see to it that you are not alarmed. These things must happen, but the end is still to come.

40:24:7.text: Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be famines and earthquakes in various places.

40:24:8.text: All these are the beginning of birth pains.

40:24:9.text: Then they will deliver you over to be persecuted and killed, and you will be hated by all nations because of My name.

40:25:1.text: “At that time the kingdom of heaven will be like ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.

40:25:10.text: But while they were on their way to buy it, the bridegroom arrived. Those who were ready went in with him to the wedding banquet, and the door was shut.

40:25:11.text: Later the other virgins arrived and said, ‘Lord, lord, open the door for us!’

40:25:12.text: But he replied, ‘Truly I tell you, I do not know you.’

40:25:13.text: Therefore keep watch, because you do not know the day or the hour.

40:25:14.text: For it is just like a man going on a journey, who called his servants and entrusted them with his possessions.

40:25:15.text: To one he gave five talents, to another two talents, and to another one talent — each according to his own ability. And he went on his journey.

40:25:16.text: The servant who had received the five talents went at once and put them to work and gained five more.

40:25:17.text: Likewise, the one with the two talents gained two more.

40:25:18.text: But the servant who had received the one talent went off, dug a hole in the ground, and hid his master’s money.

40:25:19.text: After a long time the master of those servants returned to settle accounts with them.

40:25:2.text: Five of them were foolish, and five were wise.

40:25:20.text: The servant who had received the five talents came and presented five more. ‘Master,’ he said, ‘you entrusted me with five talents. See, I have gained five more.’

40:25:21.text: His master replied, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a few things; I will put you in charge of many things. Enter into the joy of your master!’

40:25:22.text: The servant who had received the two talents also came and said, ‘Master, you entrusted me with two talents. See, I have gained two more.’

40:25:23.text: His master replied, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a few things; I will put you in charge of many things. Enter into the joy of your master!’

40:25:24.text: Finally, the servant who had received the one talent came and said, ‘Master, I knew that you are a hard man, reaping where you have not sown and gathering where you have not scattered seed.

40:25:25.text: So I was afraid and went out and hid your talent in the ground. See, you have what belongs to you.’

40:25:26.text: ‘You wicked, lazy servant!’ replied his master. ‘You knew that I reap where I have not sown and gather where I have not scattered seed.

40:25:27.text: Then you should have deposited my money with the bankers, and on my return I would have received it back with interest.

40:25:28.text: Therefore take the talent from him and give it to the one who has ten talents.

40:25:29.text: For everyone who has will be given more, and he will have an abundance. But the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.

40:25:3.text: The foolish ones took their lamps but did not take along any extra oil.

40:25:30.text: And throw that worthless servant into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.’

40:25:31.text: When the Son of Man comes in His glory, and all the angels with Him, He will sit on His glorious throne.

40:25:32.text: All the nations will be gathered before Him, and He will separate the people one from another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.

40:25:33.text: He will place the sheep on His right and the goats on His left.

40:25:34.text: Then the King will say to those on His right, ‘Come, you who are blessed by My Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.

40:25:35.text: For I was hungry and you gave Me something to eat, I was thirsty and you gave Me something to drink, I was a stranger and you took Me in,

40:25:36.text: I was naked and you clothed Me, I was sick and you looked after Me, I was in prison and you visited Me.’

40:25:37.text: Then the righteous will answer Him, ‘Lord, when did we see You hungry and feed You, or thirsty and give You something to drink?

40:25:38.text: When did we see You a stranger and take You in, or naked and clothe You?

40:25:39.text: When did we see You sick or in prison and visit You?’

40:25:4.text: But the wise ones took oil in flasks along with their lamps.

40:25:40.text: And the King will reply, ‘Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers of Mine, you did for Me.’

40:25:41.text: Then He will say to those on His left, ‘Depart from Me, you who are cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.

40:25:42.text: For I was hungry and you gave Me nothing to eat, I was thirsty and you gave Me nothing to drink,

40:25:43.text: I was a stranger and you did not take Me in, I was naked and you did not clothe Me, I was sick and in prison and you did not visit Me.’

40:25:44.text: And they too will reply, ‘Lord, when did we see You hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and did not minister to You?’

40:25:45.text: Then the King will answer, ‘Truly I tell you, whatever you did not do for one of the least of these, you did not do for Me.’

40:25:46.text: And they will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.”

40:25:5.text: When the bridegroom was delayed, they all became drowsy and fell asleep.

40:25:6.text: At midnight the cry rang out: ‘Here is the bridegroom! Come out to meet him!’

40:25:7.text: Then all the virgins woke up and trimmed their lamps.

40:25:8.text: The foolish ones said to the wise, ‘Give us some of your oil; our lamps are going out.’

40:25:9.text: ‘No,’ said the wise ones, ‘or there may not be enough for both us and you. Instead, go to those who sell oil and buy some for yourselves.’

40:26:1.text: When Jesus had finished saying all these things, He told His disciples,

40:26:10.text: Aware of this, Jesus asked, “Why are you bothering this woman? She has done a beautiful deed to Me.

40:26:11.text: The poor you will always have with you, but you will not always have Me.

40:26:12.text: By pouring this perfume on Me, she has prepared My body for burial.

40:26:13.text: Truly I tell you, wherever this gospel is preached in all the world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her.”

40:26:14.text: Then one of the Twelve, the one called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests

40:26:15.text: and asked, “What are you willing to give me if I hand Him over to you?” And they set out for him thirty pieces of silver.

40:26:16.text: So from then on Judas looked for an opportunity to betray Jesus.

40:26:17.text: On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Where do You want us to prepare for You to eat the Passover?”

40:26:18.text: He answered, “Go into the city to a certain man and tell him that the Teacher says, ‘My time is near. I will keep the Passover with My disciples at your house.’ ”

40:26:19.text: So the disciples did as Jesus had directed them and prepared the Passover.

40:26:2.text: “You know that the Passover is two days away, and the Son of Man will be handed over to be crucified.”

40:26:20.text: When evening came, Jesus was reclining with the twelve disciples.

40:26:21.text: And while they were eating, He said to them, “Truly I tell you, one of you will betray Me.”

40:26:22.text: They were deeply grieved and began to ask Him one after another, “Surely not I, Lord?”

40:26:23.text: Jesus answered, “The one who has dipped his hand into the bowl with Me will betray Me.

40:26:24.text: The Son of Man will go just as it is written about Him, but woe to that man by whom He is betrayed. It would be better for him if he had not been born.”

40:26:25.text: Then Judas, who would betray Him, said, “Surely not I, Rabbi?” Jesus answered, “You have said it yourself.”

40:26:26.text: While they were eating, Jesus took bread, spoke a blessing and broke it, and gave it to the disciples, saying, “Take and eat; this is My body.”

40:26:27.text: Then He took the cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them, saying, “Drink from it, all of you.

40:26:28.text: This is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.

40:26:29.text: I tell you, I will not drink of this fruit of the vine from now on until that day when I drink it anew with you in My Father’s kingdom.”

40:26:3.text: At that time the chief priests and elders of the people assembled in the courtyard of the high priest, whose name was Caiaphas,

40:26:30.text: And when they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.

40:26:31.text: Then Jesus said to them, “This very night you will all fall away on account of Me. For it is written: ‘I will strike the Shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.’

40:26:32.text: But after I have risen, I will go ahead of you into Galilee.”

40:26:33.text: Peter said to Him, “Even if all fall away on account of You, I never will.”

40:26:34.text: “Truly I tell you,” Jesus declared, “this very night, before the rooster crows, you will deny Me three times.”

40:26:35.text: Peter replied, “Even if I have to die with You, I will never deny You.” And all the other disciples said the same thing.

40:26:36.text: At that time Jesus went with His disciples to a place called Gethsemane, and He told them, “Sit here while I go over there and pray.”

40:26:37.text: He took with Him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee and began to be sorrowful and deeply distressed.

40:26:38.text: Then He said to them, “My soul is consumed with sorrow to the point of death. Stay here and keep watch with Me.”

40:26:39.text: Going a little farther, He fell facedown and prayed, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from Me. Yet not as I will, but as You will.”

40:26:4.text: and they conspired to arrest Jesus covertly and kill Him.

40:26:40.text: Then Jesus returned to the disciples and found them sleeping. “Were you not able to keep watch with Me for one hour?” He asked Peter.

40:26:41.text: “Watch and pray so that you will not enter into temptation. For the spirit is willing, but the body is weak.”

40:26:42.text: A second time He went away and prayed, “My Father, if this cup cannot pass unless I drink it, may Your will be done.”

40:26:43.text: And again Jesus returned and found them sleeping — for their eyes were heavy.

40:26:44.text: So He left them and went away once more and prayed a third time, saying the same thing.

40:26:45.text: Then He returned to the disciples and said, “Are you still sleeping and resting? Look, the hour is near, and the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.

40:26:46.text: Rise, let us go! See, My betrayer is approaching!”

40:26:47.text: While Jesus was still speaking, Judas, one of the Twelve, arrived, accompanied by a large crowd armed with swords and clubs, sent from the chief priests and elders of the people.

40:26:48.text: Now the betrayer had arranged a signal with them: “The One I kiss is the man; arrest Him.”

40:26:49.text: Going directly to Jesus, he said, “Greetings, Rabbi!” and kissed Him.

40:26:5.text: “But not during the feast,” they said, “or there may be a riot among the people.”

40:26:50.text: “Friend,” Jesus replied, “do what you came for.” Then the men stepped forward, seized Jesus, and arrested Him.

40:26:51.text: At this, one of Jesus’ companions drew his sword and struck the servant of the high priest, cutting off his ear.

40:26:52.text: “Put your sword back in its place,” Jesus said to him. “For all who draw the sword will die by the sword.

40:26:53.text: Are you not aware that I can call on My Father, and He will at once put at My disposal more than twelve legions of angels?

40:26:54.text: But how then would the Scriptures be fulfilled that say it must happen this way?”

40:26:55.text: At that time Jesus said to the crowd, “Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest Me as you would an outlaw? Every day I sat teaching in the temple courts, and you did not arrest Me.

40:26:56.text: But this has all happened so that the writings of the prophets would be fulfilled.” Then all the disciples deserted Him and fled.

40:26:57.text: Those who had arrested Jesus led Him away to the house of Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and elders had gathered.

40:26:58.text: But Peter followed Him at a distance, right up to the courtyard of the high priest. And he went in and sat down with the guards to see the outcome.

40:26:59.text: Now the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin were seeking false testimony against Jesus in order to put Him to death.

40:26:60.text: But they did not find any, though many false witnesses came forward. Finally two came forward

40:26:62.text: So the high priest stood up and asked Him, “Have You no answer? What are these men testifying against You?”

40:26:63.text: But Jesus remained silent. Then the high priest said to Him, “I charge You under oath by the living God: Tell us if You are the Christ, the Son of God.”

40:26:64.text: “You have said it yourself,” Jesus answered. “But I say to all of you, from now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming on the clouds of heaven.”

40:26:65.text: At this, the high priest tore his clothes and declared, “He has blasphemed! Why do we need any more witnesses? Look, now you have heard the blasphemy.

40:26:66.text: What do you think?” “He deserves to die,” they answered.

40:6:23.text: But if your eyes are bad, your whole body will be full of darkness. If then the light within you is darkness, how great is that darkness!

40:6:24.text: No one can serve two masters: Either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money.

40:6:25.text: Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat or drink; or about your body, what you will wear. Is not life more than food, and the body more than clothes?

40:6:26.text: Look at the birds of the air: They do not sow or reap or gather into barns — and yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not much more valuable than they?

40:6:27.text: Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?

40:6:28.text: And why do you worry about clothes? Consider how the lilies of the field grow: They do not labor or spin.

40:6:29.text: Yet I tell you that not even Solomon in all his glory was adorned like one of these.

40:6:3.text: But when you give to the needy, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,

40:6:30.text: If that is how God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace, will He not much more clothe you, O you of little faith?

40:6:31.text: Therefore do not worry, saying, ‘What shall we eat?’ or ‘What shall we drink?’ or ‘What shall we wear?’

40:6:32.text: For the Gentiles strive after all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them.

40:6:33.text: But seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things will be added unto you.

40:6:34.text: Therefore do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself. Today has enough trouble of its own.

40:6:4.text: so that your giving may be in secret. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.

40:6:5.text: And when you pray, do not be like the hypocrites. For they love to pray standing in the synagogues and on the street corners to be seen by men. Truly I tell you, they already have their full reward.

40:6:6.text: But when you pray, go into your inner room, shut your door, and pray to your Father, who is unseen. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.

40:6:7.text: And when you pray, do not babble on like pagans, for they think that by their many words they will be heard.

40:6:8.text: Do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask Him.

40:6:9.text: So then, this is how you should pray: ‘Our Father in heaven, hallowed be Your name.

40:7:1.text: “Do not judge, or you will be judged.

40:7:10.text: Or if he asks for a fish, will give him a snake?

40:7:11.text: So if you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask Him!

40:7:12.text: In everything, then, do to others as you would have them do to you. For this is the essence of the Law and the Prophets.

40:7:13.text: Enter through the narrow gate. For wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction, and many enter through it.

40:7:14.text: But small is the gate and narrow the way that leads to life, and only a few find it.

40:7:15.text: Beware of false prophets. They come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly they are ravenous wolves.

40:7:16.text: By their fruit you will recognize them. Are grapes gathered from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?

40:7:17.text: Likewise, every good tree bears good fruit, but a bad tree bears bad fruit.

40:7:18.text: A good tree cannot bear bad fruit, and a bad tree cannot bear good fruit.

40:7:19.text: Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.

40:7:2.text: For with the same judgment you pronounce, you will be judged; and with the measure you use, it will be measured to you.

40:7:20.text: So then, by their fruit you will recognize them.

40:7:21.text: Not everyone who says to Me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only he who does the will of My Father in heaven.

40:7:22.text: Many will say to Me on that day, ‘Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in Your name, and in Your name drive out demons and perform many miracles?’

40:7:23.text: Then I will tell them plainly, ‘I never knew you; depart from Me, you workers of lawlessness!’

40:7:24.text: Therefore everyone who hears these words of Mine and acts on them is like a wise man who built his house on the rock.

40:7:25.text: The rain fell, the torrents raged, and the winds blew and beat against that house; yet it did not fall, because its foundation was on the rock.

40:7:26.text: But everyone who hears these words of Mine and does not act on them is like a foolish man who built his house on sand.

40:7:27.text: The rain fell, the torrents raged, and the winds blew and beat against that house, and it fell — and great was its collapse!”

40:7:28.text: When Jesus had finished saying these things, the crowds were astonished at His teaching,

40:7:29.text: because He taught as one who had authority, and not as their scribes.

40:7:3.text: Why do you look at the speck in your brother’s eye, but fail to notice the beam in your own eye?

40:7:4.text: How can you say to your brother, ‘Let me take the speck out of your eye,’ while there is still a beam in your own eye?

40:7:5.text: You hypocrite! First take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.

40:7:6.text: Do not give dogs what is holy; do not throw your pearls before swine. If you do, they may trample them under their feet, and then turn and tear you to pieces.

40:7:7.text: Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you.

40:7:8.text: For everyone who asks receives; he who seeks finds; and to him who knocks, the door will be opened.

40:7:9.text: Which of you, if his son asks for bread, will give him a stone?

40:8:1.text: When Jesus came down from the mountain, large crowds followed Him.

40:8:10.text: When Jesus heard this, He marveled and said to those following Him, “Truly I tell you, I have not found anyone in Israel with such great faith.

40:8:11.text: I say to you that many will come from the east and the west to share the banquet with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven.

40:8:12.text: But the sons of the kingdom will be thrown into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.”

40:8:13.text: Then Jesus said to the centurion, “Go! As you have believed, so will it be done for you.” And his servant was healed at that very hour.

40:8:14.text: When Jesus arrived at Peter’s house, He saw Peter’s mother-in-law sick in bed with a fever.

40:8:15.text: So He touched her hand, and the fever left her, and she got up and began to serve them.

40:8:16.text: When evening came, many who were demon-possessed were brought to Jesus, and He drove out the spirits with a word and healed all the sick.

40:8:17.text: This was to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah: “He took on our infirmities and carried our diseases.”

40:8:18.text: When Jesus saw a large crowd around Him, He gave orders to cross to the other side of the sea.

40:8:19.text: And one of the scribes came to Him and said, “Teacher, I will follow You wherever You go.”

40:8:2.text: Suddenly a leper came and knelt before Him, saying, “Lord, if You are willing, You can make me clean.”

40:8:20.text: Jesus replied, “Foxes have dens and birds of the air have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to lay His head.”

40:8:21.text: Another of His disciples requested, “Lord, first let me go and bury my father.”

40:8:22.text: But Jesus told him, “Follow Me, and let the dead bury their own dead.”

40:8:23.text: When He got into the boat, His disciples followed Him.

40:8:24.text: Suddenly a violent storm came up on the sea, so that the boat was engulfed by the waves; but Jesus was sleeping.

40:8:25.text: The disciples went and woke Him, saying, “Lord, save us! We are perishing!”

40:8:26.text: “You of little faith,” Jesus replied, “why are you so afraid?” Then He got up and rebuked the winds and the sea, and it was perfectly calm.

40:8:27.text: The men were amazed and asked, “What kind of man is this? Even the winds and the sea obey Him!”

40:8:28.text: When Jesus arrived on the other side in the region of the Gadarenes, He was met by two demon-possessed men coming from the tombs. They were so violent that no one could pass that way.

40:8:29.text: “What do You want with us, Son of God?” they shouted. “Have You come here to torture us before the appointed time?”

40:8:3.text: Jesus reached out His hand and touched the man. “I am willing,” He said. “Be clean!” And immediately his leprosy was cleansed.

40:8:30.text: In the distance a large herd of pigs was feeding.

40:8:31.text: So the demons begged Jesus, “If You drive us out, send us into the herd of pigs.”

40:8:32.text: “Go!” He told them. So they came out and went into the pigs, and the whole herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea and died in the waters.

40:8:33.text: Those tending the pigs ran off into the town and reported all this, including the account of the demon-possessed men.

40:8:34.text: Then the whole town went out to meet Jesus. And when they saw Him, they begged Him to leave their region.

40:8:4.text: Then Jesus instructed him, “See that you don’t tell anyone. But go, show yourself to the priest and offer the gift prescribed by Moses, as a testimony to them.”

40:8:5.text: When Jesus had entered Capernaum, a centurion came and pleaded with Him,

40:8:6.text: “Lord, my servant lies at home, paralyzed and in terrible agony.”

40:8:7.text: “I will go and heal him,” Jesus replied.

40:8:8.text: The centurion answered, “Lord, I am not worthy to have You come under my roof. But just say the word, and my servant will be healed.

40:8:9.text: For I myself am a man under authority, with soldiers under me. I tell one to go, and he goes; and another to come, and he comes. I tell my servant to do something, and he does it.”

40:9:1.text: Jesus got into a boat, crossed over, and came to His own town.

40:9:10.text: Later, as Jesus was dining at Matthew’s house, many tax collectors and sinners came and ate with Him and His disciples.

40:9:11.text: When the Pharisees saw this, they asked His disciples, “Why does your Teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?”

40:9:12.text: On hearing this, Jesus said, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick.

40:9:13.text: But go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy, not sacrifice.’ For I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners. ”

40:9:14.text: At that time John’s disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Why is it that we and the Pharisees fast so often, but Your disciples do not fast?”

40:9:15.text: Jesus replied, “How can the guests of the bridegroom mourn while He is with them? But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them; then they will fast.

40:9:16.text: No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment. For the patch will pull away from the garment, and a worse tear will result.

40:9:17.text: Neither do men pour new wine into old wineskins. If they do, the skins will burst, the wine will spill, and the wineskins will be ruined. Instead, they pour new wine into new wineskins, and both are preserved.”

40:9:18.text: While Jesus was saying these things, a synagogue leader came and knelt before Him. “My daughter has just died,” he said. “But come and place Your hand on her, and she will live.”

40:9:19.text: So Jesus got up and went with him, along with His disciples.

40:9:2.text: Just then some men brought to Him a paralytic lying on a mat. When Jesus saw their faith, He said to the paralytic, “Take courage, son; your sins are forgiven.”

40:9:20.text: Suddenly a woman who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years came up behind Him and touched the fringe of His cloak.

40:9:21.text: She said to herself, “If only I touch His cloak, I will be healed.”

40:9:22.text: Jesus turned and saw her. “Take courage, daughter,” He said, “your faith has healed you.” And the woman was cured from that very hour.

40:9:23.text: When Jesus entered the house of the synagogue leader, He saw the flute players and the noisy crowd.

40:9:24.text: “Go away,” He told them. “The girl is not dead, but asleep.” And they laughed at Him.

40:9:25.text: After the crowd had been put outside, Jesus went in and took the girl by the hand, and she got up.

40:9:26.text: And the news about this spread throughout that region.

40:9:27.text: As Jesus went on from there, two blind men followed Him, crying out, “Have mercy on us, Son of David!”

40:9:28.text: After Jesus had entered the house, the blind men came to Him. “Do you believe that I am able to do this?” He asked. “Yes, Lord,” they answered.

40:9:29.text: Then He touched their eyes and said, “According to your faith will it be done to you.”

40:9:3.text: On seeing this, some of the scribes said to themselves, “This man is blaspheming!”

40:9:30.text: And their eyes were opened. Jesus warned them sternly, “See that no one finds out about this!”

40:9:31.text: But they went out and spread the news about Him throughout the land.

40:9:32.text: As they were leaving, a demon-possessed man who was mute was brought to Jesus.

40:9:33.text: And when the demon had been driven out, the man began to speak. The crowds were amazed and said, “Nothing like this has ever been seen in Israel!”

40:9:34.text: But the Pharisees said, “It is by the prince of demons that He drives out demons.”

40:9:35.text: Jesus went through all the towns and villages, teaching in their synagogues, preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every disease and sickness.

40:9:36.text: When He saw the crowds, He was moved with compassion for them, because they were harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd.

40:9:37.text: Then He said to His disciples, “The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few.

40:9:38.text: Ask the Lord of the harvest, therefore, to send out workers into His harvest.”

40:9:4.text: But Jesus knew what they were thinking and said, “Why do you harbor evil in your hearts?

40:9:5.text: Which is easier: to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk?’

40:9:6.text: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins...” Then He said to the paralytic, “Get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”

40:9:7.text: And the man got up and went home.

40:9:8.text: When the crowds saw this, they were filled with awe and glorified God, who had given such authority to men.

40:9:9.text: As Jesus went on from there, He saw a man named Matthew sitting at the tax booth. “Follow Me,” He told him, and Matthew got up and followed Him.

41:10:1.text: Then Jesus left that place and went into the region of Judea, beyond the Jordan. Again the crowds came to Him and He taught them, as was His custom.

41:10:10.text: When they were back inside the house, the disciples asked Jesus about this matter.

41:10:11.text: So He told them, “Whoever divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery against her.

41:10:12.text: And if a woman divorces her husband and marries another man, she commits adultery.”

41:10:13.text: Now people were bringing the little children to Jesus for Him to place His hands on them, and the disciples rebuked those who brought them.

41:10:14.text: But when Jesus saw this, He was indignant and told them, “Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them! For the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.

41:10:15.text: Truly I tell you, anyone who does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it.”

41:10:16.text: And He took the children in His arms, placed His hands on them, and blessed them.

41:10:17.text: As Jesus started on His way, a man ran up and knelt before Him. “Good Teacher,” he asked, “what must I do to inherit eternal life?”

41:10:18.text: “Why do you call Me good?” Jesus replied. “No one is good except God alone.

41:10:19.text: You know the commandments: ‘Do not murder, do not commit adultery, do not steal, do not bear false witness, do not cheat others, honor your father and mother.’ ”

41:10:2.text: Some Pharisees came to test Him. “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?” they inquired.

41:10:20.text: “Teacher,” he replied, “all these I have kept from my youth.”

41:10:21.text: Jesus looked at him, loved him, and said to him, “There is one thing you lack: Go, sell everything you own and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow Me. ”

41:10:22.text: But the man was saddened by these words and went away in sorrow, because he had great wealth.

41:10:23.text: Then Jesus looked around and said to His disciples, “How hard it is for the rich to enter the kingdom of God!”

41:10:24.text: And the disciples were amazed at His words. But Jesus said to them again, “Children, how hard it is to enter the kingdom of God!

41:10:25.text: It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.”

41:10:26.text: They were even more astonished and said to one another, “Who then can be saved?”

41:10:27.text: Jesus looked at them and said, “With man this is impossible, but not with God. For all things are possible with God.”

41:10:28.text: Peter began to say to Him, “Look, we have left everything and followed You.”

41:10:29.text: “Truly I tell you,” Jesus replied, “no one who has left home or brothers or sisters or mother or father or children or fields for My sake and for the gospel

41:10:3.text: “What did Moses command you?” He replied.

41:10:30.text: will fail to receive a hundredfold in the present age — houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and fields, along with persecutions — and in the age to come, eternal life.

41:10:31.text: But many who are first will be last, and the last will be first.”

41:10:32.text: As they were going up the road to Jerusalem, Jesus was walking ahead of them. The disciples were amazed, but those who followed were afraid. Again Jesus took the Twelve aside and began to tell them what was going to happen to Him:

41:10:33.text: “Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be delivered over to the chief priests and scribes. They will condemn Him to death and will deliver Him over to the Gentiles,

41:10:34.text: who will mock Him and spit on Him and flog Him and kill Him. And after three days He will rise again.”

41:10:35.text: Then James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came to Jesus and declared, “Teacher, we want You to do for us whatever we ask.”

41:10:36.text: “What do you want Me to do for you?” He inquired.

41:10:37.text: They answered, “Grant that one of us may sit at Your right hand and the other at Your left in Your glory.”

41:10:38.text: “You do not know what you are asking,” Jesus replied. “Can you drink the cup I will drink, or be baptized with the baptism I will undergo?”

41:10:39.text: “We can,” the brothers answered. “You will drink the cup that I drink,” Jesus said, “and you will be baptized with the baptism that I undergo.

41:10:4.text: They answered, “Moses permitted a man to write his wife a certificate of divorce and send her away.”

41:10:40.text: But to sit at My right or left is not Mine to grant. These seats belong to those for whom they have been prepared.”

41:10:41.text: When the ten heard about this, they became indignant with James and John.

41:10:42.text: So Jesus called them together and said, “You know that those regarded as rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their superiors exercise authority over them.

41:10:43.text: But it shall not be this way among you. Instead, whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant,

41:10:44.text: and whoever wants to be first must be the slave of all.

41:10:45.text: For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many.”

41:10:46.text: Next, they came to Jericho. And as Jesus and His disciples were leaving Jericho with a large crowd, a blind beggar named Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus, was sitting beside the road.

41:10:47.text: When he heard that it was Jesus of Nazareth, he began to cry out, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”

41:10:48.text: Many people admonished him to be silent, but he cried out all the louder, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”

41:10:49.text: Jesus stopped and said, “Call him.” So they called the blind man. “Take courage!” they said. “Get up! He is calling for you.”

41:10:5.text: But Jesus told them, “Moses wrote this commandment for you because of your hardness of heart.

41:10:50.text: Throwing off his cloak, Bartimaeus jumped up and came to Jesus.

41:10:51.text: “What do you want Me to do for you?” Jesus asked. “Rabboni,” said the blind man, “let me see again.”

41:10:52.text: “Go,” said Jesus, “your faith has healed you.” And immediately he received his sight and followed Jesus along the road.

41:10:6.text: However, from the beginning of creation, ‘God made them male and female.’

41:10:7.text: ‘For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife,

41:10:8.text: and the two will become one flesh.’ So they are no longer two, but one flesh.

41:10:9.text: Therefore what God has joined together, let man not separate.”

41:11:1.text: As they approached Jerusalem and came to Bethphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent out two of His disciples

41:11:10.text: “Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David!” “Hosanna in the highest!”

41:11:11.text: Then Jesus entered Jerusalem and went into the temple courts. He looked around at everything, but since it was already late, He went out to Bethany with the Twelve.

41:11:12.text: The next day, when they had left Bethany, Jesus was hungry.

41:11:13.text: Seeing in the distance a fig tree in leaf, He went to see if there was any fruit on it. But when He reached it, He found nothing on it except leaves, since it was not the season for figs.

41:11:14.text: Then He said to the tree, “May no one ever eat of your fruit again.” And His disciples heard this statement.

41:11:15.text: When they arrived in Jerusalem, Jesus entered the temple courts and began to drive out those who were buying and selling there. He overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling doves.

41:11:16.text: And He would not allow anyone to carry merchandise through the temple courts.

41:11:17.text: Then Jesus began to teach them, and He declared, “Is it not written: ‘My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations’ ? But you have made it ‘a den of robbers.’ ”

41:11:18.text: When the chief priests and scribes heard this, they looked for a way to kill Him. For they were afraid of Him, because the whole crowd was astonished at His teaching.

41:11:19.text: And when evening came, Jesus and His disciples went out of the city.

41:11:2.text: and said to them, “Go into the village ahead of you, and as soon as you enter it, you will find a colt tied there, on which no one has ever sat. Untie it and bring it here.

41:11:20.text: As they were walking back in the morning, they saw the fig tree withered from its roots.

41:11:21.text: Peter remembered it and said, “Look, Rabbi! The fig tree You cursed has withered.”

41:11:22.text: “Have faith in God,” Jesus said to them.

41:11:23.text: “Truly I tell you that if anyone says to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,’ and has no doubt in his heart but believes that it will happen, it will be done for him.

41:11:24.text: Therefore I tell you, whatever you ask for in prayer, believe that you have received it, and it will be yours.

41:11:25.text: And when you stand to pray, if you hold anything against another, forgive it, so that your Father in heaven will forgive your trespasses as well. ”

41:11:27.text: After their return to Jerusalem, Jesus was walking in the temple courts, and the chief priests, scribes, and elders came up to Him.

41:11:28.text: “By what authority are You doing these things?” they asked. “And who gave You the authority to do them?”

41:11:29.text: “I will ask you one question,” Jesus replied, “and if you answer Me, I will tell you by what authority I am doing these things.

41:11:3.text: If anyone asks, ‘Why are you doing this?’ tell him, ‘The Lord needs it and will return it shortly.’ ”

41:11:30.text: John’s baptism — was it from heaven or from men? Answer Me!”

41:11:31.text: They deliberated among themselves what they should answer: “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ He will ask, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’

41:11:32.text: But if we say, ‘From men’ ...” they were afraid of the people, for they all held that John truly was a prophet.

41:11:33.text: So they answered, “We do not know.” And Jesus replied, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things.”

41:11:4.text: So they went and found the colt outside in the street, tied at a doorway. They untied it,

41:11:5.text: and some who were standing there asked, “Why are you untying the colt?”

41:11:6.text: The disciples answered as Jesus had instructed them, and the people gave them permission.

41:11:7.text: Then they led the colt to Jesus and threw their cloaks over it, and He sat on it.

41:11:8.text: Many in the crowd spread their cloaks on the road, while others spread branches they had cut from the fields.

41:11:9.text: The ones who went ahead and those who followed were shouting: “Hosanna!” “Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!”

41:12:1.text: Then Jesus began to speak to them in parables: “A man planted a vineyard. He put a wall around it, dug a wine vat, and built a watchtower. Then he rented it out to some tenants and went away on a journey.

41:12:10.text: Have you never read this Scripture: ‘The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.

41:12:11.text: This is from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes’ ?”

41:12:12.text: At this, the leaders sought to arrest Jesus, for they knew that He had spoken this parable against them. But fearing the crowd, they left Him and went away.

41:12:13.text: Later, they sent some of the Pharisees and Herodians to catch Jesus in His words.

41:12:14.text: “Teacher,” they said, “we know that You are honest and seek favor from no one. Indeed, You are impartial and teach the way of God in accordance with the truth. Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar or not? Should we pay them or not?”

41:12:15.text: But Jesus saw through their hypocrisy and said, “Why are you testing Me? Bring Me a denarius to inspect.”

41:12:16.text: So they brought it, and He asked them, “Whose image is this? And whose inscription?” “Caesar’s,” they answered.

41:12:17.text: Then Jesus told them, “Give to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s.” And they marveled at Him.

41:12:18.text: Then the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to Jesus and questioned Him:

41:12:19.text: “Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if a man’s brother dies and leaves a wife but no children, the man is to marry his brother’s widow and raise up offspring for him.

41:12:2.text: At harvest time, he sent a servant to the tenants to collect his share of the fruit of the vineyard.

41:12:20.text: Now there were seven brothers. The first one married and died, leaving no children.

41:12:21.text: Then the second one married the widow, but he also died and left no children. And the third did likewise.

41:12:22.text: In this way, none of the seven left any children. And last of all, the woman died.

41:12:23.text: In the resurrection, then, whose wife will she be? For all seven were married to her.”

41:12:24.text: Jesus said to them, “Aren’t you mistaken, because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God?

41:1:42.text: And immediately the leprosy left him, and the man was cleansed.

41:1:7.text: And he began to proclaim: “After me will come One more powerful than I, the straps of whose sandals I am not worthy to stoop down and untie.

41:2:10.text: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins...” He said to the paralytic,

41:2:16.text: When the scribes who were Pharisees saw Jesus eating with these people, they asked His disciples, “Why does He eat with tax collectors and sinners?”

41:2:17.text: On hearing this, Jesus told them, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick. I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners.”

41:2:18.text: Now John’s disciples and the Pharisees were often fasting. So people came to Jesus and asked, “Why don’t Your disciples fast like John’s disciples and those of the Pharisees?”

41:2:23.text: One Sabbath Jesus was passing through the grainfields, and His disciples began to pick the heads of grain as they walked along.

41:2:8.text: At once Jesus knew in His spirit that they were thinking this way within themselves. “Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?” He asked.

41:2:9.text: “Which is easier: to say to a paralytic, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up, pick up your mat, and walk’ ?

41:3:1.text: Once again Jesus entered the synagogue, and a man with a withered hand was there.

41:3:10.text: For He had healed so many that all who had diseases were pressing forward to touch Him.

41:3:21.text: When His family heard about this, they went out to take custody of Him, saying, “He is out of His mind.”

41:3:22.text: And the scribes who had come down from Jerusalem were saying, “He is possessed by Beelzebul, ” and, “By the prince of the demons He drives out demons.”

41:3:23.text: So Jesus called them together and began to speak to them in parables: “How can Satan drive out Satan?

41:3:24.text: If a kingdom is divided against itself, it cannot stand.

41:3:25.text: If a house is divided against itself, it cannot stand.

41:3:26.text: And if Satan is divided and rises against himself, he cannot stand; his end has come.

41:3:27.text: Indeed, no one can enter a strong man’s house to steal his possessions unless he first ties up the strong man. Then he can plunder his house.

41:3:28.text: Truly I tell you, the sons of men will be forgiven all sins and blasphemies, as many as they utter.

41:3:29.text: But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will never be forgiven; he is guilty of eternal sin.”

41:3:3.text: Then Jesus said to the man with the withered hand, “Stand up among us.”

41:3:30.text: Jesus made this statement because they were saying, “He has an unclean spirit.”

41:3:31.text: Then Jesus’ mother and brothers came and stood outside. They sent someone in to summon Him,

41:3:32.text: and a crowd was sitting around Him. “Look,” He was told, “Your mother and brothers are outside, asking for You.”

41:3:33.text: But Jesus replied, “Who are My mother and My brothers?”

41:3:34.text: Looking at those seated in a circle around Him, He said, “Here are My mother and My brothers!

41:3:4.text: And He asked them, “Which is lawful on the Sabbath: to do good or to do evil, to save life or to destroy it?” But they were silent.

41:3:5.text: Jesus looked around at them with anger and sorrow at their hardness of heart. Then He said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” So he stretched it out, and it was restored.

41:3:6.text: At this, the Pharisees went out and began plotting with the Herodians how they might kill Jesus.

41:3:7.text: So Jesus withdrew with His disciples to the sea, accompanied by a large crowd from Galilee, Judea,

41:3:8.text: Jerusalem, Idumea, the region beyond the Jordan, and the vicinity of Tyre and Sidon. The large crowd came to Him when they heard what great things He was doing.

41:3:9.text: Jesus asked His disciples to have a boat ready for Him so that the crowd would not crush Him.

41:4:1.text: Once again Jesus began to teach beside the sea, and such a large crowd gathered around Him that He got into a boat and sat in it, while all the people crowded along the shore.

41:4:18.text: Others are like the seeds sown among the thorns. They hear the word,

41:4:27.text: Night and day he sleeps and wakes, and the seed sprouts and grows, though he knows not how.

41:4:28.text: All by itself the earth produces a crop — first the stalk, then the head, then grain that ripens within.

41:4:3.text: “Listen! A farmer went out to sow his seed.

41:4:35.text: When that evening came, He said to His disciples, “Let us cross to the other side.”

41:4:37.text: Soon a violent windstorm came up, and the waves were breaking over the boat, so that it was being swamped.

41:4:38.text: But Jesus was in the stern, sleeping on the cushion. So they woke Him and said, “Teacher, don’t You care that we are perishing?”

41:4:39.text: Then Jesus got up and rebuked the wind and the sea. “Silence!” He commanded. “Be still!” And the wind died down, and it was perfectly calm.

41:4:4.text: And as he was sowing, some seed fell along the path, and the birds came and devoured it.

41:4:40.text: “Why are you so afraid?” He asked. “Do you still have no faith?”

41:4:41.text: Overwhelmed with fear, they asked one another, “Who is this, that even the wind and the sea obey Him?”

41:4:5.text: Some fell on rocky ground, where it did not have much soil. It sprang up quickly because the soil was shallow.

41:4:6.text: But when the sun rose, the seedlings were scorched, and they withered because they had no root.

41:4:7.text: Other seed fell among thorns, which grew up and choked the seedlings, and they yielded no crop.

41:5:12.text: So the demons begged Jesus, “Send us to the pigs, so that we may enter them.”

41:5:13.text: He gave them permission, and the unclean spirits came out and went into the pigs, and the herd of about two thousand rushed down the steep bank into the sea and drowned in the water.

41:5:14.text: Those tending the pigs ran off and reported this in the town and countryside, and the people went out to see what had happened.

41:5:15.text: When they came to Jesus, they saw the man who had been possessed by the legion of demons sitting there, clothed and in his right mind; and they were afraid.

41:5:16.text: Those who had seen it described what had happened to the demon-possessed man and also to the pigs.

41:5:17.text: And the people began to beg Jesus to leave their region.

41:5:18.text: As He was getting into the boat, the man who had been possessed by the demons begged to go with Him.

41:5:19.text: But Jesus would not allow him. “Go home to your own people,” He said, “and tell them how much the Lord has done for you, and what mercy He has shown you.”

41:5:2.text: As soon as Jesus got out of the boat, He was met by a man with an unclean spirit, who was coming from the tombs.

41:5:20.text: So the man went away and began to proclaim throughout the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him. And everyone was amazed.

41:5:21.text: When Jesus had again crossed by boat to the other side, a large crowd gathered around Him beside the sea.

41:5:22.text: A synagogue leader named Jairus arrived, and seeing Jesus, he fell at His feet

41:5:23.text: and pleaded with Him urgently, “My little daughter is near death. Please come and place Your hands on her, so that she will be healed and live.”

41:5:24.text: So Jesus went with him, and a large crowd followed and pressed around Him.

41:5:25.text: And a woman was there who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years.

41:5:26.text: She had borne much agony under the care of many physicians and had spent all she had, but to no avail. Instead, her condition had only grown worse.

41:5:27.text: When the woman heard about Jesus, she came up through the crowd behind Him and touched His cloak.

41:5:28.text: For she kept saying, “If only I touch His garments, I will be healed.”

41:5:29.text: Immediately her bleeding stopped, and she sensed in her body that she was healed of her affliction.

41:5:3.text: This man had been living in the tombs and could no longer be restrained, even with chains.

41:5:30.text: At once Jesus was aware that power had gone out from Him. Turning to the crowd, He asked, “Who touched My garments?”

41:5:31.text: His disciples answered, “You can see the crowd pressing in on You, and yet You ask, ‘Who touched Me?’ ”

41:5:32.text: But He kept looking around to see who had done this.

41:5:33.text: Then the woman, knowing what had happened to her, came and fell down before Him trembling in fear, and she told Him the whole truth.

41:5:34.text: “Daughter,” said Jesus, “your faith has healed you. Go in peace and be free of your affliction.”

41:5:35.text: While He was still speaking, messengers from the house of Jairus arrived and said, “Your daughter is dead; why bother the Teacher anymore?”

41:5:36.text: But Jesus overheard their conversation and said to Jairus, “Do not be afraid; just believe.”

41:5:37.text: And He did not allow anyone to accompany Him except Peter, James, and John the brother of James.

41:5:38.text: When they arrived at the house of the synagogue leader, Jesus saw the commotion and the people weeping and wailing loudly.

41:5:39.text: He went inside and asked, “Why all this commotion and weeping? The child is not dead, but asleep.”

41:5:4.text: Though he was often bound with chains and shackles, he had broken the chains and shattered the shackles. Now there was no one with the strength to subdue him.

41:5:42.text: Immediately the girl got up and began to walk around. She was twelve years old, and at once they were utterly astounded.

41:5:43.text: Then Jesus gave strict orders that no one should know about this, and He told them to give her something to eat.

41:6:27.text: So without delay, the king commanded that John’s head be brought in. He sent an executioner, who went and beheaded him in the prison.

41:6:31.text: And He said to them, “Come with Me privately to a solitary place, and let us rest for a while.” For many people were coming and going, and they did not even have time to eat.

41:6:38.text: “Go and see how many loaves you have,” He told them. And after checking, they said, “Five — and two fish.”

41:6:39.text: Then Jesus directed them to have the people sit in groups on the green grass.

41:6:4.text: Then Jesus said to them, “Only in his hometown, among his relatives, and in his own household is a prophet without honor.”

41:6:40.text: So they sat down in groups of hundreds and fifties.

41:6:41.text: Taking the five loaves and the two fish and looking up to heaven, Jesus spoke a blessing and broke the loaves. Then He gave them to His disciples to set before the people. And He divided the two fish among them all.

41:6:42.text: They all ate and were satisfied,
