43:8:28.text: So Jesus said, “When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am He, and that I do nothing on My own, but speak exactly what the Father has taught Me.

43:8:29.text: He who sent Me is with Me. He has not left Me alone, because I always do what pleases Him.”

43:8:3.text: The scribes and Pharisees, however, brought to Him a woman caught in adultery. They made her stand before them

43:8:30.text: As Jesus spoke these things, many believed in Him.

43:8:31.text: So He said to the Jews who had believed Him, “If you continue in My word, you are truly My disciples.

43:8:32.text: Then you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.”

43:8:33.text: “We are Abraham’s descendants,” they answered. “We have never been slaves to anyone. How can You say we will be set free?”

43:8:34.text: Jesus replied, “Truly, truly, I tell you, everyone who sins is a slave to sin.

43:8:35.text: A slave is not a permanent member of the family, but a son belongs to it forever.

43:8:36.text: So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed.

43:8:37.text: I know you are Abraham’s descendants, but you are trying to kill Me because My word has no place within you.

43:8:38.text: I speak of what I have seen in the presence of the Father, and you do what you have heard from your father.”

43:8:39.text: “Abraham is our father,” they replied. “If you were children of Abraham,” said Jesus, “you would do the works of Abraham.

43:8:4.text: and said, “Teacher, this woman was caught in the act of adultery.

43:8:40.text: But now you are trying to kill Me, a man who has told you the truth that I heard from God. Abraham never did such a thing.

43:8:41.text: You are doing the works of your father.” “We are not illegitimate children,” they declared. “Our only Father is God Himself.”

43:8:42.text: Jesus said to them, “If God were your Father, you would love Me, for I have come here from God. I have not come on My own, but He sent Me.

43:8:43.text: Why do you not understand what I am saying? It is because you are unable to accept My message.

43:8:44.text: You belong to your father, the devil, and you want to carry out his desires. He was a murderer from the beginning, refusing to uphold the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks his native language, because he is a liar and the father of lies.

43:8:45.text: But because I speak the truth, you do not believe Me!

43:8:46.text: Which of you can prove Me guilty of sin? If I speak the truth, why do you not believe Me?

43:8:47.text: Whoever belongs to God hears the words of God. The reason you do not hear is that you do not belong to God.”

43:8:48.text: The Jews answered Him, “Are we not right to say that You are a Samaritan and You have a demon?”

43:8:49.text: “I do not have a demon,” Jesus replied, “but I honor My Father, and you dishonor Me.

43:8:5.text: In the Law Moses commanded us to stone such a woman. So what do You say?”

43:8:50.text: I do not seek My own glory. There is One who seeks it, and He is the Judge.

43:8:51.text: Truly, truly, I tell you, if anyone keeps My word, he will never see death.”

43:8:52.text: “Now we know that You have a demon!” declared the Jews. “Abraham died, and so did the prophets, yet You say that anyone who keeps Your word will never taste death.

43:8:53.text: Are You greater than our father Abraham? He died, as did the prophets. Who do You claim to be?”

43:8:54.text: Jesus answered, “If I glorify Myself, My glory means nothing. The One who glorifies Me is My Father, of whom you say ‘He is our God.’

43:8:55.text: You do not know Him, but I know Him. If I said I did not know Him, I would be a liar like you. But I do know Him, and I keep His word.

43:8:56.text: Your father Abraham rejoiced that he would see My day. He saw it and was glad.”

43:8:57.text: Then the Jews said to Him, “You are not yet fifty years old, and You have seen Abraham?”

43:8:58.text: “Truly, truly, I tell you,” Jesus declared, “before Abraham was born, I am! ”

43:8:59.text: At this, they picked up stones to throw at Him. But Jesus was hidden and went out of the temple area.

43:8:6.text: They said this to test Him, in order to have a basis for accusing Him. But Jesus bent down and began to write on the ground with His finger.

43:8:7.text: When they continued to question Him, He straightened up and said to them, “Let him who is without sin among you be the first to cast a stone at her.”

43:8:8.text: And again He bent down and wrote on the ground.

43:8:9.text: When they heard this, they began to go away one by one, beginning with the older ones, until only Jesus was left, with the woman standing there.

43:9:1.text: Now as Jesus was passing by, He saw a man blind from birth,

43:9:10.text: “How then were your eyes opened?” they asked.

43:9:11.text: He answered, “The man they call Jesus made some mud and anointed my eyes, and He told me to go to Siloam and wash. So I went and washed and received my sight.”

43:9:12.text: “Where is He?” they asked. “I do not know,” he answered.

43:9:13.text: They brought to the Pharisees the man who had been blind.

43:9:14.text: Now the day on which Jesus had made the mud and opened his eyes was a Sabbath.

43:9:15.text: So the Pharisees also asked him how he had received his sight. The man answered, “He put mud on my eyes, and I washed, and now I can see.”

43:9:16.text: Because of this, some of the Pharisees said, “This man is not from God, for He does not keep the Sabbath.” But others said, “How can a sinful man perform such signs?” And there was division among them.

43:9:17.text: So once again they asked the man who had been blind, “What do you say about Him, since it was your eyes He opened?” “He is a prophet,” the man replied.

43:9:18.text: The Jews still did not believe that the man had been blind and had received his sight until they summoned his parents

43:9:19.text: and asked, “Is this your son, the one you say was born blind? So how is it that he can now see?”

43:9:2.text: and His disciples asked Him, “Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he was born blind?”

43:9:20.text: His parents answered, “We know he is our son, and we know he was born blind.

43:9:21.text: But how he can now see or who opened his eyes, we do not know. Ask him. He is old enough to speak for himself.”

43:9:22.text: His parents said this because they were afraid of the Jews. For the Jews had already determined that anyone who confessed Jesus as the Christ would be put out of the synagogue.

43:9:23.text: That was why his parents said, “He is old enough. Ask him.”

43:9:24.text: So a second time they called for the man who had been blind and said, “Give glory to God! We know that this man is a sinner.”

43:9:25.text: He answered, “Whether He is a sinner I do not know. There is one thing I do know: I was blind, but now I see!”

43:9:26.text: “What did He do to you?” they asked. “How did He open your eyes?”

43:9:27.text: He replied, “I already told you, and you did not listen. Why do you want to hear it again? Do you also want to become His disciples?”

43:9:28.text: Then they heaped insults on him and said, “You are His disciple; we are disciples of Moses.

43:9:29.text: We know that God spoke to Moses, but we do not know where this man is from.”

43:9:3.text: Jesus answered, “Neither this man nor his parents sinned, but this happened so that the works of God would be displayed in him.

43:9:30.text: “That is remarkable indeed!” the man said. “You do not know where He is from, and yet He opened my eyes.

43:9:31.text: We know that God does not listen to sinners, but He does listen to the one who worships Him and does His will.

43:9:32.text: Never before has anyone heard of opening the eyes of a man born blind.

43:9:33.text: If this man were not from God, He could do no such thing.”

43:9:34.text: They replied, “You were born in utter sin, and you are instructing us?” And they threw him out.

43:9:35.text: When Jesus heard that they had thrown him out, He found the man and said, “Do you believe in the Son of Man?”

43:9:36.text: “Who is He, Sir?” he replied. “Tell me so that I may believe in Him.”

43:9:37.text: “You have already seen Him,” Jesus answered. “He is the One speaking with you.”

43:9:38.text: “Lord, I believe,” he said. And he worshiped Jesus.

43:9:39.text: Then Jesus declared, “For judgment I have come into this world, so that the blind may see and those who see may become blind.”

43:9:4.text: While it is daytime, we must do the works of Him who sent Me. Night is coming, when no one can work.

43:9:40.text: Some of the Pharisees who were with Him heard this, and they asked Him, “Are we blind too?”

43:9:41.text: “If you were blind,” Jesus replied, “you would not be guilty of sin. But since you claim you can see, your guilt remains.”

43:9:5.text: While I am in the world, I am the light of the world.”

43:9:6.text: When Jesus had said this, He spit on the ground, made some mud, and applied it to the man’s eyes.

43:9:7.text: Then He told him, “Go, wash in the Pool of Siloam” (which means “Sent”). So the man went and washed, and came back seeing.

43:9:8.text: At this, his neighbors and those who had formerly seen him begging began to ask, “Isn’t this the man who used to sit and beg?”

43:9:9.text: Some claimed that he was, but others said, “No, he just looks like him.” But the man kept saying, “I am the one.”

44:10:1.text: At Caesarea there was a man named Cornelius, a centurion in what was called the Italian Regiment.

44:10:10.text: He became hungry and wanted something to eat, but while the meal was being prepared, he fell into a trance.

44:10:11.text: He saw heaven open and something like a large sheet being let down to earth by its four corners.

44:10:12.text: It contained all kinds of four-footed animals and reptiles of the earth, as well as birds of the air.

44:10:13.text: Then a voice said to him: “Get up, Peter, kill and eat!”

44:10:14.text: “No, Lord!” Peter answered. “I have never eaten anything impure or unclean.”

44:10:15.text: The voice spoke to him a second time: “Do not call anything impure that God has made clean.”

44:10:16.text: This happened three times, and all at once the sheet was taken back up into heaven.

44:10:17.text: While Peter was puzzling over the meaning of the vision, the men sent by Cornelius found Simon’s house and approached the gate.

44:10:18.text: They called out to ask if Simon called Peter was staying there.

44:10:19.text: As Peter continued to reflect on the vision, the Spirit said to him, “Behold, three men are looking for you.

44:10:2.text: He and all his household were devout and God-fearing. He gave generously to the people and prayed to God regularly.

44:10:20.text: So get up! Go downstairs and accompany them without hesitation, because I have sent them.”

44:10:21.text: So Peter went down to the men and said, “Here am I, the one you are looking for. Why have you come?”

44:10:22.text: “Cornelius the centurion has sent us,” they said. “He is a righteous and God-fearing man with a good reputation among the whole Jewish nation. A holy angel instructed him to request your presence in his home so he could hear a message from you.”

44:10:23.text: So Peter invited them in as his guests. And the next day he got ready and went with them, accompanied by some of the brothers from Joppa.

44:10:24.text: The following day he arrived in Caesarea, where Cornelius was expecting them and had called together his relatives and close friends.

44:10:25.text: As Peter was about to enter, Cornelius met him and fell at his feet to worship him.

44:10:26.text: But Peter helped him up. “Stand up,” he said, “I am only a man myself.”

44:10:27.text: As Peter talked with him, he went inside and found many people gathered together.

44:10:28.text: He said to them, “You know how unlawful it is for a Jew to associate with a foreigner or visit him. But God has shown me that I should not call any man impure or unclean.

44:10:29.text: So when I was invited, I came without objection. I ask, then, why have you sent for me?”

44:10:3.text: One day at about the ninth hour, he had a clear vision of an angel of God who came to him and said, “Cornelius!”

44:10:30.text: Cornelius answered: “Four days ago I was in my house praying at this, the ninth hour. Suddenly a man in radiant clothing stood before me

44:10:31.text: and said, ‘Cornelius, your prayer has been heard, and your gifts to the poor have been remembered before God.

44:10:32.text: Therefore send to Joppa for Simon, who is called Peter. He is a guest in the home of Simon the tanner, by the sea.’

44:10:33.text: So I sent for you immediately, and you were kind enough to come. Now then, we are all here in the presence of God to listen to everything the Lord has instructed you to tell us.”

44:10:34.text: Then Peter began to speak: “I now truly understand that God does not show favoritism,

44:10:35.text: but welcomes those from every nation who fear Him and do what is right.

44:10:36.text: He has sent this message to the people of Israel, proclaiming the gospel of peace through Jesus Christ, who is Lord of all.

44:10:37.text: You yourselves know what has happened throughout Judea, beginning in Galilee with the baptism that John proclaimed:

44:10:38.text: how God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and with power, and how Jesus went around doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, because God was with Him.

44:10:39.text: We are witnesses of all that He did, both in the land of the Jews and in Jerusalem. And although they put Him to death by hanging Him on a tree,

44:10:4.text: Cornelius stared at him in fear and asked, “What is it, Lord?” The angel answered, “Your prayers and gifts to the poor have ascended as a memorial offering before God.

44:10:40.text: God raised Him up on the third day and caused Him to be seen —

44:10:41.text: not by all the people, but by the witnesses God had chosen beforehand, by us who ate and drank with Him after He rose from the dead.

44:10:42.text: And He commanded us to preach to the people and to testify that He is the One appointed by God to judge the living and the dead.

44:10:43.text: All the prophets testify about Him that everyone who believes in Him receives forgiveness of sins through His name.”

44:10:44.text: While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell upon all who heard his message.

44:10:45.text: All the circumcised believers who had accompanied Peter were astounded that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on the Gentiles.

44:10:46.text: For they heard them speaking in tongues and exalting God. Then Peter said,

44:10:47.text: “Can anyone withhold the water to baptize these people? They have received the Holy Spirit just as we have!”

44:10:48.text: So he ordered that they be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they asked him to stay for a few days.

44:10:5.text: Now send men to Joppa to call for a man named Simon who is called Peter.

44:10:6.text: He is staying with Simon the tanner, whose house is by the sea. ”

44:10:7.text: When the angel who spoke to him had gone, Cornelius called two of his servants and a devout soldier from among his attendants.

44:10:8.text: He explained what had happened and sent them to Joppa.

44:10:9.text: The next day at about the sixth hour, as the men were approaching the city on their journey, Peter went up on the roof to pray.

44:11:1.text: The apostles and brothers throughout Judea soon heard that the Gentiles also had received the word of God.

44:11:10.text: This happened three times, and everything was drawn back up into heaven.

44:11:11.text: Just then three men sent to me from Caesarea stopped at the house where I was staying.

44:11:12.text: The Spirit told me to accompany them without hesitation. These six brothers also went with me, and we entered the man’s home.

44:11:13.text: He told us how he had seen an angel standing in his house and saying, ‘Send to Joppa for Simon who is called Peter.

44:11:14.text: He will convey to you a message by which you and all your household will be saved.’

44:11:15.text: As I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell upon them, just as He had fallen upon us at the beginning.

44:11:16.text: Then I remembered the word of the Lord, as He used to say, ‘John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.’

44:11:17.text: So if God gave them the same gift He gave us who believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I to hinder the work of God?”

44:11:18.text: When they heard this, their objections were put to rest, and they glorified God, saying, “So then, God has granted even the Gentiles repentance unto life.”

44:11:19.text: Meanwhile those scattered by the persecution that began with Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch, speaking the message only to Jews.

44:11:2.text: So when Peter went up to Jerusalem, the circumcised believers took issue with him

44:11:20.text: But some of them, men from Cyprus and Cyrene, went to Antioch and began speaking to the Greeks as well, proclaiming the good news about the Lord Jesus.

44:11:21.text: The hand of the Lord was with them, and a great number of people believed and turned to the Lord.

44:11:22.text: When news of this reached the ears of the church in Jerusalem, they sent Barnabas to Antioch.

44:11:23.text: When he arrived and saw the grace of God, he rejoiced and encouraged them all to abide in the Lord with all their hearts.

44:11:24.text: Barnabas was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and faith, and a great number of people were brought to the Lord.

44:11:25.text: Then Barnabas went to Tarsus to look for Saul,

44:11:26.text: and when he found him, he brought him back to Antioch. So for a full year they met together with the church and taught large numbers of people. The disciples were first called Christians at Antioch.

44:11:27.text: In those days some prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.

44:11:28.text: One of them named Agabus stood up and predicted through the Spirit that a great famine would sweep across the whole world. (This happened under Claudius.)

44:11:29.text: So the disciples, each according to his ability, decided to send relief to the brothers living in Judea.

44:11:3.text: and said, “You visited uncircumcised men and ate with them.”

44:11:30.text: This they did, sending their gifts to the elders with Barnabas and Saul.

44:11:4.text: But Peter began and explained to them the whole sequence of events:

44:11:5.text: “I was in the city of Joppa praying, and in a trance I saw a vision of something like a large sheet being let down from heaven by its four corners, and it came right down to me.

44:11:6.text: I looked at it closely and saw four-footed animals of the earth, wild beasts, reptiles, and birds of the air.

44:11:7.text: Then I heard a voice saying to me, ‘Get up, Peter, kill and eat.’

44:11:8.text: ‘No, Lord,’ I said, ‘for nothing impure or unclean has ever entered my mouth.’

44:11:9.text: But the voice spoke from heaven a second time, ‘Do not call anything impure that God has made clean.’

44:12:1.text: About that time, King Herod reached out to harm some who belonged to the church.

44:12:10.text: They passed the first and second guards and came to the iron gate leading to the city, which opened for them by itself. When they had gone outside and walked the length of one block, the angel suddenly left him.

44:12:11.text: Then Peter came to himself and said, “Now I know for sure that the Lord has sent His angel and rescued me from Herod’s grasp and from everything the Jewish people were anticipating.”

44:12:12.text: And when he had realized this, he went to the house of Mary the mother of John, also called Mark, where many people had gathered together and were praying.

44:12:13.text: He knocked at the outer gate, and a servant girl named Rhoda came to answer it.

44:12:14.text: When she recognized Peter’s voice, she was so overjoyed that she forgot to open the gate, but ran inside and announced, “Peter is standing at the gate!”

44:12:15.text: “You are out of your mind,” they told her. But when she kept insisting it was so, they said, “It must be his angel.”

44:12:16.text: But Peter kept on knocking, and when they opened the door and saw him, they were astounded.

44:12:17.text: Peter motioned with his hand for silence, and he described how the Lord had brought him out of the prison. “Send word to James and to the brothers,” he said, and he left for another place.

44:12:18.text: At daybreak there was no small commotion among the soldiers as to what had become of Peter.

44:12:19.text: After Herod had searched for him unsuccessfully, he examined the guards and ordered that they be executed. Then he went down from Judea to Caesarea and spent some time there.

44:12:2.text: He had James, the brother of John, put to death with the sword.

44:12:20.text: Now Herod was in a furious dispute with the people of Tyre and Sidon, and they convened before him. Having secured the support of Blastus, the king’s chamberlain, they asked for peace, because their region depended on the king’s country for food.

44:12:21.text: On the appointed day, Herod donned his royal robes, sat on his throne, and addressed the people.

44:12:22.text: And they began to shout, “This is the voice of a god, not a man!”

44:12:23.text: Immediately, because Herod did not give glory to God, an angel of the Lord struck him down, and he was eaten by worms and died.

44:12:24.text: But the word of God continued to spread and multiply.

44:12:25.text: When Barnabas and Saul had fulfilled their mission to Jerusalem, they returned, bringing with them John, also called Mark.

44:12:3.text: And seeing that this pleased the Jews, Herod proceeded to seize Peter during the Feast of Unleavened Bread.

44:12:4.text: He arrested him and put him in prison, handing him over to be guarded by four squads of four soldiers each. Herod intended to bring him out to the people after the Passover.

44:12:5.text: So Peter was kept in prison, but the church was fervently praying to God for him.

44:12:6.text: On the night before Herod was to bring him to trial, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains, with sentries standing guard at the entrance to the prison.

44:12:7.text: Suddenly an angel of the Lord appeared and a light shone in the cell. He tapped Peter on the side and woke him up, saying, “Get up quickly.” And the chains fell off his wrists.

44:12:8.text: “Get dressed and put on your sandals,” said the angel. Peter did so, and the angel told him, “Wrap your cloak around you and follow me.”

44:12:9.text: So Peter followed him out, but he was unaware that what the angel was doing was real. He thought he was only seeing a vision.

44:13:1.text: Now in the church at Antioch there were prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen (who had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch), and Saul.

44:13:10.text: and said, “O child of the devil and enemy of all righteousness, you are full of all kinds of deceit and trickery! Will you never stop perverting the straight ways of the Lord?

44:13:11.text: Now look, the hand of the Lord is against you, and for a time you will be blind and unable to see the light of the sun.” Immediately mist and darkness came over him, and he groped about, seeking someone to lead him by the hand.

44:13:12.text: When the proconsul saw what had happened, he believed, for he was astonished at the teaching about the Lord.

44:13:13.text: After setting sail from Paphos, Paul and his companions came to Perga in Pamphylia, where John left them to return to Jerusalem.

44:13:14.text: And from Perga, they traveled inland to Pisidian Antioch, where they entered the synagogue on the Sabbath and sat down.

44:13:15.text: After the reading from the Law and the Prophets, the synagogue leaders sent word to them: “Brothers, if you have a word of encouragement for the people, please speak.”

44:13:16.text: Paul stood up, motioned with his hand, and began to speak: “Men of Israel and you Gentiles who fear God, listen to me!

44:13:17.text: The God of the people of Israel chose our fathers. He made them into a great people during their stay in Egypt, and with an uplifted arm He led them out of that land.

44:13:18.text: He endured their conduct for about forty years in the wilderness.

44:13:19.text: And having vanquished seven nations in Canaan, He gave their land to His people as an inheritance.

44:13:2.text: While they were worshiping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, “Set apart for Me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.”

44:13:20.text: All this took about 450 years. After this, God gave them judges until the time of Samuel the prophet.

44:13:21.text: Then the people asked for a king, and God gave them forty years under Saul son of Kish, from the tribe of Benjamin.

44:13:22.text: After removing Saul, He raised up David as their king and testified about him: ‘I have found David son of Jesse a man after My own heart; he will carry out My will in its entirety.’

44:13:23.text: From the descendants of this man, God has brought to Israel the Savior Jesus, as He promised.

44:13:24.text: Before the arrival of Jesus, John preached a baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel.

44:13:25.text: As John was completing his course, he said, ‘Who do you suppose I am? I am not that One. But He is coming after me whose sandals I am not worthy to untie.’

44:13:26.text: Brothers, children of Abraham, and you Gentiles who fear God, it is to us that this message of salvation has been sent.

44:13:27.text: The people of Jerusalem and their rulers did not recognize Jesus, yet in condemning Him they fulfilled the words of the prophets that are read every Sabbath.

44:13:28.text: And though they found no ground for a death sentence, they asked Pilate to have Him executed.

44:13:29.text: When they had carried out all that was written about Him, they took Him down from the tree and laid Him in a tomb.

44:13:3.text: And after they had fasted and prayed, they laid their hands on them and sent them off.

44:13:30.text: But God raised Him from the dead,

44:13:31.text: and for many days He was seen by those who had accompanied Him from Galilee to Jerusalem. They are now His witnesses to our people.

44:13:32.text: And now we proclaim to you the good news: What God promised our fathers

44:13:33.text: He has fulfilled for us, their children, by raising up Jesus. As it is written in the second Psalm: ‘You are My Son; today I have become Your Father.’

44:13:34.text: In fact, God raised Him from the dead, never to see decay. As He has said: ‘I will give you the holy and sure blessings promised to David.’

44:13:35.text: So also, He says in another Psalm: ‘You will not let Your Holy One see decay.’

44:13:36.text: For when David had served God’s purpose in his own generation, he fell asleep. His body was buried with his fathers and saw decay.

44:13:37.text: But the One whom God raised from the dead did not see decay.

44:13:38.text: Therefore let it be known to you, brothers, that through Jesus the forgiveness of sins is proclaimed to you.

44:13:39.text: Through Him everyone who believes is justified from everything you could not be justified from by the law of Moses.

44:13:4.text: So Barnabas and Saul, sent forth by the Holy Spirit, went down to Seleucia and sailed from there to Cyprus.

44:13:40.text: Watch out, then, that what was spoken by the prophets does not happen to you:

44:13:41.text: ‘Look, you scoffers, wonder and perish! For I am doing a work in your days that you would never believe, even if someone told you.’ ”

44:13:42.text: As Paul and Barnabas were leaving the synagogue, the people urged them to continue this message on the next Sabbath.

44:13:43.text: After the synagogue was dismissed, many of the Jews and devout converts to Judaism followed Paul and Barnabas, who spoke to them and urged them to continue in the grace of God.

44:13:44.text: On the following Sabbath, nearly the whole city gathered to hear the word of the Lord.

44:13:45.text: But when the Jews saw the crowds, they were filled with jealousy, and they blasphemously contradicted what Paul was saying.

44:13:46.text: Then Paul and Barnabas answered them boldly: “It was necessary to speak the word of God to you first. But since you reject it and do not consider yourselves worthy of eternal life, we now turn to the Gentiles.

44:13:47.text: For this is what the Lord has commanded us: ‘I have made you a light for the Gentiles, to bring salvation to the ends of the earth.’ ”

44:13:48.text: When the Gentiles heard this, they rejoiced and glorified the word of the Lord, and all who were appointed for eternal life believed.

44:13:49.text: And the word of the Lord spread throughout that region.

44:13:5.text: When they arrived at Salamis, they proclaimed the word of God in the Jewish synagogues. And John was with them as their helper.

44:13:50.text: The Jews, however, incited the religious women of prominence and the leading men of the city. They stirred up persecution against Paul and Barnabas and drove them out of their district.

44:13:51.text: So they shook the dust off their feet in protest against them and went to Iconium.

44:13:52.text: And the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.

44:13:6.text: They traveled through the whole island as far as Paphos, where they found a Jewish sorcerer and false prophet named Bar-Jesus,

44:13:7.text: an attendant of the proconsul, Sergius Paulus. The proconsul, a man of intelligence, summoned Barnabas and Saul because he wanted to hear the word of God.

44:13:8.text: But Elymas the sorcerer (for that is what his name means) opposed them and tried to turn the proconsul from the faith.

44:13:9.text: Then Saul, who was also called Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, looked directly at Elymas

44:14:1.text: At Iconium, Paul and Barnabas went as usual into the Jewish synagogue, where they spoke so well that a great number of Jews and Greeks believed.

44:14:10.text: In a loud voice Paul called out, “Stand up on your feet!” And the man jumped up and began to walk.

44:14:11.text: When the crowds saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voices in the Lycaonian language: “The gods have come down to us in human form!”

44:14:12.text: Barnabas they called Zeus, and Paul they called Hermes, because he was the chief speaker.

44:14:13.text: The priest of Zeus, whose temple was just outside the city, brought bulls and wreaths to the city gates, hoping to offer a sacrifice along with the crowds.

44:14:14.text: But when the apostles Barnabas and Paul found out about this, they tore their clothes and rushed into the crowd, shouting,

44:14:15.text: “Men, why are you doing this? We too are only men, human like you. We are bringing you good news that you should turn from these worthless things to the living God, who made heaven and earth and sea and everything in them.

44:14:16.text: In past generations, He let all nations go their own way.

44:14:17.text: Yet He has not left Himself without testimony to His goodness: He gives you rain from heaven and fruitful seasons, filling your hearts with food and gladness.”

44:1:20.text: “For it is written in the book of Psalms: ‘May his place be deserted; let there be no one to dwell in it,’ and, ‘May another take his position.’

44:1:21.text: Therefore it is necessary to choose one of the men who have accompanied us the whole time the Lord Jesus went in and out among us,

44:1:22.text: beginning from John’s baptism until the day Jesus was taken up from us. For one of these must become a witness with us of His resurrection.”

44:1:23.text: So they proposed two men: Joseph called Barsabbas (also known as Justus) and Matthias.

44:1:24.text: And they prayed, “Lord, You know everyone’s heart. Show us which of these two You have chosen

44:1:25.text: to take up this ministry and apostleship, which Judas abandoned to go to his rightful place.”

44:1:26.text: Then they cast lots, and the lot fell to Matthias; so he was added to the eleven apostles.

44:1:3.text: After His suffering, He presented Himself to them with many convincing proofs that He was alive. He appeared to them over a span of forty days and spoke about the kingdom of God.

44:1:4.text: And while they were gathered together, He commanded them: “Do not leave Jerusalem, but wait for the gift the Father promised, which you have heard Me discuss.

44:1:5.text: For John baptized with water, but in a few days you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit. ”

44:1:6.text: So when they came together, they asked Him, “Lord, will You at this time restore the kingdom to Israel?”

44:1:7.text: Jesus replied, “It is not for you to know times or seasons that the Father has fixed by His own authority.

44:1:8.text: But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes upon you, and you will be My witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.”

44:1:9.text: After He had said this, they watched as He was taken up, and a cloud hid Him from their sight.

44:20:1.text: When the uproar had ended, Paul sent for the disciples. And after encouraging them, he said goodbye to them and left for Macedonia.

44:20:10.text: But Paul went down, threw himself on the young man, and embraced him. “Do not be alarmed!” he said. “He is still alive!”

44:20:11.text: Then Paul went back upstairs, broke bread, and ate. And after speaking until daybreak, he departed.

44:20:12.text: And the people were greatly relieved to take the boy home alive.

44:20:13.text: We went on ahead to the ship and sailed to Assos, where we were to take Paul aboard. He had arranged this because he was going there on foot.

44:20:14.text: And when he met us at Assos, we took him aboard and went on to Mitylene.

44:20:15.text: Sailing on from there, we arrived the next day opposite Chios. The day after that we arrived at Samos, and on the following day we came to Miletus.

44:20:16.text: Paul had decided to sail past Ephesus to avoid spending time in the province of Asia, because he was in a hurry to reach Jerusalem, if possible, by the day of Pentecost.

44:20:17.text: From Miletus, Paul sent to Ephesus for the elders of the church.

44:20:18.text: When they came to him, he said, “You know how I lived the whole time I was with you, from the first day I arrived in the province of Asia.

44:20:19.text: I served the Lord with great humility and with tears, especially in the trials that came upon me through the plots of the Jews.

44:20:2.text: After traveling through that area and speaking many words of encouragement, he arrived in Greece,

44:20:20.text: I did not shrink back from declaring anything that was helpful to you as I taught you publicly and from house to house,

44:20:21.text: testifying to Jews and Greeks alike about repentance to God and faith in our Lord Jesus Christ.

44:20:22.text: And now, compelled by the Spirit, I am going to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to me there.

44:20:23.text: I only know that in town after town the Holy Spirit warns me that chains and afflictions await me.

44:20:24.text: But I consider my life of no value to me, if only I may finish my course and complete the ministry I have received from the Lord Jesus — the ministry of testifying to the good news of God’s grace.

44:20:25.text: Now I know that none of you among whom I have preached the kingdom will see my face again.

44:20:26.text: Therefore I testify to you this day that I am innocent of the blood of all men.

44:20:27.text: For I did not shrink back from declaring to you the whole will of God.

44:20:28.text: Keep watch over yourselves and the entire flock of which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers. Be shepherds of the church of God, which He purchased with His own blood.

44:20:29.text: I know that after my departure, savage wolves will come in among you and will not spare the flock.

44:20:3.text: where he stayed three months. And when the Jews formed a plot against him as he was about to sail for Syria, he decided to go back through Macedonia.

44:20:30.text: Even from your own number, men will rise up and distort the truth to draw away disciples after them.

44:20:31.text: Therefore be alert and remember that for three years I never stopped warning each of you night and day with tears.

44:20:32.text: And now I commit you to God and to the word of His grace, which can build you up and give you an inheritance among all who are sanctified.

44:20:33.text: I have not coveted anyone’s silver or gold or clothing.

44:20:34.text: You yourselves know that these hands of mine have ministered to my own needs and those of my companions.

44:20:35.text: In everything, I showed you that by this kind of hard work we must help the weak, remembering the words of the Lord Jesus Himself: ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’ ”

44:20:36.text: When Paul had said this, he knelt down with all of them and prayed.

44:20:37.text: They all wept openly as they embraced Paul and kissed him.

44:20:38.text: They were especially grieved by his statement that they would never see his face again. Then they accompanied him to the ship.

44:20:4.text: Paul was accompanied by Sopater son of Pyrrhus from Berea, Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica, Gaius from Derbe, Timothy, and Tychicus and Trophimus from the province of Asia.

44:20:5.text: These men went on ahead and waited for us in Troas.

44:20:6.text: And after the Feast of Unleavened Bread, we sailed from Philippi, and five days later we rejoined them in Troas, where we stayed seven days.

44:20:7.text: On the first day of the week we came together to break bread. Since Paul was ready to leave the next day, he talked to them and kept on speaking until midnight.

44:20:8.text: Now there were many lamps in the upper room where we were gathered.

44:20:9.text: And a certain young man named Eutychus, seated in the window, was sinking into a deep sleep as Paul talked on and on. When he was sound asleep, he fell from the third story and was picked up dead.

44:21:1.text: After we had torn ourselves away from them, we sailed directly to Cos, and the next day on to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.

44:21:10.text: After we had been there several days, a prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.

44:21:11.text: Coming over to us, he took Paul’s belt, bound his own feet and hands, and said, “The Holy Spirit says: ‘In this way the Jews of Jerusalem will bind the owner of this belt and hand him over to the Gentiles.’ ”

44:21:12.text: When we heard this, we and the people there pleaded with Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.

44:21:13.text: Then Paul answered, “Why are you weeping and breaking my heart? I am ready not only to be bound, but also to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.”

44:21:14.text: When he would not be dissuaded, we fell silent and said, “The Lord’s will be done.”

44:21:15.text: After these days, we packed up and went on to Jerusalem.

44:21:16.text: Some of the disciples from Caesarea accompanied us, and they took us to stay at the home of Mnason the Cypriot, an early disciple.

44:21:17.text: When we arrived in Jerusalem, the brothers welcomed us joyfully.

44:21:18.text: The next day Paul went in with us to see James, and all the elders were present.

44:21:19.text: Paul greeted them and recounted one by one the things that God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry.

44:21:2.text: Finding a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, we boarded it and set sail.

44:21:20.text: When they heard this, they glorified God. Then they said to Paul, “You see, brother, how many thousands of Jews have believed, and all of them are zealous for the law.

44:21:21.text: But they are under the impression that you teach all the Jews who live among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children or observe our customs.

44:21:22.text: What then should we do? They will certainly hear that you have come.

44:21:23.text: Therefore do what we advise you. There are four men with us who have taken a vow.

44:21:24.text: Take these men, purify yourself along with them, and pay their expenses so they can have their heads shaved. Then everyone will know that there is no truth to these rumors about you, but that you also live in obedience to the law.

44:21:25.text: As for the Gentile believers, we have written to them our decision that they must abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals, and from sexual immorality.”

44:21:26.text: So the next day Paul took the men and purified himself along with them. Then he entered the temple to give notice of the date when their purification would be complete and the offering would be made for each of them.

44:21:27.text: When the seven days were almost over, some Jews from the province of Asia saw Paul at the temple. They stirred up the whole crowd and seized him,

44:21:28.text: crying out, “Men of Israel, help us! This is the man who teaches everywhere against our people and against our law and against this place. Furthermore, he has brought Greeks into the temple and defiled this holy place.”

44:21:29.text: For they had previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian with him in the city, and they assumed that Paul had brought him into the temple.

44:21:3.text: After sighting Cyprus and passing south of it, we sailed on to Syria and landed at Tyre, where the ship was to unload its cargo.

44:21:30.text: The whole city was stirred up, and the people rushed together. They seized Paul and dragged him out of the temple, and at once the gates were shut.

44:21:31.text: While they were trying to kill him, the commander of the Roman regiment received a report that all Jerusalem was in turmoil.

44:21:32.text: Immediately he took some soldiers and centurions and ran down to the crowd. When the people saw the commander and the soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.

44:21:33.text: The commander came up and arrested Paul, ordering that he be bound with two chains. Then he asked who he was and what he had done.

44:21:34.text: Some in the crowd were shouting one thing, and some another. And since the commander could not get at the truth because of the uproar, he ordered that Paul be brought into the barracks.

44:21:35.text: When Paul reached the steps, he had to be carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the mob.

44:21:36.text: For the crowd that followed him kept shouting, “Away with him!”

44:21:37.text: As they were about to take Paul into the barracks, he asked the commander, “May I say something to you?” “Do you speak Greek?” he replied.

44:21:38.text: “Aren’t you the Egyptian who incited a rebellion some time ago and led four thousand members of the ‘Assassins’ into the wilderness?”

44:21:39.text: But Paul answered, “I am a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no ordinary city. Now I beg you to allow me to speak to the people.”

44:21:4.text: We sought out the disciples in Tyre and stayed with them seven days. Through the Spirit they kept telling Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.

44:21:40.text: Having received permission, Paul stood on the steps and motioned to the crowd. A great hush came over the crowd, and he addressed them in Hebrew:

44:21:5.text: But when our time there had ended, we set out on our journey. All the disciples, with their wives and children, accompanied us out of the city and knelt down on the beach to pray with us.

44:21:6.text: And after we had said our farewells, we went aboard the ship, and they returned home.

44:21:7.text: When we had finished our voyage from Tyre, we landed at Ptolemais, where we greeted the brothers and stayed with them for a day.

44:21:8.text: Leaving the next day, we went on to Caesarea and stayed at the home of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the Seven.

44:21:9.text: He had four unmarried daughters who prophesied.

44:23:1.text: Paul looked directly at the Sanhedrin and said, “Brothers, I have conducted myself before God in all good conscience to this day.”

44:23:10.text: The dispute grew so violent that the commander was afraid they would tear Paul to pieces. He ordered the soldiers to go down and remove him by force and bring him into the barracks.

44:23:11.text: The following night the Lord stood near Paul and said, “Take courage! As you have testified about Me in Jerusalem, so also you must testify in Rome.”

44:23:12.text: When daylight came, the Jews formed a conspiracy and bound themselves with an oath not to eat or drink until they had killed Paul.

44:23:13.text: More than forty of them were involved in this plot.

44:23:14.text: They went to the chief priests and elders and said, “We have bound ourselves with a solemn oath not to eat anything until we have killed Paul.

44:23:15.text: Now then, you and the Sanhedrin petition the commander to bring him down to you on the pretext of examining his case more carefully. We are ready to kill him on the way.”

44:23:16.text: But when the son of Paul’s sister heard about the plot, he went into the barracks and told Paul.

44:23:17.text: Then Paul called one of the centurions and said, “Take this young man to the commander; he has something to tell him.”

44:23:18.text: So the centurion took him to the commander and said, “Paul the prisoner sent and asked me to bring this young man to you. He has something to tell you.”

44:23:19.text: The commander took the young man by the hand, drew him aside, and asked, “What do you need to tell me?”

44:23:2.text: At this, the high priest Ananias ordered those standing near Paul to strike him on the mouth.

44:23:20.text: He answered, “The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul to the Sanhedrin tomorrow on the pretext of acquiring more information about him.

44:23:21.text: Do not let them persuade you, because more than forty men are waiting to ambush him. They have bound themselves with an oath not to eat or drink until they have killed him; they are ready now, awaiting your consent.”

44:23:22.text: So the commander dismissed the young man and instructed him, “Do not tell anyone that you have reported this to me.”

44:23:23.text: Then he called two of his centurions and said, “Prepare two hundred soldiers, seventy horsemen, and two hundred spearmen to go to Caesarea in the third hour of the night.

44:23:24.text: Provide mounts for Paul to take him safely to Governor Felix.”

44:23:25.text: And he wrote the following letter:

44:23:26.text: Claudius Lysias, To His Excellency, Governor Felix: Greetings.

44:23:27.text: This man was seized by the Jews, and they were about to kill him when I came with my troops to rescue him. For I had learned that he is a Roman citizen,

44:23:28.text: and since I wanted to understand their charges against him, I brought him down to their Sanhedrin.

44:23:29.text: I found that the accusation involved questions about their own law, but there was no charge worthy of death or imprisonment.

44:23:3.text: Then Paul said to him, “God will strike you, you whitewashed wall! You sit here to judge me according to the law, yet you yourself violate the law by commanding that I be struck.”

44:23:30.text: When I was informed that there was a plot against the man, I sent him to you at once. I also instructed his accusers to present their case against him before you.

44:23:31.text: So the soldiers followed their orders and brought Paul by night to Antipatris.

44:23:32.text: The next day they returned to the barracks and let the horsemen go on with him.

44:23:33.text: When the horsemen arrived in Caesarea, they delivered the letter to the governor and presented Paul to him.

44:23:34.text: The governor read the letter and asked what province Paul was from. Learning that he was from Cilicia,

44:23:35.text: he said, “I will hear your case when your accusers arrive.” Then he ordered that Paul be kept under guard in Herod’s Praetorium.

44:23:4.text: But those standing nearby said, “How dare you insult the high priest of God!”

44:23:5.text: “Brothers,” Paul replied, “I was not aware that he was the high priest, for it is written: ‘Do not speak evil about the ruler of your people.’ ”

44:23:6.text: Then Paul, knowing that some of them were Sadducees and others Pharisees, called out in the Sanhedrin, “Brothers, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee. It is because of my hope in the resurrection of the dead that I am on trial.”

44:23:7.text: As soon as he had said this, a dispute broke out between the Pharisees and Sadducees, and the assembly was divided.

44:23:8.text: For the Sadducees say that there is neither a resurrection, nor angels, nor spirits, but the Pharisees acknowledge them all.

44:23:9.text: A great clamor arose, and some scribes from the party of the Pharisees got up and contended sharply, “We find nothing wrong with this man. What if a spirit or an angel has spoken to him?”

44:25:1.text: Three days after his arrival in the province, Festus went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem,

44:25:10.text: Paul replied, “I am standing before the judgment seat of Caesar, where I ought to be tried. I have done nothing wrong to the Jews, as you yourself know very well.

44:25:11.text: If, however, I am guilty of anything worthy of death, I do not refuse to die. But if there is no truth to their accusations against me, no one has the right to hand me over to them. I appeal to Caesar!”

44:25:12.text: Then Festus conferred with his council and replied, “You have appealed to Caesar. To Caesar you will go!”

44:25:13.text: After several days had passed, King Agrippa and Bernice came down to Caesarea to pay their respects to Festus.

44:25:14.text: Since they were staying several days, Festus laid out Paul’s case before the king: “There is a certain man whom Felix left in prison.

44:25:15.text: While I was in Jerusalem, the chief priests and elders of the Jews presented their case and requested a judgment against him.

44:25:16.text: I told them that it is not the Roman custom to hand a man over before he has had an opportunity to face his accusers and defend himself against their charges.

44:25:17.text: So when they came here with me, I did not delay. The next day I sat on the judgment seat and ordered that the man be brought in.

44:25:18.text: But when his accusers rose to speak, they did not charge him with any of the crimes I had expected.

44:25:19.text: They only had some contentions with him regarding their own religion and a certain Jesus who had died, but whom Paul affirmed to be alive.

44:25:2.text: where the chief priests and Jewish leaders presented their case against Paul. They urged Festus

44:25:20.text: Since I was at a loss as to how to investigate these matters, I asked if he was willing to go to Jerusalem and be tried there on these charges.

44:25:21.text: But when Paul appealed to be held over for the decision of the Emperor, I ordered that he be held until I could send him to Caesar.”

44:25:22.text: Then Agrippa said to Festus, “I would like to hear this man myself.” “Tomorrow you will hear him,” Festus declared.

44:25:23.text: The next day Agrippa and Bernice came with great pomp and entered the auditorium, along with the commanders and leading men of the city. And Festus ordered that Paul be brought in.

44:25:24.text: Then Festus said, “King Agrippa and all who are present with us, you see this man. The whole Jewish community has petitioned me about him, both here and in Jerusalem, crying out that he ought not to live any longer.

44:25:25.text: But I found he had done nothing worthy of death, and since he has now appealed to the Emperor, I decided to send him.

44:25:26.text: I have nothing definite to write to our sovereign one about him. Therefore I have brought him before all of you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that after this inquiry I may have something to write.

44:25:27.text: For it seems unreasonable to me to send on a prisoner without specifying the charges against him.”

44:25:3.text: to grant them a concession against Paul by summoning him to Jerusalem, because they were preparing an ambush to kill him along the way.

44:25:4.text: But Festus replied, “Paul is being held in Caesarea, and I myself am going there soon.

44:25:5.text: So if this man has done anything wrong, let some of your leaders come down with me and accuse him there.”

44:25:6.text: After spending no more than eight or ten days with them, Festus went down to Caesarea. The next day he sat on the judgment seat and ordered that Paul be brought in.

44:25:7.text: When Paul arrived, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him, bringing many serious charges that they could not prove.

44:25:8.text: Then Paul made his defense: “I have committed no offense against the law of the Jews or against the temple or against Caesar.”

44:25:9.text: But Festus, wishing to do the Jews a favor, said to Paul, “Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem to stand trial before me on these charges?”

44:27:1.text: When it was decided that we would sail for Italy, Paul and some other prisoners were handed over to a centurion named Julius, who belonged to the Imperial Regiment.

44:27:10.text: “Men, I can see that our voyage will be filled with disaster and great loss, not only to ship and cargo, but to our own lives as well.”

44:27:11.text: But contrary to Paul’s advice, the centurion was persuaded by the pilot and by the owner of the ship.

44:27:12.text: Since the harbor was unsuitable to winter in, the majority decided to sail on, if somehow they could reach Phoenix to winter there. Phoenix was a harbor in Crete facing both southwest and northwest.

44:27:13.text: When a gentle south wind began to blow, they thought they had their opportunity. So they weighed anchor and sailed along, hugging the coast of Crete.

44:27:14.text: But it was not long before a cyclone called the Northeaster swept down across the island.

44:27:15.text: Unable to head into the wind, the ship was caught up. So we gave way and let ourselves be driven along.

44:27:16.text: Passing to the lee of a small island called Cauda, we barely managed to secure the lifeboat.

44:27:17.text: After hoisting it up, the crew used ropes to undergird the ship. And fearing that they would run aground on the sandbars of Syrtis, they lowered the sea anchor and were driven along.

44:27:18.text: We were tossed so violently that the next day the men began to jettison the cargo.

44:27:19.text: On the third day, they threw the ship’s tackle overboard with their own hands.

44:27:2.text: We boarded an Adramyttian ship about to sail for ports along the coast of Asia, and we put out to sea. Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, was with us.

44:27:20.text: When neither sun nor stars appeared for many days and the great storm continued to batter us, we abandoned all hope of being saved.

44:27:21.text: After the men had gone a long time without food, Paul stood up among them and said, “Men, you should have followed my advice not to sail from Crete. Then you would have averted this disaster and loss.

44:27:22.text: But now I urge you to keep up your courage, because you will not experience any loss of life, but only of the ship.

44:27:23.text: For just last night an angel of God, whose I am and whom I serve, stood beside me

44:27:24.text: and said, ‘Do not be afraid, Paul; you must stand before Caesar. And look, God has granted you the lives of all who sail with you.’

44:27:25.text: So take courage, men, for I believe God that it will happen just as He told me.

44:27:26.text: However, we must run aground on some island.”

44:27:27.text: On the fourteenth night we were still being driven across the Adriatic Sea. About midnight the sailors sensed they were approaching land.

44:27:28.text: They took soundings and found that the water was twenty fathoms deep. Going a little farther, they took another set of soundings that read fifteen fathoms.

44:27:29.text: Fearing that we would run aground on the rocks, they dropped four anchors from the stern and prayed for daybreak.

44:27:3.text: The next day we landed at Sidon, and Julius treated Paul with consideration, allowing him to visit his friends and receive their care.

44:27:30.text: Meanwhile, the sailors attempted to escape from the ship. Pretending to lower anchors from the bow, they let the lifeboat down into the sea.

44:27:31.text: But Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, “Unless these men remain with the ship, you cannot be saved.”

44:27:32.text: So the soldiers cut the ropes to the lifeboat and set it adrift.

44:27:33.text: Right up to daybreak, Paul kept urging them all to eat: “Today is your fourteenth day in constant suspense, without taking any food.

44:27:34.text: So for your own preservation, I urge you to eat something, because not a single hair of your head will be lost.”

44:27:35.text: After he had said this, Paul took bread and gave thanks to God in front of them all. Then he broke it and began to eat.

44:27:36.text: They were all encouraged and took some food themselves.

44:27:37.text: In all, there were 276 of us on board.

44:27:38.text: After the men had eaten their fill, they lightened the ship by throwing the grain into the sea.

44:27:39.text: When daylight came, they did not recognize the land, but they sighted a bay with a sandy beach, where they decided to run the ship aground if they could.

44:27:4.text: After putting out from there, we sailed to the lee of Cyprus because the winds were against us.

44:27:40.text: Cutting away the anchors, they left them in the sea as they loosened the ropes that held the rudders. Then they hoisted the foresail to the wind and made for the beach.

44:27:41.text: But the vessel struck a sandbar and ran aground. The bow stuck fast and would not move, and the stern was being broken up by the pounding of the waves.

44:27:42.text: The soldiers planned to kill the prisoners so none of them could swim to freedom.

44:27:43.text: But the centurion, wanting to spare Paul’s life, thwarted their plan. He commanded those who could swim to jump overboard first and get to land.

44:27:44.text: The rest were to follow on planks and various parts of the ship. In this way everyone was brought safely to land.

44:27:5.text: And when we had sailed across the open sea off the coast of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra in Lycia.

44:27:6.text: There the centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing for Italy and put us on board.

44:27:7.text: After sailing slowly for many days, we arrived off Cnidus. When the wind impeded us, we sailed to the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.

44:27:8.text: After we had moved along the coast with difficulty, we came to a place called Fair Havens, near the town of Lasea.

44:27:9.text: By now much time had passed, and the voyage had already become dangerous because it was after the Fast. So Paul advised them,

44:28:1.text: Once we were safely ashore, we learned that the island was called Malta.

44:28:10.text: The islanders honored us in many ways and supplied our needs when we were ready to sail.

44:28:11.text: After three months we set sail in an Alexandrian ship that had wintered in the island. It had the Twin Brothers as a figurehead.

44:28:12.text: Putting in at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.

44:28:13.text: From there we weighed anchor and came to Rhegium. After one day, a south wind came up, and on the second day we arrived at Puteoli.

44:28:14.text: There we found some brothers who invited us to spend the week with them. And so we came to Rome.

44:28:15.text: The brothers there had heard about us and traveled as far as the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns to meet us. When Paul saw them, he was encouraged and gave thanks to God.

44:28:16.text: When we arrived in Rome, Paul was permitted to stay by himself, with a soldier to guard him.

44:28:17.text: After three days, he called together the leaders of the Jews. When they had gathered, he said to them, “Brothers, although I have done nothing against our people or the customs of our fathers, I was taken prisoner in Jerusalem and handed over to the Romans.

44:28:18.text: They examined me and wanted to release me, because there was no basis for a death sentence against me.

44:28:19.text: But when the Jews objected, I was compelled to appeal to Caesar, even though I have no charge to bring against my nation.

44:28:2.text: The islanders showed us extraordinary kindness. They kindled a fire and welcomed all of us because it was raining and cold.

44:7:43.text: You have taken along the tabernacle of Molech and the star of your god Rephan, the idols you made to worship. Therefore I will send you into exile beyond Babylon.’

44:7:44.text: Our fathers had the tabernacle of the Testimony with them in the wilderness. It was constructed exactly as God had directed Moses, according to the pattern he had seen.

44:7:45.text: And our fathers who received it brought it in with Joshua when they dispossessed the nations God drove out before them. It remained until the time of David,

44:7:46.text: who found favor in the sight of God and asked to provide a dwelling place for the God of Jacob.

44:7:47.text: But it was Solomon who built the house for Him.

44:7:48.text: However, the Most High does not dwell in houses made by human hands. As the prophet says:

44:7:49.text: ‘Heaven is My throne and the earth is My footstool. What kind of house will you build for Me, says the Lord, or where will My place of repose be?

44:7:5.text: He gave him no inheritance here, not even a foot of ground. But God promised to give possession of the land to Abraham and his descendants, even though he did not yet have a child.

44:7:50.text: Has not My hand made all these things?’

44:7:51.text: You stiff-necked people with uncircumcised hearts and ears! You always resist the Holy Spirit, just as your fathers did.

44:7:52.text: Which of the prophets did your fathers fail to persecute? They even killed those who foretold the coming of the Righteous One. And now you are His betrayers and murderers —

44:7:53.text: you who received the law ordained by angels, yet have not kept it.”

44:7:54.text: On hearing this, the members of the Sanhedrin were enraged, and they gnashed their teeth at him.

44:7:55.text: But Stephen, full of the Holy Spirit, looked intently into heaven and saw the glory of God and Jesus standing at the right hand of God.

44:7:56.text: “Look,” he said, “I see heaven open and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God.”

44:7:57.text: At this they covered their ears, cried out in a loud voice, and rushed together at him.

44:7:58.text: They dragged him out of the city and began to stone him. Meanwhile the witnesses laid their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul.

44:7:59.text: While they were stoning him, Stephen appealed, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.”

44:7:6.text: God told him that his descendants would be foreigners in a strange land, and that they would be enslaved and mistreated four hundred years.

44:7:60.text: Falling on his knees, he cried out in a loud voice, “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.” And when he had said this, he fell asleep.

44:7:7.text: ‘But I will punish the nation that enslaves them,’ God said, ‘and afterward they will come forth and worship Me in this place.’

44:7:8.text: Then God gave Abraham the covenant of circumcision, and Abraham became the father of Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day. And Isaac became the father of Jacob, and Jacob of the twelve patriarchs.

44:7:9.text: Because the patriarchs were jealous of Joseph, they sold him as a slave into Egypt. But God was with him

44:8:1.text: And Saul was there, giving approval to Stephen’s death. On that day a great persecution broke out against the church in Jerusalem, and all except the apostles were scattered throughout Judea and Samaria.

44:8:10.text: and all the people, from the least to the greatest, heeded his words and said, “This man is the divine power called the Great Power.”

44:8:11.text: They paid close attention to him because he had astounded them for a long time with his sorcery.

44:8:12.text: But when they believed Philip as he preached the gospel of the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women.

44:8:13.text: Even Simon himself believed and was baptized. He followed Philip closely and was astounded by the great signs and miracles he observed.

44:8:14.text: When the apostles in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them.

44:8:15.text: On their arrival, they prayed for them to receive the Holy Spirit.

44:8:16.text: For the Holy Spirit had not yet fallen upon any of them; they had simply been baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.

44:8:17.text: Then Peter and John laid their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.

44:8:18.text: When Simon saw that the Spirit was given through the laying on of the apostles’ hands, he offered them money.

44:8:19.text: “Give me this power as well,” he said, “so that everyone on whom I lay my hands may receive the Holy Spirit.”

44:8:2.text: God-fearing men buried Stephen and mourned deeply over him.

44:8:20.text: But Peter replied, “May your silver perish with you, because you thought you could buy the gift of God with money!

44:8:21.text: You have no part or share in our ministry, because your heart is not right before God.

44:8:22.text: Repent, therefore, of your wickedness, and pray to the Lord. Perhaps He will forgive you for the intent of your heart.

44:8:23.text: For I see that you are poisoned by bitterness and captive to iniquity.”

44:8:24.text: Then Simon answered, “Pray to the Lord for me, so that nothing you have said may happen to me.”

44:8:25.text: And after Peter and John had testified and spoken the word of the Lord, they returned to Jerusalem, preaching the gospel in many of the Samaritan villages.

44:8:26.text: Now an angel of the Lord said to Philip, “Get up and go south to the desert road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza.”

44:8:27.text: So he started out, and on his way he met an Ethiopian eunuch, a court official in charge of the entire treasury of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians. He had gone to Jerusalem to worship,

44:8:28.text: and on his return was sitting in his chariot reading Isaiah the prophet.

44:8:29.text: The Spirit said to Philip, “Go over to that chariot and stay by it.”

44:8:3.text: But Saul began to destroy the church. Going from house to house, he dragged off men and women and put them in prison.

44:8:30.text: So Philip ran up and heard the man reading Isaiah the prophet. “Do you understand what you are reading?” Philip asked.

44:8:31.text: “How can I,” he said, “unless someone guides me?” And he invited Philip to come up and sit with him.

44:8:32.text: The eunuch was reading this passage of Scripture: “He was led like a sheep to the slaughter, and as a lamb before the shearer is silent, so He did not open His mouth.

44:8:33.text: In His humiliation He was deprived of justice. Who can recount His descendants? For His life was removed from the earth.”

44:8:34.text: “Tell me,” said the eunuch, “who is the prophet talking about, himself or someone else?”

44:8:35.text: Then Philip began with this very Scripture and told him the good news about Jesus.

44:8:36.text: As they traveled along the road and came to some water, the eunuch said, “Look, here is water! What is there to prevent me from being baptized?”

44:8:38.text: And he gave orders to stop the chariot. Then both Philip and the eunuch went down into the water, and Philip baptized him.

44:8:39.text: When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord carried Philip away, and the eunuch saw him no more, but went on his way rejoicing.

44:8:4.text: Those who had been scattered preached the word wherever they went.

44:8:40.text: But Philip appeared at Azotus and traveled through that region, preaching the gospel in all the towns until he came to Caesarea.

44:8:5.text: Philip went down to a city in Samaria and proclaimed the Christ to them.

44:8:6.text: The crowds gave their undivided attention to Philip’s message and to the signs they saw him perform.

44:8:7.text: With loud shrieks, unclean spirits came out of many who were possessed, and many of the paralyzed and lame were healed.

44:8:8.text: So there was great joy in that city.

44:8:9.text: Prior to that time, a man named Simon had practiced sorcery in the city and astounded the people of Samaria. He claimed to be someone great,

44:9:1.text: Meanwhile, Saul was still breathing out murderous threats against the disciples of the Lord. He approached the high priest

44:9:10.text: In Damascus there was a disciple named Ananias. The Lord spoke to him in a vision, “Ananias!” “Here I am, Lord,” he answered.

44:9:11.text: “Get up!” the Lord told him. “Go to the house of Judas on Straight Street and ask for a man from Tarsus named Saul, for he is praying.

44:9:12.text: In a vision he has seen a man named Ananias come and place his hands on him to restore his sight.”

44:9:13.text: But Ananias answered, “Lord, many people have told me about this man and all the harm he has done to Your saints in Jerusalem.

44:9:14.text: And now he is here with authority from the chief priests to arrest all who call on Your name.”

44:9:15.text: “Go!” said the Lord. “This man is My chosen instrument to carry My name before the Gentiles and their kings, and before the people of Israel.

44:9:16.text: I will show him how much he must suffer for My name.”

44:9:17.text: So Ananias went to the house, and when he arrived, he placed his hands on Saul. “Brother Saul,” he said, “the Lord Jesus, who appeared to you on the road as you were coming here, has sent me so that you may see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit.”

44:9:18.text: At that instant, something like scales fell from Saul’s eyes, and his sight was restored. He got up and was baptized,

44:9:19.text: and after taking some food, he regained his strength. And he spent several days with the disciples in Damascus.

44:9:2.text: and requested letters to the synagogues in Damascus, so that if he found any men or women belonging to the Way, he could bring them as prisoners to Jerusalem.

44:9:20.text: Saul promptly began to proclaim Jesus in the synagogues, declaring, “He is the Son of God.”

44:9:21.text: All who heard him were astounded and asked, “Isn’t this the man who wreaked havoc in Jerusalem on those who call on this name? And hasn’t he come here to take them as prisoners to the chief priests?”

44:9:22.text: But Saul was empowered all the more, and he confounded the Jews living in Damascus by proving that Jesus is the Christ.

44:9:23.text: After many days had passed, the Jews conspired to kill him,

44:9:24.text: but Saul learned of their plot. Day and night they watched the city gates in order to kill him.

44:9:25.text: One night, however, his disciples took him and lowered him in a basket through a window in the wall.

44:9:26.text: When Saul arrived in Jerusalem, he tried to join the disciples, but they were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple.

44:9:27.text: Then Barnabas brought him to the apostles and described how Saul had seen the Lord, who spoke to him on the road to Damascus, and how Saul had spoken boldly in that city in the name of Jesus.

44:9:28.text: So Saul stayed with them, moving about freely in Jerusalem and speaking boldly in the name of the Lord.

44:9:29.text: He talked and debated with the Grecian Jews, but they tried to kill him.

44:9:3.text: As Saul drew near to Damascus on his journey, suddenly a light from heaven flashed around him.

44:9:30.text: When the brothers learned of this, they took him down to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus.

44:9:31.text: Then the church throughout Judea, Galilee, and Samaria experienced a time of peace. It grew in strength and numbers, living in the fear of the Lord and the encouragement of the Holy Spirit.

44:9:32.text: As Peter traveled throughout the area, he went to visit the saints in Lydda.

44:9:33.text: There he found a man named Aeneas, who had been paralyzed and bedridden for eight years.

44:9:34.text: “Aeneas,” Peter said to him, “Jesus Christ heals you! Get up and put away your mat.” Immediately Aeneas got up,

44:9:35.text: and all who lived in Lydda and Sharon saw him and turned to the Lord.

44:9:36.text: In Joppa there was a disciple named Tabitha (which is translated as Dorcas), who was always occupied with works of kindness and charity.

44:9:37.text: At that time, however, she became sick and died, and her body was washed and placed in an upper room.

44:9:38.text: Since Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples heard that Peter was there and sent two men to urge him, “Come to us without delay.”

44:9:39.text: So Peter got up and went with them. On his arrival, they took him to the upper room. All the widows stood around him, weeping and showing him the tunics and other clothing that Dorcas had made while she was still with them.

44:9:4.text: He fell to the ground and heard a voice say to him, “Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me?”

44:9:40.text: Then Peter sent them all out of the room. He knelt down and prayed, and turning toward her body, he said, “Tabitha, get up!” She opened her eyes, and seeing Peter, she sat up.

44:9:41.text: Peter took her by the hand and helped her up. Then he called the saints and widows and presented her to them alive.

44:9:42.text: This became known all over Joppa, and many people believed in the Lord.

44:9:43.text: And Peter stayed for several days in Joppa with a tanner named Simon.

44:9:5.text: “Who are You, Lord?” Saul asked. “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting,” He replied.

44:9:6.text: “Now get up and go into the city, and you will be told what you must do.”

44:9:7.text: The men traveling with Saul stood there speechless. They heard the voice but did not see anyone.

44:9:8.text: Saul got up from the ground, but when he opened his eyes he could not see a thing. So they led him by the hand into Damascus.

44:9:9.text: For three days he was without sight, and he did not eat or drink anything.

45:10:1.text: Brothers, my heart’s desire and prayer to God for the Israelites is for their salvation.

45:10:10.text: For with your heart you believe and are justified, and with your mouth you confess and are saved.

45:10:11.text: It is just as the Scripture says: “Anyone who believes in Him will never be put to shame.”

45:10:12.text: For there is no difference between Jew and Greek: The same Lord is Lord of all, and gives richly to all who call on Him,

45:10:13.text: for, “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.”

45:10:14.text: How then can they call on the One in whom they have not believed? And how can they believe in the One of whom they have not heard? And how can they hear without someone to preach?

45:10:15.text: And how can they preach unless they are sent? As it is written: “How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!”

45:10:16.text: But not all of them welcomed the good news. For Isaiah says, “Lord, who has believed our message?”

45:10:17.text: Consequently, faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of Christ.

45:10:18.text: But I ask, did they not hear? Indeed they did: “Their voice has gone out into all the earth, their words to the ends of the world.”

45:10:19.text: I ask instead, did Israel not understand? First, Moses says: “I will make you jealous by those who are not a nation; I will make you angry by a nation without understanding.”

45:10:2.text: For I testify about them that they are zealous for God, but not on the basis of knowledge.

45:10:20.text: And Isaiah boldly says: “I was found by those who did not seek Me; I revealed Myself to those who did not ask for Me.”

45:10:21.text: But as for Israel he says: “All day long I have held out My hands to a disobedient and obstinate people.”

45:10:3.text: Because they were ignorant of God’s righteousness and sought to establish their own, they did not submit to God’s righteousness.

45:10:4.text: For Christ is the end of the law, to bring righteousness to everyone who believes.

45:10:5.text: For concerning the righteousness that is by the law, Moses writes: “The man who does these things will live by them.”

45:10:6.text: But the righteousness that is by faith says: “Do not say in your heart, ‘Who will ascend into heaven?’ (that is, to bring Christ down)

45:10:7.text: or, ‘Who will descend into the Abyss?’ (that is, to bring Christ up from the dead).”

45:10:8.text: But what does it say? “The word is near you; it is in your mouth and in your heart,” that is, the word of faith we are proclaiming:

45:10:9.text: that if you confess with your mouth, “Jesus is Lord,” and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved.

45:11:1.text: I ask then, did God reject His people? Certainly not! I am an Israelite myself, a descendant of Abraham, from the tribe of Benjamin.

45:11:10.text: May their eyes be darkened so they cannot see, and their backs be bent forever.”

45:11:11.text: I ask then, did they stumble so as to fall beyond recovery? Certainly not! However, because of their trespass, salvation has come to the Gentiles to make Israel jealous.

45:11:12.text: But if their trespass means riches for the world, and their failure means riches for the Gentiles, how much greater riches will their fullness bring!

45:11:13.text: I am speaking to you Gentiles. Inasmuch as I am the apostle to the Gentiles, I magnify my ministry

45:11:14.text: in the hope that I may provoke my own people to jealousy and save some of them.

45:11:15.text: For if their rejection is the reconciliation of the world, what will their acceptance be but life from the dead?

45:11:16.text: If the first part of the dough is holy, so is the whole batch; if the root is holy, so are the branches.

45:11:17.text: Now if some branches have been broken off, and you, a wild olive shoot, have been grafted in among the others to share in the nourishment of the olive root,

45:11:18.text: do not boast over those branches. If you do, remember this: You do not support the root, but the root supports you.

45:11:19.text: You will say then, “Branches were broken off so that I could be grafted in.”

45:11:2.text: God did not reject His people, whom He foreknew. Do you not know what the Scripture says about Elijah, how he appealed to God against Israel:

45:11:20.text: That is correct: They were broken off because of unbelief, but you stand by faith. Do not be arrogant, but be afraid.

45:11:21.text: For if God did not spare the natural branches, He will certainly not spare you either.

45:11:22.text: Take notice, therefore, of the kindness and severity of God: severity to those who fell, but kindness to you, if you continue in His kindness. Otherwise you also will be cut off.

45:11:23.text: And if they do not persist in unbelief, they will be grafted in, for God is able to graft them in again.

45:11:24.text: For if you were cut from a wild olive tree, and contrary to nature were grafted into one that is cultivated, how much more readily will these, the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree!

45:11:25.text: I do not want you to be ignorant of this mystery, brothers, so that you will not be conceited: A hardening in part has come to Israel, until the full number of the Gentiles has come in.

45:11:26.text: And so all Israel will be saved, as it is written: “The Deliverer will come from Zion; He will remove godlessness from Jacob.
