45:11:27.text: And this is My covenant with them when I take away their sins.”

45:11:28.text: Regarding the gospel, they are enemies on your account; but regarding election, they are loved on account of the patriarchs.

45:11:29.text: For God’s gifts and His call are irrevocable.

45:11:3.text: “Lord, they have killed Your prophets and torn down Your altars. I am the only one left, and they are seeking my life as well”?

45:11:30.text: Just as you who formerly disobeyed God have now received mercy through their disobedience,

45:11:31.text: so they too have now disobeyed, in order that they too may now receive mercy through the mercy shown to you.

45:11:32.text: For God has consigned everyone to disobedience so that He may have mercy on everyone.

45:11:33.text: O, the depth of the riches of the wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are His judgments, and untraceable His ways!

45:11:34.text: “Who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who has been His counselor?”

45:11:35.text: “Who has first given to God, that God should repay him?”

45:11:36.text: For from Him and through Him and to Him are all things. To Him be the glory forever! Amen.

45:11:4.text: And what was the divine reply to him? “I have reserved for Myself seven thousand men who have not bowed the knee to Baal.”

45:11:5.text: In the same way, at the present time there is a remnant chosen by grace.

45:11:6.text: And if it is by grace, then it is no longer by works. Otherwise, grace would no longer be grace.

45:11:7.text: What then? What Israel was seeking, it failed to obtain, but the elect did. The others were hardened,

45:11:8.text: as it is written: “God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that could not see, and ears that could not hear, to this very day.”

45:11:9.text: And David says: “May their table become a snare and a trap, a stumbling block and a retribution to them.

45:12:1.text: Therefore I urge you, brothers, on account of God’s mercy, to offer your bodies as living sacrifices, holy and pleasing to God, which is your spiritual service of worship.

45:12:10.text: Be devoted to one another in brotherly love. Outdo yourselves in honoring one another.

45:12:11.text: Do not let your zeal subside; keep your spiritual fervor, serving the Lord.

45:12:12.text: Be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, persistent in prayer.

45:12:13.text: Share with the saints who are in need. Practice hospitality.

45:12:14.text: Bless those who persecute you. Bless and do not curse.

45:12:15.text: Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep.

45:12:16.text: Live in harmony with one another. Do not be proud, but enjoy the company of the lowly. Do not be conceited.

45:12:17.text: Do not repay anyone evil for evil. Carefully consider what is right in the eyes of everybody.

45:12:18.text: If it is possible on your part, live at peace with everyone.

45:12:19.text: Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but leave room for God’s wrath. For it is written: “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay, says the Lord.”

45:12:2.text: Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind. Then you will be able to test and approve what is the good, pleasing, and perfect will of God.

45:12:20.text: On the contrary, “If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink. For in so doing, you will heap burning coals on his head.”

45:12:21.text: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.

45:12:3.text: For by the grace given me I say to every one of you: Do not think of yourself more highly than you ought, but think of yourself with sober judgment, according to the measure of faith God has given you.

45:12:4.text: Just as each of us has one body with many members, and not all members have the same function,

45:12:5.text: so in Christ we who are many are one body, and each member belongs to one another.

45:12:6.text: We have different gifts according to the grace given us. If one’s gift is prophecy, let him use it in proportion to his faith;

45:12:7.text: if it is serving, let him serve; if it is teaching, let him teach;

45:12:8.text: if it is encouraging, let him encourage; if it is giving, let him give generously; if it is leading, let him lead with diligence; if it is showing mercy, let him do it cheerfully.

45:12:9.text: Love must be sincere. Detest what is evil; cling to what is good.

45:13:1.text: Everyone must submit himself to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except that which is from God. The authorities that exist have been appointed by God.

45:13:10.text: Love does no wrong to its neighbor. Therefore love is the fulfillment of the law.

45:13:11.text: And do this, understanding the occasion. The hour has come for you to wake up from your slumber, for our salvation is nearer now than when we first believed.

45:13:12.text: The night is nearly over; the day has drawn near. So let us lay aside the deeds of darkness and put on the armor of light.

45:13:13.text: Let us behave decently, as in the daytime, not in carousing and drunkenness, not in sexual immorality and debauchery, not in dissension and jealousy.

45:13:14.text: Instead, clothe yourselves with the Lord Jesus Christ, and make no provision for the desires of the flesh.

45:13:2.text: Consequently, whoever resists authority is opposing what God has set in place, and those who do so will bring judgment on themselves.

45:13:3.text: For rulers are not a terror to good conduct, but to bad. Do you want to be unafraid of the one in authority? Then do what is right, and you will have his approval.

45:13:4.text: For he is God’s servant for your good. But if you do wrong, be afraid, for he does not carry the sword in vain. He is God’s servant, an agent of retribution to the wrongdoer.

45:13:5.text: Therefore it is necessary to submit to authority, not only to avoid punishment, but also as a matter of conscience.

45:13:6.text: This is also why you pay taxes. For the authorities are God’s servants, who devote themselves to their work.

45:13:7.text: Pay everyone what you owe him: taxes to whom taxes are due, revenue to whom revenue is due, respect to whom respect is due, honor to whom honor is due.

45:13:8.text: Be indebted to no one, except to one another in love. For he who loves his neighbor has fulfilled the law.

45:13:9.text: The commandments “Do not commit adultery,” “Do not murder,” “Do not steal,” “Do not covet,” and any other commandments, are summed up in this one decree: “Love your neighbor as yourself.”

45:14:1.text: Accept him whose faith is weak, without passing judgment on his opinions.

45:14:10.text: Why, then, do you judge your brother? Or why do you belittle your brother? For we will all stand before God’s judgment seat.

45:14:11.text: It is written: “As surely as I live, says the Lord, every knee will bow before Me; every tongue will confess to God.”

45:14:12.text: So then, each of us will give an account of himself to God.

45:14:13.text: Therefore let us stop judging one another. Instead, make up your mind not to put any stumbling block or obstacle in your brother’s way.

45:14:14.text: I am convinced and fully persuaded in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself. But if anyone regards something as unclean, then for him it is unclean.

45:14:15.text: If your brother is distressed by what you eat, you are no longer acting in love. Do not by your eating destroy your brother, for whom Christ died.

45:14:16.text: Do not allow what you consider good, then, to be spoken of as evil.

45:14:17.text: For the kingdom of God is not a matter of eating and drinking, but of righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.

45:14:18.text: For whoever serves Christ in this way is pleasing to God and approved by men.

45:14:19.text: So then, let us pursue what leads to peace and to mutual edification.

45:14:2.text: For one person has faith to eat all things, while another, who is weak, eats only vegetables.

45:14:20.text: Do not destroy the work of God for the sake of food. All food is clean, but it is wrong for a man to let his eating be a stumbling block.

45:14:21.text: It is better not to eat meat or drink wine or to do anything to cause your brother to stumble.

45:14:22.text: Keep your belief about such matters between yourself and God. Blessed is the one who does not condemn himself by what he approves.

45:14:23.text: But the one who has doubts is condemned if he eats, because his eating is not from faith; and everything that is not from faith is sin.

45:14:3.text: The one who eats everything must not belittle the one who does not, and the one who does not eat everything must not judge the one who does, for God has accepted him.

45:14:4.text: Who are you to judge someone else’s servant? To his own master he stands or falls. And he will stand, for the Lord is able to make him stand.

45:14:5.text: One person regards a certain day above the others, while someone else considers every day alike. Each one should be fully convinced in his own mind.

45:14:6.text: He who observes a special day does so to the Lord; he who eats does so to the Lord, for he gives thanks to God; and he who abstains does so to the Lord and gives thanks to God.

45:14:7.text: For none of us lives to himself alone, and none of us dies to himself alone.

45:14:8.text: If we live, we live to the Lord, and if we die, we die to the Lord. So whether we live or die, we belong to the Lord.

45:14:9.text: For this reason Christ died and returned to life, that He might be the Lord of both the dead and the living.

45:15:1.text: We who are strong ought to bear with the shortcomings of the weak and not to please ourselves.

45:15:10.text: Again, it says: “Rejoice, O Gentiles, with His people.”

45:15:11.text: And again: “Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles, and extol Him, all you peoples.”

45:15:12.text: And once more, Isaiah says: “The Root of Jesse will appear, One who will arise to rule over the Gentiles; in Him the Gentiles will put their hope.”

45:15:13.text: Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace as you believe in Him, so that you may overflow with hope by the power of the Holy Spirit.

45:15:14.text: I myself am convinced, my brothers, that you yourselves are full of goodness, brimming with knowledge, and able to instruct one another.

45:15:15.text: However, I have written you a bold reminder on some points, because of the grace God has given me

45:15:16.text: to be a minister of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles in the priestly service of the gospel of God, so that the Gentiles might become an offering acceptable to God, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.

45:15:17.text: Therefore I exult in Christ Jesus in my service to God.

45:15:18.text: I will not presume to speak of anything except what Christ has accomplished through me in leading the Gentiles to obedience by word and deed,

45:15:19.text: by the power of signs and wonders, and by the power of the Spirit of God. So from Jerusalem all the way around to Illyricum, I have fully proclaimed the gospel of Christ.

45:15:2.text: Each of us should please his neighbor for his good, to build him up.

45:15:20.text: In this way I have aspired to preach the gospel where Christ was not known, so that I would not be building on someone else’s foundation.

45:15:21.text: Rather, as it is written: “Those who were not told about Him will see, and those who have not heard will understand.”

45:15:22.text: That is why I have often been hindered from coming to you.

45:15:23.text: But now that there are no further opportunities for me in these regions, and since I have longed for many years to visit you,

45:15:24.text: I hope to see you on my way to Spain. And after I have enjoyed your company for a while, you can equip me for my journey.

45:15:25.text: Now, however, I am on my way to Jerusalem to serve the saints there.

45:15:26.text: For Macedonia and Achaia were pleased to make a contribution for the poor among the saints in Jerusalem.

45:15:27.text: They were pleased to do it, and indeed they owe it to them. For if the Gentiles have shared in their spiritual blessings, they are obligated to minister to them with material blessings.

45:15:28.text: So after I have completed this service and have safely delivered this bounty to them, I will set off to Spain by way of you.

45:15:29.text: I know that when I come to you, I will come in the fullness of the blessing of Christ.

45:15:3.text: For even Christ did not please Himself, but as it is written: “The insults of those who insult You have fallen on Me.”

45:15:30.text: Now I urge you, brothers, by our Lord Jesus Christ and by the love of the Spirit, to join me in my struggle by praying to God for me.

45:15:31.text: Pray that I may be delivered from the unbelievers in Judea, and that my service in Jerusalem may be acceptable to the saints there,

45:15:32.text: so that by God’s will I may come to you with joy and together with you be refreshed.

45:15:33.text: The God of peace be with all of you. Amen.

45:15:4.text: For everything that was written in the past was written for our instruction, so that through endurance and the encouragement of the Scriptures, we might have hope.

45:15:5.text: Now may the God who gives endurance and encouragement grant you harmony with one another in Christ Jesus,

45:15:6.text: so that with one mind and one voice you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.

45:15:7.text: Accept one another, then, just as Christ accepted you, in order to bring glory to God.

45:15:8.text: For I tell you that Christ has become a servant of the circumcised on behalf of God’s truth, to confirm the promises made to the patriarchs,

45:15:9.text: so that the Gentiles may glorify God for His mercy. As it is written: “Therefore I will praise You among the Gentiles; I will sing hymns to Your name.”

45:16:1.text: I commend to you our sister Phoebe, a servant of the church in Cenchrea.

45:16:10.text: Greet Apelles, who is approved in Christ. Greet those who belong to the household of Aristobulus.

45:16:11.text: Greet Herodion, my fellow countryman. Greet those from the household of Narcissus who are in the Lord.

45:16:12.text: Greet Tryphena and Tryphosa, women who have worked hard in the Lord. Greet my beloved Persis, who has worked very hard in the Lord.

45:16:13.text: Greet Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and his mother, who has been a mother to me as well.

45:16:14.text: Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers with them.

45:16:15.text: Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas and all the saints with them.

45:16:16.text: Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the churches of Christ send you greetings.

45:16:17.text: Now I urge you, brothers, to watch out for those who create divisions and obstacles that are contrary to the teaching you have learned. Turn away from them.

45:16:18.text: For such people are not serving our Lord Christ, but their own appetites. By smooth talk and flattery they deceive the hearts of the naive.

45:16:19.text: Everyone has heard about your obedience, so I rejoice over you. But I want you to be wise about what is good and innocent about what is evil.

45:16:2.text: Welcome her in the Lord in a manner worthy of the saints, and assist her with anything she may need from you. For she has been a great help to many people, including me.

45:16:20.text: The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.

45:16:21.text: Timothy, my fellow worker, sends you greetings, as do Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater, my fellow countrymen.

45:16:22.text: I, Tertius, who wrote down this letter, greet you in the Lord.

45:16:23.text: Gaius, who has hosted me and all the church, sends you greetings. Erastus, the city treasurer, sends you greetings, as does our brother Quartus.

45:16:25.text: Now to Him who is able to strengthen you by my gospel and by the proclamation of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery concealed for ages past

45:16:26.text: but now revealed and made known through the writings of the prophets by the command of the eternal God, in order to lead all nations to the obedience that comes from faith —

45:16:27.text: to the only wise God be glory forever through Jesus Christ! Amen.

45:16:3.text: Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus,

45:16:4.text: who have risked their lives for me. Not only I but all the churches of the Gentiles are grateful to them.

45:16:5.text: Greet also the church that meets at their house. Greet my beloved Epenetus, who was the first convert to Christ in the province of Asia.

45:16:6.text: Greet Mary, who has worked very hard for you.

45:16:7.text: Greet Andronicus and Junia, my fellow countrymen and fellow prisoners. They are outstanding among the apostles, and they were in Christ before I was.

45:16:8.text: Greet Ampliatus, my beloved in the Lord.

45:16:9.text: Greet Urbanus, our fellow worker in Christ, and my beloved Stachys.

45:1:1.text: Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus, called to be an apostle, and set apart for the gospel of God —

45:1:10.text: in my prayers at all times, asking that now at last by God’s will I may succeed in coming to you.

45:1:11.text: For I long to see you so that I may impart to you some spiritual gift to strengthen you,

45:1:12.text: that is, that you and I may be mutually encouraged by each other’s faith.

45:1:13.text: I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, how often I planned to come to you (but have been prevented from visiting until now), in order that I might have a harvest among you, just as I have had among the other Gentiles.

45:1:14.text: I am obligated both to Greeks and non-Greeks, both to the wise and the foolish.

45:1:15.text: That is why I am so eager to preach the gospel also to you who are in Rome.

45:1:16.text: I am not ashamed of the gospel, because it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, first to the Jew, then to the Greek.

45:1:17.text: For the gospel reveals the righteousness of God that comes by faith from start to finish, just as it is written: “The righteous will live by faith.”

45:1:18.text: The wrath of God is being revealed from heaven against all the godlessness and wickedness of men who suppress the truth by their wickedness.

45:1:19.text: For what may be known about God is plain to them, because God has made it plain to them.

45:1:2.text: the gospel He promised beforehand through His prophets in the Holy Scriptures,

45:1:20.text: For since the creation of the world God’s invisible qualities, His eternal power and divine nature, have been clearly seen, being understood from His workmanship, so that men are without excuse.

45:1:21.text: For although they knew God, they neither glorified Him as God nor gave thanks to Him, but they became futile in their thinking and darkened in their foolish hearts.

45:1:22.text: Although they claimed to be wise, they became fools,

45:1:23.text: and exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images of mortal man and birds and animals and reptiles.

45:1:24.text: Therefore God gave them over in the desires of their hearts to impurity for the dishonoring of their bodies with one another.

45:1:25.text: They exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is forever worthy of praise! Amen.

45:1:26.text: For this reason God gave them over to dishonorable passions. Even their women exchanged natural relations for unnatural ones.

45:1:27.text: Likewise, the men abandoned natural relations with women and burned with lust for one another. Men committed indecent acts with other men, and received in themselves the due penalty for their error.

45:1:28.text: Furthermore, since they did not see fit to acknowledge God, He gave them up to a depraved mind, to do what ought not to be done.

45:1:29.text: They have become filled with every kind of wickedness, evil, greed, and depravity. They are full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, and malice. They are gossips,

45:1:3.text: regarding His Son, who was a descendant of David according to the flesh,

45:1:30.text: slanderers, God-haters, insolent, arrogant, and boastful. They invent new forms of evil; they disobey their parents.

45:1:31.text: They are senseless, faithless, heartless, merciless.

45:1:32.text: Although they know God’s righteous decree that those who do such things are worthy of death, they not only continue to do these things, but also approve of those who practice them.

45:1:4.text: and who through the Spirit of holiness was declared with power to be the Son of God by His resurrection from the dead: Jesus Christ our Lord.

45:1:5.text: Through Him and on behalf of His name, we received grace and apostleship to call all those among the Gentiles to the obedience that comes from faith.

45:1:6.text: And you also are among those who are called to belong to Jesus Christ.

45:1:7.text: To all in Rome who are loved by God and called to be saints: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

45:1:8.text: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is being proclaimed all over the world.

45:1:9.text: God, whom I serve with my spirit in preaching the gospel of His Son, is my witness how constantly I remember you

45:2:1.text: You, therefore, have no excuse, you who pass judgment on another. For on whatever grounds you judge the other, you are condemning yourself, because you who pass judgment do the same things.

45:2:10.text: but glory, honor, and peace for everyone who does good, first for the Jew, then for the Greek.

45:2:11.text: For God does not show favoritism.

45:2:12.text: All who sin apart from the law will also perish apart from the law, and all who sin under the law will be judged by the law.

45:2:13.text: For it is not the hearers of the law who are righteous before God, but it is the doers of the law who will be declared righteous.

45:2:14.text: Indeed, when Gentiles, who do not have the law, do by nature what the law requires, they are a law to themselves, even though they do not have the law.

45:2:15.text: So they show that the work of the law is written on their hearts, their consciences also bearing witness, and their thoughts either accusing or defending them

45:2:16.text: on the day when God will judge men’s secrets through Christ Jesus, as proclaimed by my gospel.

45:2:17.text: Now you, if you call yourself a Jew; if you rely on the law and boast in God;

45:2:18.text: if you know His will and approve of what is superior because you are instructed by the law;

45:2:19.text: if you are convinced that you are a guide for the blind, a light for those in darkness,

45:2:2.text: And we know that God’s judgment against those who do such things is based on truth.

45:2:20.text: an instructor of the foolish, a teacher of infants, because you have in the law the embodiment of knowledge and truth —

45:2:21.text: you, then, who teach others, do you not teach yourself? You who preach against stealing, do you steal?

45:2:22.text: You who forbid adultery, do you commit adultery? You who abhor idols, do you rob temples?

45:2:23.text: You who boast in the law, do you dishonor God by breaking the law?

45:2:24.text: As it is written: “God’s name is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you.”

45:2:25.text: Circumcision has value if you observe the law, but if you break the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.

45:2:26.text: If a man who is not circumcised keeps the requirements of the law, will not his uncircumcision be regarded as circumcision?

45:2:27.text: The one who is physically uncircumcised yet keeps the law will condemn you who, even though you have the written code and circumcision, are a lawbreaker.

45:2:28.text: A man is not a Jew because he is one outwardly, nor is circumcision only outward and physical.

45:2:29.text: No, a man is a Jew because he is one inwardly, and circumcision is a matter of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the written code. Such a man’s praise does not come from men, but from God.

45:2:3.text: So when you, O man, pass judgment on others, yet do the same things, do you think you will escape God’s judgment?

45:2:4.text: Or do you disregard the riches of His kindness, tolerance, and patience, not realizing that God’s kindness leads you to repentance?

45:2:5.text: But because of your hard and unrepentant heart, you are storing up wrath against yourself for the day of wrath, when God’s righteous judgment will be revealed.

45:2:6.text: God “will repay each one according to his deeds.”

45:2:7.text: To those who by perseverance in doing good seek glory, honor, and immortality, He will give eternal life.

45:2:8.text: But for those who are self-seeking and who reject the truth and follow wickedness, there will be wrath and anger.

45:2:9.text: There will be trouble and distress for every human being who does evil, first for the Jew, then for the Greek;

45:3:1.text: What, then, is the advantage of being a Jew? Or what is the value of circumcision?

45:3:10.text: As it is written: “There is no one righteous, not even one.

45:3:11.text: There is no one who understands, no one who seeks God.

45:3:12.text: All have turned away, they have together become worthless; there is no one who does good, not even one.”

45:3:13.text: “Their throats are open graves; their tongues practice deceit.” “The venom of vipers is on their lips.”

45:3:14.text: “Their mouths are full of cursing and bitterness.”

45:3:15.text: “Their feet are swift to shed blood;

45:3:16.text: ruin and misery lie in their wake,

45:3:17.text: and the way of peace they have not known.”

45:3:18.text: “There is no fear of God before their eyes.”

45:3:19.text: Now we know that whatever the law says, it says to those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be silenced and the whole world held accountable to God.

45:3:2.text: Much in every way. First of all, they have been entrusted with the very words of God.

45:3:20.text: Therefore no one will be justified in His sight by works of the law. For the law merely brings awareness of sin.

45:3:21.text: But now, apart from the law, the righteousness of God has been revealed, as attested by the Law and the Prophets.

45:3:22.text: And this righteousness from God comes through faith in Jesus Christ to all who believe. There is no distinction,

45:3:23.text: for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God,

45:3:24.text: and are justified freely by His grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus.

45:3:25.text: God presented Him as the atoning sacrifice through faith in His blood, in order to demonstrate His righteousness, because in His forbearance He had passed over the sins committed beforehand.

45:3:26.text: He did this to demonstrate His righteousness at the present time, so as to be just and to justify the one who has faith in Jesus.

45:3:27.text: Where, then, is boasting? It is excluded. On what principle? On that of works? No, but on that of faith.

45:3:28.text: For we maintain that a man is justified by faith apart from works of the law.

45:3:29.text: Is God the God of Jews only? Is He not the God of Gentiles too? Yes, of Gentiles too,

45:3:3.text: What if some did not have faith? Will their lack of faith nullify God’s faithfulness?

45:3:30.text: since there is only one God, who will justify the circumcised by faith and the uncircumcised through that same faith.

45:3:31.text: Do we, then, nullify the law by this faith? Certainly not! Instead, we uphold the law.

45:3:4.text: Certainly not! Let God be true and every man a liar. As it is written: “So that You may be proved right when You speak and victorious when You judge.”

45:3:5.text: But if our unrighteousness highlights the righteousness of God, what shall we say? That God is unjust to inflict His wrath on us? I am speaking in human terms.

45:3:6.text: Certainly not! In that case, how could God judge the world?

45:3:7.text: However, if my falsehood accentuates God’s truthfulness, to the increase of His glory, why am I still condemned as a sinner?

45:3:8.text: Why not say, as some slanderously claim that we say, “Let us do evil that good may result”? Their condemnation is deserved!

45:3:9.text: What then? Are we any better? Not at all. For we have already made the charge that Jews and Greeks alike are all under sin.

45:4:1.text: What then shall we say that Abraham, our forefather, has discovered?

45:4:10.text: In what context was it credited? Was it after his circumcision, or before? It was not after, but before.

45:4:11.text: And he received the sign of circumcision as a seal of the righteousness that he had by faith while he was still uncircumcised. So then, he is the father of all who believe but are not circumcised, in order that righteousness might be credited to them.

45:4:12.text: And he is also the father of the circumcised who not only are circumcised, but who also walk in the footsteps of the faith that our father Abraham had before he was circumcised.

45:4:13.text: For the promise to Abraham and his offspring that he would be heir of the world was not given through the law, but through the righteousness that comes by faith.

45:4:14.text: For if those who live by the law are heirs, faith is useless and the promise is worthless,

45:4:15.text: because the law brings wrath. And where there is no law, there is no transgression.

45:4:16.text: Therefore, the promise comes by faith, so that it may rest on grace and may be guaranteed to all Abraham’s offspring — not only to those who are of the law, but also to those who are of the faith of Abraham. He is the father of us all.

45:4:17.text: As it is written: “I have made you a father of many nations.” He is our father in the presence of God, in whom he believed, the God who gives life to the dead and calls into being what does not yet exist.

45:4:18.text: Against all hope, Abraham in hope believed and so became the father of many nations, just as he had been told, “So shall your offspring be.”

45:4:19.text: Without weakening in his faith, he acknowledged the decrepitness of his body (since he was about a hundred years old) and the lifelessness of Sarah’s womb.

45:4:2.text: If Abraham was indeed justified by works, he had something to boast about, but not before God.

45:4:20.text: Yet he did not waver through disbelief in the promise of God, but was strengthened in his faith and gave glory to God,

45:4:21.text: being fully persuaded that God was able to do what He had promised.

45:4:22.text: This is why “it was credited to him as righteousness.”

45:4:23.text: Now the words “it was credited to him” were written not only for Abraham,

45:4:24.text: but also for us, to whom righteousness will be credited — for us who believe in Him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead.

45:4:25.text: He was delivered over to death for our trespasses and was raised to life for our justification.

45:4:3.text: For what does the Scripture say? “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.”

45:4:4.text: Now the wages of the worker are not credited as a gift, but as an obligation.

45:4:5.text: However, to the one who does not work, but believes in Him who justifies the wicked, his faith is credited as righteousness.

45:4:6.text: And David speaks likewise of the blessedness of the man to whom God credits righteousness apart from works:

45:4:7.text: “Blessed are they whose lawless acts are forgiven, whose sins are covered.

45:4:8.text: Blessed is the man whose sin the Lord will never count against him.”

45:4:9.text: Is this blessing only on the circumcised, or also on the uncircumcised? We have been saying that Abraham’s faith was credited to him as righteousness.

45:5:1.text: Therefore, since we have been justified through faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ,

45:5:10.text: For if, when we were enemies of God, we were reconciled to Him through the death of His Son, how much more, having been reconciled, shall we be saved through His life!

45:5:11.text: Not only that, but we also rejoice in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received reconciliation.

45:5:12.text: Therefore, just as sin entered the world through one man, and death through sin, so also death was passed on to all men, because all sinned.

45:5:13.text: For sin was in the world before the law was given; but sin is not taken into account when there is no law.

45:5:14.text: Nevertheless, death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over those who did not sin in the way that Adam transgressed. He is a pattern of the One to come.

45:5:15.text: But the gift is not like the trespass. For if the many died by the trespass of the one man, how much more did God’s grace and the gift that came by the grace of the one man, Jesus Christ, abound to the many!

45:5:16.text: Again, the gift is not like the result of the one man’s sin: The judgment that followed one sin brought condemnation, but the gift that followed many trespasses brought justification.

45:5:17.text: For if, by the trespass of the one man, death reigned through that one man, how much more will those who receive an abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness reign in life through the one man, Jesus Christ!

45:5:18.text: So then, just as one trespass brought condemnation for all men, so also one act of righteousness brought justification and life for all men.

45:5:19.text: For just as through the disobedience of the one man the many were made sinners, so also through the obedience of the one man the many will be made righteous.

45:5:2.text: through whom we have gained access by faith into this grace in which we stand. And we rejoice in the hope of the glory of God.

45:5:20.text: The law came in so that the trespass would increase; but where sin increased, grace increased all the more,

45:5:21.text: so that, just as sin reigned in death, so also grace might reign through righteousness to bring eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

45:5:3.text: Not only that, but we also rejoice in our sufferings, because we know that suffering produces perseverance;

45:5:5.text: And hope does not disappoint us, because God has poured out His love into our hearts through the Holy Spirit, whom He has given us.

45:5:6.text: For at just the right time, while we were still powerless, Christ died for the ungodly.

45:5:7.text: Very rarely will anyone die for a righteous man, though for a good man someone might possibly dare to die.

45:5:8.text: But God proves His love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.

45:5:9.text: Therefore, since we have now been justified by His blood, how much more shall we be saved from wrath through Him!

45:6:1.text: What then shall we say? Shall we continue in sin so that grace may increase?

45:6:10.text: The death He died, He died to sin once for all; but the life He lives, He lives to God.

45:6:11.text: So you too must count yourselves dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus.

45:6:12.text: Therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body so that you obey its desires.

45:6:13.text: Do not present the parts of your body to sin as instruments of wickedness, but present yourselves to God as those who have been brought from death to life; and present the parts of your body to Him as instruments of righteousness.

45:6:14.text: For sin shall not be your master, because you are not under law, but under grace.

45:6:15.text: What then? Shall we sin because we are not under law, but under grace? Certainly not!

45:6:16.text: Do you not know that when you offer yourselves as obedient slaves, you are slaves to the one you obey, whether you are slaves to sin leading to death, or to obedience leading to righteousness?

45:6:17.text: But thanks be to God that, though you once were slaves to sin, you wholeheartedly obeyed the form of teaching to which you were committed.

45:6:18.text: You have been set free from sin and have become slaves to righteousness.

45:6:19.text: I am speaking in human terms because of the weakness of your flesh. Just as you used to offer the parts of your body in slavery to impurity and to escalating wickedness, so now offer them in slavery to righteousness leading to holiness.

45:6:2.text: Certainly not! How can we who died to sin live in it any longer?

45:6:20.text: For when you were slaves to sin, you were free of obligation to righteousness.

45:6:21.text: What fruit did you reap at that time from the things of which you are now ashamed? The outcome of those things is death.

45:6:22.text: But now that you have been set free from sin and have become slaves to God, the fruit you reap leads to holiness, and the outcome is eternal life.

45:6:23.text: For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.

45:6:3.text: Or aren’t you aware that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into His death?

45:6:4.text: We were therefore buried with Him through baptism into death, in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, we too may walk in newness of life.

45:6:5.text: For if we have been united with Him like this in His death, we will certainly also be united with Him in His resurrection.

45:6:6.text: We know that our old self was crucified with Him so that the body of sin might be rendered powerless, that we should no longer be slaves to sin.

45:6:7.text: For anyone who has died has been freed from sin.

45:6:8.text: Now if we died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with Him.

45:6:9.text: For we know that since Christ was raised from the dead, He cannot die again; death no longer has dominion over Him.

45:7:1.text: Do you not know, brothers (for I am speaking to those who know the law), that the law has authority over a man only as long as he lives?

45:7:10.text: So I discovered that the very commandment that was meant to bring life actually brought death.

45:7:11.text: For sin, seizing its opportunity through the commandment, deceived me and through the commandment put me to death.

45:7:12.text: So then, the law is holy, and the commandment is holy, righteous, and good.

45:7:13.text: Did that which is good, then, become death to me? Certainly not! But in order that sin might be exposed as sin, it produced death in me through what was good, so that through the commandment sin might become utterly sinful.

45:7:14.text: We know that the law is spiritual; but I am unspiritual, sold as a slave to sin.

45:7:15.text: I do not understand what I do. For what I want to do, I do not do. But what I hate, I do.

45:7:16.text: And if I do what I do not want to do, I admit that the law is good.

45:7:17.text: In that case, it is no longer I who do it, but it is sin living in me that does it.

45:7:18.text: I know that nothing good lives in me, that is, in my flesh; for I have the desire to do what is good, but I cannot carry it out.

45:7:19.text: For I do not do the good I want to do. Instead, I keep on doing the evil I do not want to do.

45:7:2.text: For instance, a married woman is bound by law to her husband as long as he lives. But if her husband dies, she is released from the law of marriage.

45:7:20.text: And if I do what I do not want, it is no longer I who do it, but it is sin living in me that does it.

45:7:21.text: So this is the principle I have discovered: When I want to do good, evil is right there with me.

45:7:22.text: For in my inner being I delight in God’s law.

45:7:23.text: But I see another law at work in my body, warring against the law of my mind and holding me captive to the law of sin that dwells within me.

45:7:24.text: What a wretched man I am! Who will rescue me from this body of death?

45:7:25.text: Thanks be to God, through Jesus Christ our Lord! So then, with my mind I serve the law of God, but with my flesh I serve the law of sin.

45:7:3.text: So then, if she is joined to another man while her husband is still alive, she is called an adulteress; but if her husband dies, she is free from that law and is not an adulteress, even if she marries another man.

45:7:4.text: Therefore, my brothers, you also died to the law through the body of Christ, that you might belong to another, to Him who was raised from the dead, in order that we might bear fruit to God.

45:7:5.text: For when we lived according to the flesh, the sinful passions aroused by the law were at work in our bodies, bearing fruit for death.

45:7:6.text: But now, having died to what bound us, we have been released from the law, so that we serve in the new way of the Spirit, and not in the old way of the written code.

45:7:7.text: What then shall we say? Is the law sin? Certainly not! Indeed, I would not have been mindful of sin if not for the law. For I would not have been aware of coveting if the law had not said, “Do not covet.”

45:7:8.text: But sin, seizing its opportunity through the commandment, produced in me every kind of covetous desire. For apart from the law, sin is dead.

45:7:9.text: Once I was alive apart from the law; but when the commandment came, sin sprang to life and I died.

45:8:1.text: Therefore, there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.

45:8:10.text: But if Christ is in you, your body is dead because of sin, yet your spirit is alive because of righteousness.

45:8:11.text: And if the Spirit of Him who raised Jesus from the dead is living in you, He who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through His Spirit, who lives in you.

45:8:12.text: Therefore, brothers, we have an obligation, but it is not to the flesh, to live according to it.

45:8:13.text: For if you live according to the flesh, you will die; but if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will live.

45:8:14.text: For all who are led by the Spirit of God are sons of God.

45:8:15.text: For you did not receive a spirit of slavery that returns you to fear, but you received the Spirit of sonship, by whom we cry, “Abba! Father!”

45:8:16.text: The Spirit Himself testifies with our spirit that we are God’s children.

45:8:17.text: And if we are children, then we are heirs: heirs of God and co-heirs with Christ — if indeed we suffer with Him, so that we may also be glorified with Him.

45:8:18.text: I consider that our present sufferings are not comparable to the glory that will be revealed in us.

45:8:19.text: The creation waits in eager expectation for the revelation of the sons of God.

45:8:2.text: For in Christ Jesus the law of the Spirit of life set you free from the law of sin and death.

45:8:20.text: For the creation was subjected to futility, not by its own will, but because of the One who subjected it, in hope

45:8:21.text: that the creation itself will be set free from its bondage to decay and brought into the glorious freedom of the children of God.

45:8:22.text: We know that the whole creation has been groaning together in the pains of childbirth until the present time.

45:8:23.text: Not only that, but we ourselves, who have the firstfruits of the Spirit, groan inwardly as we wait eagerly for our adoption as sons, the redemption of our bodies.

45:8:24.text: For in this hope we were saved; but hope that is seen is no hope at all. Who hopes for what he can already see?

45:8:25.text: But if we hope for what we do not yet see, we wait for it patiently.

45:8:26.text: In the same way, the Spirit helps us in our weakness. For we do not know how we ought to pray, but the Spirit Himself intercedes for us with groans too deep for words.

45:8:27.text: And He who searches our hearts knows the mind of the Spirit, because the Spirit intercedes for the saints according to the will of God.

45:8:28.text: And we know that God works all things together for the good of those who love Him, who are called according to His purpose.

45:8:29.text: For those God foreknew, He also predestined to be conformed to the image of His Son, so that He would be the firstborn among many brothers.

45:8:3.text: For what the law was powerless to do in that it was weakened by the flesh, God did by sending His own Son in the likeness of sinful man, as an offering for sin. He thus condemned sin in the flesh,

45:8:30.text: And those He predestined, He also called; those He called, He also justified; those He justified, He also glorified.

45:8:31.text: What then shall we say in response to these things? If God is for us, who can be against us?

45:8:32.text: He who did not spare His own Son but gave Him up for us all, how will He not also, along with Him, freely give us all things?

45:8:33.text: Who will bring any charge against God’s elect? It is God who justifies.

45:8:34.text: Who is there to condemn us? For Christ Jesus, who died, and more than that was raised to life, is at the right hand of God — and He is interceding for us.

45:8:35.text: Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Shall trouble or distress or persecution or famine or nakedness or danger or sword?

45:8:36.text: As it is written: “For Your sake we face death all day long; we are considered as sheep to be slaughtered.”

45:8:37.text: No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through Him who loved us.

45:8:38.text: For I am convinced that neither death nor life, neither angels nor principalities, neither the present nor the future, nor any powers,

45:8:39.text: neither height nor depth, nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

45:8:4.text: so that the righteous standard of the law might be fulfilled in us, who do not walk according to the flesh but according to the Spirit.

45:8:5.text: Those who live according to the flesh set their minds on the things of the flesh; but those who live according to the Spirit set their minds on the things of the Spirit.

45:8:6.text: The mind of the flesh is death, but the mind of the Spirit is life and peace,

45:8:7.text: because the mind of the flesh is hostile to God: It does not submit to God’s law, nor can it do so.

45:8:8.text: Those controlled by the flesh cannot please God.

45:8:9.text: You, however, are controlled not by the flesh, but by the Spirit, if the Spirit of God lives in you. And if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, he does not belong to Christ.

45:9:1.text: I speak the truth in Christ; I am not lying, as confirmed by my conscience in the Holy Spirit.

45:9:10.text: Not only that, but Rebecca’s children were conceived by one man, our father Isaac.

45:9:11.text: Yet before the twins were born or had done anything good or bad, in order that God’s plan of election might stand,

45:9:12.text: not by works but by Him who calls, she was told, “The older will serve the younger.”

45:9:13.text: So it is written: “Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated.”

45:9:14.text: What then shall we say? Is God unjust? Certainly not!

45:9:15.text: For He says to Moses: “I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I have compassion.”

45:9:16.text: So then, it does not depend on man’s desire or effort, but on God’s mercy.

45:9:17.text: For the Scripture says to Pharaoh: “I raised you up for this very purpose, that I might display My power in you, and that My name might be proclaimed in all the earth.”

45:9:18.text: Therefore God has mercy on whom He wants to have mercy, and He hardens whom He wants to harden.

45:9:19.text: One of you will say to me, “Then why does God still find fault? For who can resist His will?”

45:9:2.text: I have deep sorrow and unceasing anguish in my heart.

45:9:20.text: But who are you, O man, to talk back to God? Shall what is formed say to Him who formed it, “Why did You make me like this?”

45:9:21.text: Does not the potter have the right to make from the same lump of clay one vessel for special occasions and another for common use?

45:9:22.text: What if God, intending to show His wrath and make His power known, bore with great patience the vessels of His wrath, prepared for destruction?

45:9:23.text: What if He did this to make the riches of His glory known to the vessels of His mercy, whom He prepared in advance for glory —

45:9:24.text: including us, whom He has called not only from the Jews, but also from the Gentiles?

45:9:25.text: As He says in Hosea: “I will call them ‘My People’ who are not My people, and I will call her ‘My Beloved’ who is not My beloved,”

45:9:26.text: and, “It will happen that in the very place where it was said to them, ‘You are not My people,’they will be called‘ sons of the living God.’ ”

45:9:27.text: Isaiah cries out concerning Israel: “Though the number of the Israelites is like the sand of the sea, only the remnant will be saved.

45:9:28.text: For the Lord will carry out His sentence on the earth thoroughly and decisively.”

45:9:29.text: It is just as Isaiah foretold: “Unless the Lord of Hosts had left us descendants, we would have become like Sodom, we would have resembled Gomorrah.”

45:9:3.text: For I could wish that I myself were cursed and cut off from Christ for the sake of my brothers, my own flesh and blood,

45:9:30.text: What then will we say? That the Gentiles, who did not pursue righteousness, have obtained it, a righteousness that is by faith;

45:9:31.text: but Israel, who pursued a law of righteousness, has not attained it.

45:9:32.text: Why not? Because their pursuit was not by faith, but as if it were by works. They stumbled over the stumbling stone,

45:9:33.text: as it is written: “See, I lay in Zion a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense; and the one who believes in Him will never be put to shame.”

45:9:4.text: the people of Israel. Theirs is the adoption as sons; theirs the divine glory and the covenants; theirs the giving of the law, the temple worship, and the promises.

45:9:5.text: Theirs are the patriarchs, and from them proceeds the human descent of Christ, who is God over all, forever worthy of praise! Amen.

45:9:6.text: It is not as though God’s word has failed. For not all who are descended from Israel are Israel.

45:9:7.text: Nor because they are Abraham’s descendants are they all his children. On the contrary, “Through Isaac your offspring will be reckoned.”

45:9:8.text: So it is not the children of the flesh who are God’s children, but it is the children of the promise who are regarded as offspring.

45:9:9.text: For this is what the promise stated: “At the appointed time I will return, and Sarah will have a son.”

46:10:1.text: I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, that our forefathers were all under the cloud, and that they all passed through the sea.

46:10:10.text: And do not complain, as some of them did, and were killed by the destroying angel.

46:10:11.text: Now these things happened to them as examples and were written down as warnings for us, on whom the fulfillment of the ages has come.

46:10:12.text: So the one who thinks he is standing firm should be careful not to fall.

46:10:13.text: No temptation has seized you except what is common to man. And God is faithful; He will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear. But when you are tempted, He will also provide an escape, so that you can stand up under it.

46:10:14.text: Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.

46:10:15.text: I speak to reasonable people; judge for yourselves what I say.

46:10:16.text: Is not the cup of blessing that we bless a participation in the blood of Christ? And is not the bread that we break a participation in the body of Christ?

46:10:17.text: Because there is one loaf, we who are many are one body; for we all partake of the one loaf.

46:10:18.text: Consider the people of Israel: Are not those who eat the sacrifices fellow partakers in the altar?

46:10:19.text: Am I suggesting, then, that food sacrificed to an idol is anything, or that an idol is anything?

46:10:2.text: They were all baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea.

46:10:20.text: No, but the sacrifices of pagans are offered to demons, not to God. And I do not want you to be participants with demons.

46:10:21.text: You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons too; you cannot partake in the table of the Lord and the table of demons too.

46:10:22.text: Are we trying to provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than He?

46:10:23.text: “Everything is permissible,” but not everything is beneficial. “Everything is permissible,” but not everything is edifying.

46:10:24.text: No one should seek his own good, but the good of others.

46:10:25.text: Eat anything sold in the meat market without raising questions of conscience,

46:10:26.text: for, “The earth is the Lord’s, and the fullness thereof.”

46:10:27.text: If an unbeliever invites you to a meal and you want to go, eat anything set before you without raising questions of conscience.

46:10:28.text: But if someone tells you, “This food was offered to idols,” then do not eat it, for the sake of the one who told you and for the sake of conscience —

46:10:29.text: the other one’s conscience, I mean, not your own. For why should my freedom be determined by someone else’s conscience?

46:10:3.text: They all ate the same spiritual food

46:10:30.text: If I partake in the meal with thankfulness, why am I denounced because of that for which I give thanks?

46:10:31.text: So whether you eat or drink or whatever you do, do it all to the glory of God.

46:10:32.text: Do not become a stumbling block, whether to Jews or Greeks or the church of God —

46:10:33.text: as I also try to please everyone in all I do. For I am not seeking my own good, but the good of many, that they may be saved.

46:10:4.text: and drank the same spiritual drink; for they drank from the spiritual rock that accompanied them, and that rock was Christ.

46:10:5.text: Nevertheless, God was not pleased with most of them, for they were struck down in the wilderness.

46:10:6.text: These things took place as examples to keep us from craving evil things as they did.

46:10:7.text: Do not be idolaters, as some of them were. As it is written: “The people sat down to eat and to drink, and got up to indulge in revelry.”

46:10:8.text: We should not commit sexual immorality, as some of them did, and in one day twenty-three thousand of them died.

46:10:9.text: We should not test Christ, as some of them did, and were killed by snakes.

46:11:1.text: You are to imitate me, just as I imitate Christ.

46:11:10.text: For this reason a woman ought to have a sign of authority on her head, because of the angels.

46:11:11.text: In the Lord, however, woman is not independent of man, nor is man independent of woman.

46:11:12.text: For just as woman came from man, so also man is born of woman. But everything comes from God.

46:11:13.text: Judge for yourselves: Is it proper for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?

46:11:14.text: Doesn’t nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair, it is a disgrace to him,

46:11:15.text: but that if a woman has long hair, it is her glory? For long hair is given to her as a covering.

46:11:16.text: If anyone is inclined to dispute this, we have no other practice, nor do the churches of God.

46:11:17.text: In the following instructions I have no praise to offer, because your gatherings do more harm than good.

46:11:18.text: First of all, I hear that when you come together as a church, there are divisions among you, and in part I believe it.

46:11:19.text: And indeed, there must be differences among you to show which of you are approved.

46:11:2.text: Now I commend you for remembering me in everything and for maintaining the traditions, just as I passed them on to you.

46:11:20.text: Now then, when you come together, it is not the Lord’s Supper you eat.

46:11:21.text: For as you eat, each of you goes ahead without sharing his meal. While one remains hungry, another gets drunk.

46:11:22.text: Don’t you have your own homes in which to eat and drink? Or do you despise the church of God and humiliate those who have nothing? What can I say to you? Shall I praise you for this? No, I will not!

46:11:23.text: For I received from the Lord what I also passed on to you: The Lord Jesus, on the night He was betrayed, took bread,

46:11:24.text: and when He had given thanks, He broke it and said, “This is My body, which is for you; do this in remembrance of Me.”

46:11:25.text: In the same way, after supper He took the cup, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood; do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of Me.”

46:11:26.text: For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until He comes.

46:11:27.text: Therefore, whoever eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord in an unworthy manner will be guilty of sinning against the body and blood of the Lord.

46:11:28.text: Each one must examine himself before he eats of the bread and drinks of the cup.

46:11:29.text: For anyone who eats and drinks without recognizing the body eats and drinks judgment on himself.

46:11:3.text: But I want you to understand that the head of every man is Christ, and the head of the woman is man, and the head of Christ is God.

46:11:30.text: That is why many among you are weak and sick, and a number of you have fallen asleep.

46:11:31.text: Now if we judged ourselves properly, we would not come under judgment.

46:11:32.text: But when we are judged by the Lord, we are being disciplined so that we will not be condemned with the world.

46:11:33.text: So, my brothers, when you come together to eat, wait for one another.

46:11:34.text: If anyone is hungry, he should eat at home, so that when you come together it will not result in judgment. And when I come, I will give instructions about the remaining matters.

46:11:4.text: Every man who prays or prophesies with his head covered dishonors his head.

46:11:5.text: And every woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered dishonors her head, for it is just as if her head were shaved.

46:11:6.text: If a woman does not cover her head, she should have her hair cut off. And if it is shameful for a woman to have her hair cut or shaved off, she should cover her head.

46:11:7.text: A man ought not to cover his head, since he is the image and glory of God; but the woman is the glory of man.

46:11:8.text: For man did not come from woman, but woman from man.

46:11:9.text: Neither was man created for woman, but woman for man.

46:12:1.text: Now about spiritual gifts, brothers, I do not want you to be uninformed.

46:12:10.text: to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another distinguishing between spirits, to another speaking in various tongues, and to still another the interpretation of tongues.

46:12:11.text: All these are the work of one and the same Spirit, who apportions them to each one as He determines.

46:12:12.text: The body is a unit, though it is composed of many parts. And although its parts are many, they all form one body. So it is with Christ.

46:12:13.text: For in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, slave or free, and we were all given one Spirit to drink.

46:12:14.text: For the body does not consist of one part, but of many.

46:12:15.text: If the foot should say, “Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body,” that would not make it any less a part of the body.

46:12:16.text: And if the ear should say, “Because I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body,” that would not make it any less a part of the body.

46:12:17.text: If the whole body were an eye, where would the sense of hearing be? If the whole body were an ear, where would the sense of smell be?

46:12:18.text: But in fact, God has arranged the members of the body, every one of them, according to His design.

46:12:19.text: If they were all one part, where would the body be?

46:12:2.text: You know that when you were pagans, you were influenced and led astray to mute idols.

46:12:20.text: As it is, there are many parts, but one body.

46:12:21.text: The eye cannot say to the hand, “I do not need you.” Nor can the head say to the feet, “I do not need you.”

46:12:22.text: On the contrary, the parts of the body that seem to be weaker are indispensable,

46:12:23.text: and the parts we consider less honorable, we treat with greater honor. And our unpresentable parts are treated with special modesty,

46:12:24.text: whereas our presentable parts have no such need. But God has composed the body and has given greater honor to the parts that lacked it,

46:12:25.text: so that there should be no division in the body, but that its members should have mutual concern for one another.

46:12:26.text: If one part suffers, every part suffers with it; if one part is honored, every part rejoices with it.

46:12:27.text: Now you are the body of Christ, and each of you is a member of it.

46:12:28.text: And in the church God has appointed first of all apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then workers of miracles, and those with gifts of healing, helping, administration, and various tongues.

46:12:29.text: Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Do all work miracles?

46:12:3.text: Therefore I inform you that no one who is speaking by the Spirit of God says, “Jesus be cursed,” and no one can say, “Jesus is Lord,” except by the Holy Spirit.

46:12:30.text: Do all have gifts of healing? Do all speak in tongues? Do all interpret?

46:12:31.text: But eagerly desire the greater gifts. And now I will show you the most excellent way.

46:12:4.text: There are different gifts, but the same Spirit.

46:12:5.text: There are different ministries, but the same Lord.

46:12:6.text: There are different ways of working, but the same God works all things in all people.

46:12:7.text: Now to each one the manifestation of the Spirit is given for the common good.

46:12:8.text: To one there is given through the Spirit the message of wisdom, to another the message of knowledge by the same Spirit,

46:12:9.text: to another faith by the same Spirit, to another gifts of healing by that one Spirit,

46:13:1.text: If I speak in the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I am only a ringing gong or a clanging cymbal.

46:13:10.text: but when the perfect comes, the partial passes away.

46:13:11.text: When I was a child, I talked like a child, I thought like a child, I reasoned like a child. When I became a man, I set aside childish ways.

46:13:12.text: Now we see but a dim reflection as in a mirror; then we shall see face to face. Now I know in part; then I shall know fully, even as I am fully known.

46:13:13.text: And now these three remain: faith, hope, and love; but the greatest of these is love.

46:13:2.text: If I have the gift of prophecy and can fathom all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have absolute faith so as to move mountains, but have not love, I am nothing.

46:13:3.text: If I give all I possess to the poor and exult in the surrender of my body, but have not love, I gain nothing.

46:13:4.text: Love is patient, love is kind. It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud.

46:13:5.text: It is not rude, it is not self-seeking, it is not easily angered, it keeps no account of wrongs.

46:13:6.text: Love takes no pleasure in evil, but rejoices in the truth.

46:13:7.text: It bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.

46:13:8.text: Love never fails. But where there are prophecies, they will cease; where there are tongues, they will be restrained; where there is knowledge, it will be dismissed.

46:13:9.text: For we know in part and we prophesy in part,

46:14:1.text: Earnestly pursue love and eagerly desire spiritual gifts, especially the gift of prophecy.

46:14:10.text: Assuredly, there are many different languages in the world, yet none of them is without meaning.

46:14:11.text: If, then, I do not know the meaning of someone’s language, I am a foreigner to the speaker, and he is a foreigner to me.

46:14:12.text: It is the same with you. Since you are eager to have spiritual gifts, strive to excel in gifts that build up the church.

46:14:13.text: Therefore, the one who speaks in a tongue should pray that he may interpret.

46:14:14.text: For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays, but my mind is unfruitful.

46:14:15.text: What then shall I do? I will pray with my spirit, but I will also pray with my mind. I will sing with my spirit, but I will also sing with my mind.

46:14:16.text: Otherwise, if you speak a blessing in spirit, how can someone who is uninstructed say “Amen” to your thanksgiving, since he does not know what you are saying?

46:14:17.text: You may be giving thanks well enough, but the other one is not edified.

46:14:18.text: I thank God that I speak in tongues more than all of you.

46:14:19.text: But in the church, I would rather speak five coherent words to instruct others than ten thousand words in a tongue.

46:14:2.text: For he who speaks in a tongue does not speak to men, but to God. Indeed, no one understands him; he utters mysteries in the Spirit.

46:14:20.text: Brothers, stop thinking like children. In regard to evil be infants, but in your thinking be mature.

46:14:21.text: It is written in the Law: “By strange tongues and foreign lips I will speak to this people, but even then they will not listen to Me, says the Lord.”

46:14:22.text: Tongues, then, are a sign, not for believers, but for unbelievers. Prophecy, however, is for believers, not for unbelievers.

46:14:23.text: So if the whole church comes together and everyone speaks in tongues, and some who are uninstructed or some unbelievers come in, will they not say that you are out of your minds?

46:14:24.text: But if an unbeliever or uninstructed person comes in while everyone is prophesying, he will be convicted and called to account by all,

46:14:25.text: and the secrets of his heart will be made known. So he will fall facedown and worship God, proclaiming, “God is truly among you!”

46:14:26.text: What then shall we say, brothers? When you come together, everyone has a psalm or a teaching, a revelation, a tongue, or an interpretation. All of these must be done to build up the church.

46:14:27.text: If anyone speaks in a tongue, two, or at most three, should speak in turn, and someone must interpret.

46:14:28.text: But if there is no interpreter, he should remain silent in the church and speak only to himself and God.

46:14:29.text: Two or three prophets should speak, and the others should weigh carefully what is said.

46:14:3.text: But he who prophesies speaks to men for their edification, encouragement, and comfort.

46:14:30.text: And if a revelation comes to someone who is seated, the first speaker should stop.

46:14:31.text: For you can all prophesy in turn so that everyone may be instructed and encouraged.

46:14:32.text: The spirits of prophets are subject to prophets.

46:14:33.text: For God is not a God of disorder, but of peace — as in all the churches of the saints.

46:14:34.text: Women are to be silent in the churches. They are not permitted to speak, but must be in submission, as the law says.

46:14:35.text: If they wish to inquire about something, they are to ask their own husbands at home; for it is dishonorable for a woman to speak in the church.

46:14:36.text: Did the word of God originate with you? Or are you the only ones it has reached?

46:14:37.text: If anyone considers himself a prophet or spiritual person, let him acknowledge that what I am writing you is the Lord’s command.

46:14:38.text: But if anyone ignores this, he himself will be ignored.

46:14:39.text: So, my brothers, be eager to prophesy, and do not forbid speaking in tongues.

46:14:4.text: The one who speaks in a tongue edifies himself, but the one who prophesies edifies the church.

46:14:40.text: But everything must be done in a proper and orderly manner.

46:14:5.text: I wish that all of you could speak in tongues, but I would rather have you prophesy. He who prophesies is greater than one who speaks in tongues, unless he interprets so that the church may be edified.

46:14:6.text: Now, brothers, if I come to you speaking in tongues, how will I benefit you, unless I bring you some revelation or knowledge or prophecy or teaching?

46:14:7.text: Even in the case of lifeless instruments, such as the flute or harp, how will anyone recognize the tune they are playing unless the notes are distinct?

46:14:8.text: Again, if the trumpet sounds a muffled call, who will prepare for battle?

46:14:9.text: So it is with you. Unless you speak intelligible words with your tongue, how will anyone know what you are saying? You will just be speaking into the air.

46:15:1.text: Now, brothers, I want to remind you of the gospel I preached to you, which you received, and in which you stand firm.

46:15:10.text: But by the grace of God I am what I am, and His grace to me was not in vain. No, I worked harder than all of them — yet not I, but the grace of God that was with me.

46:15:11.text: Whether, then, it was I or they, this is what we preach, and this is what you believed.

46:15:12.text: But if it is preached that Christ has been raised from the dead, how can some of you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?

46:15:13.text: If there is no resurrection of the dead, then not even Christ has been raised.

46:15:14.text: And if Christ has not been raised, our preaching is worthless, and so is your faith.

46:15:15.text: In that case, we are also exposed as false witnesses about God. For we have testified about God that He raised Christ from the dead, but He did not raise Him if in fact the dead are not raised.

46:15:16.text: For if the dead are not raised, then not even Christ has been raised.

46:15:17.text: And if Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile; you are still in your sins.

46:15:18.text: Then those also who have fallen asleep in Christ have perished.

46:15:19.text: If our hope in Christ is for this life alone, we are to be pitied more than all men.

46:15:2.text: By this gospel you are saved, if you hold firmly to the word I preached to you. Otherwise, you have believed in vain.

46:15:20.text: But Christ has indeed been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.

46:15:21.text: For since death came through a man, the resurrection of the dead comes also through a man.

46:15:22.text: For as in Adam all die, so in Christ all will be made alive.

46:15:23.text: But each in his own turn: Christ the firstfruits; then at His coming, those who belong to Him.

46:15:24.text: Then the end will come, when He hands over the kingdom to God the Father after He has destroyed all dominion, authority, and power.

46:15:25.text: For He must reign until He has put all His enemies under His feet.

46:15:26.text: The last enemy to be destroyed is death.

46:15:27.text: For “God has put everything under His feet.” Now when it says that everything has been put under Him, this clearly does not include the One who put everything under Him.

46:15:28.text: And when all things have been subjected to Him, then the Son Himself will be made subject to Him who put all things under Him, so that God may be all in all.

46:15:29.text: If these things are not so, what will those do who are baptized for the dead? If the dead are not raised at all, why are people baptized for them?

46:15:3.text: For what I received I passed on to you as of first importance: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures,

46:15:30.text: And why do we endanger ourselves every hour?

46:15:31.text: I face death every day, brothers, as surely as I boast about you in Christ Jesus our Lord.

46:15:32.text: If I fought wild beasts in Ephesus for human motives, what did I gain? If the dead are not raised, “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.”

46:15:33.text: Do not be deceived: “Bad company corrupts good character.”

46:15:34.text: Sober up as you ought, and stop sinning; for some of you are ignorant of God. I say this to your shame.

46:15:35.text: But someone will ask, “How are the dead raised? With what kind of body will they come?”

46:15:36.text: You fool! What you sow does not come to life unless it dies.

46:15:37.text: And what you sow is not the body that will be, but just a seed, perhaps of wheat or something else.

46:15:38.text: But God gives it a body as He has designed, and to each kind of seed He gives its own body.

46:15:39.text: Not all flesh is the same: Men have one kind of flesh, animals have another, birds another, and fish another.

46:15:4.text: that He was buried, that He was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures,

46:15:40.text: There are also heavenly bodies and earthly bodies. But the splendor of the heavenly bodies is of one degree, and the splendor of the earthly bodies is of another.

46:15:41.text: The sun has one degree of splendor, the moon another, and the stars another; and star differs from star in splendor.

46:15:42.text: So will it be with the resurrection of the dead: What is sown is perishable; it is raised imperishable.

46:15:43.text: It is sown in dishonor; it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness; it is raised in power.

46:15:44.text: It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body. If there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual body.

46:15:45.text: So it is written: “The first man Adam became a living being;” the last Adam a life-giving spirit.

46:15:46.text: The spiritual, however, was not first, but the natural, and then the spiritual.

46:15:47.text: The first man was of the dust of the earth, the second man from heaven.

46:15:48.text: As was the earthly man, so also are those who are of the earth; and as is the heavenly man, so also are those who are of heaven.

46:15:49.text: And just as we have borne the likeness of the earthly man, so also shall we bear the likeness of the heavenly man.

46:15:5.text: and that He appeared to Cephas and then to the Twelve.

46:15:50.text: Now I declare to you, brothers, that flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God, nor does the perishable inherit the imperishable.

46:15:51.text: Listen, I tell you a mystery: We will not all sleep, but we will all be changed —

46:15:52.text: in an instant, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, the dead will be raised imperishable, and we will be changed.

46:15:53.text: For the perishable must be clothed with the imperishable, and the mortal with immortality.

46:15:54.text: When the perishable has been clothed with the imperishable and the mortal with immortality, then the saying that is written will come to pass: “Death has been swallowed up in victory.”

46:15:55.text: “Where, O Death, is your victory? Where, O Death, is your sting?”

46:15:56.text: The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.

46:15:57.text: But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ!

46:15:58.text: Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast and immovable. Always excel in the work of the Lord, because you know that your labor in the Lord is not in vain.

46:15:6.text: After that, He appeared to more than five hundred brothers at once, most of whom are still living, though some have fallen asleep.

46:15:7.text: Then He appeared to James, then to all the apostles.

46:15:8.text: And last of all He appeared to me also, as to one of untimely birth.

46:15:9.text: For I am the least of the apostles and am unworthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.

46:16:1.text: Now about the collection for the saints, you are to do as I directed the churches of Galatia:

46:16:10.text: If Timothy comes, see to it that he has nothing to fear while he is with you, for he is doing the work of the Lord, just as I am.

46:16:11.text: No one, then, should treat him with contempt. Send him on his way in peace so that he can return to me, for I am expecting him along with the brothers.

46:16:12.text: Now about our brother Apollos: I strongly urged him to go to you with the brothers. He was not at all inclined to go now, but he will go when he has the opportunity.

46:16:13.text: Be on the alert. Stand firm in the faith. Be men of courage. Be strong.

46:16:15.text: You know that Stephanas and his household were the first converts in Achaia, and they have devoted themselves to the service of the saints. Now I urge you, brothers,

46:16:16.text: to submit to such as these, and to every fellow worker and laborer.

46:16:17.text: I am glad that Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus have arrived, because they have supplied what was lacking from you.

46:16:18.text: For they refreshed my spirit and yours as well. Show your appreciation, therefore, to such men.

46:16:19.text: The churches in the province of Asia send you greetings. Aquila and Prisca greet you warmly in the Lord, and so does the church that meets at their house.

46:16:2.text: On the first day of every week, each of you should set aside a portion of his income, saving it up, so that when I come no collections will be needed.

46:16:20.text: All the brothers here send you greetings. Greet one another with a holy kiss.

46:16:21.text: This greeting is in my own hand — Paul.

46:16:22.text: If anyone does not love the Lord, let him be under a curse. Come, O Lord!

46:16:23.text: The grace of the Lord Jesus be with you.

46:16:24.text: My love be with all of you in Christ Jesus. Amen.

46:16:3.text: Then, on my arrival, I will send letters with those you recommend to carry your gift to Jerusalem.

46:16:4.text: And if it is advisable for me to go also, they can travel with me.

46:16:5.text: After I go through Macedonia, however, I will come to you; for I will be going through Macedonia.

46:16:6.text: Perhaps I will stay with you awhile, or even spend the winter, so that you can help me on my journey, wherever I go.

46:16:7.text: For I do not want to see you now only in passing; I hope to spend some time with you, if the Lord permits.

46:16:8.text: But I will stay in Ephesus until Pentecost,

46:16:9.text: because a great door for effective work has opened to me, even though many oppose me.

46:1:1.text: Paul, called to be an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and our brother Sosthenes,

46:1:10.text: I appeal to you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that all of you agree together, so that there may be no divisions among you and that you may be united in mind and conviction.

46:1:11.text: My brothers, some from Chloe’s household have informed me that there are quarrels among you.

46:1:12.text: What I mean is this: Individuals among you are saying, “I follow Paul,” “I follow Apollos,” “I follow Cephas,” or “I follow Christ.”

46:1:13.text: Is Christ divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Were you baptized into the name of Paul?

46:1:14.text: I thank God that I did not baptize any of you except Crispus and Gaius,

46:1:15.text: so no one can say that you were baptized into my name.

46:1:16.text: Yes, I also baptized the household of Stephanas; beyond that I do not remember if I baptized anyone else.

46:1:17.text: For Christ did not send me to baptize, but to preach the gospel, not with words of wisdom, lest the cross of Christ be emptied of its power.

46:1:18.text: For the message of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.

46:1:19.text: For it is written: “I will destroy the wisdom of the wise; the intelligence of the intelligent I will frustrate.”
