46:1:2.text: To the church of God in Corinth, to those sanctified in Christ Jesus and called to be holy, together with all those everywhere who call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, their Lord and ours:

46:1:20.text: Where is the wise man? Where is the scribe? Where is the philosopher of this age? Has not God made foolish the wisdom of the world?

46:1:21.text: For since in the wisdom of God the world through its wisdom did not know Him, God was pleased through the foolishness of what was preached to save those who believe.

46:1:22.text: Jews demand signs and Greeks search for wisdom,

46:1:23.text: but we preach Christ crucified, a stumbling block to Jews and foolishness to Gentiles,

46:1:24.text: but to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God.

46:1:25.text: For the foolishness of God is wiser than man’s wisdom, and the weakness of God is stronger than man’s strength.

46:1:26.text: Brothers, consider the time of your calling: Not many of you were wise by human standards; not many were powerful; not many were of noble birth.

46:1:27.text: But God chose the foolish things of the world to shame the wise; God chose the weak things of the world to shame the strong.

46:1:28.text: He chose the lowly and despised things of the world, and the things that are not, to nullify the things that are,

46:1:29.text: so that no one may boast in His presence.

46:1:3.text: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

46:1:30.text: It is because of Him that you are in Christ Jesus, who has become for us wisdom from God: our righteousness, holiness, and redemption.

46:1:31.text: Therefore, as it is written: “Let him who boasts boast in the Lord.”

46:1:4.text: I always thank my God for you because of the grace He has given you in Christ Jesus.

46:1:5.text: For in Him you have been enriched in every way, in all speech and all knowledge,

46:1:6.text: because our testimony about Christ was confirmed in you.

46:1:7.text: Therefore you do not lack any spiritual gift as you eagerly await the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ.

46:1:8.text: He will sustain you to the end, so that you will be blameless on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.

46:1:9.text: God, who has called you into fellowship with His Son Jesus Christ our Lord, is faithful.

46:2:1.text: When I came to you, brothers, I did not come with eloquence or wisdom as I proclaimed to you the testimony about God.

46:2:10.text: But God has revealed it to us by the Spirit. The Spirit searches all things, even the deep things of God.

46:2:11.text: For who among men knows the thoughts of man except his own spirit within him? So too, no one knows the thoughts of God except the Spirit of God.

46:2:12.text: We have not received the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who is from God, that we may understand what God has freely given us.

46:2:13.text: And this is what we speak, not in words taught us by human wisdom, but in words taught by the Spirit, expressing spiritual truths in spiritual words.

46:2:14.text: The natural man does not accept the things that come from the Spirit of God. For they are foolishness to him, and he cannot understand them, because they are spiritually discerned.

46:2:15.text: The spiritual man judges all things, but he himself is not subject to anyone’s judgment.

46:2:16.text: “For who has known the mind of the Lord, so as to instruct Him?” But we have the mind of Christ.

46:2:2.text: For I resolved to know nothing while I was with you except Jesus Christ and Him crucified.

46:2:3.text: I came to you in weakness and fear, and with much trembling.

46:2:4.text: My message and my preaching were not with persuasive words of wisdom, but with a demonstration of the Spirit’s power,

46:2:5.text: so that your faith would not rest on men’s wisdom, but on God’s power.

46:2:6.text: Among the mature, however, we speak a message of wisdom — but not the wisdom of this age or of the rulers of this age, who are coming to nothing.

46:2:7.text: No, we speak of the mysterious and hidden wisdom of God, which He destined for our glory before time began.

46:2:8.text: None of the rulers of this age understood it. For if they had, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.

46:2:9.text: Rather, as it is written: “No eye has seen, no ear has heard, no heart has imagined, what God has prepared for those who love Him.”

46:3:1.text: Brothers, I could not address you as spiritual, but as worldly — as infants in Christ.

46:3:10.text: By the grace God has given me, I laid a foundation as an expert builder, and someone else is building on it. But each one must be careful how he builds.

46:3:11.text: For no one can lay a foundation other than the one already laid, which is Jesus Christ.

46:3:12.text: If anyone builds on this foundation using gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, or straw,

46:3:13.text: his workmanship will be evident, because the Day will bring it to light. It will be revealed with fire, and the fire will prove the quality of each man’s work.

46:3:14.text: If what he has built survives, he will receive a reward.

46:3:15.text: If it is burned up, he will suffer loss. He himself will be saved, but only as if through the flames.

46:3:16.text: Do you not know that you yourselves are God’s temple, and that God’s Spirit dwells in you?

46:3:17.text: If anyone destroys God’s temple, God will destroy him; for God’s temple is holy, and you are that temple.

46:3:18.text: Let no one deceive himself. If any of you thinks he is wise in this age, he should become a fool, so that he may become wise.

46:3:19.text: For the wisdom of this world is foolishness in God’s sight. As it is written: “He catches the wise in their craftiness.”

46:3:2.text: I gave you milk, not solid food, for you were not yet ready for solid food. In fact, you are still not ready,

46:3:20.text: And again, “The Lord knows that the thoughts of the wise are futile.”

46:3:21.text: Therefore, stop boasting in men. All things are yours,

46:3:22.text: whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas or the world or life or death or the present or the future. All of them belong to you,

46:3:23.text: and you belong to Christ, and Christ belongs to God.

46:3:3.text: for you are still worldly. For since there is jealousy and dissension among you, are you not worldly? Are you not walking in the way of man?

46:3:4.text: For when one of you says, “I follow Paul,” and another, “I follow Apollos,” are you not mere men?

46:3:5.text: What then is Apollos? And what is Paul? They are servants through whom you believed, as the Lord has assigned to each his role.

46:3:6.text: I planted the seed and Apollos watered it, but God made it grow.

46:3:7.text: So neither he who plants nor he who waters is anything, but only God, who makes things grow.

46:3:8.text: He who plants and he who waters are one in purpose, and each will be rewarded according to his own labor.

46:3:9.text: For we are God’s fellow workers; you are God’s field, God’s building.

46:4:1.text: So then, men ought to regard us as servants of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God.

46:4:10.text: We are fools for Christ, but you are wise in Christ. We are weak, but you are strong. You are honored, but we are dishonored.

46:4:11.text: To this very hour we are hungry and thirsty, we are poorly clothed, we are brutally treated, we are homeless.

46:4:12.text: We work hard with our own hands. When we are vilified, we bless; when we are persecuted, we endure it;

46:4:13.text: when we are slandered, we answer gently. Up to this moment we have become the scum of the earth, the refuse of the world.

46:4:14.text: I am not writing this to shame you, but to warn you as my beloved children.

46:4:15.text: Even if you have ten thousand guardians in Christ, you do not have many fathers; for in Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel.

46:4:16.text: Therefore I urge you to imitate me.

46:4:17.text: That is why I have sent you Timothy, my beloved and faithful child in the Lord. He will remind you of my way of life in Christ Jesus, which is exactly what I teach everywhere in every church.

46:4:18.text: Some of you have become arrogant, as if I were not coming to you.

46:4:19.text: But I will come to you shortly, if the Lord is willing, and then I will find out not only what these arrogant people are saying, but what power they have.

46:4:2.text: Now it is required of stewards that they be found faithful.

46:4:20.text: For the kingdom of God is not a matter of talk but of power.

46:4:21.text: Which do you prefer? Shall I come to you with a rod, or in love and with a gentle spirit?

46:4:3.text: I care very little, however, if I am judged by you or by any human court. In fact, I do not even judge myself.

46:4:4.text: My conscience is clear, but that does not vindicate me. It is the Lord who judges me.

46:4:5.text: Therefore judge nothing before the appointed time; wait until the Lord comes. He will bring to light what is hidden in darkness and will expose the motives of men’s hearts. At that time each will receive his praise from God.

46:4:6.text: Brothers, I have applied these things to myself and Apollos for your benefit, so that you may learn from us not to go beyond what is written. Then you will not take pride in one man over another.

46:4:7.text: For who makes you so superior? What do you have that you did not receive? And if you did receive it, why do you boast as though you did not?

46:4:8.text: Already you have all you want. Already you have become rich. Without us, you have become kings. How I wish you really were kings, so that we might be kings with you!

46:4:9.text: For it seems to me that God has displayed us apostles at the end of the procession, like prisoners appointed for death. We have become a spectacle to the whole world, to angels as well as to men.

46:5:1.text: It is actually reported that there is sexual immorality among you, and of a kind that is intolerable even among pagans: A man has his father’s wife.

46:5:10.text: I was not including the sexually immoral of this world, or the greedy and swindlers, or idolaters. In that case you would have to leave this world.

46:5:11.text: But now I am writing you not to associate with anyone who claims to be a brother but is sexually immoral or greedy, an idolater or a verbal abuser, a drunkard or a swindler. With such a man do not even eat.

46:5:12.text: What business of mine is it to judge those outside the church? Are you not to judge those inside?

46:5:13.text: God will judge those outside. “Expel the wicked man from among you.”

46:5:2.text: And you are proud! Shouldn’t you rather have been stricken with grief and have removed from your fellowship the man who did this?

46:5:3.text: Although I am absent from you in body, I am present with you in spirit, and I have already pronounced judgment on the one who did this, just as if I were present.

46:5:4.text: When you are assembled in the name of our Lord Jesus and I am with you in spirit, along with the power of the Lord Jesus,

46:5:5.text: hand this man over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that his spirit may be saved on the Day of the Lord.

46:5:6.text: Your boasting is not good. Do you not know that a little leaven works through the whole batch of dough?

46:5:7.text: Get rid of the old leaven, that you may be a new unleavened batch, as you really are. For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed.

46:5:8.text: Therefore let us keep the feast, not with the old bread, leavened with malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and of truth.

46:5:9.text: I wrote you in my letter not to associate with sexually immoral people.

46:6:1.text: If any of you has a grievance against another, how dare he go to law before the unrighteous instead of before the saints!

46:6:10.text: nor thieves, nor the greedy, nor drunkards, nor verbal abusers, nor swindlers, will inherit the kingdom of God.

46:6:11.text: And that is what some of you were. But you were washed, you were sanctified, you were justified, in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and by the Spirit of our God.

46:6:12.text: “Everything is permissible for me,” but not everything is beneficial. “Everything is permissible for me,” but I will not be mastered by anything.

46:6:13.text: “Food for the stomach and the stomach for food,” but God will destroy them both. The body is not intended for sexual immorality, but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.

46:6:14.text: By His power God raised the Lord from the dead, and He will raise us also.

46:6:15.text: Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? Shall I then take the members of Christ and unite them with a prostitute? Never!

46:6:16.text: Or don’t you know that he who unites himself with a prostitute is one with her in body? For it is said, “The two will become one flesh.”

46:6:17.text: But he who unites himself with the Lord is one with Him in spirit.

46:6:18.text: Flee from sexual immorality. Every other sin a man can commit is outside his body, but he who sins sexually sins against his own body.

46:6:19.text: Do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have received from God? You are not your own;

46:6:2.text: Do you not know that the saints will judge the world? And if you are to judge the world, are you not competent to judge trivial cases?

46:6:20.text: you were bought at a price. Therefore glorify God with your body.

46:6:3.text: Do you not know that we will judge angels? How much more the things of this life!

46:6:4.text: So if you need to settle everyday matters, do you appoint as judges those of no standing in the church?

46:6:5.text: I say this to your shame. Is there really no one among you wise enough to arbitrate between his brothers?

46:6:6.text: Instead, one brother goes to law against another, and this in front of unbelievers!

46:6:7.text: The very fact that you have lawsuits among you means that you are thoroughly defeated already. Why not rather be wronged? Why not rather be cheated?

46:6:8.text: Instead, you yourselves cheat and do wrong, even against your own brothers!

46:6:9.text: Do you not know that the wicked will not inherit the kingdom of God? Do not be deceived: Neither the sexually immoral, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor men who submit to or perform homosexual acts,

46:7:1.text: Now for the matters you wrote about: It is good to abstain from sexual relations.

46:7:10.text: To the married I give this command (not I, but the Lord): A wife must not separate from her husband.

46:7:11.text: But if she does, she must remain unmarried or else be reconciled to her husband. And a husband must not divorce his wife.

46:7:12.text: To the rest I say this (I, not the Lord): If a brother has an unbelieving wife and she is willing to live with him, he must not divorce her.

46:7:13.text: And if a woman has an unbelieving husband and he is willing to live with her, she must not divorce him.

46:7:14.text: For the unbelieving husband is sanctified through his believing wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified through her believing husband. Otherwise your children would be unclean, but now they are holy.

46:7:15.text: But if the unbeliever leaves, let him go. The believing brother or sister is not bound in such cases. God has called you to live in peace.

46:7:16.text: How do you know, wife, whether you will save your husband? Or how do you know, husband, whether you will save your wife?

46:7:17.text: Regardless, each one should lead the life that the Lord has assigned to him and to which God has called him. This is what I prescribe in all the churches.

46:7:18.text: Was a man already circumcised when he was called? He should not become uncircumcised. Was a man still uncircumcised when called? He should not be circumcised.

46:7:19.text: Circumcision is nothing and uncircumcision is nothing. Keeping God’s commandments is what counts.

46:7:2.text: But because there is so much sexual immorality, each man should have his own wife, and each woman her own husband.

46:7:20.text: Each one should remain in the situation he was in when he was called.

46:7:21.text: Were you a slave when you were called? Do not let it concern you — but if you can gain your freedom, take the opportunity.

46:7:22.text: For he who was a slave when he was called by the Lord is the Lord’s freedman. Conversely, he who was a free man when he was called is Christ’s slave.

46:7:23.text: You were bought at a price; do not become slaves of men.

46:7:24.text: Brothers, each one should remain in the situation he was in when God called him.

46:7:25.text: Now about virgins, I have no command from the Lord, but I give a judgment as one who by the Lord’s mercy is trustworthy.

46:7:26.text: Because of the present crisis, I think it is good for a man to remain as he is.

46:7:27.text: Are you committed to a wife? Do not seek to be released. Are you free of commitment? Do not look for a wife.

46:7:28.text: But if you do marry, you have not sinned. And if a virgin marries, she has not sinned. But those who marry will face troubles in this life, and I want to spare you this.

46:7:29.text: What I am saying, brothers, is that the time is short. From now on those who have wives should live as if they had none;

46:7:3.text: The husband should fulfill his marital duty to his wife, and likewise the wife to her husband.

46:7:30.text: those who weep, as if they did not; those who are joyful, as if they were not; those who make a purchase, as if they had nothing;

46:7:31.text: and those who use the things of this world, as if not dependent on them. For this world in its present form is passing away.

46:7:32.text: I want you to be free from concern. The unmarried man is concerned about the work of the Lord, how he can please the Lord.

46:7:33.text: But the married man is concerned about the affairs of this world, how he can please his wife,

46:7:34.text: and his interests are divided. The unmarried woman or virgin is concerned about the work of the Lord, how she can be holy in both body and spirit. But the married woman is concerned about the affairs of this world, how she can please her husband.

46:7:35.text: I am saying this for your own good, not to restrict you, but in order to promote proper decorum and undivided devotion to the Lord.

46:7:36.text: However, if someone thinks he is acting inappropriately toward his betrothed, and if she is beyond her youth and they ought to marry, let him do as he wishes; he is not sinning; they should get married.

46:7:37.text: But the man who is firmly established in his heart and under no constraint, with control over his will and resolve in his heart not to marry the virgin, he will do well.

46:7:38.text: So then, he who marries the virgin does well, but he who does not marry her does even better.

46:7:39.text: A wife is bound to her husband as long as he lives. But if her husband dies, she is free to marry anyone she wishes, as long as he belongs to the Lord.

46:7:4.text: The wife does not have authority over her own body, but the husband. Likewise the husband does not have authority over his own body, but the wife.

46:7:40.text: In my judgment, however, she is happier if she remains as she is. And I think that I too have the Spirit of God.

46:7:5.text: Do not deprive each other, except by mutual consent and for a time, so you may devote yourselves to prayer. Then come together again, so that Satan will not tempt you through your lack of self-control.

46:7:6.text: I say this as a concession, not as a command.

46:7:7.text: I wish that all men were as I am. But each man has his own gift from God; one has this gift, another has that.

46:7:8.text: Now to the unmarried and widows I say this: It is good for them to remain unmarried, as I am.

46:7:9.text: But if they cannot control themselves, let them marry. For it is better to marry than to burn with passion.

46:8:1.text: Now about food sacrificed to idols: We know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.

46:8:10.text: For if someone with a weak conscience sees you who are well informed eating in an idol’s temple, will he not be encouraged to eat food sacrificed to idols?

46:8:11.text: So this weak brother, for whom Christ died, is destroyed by your knowledge.

46:8:12.text: By sinning against your brothers in this way and wounding their weak conscience, you sin against Christ.

46:8:13.text: Therefore, if what I eat causes my brother to stumble, I will never eat meat again, so that I will not cause him to stumble.

46:8:2.text: The one who thinks he knows something does not yet know as he ought to know.

46:8:3.text: But the one who loves God is known by God.

46:8:4.text: So about eating food sacrificed to idols: We know that an idol is nothing at all in the world, and that there is no God but one.

46:8:5.text: For even if there are so-called gods, whether in heaven or on earth (as there are many so-called gods and lords),

46:8:6.text: yet for us there is but one God, the Father, from whom all things came and for whom we exist. And there is but one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things came and through whom we exist.

46:8:7.text: But not everyone has this knowledge. Some people are still so accustomed to idols that they eat such food as if it were sacrificed to an idol. And since their conscience is weak, it is defiled.

46:8:8.text: But food does not bring us closer to God: We are no worse if we do not eat, and no better if we do.

46:8:9.text: Be careful, however, that your freedom does not become a stumbling block to the weak.

46:9:1.text: Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus our Lord? Are you yourselves not my workmanship in the Lord?

46:9:10.text: Isn’t He actually speaking on our behalf? Indeed, this was written for us, because when the plowman plows and the thresher threshes, they should also expect to share in the harvest.

46:9:11.text: If we have sown spiritual seed among you, is it too much for us to reap a material harvest from you?

46:9:12.text: If others have this right to your support, shouldn’t we have it all the more? But we did not exercise this right. Instead, we put up with anything rather than hinder the gospel of Christ.

46:9:13.text: Do you not know that those who work in the temple eat of its food, and those who serve at the altar partake of its offerings?

46:9:14.text: In the same way, the Lord has prescribed that those who preach the gospel should receive their living from the gospel.

46:9:15.text: But I have not used any of these rights. And I am not writing this to suggest that something be done for me. Indeed, I would rather die than let anyone nullify my boast.

46:9:16.text: Yet when I preach the gospel, I have no reason to boast, because I am obligated to preach. Woe to me if I do not preach the gospel!

46:9:17.text: If my preaching is voluntary, I have a reward. But if it is not voluntary, I am still entrusted with a responsibility.

46:9:18.text: What then is my reward? That in preaching the gospel I may offer it free of charge, and so not use up my rights in preaching it.

46:9:19.text: Though I am free of obligation to anyone, I make myself a slave to everyone, to win as many as possible.

46:9:2.text: Even if I am not an apostle to others, surely I am to you. For you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.

46:9:20.text: To the Jews I became like a Jew, to win the Jews. To those under the law I became like one under the law (though I myself am not under the law), to win those under the law.

46:9:21.text: To those without the law I became like one without the law (though I am not outside the law of God but am under the law of Christ), to win those without the law.

46:9:22.text: To the weak I became weak, to win the weak. I have become all things to all people so that by all possible means I might save some.

46:9:23.text: I do all this for the sake of the gospel, so that I may share in its blessings.

46:9:24.text: Do you not know that in a race all the runners run, but only one receives the prize? Run in such a way as to take the prize.

46:9:25.text: Everyone who competes in the games trains with strict discipline. They do it for a crown that is perishable, but we do it for a crown that is imperishable.

46:9:26.text: Therefore I do not run aimlessly; I do not fight like I am beating the air.

46:9:27.text: No, I discipline my body and make it my slave, so that after I have preached to others, I myself will not be disqualified.

46:9:3.text: This is my defense to those who scrutinize me:

46:9:4.text: Have we no right to food and to drink?

46:9:5.text: Have we no right to take along a believing wife, as do the other apostles and the Lord’s brothers and Cephas?

46:9:6.text: Or are Barnabas and I the only apostles who must work for a living?

46:9:7.text: Who serves as a soldier at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat of its fruit? Who tends a flock and does not drink of its milk?

46:9:8.text: Do I say this from a human perspective? Doesn’t the Law say the same thing?

46:9:9.text: For it is written in the Law of Moses: “Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain.” Is it about oxen that God is concerned?

47:10:1.text: Now by the mildness and gentleness of Christ, I appeal to you — I, Paul, who am humble when face to face with you, but bold when away.

47:10:10.text: For some say, “His letters are weighty and forceful, but his physical presence is unimpressive, and his speaking is of no account.”

47:10:11.text: Such people should consider that what we are in our letters when absent, we will be in our actions when present.

47:10:12.text: We do not dare to classify or compare ourselves with some who commend themselves. When they measure themselves by themselves and compare themselves with themselves, they show their ignorance.

47:10:13.text: We, however, will not boast beyond our limits, but only within the field of influence that God has assigned to us — a field that reaches even to you.

47:10:14.text: We are not overstepping our bounds, as if we had not come to you. Indeed, we were the first to reach you with the gospel of Christ.

47:10:15.text: Neither do we boast beyond our limits in the labors of others. But we hope that as your faith increases, our area of influence among you will greatly increase as well,

47:10:16.text: so that we can preach the gospel in the regions beyond you. Then we will not be boasting in the work already done in another man’s territory.

47:10:17.text: Rather, “Let him who boasts boast in the Lord.”

47:10:18.text: For it is not the one who commends himself who is approved, but the one whom the Lord commends.

47:10:2.text: I beg you that when I come I may not need to be as bold as I expect toward those who presume that we live according to the flesh.

47:10:3.text: For though we live in the flesh, we do not wage war according to the flesh.

47:10:4.text: The weapons of our warfare are not the weapons of the world. Instead, they have divine power to demolish strongholds.

47:10:5.text: We tear down arguments and every presumption set up against the knowledge of God; and we take captive every thought to make it obedient to Christ.

47:10:6.text: And we will be ready to punish every act of disobedience, as soon as your obedience is complete.

47:10:7.text: You are looking at outward appearances. If anyone is confident that he belongs to Christ, he should remind himself that we belong to Christ just as much as he does.

47:10:8.text: For even if I boast somewhat excessively about the authority the Lord gave us for building you up rather than tearing you down, I will not be ashamed.

47:10:9.text: I do not want to seem to be trying to frighten you by my letters.

47:11:1.text: I hope you will bear with a little of my foolishness, but you are already doing that.

47:11:10.text: As surely as the truth of Christ is in me, this boasting of mine will not be silenced in the regions of Achaia.

47:11:11.text: Why? Because I do not love you? God knows I do!

47:11:12.text: But I will keep on doing what I am doing, in order to undercut those who want an opportunity to be regarded as our equals in the things of which they boast.

47:11:13.text: For such men are false apostles, deceitful workers, masquerading as apostles of Christ.

47:11:14.text: And no wonder, for Satan himself masquerades as an angel of light.

47:11:15.text: It is not surprising, then, if his servants masquerade as servants of righteousness. Their end will correspond to their actions.

47:11:16.text: I repeat: Let no one take me for a fool. But if you do, then receive me as a fool, so that I too may boast a little.

47:11:17.text: In this confident boasting of mine, I am not speaking as the Lord would, but as a fool.

47:11:18.text: Since many are boasting according to the flesh, I too will boast.

47:11:19.text: For you gladly tolerate fools, since you are so wise.

47:11:2.text: I am jealous for you with a godly jealousy. For I promised you to one husband, to present you as a pure virgin to Christ.

47:11:20.text: In fact, you even put up with anyone who enslaves you or exploits you or takes advantage of you or exalts himself or strikes you in the face.

47:11:21.text: To my shame I concede that we were too weak for that! Speaking as a fool, however, I can match what anyone else dares to boast about.

47:11:22.text: Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they descendants of Abraham? So am I.

47:11:23.text: Are they servants of Christ? I am speaking like I am out of my mind, but I am so much more: in harder labor, in more imprisonments, in worse beatings, in frequent danger of death.

47:11:24.text: Five times I received from the Jews the forty lashes minus one.

47:11:25.text: Three times I was beaten with rods, once I was stoned, three times I was shipwrecked. I spent a night and a day in the open sea.

47:11:26.text: In my frequent journeys, I have been in danger from rivers and from bandits, in danger from my countrymen and from the Gentiles, in danger in the city and in the country, in danger on the sea and among false brothers,

47:11:27.text: in labor and toil and often without sleep, in hunger and thirst and often without food, in cold and exposure.

47:11:28.text: Apart from these external trials, I face daily the pressure of my concern for all the churches.

47:11:29.text: Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is led into sin, and I do not burn with grief?

47:11:3.text: I am afraid, however, that just as Eve was deceived by the serpent’s cunning, your minds may be led astray from your simple and pure devotion to Christ.

47:11:30.text: If I must boast, I will boast of the things that show my weakness.

47:11:31.text: The God and Father of the Lord Jesus, who is forever worthy of praise, knows that I am not lying.

47:11:32.text: In Damascus, the governor under King Aretas secured the city of the Damascenes in order to arrest me.

47:11:33.text: But I was lowered in a basket through a window in the wall and escaped his grasp.

47:11:4.text: For if someone comes and proclaims a Jesus other than the One we proclaimed, or if you receive a different spirit than the One you received, or a different gospel than the one you accepted, you put up with it way too easily.

47:11:5.text: I consider myself in no way inferior to those “super-apostles.”

47:11:6.text: Although I am not a polished speaker, I am certainly not lacking in knowledge. We have made this clear to you in every way possible.

47:11:7.text: Was it a sin for me to humble myself in order to exalt you, because I preached the gospel of God to you free of charge?

47:11:8.text: I robbed other churches by accepting their support in order to serve you.

47:11:9.text: And when I was with you and in need, I was not a burden to anyone; for the brothers who came from Macedonia supplied my needs. I have refrained from being a burden to you in any way, and I will continue to do so.

47:12:1.text: I must go on boasting. Although there is nothing to gain, I will go on to visions and revelations from the Lord.

47:12:10.text: That is why, for the sake of Christ, I delight in weaknesses, in insults, in hardships, in persecutions, in difficulties. For when I am weak, then I am strong.

47:12:11.text: I have become a fool, but you drove me to it. In fact, you should have commended me, since I am in no way inferior to those “super-apostles,” even though I am nothing.

47:12:12.text: The true marks of an apostle — signs, wonders, and miracles — were performed among you with great perseverance.

47:12:13.text: In what way were you inferior to the other churches, except that I was not a burden to you? Forgive me this wrong!

47:12:14.text: See, I am ready to come to you a third time, and I will not be a burden, because I am not seeking your possessions, but you. For children should not have to save up for their parents, but parents for their children.

47:12:15.text: And for the sake of your souls, I will most gladly spend my money and myself. If I love you more, will you love me less?

47:12:16.text: Be that as it may, I was not a burden to you; but crafty as I am, I caught you by trickery.

47:12:17.text: Did I exploit you by anyone I sent you?

47:12:18.text: I urged Titus to visit you, and I sent our brother with him. Did Titus exploit you in any way? Did we not walk in the same Spirit and follow in the same footsteps?

47:12:19.text: Have you been thinking all along that we were making a defense to you? We speak before God in Christ, and all of this, beloved, is to build you up.

47:12:2.text: I know a man in Christ who fourteen years ago was caught up to the third heaven. Whether it was in the body or out of it I do not know, but God knows.

47:12:20.text: For I am afraid that when I come, I may not find you as I wish, and you may not find me as you wish. I fear that there may be quarreling, jealousy, rage, rivalry, slander, gossip, arrogance, and disorder.

47:12:21.text: I am afraid that when I come again, my God will humble me before you, and I will be grieved over many who have sinned earlier and have not repented of their acts of impurity, sexual immorality, and debauchery.

47:12:3.text: And I know that this man — whether in the body or out of it I do not know, but God knows —

47:12:4.text: was caught up to Paradise. The things he heard were too sacred for words, things that man is not permitted to tell.

47:12:5.text: I will boast about such a man, but I will not boast about myself, except in my weaknesses.

47:12:6.text: Even if I wanted to boast, I would not be a fool, because I would be speaking the truth. But I refrain, so no one will credit me with more than he sees in me or hears from me,

47:12:7.text: or because of these surpassingly great revelations. So to keep me from becoming conceited, I was given a thorn in my flesh, a messenger of Satan, to torment me.

47:12:8.text: Three times I pleaded with the Lord to take it away from me.

47:12:9.text: But He said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is perfected in weakness.” Therefore I will boast all the more gladly in my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may rest on me.

47:13:1.text: This is the third time I am coming to you. “Every matter must be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.”

47:13:10.text: This is why I write these things while absent, so that when I am present I will not need to be severe in my use of the authority that the Lord gave me for building you up, not for tearing you down.

47:13:11.text: Finally, brothers, rejoice! Aim for perfect harmony, encourage one another, be of one mind, live in peace. And the God of love and peace will be with you.

47:13:12.text: Greet one another with a holy kiss.

47:13:13.text: All the saints send you greetings.

47:13:14.text: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with all of you.

47:13:2.text: I already warned you the second time I was with you. So now in my absence I warn those who sinned earlier and everyone else: If I return, I will not spare anyone,

47:13:3.text: since you are demanding proof that Christ is speaking through me. He is not weak in dealing with you, but is powerful among you.

47:13:4.text: For He was indeed crucified in weakness, yet He lives by God’s power. And though we are weak in Him, yet by God’s power we will live with Him to serve you.

47:13:5.text: Examine yourselves to see whether you are in the faith; test yourselves. Can’t you see for yourselves that Jesus Christ is in you — unless you actually fail the test?

47:13:6.text: And I hope you will realize that we have not failed the test.

47:13:7.text: Now we pray to God that you will not do anything wrong — not that we will appear to have stood the test, but that you will do what is right, even if we appear to have failed.

47:13:8.text: For we cannot do anything against the truth, but only for the truth.

47:13:9.text: In fact, we rejoice when we are weak but you are strong, and our prayer is for your perfection.

47:1:1.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and Timothy our brother, To the church of God in Corinth, together with all the saints throughout Achaia:

47:1:10.text: He has delivered us from such a deadly peril, and He will deliver us. In Him we have placed our hope that He will yet again deliver us,

47:1:11.text: as you help us by your prayers. Then many will give thanks on our behalf for the favor shown us in answer to their prayers.

47:1:12.text: And this is our boast: Our conscience testifies that we have conducted ourselves in the world, and especially in relation to you, in the holiness and sincerity that are from God — not in worldly wisdom, but in the grace of God.

47:1:13.text: For we do not write you anything that is beyond your ability to read and understand. And I hope that you will understand us completely,

47:1:14.text: as you have already understood us in part, so that you may boast of us just as we will boast of you in the day of our Lord Jesus.

47:1:15.text: Confident of this, I planned to visit you first, so that you might receive a double blessing.

47:1:16.text: I wanted to visit you on my way to Macedonia, and to return to you from Macedonia, and then to have you help me on my way to Judea.

47:1:17.text: When I planned this, did I do it carelessly? Or do I make my plans by human standards, so as to say “Yes, yes” when I really mean “No, no”?

47:1:18.text: But as surely as God is faithful, our message to you is not “Yes” and “No.”

47:1:19.text: For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was proclaimed among you by me and Silvanus and Timothy, was not “Yes” and “No,” but in Him it has always been “Yes.”

47:1:2.text: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

47:1:20.text: For all the promises of God are “Yes” in Christ. And so through Him, our “Amen” is spoken to the glory of God.

47:1:21.text: Now it is God who establishes both us and you in Christ. He anointed us,

47:1:22.text: placed His seal on us, and put His Spirit in our hearts as a pledge of what is to come.

47:1:23.text: I call God as my witness that it was in order to spare you that I did not return to Corinth.

47:1:24.text: Not that we lord it over your faith, but we are fellow workers with you for your joy, because it is by faith that you stand firm.

47:1:3.text: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of compassion and the God of all comfort,

47:1:4.text: who comforts us in all our troubles, so that we can comfort those in any trouble with the comfort we ourselves have received from God.

47:1:5.text: For just as the sufferings of Christ overflow to us, so also through Christ our comfort overflows.

47:1:6.text: If we are afflicted, it is for your comfort and salvation; if we are comforted, it is for your comfort, which accomplishes in you patient endurance of the same sufferings we experience.

47:1:7.text: And our hope for you is sure, because we know that just as you share in our sufferings, so also you will share in our comfort.

47:1:8.text: We do not want you to be unaware, brothers, of the hardships we encountered in the province of Asia. We were under a burden far beyond our ability to endure, so that we despaired even of life.

47:1:9.text: Indeed, we felt we were under the sentence of death, in order that we would not trust in ourselves, but in God, who raises the dead.

47:2:1.text: So I made up my mind not to make another painful visit to you.

47:2:10.text: If you forgive anyone, I also forgive him. And if I have forgiven anything, I have forgiven it in the presence of Christ for your sake,

47:2:11.text: in order that Satan should not outwit us. For we are not unaware of his schemes.

47:2:12.text: Now when I went to Troas to preach the gospel of Christ and a door stood open for me in the Lord,

47:2:13.text: I had no peace in my spirit, because I did not find my brother Titus there. So I said goodbye to them and went on to Macedonia.

47:2:14.text: But thanks be to God, who always leads us triumphantly as captives in Christ and through us spreads everywhere the fragrance of the knowledge of Him.

47:2:15.text: For we are to God the sweet aroma of Christ among those who are being saved and those who are perishing.

47:2:16.text: To the one, we are an odor of death and demise; to the other, a fragrance that brings life. And who is qualified for such a task?

47:2:17.text: For we are not like so many others, who peddle the word of God for profit. On the contrary, in Christ we speak before God with sincerity, as men sent from God.

47:2:2.text: For if I grieve you, who is left to cheer me but those whom I have grieved?

47:2:3.text: I wrote as I did so that on my arrival I would not be saddened by those who ought to make me rejoice. I had confidence in all of you, that you would share my joy.

47:2:4.text: For through many tears I wrote you out of great distress and anguish of heart, not to grieve you but to let you know how much I love you.

47:2:5.text: Now if anyone has caused grief, he has not grieved me but all of you — to some degree, not to overstate it.

47:2:6.text: The punishment imposed on him by the majority is sufficient for him.

47:2:7.text: So instead, you ought to forgive and comfort him, so that he will not be overwhelmed by excessive sorrow.

47:2:8.text: Therefore I urge you to reaffirm your love for him.

47:2:9.text: My purpose in writing you was to see if you would stand the test and be obedient in everything.

47:3:1.text: Are we beginning to commend ourselves again? Or do we need, like some people, letters of recommendation to you or from you?

47:3:10.text: Indeed, what was once glorious has no glory now in comparison to the glory that surpasses it.

47:3:11.text: For if what was fading away came with glory, how much greater is the glory of that which endures!

47:3:12.text: Therefore, since we have such a hope, we are very bold.

47:3:13.text: We are not like Moses, who would put a veil over his face to keep the Israelites from gazing at the end of what was fading away.

47:3:14.text: But their minds were closed. For to this day the same veil remains at the reading of the old covenant. It has not been lifted, because only in Christ can it be removed.

47:3:15.text: And even to this day when Moses is read, a veil covers their hearts.

47:3:16.text: But whenever anyone turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.

47:3:17.text: Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.

47:3:18.text: And we, who with unveiled faces all reflect the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into His image with intensifying glory, which comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit.

47:3:2.text: You yourselves are our letter, inscribed on our hearts, known and read by everyone.

47:3:3.text: It is clear that you are a letter from Christ, the result of our ministry, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts.

47:3:4.text: Such confidence before God is ours through Christ.

47:3:5.text: Not that we are competent in ourselves to claim that anything comes from us, but our competence comes from God.

47:3:6.text: And He has qualified us as ministers of a new covenant, not of the letter but of the Spirit; for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.

47:3:7.text: Now if the ministry of death, which was engraved in letters on stone, came with such glory that the Israelites could not gaze at the face of Moses because of its fleeting glory,

47:3:8.text: will not the ministry of the Spirit be even more glorious?

47:3:9.text: For if the ministry of condemnation was glorious, how much more glorious is the ministry of righteousness!

47:4:1.text: Therefore, since God in His mercy has given us this ministry, we do not lose heart.

47:4:10.text: We always carry around in our body the death of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our body.

47:4:11.text: For we who are alive are always consigned to death for Jesus’ sake, so that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our mortal body.

47:4:12.text: So then, death is at work in us, but life is at work in you.

47:4:13.text: And in keeping with what is written: “I believed, therefore I have spoken,” we who have the same spirit of faith also believe and therefore speak,

47:4:14.text: knowing that the One who raised the Lord Jesus will also raise us with Jesus and present us with you in His presence.

47:4:15.text: All this is for your benefit, so that the grace that is extending to more and more people may overflow in thanksgiving, to the glory of God.

47:4:16.text: Therefore we do not lose heart. Though our outer self is wasting away, yet our inner self is being renewed day by day.

47:4:17.text: For our light and momentary affliction is producing for us an eternal glory that is far beyond comparison.

47:4:18.text: So we fix our eyes not on what is seen, but on what is unseen. For what is seen is temporary, but what is unseen is eternal.

47:4:2.text: Instead, we have renounced secret and shameful ways. We do not practice deceit, nor do we distort the word of God. On the contrary, by open proclamation of the truth, we commend ourselves to every man’s conscience in the sight of God.

47:4:3.text: And even if our gospel is veiled, it is veiled to those who are perishing.

47:4:4.text: The god of this age has blinded the minds of unbelievers so they cannot see the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God.

47:4:5.text: For we do not proclaim ourselves, but Jesus Christ as Lord, and ourselves as your servants for Jesus’ sake.

47:4:6.text: For God, who said, “Let light shine out of darkness,” made His light shine in our hearts to give us the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.

47:4:7.text: Now we have this treasure in jars of clay to show that this surpassingly great power is from God and not from us.

47:4:8.text: We are hard pressed on all sides, but not crushed; perplexed, but not in despair;

47:4:9.text: persecuted, but not forsaken; struck down, but not destroyed.

47:5:1.text: Now we know that if the earthly tent we live in is dismantled, we have a building from God, an eternal house in heaven, not built by human hands.

47:5:10.text: For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, that each one may receive his due for the things done in the body, whether good or bad.

47:5:11.text: Therefore, since we know what it means to fear the Lord, we try to persuade men. What we are is clear to God, and I hope it is clear to your conscience as well.

47:5:12.text: We are not commending ourselves to you again. Instead, we are giving you an occasion to be proud of us, so that you can answer those who take pride in appearances rather than in the heart.

47:5:13.text: If we are out of our mind, it is for God; if we are of sound mind, it is for you.

47:5:14.text: For Christ’s love compels us, because we are convinced that One died for all, therefore all died.

47:5:15.text: And He died for all, that those who live should no longer live for themselves, but for Him who died for them and was raised again.

47:5:16.text: So from now on we regard no one according to the flesh. Although we once regarded Christ in this way, we do so no longer.

47:5:17.text: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away. Behold, the new has come!

47:5:18.text: All this is from God, who reconciled us to Himself through Christ and gave us the ministry of reconciliation:

47:5:19.text: that God was reconciling the world to Himself in Christ, not counting men’s trespasses against them. And He has committed to us the message of reconciliation.

47:5:2.text: For in this tent we groan, longing to be clothed with our heavenly dwelling,

47:5:20.text: Therefore we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God were making His appeal through us. We implore you on behalf of Christ: Be reconciled to God.

47:5:21.text: God made Him who knew no sin to be sin on our behalf, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.

47:5:3.text: because when we are clothed, we will not be found naked.

47:5:4.text: So while we are in this tent, we groan under our burdens, because we do not wish to be unclothed but clothed, so that our mortality may be swallowed up by life.

47:5:5.text: And God has prepared us for this very purpose and has given us the Spirit as a pledge of what is to come.

47:5:6.text: Therefore we are always confident, although we know that while we are at home in the body, we are away from the Lord.

47:5:7.text: For we walk by faith, not by sight.

47:5:8.text: We are confident, then, and would prefer to be away from the body and at home with the Lord.

47:5:9.text: So we aspire to please Him, whether we are here in this body or away from it.

47:6:1.text: As God’s fellow workers, then, we urge you not to receive God’s grace in vain.

47:6:10.text: sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; poor, yet making many rich; having nothing, and yet possessing everything.

47:6:11.text: We have spoken freely to you, Corinthians. Our hearts are open wide.

47:6:12.text: It is not our affection, but yours, that is restrained.

47:6:13.text: As a fair exchange, I ask you as my children: Open wide your hearts also.

47:6:14.text: Do not be unequally yoked with unbelievers. For what partnership can righteousness have with wickedness? Or what fellowship does light have with darkness?

47:6:15.text: What harmony is there between Christ and Belial? Or what does a believer have in common with an unbeliever?

47:6:16.text: What agreement can exist between the temple of God and idols? For we are the temple of the living God. As God has said: “I will dwell with them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they will be My people.”

47:6:17.text: “Therefore come out from among them and be separate, says the Lord. Touch no unclean thing, and I will receive you.”

47:6:18.text: And: “I will be a Father to you, and you will be My sons and daughters, says the Lord Almighty.”

47:6:2.text: For He says: “In the time of favor I heard you, and in the day of salvation I helped you.” Behold, now is the time of favor; now is the day of salvation!

47:6:3.text: We put no obstacle in anyone’s way, so that no one can discredit our ministry.

47:6:4.text: Rather, as servants of God we commend ourselves in every way: in great endurance; in troubles, hardships, and calamities;

47:6:5.text: in beatings, imprisonments, and riots; in labor, sleepless nights, and hunger;

47:6:6.text: in purity, knowledge, patience, and kindness; in the Holy Spirit and in sincere love;

47:6:7.text: in truthful speech and in the power of God; with the weapons of righteousness in the right hand and in the left;

47:6:8.text: through glory and dishonor, slander and praise; viewed as imposters, yet genuine;

47:6:9.text: as unknown, yet well-known; dying, and yet we live on; punished, yet not killed;

47:7:1.text: Therefore, beloved, since we have these promises, let us cleanse ourselves from everything that defiles body and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.

47:7:10.text: Godly sorrow brings repentance that leads to salvation without regret, but worldly sorrow brings death.

47:7:11.text: Consider what this godly sorrow has produced in you: what earnestness, what eagerness to clear yourselves, what indignation, what alarm, what longing, what zeal, what vindication! In every way you have proved yourselves to be innocent in this matter.

47:7:12.text: So even though I wrote to you, it was not on account of the one who did wrong or the one who was harmed, but rather that your earnestness on our behalf would be made clear to you in the sight of God.

47:7:13.text: On account of this, we are encouraged. In addition to our own encouragement, we were even more delighted by the joy of Titus. For his spirit has been refreshed by all of you.

47:7:14.text: Indeed, I was not embarrassed by anything I had boasted to him about you. But just as everything we said to you was true, so our boasting to Titus has proved to be true as well.

47:7:15.text: And his affection for you is even greater when he remembers that you were all obedient as you welcomed him with fear and trembling.

47:7:16.text: I rejoice that I can have complete confidence in you.

47:7:2.text: Make room for us in your hearts. We have wronged no one, we have corrupted no one, we have exploited no one.

47:7:3.text: I do not say this to condemn you. I have said before that you so occupy our hearts that we live and die together with you.

47:7:4.text: Great is my confidence in you; great is my pride in you; I am filled with encouragement; in all our troubles my joy overflows.

47:7:5.text: For when we arrived in Macedonia, our bodies had no rest, but we were pressed from every direction — conflicts on the outside, fears within.

47:7:6.text: But God, who comforts the downcast, comforted us by the arrival of Titus,

47:7:7.text: and not only by his arrival, but also by the comfort he had received from you. He told us about your longing, your mourning, and your zeal for me, so that I rejoiced all the more.

47:7:8.text: Even if I caused you sorrow by my letter, I do not regret it. Although I did regret it, I now see that my letter caused you sorrow, but only for a short time.

47:7:9.text: And now I rejoice, not because you were made sorrowful, but because your sorrow led you to repentance. For you felt the sorrow that God had intended, and so were not harmed in any way by us.

47:8:1.text: Now, brothers, we want you to know about the grace that God has given the churches of Macedonia.

47:8:10.text: And this is my opinion about what is helpful for you in this matter: Last year you were the first not only to give, but even to have such a desire.

47:8:11.text: Now finish the work, so that you may complete it just as eagerly as you began, according to your means.

47:8:12.text: For if the eagerness is there, the gift is acceptable according to what one has, not according to what he does not have.

47:8:13.text: It is not our intention that others may be relieved while you are burdened, but that there may be equality.

47:8:14.text: At the present time, your surplus will meet their need, so that in turn their surplus will meet your need. Then there will be equality.

47:8:15.text: As it is written: “He who gathered much had no excess, and he who gathered little had no shortfall.”

47:8:16.text: But thanks be to God, who put into the heart of Titus the same devotion I have for you.

47:8:17.text: For not only did he welcome our appeal, but he is eagerly coming to you of his own volition.

47:8:18.text: Along with Titus we are sending the brother who is praised by all the churches for his work in the gospel.

47:8:19.text: More than that, this brother was chosen by the churches to accompany us with the offering — the gracious gift we administer to honor the Lord Himself and to show our eagerness to help.

47:8:2.text: In the terrible ordeal they suffered, their abundant joy and deep poverty overflowed into rich generosity.

47:8:20.text: We hope to avoid any criticism of the way we administer this generous gift.

47:8:21.text: For we are taking great care to do what is right, not only in the eyes of the Lord, but also in the eyes of men.

47:8:22.text: And we are sending along with them our brother whose earnestness has been proven many times and in many ways, and now even more so by his great confidence in you.

47:8:23.text: As for Titus, he is my partner and fellow worker among you. As for our brothers, they are messengers of the churches, to the glory of Christ.

47:8:24.text: In full view of the churches, then, show these men the proof of your love and the reason for our boasting about you.

47:8:3.text: For I testify that they gave according to their ability and even beyond it. Of their own accord,

47:8:4.text: they earnestly pleaded with us for the privilege of sharing in this service to the saints.

47:8:5.text: And not only did they do as we expected, but they gave themselves first to the Lord and then to us, because it was the will of God.

47:8:6.text: So we urged Titus to help complete your act of grace, just as he had started it.

47:8:7.text: But just as you excel in everything — in faith, in speech, in knowledge, in complete earnestness, and in the love we inspired in you — see that you also excel in this grace of giving.

47:8:8.text: I am not making a demand, but I am testing the sincerity of your love in comparison to the earnestness of others.

47:8:9.text: For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though He was rich, yet for your sakes He became poor, so that you through His poverty might become rich.

47:9:1.text: Now about the service to the saints, there is no need for me to write to you.

47:9:10.text: Now He who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your store of seed and will increase the harvest of your righteousness.

47:9:11.text: You will be enriched in every way to be generous on every occasion, so that through us your giving will produce thanksgiving to God.

47:9:12.text: For this ministry of service is not only supplying the needs of the saints, but is also overflowing in many expressions of thanksgiving to God.

47:9:13.text: Because of the proof this ministry provides, the saints will glorify God for your obedient confession of the gospel of Christ, and for the generosity of your contribution to them and to all the others.

47:9:14.text: And their prayers for you will express their affection for you, because of the surpassing grace God has given you.

47:9:15.text: Thanks be to God for His indescribable gift!

47:9:2.text: For I know your eagerness to help, and I have been boasting to the Macedonians that since last year you in Achaia were prepared to give. And your zeal has stirred most of them to do likewise.

47:9:3.text: But I am sending the brothers in order that our boasting about you in this matter should not prove empty, but that you will be prepared, just as I said.

47:9:4.text: Otherwise, if any Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, we — to say nothing of you — would be ashamed of having been so confident.

47:9:5.text: So I thought it necessary to urge the brothers to visit you beforehand and make arrangements for the bountiful gift you had promised. This way, your gift will be prepared generously and not begrudgingly.

47:9:6.text: Remember this: Whoever sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and whoever sows generously will also reap generously.

47:9:7.text: Each one should give what he has decided in his heart to give, not out of regret or compulsion. For God loves a cheerful giver.

47:9:8.text: And God is able to make all grace abound to you, so that in all things, at all times, having all that you need, you will abound in every good work.

47:9:9.text: As it is written: “He has scattered abroad His gifts to the poor; His righteousness endures forever.”

48:1:1.text: Paul, an apostle — sent not from men nor by man, but by Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised Him from the dead —

48:1:10.text: Am I now seeking the approval of men, or of God? Or am I striving to please men? If I were still trying to please men, I would not be a servant of Christ.

48:1:11.text: For I certify to you, brothers, that the gospel I preached was not devised by man.

48:1:12.text: I did not receive it from any man, nor was I taught it; rather, I received it by revelation from Jesus Christ.

48:1:13.text: For you have heard of my former way of life in Judaism, how severely I persecuted the church of God and tried to destroy it.

48:1:14.text: I was advancing in Judaism beyond many of my contemporaries and was extremely zealous for the traditions of my fathers.

48:1:15.text: But when God, who set me apart from my mother’s womb and called me by His grace, was pleased

48:1:16.text: to reveal His Son in me so that I might preach Him among the Gentiles, I did not rush to consult with flesh and blood,

48:1:17.text: nor did I go up to Jerusalem to the apostles who came before me, but I went into Arabia and later returned to Damascus.

48:1:18.text: Only after three years did I go up to Jerusalem to confer with Cephas, and I stayed with him fifteen days.

48:1:19.text: But I saw none of the other apostles except James, the Lord’s brother.

48:1:2.text: and all the brothers with me, To the churches of Galatia:

48:1:20.text: I assure you before God that what I am writing to you is no lie.

48:1:21.text: Later I went to the regions of Syria and Cilicia.

48:1:22.text: I was personally unknown, however, to the churches of Judea that are in Christ.

48:1:23.text: They only heard the account: “The man who formerly persecuted us is now preaching the faith he once tried to destroy.”

48:1:24.text: And they glorified God because of me.

48:1:3.text: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ,

48:1:4.text: who gave Himself for our sins to rescue us from the present evil age, according to the will of our God and Father,

48:1:5.text: to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.

48:1:6.text: I am amazed how quickly you are deserting the One who called you by the grace of Christ and are turning to a different gospel —

48:1:7.text: which is not even a gospel. Evidently some people are troubling you and trying to distort the gospel of Christ.

48:1:8.text: But even if we or an angel from heaven should preach a gospel contrary to the one we preached to you, let him be under a curse!

48:1:9.text: As we have said before, so now I say again: If anyone is preaching to you a gospel contrary to the one you received, let him be under a curse!

48:2:1.text: Fourteen years later I went up again to Jerusalem, accompanied by Barnabas. I took Titus along also.

48:2:10.text: They only asked us to remember the poor, the very thing I was eager to do.

48:2:11.text: When Cephas came to Antioch, however, I opposed him to his face, because he stood to be condemned.

48:2:12.text: For before certain men came from James, he used to eat with the Gentiles. But when they arrived, he began to draw back and separate himself, for fear of those in the circumcision group.

48:2:13.text: The other Jews joined him in his hypocrisy, so that by their hypocrisy even Barnabas was led astray.

48:2:14.text: When I saw that they were not walking in line with the truth of the gospel, I said to Cephas in front of them all, “If you, who are a Jew, live like a Gentile and not like a Jew, how can you compel the Gentiles to live like Jews?”

48:2:15.text: We who are Jews by birth and not Gentile “sinners”

48:2:16.text: know that a man is not justified by works of the law, but by faith in Jesus Christ. So we, too, have believed in Christ Jesus, that we may be justified by faith in Christ and not by works of the law, because by works of the law no one will be justified.

48:2:17.text: But if, while we seek to be justified in Christ, we ourselves are found to be sinners, does that make Christ a minister of sin? Certainly not!

48:2:18.text: If I rebuild what I have already torn down, I prove myself to be a lawbreaker.

48:2:19.text: For through the law I died to the law so that I might live to God.

48:2:2.text: I went in response to a revelation and set before them the gospel that I preach among the Gentiles. But I spoke privately to those recognized as leaders, for fear that I was running or had already run in vain.

48:2:20.text: I have been crucified with Christ, and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me. The life I live in the body, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave Himself up for me.

48:2:21.text: I do not set aside the grace of God. For if righteousness comes through the law, Christ died for nothing.

48:2:3.text: Yet not even Titus, who was with me, was compelled to be circumcised, even though he was a Greek.

48:2:4.text: This issue arose because some false brothers had come in under false pretenses to spy on our freedom in Christ Jesus, in order to enslave us.

48:2:5.text: We did not give in to them for a moment, so that the truth of the gospel would remain with you.

48:2:6.text: But as for the highly esteemed — whatever they were makes no difference to me; God does not show favoritism — those leaders added nothing to me.

48:2:7.text: On the contrary, they saw that I had been entrusted to preach the gospel to the uncircumcised, just as Peter had been to the circumcised.

48:2:8.text: For the One who was at work in Peter’s apostleship to the circumcised was also at work in my apostleship to the Gentiles.

48:2:9.text: And recognizing the grace that I had been given, James, Cephas, and John — those reputed to be pillars — gave me and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship, so that we should go to the Gentiles, and they to the circumcised.

48:3:1.text: O foolish Galatians! Who has bewitched you? Before your very eyes Jesus Christ was clearly portrayed as crucified.

48:3:10.text: All who rely on works of the law are under a curse. For it is written: “Cursed is everyone who does not continue to do everything written in the Book of the Law.”

48:3:11.text: Now it is clear that no one is justified before God by the law, because, “The righteous will live by faith.”

48:3:12.text: The law, however, is not based on faith; on the contrary, “The man who does these things will live by them.”

48:3:13.text: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us. For it is written: “Cursed is everyone who is hung on a tree.”

48:3:14.text: He redeemed us in order that the blessing promised to Abraham would come to the Gentiles in Christ Jesus, so that by faith we might receive the promise of the Spirit.

48:3:15.text: Brothers, let me put this in human terms. Even a human covenant, once it is ratified, cannot be canceled or amended.

48:3:16.text: The promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed. The Scripture does not say, “and to seeds,” meaning many, but “and to your seed,” meaning One, who is Christ.

48:3:17.text: What I mean is this: The law that came 430 years later does not revoke the covenant previously established by God, so as to nullify the promise.

48:3:18.text: For if the inheritance depends on the law, then it no longer depends on a promise; but God freely granted it to Abraham through a promise.

48:3:19.text: Why then was the law given? It was added because of transgressions, until the arrival of the seed to whom the promise referred. It was administered through angels by a mediator.

48:3:2.text: I would like to learn just one thing from you: Did you receive the Spirit by works of the law, or by hearing with faith?

48:3:20.text: A mediator is unnecessary, however, for only one party; but God is one.

48:3:21.text: Is the law, then, opposed to the promises of God? Certainly not! For if a law had been given that could impart life, then righteousness would certainly have come from the law.

48:3:22.text: But the Scripture pronounces all things confined by sin, so that by faith in Jesus Christ the promise might be given to those who believe.

48:3:23.text: Before this faith came, we were held in custody under the law, locked up until faith should be revealed.

48:3:24.text: So the law became our guardian to lead us to Christ, that we might be justified by faith.

48:3:25.text: Now that faith has come, we are no longer under a guardian.

48:3:26.text: You are all sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus.

48:3:27.text: For all of you who were baptized into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ.

48:3:28.text: There is neither Jew nor Greek, slave nor free, male nor female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus.

48:3:29.text: And if you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham’s seed and heirs according to the promise.

48:3:3.text: Are you so foolish? After starting in the Spirit, are you now finishing in the flesh?

48:3:4.text: Have you suffered so much for nothing, if it really was for nothing?

48:3:5.text: Does God lavish His Spirit on you and work miracles among you because you practice the law, or because you hear and believe?

48:3:6.text: So also, “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.”

48:3:7.text: Understand, then, that those who have faith are sons of Abraham.

48:3:8.text: The Scripture foresaw that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, and foretold the gospel to Abraham: “All nations will be blessed through you.”

48:3:9.text: So those who have faith are blessed along with Abraham, the man of faith.

48:4:1.text: What I am saying is that as long as the heir is a child, he is no different from a slave, although he is the owner of everything.

48:4:10.text: You are observing special days and months and seasons and years!

48:4:11.text: I fear for you, that my efforts for you may have been in vain.

48:4:12.text: I beg you, brothers, become like me, for I became like you. You have done me no wrong.

48:4:13.text: You know that it was because of an illness that I first preached the gospel to you.

48:4:14.text: And although my illness was a trial to you, you did not despise or reject me. Instead, you welcomed me as if I were an angel of God, as if I were Christ Jesus Himself.

48:4:15.text: What then has become of your blessing? For I can testify that, if it were possible, you would have torn out your eyes and given them to me.

48:4:16.text: Have I now become your enemy by telling you the truth?

48:4:17.text: Those people are zealous for you, but not in a good way. Instead, they want to isolate you from us, so that you may be zealous for them.

48:4:18.text: Nevertheless, it is good to be zealous if it serves a noble purpose — at any time, and not only when I am with you.

48:4:19.text: My children, for whom I am again in the pains of childbirth until Christ is formed in you,

48:4:2.text: He is subject to guardians and trustees until the date set by his father.

48:4:20.text: how I wish I could be with you now and change my tone, because I am perplexed about you.

48:4:21.text: Tell me, you who want to be under the law, do you not understand what the law says?

48:4:22.text: For it is written that Abraham had two sons, one by the slave woman and the other by the free woman.

48:4:23.text: His son by the slave woman was born according to the flesh, but his son by the free woman was born through the promise.

48:4:24.text: These things serve as illustrations, for the women represent two covenants. One covenant is from Mount Sinai and bears children into slavery: This is Hagar.

48:4:25.text: Now Hagar stands for Mount Sinai in Arabia and corresponds to the present-day Jerusalem, because she is in slavery with her children.

48:4:26.text: But the Jerusalem above is free, and she is our mother.

48:4:27.text: For it is written: “Rejoice, O barren woman, who bears no children; break forth and cry aloud, you who have never travailed; because more are the children of the desolate woman than of her who has a husband.”

48:4:28.text: Now you, brothers, like Isaac, are children of promise.

48:4:29.text: At that time, however, the son born by the flesh persecuted the son born by the Spirit. It is the same now.

48:4:3.text: So also, when we were children, we were enslaved under the basic principles of the world.

48:4:30.text: But what does the Scripture say? “Expel the slave woman and her son, for the slave woman’s son will never share in the inheritance with the free woman’s son.”

48:4:31.text: Therefore, brothers, we are not children of the slave woman, but of the free woman.

48:4:4.text: But when the time had fully come, God sent His Son, born of a woman, born under the law,

48:4:5.text: to redeem those under the law, that we might receive our adoption as sons.

48:4:6.text: And because you are sons, God sent the Spirit of His Son into our hearts, crying out, “Abba, Father!”

48:4:7.text: So you are no longer a slave, but a son; and since you are a son, you are also an heir through God.

48:4:8.text: Formerly, when you did not know God, you were slaves to those who by nature are not gods.

48:4:9.text: But now that you know God, or rather are known by God, how is it that you are turning back to those weak and worthless principles? Do you wish to be enslaved by them all over again?

48:5:1.text: It is for freedom that Christ has set us free. Stand firm, then, and do not be encumbered once more by a yoke of slavery.

48:5:10.text: I am confident in the Lord that you will take no other view. The one who is troubling you will bear the judgment, whoever he may be.

48:5:11.text: Now, brothers, if I am still preaching circumcision, why am I still being persecuted? In that case the offense of the cross has been abolished.

48:5:12.text: As for those who are agitating you, I wish they would proceed to emasculate themselves!

48:5:13.text: For you, brothers, were called to freedom; but do not use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh. Rather, serve one another in love.

48:5:14.text: The entire law is fulfilled in a single decree: “Love your neighbor as yourself.”

48:5:15.text: But if you keep on biting and devouring one another, watch out, or you will be consumed by one another.

48:5:16.text: So I say, walk by the Spirit, and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh.

48:5:17.text: For the flesh craves what is contrary to the Spirit, and the Spirit what is contrary to the flesh. They are opposed to each other, so that you do not do what you want.

48:5:18.text: But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the law.

48:5:19.text: The acts of the flesh are obvious: sexual immorality, impurity, and debauchery;

48:5:2.text: Take notice: I, Paul, tell you that if you let yourselves be circumcised, Christ will be of no value to you at all.

48:5:20.text: idolatry and sorcery; hatred, discord, jealousy, and rage; rivalries, divisions, factions,

48:5:21.text: and envy; drunkenness, orgies, and the like. I warn you, as I did before, that those who practice such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.

48:5:22.text: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,

48:5:23.text: gentleness, and self-control. Against such things there is no law.

48:5:24.text: Those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires.

48:5:25.text: Since we live by the Spirit, let us walk in step with the Spirit.

48:5:26.text: Let us not become conceited, provoking and envying one another.

48:5:3.text: Again I testify to every man who gets himself circumcised that he is obligated to obey the whole law.

48:5:4.text: You who are trying to be justified by the law have been severed from Christ; you have fallen away from grace.

48:5:5.text: But by faith we eagerly await through the Spirit the hope of righteousness.

48:5:6.text: For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision has any value. All that matters is faith, expressed through love.

48:5:7.text: You were running so well. Who has obstructed you from obeying the truth?

48:5:8.text: Such persuasion does not come from the One who calls you.

48:5:9.text: A little leaven works through the whole batch of dough.

48:6:1.text: Brothers, if someone is caught in a trespass, you who are spiritual should restore him with a spirit of gentleness. But watch yourself, or you also may be tempted.

48:6:10.text: Therefore, as we have opportunity, let us do good to everyone, and especially to the family of faith.

48:6:11.text: See what large letters I am using to write to you with my own hand!

48:6:12.text: Those who want to make a good impression outwardly are trying to compel you to be circumcised. They only do this to avoid persecution for the cross of Christ.

48:6:13.text: For the circumcised do not even keep the law themselves, yet they want you to be circumcised that they may boast in your flesh.

48:6:14.text: But as for me, may I never boast, except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.

48:6:15.text: For neither circumcision nor uncircumcision means anything. What counts is a new creation.

48:6:16.text: Peace and mercy to all who walk by this rule, even to the Israel of God.

48:6:17.text: From now on let no one cause me trouble, for I bear on my body the marks of Jesus.

48:6:18.text: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers. Amen.

48:6:2.text: Carry one another’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.

48:6:3.text: If anyone thinks he is something when he is nothing, he deceives himself.

48:6:4.text: Each one should test his own work. Then he will have reason to boast in himself alone, and not in someone else.

48:6:5.text: For each one should carry his own load.

48:6:6.text: Nevertheless, the one who receives instruction in the word must share in all good things with his instructor.

48:6:7.text: Do not be deceived: God is not to be mocked. Whatever a man sows, he will reap in return.

48:6:8.text: The one who sows to please his flesh, from the flesh will reap destruction; but the one who sows to please the Spirit, from the Spirit will reap eternal life.

48:6:9.text: Let us not grow weary in well-doing, for in due time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up.

49:1:1.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, To the saints in Ephesus, the faithful in Christ Jesus:

49:1:10.text: as a plan for the fullness of time, to bring all things in heaven and on earth together in Christ.

49:1:11.text: In Him we were also chosen as God’s own, having been predestined according to the plan of Him who works out everything by the counsel of His will,

49:1:12.text: in order that we, who were the first to hope in Christ, would be for the praise of His glory.

49:1:13.text: And in Him, having heard and believed the word of truth — the gospel of your salvation — you were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit,

49:1:14.text: who is the pledge of our inheritance until the redemption of those who are God’s possession, to the praise of His glory.

49:1:15.text: For this reason, ever since I heard about your faith in the Lord Jesus and your love for all the saints,

49:1:16.text: I have not stopped giving thanks for you, remembering you in my prayers,

49:1:17.text: that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the glorious Father, may give you a spirit of wisdom and revelation in your knowledge of Him.
