58:13:17.text: Obey your leaders and submit to them, for they watch over your souls as those who must give an account. To this end, allow them to lead with joy and not with grief, for that would be of no advantage to you.

58:13:18.text: Pray for us; we are convinced that we have a clear conscience and desire to live honorably in every way.

58:13:19.text: And I especially urge you to pray that I may be restored to you soon.

58:13:2.text: Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers, for by so doing some people have entertained angels without knowing it.

58:13:20.text: Now may the God of peace, who through the blood of the eternal covenant brought back from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great Shepherd of the sheep,

58:13:21.text: equip you with every good thing to do His will. And may He accomplish in us what is pleasing in His sight through Jesus Christ, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.

58:13:22.text: I urge you, brothers, to bear with my word of exhortation, for I have only written to you briefly.

58:13:23.text: Be aware that our brother Timothy has been released. If he arrives soon, I will come with him to see you.

58:13:24.text: Greet all your leaders and all the saints. Those from Italy send you greetings.

58:13:25.text: Grace be with all of you.

58:13:3.text: Remember those in prison as if you were bound with them, and those who are mistreated as if you were suffering with them.

58:13:4.text: Marriage should be honored by all and the marriage bed kept undefiled, for God will judge the sexually immoral and adulterers.

58:13:5.text: Keep your lives free from the love of money and be content with what you have, for God has said: “Never will I leave you, never will I forsake you.”

58:13:6.text: So we say with confidence: “The Lord is my helper; I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?”

58:13:7.text: Remember your leaders who spoke the word of God to you. Consider the outcome of their way of life and imitate their faith.

58:13:8.text: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.

58:13:9.text: Do not be carried away by all kinds of strange teachings, for it is good for the heart to be strengthened by grace and not by foods of no value to those devoted to them.

58:1:1.text: On many past occasions and in many different ways, God spoke to our fathers through the prophets.

58:1:10.text: And: “In the beginning, O Lord, You laid the foundations of the earth, and the heavens are the work of Your hands.

58:1:11.text: They will perish, but You remain; they will all wear out like a garment.

58:1:12.text: You will roll them up like a robe; like a garment they will be changed; but You remain the same, and Your years will never end.”

58:1:13.text: Yet to which of the angels did God ever say: “Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet”?

58:1:14.text: Are not the angels ministering spirits sent to serve those who will inherit salvation?

58:1:2.text: But in these last days He has spoken to us by His Son, whom He appointed heir of all things, and through whom He made the universe.

58:1:3.text: The Son is the radiance of God’s glory and the exact representation of His nature, upholding all things by His powerful word. After He had provided purification for sins, He sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high.

58:1:4.text: So He became as far superior to the angels as the name He has inherited is excellent beyond theirs.

58:1:5.text: For to which of the angels did God ever say: “You are My Son; today I have become Your Father”? Or again: “I will be His Father, and He will be My Son”?

58:1:6.text: And again, when God brings His firstborn into the world, He says: “Let all God’s angels worship Him.”

58:1:7.text: Now about the angels He says: “He makes His angels winds, His servants flames of fire.”

58:1:8.text: But about the Son He says: “Your throne, O God, endures forever and ever, and justice is the scepter of Your kingdom.

58:1:9.text: You have loved righteousness and hated wickedness; therefore God, Your God, has anointed You above Your companions with the oil of joy.”

58:2:1.text: We must pay closer attention, therefore, to what we have heard, so that we do not drift away.

58:2:10.text: In bringing many sons to glory, it was fitting for God, for whom and through whom all things exist, to make the author of their salvation perfect through suffering.

58:2:11.text: For both the One who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are of the same family. So Jesus is not ashamed to call them brothers.

58:2:12.text: He says: “I will proclaim Your name to My brothers; I will sing Your praises in the assembly.”

58:2:13.text: And again: “I will put My trust in Him.” And once again: “Here am I, and the children God has given Me.”

58:2:14.text: Now since the children have flesh and blood, He too shared in their humanity, so that by His death He might destroy him who holds the power of death, that is, the devil,

58:2:15.text: and free those who all their lives were held in slavery by their fear of death.

58:2:16.text: For surely it is not the angels He helps, but the descendants of Abraham.

58:2:17.text: For this reason He had to be made like His brothers in every way, so that He might become a merciful and faithful high priest in service to God, in order to make atonement for the sins of the people.

58:2:18.text: Because He Himself suffered when He was tempted, He is able to help those who are being tempted.

58:2:2.text: For if the message spoken by angels was binding, and every transgression and disobedience received its just punishment,

58:2:3.text: how shall we escape if we neglect such a great salvation? This salvation was first announced by the Lord, was confirmed to us by those who heard Him,

58:2:4.text: and was affirmed by God through signs, wonders, various miracles, and gifts of the Holy Spirit distributed according to His will.

58:2:5.text: For it is not to angels that He has subjected the world to come, about which we are speaking.

58:2:6.text: But somewhere it is testified in these words: “What is man that You are mindful of him, or the son of man that You care for him?

58:2:7.text: You made him a little lower than the angels; You crowned him with glory and honor

58:2:8.text: and placed everything under his feet.” When God subjected all things to him, He left nothing outside of his control. Yet at present we do not see everything subject to him.

58:2:9.text: But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels, now crowned with glory and honor because He suffered death, so that by the grace of God He might taste death for everyone.

58:3:1.text: Therefore, holy brothers, who share in the heavenly calling, set your focus on Jesus, the apostle and high priest whom we confess.

58:3:10.text: Therefore I was angry with that generation, and I said, ‘Their hearts are always going astray, and they have not known My ways.’

58:3:11.text: So I swore on oath in My anger, ‘They shall never enter My rest.’ ”

58:3:12.text: See to it, brothers, that none of you has a wicked heart of unbelief that turns away from the living God.

58:3:13.text: But exhort one another daily, as long as it is called today, so that none of you may be hardened by sin’s deceitfulness.

58:3:14.text: We have come to share in Christ if we hold firmly to the end the assurance we had at first.

58:3:15.text: As it has been said: “Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts, as you did in the rebellion.”

58:3:16.text: For who were the ones who heard and rebelled? Were they not all those Moses led out of Egypt?

58:3:17.text: And with whom was God angry for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?

58:3:18.text: And to whom did He swear that they would never enter His rest? Was it not to those who disobeyed?

58:3:19.text: So we see that it was because of their unbelief that they were unable to enter.

58:3:2.text: He was faithful to the One who appointed Him, just as Moses was faithful in all God’s house.

58:3:3.text: For Jesus has been counted worthy of greater glory than Moses, just as the builder of a house has greater honor than the house itself.

58:3:4.text: And every house is built by someone, but God is the builder of everything.

58:3:5.text: Now Moses was faithful as a servant in all God’s house, testifying to what would be spoken later.

58:3:6.text: But Christ is faithful as the Son over God’s house. And we are His house, if we hold firmly to our confidence and the hope of which we boast.

58:3:7.text: Therefore, as the Holy Spirit says: “Today, if you hear His voice,

58:3:8.text: do not harden your hearts, as you did in the rebellion, in the day of testing in the wilderness,

58:3:9.text: where your fathers tested and tried Me, and for forty years saw My works.

58:4:1.text: Therefore, while the promise of entering His rest still stands, let us be careful that none of you be deemed to have fallen short of it.

58:4:10.text: For whoever enters God’s rest also rests from his own work, just as God did from His.

58:4:11.text: Let us, therefore, make every effort to enter that rest, so that no one will fall by following the same pattern of disobedience.

58:4:12.text: For the word of God is living and active. Sharper than any double-edged sword, it pierces even to dividing soul and spirit, joints and marrow. It judges the thoughts and intentions of the heart.

58:4:13.text: Nothing in all creation is hidden from God’s sight; everything is uncovered and exposed before the eyes of Him to whom we must give account.

58:4:14.text: Therefore, since we have a great high priest who has passed through the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold firmly to what we profess.

58:4:15.text: For we do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but we have one who was tempted in every way that we are, yet was without sin.

58:4:16.text: Let us then approach the throne of grace with confidence, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help us in our time of need.

58:4:2.text: For we also received the good news just as they did; but the message they heard was of no value to them, since they did not share the faith of those who comprehended it.

58:4:3.text: Now we who have believed enter that rest. As for the others, it is just as God has said: “So I swore on oath in My anger, ‘They shall never enter My rest.’ ” And yet His works have been finished since the foundation of the world.

58:4:4.text: For somewhere He has spoken about the seventh day in this manner: “And on the seventh day God rested from all His works.”

58:4:5.text: And again, as He says in the passage above: “They shall never enter My rest.”

58:4:6.text: Since, then, it remains for some to enter His rest, and since those who formerly heard the good news did not enter because of their disobedience,

58:4:7.text: God again designated a certain day as “Today,” when a long time later He spoke through David as was just stated: “Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts.”

58:4:8.text: For if Joshua had given them rest, God would not have spoken later about another day.

58:4:9.text: There remains, then, a Sabbath rest for the people of God.

58:5:1.text: Every high priest is appointed from among men to represent them in matters relating to God, to offer gifts and sacrifices for sins.

58:5:10.text: and was designated by God as high priest in the order of Melchizedek.

58:5:11.text: We have much to say about this, but it is hard to explain, because you are dull of hearing.

58:5:12.text: Although by this time you ought to be teachers, you need someone to reteach you the basic principles of God’s word. You need milk, not solid food!

58:5:13.text: For everyone who lives on milk is still an infant, inexperienced in the message of righteousness.

58:5:14.text: But solid food is for the mature, who by constant use have trained their senses to distinguish good from evil.

58:5:2.text: He is able to deal gently with those who are ignorant and misguided, since he himself is beset by weakness.

58:5:3.text: That is why he is obligated to offer sacrifices for his own sins, as well as for the sins of the people.

58:5:4.text: No one takes this honor upon himself; he must be called by God, just as Aaron was.

58:5:5.text: So also Christ did not take upon Himself the glory of becoming a high priest, but He was called by the One who said to Him: “You are My Son; today I have become Your Father.”

58:5:6.text: And in another passage God says: “You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.”

58:5:7.text: During the days of Jesus’ earthly life, He offered up prayers and petitions with loud cries and tears to the One who could save Him from death, and He was heard because of His reverence.

58:5:8.text: Although He was a Son, He learned obedience from what He suffered.

58:5:9.text: And having been made perfect, He became the source of eternal salvation to all who obey Him

58:6:1.text: Therefore let us leave the elementary teachings about Christ and go on to maturity, not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith in God,

58:6:10.text: For God is not unjust. He will not forget your work and the love you have shown for His name as you have ministered to the saints and continue to do so.

58:6:11.text: We want each of you to show this same diligence to the very end, in order to make your hope sure.

58:6:12.text: Then you will not be sluggish, but will imitate those who through faith and patience inherit what has been promised.

58:6:13.text: When God made His promise to Abraham, since He had no one greater to swear by, He swore by Himself,

58:6:14.text: saying, “I will surely bless you and multiply your descendants.”

58:6:15.text: And so Abraham, after waiting patiently, obtained the promise.

58:6:16.text: Men swear by someone greater than themselves, and their oath serves as a confirmation to end all argument.

58:6:17.text: So when God wanted to make the unchanging nature of His purpose very clear to the heirs of the promise, He guaranteed it with an oath.

58:6:18.text: Thus by two unchangeable things in which it is impossible for God to lie, we who have fled to take hold of the hope set before us may be strongly encouraged.

58:6:19.text: We have this hope as an anchor for the soul, firm and secure. It enters the inner sanctuary behind the curtain,

58:6:2.text: instruction about baptisms, the laying on of hands, the resurrection of the dead, and eternal judgment.

58:6:20.text: where Jesus our forerunner has entered on our behalf. He has become a high priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.

58:6:3.text: And this we will do, if God permits.

58:6:4.text: It is impossible for those who have once been enlightened, who have tasted the heavenly gift, who have shared in the Holy Spirit,

58:6:5.text: who have tasted the goodness of the word of God and the powers of the coming age —

58:6:6.text: and then have fallen away — to be restored to repentance, because they themselves are crucifying the Son of God all over again and subjecting Him to open shame.

58:6:7.text: For land that drinks in the rain often falling on it and that produces a crop useful to those for whom it is tended receives the blessing of God.

58:6:8.text: But land that produces thorns and thistles is worthless, and its curse is imminent. In the end it will be burned.

58:6:9.text: Even though we speak like this, beloved, we are convinced of better things in your case — things that accompany salvation.

58:7:1.text: This Melchizedek was king of Salem and priest of God Most High. He met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him,

58:7:10.text: For when Melchizedek met Abraham, Levi was still in the loin of his ancestor.

58:7:11.text: Now if perfection could have been attained through the Levitical priesthood (for on this basis the people received the law), why was there still need for another priest to appear — one in the order of Melchizedek and not in the order of Aaron?

58:7:12.text: For when the priesthood is changed, the law must be changed as well.

58:7:13.text: He of whom these things are said belonged to a different tribe, from which no one has ever served at the altar.

58:7:14.text: For it is clear that our Lord descended from Judah, a tribe as to which Moses said nothing about priests.

58:7:15.text: And this point is even more clear if another priest like Melchizedek appears,

58:7:16.text: one who has become a priest not by a law of succession, but by the power of an indestructible life.

58:7:17.text: For it is testified: “You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.”

58:7:18.text: So the former commandment is set aside because it was weak and useless

58:7:19.text: (for the law made nothing perfect), and a better hope is introduced, by which we draw near to God.

58:7:2.text: and Abraham apportioned to him a tenth of everything. First, his name means “king of righteousness.” Then also, “king of Salem” means “king of peace.”

58:7:20.text: And none of this happened without an oath. For others became priests without an oath,

58:7:21.text: but Jesus became a priest with an oath by the One who said to Him: “The Lord has sworn and will not change His mind: ‘You are a priest forever.’ ”

58:7:22.text: Because of this oath, Jesus has become the guarantee of a better covenant.

58:7:23.text: Now there have been many other priests, since death prevented them from continuing in office.

58:7:24.text: But because Jesus lives forever, He has a permanent priesthood.

58:7:25.text: Therefore He is able to save completely those who draw near to God through Him, since He always lives to intercede for them.

58:7:26.text: Such a high priest truly befits us — One who is holy, innocent, undefiled, set apart from sinners, and exalted above the heavens.

58:7:27.text: Unlike the other high priests, He does not need to offer daily sacrifices, first for His own sins and then for the sins of the people; He sacrificed for sin once for all when He offered up Himself.

58:7:28.text: For the law appoints as high priests men who are weak; but the oath, which came after the law, appointed the Son, who has been made perfect forever.

58:7:3.text: Without father or mother or genealogy, without beginning of days or end of life, like the Son of God, he remains a priest for all time.

58:7:4.text: Consider how great Melchizedek was: Even the patriarch Abraham gave him a tenth of the plunder.

58:7:5.text: Now the law commands the sons of Levi who become priests to collect a tenth from the people — that is, from their brothers — though they too are descended from Abraham.

58:7:6.text: But Melchizedek, who did not trace his descent from Levi, collected a tenth from Abraham and blessed him who had the promises.

58:7:7.text: And indisputably, the lesser is blessed by the greater.

58:7:8.text: In the case of the Levites, mortal men collect the tenth; but in the case of Melchizedek, it is affirmed that he lives on.

58:7:9.text: And so to speak, Levi, who collects the tenth, paid the tenth through Abraham.

58:8:1.text: The point of what we are saying is this: We do have such a high priest, who sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in heaven,

58:8:10.text: For this is the covenant I will make with the house of Israel after those days, declares the Lord. I will put My laws in their minds and inscribe them on their hearts. And I will be their God, and they will be My people.

58:8:11.text: No longer will each one teach his neighbor or his brother, saying, ‘Know the Lord,’ because they will all know Me, from the least of them to the greatest.

58:8:12.text: For I will forgive their iniquities and will remember their sins no more.”

58:8:13.text: By speaking of a new covenant, He has made the first one obsolete; and what is obsolete and aging will soon disappear.

58:8:2.text: and who ministers in the sanctuary and true tabernacle set up by the Lord, not by man.

58:8:3.text: And since every high priest is appointed to offer both gifts and sacrifices, it was necessary for this One also to have something to offer.

58:8:4.text: Now if He were on earth, He would not be a priest, since there are already priests who offer gifts according to the law.

58:8:5.text: The place where they serve is a copy and shadow of what is in heaven. This is why Moses was warned when he was about to build the tabernacle: “See to it that you make everything according to the pattern shown you on the mountain.”

58:8:6.text: Now, however, Jesus has received a much more excellent ministry, just as the covenant He mediates is better and is founded on better promises.

58:8:7.text: For if that first covenant had been without fault, no place would have been sought for a second.

58:8:8.text: But God found fault with the people and said: “Behold, the days are coming, declares the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.

58:8:9.text: It will not be like the covenant I made with their fathers when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt, because they did not abide by My covenant, and I disregarded them, declares the Lord.

58:9:1.text: Now the first covenant had regulations for worship and also an earthly sanctuary.

58:9:10.text: They consist only in food and drink and special washings — external regulations imposed until the time of reform.

58:9:11.text: But when Christ came as high priest of the good things that have come, He went through the greater and more perfect tabernacle that is not made by hands and is not a part of this creation.

58:9:12.text: He did not enter by the blood of goats and calves, but He entered the Most Holy Place once for all by His own blood, thus securing eternal redemption.

58:9:13.text: For if the blood of goats and bulls and the ashes of a heifer sprinkled on those who are ceremonially unclean sanctify them so that their bodies are clean,

58:9:14.text: how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered Himself unblemished to God, purify our consciences from works of death, so that we may serve the living God!

58:9:15.text: Therefore Christ is the mediator of a new covenant, so that those who are called may receive the promised eternal inheritance, now that He has died to redeem them from the transgressions committed under the first covenant.

58:9:16.text: In the case of a will, it is necessary to establish the death of the one who made it,

58:9:17.text: because a will does not take effect until the one who made it has died; it cannot be executed while he is still alive.

58:9:18.text: That is why even the first covenant was not put into effect without blood.

58:9:19.text: For when Moses had proclaimed every commandment of the law to all the people, he took the blood of calves and goats, along with water, scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled the scroll and all the people,

58:9:2.text: A tabernacle was prepared. In its first room were the lampstand, the table, and the consecrated bread. This was called the Holy Place.

58:9:20.text: saying, “This is the blood of the covenant, which God has commanded you to keep.”

58:9:21.text: In the same way, he sprinkled with blood the tabernacle and all the vessels used in worship.

58:9:22.text: According to the law, in fact, nearly everything must be purified with blood, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.

58:9:23.text: So it was necessary for the copies of the heavenly things to be purified with these sacrifices, but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.

58:9:24.text: For Christ did not enter a man-made copy of the true sanctuary, but He entered heaven itself, now to appear on our behalf in the presence of God.

58:9:25.text: Nor did He enter heaven to offer Himself again and again, as the high priest enters the Most Holy Place every year with blood that is not his own.

58:9:26.text: Otherwise, Christ would have had to suffer repeatedly since the foundation of the world. But now He has appeared once for all at the end of the ages to do away with sin by the sacrifice of Himself.

58:9:27.text: Just as man is appointed to die once, and after that to face judgment,

58:9:28.text: so also Christ was offered once to bear the sins of many; and He will appear a second time, not to bear sin, but to bring salvation to those who eagerly await Him.

58:9:3.text: Behind the second curtain was a room called the Most Holy Place,

58:9:4.text: containing the golden altar of incense and the gold-covered ark of the covenant. Inside the ark were the gold jar of manna, Aaron’s staff that had budded, and the stone tablets of the covenant.

58:9:5.text: Above the ark were the cherubim of glory, overshadowing the mercy seat. But we cannot discuss these things in detail now.

58:9:6.text: When everything had been prepared in this way, the priests entered regularly into the first room to perform their sacred duties.

58:9:7.text: But only the high priest entered the second room, and then only once a year, and never without blood, which he offered for himself and for the sins the people had committed in ignorance.

58:9:8.text: By this arrangement the Holy Spirit was showing that the way into the Most Holy Place had not yet been disclosed as long as the first tabernacle was still standing.

58:9:9.text: It is an illustration for the present time, because the gifts and sacrifices being offered were unable to cleanse the conscience of the worshiper.

59:1:1.text: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, To the twelve tribes of the Dispersion: Greetings.

59:1:10.text: But the one who is rich should exult in his low position, because he will pass away like a flower of the field.

59:1:11.text: For the sun rises with scorching heat and withers the plant; its flower falls and its beauty is lost. So too, the rich man will fade away in the midst of his pursuits.

59:1:12.text: Blessed is the man who perseveres under trial, because when he has stood the test, he will receive the crown of life that God has promised to those who love Him.

59:1:13.text: When tempted, no one should say, “God is tempting me.” For God cannot be tempted by evil, nor does He tempt anyone.

59:1:14.text: But each one is tempted when by his own evil desires he is lured away and enticed.

59:1:15.text: Then after desire has conceived, it gives birth to sin; and sin, when it is full-grown, gives birth to death.

59:1:16.text: Do not be deceived, my beloved brothers.

59:1:17.text: Every good and perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of the heavenly lights, with whom there is no change or shifting shadow.

59:1:18.text: He chose to give us birth through the word of truth, that we would be a kind of firstfruits of His creation.

59:1:19.text: My beloved brothers, understand this: Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to anger,

59:1:2.text: Consider it pure joy, my brothers, when you encounter trials of many kinds,

59:1:20.text: for man’s anger does not bring about the righteousness that God desires.

59:1:21.text: Therefore, get rid of all moral filth and every expression of evil, and humbly accept the word planted in you, which can save your souls.

59:1:22.text: Be doers of the word, and not hearers only. Otherwise, you are deceiving yourselves.

59:1:23.text: For anyone who hears the word but does not carry it out is like a man who looks at his face in a mirror,

59:1:24.text: and after observing himself goes away and immediately forgets what he looks like.

59:1:25.text: But the one who looks intently into the perfect law of freedom, and continues to do so — not being a forgetful hearer, but an effective doer — he will be blessed in what he does.

59:1:26.text: If anyone considers himself religious and yet does not bridle his tongue, he deceives his heart and his religion is worthless.

59:1:27.text: Pure and undefiled religion before our God and Father is this: to care for orphans and widows in their distress, and to keep oneself from being polluted by the world.

59:1:3.text: because you know that the testing of your faith develops perseverance.

59:1:4.text: Allow perseverance to finish its work, so that you may be mature and complete, not lacking anything.

59:1:5.text: Now if any of you lacks wisdom, he should ask God, who gives generously to all without finding fault, and it will be given to him.

59:1:6.text: But he must ask in faith, without doubting, because he who doubts is like a wave of the sea, blown and tossed by the wind.

59:1:7.text: That man should not expect to receive anything from the Lord.

59:1:8.text: He is a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways.

59:1:9.text: The brother in humble circumstances should exult in his high position.

59:2:1.text: My brothers, as you hold out your faith in our glorious Lord Jesus Christ, do not show favoritism.

59:2:10.text: Whoever keeps the whole law but stumbles at just one point is guilty of breaking all of it.

59:2:11.text: For He who said, “Do not commit adultery,” also said, “Do not murder.” If you do not commit adultery, but do commit murder, you have become a lawbreaker.

59:2:12.text: Speak and act as those who are going to be judged by the law that gives freedom.

59:2:13.text: For judgment without mercy will be shown to anyone who has not been merciful. Mercy triumphs over judgment.

59:2:14.text: What good is it, my brothers, if someone claims to have faith, but has no deeds? Can such faith save him?

59:2:15.text: Suppose a brother or sister is without clothes and daily food.

59:2:16.text: If one of you tells him, “Go in peace; stay warm and well fed,” but does not provide for his physical needs, what good is that?

59:2:17.text: So too, faith by itself, if it does not result in action, is dead.

59:2:18.text: But someone will say, “You have faith and I have deeds.” Show me your faith without deeds, and I will show you my faith by my deeds.

59:2:19.text: You believe that God is one. Good for you! Even the demons believe that — and shudder.

59:2:2.text: Suppose a man comes into your meeting wearing a gold ring and fine clothes, and a poor man in shabby clothes also comes in.

59:2:20.text: O foolish man, do you want evidence that faith without deeds is worthless?

59:2:21.text: Was not our father Abraham justified by what he did when he offered his son Isaac on the altar?

59:2:22.text: You see that his faith was working with his actions, and his faith was perfected by what he did.

59:2:23.text: And the Scripture was fulfilled that says, “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness,” and he was called a friend of God.

59:2:24.text: As you can see, a man is justified by his deeds and not by faith alone.

59:2:25.text: In the same way, was not even Rahab the prostitute justified by her actions when she welcomed the spies and sent them off on another route?

59:2:26.text: As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without deeds is dead.

59:2:3.text: If you lavish attention on the man in fine clothes and say, “Here is a seat of honor,” but say to the poor man, “You must stand” or “Sit at my feet,”

59:2:4.text: have you not discriminated among yourselves and become judges with evil thoughts?

59:2:5.text: Listen, my beloved brothers: Has not God chosen the poor of this world to be rich in faith and to inherit the kingdom He promised those who love Him?

59:2:6.text: But you have dishonored the poor. Is it not the rich who oppress you and drag you into court?

59:2:7.text: Are they not the ones who blaspheme the noble name by which you have been called?

59:2:8.text: If you really fulfill the royal law stated in Scripture, “Love your neighbor as yourself,” you are doing well.

59:2:9.text: But if you show favoritism, you sin and are convicted by the law as transgressors.

59:3:1.text: Not many of you should become teachers, my brothers, because you know that we who teach will be judged more strictly.

59:3:10.text: Out of the same mouth come blessing and cursing. My brothers, this should not be!

59:3:11.text: Can both fresh water and salt water flow from the same spring?

59:3:12.text: My brothers, can a fig tree grow olives, or a grapevine bear figs? Neither can a salt spring produce fresh water.

59:3:13.text: Who is wise and understanding among you? Let him show it by his good conduct, by deeds done in the humility that comes from wisdom.

59:3:14.text: But if you harbor bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your hearts, do not boast in it or deny the truth.

59:3:15.text: Such wisdom does not come from above, but is earthly, unspiritual, demonic.

59:3:16.text: For where jealousy and selfish ambition exist, there will be disorder and every evil practice.

59:3:17.text: But the wisdom from above is first of all pure, then peace-loving, gentle, accommodating, full of mercy and good fruit, impartial, and sincere.

59:3:18.text: Peacemakers who sow in peace reap the fruit of righteousness.

59:3:2.text: We all stumble in many ways. If anyone is never at fault in what he says, he is a perfect man, able to control his whole body.

59:3:3.text: When we put bits into the mouths of horses to make them obey us, we can guide the whole animal.

59:3:4.text: Consider ships as well. Although they are so large and are driven by strong winds, they are steered by a very small rudder wherever the pilot is inclined.

59:3:5.text: In the same way, the tongue is a small part of the body, but it boasts of great things. Consider how small a spark sets a great forest ablaze.

59:3:6.text: The tongue also is a fire, a world of wickedness among the parts of the body. It pollutes the whole person, sets the course of his life on fire, and is itself set on fire by hell.

59:3:7.text: All kinds of animals, birds, reptiles, and creatures of the sea are being tamed and have been tamed by man,

59:3:8.text: but no man can tame the tongue. It is a restless evil, full of deadly poison.

59:3:9.text: With the tongue we bless our Lord and Father, and with it we curse men, who have been made in God’s likeness.

59:4:1.text: What causes conflicts and quarrels among you? Don’t they come from the passions at war within you?

59:4:10.text: Humble yourselves before the Lord, and He will exalt you.

59:4:11.text: Brothers, do not slander one another. Anyone who speaks against his brother or judges him speaks against the law and judges it. And if you judge the law, you are not a practitioner of the law, but a judge of it.

59:4:12.text: There is only one Lawgiver and Judge, the One who is able to save and destroy. But who are you to judge your neighbor?

59:4:13.text: Come now, you who say, “Today or tomorrow we will go to this or that city, spend a year there, carry on business, and make a profit.”

59:4:14.text: You do not even know what will happen tomorrow! What is your life? You are a mist that appears for a little while and then vanishes.

59:4:15.text: Instead, you ought to say, “If the Lord is willing, we will live and do this or that.”

59:4:16.text: As it is, you boast in your proud intentions. All such boasting is evil.

59:4:17.text: Anyone, then, who knows the right thing to do, yet fails to do it, is guilty of sin.

59:4:2.text: You crave what you do not have; you kill and covet, but are unable to obtain it. You quarrel and fight. You do not have, because you do not ask.

59:4:3.text: And when you do ask, you do not receive, because you ask with wrong motives, that you may squander it on your pleasures.

59:4:4.text: You adulteresses! Do you not know that friendship with the world is hostility toward God? Therefore, whoever chooses to be a friend of the world renders himself an enemy of God.

59:4:5.text: Or do you think the Scripture says without reason that the Spirit He caused to dwell in us yearns with envy?

59:4:6.text: But He gives us more grace. This is why it says: “God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”

59:4:7.text: Submit yourselves, then, to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.

59:4:8.text: Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you double-minded.

59:4:9.text: Grieve, mourn, and weep. Turn your laughter to mourning, and your joy to gloom.

59:5:1.text: Come now, you who are rich, weep and wail over the misery to come upon you.

59:5:10.text: Brothers, as an example of patience in affliction, take the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.

59:5:11.text: See how blessed we consider those who have persevered. You have heard of Job’s perseverance and have seen the outcome from the Lord. The Lord is full of compassion and mercy.

59:5:12.text: Above all, my brothers, do not swear, not by heaven or earth or by any other oath. Simply let your “Yes” be yes, and your “No,” no, so that you will not fall under judgment.

59:5:13.text: Is any one of you suffering? He should pray. Is anyone cheerful? He should sing praises.

59:5:14.text: Is any one of you sick? He should call the elders of the church to pray over him and anoint him with oil in the name of the Lord.

59:5:15.text: And the prayer offered in faith will restore the one who is sick. The Lord will raise him up. If he has sinned, he will be forgiven.

59:5:16.text: Therefore confess your sins to each other and pray for each other so that you may be healed. The prayer of a righteous man has great power to prevail.

59:5:17.text: Elijah was a man just like us. He prayed earnestly that it would not rain, and it did not rain on the land for three and a half years.

59:5:18.text: Again he prayed, and the heavens gave rain, and the earth yielded its crops.

59:5:19.text: My brothers, if one of you should wander from the truth and someone should bring him back,

59:5:2.text: Your riches have rotted and moths have eaten your clothes.

59:5:20.text: consider this: Whoever turns a sinner from the error of his way will save his soul from death and cover over a multitude of sins.

59:5:3.text: Your gold and silver are corroded. Their corrosion will testify against you and consume your flesh like fire. You have hoarded treasure in the last days.

59:5:4.text: Look, the wages you withheld from the workmen who mowed your fields are crying out against you. The cries of the harvesters have reached the ears of the Lord of Hosts.

59:5:5.text: You have lived on earth in luxury and self-indulgence. You have fattened your hearts in the day of slaughter.

59:5:6.text: You have condemned and murdered the righteous, who did not resist you.

59:5:7.text: Be patient, then, brothers, until the Lord’s coming. See how the farmer awaits the precious fruit of the soil — how patient he is for the fall and spring rains.

59:5:8.text: You, too, be patient and strengthen your hearts, because the Lord’s coming is near.

59:5:9.text: Do not complain about one another, brothers, so that you will not be judged. Look, the Judge is standing at the door!

60:1:1.text: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, To the elect who are exiles of the Dispersion throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia, chosen

60:1:10.text: Concerning this salvation, the prophets who foretold the grace to come to you searched and investigated carefully,

60:1:11.text: trying to determine the time and setting to which the Spirit of Christ in them was pointing when He predicted the sufferings of Christ and the glories to follow.

60:1:12.text: It was revealed to them that they were not serving themselves, but you, when they foretold the things now announced by those who preached the gospel to you by the Holy Spirit sent from heaven. Even angels long to look into these things.

60:1:13.text: Therefore prepare your minds for action. Be sober-minded. Set your hope fully on the grace to be given you at the revelation of Jesus Christ.

60:1:14.text: As obedient children, do not conform to the passions of your former ignorance.

60:1:15.text: But just as He who called you is holy, so be holy in all you do,

60:1:16.text: for it is written: “Be holy, because I am holy.”

60:1:17.text: Since you call on a Father who judges each one’s work impartially, conduct yourselves in reverent fear during your stay as foreigners.

60:1:18.text: For you know that it was not with perishable things such as silver or gold that you were redeemed from the empty way of life you inherited from your forefathers,

60:1:19.text: but with the precious blood of Christ, a lamb without blemish or spot.

60:1:2.text: according to the foreknowledge of God the Father and sanctified by the Spirit for obedience to Jesus Christ and sprinkling by His blood: Grace and peace be yours in abundance.

60:1:20.text: He was known before the foundation of the world, but was revealed in the last times for your sake.

60:1:21.text: Through Him you believe in God, who raised Him from the dead and glorified Him; and so your faith and hope are in God.

60:1:22.text: Since you have purified your souls by obedience to the truth so that you have a genuine love for your brothers, love one another deeply, from a pure heart.

60:1:23.text: For you have been born again, not of perishable seed, but of imperishable, through the living and enduring word of God.

60:1:24.text: For, “All flesh is like grass, and all its glory like the flowers of the field; the grass withers and the flowers fall,

60:1:25.text: but the word of the Lord stands forever.” And this is the word that was proclaimed to you.

60:1:3.text: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ! By His great mercy He has given us new birth into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,

60:1:4.text: and into an inheritance that is imperishable, undefiled, and unfading, reserved in heaven for you,

60:1:5.text: who through faith are shielded by God’s power for the salvation that is ready to be revealed in the last time.

60:1:6.text: In this you greatly rejoice, though now for a little while you may have had to suffer grief in various trials

60:1:7.text: so that the proven character of your faith — more precious than gold, which perishes even though refined by fire — may result in praise, glory, and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ.

60:1:8.text: Though you have not seen Him, you love Him; and though you do not see Him now, you believe in Him and rejoice with an inexpressible and glorious joy,

60:1:9.text: now that you are receiving the goal of your faith, the salvation of your souls.

60:2:1.text: Rid yourselves, therefore, of all malice, deceit, hypocrisy, envy, and slander.

60:2:10.text: Once you were not a people, but now you are the people of God; once you had not received mercy, but now you have received mercy.

60:2:11.text: Beloved, I urge you, as foreigners and exiles, to abstain from the desires of the flesh, which war against your soul.

60:2:12.text: Conduct yourselves with such honor among the Gentiles that, though they slander you as evildoers, they may see your good deeds and glorify God on the day He visits us.

60:2:13.text: Submit yourselves for the Lord’s sake to every human institution, whether to the king as the supreme authority,

60:2:14.text: or to governors as those sent by him to punish those who do wrong and to praise those who do right.

60:2:15.text: For it is God’s will that by doing good you should silence the ignorance of foolish men.

60:2:16.text: Live in freedom, but do not use your freedom as a cover-up for evil; live as servants of God.

60:2:17.text: Treat everyone with high regard: Love the brotherhood of believers, fear God, honor the king.

60:2:18.text: Servants, submit yourselves to your masters with all respect, not only to those who are good and gentle, but even to those who are unreasonable.

60:2:19.text: For if anyone endures the pain of unjust suffering because he is conscious of God, this is to be commended.

60:2:2.text: Like newborn babies, crave pure spiritual milk, so that by it you may grow up in your salvation,

60:2:20.text: How is it to your credit if you are beaten for doing wrong and you endure it? But if you suffer for doing good and you endure it, this is commendable before God.

60:2:21.text: For to this you were called, because Christ also suffered for you, leaving you an example, that you should follow in His footsteps:

60:2:22.text: “He committed no sin, and no deceit was found in His mouth.”

60:2:23.text: When they heaped abuse on Him, He did not retaliate; when He suffered, He made no threats, but entrusted Himself to Him who judges justly.

60:2:24.text: He Himself bore our sins in His body on the tree, so that we might die to sin and live to righteousness. “By His stripes you are healed.”

60:2:25.text: For “you were like sheep going astray,” but now you have returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls.

60:2:3.text: now that you have tasted that the Lord is good.

60:2:4.text: As you come to Him, the living stone, rejected by men but chosen and precious in God’s sight,

60:2:5.text: you also, like living stones, are being built into a spiritual house to be a holy priesthood, offering spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.

60:2:6.text: For it stands in Scripture: “See, I lay in Zion a stone, a chosen and precious cornerstone; and the one who believes in Him will never be put to shame.”

60:2:7.text: To you who believe, then, this stone is precious. But to those who do not believe, “The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone,”

60:2:8.text: and, “A stone of stumbling and a rock of offense.” They stumble because they disobey the word — and to this they were appointed.

60:2:9.text: But you are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God’s own possession, to proclaim the virtues of Him who called you out of darkness into His marvelous light.

60:3:1.text: Wives, in the same way, submit yourselves to your husbands, so that even if they refuse to believe the word, they will be won over without words by the behavior of their wives

60:3:10.text: For, “Whoever would love life and see good days must keep his tongue from evil and his lips from deceitful speech.

60:3:11.text: He must turn from evil and do good; he must seek peace and pursue it.

60:3:12.text: For the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous, and His ears are inclined to their prayer. But the face of the Lord is against those who do evil.”

60:3:13.text: Who can harm you if you are zealous for what is good?

60:3:14.text: But even if you should suffer for what is right, you are blessed. “Do not fear what they fear; do not be shaken.”

60:3:15.text: But in your hearts sanctify Christ as Lord. Always be prepared to give a defense to everyone who asks you the reason for the hope that is in you. But respond with gentleness and respect,

60:3:16.text: keeping a clear conscience, so that those who slander you may be put to shame by your good behavior in Christ.

60:3:17.text: For it is better, if it is God’s will, to suffer for doing good than for doing evil.

60:3:18.text: For Christ also suffered for sins once for all, the righteous for the unrighteous, to bring you to God. He was put to death in the body but made alive in the Spirit,

60:3:19.text: in whom He also went and preached to the spirits in prison

60:3:2.text: when they see your pure and reverent demeanor.

60:3:20.text: who disobeyed long ago when God waited patiently in the days of Noah while the ark was being built. In the ark a few people, only eight souls, were saved through water.

60:3:21.text: And this water symbolizes the baptism that now saves you also — not the removal of dirt from the body, but the pledge of a clear conscience toward God — through the resurrection of Jesus Christ,

60:3:22.text: who has gone into heaven and is at the right hand of God, with angels, authorities, and powers subject to Him.

60:3:3.text: Your beauty should not come from outward adornment, such as braided hair or gold jewelry or fine clothes,

60:3:4.text: but from the inner disposition of your heart, the unfading beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit, which is precious in God’s sight.

60:3:5.text: For this is how the holy women of the past adorned themselves. They put their hope in God and were submissive to their husbands,

60:3:6.text: just as Sarah obeyed Abraham and called him lord. And you are her children if you do what is right and refuse to give way to fear.

60:3:7.text: Husbands, in the same way, treat your wives with consideration as a delicate vessel, and with honor as fellow heirs of the gracious gift of life, so that your prayers will not be hindered.

60:3:8.text: Finally, all of you, be like-minded and sympathetic, love as brothers, be tenderhearted and humble.

60:3:9.text: Do not repay evil with evil or insult with insult, but with blessing, because to this you were called so that you may inherit a blessing.

60:4:1.text: Therefore, since Christ suffered in His body, arm yourselves with the same resolve, because anyone who has suffered in his body is done with sin.

60:4:10.text: As good stewards of the manifold grace of God, each of you should use whatever gift he has received to serve one another.

60:4:11.text: If anyone speaks, he should speak as one conveying the words of God. If anyone serves, he should serve with the strength God provides, so that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom be the glory and the power forever and ever. Amen.

60:4:12.text: Beloved, do not be surprised at the fiery trial that has come upon you, as though something strange were happening to you.

60:4:13.text: But rejoice that you share in the sufferings of Christ, so that you may be overjoyed at the revelation of His glory.

60:4:14.text: If you are insulted for the name of Christ, you are blessed, because the Spirit of glory and of God rests on you.

60:4:15.text: Indeed, none of you should suffer as a murderer or thief or wrongdoer, or even as a meddler.

60:4:16.text: But if you suffer as a Christian, do not be ashamed, but glorify God that you bear that name.

60:4:17.text: For it is time for judgment to begin with the family of God; and if it begins with us, what will the outcome be for those who disobey the gospel of God?

60:4:18.text: And, “If it is hard for the righteous to be saved, what will become of the ungodly and the sinner?”

60:4:19.text: So then, those who suffer according to God’s will should entrust their souls to their faithful Creator and continue to do good.

60:4:2.text: Consequently, he does not live out his remaining time on earth for human passions, but for the will of God.

60:4:3.text: For you have spent enough time in the past carrying out the same desires as the Gentiles: living in debauchery, lust, drunkenness, orgies, carousing, and detestable idolatry.

60:4:4.text: Because of this, they consider it strange of you not to plunge with them into the same flood of reckless indiscretion, and they heap abuse on you.

60:4:5.text: But they will have to give an account to Him who is ready to judge the living and the dead.

60:4:6.text: That is why the gospel was preached even to those who are now dead, so that they might be judged as men in the flesh, but live according to God in the spirit.

60:4:7.text: The end of all things is near. Therefore be clear-minded and sober, so that you can pray.

60:4:8.text: Above all, love one another deeply, because love covers over a multitude of sins.

60:4:9.text: Show hospitality to one another without complaining.

60:5:1.text: As a fellow elder, a witness of Christ’s sufferings, and a partaker of the glory to be revealed, I appeal to the elders among you:

60:5:10.text: And after you have suffered for a little while, the God of all grace, who has called you to His eternal glory in Christ, will Himself restore you, secure you, strengthen you, and establish you.

60:5:11.text: To Him be the power forever and ever. Amen.

60:5:12.text: Through Silvanus, whom I regard as a faithful brother, I have written to you briefly, encouraging you and testifying that this is the true grace of God. Stand firm in it.

60:5:13.text: The church in Babylon, chosen together with you, sends you greetings, as does my son Mark.

60:5:14.text: Greet one another with a kiss of love. Peace to all of you who are in Christ.

60:5:2.text: Be shepherds of God’s flock that is among you, watching over them not out of compulsion, but because it is God’s will; not out of greed, but out of eagerness;

60:5:3.text: not lording it over those entrusted to you, but being examples to the flock.

60:5:4.text: And when the Chief Shepherd appears, you will receive the crown of glory that will never fade away.

60:5:5.text: Young men, in the same way, submit yourselves to your elders. And all of you, clothe yourselves with humility toward one another, because, “God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”

60:5:6.text: Humble yourselves, therefore, under God’s mighty hand, so that in due time He may exalt you.

60:5:7.text: Cast all your anxiety on Him, because He cares for you.

60:5:8.text: Be sober-minded and alert. Your adversary the devil prowls around like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour.

60:5:9.text: Resist him, standing firm in your faith and in the knowledge that your brothers throughout the world are undergoing the same kinds of suffering.

61:1:1.text: Simon Peter, a servant and apostle of Jesus Christ, To those who through the righteousness of our God and Savior Jesus Christ have received a faith as precious as ours:

61:1:10.text: Therefore, brothers, strive to make your calling and election sure. For if you practice these things you will never stumble,

61:1:11.text: and you will receive a lavish reception into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.

61:1:12.text: Therefore I will always remind you of these things, even though you know them and are established in the truth you now have.

61:1:13.text: I think it is right to refresh your memory as long as I live in the tent of my body,

61:1:14.text: because I know that this tent will soon be laid aside, as our Lord Jesus Christ has made clear to me.

61:1:15.text: And I will make every effort to ensure that after my departure, you will be able to recall these things at all times.

61:1:16.text: For we did not follow cleverly devised fables when we made known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, but we were eyewitnesses of His majesty.

61:1:17.text: For He received honor and glory from God the Father when the voice came to Him from the Majestic Glory, saying, “This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.”

61:1:18.text: And we ourselves heard this voice from heaven when we were with Him on the holy mountain.

61:1:19.text: We also have the word of the prophets as confirmed beyond doubt. And you will do well to pay attention to it, as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts.

61:1:2.text: Grace and peace be multiplied to you through the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord.

61:1:20.text: Above all, you must understand that no prophecy of Scripture comes from one’s own interpretation.

61:1:21.text: For no such prophecy was ever brought forth by the will of man, but men spoke from God as they were carried along by the Holy Spirit.

61:1:3.text: His divine power has given us everything we need for life and godliness through the knowledge of Him who called us by His own glory and excellence.

61:1:4.text: Through these He has given us His precious and magnificent promises, so that through them you may become partakers of the divine nature, now that you have escaped the corruption in the world caused by evil desires.

61:1:5.text: For this very reason, make every effort to add to your faith virtue; and to virtue, knowledge;

61:1:6.text: and to knowledge, self-control; and to self-control, perseverance; and to perseverance, godliness;

61:1:7.text: and to godliness, brotherly kindness; and to brotherly kindness, love.

61:1:8.text: For if you possess these qualities and continue to grow in them, they will keep you from being ineffective and unproductive in your knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.

61:1:9.text: But whoever lacks these traits is nearsighted to the point of blindness, having forgotten that he has been cleansed from his past sins.

61:2:1.text: Now there were also false prophets among the people, just as there will be false teachers among you. They will secretly introduce destructive heresies, even denying the Master who bought them — bringing swift destruction on themselves.

61:2:10.text: Such punishment is specially reserved for those who indulge the corrupt desires of the flesh and despise authority. Bold and self-willed, they are unafraid to slander glorious beings.

61:2:11.text: Yet not even angels, though greater in strength and power, dare to bring such slanderous charges against them before the Lord.

61:2:12.text: These men are like irrational animals, creatures of instinct, born to be captured and destroyed. They blaspheme in matters they do not understand, and like such creatures, they too will be destroyed.

61:2:13.text: The harm they will suffer is the wages of their wickedness. They consider it a pleasure to carouse in broad daylight. They are blots and blemishes, reveling in their deception as they feast with you.

61:2:14.text: Their eyes are full of adultery; their desire for sin is never satisfied; they seduce the unstable. They are accursed children with hearts trained in greed.

61:2:15.text: They have left the straight way and wandered off to follow the way of Balaam son of Beor, who loved the wages of wickedness.

61:2:16.text: But he was rebuked for his transgression by a donkey, otherwise without speech, that spoke with a man’s voice and restrained the prophet’s madness.

61:2:17.text: These men are springs without water and mists driven by a storm. Blackest darkness is reserved for them.

61:2:18.text: With lofty but empty words, they appeal to the sensual passions of the flesh and entice those who are just escaping from others who live in error.

61:2:19.text: They promise them freedom, while they themselves are slaves to depravity. For a man is a slave to whatever has mastered him.

61:2:2.text: Many will follow in their depravity, and because of them the way of truth will be defamed.

61:2:20.text: If indeed they have escaped the corruption of the world through the knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, only to be entangled and overcome by it again, their final condition is worse than it was at first.

61:2:21.text: It would have been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness than to have known it and then to turn away from the holy commandment passed on to them.

61:2:22.text: Of them the proverbs are true: “A dog returns to its vomit,” and, “A sow that is washed goes back to her wallowing in the mud.”

61:2:3.text: In their greed, these false teachers will exploit you with deceptive words. The longstanding verdict against them remains in force, and their destruction does not sleep.

61:2:4.text: For if God did not spare the angels when they sinned, but cast them deep into hell, placing them in chains of darkness to be held for judgment;

61:2:5.text: if He did not spare the ancient world when He brought the flood on its ungodly people, but preserved Noah, a preacher of righteousness, among the eight;

61:2:6.text: if He condemned the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah to destruction, reducing them to ashes as an example of what is coming on the ungodly;

61:2:7.text: and if He rescued Lot, a righteous man distressed by the depraved conduct of the lawless

61:2:8.text: (for that righteous man, living among them day after day, was tormented in his righteous soul by the lawless deeds he saw and heard) —

61:2:9.text: if all this is so, then the Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trials and to hold the unrighteous for punishment on the day of judgment.

61:3:1.text: Beloved, this is now my second letter to you. Both of them are reminders to stir you to wholesome thinking

61:3:10.text: But the Day of the Lord will come like a thief. The heavens will disappear with a roar, the elements will be destroyed by fire, and the earth and its works will be laid bare.

61:3:11.text: Since everything will be destroyed in this way, what kind of people ought you to be? You ought to conduct yourselves in holiness and godliness

61:3:12.text: as you anticipate and hasten the coming of the day of God, when the heavens will be destroyed by fire and the elements will melt in the heat.

61:3:13.text: But in keeping with God’s promise, we are looking forward to a new heaven and a new earth, where righteousness dwells.

61:3:14.text: Therefore, beloved, as you anticipate these things, make every effort to be found at peace — spotless and blameless in His sight.

61:3:15.text: Consider also that our Lord’s patience brings salvation, just as our beloved brother Paul also wrote you with the wisdom God gave him.

61:3:16.text: He writes this way in all his letters, speaking in them about such matters. Some parts of his letters are hard to understand, which ignorant and unstable people distort, as they do the rest of the Scriptures, to their own destruction.

61:3:17.text: Therefore, beloved, since you already know these things, be on your guard so that you will not be carried away by the error of the lawless and fall from your secure standing.

61:3:18.text: But grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. To Him be the glory both now and to the day of eternity. Amen.

61:3:2.text: by recalling what was foretold by the holy prophets and commanded by our Lord and Savior through your apostles.

61:3:3.text: Most importantly, you must understand that in the last days scoffers will come, scoffing and following their own evil desires.

61:3:4.text: “Where is the promise of His coming?” they will ask. “Ever since our fathers fell asleep, everything continues as it has from the beginning of creation.”

61:3:5.text: But they deliberately overlook the fact that long ago by God’s word the heavens existed and the earth was formed out of water and by water,

61:3:6.text: through which the world of that time perished in the flood.

61:3:7.text: And by that same word, the present heavens and earth are reserved for fire, being kept for the day of judgment and destruction of ungodly men.

61:3:8.text: Beloved, do not let this one thing escape your notice: With the Lord a day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years are like a day.

61:3:9.text: The Lord is not slow in keeping His promise as some understand slowness, but is patient with you, not wanting anyone to perish but everyone to come to repentance.

62:1:1.text: That which was from the beginning, which we have heard, which we have seen with our own eyes, which we have gazed upon and touched with our own hands — this is the Word of life.

62:1:10.text: If we say we have not sinned, we make Him out to be a liar, and His word is not in us.

62:1:2.text: And this is the life that was revealed; we have seen it and testified to it, and we proclaim to you the eternal life that was with the Father and was revealed to us.

62:1:3.text: We proclaim to you what we have seen and heard, so that you also may have fellowship with us. And this fellowship of ours is with the Father and with His Son, Jesus Christ.

62:1:4.text: We write these things so that our joy may be complete.

62:1:5.text: And this is the message we have heard from Him and announce to you: God is light, and in Him there is no darkness at all.

62:1:6.text: If we say we have fellowship with Him yet walk in the darkness, we lie and do not practice the truth.

62:1:7.text: But if we walk in the light as He is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus His Son cleanses us from all sin.

62:1:8.text: If we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.

62:1:9.text: If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

62:2:1.text: My little children, I am writing these things to you so that you will not sin. But if anyone does sin, we have an advocate before the Father — Jesus Christ, the Righteous One.

62:2:10.text: Whoever loves his brother remains in the light, and there is no cause of stumbling in him.

62:2:11.text: But whoever hates his brother is in the darkness and walks in the darkness. He does not know where he is going, because the darkness has blinded his eyes.

62:2:12.text: I am writing to you, little children, because your sins have been forgiven through His name.

62:2:13.text: I am writing to you, fathers, because you know Him who is from the beginning. I am writing to you, young men, because you have overcome the evil one. I have written to you, children, because you know the Father.

62:2:14.text: I have written to you, fathers, because you know Him who is from the beginning. I have written to you, young men, because you are strong, and the word of God abides in you, and you have overcome the evil one.

62:2:15.text: Do not love the world or anything in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him.

62:2:16.text: For all that is in the world — the desires of the flesh, the desires of the eyes, and the pride of life — is not from the Father but from the world.

62:2:17.text: The world is passing away, along with its desires; but whoever does the will of God remains forever.

62:2:18.text: Children, it is the last hour; and just as you have heard that the antichrist is coming, so now many antichrists have appeared. This is how we know it is the last hour.

62:2:19.text: They went out from us, but they did not belong to us. For if they had belonged to us, they would have remained with us. But their departure made it clear that none of them belonged to us.

62:2:2.text: He Himself is the atoning sacrifice for our sins, and not only for ours but also for the sins of the whole world.

62:2:20.text: You, however, have an anointing from the Holy One, and all of you know the truth.

62:2:21.text: I have not written to you because you lack knowledge of the truth, but because you have it, and because no lie comes from the truth.

62:2:22.text: Who is the liar, if it is not the one who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This is the antichrist, who denies the Father and the Son.

62:2:23.text: Whoever denies the Son does not have the Father, but whoever confesses the Son has the Father as well.

62:2:24.text: As for you, let what you have heard from the beginning remain in you. If it does, you will also remain in the Son and in the Father.

62:2:25.text: And this is the promise that He Himself made to us: eternal life.

62:2:26.text: I have written these things to you about those who are trying to deceive you.

62:2:27.text: And as for you, the anointing you received from Him remains in you, and you do not need anyone to teach you. But just as His true and genuine anointing teaches you about all things, so remain in Him as you have been taught.

62:2:28.text: And now, little children, remain in Christ, so that when He appears, we may be confident and unashamed before Him at His coming.

62:2:29.text: If you know that He is righteous, you also know that everyone who practices righteousness has been born of Him.

62:2:3.text: By this we can be sure that we have come to know Him: if we keep His commandments.

62:2:4.text: If anyone says, “I know Him,” but does not keep His commandments, he is a liar, and the truth is not in him.

62:2:5.text: But if anyone keeps His word, the love of God has been truly perfected in him. By this we know that we are in Him:

62:2:6.text: Whoever claims to abide in Him must walk as Jesus walked.

62:2:7.text: Beloved, I am not writing to you a new commandment, but an old one, which you have had from the beginning. This commandment is the message you have heard.

62:2:8.text: Then again, I am also writing to you a new commandment, which is true in Him and also in you. For the darkness is fading and the true light is already shining.

62:2:9.text: If anyone claims to be in the light but hates his brother, he is still in the darkness.

62:3:1.text: Behold what manner of love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God. And that is what we are! The reason the world does not know us is that it did not know Him.

62:3:10.text: By this the children of God are distinguished from the children of the devil: Anyone who does not practice righteousness is not of God, nor is anyone who does not love his brother.

62:3:11.text: This is the message you have heard from the beginning: We should love one another.

62:3:12.text: Do not be like Cain, who belonged to the evil one and murdered his brother. And why did Cain slay him? Because his own deeds were evil, while those of his brother were righteous.

62:3:13.text: So do not be surprised, brothers, if the world hates you.

62:3:14.text: We know that we have passed from death to life, because we love our brothers. The one who does not love remains in death.

62:3:15.text: Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that eternal life does not reside in a murderer.

62:3:16.text: By this we know what love is: Jesus laid down His life for us, and we ought to lay down our lives for our brothers.

62:3:17.text: If anyone with earthly possessions sees his brother in need, but withholds his compassion from him, how can the love of God abide in him?

62:3:18.text: Little children, let us love not in word and speech, but in action and truth.

62:3:19.text: And by this we will know that we belong to the truth, and will assure our hearts in His presence:

62:3:2.text: Beloved, we are now children of God, and what we will be has not yet been revealed. We know that when Christ appears, we will be like Him, for we will see Him as He is.

62:3:20.text: Even if our hearts condemn us, God is greater than our hearts, and He knows all things.

62:3:21.text: Beloved, if our hearts do not condemn us, we have confidence before God,

62:3:22.text: and we will receive from Him whatever we ask, because we keep His commandments and do what is pleasing in His sight.

62:3:23.text: And this is His commandment: that we should believe in the name of His Son, Jesus Christ, and we should love one another just as He commanded us.

62:3:24.text: Whoever keeps His commandments remains in God, and God in him. And by this we know that He remains in us: by the Spirit He has given us.

62:3:3.text: And everyone who has this hope in Him purifies himself, just as Christ is pure.

62:3:4.text: Everyone who practices sin practices lawlessness as well. Indeed, sin is lawlessness.

62:3:5.text: But you know that Christ appeared to take away sins, and in Him there is no sin.

62:3:6.text: No one who remains in Him keeps on sinning. No one who continues to sin has seen Him or known Him.

62:3:7.text: Little children, let no one deceive you: The one who practices righteousness is righteous, just as Christ is righteous.

62:3:8.text: The one who practices sin is of the devil, because the devil has been sinning from the very start. This is why the Son of God was revealed, to destroy the works of the devil.

62:3:9.text: Anyone born of God refuses to practice sin, because God’s seed abides in him; he cannot go on sinning, because he has been born of God.

62:4:1.text: Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God. For many false prophets have gone out into the world.

62:4:10.text: And love consists in this: not that we loved God, but that He loved us and sent His Son as the atoning sacrifice for our sins.

62:4:11.text: Beloved, if God so loved us, we also ought to love one another.

62:4:12.text: No one has ever seen God; but if we love one another, God remains in us, and His love is perfected in us.

62:4:13.text: By this we know that we remain in Him, and He in us: He has given us of His Spirit.

62:4:14.text: And we have seen and testify that the Father has sent His Son to be the Savior of the world.

62:4:15.text: If anyone confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God abides in him, and he in God.

62:4:16.text: And we have come to know and believe the love that God has for us. God is love; whoever abides in love abides in God, and God in him.

62:4:17.text: In this way, love has been perfected among us, so that we may have confidence on the day of judgment; for in this world we are just like Him.

62:4:18.text: There is no fear in love, but perfect love drives out fear, because fear involves punishment. The one who fears has not been perfected in love.

62:4:19.text: We love because He first loved us.

62:4:2.text: By this you will know the Spirit of God: Every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God,

62:4:20.text: If anyone says, “I love God,” but hates his brother, he is a liar. For anyone who does not love his brother, whom he has seen, cannot love God, whom he has not seen.

62:4:21.text: And we have this commandment from Him: Whoever loves God must love his brother as well.

62:4:3.text: and every spirit that does not confess Jesus is not from God. This is the spirit of the antichrist, which you have heard is coming and which is already in the world at this time.

62:4:4.text: You, little children, are from God and have overcome them, because greater is He who is in you than he who is in the world.

62:4:5.text: They are of the world. That is why they speak from the world’s perspective, and the world listens to them.

62:4:6.text: We are from God. Whoever knows God listens to us; whoever is not from God does not listen to us. That is how we know the Spirit of truth and the spirit of deception.

62:4:7.text: Beloved, let us love one another, because love comes from God. Everyone who loves has been born of God and knows God.

62:4:8.text: Whoever does not love does not know God, because God is love.

62:4:9.text: This is how God’s love was revealed among us: God sent His one and only Son into the world, so that we might live through Him.

62:5:1.text: Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God, and everyone who loves the Father also loves those born of Him.

62:5:10.text: Whoever believes in the Son of God has this testimony within him; whoever does not believe God has made Him out to be a liar, because he has not believed in the testimony that God has given about His Son.

62:5:11.text: And this is that testimony: God has given us eternal life, and this life is in His Son.

62:5:12.text: Whoever has the Son has life; whoever does not have the Son of God does not have life.

62:5:13.text: I have written these things to you who believe in the name of the Son of God, so that you may know that you have eternal life.

62:5:14.text: And this is the confidence that we have before Him: If we ask anything according to His will, He hears us.

62:5:15.text: And if we know that He hears us in whatever we ask, we know that we already possess what we have asked of Him.

62:5:16.text: If anyone sees his brother committing a sin not leading to death, he should ask God, who will give life to those who commit this kind of sin. There is a sin that leads to death; I am not saying he should ask regarding that sin.

62:5:17.text: All unrighteousness is sin, yet there is sin that does not lead to death.

62:5:18.text: We know that anyone born of God does not keep on sinning; the One who was born of God protects him, and the evil one cannot touch him.

62:5:19.text: We know that we are of God, and that the whole world is under the power of the evil one.

62:5:2.text: By this we know that we love the children of God: when we love God and keep His commandments.

62:5:20.text: And we know that the Son of God has come and has given us understanding, so that we may know Him who is true; and we are in Him who is true — in His Son Jesus Christ. He is the true God and eternal life.

62:5:21.text: Little children, keep yourselves from idols.

62:5:3.text: For this is the love of God, that we keep His commandments. And His commandments are not burdensome,

62:5:4.text: because everyone born of God overcomes the world. And this is the victory that has overcome the world: our faith.

62:5:5.text: Who then overcomes the world? Only he who believes that Jesus is the Son of God.

62:5:6.text: This is the One who came by water and blood, Jesus Christ — not by water alone, but by water and blood. And it is the Spirit who testifies to this, because the Spirit is the truth.

62:5:7.text: For there are three that testify:

62:5:8.text: the Spirit, the water, and the blood — and these three are in agreement.

62:5:9.text: Even if we accept human testimony, the testimony of God is greater. For this is the testimony that God has given about His Son.

63:1:1.text: The elder, To the chosen lady and her children, whom I love in the truth — and not I alone, but also all who know the truth —

63:1:10.text: If anyone comes to you but does not bring this teaching, do not receive him into your home or even greet him.

63:1:11.text: Whoever greets such a person shares in his evil deeds.

63:1:12.text: I have many things to write to you, but I would prefer not to do so with paper and ink. Instead, I hope to come and speak with you face to face, so that our joy may be complete.

63:1:13.text: The children of your elect sister send you greetings.

63:1:2.text: because of the truth that abides in us and will be with us forever:

63:1:3.text: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and from Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father, will be with us in truth and love.

63:1:4.text: I was overjoyed to find some of your children walking in the truth, just as the Father has commanded us.

63:1:5.text: And now I urge you, dear lady — not as a new commandment to you, but one we have had from the beginning — that we love one another.

63:1:6.text: And this is love, that we walk according to His commandments. This is the very commandment you have heard from the beginning, that you must walk in love.

63:1:7.text: For many deceivers have gone out into the world, refusing to confess the coming of Jesus Christ in the flesh. Any such person is the deceiver and the antichrist.

63:1:8.text: Watch yourselves, so that you do not lose what we have worked for, but that you may be fully rewarded.

63:1:9.text: Anyone who runs ahead without remaining in the teaching of Christ does not have God. Whoever remains in His teaching has both the Father and the Son.

64:1:1.text: The elder, To the beloved Gaius, whom I love in the truth:

64:1:10.text: So if I come, I will call attention to his malicious slander against us. And unsatisfied with that, he refuses to welcome the brothers and forbids those who want to do so, even putting them out of the church.

64:1:11.text: Beloved, do not imitate what is evil, but what is good. The one who does good is of God; the one who does evil has not seen God.

64:1:12.text: Demetrius has received a good testimony from everyone, and from the truth itself. We also testify for him, and you know that our testimony is true.

64:1:13.text: I have many things to write to you, but I would prefer not to do so with pen and ink.

64:1:14.text: Instead, I hope to see you soon and speak with you face to face. Peace to you. The friends here send you greetings. Greet each of our friends there by name.

64:1:2.text: Beloved, I pray that in every way you may prosper and enjoy good health, as your soul also prospers.
