1:17:8.text: I will give to you, and to your offspring after you, the land where you are travelling, all the land of Canaan, for an everlasting possession. I will be their God.”

1:17:9.text: God said to Abraham, “As for you, you shall keep my covenant, you and your offspring after you throughout their generations.

1:18:1.text: The LORD appeared to him by the oaks of Mamre, as he sat in the tent door in the heat of the day.

1:18:10.text: He said, “I will certainly return to you at about this time next year; and behold, Sarah your wife will have a son.” Sarah heard in the tent door, which was behind him.

1:18:11.text: Now Abraham and Sarah were old, well advanced in age. Sarah had passed the age of childbearing.

1:18:12.text: Sarah laughed within herself, saying, “After I have grown old will I have pleasure, my lord being old also?”

1:18:13.text: The LORD said to Abraham, “Why did Sarah laugh, saying, ‘ Will I really bear a child when I am old?’

1:18:14.text: Is anything too hard for the LORD? At the set time I will return to you, when the season comes around, and Sarah will have a son.”

1:18:15.text: Then Sarah denied it, saying, “I didn’t laugh,” for she was afraid. He said, “No, but you did laugh.”

1:18:16.text: The men rose up from there, and looked towards Sodom. Abraham went with them to see them on their way.

1:18:17.text: The LORD said, “Will I hide from Abraham what I do,

1:18:18.text: since Abraham will surely become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations of the earth will be blessed in him?

1:18:19.text: For I have known him, to the end that he may command his children and his household after him, that they may keep the way of the LORD, to do righteousness and justice; to the end that the LORD may bring on Abraham that which he has spoken of him.”

1:18:2.text: He lifted up his eyes and looked, and saw that three men stood near him. When he saw them, he ran to meet them from the tent door, and bowed himself to the earth,

1:18:20.text: The LORD said, “Because the cry of Sodom and Gomorrah is great, and because their sin is very grievous,

1:18:21.text: I will go down now, and see whether their deeds are as bad as the reports which have come to me. If not, I will know.”

1:18:22.text: The men turned from there, and went towards Sodom, but Abraham stood yet before the LORD.

1:18:23.text: Abraham came near, and said, “Will you consume the righteous with the wicked?

1:18:24.text: What if there are fifty righteous within the city? Will you consume and not spare the place for the fifty righteous who are in it?

1:18:25.text: May it be far from you to do things like that, to kill the righteous with the wicked, so that the righteous should be like the wicked. May that be far from you. Shouldn’t the Judge of all the earth do right?”

1:18:26.text: The LORD said, “If I find in Sodom fifty righteous within the city, then I will spare the whole place for their sake.”

1:18:27.text: Abraham answered, “See now, I have taken it on myself to speak to the Lord, although I am dust and ashes.

1:18:28.text: What if there will lack five of the fifty righteous? Will you destroy all the city for lack of five?” He said, “I will not destroy it if I find forty-five there.”

1:18:29.text: He spoke to him yet again, and said, “What if there are forty found there?” He said, “I will not do it for the forty’s sake.”

1:18:3.text: and said, “My lord, if now I have found favour in your sight, please don’t go away from your servant.

1:18:30.text: He said, “Oh don’t let the Lord be angry, and I will speak. What if there are thirty found there?” He said, “I will not do it if I find thirty there.”

1:18:31.text: He said, “See now, I have taken it on myself to speak to the Lord. What if there are twenty found there?” He said, “I will not destroy it for the twenty’s sake.”

1:18:32.text: He said, “Oh don’t let the Lord be angry, and I will speak just once more. What if ten are found there?” He said, “I will not destroy it for the ten’s sake.”

1:18:33.text: The LORD went his way as soon as he had finished communing with Abraham, and Abraham returned to his place.

1:18:4.text: Now let a little water be fetched, wash your feet, and rest yourselves under the tree.

1:18:5.text: I will get a piece of bread so you can refresh your heart. After that you may go your way, now that you have come to your servant.” They said, “Very well, do as you have said.”

1:18:6.text: Abraham hurried into the tent to Sarah, and said, “Quickly prepare three seahs of fine meal, knead it, and make cakes.”

1:18:7.text: Abraham ran to the herd, and fetched a tender and good calf, and gave it to the servant. He hurried to dress it.

1:18:8.text: He took butter, milk, and the calf which he had dressed, and set it before them. He stood by them under the tree, and they ate.

1:18:9.text: They asked him, “Where is Sarah, your wife?” He said, “There, in the tent.”

1:1:1.text: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.

1:1:10.text: God called the dry land “earth”, and the gathering together of the waters he called “seas”. God saw that it was good.

1:1:11.text: God said, “Let the earth yield grass, herbs yielding seeds, and fruit trees bearing fruit after their kind, with their seeds in it, on the earth;” and it was so.

1:1:12.text: The earth yielded grass, herbs yielding seed after their kind, and trees bearing fruit, with their seeds in it, after their kind; and God saw that it was good.

1:1:13.text: There was evening and there was morning, a third day.

1:1:14.text: God said, “Let there be lights in the expanse of the sky to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs to mark seasons, days, and years;

1:1:15.text: and let them be for lights in the expanse of the sky to give light on the earth;” and it was so.

1:1:16.text: God made the two great lights: the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night. He also made the stars.

1:1:17.text: God set them in the expanse of the sky to give light to the earth,

1:1:18.text: and to rule over the day and over the night, and to divide the light from the darkness. God saw that it was good.

1:1:19.text: There was evening and there was morning, a fourth day.

1:1:2.text: The earth was formless and empty. Darkness was on the surface of the deep and God’s Spirit was hovering over the surface of the waters.

1:1:20.text: God said, “Let the waters abound with living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth in the open expanse of the sky.”

1:1:21.text: God created the large sea creatures and every living creature that moves, with which the waters swarmed, after their kind, and every winged bird after its kind. God saw that it was good.

1:1:22.text: God blessed them, saying, “Be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas, and let birds multiply on the earth.”

1:1:23.text: There was evening and there was morning, a fifth day.

1:1:24.text: God said, “Let the earth produce living creatures after their kind, livestock, creeping things, and animals of the earth after their kind;” and it was so.

1:1:25.text: God made the animals of the earth after their kind, and the livestock after their kind, and everything that creeps on the ground after its kind. God saw that it was good.

1:1:26.text: God said, “Let’s make man in our image, after our likeness. Let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the birds of the sky, and over the livestock, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creeps on the earth.”

1:1:27.text: God created man in his own image. In God’s image he created him; male and female he created them.

1:1:28.text: God blessed them. God said to them, “Be fruitful, multiply, fill the earth, and subdue it. Have dominion over the fish of the sea, over the birds of the sky, and over every living thing that moves on the earth.”

1:1:29.text: God said, “Behold, I have given you every herb yielding seed, which is on the surface of all the earth, and every tree, which bears fruit yielding seed. It will be your food.

1:1:3.text: God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light.

1:1:30.text: To every animal of the earth, and to every bird of the sky, and to everything that creeps on the earth, in which there is life, I have given every green herb for food;” and it was so.

1:1:31.text: God saw everything that he had made, and, behold, it was very good. There was evening and there was morning, a sixth day.

1:1:4.text: God saw the light, and saw that it was good. God divided the light from the darkness.

1:1:5.text: God called the light “day”, and the darkness he called “night”. There was evening and there was morning, the first day.

1:1:6.text: God said, “Let there be an expanse in the middle of the waters, and let it divide the waters from the waters.”

1:1:7.text: God made the expanse, and divided the waters which were under the expanse from the waters which were above the expanse; and it was so.

1:1:8.text: God called the expanse “sky”. There was evening and there was morning, a second day.

1:1:9.text: God said, “Let the waters under the sky be gathered together to one place, and let the dry land appear;” and it was so.

1:22:1.text: After these things, God tested Abraham, and said to him, “Abraham!” He said, “Here I am.”

1:22:10.text: Abraham stretched out his hand, and took the knife to kill his son.

1:22:11.text: The LORD’s angel called to him out of the sky, and said, “Abraham, Abraham!” He said, “Here I am.”

1:22:12.text: He said, “Don’t lay your hand on the boy or do anything to him. For now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld your son, your only son, from me.”

1:22:13.text: Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and saw that behind him was a ram caught in the thicket by his horns. Abraham went and took the ram, and offered him up for a burnt offering instead of his son.

1:22:14.text: Abraham called the name of that place “The LORD Will Provide”. As it is said to this day, “On the LORD’s mountain, it will be provided.”

1:22:15.text: The LORD’s angel called to Abraham a second time out of the sky,

1:22:16.text: and said, “‘ I have sworn by myself,’ says the LORD, ‘ because you have done this thing, and have not withheld your son, your only son,

1:22:17.text: that I will bless you greatly, and I will multiply your offspring greatly like the stars of the heavens, and like the sand which is on the seashore. Your offspring will possess the gate of his enemies.

1:22:18.text: All the nations of the earth will be blessed by your offspring, because you have obeyed my voice.’ ”

1:22:19.text: So Abraham returned to his young men, and they rose up and went together to Beersheba. Abraham lived at Beersheba.

1:22:2.text: He said, “Now take your son, your only son, Isaac, whom you love, and go into the land of Moriah. Offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains which I will tell you of.”

1:22:20.text: After these things, Abraham was told, “Behold, Milcah, she also has borne children to your brother Nahor:

1:22:21.text: Uz his firstborn, Buz his brother, Kemuel the father of Aram,

1:22:22.text: Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel.”

1:22:23.text: Bethuel became the father of Rebekah. These eight Milcah bore to Nahor, Abraham’s brother.

1:22:24.text: His concubine, whose name was Reumah, also bore Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.

1:22:3.text: Abraham rose early in the morning, and saddled his donkey; and took two of his young men with him, and Isaac his son. He split the wood for the burnt offering, and rose up, and went to the place of which God had told him.

1:22:4.text: On the third day Abraham lifted up his eyes, and saw the place far off.

1:22:5.text: Abraham said to his young men, “Stay here with the donkey. The boy and I will go over there. We will worship, and come back to you.”

1:22:6.text: Abraham took the wood of the burnt offering and laid it on Isaac his son. He took in his hand the fire and the knife. They both went together.

1:22:7.text: Isaac spoke to Abraham his father, and said, “My father?” He said, “Here I am, my son.” He said, “Here is the fire and the wood, but where is the lamb for a burnt offering?”

1:22:8.text: Abraham said, “God will provide himself the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.” So they both went together.

1:22:9.text: They came to the place which God had told him of. Abraham built the altar there, and laid the wood in order, bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar, on the wood.

1:27:1.text: When Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim, so that he could not see, he called Esau his elder son, and said to him, “My son?” He said to him, “Here I am.”

1:27:10.text: You shall bring it to your father, that he may eat, so that he may bless you before his death.”

1:27:11.text: Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, “Behold, Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man.

1:27:12.text: What if my father touches me? I will seem to him as a deceiver, and I would bring a curse on myself, and not a blessing.”

1:27:13.text: His mother said to him, “Let your curse be on me, my son. Only obey my voice, and go get them for me.”

1:27:14.text: He went, and got them, and brought them to his mother. His mother made savoury food, such as his father loved.

1:27:15.text: Rebekah took the good clothes of Esau, her elder son, which were with her in the house, and put them on Jacob, her younger son.

1:27:16.text: She put the skins of the young goats on his hands, and on the smooth of his neck.

1:27:17.text: She gave the savoury food and the bread, which she had prepared, into the hand of her son Jacob.

1:27:18.text: He came to his father, and said, “My father?” He said, “Here I am. Who are you, my son?”

1:27:19.text: Jacob said to his father, “I am Esau your firstborn. I have done what you asked me to do. Please arise, sit and eat of my venison, that your soul may bless me.”

1:27:2.text: He said, “See now, I am old. I don’t know the day of my death.

1:27:20.text: Isaac said to his son, “How is it that you have found it so quickly, my son?” He said, “Because the LORD your God gave me success.”

1:27:21.text: Isaac said to Jacob, “Please come near, that I may feel you, my son, whether you are really my son Esau or not.”

1:27:22.text: Jacob went near to Isaac his father. He felt him, and said, “The voice is Jacob’s voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.”

1:27:23.text: He didn’t recognise him, because his hands were hairy, like his brother Esau’s hands. So he blessed him.

1:27:24.text: He said, “Are you really my son Esau?” He said, “I am.”

1:27:25.text: He said, “Bring it near to me, and I will eat of my son’s venison, that my soul may bless you.” He brought it near to him, and he ate. He brought him wine, and he drank.

1:27:26.text: His father Isaac said to him, “Come near now, and kiss me, my son.”

1:27:27.text: He came near, and kissed him. He smelled the smell of his clothing, and blessed him, and said, “Behold, the smell of my son is as the smell of a field which the LORD has blessed.

1:27:28.text: God give you of the dew of the sky, of the fatness of the earth, and plenty of grain and new wine.

1:27:29.text: Let peoples serve you, and nations bow down to you. Be lord over your brothers. Let your mother’s sons bow down to you. Cursed be everyone who curses you. Blessed be everyone who blesses you.”

1:27:3.text: Now therefore, please take your weapons, your quiver and your bow, and go out to the field, and get me venison.

1:27:30.text: As soon as Isaac had finished blessing Jacob, and Jacob had just gone out from the presence of Isaac his father, Esau his brother came in from his hunting.

1:27:31.text: He also made savoury food, and brought it to his father. He said to his father, “Let my father arise, and eat of his son’s venison, that your soul may bless me.”

1:27:32.text: Isaac his father said to him, “Who are you?” He said, “I am your son, your firstborn, Esau.”

1:27:33.text: Isaac trembled violently, and said, “Who, then, is he who has taken venison, and brought it to me, and I have eaten of all before you came, and have blessed him? Yes, he will be blessed.”

1:27:34.text: When Esau heard the words of his father, he cried with an exceedingly great and bitter cry, and said to his father, “Bless me, even me also, my father.”

1:27:35.text: He said, “Your brother came with deceit, and has taken away your blessing.”

1:27:36.text: He said, “Isn’t he rightly named Jacob? For he has supplanted me these two times. He took away my birthright. See, now he has taken away my blessing.” He said, “Haven’t you reserved a blessing for me?”

1:27:37.text: Isaac answered Esau, “Behold, I have made him your lord, and all his brothers I have given to him for servants. I have sustained him with grain and new wine. What then will I do for you, my son?”

1:27:38.text: Esau said to his father, “Do you have just one blessing, my father? Bless me, even me also, my father.” Esau lifted up his voice, and wept.

1:27:39.text: Isaac his father answered him, “Behold, your dwelling will be of the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of the sky from above.

1:27:4.text: Make me savoury food, such as I love, and bring it to me, that I may eat, and that my soul may bless you before I die.”

1:27:40.text: You will live by your sword, and you will serve your brother. It will happen, when you will break loose, that you will shake his yoke from off your neck.”

1:27:41.text: Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing with which his father blessed him. Esau said in his heart, “The days of mourning for my father are at hand. Then I will kill my brother Jacob.”

1:27:42.text: The words of Esau, her elder son, were told to Rebekah. She sent and called Jacob, her younger son, and said to him, “Behold, your brother Esau comforts himself about you by planning to kill you.

1:27:43.text: Now therefore, my son, obey my voice. Arise, flee to Laban, my brother, in Haran.

1:27:44.text: Stay with him a few days, until your brother’s fury turns away —

1:27:45.text: until your brother’s anger turns away from you, and he forgets what you have done to him. Then I will send, and get you from there. Why should I be bereaved of you both in one day?”

1:27:46.text: Rebekah said to Isaac, “I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Heth. If Jacob takes a wife of the daughters of Heth, such as these, of the daughters of the land, what good will my life do me?”

1:27:5.text: Rebekah heard when Isaac spoke to Esau his son. Esau went to the field to hunt for venison, and to bring it.

1:27:6.text: Rebekah spoke to Jacob her son, saying, “Behold, I heard your father speak to Esau your brother, saying,

1:27:7.text: ‘ Bring me venison, and make me savoury food, that I may eat, and bless you before the LORD before my death.’

1:27:8.text: Now therefore, my son, obey my voice according to that which I command you.

1:27:9.text: Go now to the flock and get me two good young goats from there. I will make them savoury food for your father, such as he loves.

1:2:1.text: The heavens, the earth, and all their vast array were finished.

1:2:10.text: A river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from there it was parted, and became the source of four rivers.

1:2:11.text: The name of the first is Pishon: it flows through the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold;

1:2:12.text: and the gold of that land is good. Bdellium and onyx stone are also there.

1:2:13.text: The name of the second river is Gihon. It is the same river that flows through the whole land of Cush.

1:2:14.text: The name of the third river is Hiddekel. This is the one which flows in front of Assyria. The fourth river is the Euphrates.

1:2:15.text: The LORD God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it.

1:2:16.text: The LORD God commanded the man, saying, “You may freely eat of every tree of the garden;

1:2:17.text: but you shall not eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil; for in the day that you eat of it, you will surely die.”

1:2:18.text: The LORD God said, “It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make him a helper comparable to him.”

1:2:19.text: Out of the ground the LORD God formed every animal of the field, and every bird of the sky, and brought them to the man to see what he would call them. Whatever the man called every living creature became its name.

1:2:2.text: On the seventh day God finished his work which he had done; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had done.

1:2:20.text: The man gave names to all livestock, and to the birds of the sky, and to every animal of the field; but for man there was not found a helper comparable to him.

1:2:21.text: The LORD God caused the man to fall into a deep sleep. As the man slept, he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh in its place.

1:2:22.text: The LORD God made a woman from the rib which he had taken from the man, and brought her to the man.

1:2:23.text: The man said, “This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh. She will be called ‘woman,’ because she was taken out of Man.”

1:2:24.text: Therefore a man will leave his father and his mother, and will join with his wife, and they will be one flesh.

1:2:25.text: The man and his wife were both naked, and they were not ashamed.

1:2:3.text: God blessed the seventh day, and made it holy, because he rested in it from all his work of creation which he had done.

1:2:4.text: This is the history of the generations of the heavens and of the earth when they were created, in the day that the LORD God made the earth and the heavens.

1:2:5.text: No plant of the field was yet in the earth, and no herb of the field had yet sprung up; for the LORD God had not caused it to rain on the earth. There was not a man to till the ground,

1:2:6.text: but a mist went up from the earth, and watered the whole surface of the ground.

1:2:7.text: The LORD God formed man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.

1:2:8.text: The LORD God planted a garden eastward, in Eden, and there he put the man whom he had formed.

1:2:9.text: Out of the ground the LORD God made every tree to grow that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food, including the tree of life in the middle of the garden and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.

1:31:1.text: Jacob heard Laban’s sons’ words, saying, “Jacob has taken away all that was our father’s. He has obtained all this wealth from that which was our father’s.”

1:31:10.text: During mating season, I lifted up my eyes, and saw in a dream, and behold, the male goats which leapt on the flock were streaked, speckled, and grizzled.

1:31:11.text: The angel of God said to me in the dream, ‘ Jacob,’ and I said, ‘ Here I am.’

1:31:12.text: He said, ‘ Now lift up your eyes, and behold, all the male goats which leap on the flock are streaked, speckled, and grizzled, for I have seen all that Laban does to you.

1:31:13.text: I am the God of Bethel, where you anointed a pillar, where you vowed a vow to me. Now arise, get out from this land, and return to the land of your birth.’ ”

1:31:14.text: Rachel and Leah answered him, “Is there yet any portion or inheritance for us in our father’s house?

1:31:15.text: Aren’t we considered as foreigners by him? For he has sold us, and has also used up our money.

1:31:16.text: For all the riches which God has taken away from our father are ours and our children’s. Now then, whatever God has said to you, do.”

1:31:17.text: Then Jacob rose up, and set his sons and his wives on the camels,

1:31:18.text: and he took away all his livestock, and all his possessions which he had gathered, including the livestock which he had gained in Paddan Aram, to go to Isaac his father, to the land of Canaan.

1:31:19.text: Now Laban had gone to shear his sheep; and Rachel stole the teraphim that were her father’s.

1:31:2.text: Jacob saw the expression on Laban’s face, and, behold, it was not towards him as before.

1:31:20.text: Jacob deceived Laban the Syrian, in that he didn’t tell him that he was running away.

1:31:21.text: So he fled with all that he had. He rose up, passed over the River, and set his face towards the mountain of Gilead.

1:31:22.text: Laban was told on the third day that Jacob had fled.

1:31:23.text: He took his relatives with him, and pursued him seven days’ journey. He overtook him in the mountain of Gilead.

1:31:24.text: God came to Laban the Syrian in a dream of the night, and said to him, “Be careful that you don’t speak to Jacob either good or bad.”

1:31:25.text: Laban caught up with Jacob. Now Jacob had pitched his tent in the mountain, and Laban with his relatives encamped in the mountain of Gilead.

1:31:26.text: Laban said to Jacob, “What have you done, that you have deceived me, and carried away my daughters like captives of the sword?

1:31:27.text: Why did you flee secretly, and deceive me, and didn’t tell me, that I might have sent you away with mirth and with songs, with tambourine and with harp;

1:31:28.text: and didn’t allow me to kiss my sons and my daughters? Now you have done foolishly.

1:31:29.text: It is in the power of my hand to hurt you, but the God of your father spoke to me last night, saying, ‘ Be careful that you don’t speak to Jacob either good or bad.’

1:31:3.text: The LORD said to Jacob, “Return to the land of your fathers, and to your relatives, and I will be with you.”

1:31:30.text: Now, you want to be gone, because you greatly longed for your father’s house, but why have you stolen my gods?”

1:31:31.text: Jacob answered Laban, “Because I was afraid, for I said, ‘ Lest you should take your daughters from me by force.’

1:31:32.text: Anyone you find your gods with shall not live. Before our relatives, discern what is yours with me, and take it.” For Jacob didn’t know that Rachel had stolen them.

1:31:33.text: Laban went into Jacob’s tent, into Leah’s tent, and into the tent of the two female servants; but he didn’t find them. He went out of Leah’s tent, and entered into Rachel’s tent.

1:31:34.text: Now Rachel had taken the teraphim, put them in the camel’s saddle, and sat on them. Laban felt around all the tent, but didn’t find them.

1:31:35.text: She said to her father, “Don’t let my lord be angry that I can’t rise up before you; for I’m having my period.” He searched, but didn’t find the teraphim.

1:31:36.text: Jacob was angry, and argued with Laban. Jacob answered Laban, “What is my trespass? What is my sin, that you have hotly pursued me?

1:31:37.text: Now that you have felt around in all my stuff, what have you found of all your household stuff? Set it here before my relatives and your relatives, that they may judge between us two.

1:31:38.text: “These twenty years I have been with you. Your ewes and your female goats have not cast their young, and I haven’t eaten the rams of your flocks.

1:31:39.text: That which was torn of animals, I didn’t bring to you. I bore its loss. Of my hand you required it, whether stolen by day or stolen by night.

1:31:4.text: Jacob sent and called Rachel and Leah to the field to his flock,

1:31:40.text: This was my situation: in the day the drought consumed me, and the frost by night; and my sleep fled from my eyes.

1:31:41.text: These twenty years I have been in your house. I served you fourteen years for your two daughters, and six years for your flock, and you have changed my wages ten times.

1:31:42.text: Unless the God of my father, the God of Abraham, and the fear of Isaac, had been with me, surely now you would have sent me away empty. God has seen my affliction and the labour of my hands, and rebuked you last night.”

1:31:43.text: Laban answered Jacob, “The daughters are my daughters, the children are my children, the flocks are my flocks, and all that you see is mine! What can I do today to these my daughters, or to their children whom they have borne?

1:31:44.text: Now come, let’s make a covenant, you and I. Let it be for a witness between me and you.”

1:31:45.text: Jacob took a stone, and set it up for a pillar.

1:31:46.text: Jacob said to his relatives, “Gather stones.” They took stones, and made a heap. They ate there by the heap.

1:31:47.text: Laban called it Jegar Sahadutha, but Jacob called it Galeed.

1:31:48.text: Laban said, “This heap is witness between me and you today.” Therefore it was named Galeed

1:31:49.text: and Mizpah, for he said, “The LORD watch between me and you, when we are absent one from another.

1:31:5.text: and said to them, “I see the expression on your father’s face, that it is not towards me as before; but the God of my father has been with me.

1:31:50.text: If you afflict my daughters, or if you take wives in addition to my daughters, no man is with us; behold, God is witness between me and you.”

1:31:51.text: Laban said to Jacob, “See this heap, and see the pillar, which I have set between me and you.

1:31:52.text: May this heap be a witness, and the pillar be a witness, that I will not pass over this heap to you, and that you will not pass over this heap and this pillar to me, for harm.

1:31:53.text: The God of Abraham, and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge between us.” Then Jacob swore by the fear of his father, Isaac.

1:31:54.text: Jacob offered a sacrifice in the mountain, and called his relatives to eat bread. They ate bread, and stayed all night in the mountain.

1:31:55.text: Early in the morning, Laban rose up, and kissed his sons and his daughters, and blessed them. Laban departed and returned to his place.

1:31:6.text: You know that I have served your father with all of my strength.

1:31:7.text: Your father has deceived me, and changed my wages ten times, but God didn’t allow him to hurt me.

1:31:8.text: If he said, ‘ The speckled will be your wages,’ then all the flock bore speckled. If he said, ‘ The streaked will be your wages,’ then all the flock bore streaked.

1:31:9.text: Thus God has taken away your father’s livestock, and given them to me.

1:3:1.text: Now the serpent was more subtle than any animal of the field which the LORD God had made. He said to the woman, “Has God really said, ‘ You shall not eat of any tree of the garden’ ?”

1:3:10.text: The man said, “I heard your voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; so I hid myself.”

1:3:11.text: God said, “Who told you that you were naked? Have you eaten from the tree that I commanded you not to eat from?”

1:3:12.text: The man said, “The woman whom you gave to be with me, she gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate it.”

1:3:13.text: The LORD God said to the woman, “What have you done?” The woman said, “The serpent deceived me, and I ate.”

1:3:14.text: The LORD God said to the serpent, “Because you have done this, you are cursed above all livestock, and above every animal of the field. You shall go on your belly and you shall eat dust all the days of your life.

1:3:15.text: I will put hostility between you and the woman, and between your offspring and her offspring. He will bruise your head, and you will bruise his heel.”

1:3:16.text: To the woman he said, “I will greatly multiply your pain in childbirth. You will bear children in pain. Your desire will be for your husband, and he will rule over you.”

1:3:17.text: To Adam he said, “Because you have listened to your wife’s voice, and have eaten from the tree, about which I commanded you, saying, ‘ You shall not eat of it,’the ground is cursed for your sake. You will eat from it with much labour all the days of your life.

1:3:18.text: It will yield thorns and thistles to you; and you will eat the herb of the field.

1:3:19.text: You will eat bread by the sweat of your face until you return to the ground, for you were taken out of it. For you are dust, and you shall return to dust.”

1:3:2.text: The woman said to the serpent, “We may eat fruit from the trees of the garden,

1:3:20.text: The man called his wife Eve because she would be the mother of all the living.

1:3:21.text: The LORD God made garments of animal skins for Adam and for his wife, and clothed them.

1:3:22.text: The LORD God said, “Behold, the man has become like one of us, knowing good and evil. Now, lest he reach out his hand, and also take of the tree of life, and eat, and live forever — ”

1:3:23.text: Therefore the LORD God sent him out from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from which he was taken.

1:3:24.text: So he drove out the man; and he placed cherubim at the east of the garden of Eden, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to guard the way to the tree of life.

1:3:3.text: but not the fruit of the tree which is in the middle of the garden. God has said, ‘ You shall not eat of it. You shall not touch it, lest you die.’ ”

1:3:4.text: The serpent said to the woman, “You won’t really die,

1:3:5.text: for God knows that in the day you eat it, your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God, knowing good and evil.”

1:3:6.text: When the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was a delight to the eyes, and that the tree was to be desired to make one wise, she took some of its fruit, and ate. Then she gave some to her husband with her, and he ate it, too.

1:3:7.text: Their eyes were opened, and they both knew that they were naked. They sewed fig leaves together, and made coverings for themselves.

1:3:8.text: They heard the LORD God’s voice walking in the garden in the cool of the day, and the man and his wife hid themselves from the presence of the LORD God amongst the trees of the garden.

1:3:9.text: The LORD God called to the man, and said to him, “Where are you?”

1:43:1.text: The famine was severe in the land.

1:43:10.text: for if we hadn’t delayed, surely we would have returned a second time by now.”

1:43:11.text: Their father, Israel, said to them, “If it must be so, then do this: Take from the choice fruits of the land in your bags, and carry down a present for the man, a little balm, a little honey, spices and myrrh, nuts, and almonds;

1:43:12.text: and take double money in your hand, and take back the money that was returned in the mouth of your sacks. Perhaps it was an oversight.

1:43:13.text: Take your brother also, get up, and return to the man.

1:43:14.text: May God Almighty give you mercy before the man, that he may release to you your other brother and Benjamin. If I am bereaved of my children, I am bereaved.”

1:43:15.text: The men took that present, and they took double money in their hand, and Benjamin; and got up, went down to Egypt, and stood before Joseph.

1:43:16.text: When Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he said to the steward of his house, “Bring the men into the house, and butcher an animal, and prepare; for the men will dine with me at noon.”

1:43:17.text: The man did as Joseph commanded, and the man brought the men to Joseph’s house.

1:43:18.text: The men were afraid, because they were brought to Joseph’s house; and they said, “Because of the money that was returned in our sacks the first time, we’re brought in; that he may seek occasion against us, attack us, and seize us as slaves, along with our donkeys.”

1:43:19.text: They came near to the steward of Joseph’s house, and they spoke to him at the door of the house,

1:43:2.text: When they had eaten up the grain which they had brought out of Egypt, their father said to them, “Go again, buy us a little more food.”

1:43:20.text: and said, “Oh, my lord, we indeed came down the first time to buy food.

1:43:21.text: When we came to the lodging place, we opened our sacks, and behold, each man’s money was in the mouth of his sack, our money in full weight. We have brought it back in our hand.

1:43:22.text: We have brought down other money in our hand to buy food. We don’t know who put our money in our sacks.”

1:43:23.text: He said, “Peace be to you. Don’t be afraid. Your God, and the God of your father, has given you treasure in your sacks. I received your money.” He brought Simeon out to them.

1:43:24.text: The man brought the men into Joseph’s house, and gave them water, and they washed their feet. He gave their donkeys fodder.

1:43:25.text: They prepared the present for Joseph’s coming at noon, for they heard that they should eat bread there.

1:43:26.text: When Joseph came home, they brought him the present which was in their hand into the house, and bowed themselves down to the earth before him.

1:43:27.text: He asked them of their welfare, and said, “Is your father well, the old man of whom you spoke? Is he yet alive?”

1:43:28.text: They said, “Your servant, our father, is well. He is still alive.” They bowed down humbly.

1:43:29.text: He lifted up his eyes, and saw Benjamin, his brother, his mother’s son, and said, “Is this your youngest brother, of whom you spoke to me?” He said, “God be gracious to you, my son.”

1:43:3.text: Judah spoke to him, saying, “The man solemnly warned us, saying, ‘ You shall not see my face, unless your brother is with you.’

1:43:30.text: Joseph hurried, for his heart yearned over his brother; and he sought a place to weep. He entered into his room, and wept there.

1:43:31.text: He washed his face, and came out. He controlled himself, and said, “Serve the meal.”

1:43:32.text: They served him by himself, and them by themselves, and the Egyptians who ate with him by themselves, because the Egyptians don’t eat with the Hebrews, for that is an abomination to the Egyptians.

1:43:33.text: They sat before him, the firstborn according to his birthright, and the youngest according to his youth, and the men marvelled with one another.

1:43:34.text: He sent portions to them from before him, but Benjamin’s portion was five times as much as any of theirs. They drank, and were merry with him.

1:43:4.text: If you’ll send our brother with us, we’ll go down and buy you food;

1:43:5.text: but if you don’t send him, we won’t go down, for the man said to us, ‘ You shall not see my face, unless your brother is with you.’ ”

1:43:6.text: Israel said, “Why did you treat me so badly, telling the man that you had another brother?”

1:43:7.text: They said, “The man asked directly concerning ourselves, and concerning our relatives, saying, ‘ Is your father still alive? Have you another brother?’ We just answered his questions. Is there any way we could know that he would say, ‘ Bring your brother down’ ?”

1:43:8.text: Judah said to Israel, his father, “Send the boy with me, and we’ll get up and go, so that we may live, and not die, both we, and you, and also our little ones.

1:43:9.text: I’ll be collateral for him. From my hand will you require him. If I don’t bring him to you, and set him before you, then let me bear the blame forever;

1:45:1.text: Then Joseph couldn’t control himself before all those who stood before him, and he called out, “Cause everyone to go out from me!” No one else stood with him, while Joseph made himself known to his brothers.

1:45:10.text: You shall dwell in the land of Goshen, and you will be near to me, you, your children, your children’s children, your flocks, your herds, and all that you have.

1:45:11.text: There I will provide for you; for there are yet five years of famine; lest you come to poverty, you, and your household, and all that you have.”’

1:45:12.text: Behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my mouth that speaks to you.

1:45:13.text: You shall tell my father of all my glory in Egypt, and of all that you have seen. You shall hurry and bring my father down here.”

1:45:14.text: He fell on his brother Benjamin’s neck and wept, and Benjamin wept on his neck.

1:45:15.text: He kissed all his brothers, and wept on them. After that his brothers talked with him.

1:45:16.text: The report of it was heard in Pharaoh’s house, saying, “Joseph’s brothers have come.” It pleased Pharaoh well, and his servants.

1:45:17.text: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Tell your brothers, ‘ Do this: Load your animals, and go, travel to the land of Canaan.

1:45:18.text: Take your father and your households, and come to me, and I will give you the good of the land of Egypt, and you will eat the fat of the land.’

1:45:19.text: Now you are commanded to do this: Take wagons out of the land of Egypt for your little ones, and for your wives, and bring your father, and come.

1:45:2.text: He wept aloud. The Egyptians heard, and the house of Pharaoh heard.

1:45:20.text: Also, don’t concern yourselves about your belongings, for the good of all the land of Egypt is yours.”

1:45:21.text: The sons of Israel did so. Joseph gave them wagons, according to the commandment of Pharaoh, and gave them provision for the way.

1:45:22.text: He gave each one of them changes of clothing, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of clothing.

1:45:23.text: He sent the following to his father: ten donkeys loaded with the good things of Egypt, and ten female donkeys loaded with grain and bread and provision for his father by the way.

1:45:24.text: So he sent his brothers away, and they departed. He said to them, “See that you don’t quarrel on the way.”

1:45:25.text: They went up out of Egypt, and came into the land of Canaan, to Jacob their father.

1:45:26.text: They told him, saying, “Joseph is still alive, and he is ruler over all the land of Egypt.” His heart fainted, for he didn’t believe them.

1:45:27.text: They told him all the words of Joseph, which he had said to them. When he saw the wagons which Joseph had sent to carry him, the spirit of Jacob, their father, revived.

1:45:28.text: Israel said, “It is enough. Joseph my son is still alive. I will go and see him before I die.”

1:45:3.text: Joseph said to his brothers, “I am Joseph! Does my father still live?” His brothers couldn’t answer him; for they were terrified at his presence.

1:45:4.text: Joseph said to his brothers, “Come near to me, please.” They came near. He said, “I am Joseph, your brother, whom you sold into Egypt.

1:45:5.text: Now don’t be grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that you sold me here, for God sent me before you to preserve life.

1:45:6.text: For these two years the famine has been in the land, and there are yet five years, in which there will be no ploughing and no harvest.

1:45:7.text: God sent me before you to preserve for you a remnant in the earth, and to save you alive by a great deliverance.

1:45:8.text: So now it wasn’t you who sent me here, but God, and he has made me a father to Pharaoh, lord of all his house, and ruler over all the land of Egypt.

1:45:9.text: Hurry, and go up to my father, and tell him, ‘ This is what your son Joseph says, “God has made me lord of all Egypt. Come down to me. Don’t wait.

1:46:1.text: Israel travelled with all that he had, and came to Beersheba, and offered sacrifices to the God of his father, Isaac.

1:46:10.text: The sons of Simeon: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanite woman.

1:46:11.text: The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.

1:46:12.text: The sons of Judah: Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, and Zerah; but Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan. The sons of Perez were Hezron and Hamul.

1:46:13.text: The sons of Issachar: Tola, Puvah, Iob, and Shimron.

1:46:14.text: The sons of Zebulun: Sered, Elon, and Jahleel.

1:46:15.text: These are the sons of Leah, whom she bore to Jacob in Paddan Aram, with his daughter Dinah. All the souls of his sons and his daughters were thirty-three.

1:46:16.text: The sons of Gad: Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi, and Areli.

1:46:17.text: The sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, Beriah, and Serah their sister. The sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel.

1:46:18.text: These are the sons of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to Leah, his daughter, and these she bore to Jacob, even sixteen souls.

1:46:19.text: The sons of Rachel, Jacob’s wife: Joseph and Benjamin.

1:46:2.text: God spoke to Israel in the visions of the night, and said, “Jacob, Jacob!” He said, “Here I am.”

1:46:20.text: To Joseph in the land of Egypt were born Manasseh and Ephraim, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, bore to him.

1:46:21.text: The sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim, and Ard.

1:46:22.text: These are the sons of Rachel, who were born to Jacob: all the souls were fourteen.

1:46:24.text: The sons of Naphtali: Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.

1:46:25.text: These are the sons of Bilhah, whom Laban gave to Rachel, his daughter, and these she bore to Jacob: all the souls were seven.

1:46:26.text: All the souls who came with Jacob into Egypt, who were his direct offspring, in addition to Jacob’s sons’ wives, all the souls were sixty-six.

1:46:27.text: The sons of Joseph, who were born to him in Egypt, were two souls. All the souls of the house of Jacob, who came into Egypt, were seventy.

1:46:28.text: Jacob sent Judah before him to Joseph, to show the way before him to Goshen, and they came into the land of Goshen.

1:46:29.text: Joseph prepared his chariot, and went up to meet Israel, his father, in Goshen. He presented himself to him, and fell on his neck, and wept on his neck a good while.

1:46:3.text: He said, “I am God, the God of your father. Don’t be afraid to go down into Egypt, for there I will make of you a great nation.

1:46:30.text: Israel said to Joseph, “Now let me die, since I have seen your face, that you are still alive.”

1:46:31.text: Joseph said to his brothers, and to his father’s house, “I will go up, and speak with Pharaoh, and will tell him, ‘ My brothers, and my father’s house, who were in the land of Canaan, have come to me.

1:46:32.text: These men are shepherds, for they have been keepers of livestock, and they have brought their flocks, and their herds, and all that they have.’

1:46:33.text: It will happen, when Pharaoh summons you, and will say, ‘ What is your occupation?’

1:46:34.text: that you shall say, ‘ Your servants have been keepers of livestock from our youth even until now, both we, and our fathers:’ that you may dwell in the land of Goshen; for every shepherd is an abomination to the Egyptians.”

1:46:4.text: I will go down with you into Egypt. I will also surely bring you up again. Joseph’s hand will close your eyes.”

1:46:5.text: Jacob rose up from Beersheba, and the sons of Israel carried Jacob, their father, their little ones, and their wives, in the wagons which Pharaoh had sent to carry him.

1:46:6.text: They took their livestock, and their goods, which they had gotten in the land of Canaan, and came into Egypt — Jacob, and all his offspring with him,

1:46:7.text: his sons, and his sons’ sons with him, his daughters, and his sons’ daughters, and he brought all his offspring with him into Egypt.

1:46:8.text: These are the names of the children of Israel, who came into Egypt, Jacob and his sons: Reuben, Jacob’s firstborn.

1:46:9.text: The sons of Reuben: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.

1:49:11.text: Binding his foal to the vine, his donkey’s colt to the choice vine, he has washed his garments in wine, his robes in the blood of grapes.

1:49:12.text: His eyes will be red with wine, his teeth white with milk.

1:49:13.text: “Zebulun will dwell at the haven of the sea. He will be for a haven of ships. His border will be on Sidon.

1:49:14.text: “Issachar is a strong donkey, lying down between the saddlebags.

1:49:15.text: He saw a resting place, that it was good, the land, that it was pleasant. He bows his shoulder to the burden, and becomes a servant doing forced labour.

1:49:16.text: “Dan will judge his people, as one of the tribes of Israel.

1:49:17.text: Dan will be a serpent on the trail, an adder in the path, that bites the horse’s heels, so that his rider falls backward.

1:49:18.text: I have waited for your salvation, LORD.

1:49:19.text: “A troop will press on Gad, but he will press on their heel.

1:49:2.text: Assemble yourselves, and hear, you sons of Jacob. Listen to Israel, your father.

1:49:20.text: “Asher’s food will be rich. He will produce royal dainties.

1:49:21.text: “Naphtali is a doe set free, who bears beautiful fawns.

1:49:22.text: “Joseph is a fruitful vine, a fruitful vine by a spring. His branches run over the wall.

1:49:23.text: The archers have severely grieved him, shot at him, and persecuted him:

1:49:24.text: But his bow remained strong. The arms of his hands were made strong, by the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob, (from there is the shepherd, the stone of Israel),

1:49:25.text: even by the God of your father, who will help you, by the Almighty, who will bless you, with blessings of heaven above, blessings of the deep that lies below, blessings of the breasts, and of the womb.

1:49:26.text: The blessings of your father have prevailed above the blessings of my ancestors, above the boundaries of the ancient hills. They will be on the head of Joseph, on the crown of the head of him who is separated from his brothers.

1:49:27.text: “Benjamin is a ravenous wolf. In the morning he will devour the prey. At evening he will divide the plunder.”

1:49:28.text: All these are the twelve tribes of Israel, and this is what their father spoke to them, and blessed them. He blessed everyone according to his own blessing.

1:49:29.text: He instructed them, and said to them, “I am to be gathered to my people. Bury me with my fathers in the cave that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite,

1:49:3.text: “Reuben, you are my firstborn, my might, and the beginning of my strength, excelling in dignity, and excelling in power.

1:49:30.text: in the cave that is in the field of Machpelah, which is before Mamre, in the land of Canaan, which Abraham bought with the field from Ephron the Hittite as a burial place.

1:49:31.text: There they buried Abraham and Sarah, his wife. There they buried Isaac and Rebekah, his wife, and there I buried Leah:

1:49:32.text: the field and the cave that is therein, which was purchased from the children of Heth.”

1:49:33.text: When Jacob finished charging his sons, he gathered up his feet into the bed, breathed his last breath, and was gathered to his people.

1:49:4.text: Boiling over like water, you shall not excel, because you went up to your father’s bed, then defiled it. He went up to my couch.

1:49:5.text: “Simeon and Levi are brothers. Their swords are weapons of violence.

1:49:6.text: My soul, don’t come into their council. My glory, don’t be united to their assembly; for in their anger they killed men. In their self-will they hamstrung cattle.

1:49:7.text: Cursed be their anger, for it was fierce; and their wrath, for it was cruel. I will divide them in Jacob, and scatter them in Israel.

1:49:8.text: “Judah, your brothers will praise you. Your hand will be on the neck of your enemies. Your father’s sons will bow down before you.

1:49:9.text: Judah is a lion’s cub. From the prey, my son, you have gone up. He stooped down, he crouched as a lion, as a lioness. Who will rouse him up?

1:4:1.text: The man knew Eve his wife. She conceived, and gave birth to Cain, and said, “I have gotten a man with the LORD’s help.”

1:4:10.text: The LORD said, “What have you done? The voice of your brother’s blood cries to me from the ground.

1:4:11.text: Now you are cursed because of the ground, which has opened its mouth to receive your brother’s blood from your hand.

1:4:12.text: From now on, when you till the ground, it won’t yield its strength to you. You will be a fugitive and a wanderer in the earth.”

1:4:13.text: Cain said to the LORD, “My punishment is greater than I can bear.

1:4:14.text: Behold, you have driven me out today from the surface of the ground. I will be hidden from your face, and I will be a fugitive and a wanderer in the earth. Whoever finds me will kill me.”

1:4:15.text: The LORD said to him, “Therefore whoever slays Cain, vengeance will be taken on him sevenfold.” The LORD appointed a sign for Cain, so that anyone finding him would not strike him.

1:4:16.text: Cain left the LORD’s presence, and lived in the land of Nod, east of Eden.

1:4:17.text: Cain knew his wife. She conceived, and gave birth to Enoch. He built a city, and named the city after the name of his son, Enoch.

1:4:18.text: Irad was born to Enoch. Irad became the father of Mehujael. Mehujael became the father of Methushael. Methushael became the father of Lamech.

1:4:19.text: Lamech took two wives: the name of the first one was Adah, and the name of the second one was Zillah.

1:4:2.text: Again she gave birth, to Cain’s brother Abel. Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.

1:4:20.text: Adah gave birth to Jabal, who was the father of those who dwell in tents and have livestock.

1:4:21.text: His brother’s name was Jubal, who was the father of all who handle the harp and pipe.

1:4:22.text: Zillah also gave birth to Tubal Cain, the forger of every cutting instrument of bronze and iron. Tubal Cain’s sister was Naamah.

1:4:23.text: Lamech said to his wives, “Adah and Zillah, hear my voice. You wives of Lamech, listen to my speech, for I have slain a man for wounding me, a young man for bruising me.

1:4:24.text: If Cain will be avenged seven times, truly Lamech seventy-seven times.”

1:4:25.text: Adam knew his wife again. She gave birth to a son, and named him Seth, saying, “for God has given me another child instead of Abel, for Cain killed him.”

1:4:26.text: A son was also born to Seth, and he named him Enosh. At that time men began to call on the LORD’s name.

1:4:3.text: As time passed, Cain brought an offering to the LORD from the fruit of the ground.

1:4:4.text: Abel also brought some of the firstborn of his flock and of its fat. The LORD respected Abel and his offering,

1:4:5.text: but he didn’t respect Cain and his offering. Cain was very angry, and the expression on his face fell.

1:4:6.text: The LORD said to Cain, “Why are you angry? Why has the expression of your face fallen?

1:4:7.text: If you do well, won’t it be lifted up? If you don’t do well, sin crouches at the door. Its desire is for you, but you are to rule over it.”

1:4:8.text: Cain said to Abel, his brother, “Let’s go into the field.” While they were in the field, Cain rose up against Abel, his brother, and killed him.

1:4:9.text: The LORD said to Cain, “Where is Abel, your brother?” He said, “I don’t know. Am I my brother’s keeper?”

1:50:1.text: Joseph fell on his father’s face, wept on him, and kissed him.

1:50:10.text: They came to the threshing floor of Atad, which is beyond the Jordan, and there they lamented with a very great and severe lamentation. He mourned for his father seven days.

1:50:11.text: When the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, saw the mourning in the floor of Atad, they said, “This is a grievous mourning by the Egyptians.” Therefore its name was called Abel Mizraim, which is beyond the Jordan.

1:50:12.text: His sons did to him just as he commanded them,

1:50:13.text: for his sons carried him into the land of Canaan, and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, which Abraham bought with the field, as a possession for a burial site, from Ephron the Hittite, near Mamre.

1:50:14.text: Joseph returned into Egypt — he, and his brothers, and all that went up with him to bury his father, after he had buried his father.

1:50:15.text: When Joseph’s brothers saw that their father was dead, they said, “It may be that Joseph will hate us, and will fully pay us back for all the evil which we did to him.”

1:50:16.text: They sent a message to Joseph, saying, “Your father commanded before he died, saying,

1:50:17.text: ‘ You shall tell Joseph, “Now please forgive the disobedience of your brothers, and their sin, because they did evil to you.”’ Now, please forgive the disobedience of the servants of the God of your father.” Joseph wept when they spoke to him.

1:50:18.text: His brothers also went and fell down before his face; and they said, “Behold, we are your servants.”

1:50:19.text: Joseph said to them, “Don’t be afraid, for am I in the place of God?

1:50:2.text: Joseph commanded his servants, the physicians, to embalm his father; and the physicians embalmed Israel.

1:50:20.text: As for you, you meant evil against me, but God meant it for good, to save many people alive, as is happening today.

1:50:21.text: Now therefore don’t be afraid. I will provide for you and your little ones.” He comforted them, and spoke kindly to them.

1:50:22.text: Joseph lived in Egypt, he, and his father’s house. Joseph lived one hundred and ten years.

1:50:23.text: Joseph saw Ephraim’s children to the third generation. The children also of Machir, the son of Manasseh, were born on Joseph’s knees.

1:50:24.text: Joseph said to his brothers, “I am dying, but God will surely visit you, and bring you up out of this land to the land which he swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.”

1:50:25.text: Joseph took an oath from the children of Israel, saying, “God will surely visit you, and you shall carry up my bones from here.”

1:50:26.text: So Joseph died, being one hundred and ten years old, and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.

1:50:3.text: Forty days were used for him, for that is how many days it takes to embalm. The Egyptians wept for Israel for seventy days.

1:50:4.text: When the days of weeping for him were past, Joseph spoke to Pharaoh’s staff, saying, “If now I have found favour in your eyes, please speak in the ears of Pharaoh, saying,

1:50:5.text: ‘ My father made me swear, saying, “Behold, I am dying. Bury me in my grave which I have dug for myself in the land of Canaan.” Now therefore, please let me go up and bury my father, and I will come again.’ ”

1:50:6.text: Pharaoh said, “Go up, and bury your father, just like he made you swear.”

1:50:7.text: Joseph went up to bury his father; and with him went up all the servants of Pharaoh, the elders of his house, all the elders of the land of Egypt,

1:50:8.text: all the house of Joseph, his brothers, and his father’s house. Only their little ones, their flocks, and their herds, they left in the land of Goshen.

1:50:9.text: Both chariots and horsemen went up with him. It was a very great company.

1:5:1.text: This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day that God created man, he made him in God’s likeness.

1:5:10.text: Enosh lived after he became the father of Kenan eight hundred and fifteen years, and became the father of other sons and daughters.

1:5:11.text: All of the days of Enosh were nine hundred and five years, then he died.

1:5:12.text: Kenan lived seventy years, then became the father of Mahalalel.

1:5:13.text: Kenan lived after he became the father of Mahalalel eight hundred and forty years, and became the father of other sons and daughters

1:5:14.text: and all of the days of Kenan were nine hundred and ten years, then he died.

1:5:15.text: Mahalalel lived sixty-five years, then became the father of Jared.

1:5:16.text: Mahalalel lived after he became the father of Jared eight hundred and thirty years, and became the father of other sons and daughters.

1:5:17.text: All of the days of Mahalalel were eight hundred and ninety-five years, then he died.

1:5:18.text: Jared lived one hundred and sixty-two years, then became the father of Enoch.

1:5:19.text: Jared lived after he became the father of Enoch eight hundred years, and became the father of other sons and daughters.

1:5:2.text: He created them male and female, and blessed them. On the day they were created, he named them Adam.

1:5:20.text: All of the days of Jared were nine hundred and sixty-two years, then he died.

1:5:21.text: Enoch lived sixty-five years, then became the father of Methuselah.

1:5:22.text: After Methuselah’s birth, Enoch walked with God for three hundred years, and became the father of more sons and daughters.

1:5:23.text: All the days of Enoch were three hundred and sixty-five years.

1:5:24.text: Enoch walked with God, and he was not found, for God took him.

1:5:25.text: Methuselah lived one hundred and eighty-seven years, then became the father of Lamech.

1:5:26.text: Methuselah lived after he became the father of Lamech seven hundred and eighty-two years, and became the father of other sons and daughters.

1:5:27.text: All the days of Methuselah were nine hundred and sixty-nine years, then he died.

1:5:28.text: Lamech lived one hundred and eighty-two years, then became the father of a son.

1:5:29.text: He named him Noah, saying, “This one will comfort us in our work and in the toil of our hands, caused by the ground which the LORD has cursed.”

1:5:3.text: Adam lived one hundred and thirty years, and became the father of a son in his own likeness, after his image, and named him Seth.

1:5:30.text: Lamech lived after he became the father of Noah five hundred and ninety-five years, and became the father of other sons and daughters.

1:5:31.text: All the days of Lamech were seven hundred and seventy-seven years, then he died.

1:5:32.text: Noah was five hundred years old, then Noah became the father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

1:5:4.text: The days of Adam after he became the father of Seth were eight hundred years, and he became the father of other sons and daughters.

1:5:5.text: All the days that Adam lived were nine hundred and thirty years, then he died.

1:5:6.text: Seth lived one hundred and five years, then became the father of Enosh.

1:5:7.text: Seth lived after he became the father of Enosh eight hundred and seven years, and became the father of other sons and daughters.

1:5:8.text: All of the days of Seth were nine hundred and twelve years, then he died.

1:5:9.text: Enosh lived ninety years, and became the father of Kenan.

1:6:1.text: When men began to multiply on the surface of the ground, and daughters were born to them,

1:6:10.text: Noah became the father of three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

1:6:11.text: The earth was corrupt before God, and the earth was filled with violence.

1:6:12.text: God saw the earth, and saw that it was corrupt, for all flesh had corrupted their way on the earth.

1:6:13.text: God said to Noah, “I will bring an end to all flesh, for the earth is filled with violence through them. Behold, I will destroy them and the earth.

1:6:14.text: Make a ship of gopher wood. You shall make rooms in the ship, and shall seal it inside and outside with pitch.

1:6:15.text: This is how you shall make it. The length of the ship shall be three hundred cubits, its width fifty cubits, and its height thirty cubits.

1:6:16.text: You shall make a roof in the ship, and you shall finish it to a cubit upward. You shall set the door of the ship in its side. You shall make it with lower, second, and third levels.

1:6:17.text: I, even I, will bring the flood of waters on this earth, to destroy all flesh having the breath of life from under the sky. Everything that is in the earth will die.

1:6:18.text: But I will establish my covenant with you. You shall come into the ship, you, your sons, your wife, and your sons’ wives with you.

1:6:19.text: Of every living thing of all flesh, you shall bring two of every sort into the ship, to keep them alive with you. They shall be male and female.

1:6:2.text: God’s sons saw that men’s daughters were beautiful, and they took any that they wanted for themselves as wives.

1:6:20.text: Of the birds after their kind, of the livestock after their kind, of every creeping thing of the ground after its kind, two of every sort will come to you, to keep them alive.

1:6:21.text: Take with you some of all food that is eaten, and gather it to yourself; and it will be for food for you, and for them.”

1:6:22.text: Thus Noah did. He did all that God commanded him.

1:6:3.text: The LORD said, “My Spirit will not strive with man forever, because he also is flesh; so his days will be one hundred and twenty years.”

1:6:4.text: The Nephilim were in the earth in those days, and also after that, when God’s sons came in to men’s daughters and had children with them. Those were the mighty men who were of old, men of renown.

1:6:5.text: The LORD saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of man’s heart was continually only evil.

1:6:6.text: The LORD was sorry that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him in his heart.

1:6:7.text: The LORD said, “I will destroy man whom I have created from the surface of the ground — man, along with animals, creeping things, and birds of the sky — for I am sorry that I have made them.”

1:6:8.text: But Noah found favour in the LORD’s eyes.

1:6:9.text: This is the history of the generations of Noah: Noah was a righteous man, blameless amongst the people of his time. Noah walked with God.

1:7:1.text: The LORD said to Noah, “Come with all of your household into the ship, for I have seen your righteousness before me in this generation.

1:7:10.text: After the seven days, the floodwaters came on the earth.

1:7:11.text: In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on that day all the fountains of the great deep burst open, and the sky’s windows opened.

1:7:12.text: It rained on the earth forty days and forty nights.

1:7:13.text: In the same day Noah, and Shem, Ham, and Japheth — the sons of Noah — and Noah’s wife and the three wives of his sons with them, entered into the ship —

1:7:14.text: they, and every animal after its kind, all the livestock after their kind, every creeping thing that creeps on the earth after its kind, and every bird after its kind, every bird of every sort.

1:7:15.text: Pairs from all flesh with the breath of life in them went into the ship to Noah.

1:7:16.text: Those who went in, went in male and female of all flesh, as God commanded him; then the LORD shut him in.

1:7:17.text: The flood was forty days on the earth. The waters increased, and lifted up the ship, and it was lifted up above the earth.

1:7:18.text: The waters rose, and increased greatly on the earth; and the ship floated on the surface of the waters.

1:7:19.text: The waters rose very high on the earth. All the high mountains that were under the whole sky were covered.

1:7:2.text: You shall take seven pairs of every clean animal with you, the male and his female. Of the animals that are not clean, take two, the male and his female.

1:7:20.text: The waters rose fifteen cubits higher, and the mountains were covered.

1:7:21.text: All flesh died that moved on the earth, including birds, livestock, animals, every creeping thing that creeps on the earth, and every man.

1:7:22.text: All on the dry land, in whose nostrils was the breath of the spirit of life, died.

1:7:23.text: Every living thing was destroyed that was on the surface of the ground, including man, livestock, creeping things, and birds of the sky. They were destroyed from the earth. Only Noah was left, and those who were with him in the ship.

1:7:24.text: The waters flooded the earth one hundred and fifty days.

1:7:3.text: Also of the birds of the sky, seven and seven, male and female, to keep seed alive on the surface of all the earth.

1:7:4.text: In seven days, I will cause it to rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights. I will destroy every living thing that I have made from the surface of the ground.”

1:7:5.text: Noah did everything that the LORD commanded him.

1:7:6.text: Noah was six hundred years old when the flood of waters came on the earth.

1:7:7.text: Noah went into the ship with his sons, his wife, and his sons’ wives, because of the floodwaters.

1:7:8.text: Clean animals, unclean animals, birds, and everything that creeps on the ground

1:7:9.text: went by pairs to Noah into the ship, male and female, as God commanded Noah.

1:8:1.text: God remembered Noah, all the animals, and all the livestock that were with him in the ship; and God made a wind to pass over the earth. The waters subsided.

1:8:10.text: He waited yet another seven days; and again he sent the dove out of the ship.

1:8:11.text: The dove came back to him at evening and, behold, in her mouth was a freshly plucked olive leaf. So Noah knew that the waters were abated from the earth.

1:8:12.text: He waited yet another seven days, and sent out the dove; and she didn’t return to him any more.

1:8:13.text: In the six hundred and first year, in the first month, the first day of the month, the waters were dried up from the earth. Noah removed the covering of the ship, and looked. He saw that the surface of the ground was dry.

1:8:14.text: In the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, the earth was dry.

1:8:16.text: “Go out of the ship, you, your wife, your sons, and your sons’ wives with you.

1:8:17.text: Bring out with you every living thing that is with you of all flesh, including birds, livestock, and every creeping thing that creeps on the earth, that they may breed abundantly in the earth, and be fruitful, and multiply on the earth.”

1:8:18.text: Noah went out, with his sons, his wife, and his sons’ wives with him.

1:8:19.text: Every animal, every creeping thing, and every bird, whatever moves on the earth, after their families, went out of the ship.

1:8:2.text: The deep’s fountains and the sky’s windows were also stopped, and the rain from the sky was restrained.

1:8:20.text: Noah built an altar to the LORD, and took of every clean animal, and of every clean bird, and offered burnt offerings on the altar.

1:8:21.text: The LORD smelled the pleasant aroma. The LORD said in his heart, “I will not again curse the ground any more for man’s sake because the imagination of man’s heart is evil from his youth. I will never again strike every living thing, as I have done.

1:8:22.text: While the earth remains, seed time and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night will not cease.”

1:8:3.text: The waters continually receded from the earth. After the end of one hundred and fifty days the waters receded.

1:8:4.text: The ship rested in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on Ararat’s mountains.

1:8:5.text: The waters receded continually until the tenth month. In the tenth month, on the first day of the month, the tops of the mountains were visible.

1:8:6.text: At the end of forty days, Noah opened the window of the ship which he had made,

1:8:7.text: and he sent out a raven. It went back and forth, until the waters were dried up from the earth.

1:8:8.text: He himself sent out a dove to see if the waters were abated from the surface of the ground,

1:8:9.text: but the dove found no place to rest her foot, and she returned into the ship to him, for the waters were on the surface of the whole earth. He put out his hand, and took her, and brought her to him into the ship.

1:9:1.text: God blessed Noah and his sons, and said to them, “Be fruitful, multiply, and replenish the earth.

1:9:10.text: and with every living creature that is with you: the birds, the livestock, and every animal of the earth with you, of all that go out of the ship, even every animal of the earth.

1:9:11.text: I will establish my covenant with you: All flesh will not be cut off any more by the waters of the flood. There will never again be a flood to destroy the earth.”

1:9:12.text: God said, “This is the token of the covenant which I make between me and you and every living creature that is with you, for perpetual generations:

1:9:13.text: I set my rainbow in the cloud, and it will be a sign of a covenant between me and the earth.

1:9:14.text: When I bring a cloud over the earth, that the rainbow will be seen in the cloud,

1:9:15.text: I will remember my covenant, which is between me and you and every living creature of all flesh, and the waters will no more become a flood to destroy all flesh.

1:9:16.text: The rainbow will be in the cloud. I will look at it, that I may remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh that is on the earth.”

1:9:17.text: God said to Noah, “This is the token of the covenant which I have established between me and all flesh that is on the earth.”

1:9:18.text: The sons of Noah who went out from the ship were Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Ham is the father of Canaan.

1:9:19.text: These three were the sons of Noah, and from these the whole earth was populated.

1:9:2.text: The fear of you and the dread of you will be on every animal of the earth, and on every bird of the sky. Everything that moves along the ground, and all the fish of the sea, are delivered into your hand.

1:9:20.text: Noah began to be a farmer, and planted a vineyard.

1:9:21.text: He drank of the wine and got drunk. He was uncovered within his tent.

1:9:22.text: Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father, and told his two brothers outside.

1:9:23.text: Shem and Japheth took a garment, and laid it on both their shoulders, went in backwards, and covered the nakedness of their father. Their faces were backwards, and they didn’t see their father’s nakedness.

1:9:24.text: Noah awoke from his wine, and knew what his youngest son had done to him.

1:9:25.text: He said, “Canaan is cursed. He will be a servant of servants to his brothers.”

1:9:26.text: He said, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Shem. Let Canaan be his servant.

1:9:27.text: May God enlarge Japheth. Let him dwell in the tents of Shem. Let Canaan be his servant.”

1:9:28.text: Noah lived three hundred and fifty years after the flood.

1:9:29.text: All the days of Noah were nine hundred and fifty years, and then he died.

1:9:3.text: Every moving thing that lives will be food for you. As I gave you the green herb, I have given everything to you.

1:9:4.text: But flesh with its life, that is, its blood, you shall not eat.

1:9:5.text: I will surely require accounting for your life’s blood. At the hand of every animal I will require it. At the hand of man, even at the hand of every man’s brother, I will require the life of man.

1:9:6.text: Whoever sheds man’s blood, his blood will be shed by man, for God made man in his own image.

1:9:7.text: Be fruitful and multiply. Increase abundantly in the earth, and multiply in it.”

1:9:8.text: God spoke to Noah and to his sons with him, saying,

1:9:9.text: “As for me, behold, I establish my covenant with you, and with your offspring after you,

20:10:1.text: The proverbs of Solomon. A wise son makes a glad father; but a foolish son brings grief to his mother.

20:10:10.text: One who winks with the eye causes sorrow, but a chattering fool will fall.

20:10:11.text: The mouth of the righteous is a spring of life, but violence covers the mouth of the wicked.

20:10:12.text: Hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all wrongs.

20:10:13.text: Wisdom is found on the lips of him who has discernment, but a rod is for the back of him who is void of understanding.

20:10:14.text: Wise men lay up knowledge, but the mouth of the foolish is near ruin.

20:10:15.text: The rich man’s wealth is his strong city. The destruction of the poor is their poverty.

20:10:16.text: The labour of the righteous leads to life. The increase of the wicked leads to sin.

20:10:17.text: He is in the way of life who heeds correction, but he who forsakes reproof leads others astray.

20:10:18.text: He who hides hatred has lying lips. He who utters a slander is a fool.

20:10:19.text: In the multitude of words there is no lack of disobedience, but he who restrains his lips does wisely.

20:10:2.text: Treasures of wickedness profit nothing, but righteousness delivers from death.

20:10:20.text: The tongue of the righteous is like choice silver. The heart of the wicked is of little worth.

20:10:21.text: The lips of the righteous feed many, but the foolish die for lack of understanding.

20:10:22.text: The LORD’s blessing brings wealth, and he adds no trouble to it.

20:10:23.text: It is a fool’s pleasure to do wickedness, but wisdom is a man of understanding’s pleasure.

20:10:24.text: What the wicked fear will overtake them, but the desire of the righteous will be granted.

20:10:25.text: When the whirlwind passes, the wicked is no more; but the righteous stand firm forever.

20:10:26.text: As vinegar to the teeth, and as smoke to the eyes, so is the sluggard to those who send him.

20:10:27.text: The fear of the LORD prolongs days, but the years of the wicked shall be shortened.

20:10:28.text: The prospect of the righteous is joy, but the hope of the wicked will perish.

20:10:29.text: The way of the LORD is a stronghold to the upright, but it is a destruction to the workers of iniquity.

20:10:3.text: The LORD will not allow the soul of the righteous to go hungry, but he thrusts away the desire of the wicked.

20:10:30.text: The righteous will never be removed, but the wicked will not dwell in the land.

20:10:31.text: The mouth of the righteous produces wisdom, but the perverse tongue will be cut off.

20:10:32.text: The lips of the righteous know what is acceptable, but the mouth of the wicked is perverse.

20:10:4.text: He becomes poor who works with a lazy hand, but the hand of the diligent brings wealth.

20:10:5.text: He who gathers in summer is a wise son, but he who sleeps during the harvest is a son who causes shame.

20:10:6.text: Blessings are on the head of the righteous, but violence covers the mouth of the wicked.

20:10:7.text: The memory of the righteous is blessed, but the name of the wicked will rot.

20:10:8.text: The wise in heart accept commandments, but a chattering fool will fall.

20:10:9.text: He who walks blamelessly walks surely, but he who perverts his ways will be found out.

20:11:1.text: A false balance is an abomination to the LORD, but accurate weights are his delight.

20:11:10.text: When it goes well with the righteous, the city rejoices. When the wicked perish, there is shouting.

20:11:11.text: By the blessing of the upright, the city is exalted, but it is overthrown by the mouth of the wicked.

20:11:12.text: One who despises his neighbour is void of wisdom, but a man of understanding holds his peace.

20:11:13.text: One who brings gossip betrays a confidence, but one who is of a trustworthy spirit is one who keeps a secret.

20:11:14.text: Where there is no wise guidance, the nation falls, but in the multitude of counsellors there is victory.

20:11:15.text: He who is collateral for a stranger will suffer for it, but he who refuses pledges of collateral is secure.

20:11:16.text: A gracious woman obtains honour, but violent men obtain riches.

20:11:17.text: The merciful man does good to his own soul, but he who is cruel troubles his own flesh.

20:11:18.text: Wicked people earn deceitful wages, but one who sows righteousness reaps a sure reward.

20:11:19.text: He who is truly righteous gets life. He who pursues evil gets death.

20:11:2.text: When pride comes, then comes shame, but with humility comes wisdom.

20:11:20.text: Those who are perverse in heart are an abomination to the LORD, but those whose ways are blameless are his delight.

20:11:21.text: Most certainly, the evil man will not be unpunished, but the offspring of the righteous will be delivered.

20:11:22.text: Like a gold ring in a pig’s snout, is a beautiful woman who lacks discretion.

20:11:23.text: The desire of the righteous is only good. The expectation of the wicked is wrath.

20:11:24.text: There is one who scatters, and increases yet more. There is one who withholds more than is appropriate, but gains poverty.

20:11:25.text: The liberal soul shall be made fat. He who waters shall be watered also himself.

20:11:26.text: People curse someone who withholds grain, but blessing will be on the head of him who sells it.
