20:11:27.text: He who diligently seeks good seeks favour, but he who searches after evil, it shall come to him.

20:11:28.text: He who trusts in his riches will fall, but the righteous shall flourish as the green leaf.

20:11:29.text: He who troubles his own house shall inherit the wind. The foolish shall be servant to the wise of heart.

20:11:3.text: The integrity of the upright shall guide them, but the perverseness of the treacherous shall destroy them.

20:11:30.text: The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life. He who is wise wins souls.

20:11:31.text: Behold, the righteous shall be repaid in the earth, how much more the wicked and the sinner!

20:11:4.text: Riches don’t profit in the day of wrath, but righteousness delivers from death.

20:11:5.text: The righteousness of the blameless will direct his way, but the wicked shall fall by his own wickedness.

20:11:6.text: The righteousness of the upright shall deliver them, but the unfaithful will be trapped by evil desires.

20:11:7.text: When a wicked man dies, hope perishes, and expectation of power comes to nothing.

20:11:8.text: A righteous person is delivered out of trouble, and the wicked takes his place.

20:11:9.text: With his mouth the godless man destroys his neighbour, but the righteous will be delivered through knowledge.

20:12:1.text: Whoever loves correction loves knowledge, but he who hates reproof is stupid.

20:12:10.text: A righteous man respects the life of his animal, but the tender mercies of the wicked are cruel.

20:12:11.text: He who tills his land shall have plenty of bread, but he who chases fantasies is void of understanding.

20:12:12.text: The wicked desires the plunder of evil men, but the root of the righteous flourishes.

20:12:13.text: An evil man is trapped by sinfulness of lips, but the righteous shall come out of trouble.

20:12:14.text: A man shall be satisfied with good by the fruit of his mouth. The work of a man’s hands shall be rewarded to him.

20:12:15.text: The way of a fool is right in his own eyes, but he who is wise listens to counsel.

20:12:16.text: A fool shows his annoyance the same day, but one who overlooks an insult is prudent.

20:12:17.text: He who is truthful testifies honestly, but a false witness lies.

20:12:18.text: There is one who speaks rashly like the piercing of a sword, but the tongue of the wise heals.

20:12:19.text: Truth’s lips will be established forever, but a lying tongue is only momentary.

20:12:2.text: A good man shall obtain favour from the LORD, but he will condemn a man of wicked plans.

20:12:20.text: Deceit is in the heart of those who plot evil, but joy comes to the promoters of peace.

20:12:21.text: No mischief shall happen to the righteous, but the wicked shall be filled with evil.

20:12:22.text: Lying lips are an abomination to the LORD, but those who do the truth are his delight.

20:12:23.text: A prudent man keeps his knowledge, but the hearts of fools proclaim foolishness.

20:12:24.text: The hands of the diligent ones shall rule, but laziness ends in slave labour.

20:12:25.text: Anxiety in a man’s heart weighs it down, but a kind word makes it glad.

20:12:26.text: A righteous person is cautious in friendship, but the way of the wicked leads them astray.

20:12:27.text: The slothful man doesn’t roast his game, but the possessions of diligent men are prized.

20:12:28.text: In the way of righteousness is life; in its path there is no death.

20:12:3.text: A man shall not be established by wickedness, but the root of the righteous shall not be moved.

20:12:4.text: A worthy woman is the crown of her husband, but a disgraceful wife is as rottenness in his bones.

20:12:5.text: The thoughts of the righteous are just, but the advice of the wicked is deceitful.

20:12:6.text: The words of the wicked are about lying in wait for blood, but the speech of the upright rescues them.

20:12:7.text: The wicked are overthrown, and are no more, but the house of the righteous shall stand.

20:12:8.text: A man shall be commended according to his wisdom, but he who has a warped mind shall be despised.

20:12:9.text: Better is he who is little known, and has a servant, than he who honours himself and lacks bread.

20:13:1.text: A wise son listens to his father’s instruction, but a scoffer doesn’t listen to rebuke.

20:13:10.text: Pride only breeds quarrels, but wisdom is with people who take advice.

20:13:11.text: Wealth gained dishonestly dwindles away, but he who gathers by hand makes it grow.

20:13:12.text: Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but when longing is fulfilled, it is a tree of life.

20:13:13.text: Whoever despises instruction will pay for it, but he who respects a command will be rewarded.

20:13:14.text: The teaching of the wise is a spring of life, to turn from the snares of death.

20:13:15.text: Good understanding wins favour, but the way of the unfaithful is hard.

20:13:16.text: Every prudent man acts from knowledge, but a fool exposes folly.

20:13:17.text: A wicked messenger falls into trouble, but a trustworthy envoy gains healing.

20:13:18.text: Poverty and shame come to him who refuses discipline, but he who heeds correction shall be honoured.

20:13:19.text: Longing fulfilled is sweet to the soul, but fools detest turning from evil.

20:13:2.text: By the fruit of his lips, a man enjoys good things, but the unfaithful crave violence.

20:13:20.text: One who walks with wise men grows wise, but a companion of fools suffers harm.

20:13:21.text: Misfortune pursues sinners, but prosperity rewards the righteous.

20:13:22.text: A good man leaves an inheritance to his children’s children, but the wealth of the sinner is stored for the righteous.

20:13:23.text: An abundance of food is in poor people’s fields, but injustice sweeps it away.

20:13:24.text: One who spares the rod hates his son, but one who loves him is careful to discipline him.

20:13:25.text: The righteous one eats to the satisfying of his soul, but the belly of the wicked goes hungry.

20:13:3.text: He who guards his mouth guards his soul. One who opens wide his lips comes to ruin.

20:13:4.text: The soul of the sluggard desires, and has nothing, but the desire of the diligent shall be fully satisfied.

20:13:5.text: A righteous man hates lies, but a wicked man brings shame and disgrace.

20:13:6.text: Righteousness guards the way of integrity, but wickedness overthrows the sinner.

20:13:7.text: There are some who pretend to be rich, yet have nothing. There are some who pretend to be poor, yet have great wealth.

20:13:8.text: The ransom of a man’s life is his riches, but the poor hear no threats.

20:13:9.text: The light of the righteous shines brightly, but the lamp of the wicked is snuffed out.

20:14:1.text: Every wise woman builds her house, but the foolish one tears it down with her own hands.

20:14:10.text: The heart knows its own bitterness and joy; he will not share these with a stranger.

20:14:11.text: The house of the wicked will be overthrown, but the tent of the upright will flourish.

20:14:12.text: There is a way which seems right to a man, but in the end it leads to death.

20:14:13.text: Even in laughter the heart may be sorrowful, and mirth may end in heaviness.

20:14:14.text: The unfaithful will be repaid for his own ways; likewise a good man will be rewarded for his ways.

20:14:15.text: A simple man believes everything, but the prudent man carefully considers his ways.

20:14:16.text: A wise man fears and shuns evil, but the fool is hot headed and reckless.

20:14:17.text: He who is quick to become angry will commit folly, and a crafty man is hated.

20:14:18.text: The simple inherit folly, but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.

20:14:19.text: The evil bow down before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.

20:14:2.text: He who walks in his uprightness fears the LORD, but he who is perverse in his ways despises him.

20:14:20.text: The poor person is shunned even by his own neighbour, but the rich person has many friends.

20:14:21.text: He who despises his neighbour sins, but he who has pity on the poor is blessed.

20:14:22.text: Don’t they go astray who plot evil? But love and faithfulness belong to those who plan good.

20:14:23.text: In all hard work there is profit, but the talk of the lips leads only to poverty.

20:14:24.text: The crown of the wise is their riches, but the folly of fools crowns them with folly.

20:14:25.text: A truthful witness saves souls, but a false witness is deceitful.

20:14:26.text: In the fear of the LORD is a secure fortress, and he will be a refuge for his children.

20:14:27.text: The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, turning people from the snares of death.

20:14:28.text: In the multitude of people is the king’s glory, but in the lack of people is the destruction of the prince.

20:14:29.text: He who is slow to anger has great understanding, but he who has a quick temper displays folly.

20:14:3.text: The fool’s talk brings a rod to his back, but the lips of the wise protect them.

20:14:30.text: The life of the body is a heart at peace, but envy rots the bones.

20:14:31.text: He who oppresses the poor shows contempt for his Maker, but he who is kind to the needy honours him.

20:14:32.text: The wicked is brought down in his calamity, but in death, the righteous has a refuge.

20:14:33.text: Wisdom rests in the heart of one who has understanding, and is even made known in the inward part of fools.

20:14:34.text: Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin is a disgrace to any people.

20:14:35.text: The king’s favour is towards a servant who deals wisely, but his wrath is towards one who causes shame.

20:14:4.text: Where no oxen are, the crib is clean, but much increase is by the strength of the ox.

20:14:5.text: A truthful witness will not lie, but a false witness pours out lies.

20:14:6.text: A scoffer seeks wisdom, and doesn’t find it, but knowledge comes easily to a discerning person.

20:14:7.text: Stay away from a foolish man, for you won’t find knowledge on his lips.

20:14:8.text: The wisdom of the prudent is to think about his way, but the folly of fools is deceit.

20:14:9.text: Fools mock at making atonement for sins, but amongst the upright there is good will.

20:15:1.text: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.

20:15:10.text: There is stern discipline for one who forsakes the way. Whoever hates reproof shall die.

20:15:11.text: Sheol and Abaddon are before the LORD — how much more then the hearts of the children of men!

20:15:12.text: A scoffer doesn’t love to be reproved; he will not go to the wise.

20:15:13.text: A glad heart makes a cheerful face, but an aching heart breaks the spirit.

20:15:14.text: The heart of one who has understanding seeks knowledge, but the mouths of fools feed on folly.

20:15:15.text: All the days of the afflicted are wretched, but one who has a cheerful heart enjoys a continual feast.

20:15:16.text: Better is little, with the fear of the LORD, than great treasure with trouble.

20:15:17.text: Better is a dinner of herbs, where love is, than a fattened calf with hatred.

20:15:18.text: A wrathful man stirs up contention, but one who is slow to anger appeases strife.

20:15:19.text: The way of the sluggard is like a thorn patch, but the path of the upright is a highway.

20:15:2.text: The tongue of the wise commends knowledge, but the mouths of fools gush out folly.

20:15:20.text: A wise son makes a father glad, but a foolish man despises his mother.

20:15:21.text: Folly is joy to one who is void of wisdom, but a man of understanding keeps his way straight.

20:15:22.text: Where there is no counsel, plans fail; but in a multitude of counsellors they are established.

20:15:23.text: Joy comes to a man with the reply of his mouth. How good is a word at the right time!

20:15:24.text: The path of life leads upward for the wise, to keep him from going downward to Sheol.

20:15:25.text: The LORD will uproot the house of the proud, but he will keep the widow’s borders intact.

20:15:26.text: The LORD detests the thoughts of the wicked, but the thoughts of the pure are pleasing.

20:15:27.text: He who is greedy for gain troubles his own house, but he who hates bribes will live.

20:15:28.text: The heart of the righteous weighs answers, but the mouth of the wicked gushes out evil.

20:15:29.text: The LORD is far from the wicked, but he hears the prayer of the righteous.

20:15:3.text: The LORD’s eyes are everywhere, keeping watch on the evil and the good.

20:15:30.text: The light of the eyes rejoices the heart. Good news gives health to the bones.

20:15:31.text: The ear that listens to reproof lives, and will be at home amongst the wise.

20:15:32.text: He who refuses correction despises his own soul, but he who listens to reproof gets understanding.

20:15:33.text: The fear of the LORD teaches wisdom. Before honour is humility.

20:15:4.text: A gentle tongue is a tree of life, but deceit in it crushes the spirit.

20:15:5.text: A fool despises his father’s correction, but he who heeds reproof shows prudence.

20:15:6.text: In the house of the righteous is much treasure, but the income of the wicked brings trouble.

20:15:7.text: The lips of the wise spread knowledge; not so with the heart of fools.

20:15:8.text: The sacrifice made by the wicked is an abomination to the LORD, but the prayer of the upright is his delight.

20:15:9.text: The way of the wicked is an abomination to the LORD, but he loves him who follows after righteousness.

20:16:1.text: The plans of the heart belong to man, but the answer of the tongue is from the LORD.

20:16:10.text: Inspired judgements are on the lips of the king. He shall not betray his mouth.

20:16:11.text: Honest balances and scales are the LORD’s; all the weights in the bag are his work.

20:16:12.text: It is an abomination for kings to do wrong, for the throne is established by righteousness.

20:16:13.text: Righteous lips are the delight of kings. They value one who speaks the truth.

20:16:14.text: The king’s wrath is a messenger of death, but a wise man will pacify it.

20:16:15.text: In the light of the king’s face is life. His favour is like a cloud of the spring rain.

20:16:16.text: How much better it is to get wisdom than gold! Yes, to get understanding is to be chosen rather than silver.

20:16:17.text: The highway of the upright is to depart from evil. He who keeps his way preserves his soul.

20:16:18.text: Pride goes before destruction, and an arrogant spirit before a fall.

20:16:19.text: It is better to be of a lowly spirit with the poor, than to divide the plunder with the proud.

20:16:2.text: All the ways of a man are clean in his own eyes, but the LORD weighs the motives.

20:16:20.text: He who heeds the Word finds prosperity. Whoever trusts in the LORD is blessed.

20:16:21.text: The wise in heart shall be called prudent. Pleasantness of the lips promotes instruction.

20:16:22.text: Understanding is a fountain of life to one who has it, but the punishment of fools is their folly.

20:16:23.text: The heart of the wise instructs his mouth, and adds learning to his lips.

20:16:24.text: Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.

20:16:25.text: There is a way which seems right to a man, but in the end it leads to death.

20:16:26.text: The appetite of the labouring man labours for him, for his mouth urges him on.

20:16:27.text: A worthless man devises mischief. His speech is like a scorching fire.

20:16:28.text: A perverse man stirs up strife. A whisperer separates close friends.

20:16:29.text: A man of violence entices his neighbour, and leads him in a way that is not good.

20:16:3.text: Commit your deeds to the LORD, and your plans shall succeed.

20:16:30.text: One who winks his eyes to plot perversities, one who compresses his lips, is bent on evil.

20:16:31.text: Grey hair is a crown of glory. It is attained by a life of righteousness.

20:16:32.text: One who is slow to anger is better than the mighty; one who rules his spirit, than he who takes a city.

20:16:33.text: The lot is cast into the lap, but its every decision is from the LORD.

20:16:4.text: The LORD has made everything for its own end — yes, even the wicked for the day of evil.

20:16:5.text: Everyone who is proud in heart is an abomination to the LORD; they shall certainly not be unpunished.

20:16:6.text: By mercy and truth iniquity is atoned for. By the fear of the LORD men depart from evil.

20:16:7.text: When a man’s ways please the LORD, he makes even his enemies to be at peace with him.

20:16:8.text: Better is a little with righteousness, than great revenues with injustice.

20:16:9.text: A man’s heart plans his course, but the LORD directs his steps.

20:17:1.text: Better is a dry morsel with quietness, than a house full of feasting with strife.

20:17:10.text: A rebuke enters deeper into one who has understanding than a hundred lashes into a fool.

20:17:11.text: An evil man seeks only rebellion; therefore a cruel messenger shall be sent against him.

20:17:12.text: Let a bear robbed of her cubs meet a man, rather than a fool in his folly.

20:17:13.text: Whoever rewards evil for good, evil shall not depart from his house.

20:17:14.text: The beginning of strife is like breaching a dam, therefore stop contention before quarrelling breaks out.

20:17:15.text: He who justifies the wicked, and he who condemns the righteous, both of them alike are an abomination to the LORD.

20:17:16.text: Why is there money in the hand of a fool to buy wisdom, since he has no understanding?

20:17:17.text: A friend loves at all times; and a brother is born for adversity.

20:17:18.text: A man void of understanding strikes hands, and becomes collateral in the presence of his neighbour.

20:17:19.text: He who loves disobedience loves strife. One who builds a high gate seeks destruction.

20:17:2.text: A servant who deals wisely will rule over a son who causes shame, and shall have a part in the inheritance amongst the brothers.

20:17:20.text: One who has a perverse heart doesn’t find prosperity, and one who has a deceitful tongue falls into trouble.

20:17:21.text: He who becomes the father of a fool grieves. The father of a fool has no joy.

20:17:22.text: A cheerful heart makes good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones.

20:17:23.text: A wicked man receives a bribe in secret, to pervert the ways of justice.

20:17:24.text: Wisdom is before the face of one who has understanding, but the eyes of a fool wander to the ends of the earth.

20:17:25.text: A foolish son brings grief to his father, and bitterness to her who bore him.

20:17:26.text: Also to punish the righteous is not good, nor to flog officials for their integrity.

20:17:27.text: He who spares his words has knowledge. He who is even tempered is a man of understanding.

20:17:28.text: Even a fool, when he keeps silent, is counted wise. When he shuts his lips, he is thought to be discerning.

20:17:3.text: The refining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold, but the LORD tests the hearts.

20:17:4.text: An evildoer heeds wicked lips. A liar gives ear to a mischievous tongue.

20:17:5.text: Whoever mocks the poor reproaches his Maker. He who is glad at calamity shall not be unpunished.

20:17:6.text: Children’s children are the crown of old men; the glory of children is their parents.

20:17:7.text: Excellent speech isn’t fitting for a fool, much less do lying lips fit a prince.

20:17:8.text: A bribe is a precious stone in the eyes of him who gives it; wherever he turns, he prospers.

20:17:9.text: He who covers an offence promotes love; but he who repeats a matter separates best friends.

20:18:1.text: A man who isolates himself pursues selfishness, and defies all sound judgement.

20:18:10.text: The LORD’s name is a strong tower: the righteous run to him, and are safe.

20:18:11.text: The rich man’s wealth is his strong city, like an unscalable wall in his own imagination.

20:18:12.text: Before destruction the heart of man is proud, but before honour is humility.

20:18:13.text: He who answers before he hears, that is folly and shame to him.

20:18:14.text: A man’s spirit will sustain him in sickness, but a crushed spirit, who can bear?

20:18:15.text: The heart of the discerning gets knowledge. The ear of the wise seeks knowledge.

20:18:16.text: A man’s gift makes room for him, and brings him before great men.

20:18:17.text: He who pleads his cause first seems right — until another comes and questions him.

20:18:18.text: The lot settles disputes, and keeps strong ones apart.

20:18:19.text: A brother offended is more difficult than a fortified city. Disputes are like the bars of a fortress.

20:18:2.text: A fool has no delight in understanding, but only in revealing his own opinion.

20:18:20.text: A man’s stomach is filled with the fruit of his mouth. With the harvest of his lips he is satisfied.

20:18:21.text: Death and life are in the power of the tongue; those who love it will eat its fruit.

20:18:22.text: Whoever finds a wife finds a good thing, and obtains favour of the LORD.

20:18:23.text: The poor plead for mercy, but the rich answer harshly.

20:18:24.text: A man of many companions may be ruined, but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.

20:18:3.text: When wickedness comes, contempt also comes, and with shame comes disgrace.

20:18:4.text: The words of a man’s mouth are like deep waters. The fountain of wisdom is like a flowing brook.

20:18:5.text: To be partial to the faces of the wicked is not good, nor to deprive the innocent of justice.

20:18:6.text: A fool’s lips come into strife, and his mouth invites beatings.

20:18:7.text: A fool’s mouth is his destruction, and his lips are a snare to his soul.

20:18:8.text: The words of a gossip are like dainty morsels: they go down into a person’s innermost parts.

20:18:9.text: One who is slack in his work is brother to him who is a master of destruction.

20:19:1.text: Better is the poor who walks in his integrity than he who is perverse in his lips and is a fool.

20:19:10.text: Delicate living is not appropriate for a fool, much less for a servant to have rule over princes.

20:19:11.text: The discretion of a man makes him slow to anger. It is his glory to overlook an offence.

20:19:12.text: The king’s wrath is like the roaring of a lion, but his favour is like dew on the grass.

20:19:13.text: A foolish son is the calamity of his father. A wife’s quarrels are a continual dripping.

20:19:14.text: House and riches are an inheritance from fathers, but a prudent wife is from the LORD.

20:19:15.text: Slothfulness casts into a deep sleep. The idle soul shall suffer hunger.

20:19:16.text: He who keeps the commandment keeps his soul, but he who is contemptuous in his ways shall die.

20:19:17.text: He who has pity on the poor lends to the LORD; he will reward him.

20:19:18.text: Discipline your son, for there is hope; don’t be a willing party to his death.

20:19:19.text: A hot-tempered man must pay the penalty, for if you rescue him, you must do it again.

20:19:2.text: It isn’t good to have zeal without knowledge, nor being hasty with one’s feet and missing the way.

20:19:20.text: Listen to counsel and receive instruction, that you may be wise in your latter end.

20:19:21.text: There are many plans in a man’s heart, but the LORD’s counsel will prevail.

20:19:22.text: That which makes a man to be desired is his kindness. A poor man is better than a liar.

20:19:23.text: The fear of the LORD leads to life, then contentment; he rests and will not be touched by trouble.

20:19:24.text: The sluggard buries his hand in the dish; he will not so much as bring it to his mouth again.

20:19:25.text: Flog a scoffer, and the simple will learn prudence; rebuke one who has understanding, and he will gain knowledge.

20:19:26.text: He who robs his father and drives away his mother is a son who causes shame and brings reproach.

20:19:27.text: If you stop listening to instruction, my son, you will stray from the words of knowledge.

20:19:28.text: A corrupt witness mocks justice, and the mouth of the wicked gulps down iniquity.

20:19:29.text: Penalties are prepared for scoffers, and beatings for the backs of fools.

20:19:3.text: The foolishness of man subverts his way; his heart rages against the LORD.

20:19:4.text: Wealth adds many friends, but the poor is separated from his friend.

20:19:5.text: A false witness shall not be unpunished. He who pours out lies shall not go free.

20:19:6.text: Many will entreat the favour of a ruler, and everyone is a friend to a man who gives gifts.

20:19:7.text: All the relatives of the poor shun him; how much more do his friends avoid him! He pursues them with pleas, but they are gone.

20:19:8.text: He who gets wisdom loves his own soul. He who keeps understanding shall find good.

20:19:9.text: A false witness shall not be unpunished. He who utters lies shall perish.

20:1:1.text: The proverbs of Solomon, the son of David, king of Israel:

20:1:10.text: My son, if sinners entice you, don’t consent.

20:1:11.text: If they say, “Come with us. Let’s lie in wait for blood. Let’s lurk secretly for the innocent without cause.

20:1:12.text: Let’s swallow them up alive like Sheol, and whole, like those who go down into the pit.

20:1:13.text: We’ll find all valuable wealth. We’ll fill our houses with plunder.

20:1:14.text: You shall cast your lot amongst us. We’ll all have one purse” —

20:1:15.text: my son, don’t walk on the path with them. Keep your foot from their path,

20:1:16.text: for their feet run to evil. They hurry to shed blood.

20:1:17.text: For the net is spread in vain in the sight of any bird;

20:1:18.text: but these lay in wait for their own blood. They lurk secretly for their own lives.

20:1:19.text: So are the ways of everyone who is greedy for gain. It takes away the life of its owners.

20:1:2.text: to know wisdom and instruction; to discern the words of understanding;

20:1:20.text: Wisdom calls aloud in the street. She utters her voice in the public squares.

20:1:21.text: She calls at the head of noisy places. At the entrance of the city gates, she utters her words:

20:1:22.text: “How long, you simple ones, will you love simplicity? How long will mockers delight themselves in mockery, and fools hate knowledge?

20:1:23.text: Turn at my reproof. Behold, I will pour out my spirit on you. I will make known my words to you.

20:1:24.text: Because I have called, and you have refused; I have stretched out my hand, and no one has paid attention;

20:1:25.text: but you have ignored all my counsel, and wanted none of my reproof;

20:1:26.text: I also will laugh at your disaster. I will mock when calamity overtakes you,

20:1:27.text: when calamity overtakes you like a storm, when your disaster comes on like a whirlwind, when distress and anguish come on you.

20:1:28.text: Then they will call on me, but I will not answer. They will seek me diligently, but they will not find me,

20:1:29.text: because they hated knowledge, and didn’t choose the fear of the LORD.

20:1:3.text: to receive instruction in wise dealing, in righteousness, justice, and equity;

20:1:30.text: They wanted none of my counsel. They despised all my reproof.

20:1:31.text: Therefore they will eat of the fruit of their own way, and be filled with their own schemes.

20:1:32.text: For the backsliding of the simple will kill them. The careless ease of fools will destroy them.

20:1:33.text: But whoever listens to me will dwell securely, and will be at ease, without fear of harm.”

20:1:4.text: to give prudence to the simple, knowledge and discretion to the young man —

20:1:5.text: that the wise man may hear, and increase in learning; that the man of understanding may attain to sound counsel;

20:1:6.text: to understand a proverb and parables, the words and riddles of the wise.

20:1:7.text: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge, but the foolish despise wisdom and instruction.

20:1:8.text: My son, listen to your father’s instruction, and don’t forsake your mother’s teaching;

20:1:9.text: for they will be a garland to grace your head, and chains around your neck.

20:21:1.text: The king’s heart is in the LORD’s hand like the watercourses. He turns it wherever he desires.

20:21:10.text: The soul of the wicked desires evil; his neighbour finds no mercy in his eyes.

20:21:11.text: When the mocker is punished, the simple gains wisdom. When the wise is instructed, he receives knowledge.

20:21:12.text: The Righteous One considers the house of the wicked, and brings the wicked to ruin.

20:21:13.text: Whoever stops his ears at the cry of the poor, he will also cry out, but shall not be heard.

20:21:14.text: A gift in secret pacifies anger, and a bribe in the cloak, strong wrath.

20:21:15.text: It is joy to the righteous to do justice; but it is a destruction to the workers of iniquity.

20:21:16.text: The man who wanders out of the way of understanding shall rest in the assembly of the departed spirits.

20:21:17.text: He who loves pleasure will be a poor man. He who loves wine and oil won’t be rich.

20:21:18.text: The wicked is a ransom for the righteous, the treacherous for the upright.

20:21:19.text: It is better to dwell in a desert land, than with a contentious and fretful woman.

20:21:2.text: Every way of a man is right in his own eyes, but the LORD weighs the hearts.

20:21:20.text: There is precious treasure and oil in the dwelling of the wise, but a foolish man swallows it up.

20:21:21.text: He who follows after righteousness and kindness finds life, righteousness, and honour.

20:21:22.text: A wise man scales the city of the mighty, and brings down the strength of its confidence.

20:21:23.text: Whoever guards his mouth and his tongue keeps his soul from troubles.

20:21:24.text: The proud and arrogant man — “Scoffer” is his name — he works in the arrogance of pride.

20:21:25.text: The desire of the sluggard kills him, for his hands refuse to labour.

20:21:26.text: There are those who covet greedily all day long; but the righteous give and don’t withhold.

20:21:27.text: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination — how much more, when he brings it with a wicked mind!

20:21:28.text: A false witness will perish. A man who listens speaks to eternity.

20:21:29.text: A wicked man hardens his face; but as for the upright, he establishes his ways.

20:21:3.text: To do righteousness and justice is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice.

20:21:30.text: There is no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against the LORD.

20:21:31.text: The horse is prepared for the day of battle; but victory is with the LORD.

20:21:4.text: A high look and a proud heart, the lamp of the wicked, is sin.

20:21:5.text: The plans of the diligent surely lead to profit; and everyone who is hasty surely rushes to poverty.

20:21:6.text: Getting treasures by a lying tongue is a fleeting vapour for those who seek death.

20:21:7.text: The violence of the wicked will drive them away, because they refuse to do what is right.

20:21:8.text: The way of the guilty is devious, but the conduct of the innocent is upright.

20:21:9.text: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop than to share a house with a contentious woman.

20:22:1.text: A good name is more desirable than great riches, and loving favour is better than silver and gold.

20:22:10.text: Drive out the mocker, and strife will go out; yes, quarrels and insults will stop.

20:22:11.text: He who loves purity of heart and speaks gracefully is the king’s friend.

20:22:12.text: The LORD’s eyes watch over knowledge, but he frustrates the words of the unfaithful.

20:22:13.text: The sluggard says, “There is a lion outside! I will be killed in the streets!”

20:22:14.text: The mouth of an adulteress is a deep pit. He who is under the LORD’s wrath will fall into it.

20:22:15.text: Folly is bound up in the heart of a child; the rod of discipline drives it far from him.

20:22:16.text: Whoever oppresses the poor for his own increase and whoever gives to the rich, both come to poverty.

20:22:17.text: Turn your ear, and listen to the words of the wise. Apply your heart to my teaching.

20:22:18.text: For it is a pleasant thing if you keep them within you, if all of them are ready on your lips.

20:22:19.text: I teach you today, even you, so that your trust may be in the LORD.

20:22:2.text: The rich and the poor have this in common: The LORD is the maker of them all.

20:22:20.text: Haven’t I written to you thirty excellent things of counsel and knowledge,

20:22:21.text: To teach you truth, reliable words, to give sound answers to the ones who sent you?

20:22:22.text: Don’t exploit the poor because he is poor; and don’t crush the needy in court;

20:22:23.text: for the LORD will plead their case, and plunder the life of those who plunder them.

20:22:24.text: Don’t befriend a hot-tempered man. Don’t associate with one who harbours anger,

20:22:25.text: lest you learn his ways and ensnare your soul.

20:22:26.text: Don’t you be one of those who strike hands, of those who are collateral for debts.

20:22:27.text: If you don’t have means to pay, why should he take away your bed from under you?

20:22:28.text: Don’t move the ancient boundary stone which your fathers have set up.

20:22:29.text: Do you see a man skilled in his work? He will serve kings. He won’t serve obscure men.

20:22:3.text: A prudent man sees danger and hides himself; but the simple pass on, and suffer for it.

20:22:4.text: The result of humility and the fear of the LORD is wealth, honour, and life.

20:22:5.text: Thorns and snares are in the path of the wicked; whoever guards his soul stays far from them.

20:22:6.text: Train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old he will not depart from it.

20:22:7.text: The rich rule over the poor. The borrower is servant to the lender.

20:22:8.text: He who sows wickedness reaps trouble, and the rod of his fury will be destroyed.

20:22:9.text: He who has a generous eye will be blessed, for he shares his food with the poor.

20:23:1.text: When you sit to eat with a ruler, consider diligently what is before you;

20:23:10.text: Don’t move the ancient boundary stone. Don’t encroach on the fields of the fatherless,

20:23:11.text: for their Defender is strong. He will plead their case against you.

20:23:12.text: Apply your heart to instruction, and your ears to the words of knowledge.

20:23:13.text: Don’t withhold correction from a child. If you punish him with the rod, he will not die.

20:23:14.text: Punish him with the rod, and save his soul from Sheol.

20:23:15.text: My son, if your heart is wise, then my heart will be glad, even mine.

20:23:16.text: Yes, my heart will rejoice when your lips speak what is right.

20:23:17.text: Don’t let your heart envy sinners, but rather fear the LORD all day long.

20:23:18.text: Indeed surely there is a future hope, and your hope will not be cut off.

20:23:19.text: Listen, my son, and be wise, and keep your heart on the right path!

20:23:2.text: put a knife to your throat if you are a man given to appetite.

20:23:20.text: Don’t be amongst ones drinking too much wine, or those who gorge themselves on meat;

20:23:21.text: for the drunkard and the glutton shall become poor; and drowsiness clothes them in rags.

20:23:22.text: Listen to your father who gave you life, and don’t despise your mother when she is old.

20:23:23.text: Buy the truth, and don’t sell it. Get wisdom, discipline, and understanding.

20:23:24.text: The father of the righteous has great joy. Whoever fathers a wise child delights in him.

20:23:25.text: Let your father and your mother be glad! Let her who bore you rejoice!

20:23:26.text: My son, give me your heart; and let your eyes keep in my ways.

20:23:27.text: For a prostitute is a deep pit; and a wayward wife is a narrow well.

20:23:28.text: Yes, she lies in wait like a robber, and increases the unfaithful amongst men.

20:23:29.text: Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has strife? Who has complaints? Who has needless bruises? Who has bloodshot eyes?

20:23:3.text: Don’t be desirous of his dainties, since they are deceitful food.

20:23:30.text: Those who stay long at the wine; those who go to seek out mixed wine.

20:23:31.text: Don’t look at the wine when it is red, when it sparkles in the cup, when it goes down smoothly.

20:23:32.text: In the end, it bites like a snake, and poisons like a viper.

20:23:33.text: Your eyes will see strange things, and your mind will imagine confusing things.

20:23:34.text: Yes, you will be as he who lies down in the middle of the sea, or as he who lies on top of the rigging:

20:23:35.text: “They hit me, and I was not hurt! They beat me, and I don’t feel it! When will I wake up? I can do it again. I will look for more.”

20:23:4.text: Don’t weary yourself to be rich. In your wisdom, show restraint.

20:23:5.text: Why do you set your eyes on that which is not? For it certainly sprouts wings like an eagle and flies in the sky.

20:23:6.text: Don’t eat the food of him who has a stingy eye, and don’t crave his delicacies,

20:23:7.text: for as he thinks about the cost, so he is. “Eat and drink!” he says to you, but his heart is not with you.

20:23:8.text: You will vomit up the morsel which you have eaten and waste your pleasant words.

20:23:9.text: Don’t speak in the ears of a fool, for he will despise the wisdom of your words.

20:24:1.text: Don’t be envious of evil men, neither desire to be with them;

20:24:10.text: If you falter in the time of trouble, your strength is small.

20:24:11.text: Rescue those who are being led away to death! Indeed, hold back those who are staggering to the slaughter!

20:24:12.text: If you say, “Behold, we didn’t know this,” doesn’t he who weighs the hearts consider it? He who keeps your soul, doesn’t he know it? Shall he not give to every man according to his work?

20:24:13.text: My son, eat honey, for it is good, the droppings of the honeycomb, which are sweet to your taste;

20:24:14.text: so you shall know wisdom to be to your soul. If you have found it, then there will be a reward: Your hope will not be cut off.

20:24:15.text: Don’t lay in wait, wicked man, against the habitation of the righteous. Don’t destroy his resting place;

20:24:16.text: for a righteous man falls seven times and rises up again, but the wicked are overthrown by calamity.

20:24:17.text: Don’t rejoice when your enemy falls. Don’t let your heart be glad when he is overthrown,

20:24:18.text: lest the LORD see it, and it displease him, and he turn away his wrath from him.

20:24:19.text: Don’t fret yourself because of evildoers, neither be envious of the wicked;

20:24:2.text: for their hearts plot violence and their lips talk about mischief.

20:24:20.text: for there will be no reward to the evil man. The lamp of the wicked will be snuffed out.

20:24:21.text: My son, fear the LORD and the king. Don’t join those who are rebellious,

20:24:22.text: for their calamity will rise suddenly. Who knows what destruction may come from them both?

20:24:23.text: These also are sayings of the wise: To show partiality in judgement is not good.

20:24:24.text: He who says to the wicked, “You are righteous,” peoples will curse him, and nations will abhor him —

20:24:25.text: but it will go well with those who convict the guilty, and a rich blessing will come on them.

20:24:26.text: An honest answer is like a kiss on the lips.

20:24:27.text: Prepare your work outside, and get your fields ready. Afterwards, build your house.

20:24:28.text: Don’t be a witness against your neighbour without cause. Don’t deceive with your lips.

20:24:29.text: Don’t say, “I will do to him as he has done to me; I will repay the man according to his work.”

20:24:3.text: Through wisdom a house is built; by understanding it is established;

20:24:30.text: I went by the field of the sluggard, by the vineyard of the man void of understanding.

20:24:31.text: Behold, it was all grown over with thorns. Its surface was covered with nettles, and its stone wall was broken down.

20:24:32.text: Then I saw, and considered well. I saw, and received instruction:

20:24:33.text: a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep,

20:24:34.text: so your poverty will come as a robber and your want as an armed man.

20:24:4.text: by knowledge the rooms are filled with all rare and beautiful treasure.

20:24:5.text: A wise man has great power. A knowledgeable man increases strength,

20:24:6.text: for by wise guidance you wage your war, and victory is in many advisors.

20:24:7.text: Wisdom is too high for a fool. He doesn’t open his mouth in the gate.

20:24:8.text: One who plots to do evil will be called a schemer.

20:24:9.text: The schemes of folly are sin. The mocker is detested by men.

20:2:1.text: My son, if you will receive my words, and store up my commandments within you,

20:2:10.text: For wisdom will enter into your heart. Knowledge will be pleasant to your soul.

20:2:11.text: Discretion will watch over you. Understanding will keep you,

20:2:12.text: to deliver you from the way of evil, from the men who speak perverse things,

20:2:13.text: who forsake the paths of uprightness, to walk in the ways of darkness,

20:2:14.text: who rejoice to do evil, and delight in the perverseness of evil,

20:2:15.text: who are crooked in their ways, and wayward in their paths,

20:2:16.text: to deliver you from the strange woman, even from the foreigner who flatters with her words,

20:2:17.text: who forsakes the friend of her youth, and forgets the covenant of her God;

20:2:18.text: for her house leads down to death, her paths to the departed spirits.

20:2:19.text: None who go to her return again, neither do they attain to the paths of life.

20:2:2.text: so as to turn your ear to wisdom, and apply your heart to understanding;

20:2:20.text: Therefore walk in the way of good men, and keep the paths of the righteous.

20:2:21.text: For the upright will dwell in the land. The perfect will remain in it.

20:2:22.text: But the wicked will be cut off from the land. The treacherous will be rooted out of it.

20:2:3.text: yes, if you call out for discernment, and lift up your voice for understanding;

20:2:4.text: if you seek her as silver, and search for her as for hidden treasures;

20:2:5.text: then you will understand the fear of the LORD, and find the knowledge of God.

20:2:6.text: For the LORD gives wisdom. Out of his mouth comes knowledge and understanding.

20:2:7.text: He lays up sound wisdom for the upright. He is a shield to those who walk in integrity,

20:2:8.text: that he may guard the paths of justice, and preserve the way of his saints.

20:2:9.text: Then you will understand righteousness and justice, equity and every good path.

20:31:1.text: The words of King Lemuel — the revelation which his mother taught him:

20:31:10.text: Who can find a worthy woman? For her value is far above rubies.

20:31:11.text: The heart of her husband trusts in her. He shall have no lack of gain.

20:31:12.text: She does him good, and not harm, all the days of her life.

20:31:13.text: She seeks wool and flax, and works eagerly with her hands.

20:31:14.text: She is like the merchant ships. She brings her bread from afar.

20:31:15.text: She rises also while it is yet night, gives food to her household, and portions for her servant girls.

20:31:16.text: She considers a field, and buys it. With the fruit of her hands, she plants a vineyard.

20:31:17.text: She arms her waist with strength, and makes her arms strong.

20:31:18.text: She perceives that her merchandise is profitable. Her lamp doesn’t go out by night.

20:31:19.text: She lays her hands to the distaff, and her hands hold the spindle.

20:31:2.text: “Oh, my son! Oh, son of my womb! Oh, son of my vows!

20:31:20.text: She opens her arms to the poor; yes, she extends her hands to the needy.

20:31:21.text: She is not afraid of the snow for her household, for all her household are clothed with scarlet.

20:31:22.text: She makes for herself carpets of tapestry. Her clothing is fine linen and purple.

20:31:23.text: Her husband is respected in the gates, when he sits amongst the elders of the land.

20:31:24.text: She makes linen garments and sells them, and delivers sashes to the merchant.

20:31:25.text: Strength and dignity are her clothing. She laughs at the time to come.

20:31:26.text: She opens her mouth with wisdom. Kind instruction is on her tongue.

20:31:27.text: She looks well to the ways of her household, and doesn’t eat the bread of idleness.

20:31:28.text: Her children rise up and call her blessed. Her husband also praises her:

20:31:29.text: “Many women do noble things, but you excel them all.”

20:31:3.text: Don’t give your strength to women, nor your ways to that which destroys kings.

20:31:30.text: Charm is deceitful, and beauty is vain; but a woman who fears the LORD, she shall be praised.

20:31:31.text: Give her of the fruit of her hands! Let her works praise her in the gates!

20:31:4.text: It is not for kings, Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine, nor for princes to say, ‘Where is strong drink?’

20:31:5.text: lest they drink, and forget the law, and pervert the justice due to anyone who is afflicted.

20:31:6.text: Give strong drink to him who is ready to perish, and wine to the bitter in soul.

20:31:7.text: Let him drink, and forget his poverty, and remember his misery no more.

20:31:8.text: Open your mouth for the mute, in the cause of all who are left desolate.

20:31:9.text: Open your mouth, judge righteously, and serve justice to the poor and needy.”

20:3:1.text: My son, don’t forget my teaching, but let your heart keep my commandments,

20:3:10.text: so your barns will be filled with plenty, and your vats will overflow with new wine.

20:3:11.text: My son, don’t despise the LORD’s discipline, neither be weary of his correction;

20:3:12.text: for whom the LORD loves, he corrects, even as a father reproves the son in whom he delights.

20:3:13.text: Happy is the man who finds wisdom, the man who gets understanding.

20:3:14.text: For her good profit is better than getting silver, and her return is better than fine gold.

20:3:15.text: She is more precious than rubies. None of the things you can desire are to be compared to her.

20:3:16.text: Length of days is in her right hand. In her left hand are riches and honour.

20:3:17.text: Her ways are ways of pleasantness. All her paths are peace.

20:3:18.text: She is a tree of life to those who lay hold of her. Happy is everyone who retains her.

20:3:19.text: By wisdom the LORD founded the earth. By understanding, he established the heavens.

20:3:2.text: for they will add to you length of days, years of life, and peace.

20:3:20.text: By his knowledge, the depths were broken up, and the skies drop down the dew.

20:3:21.text: My son, let them not depart from your eyes. Keep sound wisdom and discretion,

20:3:22.text: so they will be life to your soul, and grace for your neck.

20:3:23.text: Then you shall walk in your way securely. Your foot won’t stumble.

20:3:24.text: When you lie down, you will not be afraid. Yes, you will lie down, and your sleep will be sweet.

20:3:25.text: Don’t be afraid of sudden fear, neither of the desolation of the wicked, when it comes;

20:3:26.text: for the LORD will be your confidence, and will keep your foot from being taken.

20:3:27.text: Don’t withhold good from those to whom it is due, when it is in the power of your hand to do it.

20:3:28.text: Don’t say to your neighbour, “Go, and come again; tomorrow I will give it to you,” when you have it by you.

20:3:29.text: Don’t devise evil against your neighbour, since he dwells securely by you.

20:3:3.text: Don’t let kindness and truth forsake you. Bind them around your neck. Write them on the tablet of your heart.

20:3:30.text: Don’t strive with a man without cause, if he has done you no harm.

20:3:31.text: Don’t envy the man of violence. Choose none of his ways.

20:3:32.text: For the perverse is an abomination to the LORD, but his friendship is with the upright.

20:3:33.text: The LORD’s curse is in the house of the wicked, but he blesses the habitation of the righteous.

20:3:34.text: Surely he mocks the mockers, but he gives grace to the humble.

20:3:35.text: The wise will inherit glory, but shame will be the promotion of fools.

20:3:4.text: So you will find favour, and good understanding in the sight of God and man.

20:3:5.text: Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and don’t lean on your own understanding.

20:3:6.text: In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make your paths straight.

20:3:7.text: Don’t be wise in your own eyes. Fear the LORD, and depart from evil.

20:3:8.text: It will be health to your body, and nourishment to your bones.

20:3:9.text: Honour the LORD with your substance, with the first fruits of all your increase;

20:4:1.text: Listen, sons, to a father’s instruction. Pay attention and know understanding;

20:4:10.text: Listen, my son, and receive my sayings. The years of your life will be many.

20:4:11.text: I have taught you in the way of wisdom. I have led you in straight paths.

20:4:12.text: When you go, your steps will not be hampered. When you run, you will not stumble.

20:4:13.text: Take firm hold of instruction. Don’t let her go. Keep her, for she is your life.

20:4:14.text: Don’t enter into the path of the wicked. Don’t walk in the way of evil men.

20:4:15.text: Avoid it, and don’t pass by it. Turn from it, and pass on.

20:4:16.text: For they don’t sleep unless they do evil. Their sleep is taken away, unless they make someone fall.

20:4:17.text: For they eat the bread of wickedness and drink the wine of violence.

20:4:18.text: But the path of the righteous is like the dawning light that shines more and more until the perfect day.

20:4:19.text: The way of the wicked is like darkness. They don’t know what they stumble over.

20:4:2.text: for I give you sound learning. Don’t forsake my law.

20:4:20.text: My son, attend to my words. Turn your ear to my sayings.

20:4:21.text: Let them not depart from your eyes. Keep them in the centre of your heart.

20:4:22.text: For they are life to those who find them, and health to their whole body.

20:4:23.text: Keep your heart with all diligence, for out of it is the wellspring of life.

20:4:24.text: Put away from yourself a perverse mouth. Put corrupt lips far from you.

20:4:25.text: Let your eyes look straight ahead. Fix your gaze directly before you.

20:4:26.text: Make the path of your feet level. Let all of your ways be established.

20:4:27.text: Don’t turn to the right hand nor to the left. Remove your foot from evil.

20:4:3.text: For I was a son to my father, tender and an only child in the sight of my mother.

20:4:4.text: He taught me, and said to me: “Let your heart retain my words. Keep my commandments, and live.

20:4:5.text: Get wisdom. Get understanding. Don’t forget, and don’t deviate from the words of my mouth.

20:4:6.text: Don’t forsake her, and she will preserve you. Love her, and she will keep you.

20:4:7.text: Wisdom is supreme. Get wisdom. Yes, though it costs all your possessions, get understanding.

20:4:8.text: Esteem her, and she will exalt you. She will bring you to honour when you embrace her.

20:4:9.text: She will give to your head a garland of grace. She will deliver a crown of splendour to you.”

20:5:1.text: My son, pay attention to my wisdom. Turn your ear to my understanding,

20:5:10.text: lest strangers feast on your wealth, and your labours enrich another man’s house.

20:5:11.text: You will groan at your latter end, when your flesh and your body are consumed,

20:5:12.text: and say, “How I have hated instruction, and my heart despised reproof.

20:5:13.text: I haven’t obeyed the voice of my teachers, nor turned my ear to those who instructed me!

20:5:14.text: I have come to the brink of utter ruin, amongst the gathered assembly.”

20:5:15.text: Drink water out of your own cistern, running water out of your own well.

20:5:16.text: Should your springs overflow in the streets, streams of water in the public squares?

20:5:17.text: Let them be for yourself alone, not for strangers with you.

20:5:18.text: Let your spring be blessed. Rejoice in the wife of your youth.

20:5:19.text: A loving doe and a graceful deer — let her breasts satisfy you at all times. Be captivated always with her love.

20:5:2.text: that you may maintain discretion, that your lips may preserve knowledge.

20:5:20.text: For why should you, my son, be captivated with an adulteress? Why embrace the bosom of another?

20:5:21.text: For the ways of man are before the LORD’s eyes. He examines all his paths.

20:5:22.text: The evil deeds of the wicked ensnare him. The cords of his sin hold him firmly.

20:5:23.text: He will die for lack of instruction. In the greatness of his folly, he will go astray.

20:5:3.text: For the lips of an adulteress drip honey. Her mouth is smoother than oil,

20:5:4.text: but in the end she is as bitter as wormwood, and as sharp as a two-edged sword.

20:5:5.text: Her feet go down to death. Her steps lead straight to Sheol.

20:5:6.text: She gives no thought to the way of life. Her ways are crooked, and she doesn’t know it.

20:5:7.text: Now therefore, my sons, listen to me. Don’t depart from the words of my mouth.

20:5:8.text: Remove your way far from her. Don’t come near the door of her house,

20:5:9.text: lest you give your honour to others, and your years to the cruel one;

20:6:1.text: My son, if you have become collateral for your neighbour, if you have struck your hands in pledge for a stranger,

20:6:10.text: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep —

20:6:11.text: so your poverty will come as a robber, and your scarcity as an armed man.

20:6:12.text: A worthless person, a man of iniquity, is he who walks with a perverse mouth,

20:6:13.text: who winks with his eyes, who signals with his feet, who motions with his fingers,

20:6:14.text: in whose heart is perverseness, who devises evil continually, who always sows discord.

20:6:15.text: Therefore his calamity will come suddenly. He will be broken suddenly, and that without remedy.

20:6:16.text: There are six things which the LORD hates; yes, seven which are an abomination to him:

20:6:17.text: arrogant eyes, a lying tongue, hands that shed innocent blood,

20:6:18.text: a heart that devises wicked schemes, feet that are swift in running to mischief,

20:6:19.text: a false witness who utters lies, and he who sows discord amongst brothers.

20:6:2.text: you are trapped by the words of your mouth; you are ensnared with the words of your mouth.

20:6:20.text: My son, keep your father’s commandment, and don’t forsake your mother’s teaching.

20:6:21.text: Bind them continually on your heart. Tie them around your neck.

20:6:22.text: When you walk, it will lead you. When you sleep, it will watch over you. When you awake, it will talk with you.

20:6:23.text: For the commandment is a lamp, and the law is light. Reproofs of instruction are the way of life,

20:6:24.text: to keep you from the immoral woman, from the flattery of the wayward wife’s tongue.

20:6:25.text: Don’t lust after her beauty in your heart, neither let her captivate you with her eyelids.

20:6:26.text: For a prostitute reduces you to a piece of bread. The adulteress hunts for your precious life.

20:6:27.text: Can a man scoop fire into his lap, and his clothes not be burnt?

20:6:28.text: Or can one walk on hot coals, and his feet not be scorched?

20:6:29.text: So is he who goes in to his neighbour’s wife. Whoever touches her will not be unpunished.

20:6:3.text: Do this now, my son, and deliver yourself, since you have come into the hand of your neighbour. Go, humble yourself. Press your plea with your neighbour.

20:6:30.text: Men don’t despise a thief if he steals to satisfy himself when he is hungry,

20:6:31.text: but if he is found, he shall restore seven times. He shall give all the wealth of his house.

20:6:32.text: He who commits adultery with a woman is void of understanding. He who does it destroys his own soul.

20:6:33.text: He will get wounds and dishonour. His reproach will not be wiped away.

20:6:34.text: For jealousy arouses the fury of the husband. He won’t spare in the day of vengeance.

20:6:35.text: He won’t regard any ransom, neither will he rest content, though you give many gifts.

20:6:4.text: Give no sleep to your eyes, nor slumber to your eyelids.

20:6:5.text: Free yourself, like a gazelle from the hand of the hunter, like a bird from the snare of the fowler.

20:6:6.text: Go to the ant, you sluggard. Consider her ways, and be wise;

20:6:7.text: which having no chief, overseer, or ruler,

20:6:8.text: provides her bread in the summer, and gathers her food in the harvest.

20:6:9.text: How long will you sleep, sluggard? When will you arise out of your sleep?

20:7:1.text: My son, keep my words. Lay up my commandments within you.

20:7:10.text: Behold, there a woman met him with the attire of a prostitute, and with crafty intent.

20:7:11.text: She is loud and defiant. Her feet don’t stay in her house.

20:7:12.text: Now she is in the streets, now in the squares, and lurking at every corner.

20:7:13.text: So she caught him, and kissed him. With an impudent face she said to him:

20:7:14.text: “Sacrifices of peace offerings are with me. Today I have paid my vows.

20:7:15.text: Therefore I came out to meet you, to diligently seek your face, and I have found you.

20:7:16.text: I have spread my couch with carpets of tapestry, with striped cloths of the yarn of Egypt.

20:7:17.text: I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.

20:7:18.text: Come, let’s take our fill of loving until the morning. Let’s solace ourselves with loving.

20:7:19.text: For my husband isn’t at home. He has gone on a long journey.

20:7:2.text: Keep my commandments and live! Guard my teaching as the apple of your eye.

20:7:20.text: He has taken a bag of money with him. He will come home at the full moon.”

20:7:21.text: With persuasive words, she led him astray. With the flattering of her lips, she seduced him.

20:7:22.text: He followed her immediately, as an ox goes to the slaughter, as a fool stepping into a noose.

20:7:23.text: Until an arrow strikes through his liver, as a bird hurries to the snare, and doesn’t know that it will cost his life.

20:7:24.text: Now therefore, sons, listen to me. Pay attention to the words of my mouth.

20:7:25.text: Don’t let your heart turn to her ways. Don’t go astray in her paths,

20:7:26.text: for she has thrown down many wounded. Yes, all her slain are a mighty army.

20:7:27.text: Her house is the way to Sheol, going down to the rooms of death.

20:7:3.text: Bind them on your fingers. Write them on the tablet of your heart.

20:7:4.text: Tell wisdom, “You are my sister.” Call understanding your relative,

20:7:5.text: that they may keep you from the strange woman, from the foreigner who flatters with her words.

20:7:6.text: For at the window of my house, I looked out through my lattice.

20:7:7.text: I saw amongst the simple ones. I discerned amongst the youths a young man void of understanding,

20:7:8.text: passing through the street near her corner, he went the way to her house,

20:7:9.text: in the twilight, in the evening of the day, in the middle of the night and in the darkness.

20:8:1.text: Doesn’t wisdom cry out? Doesn’t understanding raise her voice?

20:8:10.text: Receive my instruction rather than silver, knowledge rather than choice gold.

20:8:11.text: For wisdom is better than rubies. All the things that may be desired can’t be compared to it.

20:8:12.text: “I, wisdom, have made prudence my dwelling. Find out knowledge and discretion.

20:8:13.text: The fear of the LORD is to hate evil. I hate pride, arrogance, the evil way, and the perverse mouth.

20:8:14.text: Counsel and sound knowledge are mine. I have understanding and power.

20:8:15.text: By me kings reign, and princes decree justice.

20:8:16.text: By me princes rule, nobles, and all the righteous rulers of the earth.

20:8:17.text: I love those who love me. Those who seek me diligently will find me.

20:8:18.text: With me are riches, honour, enduring wealth, and prosperity.

20:8:19.text: My fruit is better than gold, yes, than fine gold, my yield than choice silver.

20:8:2.text: On the top of high places by the way, where the paths meet, she stands.

20:8:20.text: I walk in the way of righteousness, in the middle of the paths of justice,

20:8:21.text: that I may give wealth to those who love me. I fill their treasuries.

20:8:22.text: “The LORD possessed me in the beginning of his work, before his deeds of old.

20:8:23.text: I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, before the earth existed.

20:8:24.text: When there were no depths, I was born, when there were no springs abounding with water.

20:8:25.text: Before the mountains were settled in place, before the hills, I was born;

20:8:26.text: while as yet he had not made the earth, nor the fields, nor the beginning of the dust of the world.

20:8:27.text: When he established the heavens, I was there. When he set a circle on the surface of the deep,

20:8:28.text: when he established the clouds above, when the springs of the deep became strong,

20:8:29.text: when he gave to the sea its boundary, that the waters should not violate his commandment, when he marked out the foundations of the earth,

20:8:3.text: Beside the gates, at the entry of the city, at the entry doors, she cries aloud:

20:8:30.text: then I was the craftsman by his side. I was a delight day by day, always rejoicing before him,

20:8:31.text: rejoicing in his whole world. My delight was with the sons of men.

20:8:32.text: “Now therefore, my sons, listen to me, for blessed are those who keep my ways.

20:8:33.text: Hear instruction, and be wise. Don’t refuse it.

20:8:34.text: Blessed is the man who hears me, watching daily at my gates, waiting at my door posts.

20:8:35.text: For whoever finds me finds life, and will obtain favour from the LORD.

20:8:36.text: But he who sins against me wrongs his own soul. All those who hate me love death.”

20:8:4.text: “I call to you men! I send my voice to the sons of mankind.

20:8:5.text: You simple, understand prudence! You fools, be of an understanding heart!

20:8:6.text: Hear, for I will speak excellent things. The opening of my lips is for right things.

20:8:7.text: For my mouth speaks truth. Wickedness is an abomination to my lips.

20:8:8.text: All the words of my mouth are in righteousness. There is nothing crooked or perverse in them.

20:8:9.text: They are all plain to him who understands, right to those who find knowledge.

20:9:1.text: Wisdom has built her house. She has carved out her seven pillars.

20:9:10.text: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom. The knowledge of the Holy One is understanding.

20:9:11.text: For by me your days will be multiplied. The years of your life will be increased.

20:9:12.text: If you are wise, you are wise for yourself. If you mock, you alone will bear it.

20:9:13.text: The foolish woman is loud, undisciplined, and knows nothing.

20:9:14.text: She sits at the door of her house, on a seat in the high places of the city,

20:9:15.text: to call to those who pass by, who go straight on their ways,

20:9:16.text: “Whoever is simple, let him turn in here.” As for him who is void of understanding, she says to him,

20:9:17.text: “Stolen water is sweet. Food eaten in secret is pleasant.”

20:9:18.text: But he doesn’t know that the departed spirits are there, that her guests are in the depths of Sheol.

20:9:2.text: She has prepared her meat. She has mixed her wine. She has also set her table.

20:9:3.text: She has sent out her maidens. She cries from the highest places of the city:

20:9:4.text: “Whoever is simple, let him turn in here!” As for him who is void of understanding, she says to him,

20:9:5.text: “Come, eat some of my bread, Drink some of the wine which I have mixed!

20:9:6.text: Leave your simple ways, and live. Walk in the way of understanding.”

20:9:7.text: One who corrects a mocker invites insult. One who reproves a wicked man invites abuse.

20:9:8.text: Don’t reprove a scoffer, lest he hate you. Reprove a wise person, and he will love you.

20:9:9.text: Instruct a wise person, and he will be still wiser. Teach a righteous person, and he will increase in learning.

23:10:1.text: Woe to those who decree unrighteous decrees, and to the writers who write oppressive decrees

23:10:10.text: As my hand has found the kingdoms of the idols, whose engraved images exceeded those of Jerusalem and of Samaria,

23:10:11.text: shall I not, as I have done to Samaria and her idols, so do to Jerusalem and her idols?

23:10:12.text: Therefore it will happen that when the Lord has performed his whole work on Mount Zion and on Jerusalem, I will punish the fruit of the wilful proud heart of the king of Assyria, and the insolence of his arrogant looks.

23:10:13.text: For he has said, “By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom, for I have understanding. I have removed the boundaries of the peoples, and have robbed their treasures. Like a valiant man I have brought down their rulers.

23:10:14.text: My hand has found the riches of the peoples like a nest, and like one gathers eggs that are abandoned, I have gathered all the earth. There was no one who moved their wing, or that opened their mouth, or chirped.”

23:10:15.text: Should an axe brag against him who chops with it? Should a saw exalt itself above him who saws with it? As if a rod should lift those who lift it up, or as if a staff should lift up someone who is not wood.

23:10:16.text: Therefore the Lord, GOD of Armies, will send amongst his fat ones leanness; and under his glory a burning will be kindled like the burning of fire.

23:10:17.text: The light of Israel will be for a fire, and his Holy One for a flame; and it will burn and devour his thorns and his briers in one day.

23:10:18.text: He will consume the glory of his forest and of his fruitful field, both soul and body. It will be as when a standard bearer faints.

23:10:19.text: The remnant of the trees of his forest shall be few, so that a child could write their number.

23:10:2.text: to deprive the needy of justice, and to rob the poor amongst my people of their rights, that widows may be their plunder, and that they may make the fatherless their prey!

23:10:20.text: It will come to pass in that day that the remnant of Israel, and those who have escaped from the house of Jacob will no more again lean on him who struck them, but shall lean on the LORD, the Holy One of Israel, in truth.

23:10:21.text: A remnant will return, even the remnant of Jacob, to the mighty God.

23:10:22.text: For though your people, Israel, are like the sand of the sea, only a remnant of them will return. A destruction is determined, overflowing with righteousness.

23:10:23.text: For the Lord, GOD of Armies, will make a full end, and that determined, throughout all the earth.

23:10:24.text: Therefore the Lord, GOD of Armies, says, “My people who dwell in Zion, don’t be afraid of the Assyrian, though he strike you with the rod, and lift up his staff against you, as Egypt did.

23:10:25.text: For yet a very little while, and the indignation against you will be accomplished, and my anger will be directed to his destruction.”

23:10:26.text: The LORD of Armies will stir up a scourge against him, as in the slaughter of Midian at the rock of Oreb. His rod will be over the sea, and he will lift it up like he did against Egypt.

23:10:27.text: It will happen in that day that his burden will depart from off your shoulder, and his yoke from off your neck, and the yoke shall be destroyed because of the anointing oil.

23:10:28.text: He has come to Aiath. He has passed through Migron. At Michmash he stores his baggage.

23:10:29.text: They have gone over the pass. They have taken up their lodging at Geba. Ramah trembles. Gibeah of Saul has fled.

23:10:3.text: What will you do in the day of visitation, and in the desolation which will come from afar? To whom will you flee for help? Where will you leave your wealth?

23:10:30.text: Cry aloud with your voice, daughter of Gallim! Listen, Laishah! You poor Anathoth!

23:10:31.text: Madmenah is a fugitive. The inhabitants of Gebim flee for safety.

23:10:32.text: This very day he will halt at Nob. He shakes his hand at the mountain of the daughter of Zion, the hill of Jerusalem.

23:10:33.text: Behold, the Lord, GOD of Armies, will lop the boughs with terror. The tall will be cut down, and the lofty will be brought low.

23:10:34.text: He will cut down the thickets of the forest with iron, and Lebanon will fall by the Mighty One.

23:10:4.text: They will only bow down under the prisoners, and will fall under the slain. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.

23:10:5.text: Alas Assyrian, the rod of my anger, the staff in whose hand is my indignation!

23:10:6.text: I will send him against a profane nation, and against the people who anger me I will give him a command to take the plunder and to take the prey, and to tread them down like the mire of the streets.

23:10:7.text: However, he doesn’t mean so, neither does his heart think so; but it is in his heart to destroy, and to cut off not a few nations.

23:10:8.text: For he says, “Aren’t all of my princes kings?

23:10:9.text: Isn’t Calno like Carchemish? Isn’t Hamath like Arpad? Isn’t Samaria like Damascus?”

23:11:1.text: A shoot will come out of the stock of Jesse, and a branch out of his roots will bear fruit.

23:11:10.text: It will happen in that day that the nations will seek the root of Jesse, who stands as a banner of the peoples; and his resting place will be glorious.

23:11:11.text: It will happen in that day that the Lord will set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant that is left of his people from Assyria, from Egypt, from Pathros, from Cush, from Elam, from Shinar, from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.

23:11:12.text: He will set up a banner for the nations, and will assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.

23:11:13.text: The envy also of Ephraim will depart, and those who persecute Judah will be cut off. Ephraim won’t envy Judah, and Judah won’t persecute Ephraim.

23:11:14.text: They will fly down on the shoulders of the Philistines on the west. Together they will plunder the children of the east. They will extend their power over Edom and Moab, and the children of Ammon will obey them.

23:11:15.text: The LORD will utterly destroy the tongue of the Egyptian sea; and with his scorching wind he will wave his hand over the River, and will split it into seven streams, and cause men to march over in sandals.

23:11:16.text: There will be a highway for the remnant that is left of his people from Assyria, like there was for Israel in the day that he came up out of the land of Egypt.

23:11:2.text: The LORD’s Spirit will rest on him: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the LORD.

23:11:3.text: His delight will be in the fear of the LORD. He will not judge by the sight of his eyes, neither decide by the hearing of his ears;

23:11:4.text: but he will judge the poor with righteousness, and decide with equity for the humble of the earth. He will strike the earth with the rod of his mouth; and with the breath of his lips he will kill the wicked.

23:11:5.text: Righteousness will be the belt around his waist, and faithfulness the belt around his waist.

23:11:6.text: The wolf will live with the lamb, and the leopard will lie down with the young goat, the calf, the young lion, and the fattened calf together; and a little child will lead them.

23:11:7.text: The cow and the bear will graze. Their young ones will lie down together. The lion will eat straw like the ox.

23:11:8.text: The nursing child will play near a cobra’s hole, and the weaned child will put his hand on the viper’s den.

23:11:9.text: They will not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain; for the earth will be full of the knowledge of the LORD, as the waters cover the sea.

23:12:1.text: In that day you will say, “I will give thanks to you, the LORD; for though you were angry with me, your anger has turned away and you comfort me.

23:12:2.text: Behold, God is my salvation. I will trust, and will not be afraid; for the LORD, the LORD, is my strength and song; and he has become my salvation.”

23:12:3.text: Therefore with joy you will draw water out of the wells of salvation.

23:12:4.text: In that day you will say, “Give thanks to the LORD! Call on his name! Declare his doings amongst the peoples! Proclaim that his name is exalted!

23:12:5.text: Sing to the LORD, for he has done excellent things! Let this be known in all the earth!

23:12:6.text: Cry aloud and shout, you inhabitant of Zion, for the Holy One of Israel is great amongst you!”

23:13:1.text: The burden of Babylon, which Isaiah the son of Amoz saw.

23:13:10.text: For the stars of the sky and its constellations will not give their light. The sun will be darkened in its going out, and the moon will not cause its light to shine.

23:13:11.text: I will punish the world for their evil, and the wicked for their iniquity. I will cause the arrogance of the proud to cease, and will humble the arrogance of the terrible.

23:13:12.text: I will make people more rare than fine gold, even a person than the pure gold of Ophir.

23:13:13.text: Therefore I will make the heavens tremble, and the earth will be shaken out of its place in the LORD of Armies’ wrath, and in the day of his fierce anger.

23:13:14.text: It will happen that like a hunted gazelle and like sheep that no one gathers, they will each turn to their own people, and will each flee to their own land.

23:13:15.text: Everyone who is found will be thrust through. Everyone who is captured will fall by the sword.

23:13:16.text: Their infants also will be dashed in pieces before their eyes. Their houses will be ransacked, and their wives raped.

23:13:17.text: Behold, I will stir up the Medes against them, who will not value silver, and as for gold, they will not delight in it.

23:13:18.text: Their bows will dash the young men in pieces; and they shall have no pity on the fruit of the womb. Their eyes will not spare children.

23:13:19.text: Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldeans’ pride, will be like when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.

23:13:2.text: Set up a banner on the bare mountain! Lift up your voice to them! Wave your hand, that they may go into the gates of the nobles.

23:13:20.text: It will never be inhabited, neither will it be lived in from generation to generation. The Arabian will not pitch a tent there, neither will shepherds make their flocks lie down there.

23:13:21.text: But wild animals of the desert will lie there, and their houses will be full of jackals. Ostriches will dwell there, and wild goats will frolic there.

23:13:22.text: Hyenas will cry in their fortresses, and jackals in the pleasant palaces. Her time is near to come, and her days will not be prolonged.

23:13:3.text: I have commanded my consecrated ones; yes, I have called my mighty men for my anger, even my proudly exulting ones.

23:13:4.text: The noise of a multitude is in the mountains, as of a great people; the noise of an uproar of the kingdoms of the nations gathered together! The LORD of Armies is mustering the army for the battle.

23:13:5.text: They come from a far country, from the uttermost part of heaven, even the LORD, and the weapons of his indignation, to destroy the whole land.

23:13:6.text: Wail, for the LORD’s day is at hand! It will come as destruction from the Almighty.

23:13:7.text: Therefore all hands will be feeble, and everyone’s heart will melt.

23:13:8.text: They will be dismayed. Pangs and sorrows will seize them. They will be in pain like a woman in labour. They will look in amazement one at another. Their faces will be faces of flame.

23:13:9.text: Behold, the day of the LORD comes, cruel, with wrath and fierce anger; to make the land a desolation, and to destroy its sinners out of it.

23:14:1.text: For the LORD will have compassion on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land. The foreigner will join himself with them, and they will unite with the house of Jacob.

23:14:10.text: They all will answer and ask you, “Have you also become as weak as we are? Have you become like us?”

23:14:11.text: Your pomp is brought down to Sheol, with the sound of your stringed instruments. Maggots are spread out under you, and worms cover you.

23:14:12.text: How you have fallen from heaven, shining one, son of the dawn! How you are cut down to the ground, who laid the nations low!

23:14:13.text: You said in your heart, “I will ascend into heaven! I will exalt my throne above the stars of God! I will sit on the mountain of assembly, in the far north!

23:14:14.text: I will ascend above the heights of the clouds! I will make myself like the Most High!”

23:14:15.text: Yet you shall be brought down to Sheol, to the depths of the pit.

23:14:16.text: Those who see you will stare at you. They will ponder you, saying, “Is this the man who made the earth to tremble, who shook kingdoms,

23:14:17.text: who made the world like a wilderness, and overthrew its cities, who didn’t release his prisoners to their home?”

23:14:18.text: All the kings of the nations sleep in glory, everyone in his own house.

23:14:19.text: But you are cast away from your tomb like an abominable branch, clothed with the slain who are thrust through with the sword, who go down to the stones of the pit; like a dead body trodden under foot.

23:14:2.text: The peoples will take them, and bring them to their place. The house of Israel will possess them in the LORD’s land for servants and for handmaids. They will take as captives those whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors.

23:14:20.text: You will not join them in burial, because you have destroyed your land. You have killed your people. The offspring of evildoers will not be named forever.

23:14:21.text: Prepare for slaughter of his children because of the iniquity of their fathers, that they not rise up and possess the earth, and fill the surface of the world with cities.

23:14:22.text: “I will rise up against them,” says the LORD of Armies, “and cut off from Babylon name and remnant, and son and son’s son,” says the LORD.

23:14:23.text: “I will also make it a possession for the porcupine, and pools of water. I will sweep it with the broom of destruction,” says the LORD of Armies.

23:14:24.text: The LORD of Armies has sworn, saying, “Surely, as I have thought, so shall it happen; and as I have purposed, so shall it stand:

23:14:25.text: that I will break the Assyrian in my land, and tread him under foot on my mountains. Then his yoke will leave them, and his burden leave their shoulders.

23:14:26.text: This is the plan that is determined for the whole earth. This is the hand that is stretched out over all the nations.

23:14:27.text: For the LORD of Armies has planned, and who can stop it? His hand is stretched out, and who can turn it back?”
