23:14:28.text: This burden was in the year that King Ahaz died.

23:14:29.text: Don’t rejoice, O Philistia, all of you, because the rod that struck you is broken; for out of the serpent’s root an adder will emerge, and his fruit will be a fiery flying serpent.

23:14:3.text: It will happen in the day that the LORD will give you rest from your sorrow, from your trouble, and from the hard service in which you were made to serve,

23:14:30.text: The firstborn of the poor will eat, and the needy will lie down in safety; and I will kill your root with famine, and your remnant will be killed.

23:14:31.text: Howl, gate! Cry, city! You are melted away, Philistia, all of you; for smoke comes out of the north, and there is no straggler in his ranks.

23:14:32.text: What will they answer the messengers of the nation? That the LORD has founded Zion, and in her the afflicted of his people will take refuge.

23:14:4.text: that you will take up this parable against the king of Babylon, and say, “How the oppressor has ceased! The golden city has ceased!”

23:14:5.text: The LORD has broken the staff of the wicked, the sceptre of the rulers,

23:14:6.text: who struck the peoples in wrath with a continual stroke, who ruled the nations in anger, with a persecution that no one restrained.

23:14:7.text: The whole earth is at rest, and is quiet. They break out in song.

23:14:8.text: Yes, the cypress trees rejoice with you, with the cedars of Lebanon, saying, “Since you are humbled, no lumberjack has come up against us.”

23:14:9.text: Sheol from beneath has moved for you to meet you at your coming. It stirs up the departed spirits for you, even all the rulers of the earth. It has raised up from their thrones all the kings of the nations.

23:1:1.text: The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.

23:1:10.text: Hear the LORD’s word, you rulers of Sodom! Listen to the law of our God, you people of Gomorrah!

23:1:11.text: “What are the multitude of your sacrifices to me?”, says the LORD. “I have had enough of the burnt offerings of rams and the fat of fed animals. I don’t delight in the blood of bulls, or of lambs, or of male goats.

23:1:12.text: When you come to appear before me, who has required this at your hand, to trample my courts?

23:1:13.text: Bring no more vain offerings. Incense is an abomination to me. New moons, Sabbaths, and convocations — I can’t stand evil assemblies.

23:1:14.text: My soul hates your New Moons and your appointed feasts. They are a burden to me. I am weary of bearing them.

23:1:15.text: When you spread out your hands, I will hide my eyes from you. Yes, when you make many prayers, I will not hear. Your hands are full of blood.

23:1:16.text: Wash yourselves. Make yourself clean. Put away the evil of your doings from before my eyes. Cease to do evil.

23:1:17.text: Learn to do well. Seek justice. Relieve the oppressed. Defend the fatherless. Plead for the widow.”

23:1:18.text: “Come now, and let’s reason together,” says the LORD: “Though your sins are as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow. Though they are red like crimson, they shall be as wool.

23:1:19.text: If you are willing and obedient, you will eat the good of the land;

23:1:2.text: Hear, heavens, and listen, earth; for the LORD has spoken: “I have nourished and brought up children and they have rebelled against me.

23:1:20.text: but if you refuse and rebel, you will be devoured with the sword; for the LORD’s mouth has spoken it.”

23:1:21.text: How the faithful city has become a prostitute! She was full of justice. Righteousness lodged in her, but now there are murderers.

23:1:22.text: Your silver has become dross, your wine mixed with water.

23:1:23.text: Your princes are rebellious and companions of thieves. Everyone loves bribes and follows after rewards. They don’t defend the fatherless, neither does the cause of the widow come to them.

23:1:24.text: Therefore the Lord, GOD of Armies, the Mighty One of Israel, says: “Ah, I will get relief from my adversaries, and avenge myself on my enemies.

23:1:25.text: I will turn my hand on you, thoroughly purge away your dross, and will take away all your tin.

23:1:26.text: I will restore your judges as at the first, and your counsellors as at the beginning. Afterward you shall be called ‘ The city of righteousness, a faithful town.’

23:1:27.text: Zion shall be redeemed with justice, and her converts with righteousness.

23:1:28.text: But the destruction of transgressors and sinners shall be together, and those who forsake the LORD shall be consumed.

23:1:29.text: For they shall be ashamed of the oaks which you have desired, and you shall be confounded for the gardens that you have chosen.

23:1:3.text: The ox knows his owner, and the donkey his master’s crib; but Israel doesn’t know. My people don’t consider.”

23:1:30.text: For you shall be as an oak whose leaf fades, and as a garden that has no water.

23:1:31.text: The strong will be like tinder, and his work like a spark. They will both burn together, and no one will quench them.”

23:1:4.text: Ah sinful nation, a people loaded with iniquity, offspring of evildoers, children who deal corruptly! They have forsaken the LORD. They have despised the Holy One of Israel. They are estranged and backward.

23:1:5.text: Why should you be beaten more, that you revolt more and more? The whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint.

23:1:6.text: From the sole of the foot even to the head there is no soundness in it, but wounds, welts, and open sores. They haven’t been closed, bandaged, or soothed with oil.

23:1:7.text: Your country is desolate. Your cities are burnt with fire. Strangers devour your land in your presence and it is desolate, as overthrown by strangers.

23:1:8.text: The daughter of Zion is left like a shelter in a vineyard, like a hut in a field of melons, like a besieged city.

23:1:9.text: Unless the LORD of Armies had left to us a very small remnant, we would have been as Sodom. We would have been like Gomorrah.

23:25:1.text: The LORD, you are my God. I will exalt you! I will praise your name, for you have done wonderful things, things planned long ago, in complete faithfulness and truth.

23:25:10.text: For the LORD’s hand will rest in this mountain. Moab will be trodden down in his place, even like straw is trodden down in the water of the dunghill.

23:25:11.text: He will spread out his hands in the middle of it, like one who swims spreads out hands to swim, but his pride will be humbled together with the craft of his hands.

23:25:12.text: He has brought the high fortress of your walls down, laid low, and brought to the ground, even to the dust.

23:25:2.text: For you have made a city into a heap, a fortified city into a ruin, a palace of strangers to be no city. It will never be built.

23:25:3.text: Therefore a strong people will glorify you. A city of awesome nations will fear you.

23:25:4.text: For you have been a stronghold to the poor, a stronghold to the needy in his distress, a refuge from the storm, a shade from the heat, when the blast of the dreaded ones is like a storm against the wall.

23:25:5.text: As the heat in a dry place you will bring down the noise of strangers; as the heat by the shade of a cloud, the song of the dreaded ones will be brought low.

23:25:6.text: In this mountain, the LORD of Armies will make all peoples a feast of choice meat, a feast of choice wines, of choice meat full of marrow, of well refined choice wines.

23:25:7.text: He will destroy in this mountain the surface of the covering that covers all peoples, and the veil that is spread over all nations.

23:25:8.text: He has swallowed up death forever! The Lord GOD will wipe away tears from off all faces. He will take the reproach of his people away from off all the earth, for the LORD has spoken it.

23:25:9.text: It shall be said in that day, “Behold, this is our God! We have waited for him, and he will save us! This is the LORD! We have waited for him. We will be glad and rejoice in his salvation!”

23:26:1.text: In that day, this song will be sung in the land of Judah: “We have a strong city. God appoints salvation for walls and bulwarks.

23:26:10.text: Let favour be shown to the wicked, yet he will not learn righteousness. In the land of uprightness he will deal wrongfully, and will not see the LORD’s majesty.

23:26:11.text: LORD, your hand is lifted up, yet they don’t see; but they will see your zeal for the people and be disappointed. Yes, fire will consume your adversaries.

23:26:12.text: LORD, you will ordain peace for us, for you have also done all our work for us.

23:26:13.text: LORD our God, other lords besides you have had dominion over us, but we will only acknowledge your name.

23:26:14.text: The dead shall not live. The departed spirits shall not rise. Therefore you have visited and destroyed them, and caused all memory of them to perish.

23:26:15.text: You have increased the nation, O LORD. You have increased the nation! You are glorified! You have enlarged all the borders of the land.

23:26:16.text: LORD, in trouble they have visited you. They poured out a prayer when your chastening was on them.

23:26:17.text: Just as a woman with child, who draws near the time of her delivery, is in pain and cries out in her pangs, so we have been before you, LORD.

23:26:18.text: We have been with child. We have been in pain. We gave birth, it seems, only to wind. We have not worked any deliverance in the earth; neither have the inhabitants of the world fallen.

23:26:19.text: Your dead shall live. Their dead bodies shall arise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust; for your dew is like the dew of herbs, and the earth will cast out the departed spirits.

23:26:2.text: Open the gates, that the righteous nation may enter: the one which keeps faith.

23:26:20.text: Come, my people, enter into your rooms, and shut your doors behind you. Hide yourself for a little moment, until the indignation is past.

23:26:21.text: For, behold, the LORD comes out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity. The earth also will disclose her blood, and will no longer cover her slain.

23:26:3.text: You will keep whoever’s mind is steadfast in perfect peace, because he trusts in you.

23:26:4.text: Trust in the LORD forever; for in the LORD, the LORD, is an everlasting Rock.

23:26:5.text: For he has brought down those who dwell on high, the lofty city. He lays it low. He lays it low even to the ground. He brings it even to the dust.

23:26:6.text: The foot shall tread it down, even the feet of the poor and the steps of the needy.”

23:26:7.text: The way of the just is uprightness. You who are upright make the path of the righteous level.

23:26:8.text: Yes, in the way of your judgements, LORD, we have waited for you. Your name and your renown are the desire of our soul.

23:26:9.text: With my soul I have desired you in the night. Yes, with my spirit within me I will seek you earnestly; for when your judgements are in the earth, the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness.

23:27:1.text: In that day, the LORD with his hard and great and strong sword will punish leviathan, the fleeing serpent, and leviathan, the twisted serpent; and he will kill the dragon that is in the sea.

23:27:10.text: For the fortified city is solitary, a habitation deserted and forsaken, like the wilderness. The calf will feed there, and there he will lie down, and consume its branches.

23:27:11.text: When its boughs are withered, they will be broken off. The women will come and set them on fire, for they are a people of no understanding. Therefore he who made them will not have compassion on them, and he who formed them will show them no favour.

23:27:12.text: It will happen in that day that the LORD will thresh from the flowing stream of the Euphrates to the brook of Egypt; and you will be gathered one by one, children of Israel.

23:27:13.text: It will happen in that day that a great trumpet will be blown; and those who were ready to perish in the land of Assyria, and those who were outcasts in the land of Egypt, shall come; and they will worship the LORD in the holy mountain at Jerusalem.

23:27:2.text: In that day, sing to her, “A pleasant vineyard!

23:27:3.text: I, the LORD, am its keeper. I will water it every moment. Lest anyone damage it, I will keep it night and day.

23:27:4.text: Wrath is not in me, but if I should find briers and thorns, I would do battle! I would march on them and I would burn them together.

23:27:5.text: Or else let him take hold of my strength, that he may make peace with me. Let him make peace with me.”

23:27:6.text: In days to come, Jacob will take root. Israel will blossom and bud. They will fill the surface of the world with fruit.

23:27:7.text: Has he struck them as he struck those who struck them? Or are they killed like those who killed them were killed?

23:27:8.text: In measure, when you send them away, you contend with them. He has removed them with his rough blast in the day of the east wind.

23:27:9.text: Therefore by this the iniquity of Jacob will be forgiven, and this is all the fruit of taking away his sin: that he makes all the stones of the altar as chalk stones that are beaten in pieces, so that the Asherah poles and the incense altars shall rise no more.

23:28:1.text: Woe to the crown of pride of the drunkards of Ephraim, and to the fading flower of his glorious beauty, which is on the head of the fertile valley of those who are overcome with wine!

23:28:10.text: For it is precept on precept, precept on precept; line on line, line on line; here a little, there a little.

23:28:11.text: But he will speak to this nation with stammering lips and in another language,

23:28:12.text: to whom he said, “This is the resting place. Give rest to the weary,” and “This is the refreshing;” yet they would not hear.

23:28:13.text: Therefore the LORD’s word will be to them precept on precept, precept on precept; line on line, line on line; here a little, there a little; that they may go, fall backward, be broken, be snared, and be taken.

23:28:14.text: Therefore hear the LORD’s word, you scoffers, that rule this people in Jerusalem:

23:28:15.text: “Because you have said, ‘ We have made a covenant with death, and we are in agreement with Sheol. When the overflowing scourge passes through, it won’t come to us; for we have made lies our refuge, and we have hidden ourselves under falsehood.’ ”

23:28:16.text: Therefore the Lord GOD says, “Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious cornerstone of a sure foundation. He who believes shall not act hastily.

23:28:17.text: I will make justice the measuring line, and righteousness the plumb line. The hail will sweep away the refuge of lies, and the waters will overflow the hiding place.

23:28:18.text: Your covenant with death shall be annulled, and your agreement with Sheol shall not stand. When the overflowing scourge passes through, then you will be trampled down by it.

23:28:19.text: As often as it passes through, it will seize you; for morning by morning it will pass through, by day and by night; and it will be nothing but terror to understand the message.”

23:28:2.text: Behold, the Lord has one who is mighty and strong. Like a storm of hail, a destroying storm, and like a storm of mighty waters overflowing, he will cast them down to the earth with his hand.

23:28:20.text: For the bed is too short to stretch out on, and the blanket is too narrow to wrap oneself in.

23:28:21.text: For the LORD will rise up as on Mount Perazim. He will be angry as in the valley of Gibeon; that he may do his work, his unusual work, and bring to pass his act, his extraordinary act.

23:28:22.text: Now therefore don’t be scoffers, lest your bonds be made strong; for I have heard a decree of destruction from the Lord, GOD of Armies, on the whole earth.

23:28:23.text: Give ear, and hear my voice! Listen, and hear my speech!

23:28:24.text: Does he who ploughs to sow plough continually? Does he keep turning the soil and breaking the clods?

23:28:25.text: When he has levelled its surface, doesn’t he plant the dill, and scatter the cumin seed, and put in the wheat in rows, the barley in the appointed place, and the spelt in its place?

23:28:26.text: For his God instructs him in right judgement and teaches him.

23:28:27.text: For the dill isn’t threshed with a sharp instrument, neither is a cart wheel turned over the cumin; but the dill is beaten out with a stick, and the cumin with a rod.

23:28:28.text: Bread flour must be ground; so he will not always be threshing it. Although he drives the wheel of his threshing cart over it, his horses don’t grind it.

23:28:29.text: This also comes out from the LORD of Armies, who is wonderful in counsel, and excellent in wisdom.

23:28:3.text: The crown of pride of the drunkards of Ephraim will be trodden under foot.

23:28:4.text: The fading flower of his glorious beauty, which is on the head of the fertile valley, shall be like the first-ripe fig before the summer, which someone picks and eats as soon as he sees it.

23:28:5.text: In that day, the LORD of Armies will become a crown of glory and a diadem of beauty to the residue of his people,

23:28:6.text: and a spirit of justice to him who sits in judgement, and strength to those who turn back the battle at the gate.

23:28:7.text: They also reel with wine, and stagger with strong drink. The priest and the prophet reel with strong drink. They are swallowed up by wine. They stagger with strong drink. They err in vision. They stumble in judgement.

23:28:8.text: For all tables are completely full of filthy vomit and filthiness.

23:28:9.text: Whom will he teach knowledge? To whom will he explain the message? Those who are weaned from the milk, and drawn from the breasts?

23:29:1.text: Woe to Ariel! Ariel, the city where David encamped! Add year to year; let the feasts come around;

23:29:10.text: For the LORD has poured out on you a spirit of deep sleep, and has closed your eyes, the prophets; and he has covered your heads, the seers.

23:29:11.text: All vision has become to you like the words of a book that is sealed, which men deliver to one who is educated, saying, “Read this, please;” and he says, “I can’t, for it is sealed;”

23:29:12.text: and the book is delivered to one who is not educated, saying, “Read this, please;” and he says, “I can’t read.”

23:29:13.text: The Lord said, “Because this people draws near with their mouth and honours me with their lips, but they have removed their heart far from me, and their fear of me is a commandment of men which has been taught;

23:29:14.text: therefore, behold, I will proceed to do a marvellous work amongst this people, even a marvellous work and a wonder; and the wisdom of their wise men will perish, and the understanding of their prudent men will be hidden.”

23:29:15.text: Woe to those who deeply hide their counsel from the LORD, and whose deeds are in the dark, and who say, “Who sees us?” and “Who knows us?”

23:29:16.text: You turn things upside down! Should the potter be thought to be like clay, that the thing made should say about him who made it, “He didn’t make me;” or the thing formed say of him who formed it, “He has no understanding”?

23:29:17.text: Isn’t it yet a very little while, and Lebanon will be turned into a fruitful field, and the fruitful field will be regarded as a forest?

23:29:18.text: In that day, the deaf will hear the words of the book, and the eyes of the blind will see out of obscurity and out of darkness.

23:29:19.text: The humble also will increase their joy in the LORD, and the poor amongst men will rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.

23:29:2.text: then I will distress Ariel, and there will be mourning and lamentation. She shall be to me as an altar hearth.

23:29:20.text: For the ruthless is brought to nothing, and the scoffer ceases, and all those who are alert to do evil are cut off —

23:29:21.text: who cause a person to be indicted by a word, and lay a snare for one who reproves in the gate, and who deprive the innocent of justice with false testimony.

23:29:22.text: Therefore the LORD, who redeemed Abraham, says concerning the house of Jacob: “Jacob shall no longer be ashamed, neither shall his face grow pale.

23:29:23.text: But when he sees his children, the work of my hands, in the middle of him, they will sanctify my name. Yes, they will sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and will stand in awe of the God of Israel.

23:29:24.text: They also who err in spirit will come to understanding, and those who grumble will receive instruction.”

23:29:3.text: I will encamp against you all around you, and will lay siege against you with posted troops. I will raise siege works against you.

23:29:4.text: You will be brought down, and will speak out of the ground. Your speech will mumble out of the dust. Your voice will be as of one who has a familiar spirit, out of the ground, and your speech will whisper out of the dust.

23:29:5.text: But the multitude of your foes will be like fine dust, and the multitude of the ruthless ones like chaff that blows away. Yes, it will be in an instant, suddenly.

23:29:6.text: She will be visited by the LORD of Armies with thunder, with earthquake, with great noise, with whirlwind and storm, and with the flame of a devouring fire.

23:29:7.text: The multitude of all the nations that fight against Ariel, even all who fight against her and her stronghold, and who distress her, will be like a dream, a vision of the night.

23:29:8.text: It will be like when a hungry man dreams, and behold, he eats; but he awakes, and his hunger isn’t satisfied; or like when a thirsty man dreams, and behold, he drinks; but he awakes, and behold, he is faint, and he is still thirsty. The multitude of all the nations that fight against Mount Zion will be like that.

23:29:9.text: Pause and wonder! Blind yourselves and be blind! They are drunken, but not with wine; they stagger, but not with strong drink.

23:2:1.text: This is what Isaiah the son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem.

23:2:10.text: Enter into the rock, and hide in the dust, from before the terror of the LORD, and from the glory of his majesty.

23:2:11.text: The lofty looks of man will be brought low, the arrogance of men will be bowed down, and the LORD alone will be exalted in that day.

23:2:12.text: For there will be a day of the LORD of Armies for all that is proud and arrogant, and for all that is lifted up, and it shall be brought low —

23:2:13.text: for all the cedars of Lebanon, that are high and lifted up, for all the oaks of Bashan,

23:2:14.text: for all the high mountains, for all the hills that are lifted up,

23:2:15.text: for every lofty tower, for every fortified wall,

23:2:16.text: for all the ships of Tarshish, and for all pleasant imagery.

23:2:17.text: The loftiness of man shall be bowed down, and the arrogance of men shall be brought low; and the LORD alone shall be exalted in that day.

23:2:18.text: The idols shall utterly pass away.

23:2:19.text: Men shall go into the caves of the rocks, and into the holes of the earth, from before the terror of the LORD, and from the glory of his majesty, when he arises to shake the earth mightily.

23:2:2.text: It shall happen in the latter days, that the mountain of the LORD’s house shall be established on the top of the mountains, and shall be raised above the hills; and all nations shall flow to it.

23:2:20.text: In that day, men shall cast away their idols of silver and their idols of gold, which have been made for themselves to worship, to the moles and to the bats,

23:2:21.text: to go into the caverns of the rocks, and into the clefts of the ragged rocks, from before the terror of the LORD, and from the glory of his majesty, when he arises to shake the earth mightily.

23:2:22.text: Stop trusting in man, whose breath is in his nostrils; for of what account is he?

23:2:3.text: Many peoples shall go and say, “Come, let’s go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths.” For the law shall go out of Zion, and the LORD’s word from Jerusalem.

23:2:4.text: He will judge between the nations, and will decide concerning many peoples. They shall beat their swords into ploughshares, and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.

23:2:5.text: House of Jacob, come, and let’s walk in the light of the LORD.

23:2:6.text: For you have forsaken your people, the house of Jacob, because they are filled from the east, with those who practise divination like the Philistines, and they clasp hands with the children of foreigners.

23:2:7.text: Their land is full of silver and gold, neither is there any end of their treasures. Their land also is full of horses, neither is there any end of their chariots.

23:2:8.text: Their land also is full of idols. They worship the work of their own hands, that which their own fingers have made.

23:2:9.text: Man is brought low, and mankind is humbled; therefore don’t forgive them.

23:37:1.text: When King Hezekiah heard it, he tore his clothes, covered himself with sackcloth, and went into the LORD’s house.

23:37:10.text: “Thus you shall speak to Hezekiah king of Judah, saying, ‘Don’t let your God in whom you trust deceive you, saying, “Jerusalem won’t be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.”

23:37:11.text: Behold, you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all lands, by destroying them utterly. Shall you be delivered?

23:37:12.text: Have the gods of the nations delivered them, which my fathers have destroyed, Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the children of Eden who were in Telassar?

23:37:13.text: Where is the king of Hamath, and the king of Arpad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena, and Ivvah?’ ”

23:37:14.text: Hezekiah received the letter from the hand of the messengers and read it. Then Hezekiah went up to the LORD’s house, and spread it before the LORD.

23:37:15.text: Hezekiah prayed to the LORD, saying,

23:37:16.text: “LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, who is enthroned amongst the cherubim, you are the God, even you alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth. You have made heaven and earth.

23:37:17.text: Turn your ear, LORD, and hear. Open your eyes, LORD, and behold. Hear all of the words of Sennacherib, who has sent to defy the living God.

23:37:18.text: Truly, LORD, the kings of Assyria have destroyed all the countries and their land,

23:37:19.text: and have cast their gods into the fire; for they were no gods, but the work of men’s hands, wood and stone; therefore they have destroyed them.

23:37:2.text: He sent Eliakim, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz.

23:37:20.text: Now therefore, LORD our God, save us from his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you are the LORD, even you only.”

23:37:21.text: Then Isaiah the son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying, “The LORD, the God of Israel says, ‘ Because you have prayed to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria,

23:37:22.text: this is the word which the LORD has spoken concerning him: The virgin daughter of Zion has despised you and ridiculed you. The daughter of Jerusalem has shaken her head at you.

23:37:23.text: Whom have you defied and blasphemed? Against whom have you exalted your voice and lifted up your eyes on high? Against the Holy One of Israel.

23:37:24.text: By your servants, you have defied the Lord, and have said, “With the multitude of my chariots I have come up to the height of the mountains, to the innermost parts of Lebanon. I will cut down its tall cedars and its choice cypress trees. I will enter into its farthest height, the forest of its fruitful field.

23:37:25.text: I have dug and drunk water, and with the sole of my feet I will dry up all the rivers of Egypt.”

23:37:26.text: “‘ Have you not heard how I have done it long ago, and formed it in ancient times? Now I have brought it to pass, that it should be yours to destroy fortified cities, turning them into ruinous heaps.

23:37:27.text: Therefore their inhabitants had little power. They were dismayed and confounded. They were like the grass of the field, and like the green herb, like the grass on the housetops, and like a field before its crop has grown.

23:37:28.text: But I know your sitting down, your going out, your coming in, and your raging against me.

23:37:29.text: Because of your raging against me, and because your arrogance has come up into my ears, therefore I will put my hook in your nose and my bridle in your lips, and I will turn you back by the way by which you came.

23:37:3.text: They said to him, “Hezekiah says, ‘ Today is a day of trouble, and of rebuke, and of rejection; for the children have come to the birth, and there is no strength to give birth.

23:37:30.text: “‘ This shall be the sign to you: You will eat this year that which grows of itself, and in the second year that which springs from it; and in the third year sow and reap and plant vineyards, and eat their fruit.

23:37:31.text: The remnant that is escaped of the house of Judah will again take root downward, and bear fruit upward.

23:37:32.text: For out of Jerusalem a remnant will go out, and survivors will escape from Mount Zion. The zeal of the LORD of Armies will perform this.’

23:37:33.text: “Therefore the LORD says concerning the king of Assyria, ‘ He will not come to this city, nor shoot an arrow there, neither will he come before it with shield, nor cast up a mound against it.

23:37:34.text: He will return the way that he came, and he won’t come to this city,’ says the LORD.

23:37:35.text: ‘ For I will defend this city to save it, for my own sake, and for my servant David’s sake.’ ”

23:37:36.text: Then the LORD’s angel went out and struck one hundred and eighty-five thousand men in the camp of the Assyrians. When men arose early in the morning, behold, these were all dead bodies.

23:37:37.text: So Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, went away, returned to Nineveh, and stayed there.

23:37:38.text: As he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch his god, Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons struck him with the sword; and they escaped into the land of Ararat. Esar Haddon his son reigned in his place.

23:37:4.text: It may be the LORD your God will hear the words of Rabshakeh, whom the king of Assyria his master has sent to defy the living God, and will rebuke the words which the LORD your God has heard. Therefore lift up your prayer for the remnant that is left.’ ”

23:37:5.text: So the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.

23:37:6.text: Isaiah said to them, “Tell your master, ‘ The LORD says, “Don’t be afraid of the words that you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me.

23:37:7.text: Behold, I will put a spirit in him and he will hear news, and will return to his own land. I will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land.”’ ”

23:37:8.text: So Rabshakeh returned, and found the king of Assyria warring against Libnah, for he heard that he had departed from Lachish.

23:37:9.text: He heard news concerning Tirhakah king of Ethiopia, “He has come out to fight against you.” When he heard it, he sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying,

23:38:1.text: In those days Hezekiah was sick and near death. Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, came to him, and said to him, “The LORD says, ‘ Set your house in order, for you will die, and not live.’ ”

23:38:10.text: I said, “In the middle of my life I go into the gates of Sheol. I am deprived of the residue of my years.”

23:38:11.text: I said, “I won’t see the LORD, the LORD in the land of the living. I will see man no more with the inhabitants of the world.

23:38:12.text: My dwelling is removed, and is carried away from me like a shepherd’s tent. I have rolled up my life like a weaver. He will cut me off from the loom. From day even to night you will make an end of me.

23:38:13.text: I waited patiently until morning. He breaks all my bones like a lion. From day even to night you will make an end of me.

23:38:14.text: I chattered like a swallow or a crane. I moaned like a dove. My eyes weaken looking upward. Lord, I am oppressed. Be my security.”

23:38:15.text: What will I say? He has both spoken to me, and himself has done it. I will walk carefully all my years because of the anguish of my soul.

23:38:16.text: Lord, men live by these things; and my spirit finds life in all of them. You restore me, and cause me to live.

23:38:17.text: Behold, for peace I had great anguish, but you have in love for my soul delivered it from the pit of corruption; for you have cast all my sins behind your back.

23:38:18.text: For Sheol can’t praise you. Death can’t celebrate you. Those who go down into the pit can’t hope for your truth.

23:38:19.text: The living, the living, he shall praise you, as I do today. The father shall make known your truth to the children.

23:38:2.text: Then Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD,

23:38:20.text: The LORD will save me. Therefore we will sing my songs with stringed instruments all the days of our life in the LORD’s house.

23:38:21.text: Now Isaiah had said, “Let them take a cake of figs, and lay it for a poultice on the boil, and he shall recover.”

23:38:22.text: Hezekiah also had said, “What is the sign that I will go up to the LORD’s house?”

23:38:3.text: and said, “Remember now, LORD, I beg you, how I have walked before you in truth and with a perfect heart, and have done that which is good in your sight.” Then Hezekiah wept bitterly.

23:38:4.text: Then the LORD’s word came to Isaiah, saying,

23:38:5.text: “Go, and tell Hezekiah, ‘ The LORD, the God of David your father, says, “I have heard your prayer. I have seen your tears. Behold, I will add fifteen years to your life.

23:38:6.text: I will deliver you and this city out of the hand of the king of Assyria, and I will defend this city.

23:38:7.text: This shall be the sign to you from the LORD, that the LORD will do this thing that he has spoken.

23:38:8.text: Behold, I will cause the shadow on the sundial, which has gone down on the sundial of Ahaz with the sun, to return backward ten steps.”’ ” So the sun returned ten steps on the sundial on which it had gone down.

23:38:9.text: The writing of Hezekiah king of Judah, when he had been sick, and had recovered of his sickness:

23:3:1.text: For, behold, the Lord, GOD of Armies, takes away from Jerusalem and from Judah supply and support, the whole supply of bread, and the whole supply of water;

23:3:10.text: Tell the righteous that it will be well with them, for they will eat the fruit of their deeds.

23:3:11.text: Woe to the wicked! Disaster is upon them, for the deeds of their hands will be paid back to them.

23:3:12.text: As for my people, children are their oppressors, and women rule over them. My people, those who lead you cause you to err, and destroy the way of your paths.

23:3:13.text: The LORD stands up to contend, and stands to judge the peoples.

23:3:14.text: The LORD will enter into judgement with the elders of his people and their leaders: “It is you who have eaten up the vineyard. The plunder of the poor is in your houses.

23:3:15.text: What do you mean that you crush my people, and grind the face of the poor?” says the Lord, GOD of Armies.

23:3:16.text: Moreover the LORD said, “Because the daughters of Zion are arrogant, and walk with outstretched necks and flirting eyes, walking daintily as they go, jingling ornaments on their feet;

23:3:17.text: therefore the Lord brings sores on the crown of the head of the women of Zion, and the LORD will make their scalps bald.”

23:3:18.text: In that day the Lord will take away the beauty of their anklets, the headbands, the crescent necklaces,

23:3:19.text: the earrings, the bracelets, the veils,

23:3:2.text: the mighty man, the man of war, the judge, the prophet, the diviner, the elder,

23:3:20.text: the headdresses, the ankle chains, the sashes, the perfume containers, the charms,

23:3:21.text: the signet rings, the nose rings,

23:3:22.text: the fine robes, the capes, the cloaks, the purses,

23:3:23.text: the hand mirrors, the fine linen garments, the tiaras, and the shawls.

23:3:24.text: It shall happen that instead of sweet spices, there shall be rottenness; instead of a belt, a rope; instead of well set hair, baldness; instead of a robe, a wearing of sackcloth; and branding instead of beauty.

23:3:25.text: Your men shall fall by the sword, and your mighty in the war.

23:3:26.text: Her gates shall lament and mourn. She shall be desolate and sit on the ground.

23:3:3.text: the captain of fifty, the honourable man, the counsellor, the skilled craftsman, and the clever enchanter.

23:3:4.text: I will give boys to be their princes, and children shall rule over them.

23:3:5.text: The people will be oppressed, everyone by another, and everyone by his neighbour. The child will behave himself proudly against the old man, and the wicked against the honourable.

23:3:6.text: Indeed a man shall take hold of his brother in the house of his father, saying, “You have clothing, you be our ruler, and let this ruin be under your hand.”

23:3:7.text: In that day he will cry out, saying, “I will not be a healer; for in my house is neither bread nor clothing. You shall not make me ruler of the people.”

23:3:8.text: For Jerusalem is ruined, and Judah is fallen; because their tongue and their doings are against the LORD, to provoke the eyes of his glory.

23:3:9.text: The look of their faces testify against them. They parade their sin like Sodom. They don’t hide it. Woe to their soul! For they have brought disaster upon themselves.

23:40:1.text: “Comfort, comfort my people,” says your God.

23:40:10.text: Behold, the Lord GOD will come as a mighty one, and his arm will rule for him. Behold, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.

23:40:11.text: He will feed his flock like a shepherd. He will gather the lambs in his arm, and carry them in his bosom. He will gently lead those who have their young.

23:40:12.text: Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, and marked off the sky with his span, and calculated the dust of the earth in a measuring basket, and weighed the mountains in scales, and the hills in a balance?

23:40:13.text: Who has directed the LORD’s Spirit, or has taught him as his counsellor?

23:40:14.text: Who did he take counsel with, and who instructed him, and taught him in the path of justice, and taught him knowledge, and showed him the way of understanding?

23:40:15.text: Behold, the nations are like a drop in a bucket, and are regarded as a speck of dust on a balance. Behold, he lifts up the islands like a very little thing.

23:40:16.text: Lebanon is not sufficient to burn, nor its animals sufficient for a burnt offering.

23:40:17.text: All the nations are like nothing before him. They are regarded by him as less than nothing, and vanity.

23:40:18.text: To whom then will you liken God? Or what likeness will you compare to him?

23:40:19.text: A workman has cast an image, and the goldsmith overlays it with gold, and casts silver chains for it.

23:40:2.text: “Speak comfortably to Jerusalem, and call out to her that her warfare is accomplished, that her iniquity is pardoned, that she has received of the LORD’s hand double for all her sins.”

23:40:20.text: He who is too impoverished for such an offering chooses a tree that will not rot. He seeks a skilful workman to set up a carved image for him that will not be moved.

23:40:21.text: Haven’t you known? Haven’t you heard? Haven’t you been told from the beginning? Haven’t you understood from the foundations of the earth?

23:40:22.text: It is he who sits above the circle of the earth, and its inhabitants are like grasshoppers; who stretches out the heavens like a curtain, and spreads them out like a tent to dwell in,

23:40:23.text: who brings princes to nothing, who makes the judges of the earth meaningless.

23:40:24.text: They are planted scarcely. They are sown scarcely. Their stock has scarcely taken root in the ground. He merely blows on them, and they wither, and the whirlwind takes them away as stubble.

23:40:25.text: “To whom then will you liken me? Who is my equal?” says the Holy One.

23:40:26.text: Lift up your eyes on high, and see who has created these, who brings out their army by number. He calls them all by name. By the greatness of his might, and because he is strong in power, not one is lacking.

23:40:27.text: Why do you say, Jacob, and speak, Israel, “My way is hidden from the LORD, and the justice due me is disregarded by my God”?

23:40:28.text: Haven’t you known? Haven’t you heard? The everlasting God, the LORD, the Creator of the ends of the earth, doesn’t faint. He isn’t weary. His understanding is unsearchable.

23:40:29.text: He gives power to the weak. He increases the strength of him who has no might.

23:40:3.text: The voice of one who calls out, “Prepare the way of the LORD in the wilderness! Make a level highway in the desert for our God.

23:40:30.text: Even the youths faint and get weary, and the young men utterly fall;

23:40:31.text: but those who wait for the LORD will renew their strength. They will mount up with wings like eagles. They will run, and not be weary. They will walk, and not faint.

23:40:4.text: Every valley shall be exalted, and every mountain and hill shall be made low. The uneven shall be made level, and the rough places a plain.

23:40:5.text: The LORD’s glory shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together; for the mouth of the LORD has spoken it.”

23:40:6.text: The voice of one saying, “Cry out!” One said, “What shall I cry?” “All flesh is like grass, and all its glory is like the flower of the field.

23:40:7.text: The grass withers, the flower fades, because the LORD’s breath blows on it. Surely the people are like grass.

23:40:8.text: The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God stands forever.”

23:40:9.text: You who tell good news to Zion, go up on a high mountain. You who tell good news to Jerusalem, lift up your voice with strength! Lift it up! Don’t be afraid! Say to the cities of Judah, “Behold, your God!”

23:41:1.text: “Keep silent before me, islands, and let the peoples renew their strength. Let them come near, then let them speak. Let’s meet together for judgement.

23:41:10.text: Don’t you be afraid, for I am with you. Don’t be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you. Yes, I will help you. Yes, I will uphold you with the right hand of my righteousness.

23:41:11.text: Behold, all those who are incensed against you will be disappointed and confounded. Those who strive with you will be like nothing, and shall perish.

23:41:12.text: You will seek them, and won’t find them, even those who contend with you. Those who war against you will be as nothing, as a nonexistent thing.

23:41:13.text: For I, the LORD your God, will hold your right hand, saying to you, ‘Don’t be afraid. I will help you.’

23:41:14.text: Don’t be afraid, you worm Jacob, and you men of Israel. I will help you,” says the LORD. “Your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel.

23:41:15.text: Behold, I have made you into a new sharp threshing instrument with teeth. You will thresh the mountains, and beat them small, and will make the hills like chaff.

23:41:16.text: You will winnow them, and the wind will carry them away, and the whirlwind will scatter them. You will rejoice in the LORD. You will glory in the Holy One of Israel.

23:41:17.text: The poor and needy seek water, and there is none. Their tongue fails for thirst. I, the LORD, will answer them. I, the God of Israel, will not forsake them.

23:41:18.text: I will open rivers on the bare heights, and springs in the middle of the valleys. I will make the wilderness a pool of water, and the dry land springs of water.

23:41:19.text: I will put cedar, acacia, myrtle, and oil trees in the wilderness. I will set cypress trees, pine, and box trees together in the desert;

23:41:2.text: Who has raised up one from the east? Who called him to his feet in righteousness? He hands over nations to him and makes him rule over kings. He gives them like the dust to his sword, like the driven stubble to his bow.

23:41:20.text: that they may see, know, consider, and understand together, that the LORD’s hand has done this, and the Holy One of Israel has created it.

23:41:21.text: Produce your cause,” says the LORD. “Bring out your strong reasons!” says the King of Jacob.

23:41:22.text: “Let them announce and declare to us what will happen! Declare the former things, what they are, that we may consider them, and know the latter end of them; or show us things to come.

23:41:23.text: Declare the things that are to come hereafter, that we may know that you are gods. Yes, do good, or do evil, that we may be dismayed, and see it together.

23:41:24.text: Behold, you are nothing, and your work is nothing. He who chooses you is an abomination.

23:41:25.text: “I have raised up one from the north, and he has come, from the rising of the sun, one who calls on my name, and he shall come on rulers as on mortar, and as the potter treads clay.

23:41:26.text: Who has declared it from the beginning, that we may know? and before, that we may say, ‘ He is right’ ? Surely, there is no one who declares. Surely, there is no one who shows. Surely, there is no one who hears your words.

23:41:27.text: I am the first to say to Zion, ‘ Behold, look at them;’ and I will give one who brings good news to Jerusalem.

23:41:28.text: When I look, there is no man, even amongst them there is no counsellor who, when I ask, can answer a word.

23:41:29.text: Behold, all of their deeds are vanity and nothing. Their molten images are wind and confusion.

23:41:3.text: He pursues them and passes by safely, even by a way that he had not gone with his feet.

23:41:4.text: Who has worked and done it, calling the generations from the beginning? I, the LORD, the first, and with the last, I am he.”

23:41:5.text: The islands have seen, and fear. The ends of the earth tremble. They approach, and come.

23:41:6.text: Everyone helps his neighbour. They say to their brothers, “Be strong!”

23:41:7.text: So the carpenter encourages the goldsmith. He who smooths with the hammer encourages him who strikes the anvil, saying of the soldering, “It is good;” and he fastens it with nails, that it might not totter.

23:41:8.text: “But you, Israel, my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the offspring of Abraham my friend,

23:41:9.text: you whom I have taken hold of from the ends of the earth, and called from its corners, and said to you, ‘ You are my servant. I have chosen you and have not cast you away.’

23:42:1.text: “Behold, my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen, in whom my soul delights: I have put my Spirit on him. He will bring justice to the nations.

23:42:10.text: Sing to the LORD a new song, and his praise from the end of the earth, you who go down to the sea, and all that is therein, the islands and their inhabitants.

23:42:11.text: Let the wilderness and its cities raise their voices, with the villages that Kedar inhabits. Let the inhabitants of Sela sing. Let them shout from the top of the mountains!

23:42:12.text: Let them give glory to the LORD, and declare his praise in the islands.

23:42:13.text: The LORD will go out like a mighty man. He will stir up zeal like a man of war. He will raise a war cry. Yes, he will shout aloud. He will triumph over his enemies.

23:42:14.text: “I have been silent a long time. I have been quiet and restrained myself. Now I will cry out like a travailing woman. I will both gasp and pant.

23:42:15.text: I will destroy mountains and hills, and dry up all their herbs. I will make the rivers islands, and will dry up the pools.

23:42:16.text: I will bring the blind by a way that they don’t know. I will lead them in paths that they don’t know. I will make darkness light before them, and crooked places straight. I will do these things, and I will not forsake them.

23:42:17.text: “Those who trust in engraved images, who tell molten images, ‘You are our gods,’ will be turned back. They will be utterly disappointed.

23:42:18.text: “Hear, you deaf, and look, you blind, that you may see.

23:42:19.text: Who is blind, but my servant? Or who is as deaf as my messenger whom I send? Who is as blind as he who is at peace, and as blind as the LORD’s servant?

23:42:2.text: He will not shout, nor raise his voice, nor cause it to be heard in the street.

23:42:20.text: You see many things, but don’t observe. His ears are open, but he doesn’t listen.

23:42:21.text: It pleased the LORD, for his righteousness’ sake, to magnify the law and make it honourable.

23:42:22.text: But this is a robbed and plundered people. All of them are snared in holes, and they are hidden in prisons. They have become captives, and no one delivers, and a plunder, and no one says, ‘ Restore them!’

23:42:23.text: Who is there amongst you who will give ear to this? Who will listen and hear for the time to come?

23:42:24.text: Who gave Jacob as plunder, and Israel to the robbers? Didn’t the LORD, he against whom we have sinned? For they would not walk in his ways, and they disobeyed his law.

23:42:25.text: Therefore he poured the fierceness of his anger on him, and the strength of battle. It set him on fire all around, but he didn’t know. It burnt him, but he didn’t take it to heart.”

23:42:3.text: He won’t break a bruised reed. He won’t quench a dimly burning wick. He will faithfully bring justice.

23:42:4.text: He will not fail nor be discouraged, until he has set justice in the earth, and the islands wait for his law.”

23:42:5.text: God the LORD, he who created the heavens and stretched them out, he who spread out the earth and that which comes out of it, he who gives breath to its people and spirit to those who walk in it, says:

23:42:6.text: “I, the LORD, have called you in righteousness. I will hold your hand. I will keep you, and make you a covenant for the people, as a light for the nations,

23:42:7.text: to open the blind eyes, to bring the prisoners out of the dungeon, and those who sit in darkness out of the prison.

23:42:8.text: “I am the LORD. That is my name. I will not give my glory to another, nor my praise to engraved images.

23:42:9.text: Behold, the former things have happened and I declare new things. I tell you about them before they come up.”

23:45:1.text: The LORD says to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have held to subdue nations before him and strip kings of their armour, to open the doors before him, and the gates shall not be shut:

23:45:10.text: Woe to him who says to a father, ‘ What have you become the father of?’ or to a mother, ‘ What have you given birth to?’ ”

23:45:11.text: The LORD, the Holy One of Israel and his Maker says: “You ask me about the things that are to come, concerning my sons, and you command me concerning the work of my hands!

23:45:12.text: I have made the earth, and created man on it. I, even my hands, have stretched out the heavens. I have commanded all their army.

23:45:13.text: I have raised him up in righteousness, and I will make all his ways straight. He shall build my city, and he shall let my exiles go free, not for price nor reward,” says the LORD of Armies.

23:45:14.text: The LORD says: “The labour of Egypt, and the merchandise of Ethiopia, and the Sabeans, men of stature, will come over to you, and they will be yours. They will go after you. They shall come over in chains. They will bow down to you. They will make supplication to you: ‘ Surely God is in you; and there is no one else. There is no other god.

23:45:15.text: Most certainly you are a God who has hidden yourself, God of Israel, the Saviour.’ ”

23:45:16.text: They will be disappointed, yes, confounded, all of them. Those who are makers of idols will go into confusion together.

23:45:17.text: Israel will be saved by the LORD with an everlasting salvation. You will not be disappointed nor confounded to ages everlasting.

23:45:18.text: For the LORD who created the heavens, the God who formed the earth and made it, who established it and didn’t create it a waste, who formed it to be inhabited says: “I am the LORD. There is no other.

23:45:19.text: I have not spoken in secret, in a place of the land of darkness. I didn’t say to the offspring of Jacob, ‘ Seek me in vain.’ I, the LORD, speak righteousness. I declare things that are right.

23:45:2.text: “I will go before you and make the rough places smooth. I will break the doors of bronze in pieces and cut apart the bars of iron.

23:45:20.text: “Assemble yourselves and come. Draw near together, you who have escaped from the nations. Those have no knowledge who carry the wood of their engraved image, and pray to a god that can’t save.

23:45:21.text: Declare and present it. Yes, let them take counsel together. Who has shown this from ancient time? Who has declared it of old? Haven’t I, the LORD? There is no other God besides me, a just God and a Saviour. There is no one besides me.

23:45:22.text: “Look to me, and be saved, all the ends of the earth; for I am God, and there is no other.

23:45:23.text: I have sworn by myself. The word has gone out of my mouth in righteousness, and will not be revoked, that to me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall take an oath.

23:45:24.text: They will say of me, ‘ There is righteousness and strength only in the LORD.’ ” Even to him will men come. All those who raged against him will be disappointed.

23:45:25.text: All the offspring of Israel will be justified in the LORD, and will rejoice!

23:45:3.text: I will give you the treasures of darkness and hidden riches of secret places, that you may know that it is I, the LORD, who calls you by your name, even the God of Israel.

23:45:4.text: For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel my chosen, I have called you by your name. I have given you a title, though you have not known me.

23:45:5.text: I am the LORD, and there is no one else. Besides me, there is no God. I will strengthen you, though you have not known me,

23:45:6.text: that they may know from the rising of the sun, and from the west, that there is no one besides me. I am the LORD, and there is no one else.

23:45:7.text: I form the light and create darkness. I make peace and create calamity. I am the LORD, who does all these things.

23:45:8.text: Rain, you heavens, from above, and let the skies pour down righteousness. Let the earth open, that it may produce salvation, and let it cause righteousness to spring up with it. I, the LORD, have created it.

23:45:9.text: Woe to him who strives with his Maker — a clay pot amongst the clay pots of the earth! Shall the clay ask him who fashions it, ‘ What are you making?’ or your work, ‘ He has no hands’ ?

23:48:1.text: “Hear this, house of Jacob, you who are called by the name of Israel, and have come out of the waters of Judah. You swear by the LORD’s name, and make mention of the God of Israel, but not in truth, nor in righteousness —

23:48:10.text: Behold, I have refined you, but not as silver. I have chosen you in the furnace of affliction.

23:48:11.text: For my own sake, for my own sake, I will do it; for how would my name be profaned? I will not give my glory to another.

23:48:12.text: “Listen to me, O Jacob, and Israel my called: I am he. I am the first. I am also the last.

23:48:13.text: Yes, my hand has laid the foundation of the earth, and my right hand has spread out the heavens. when I call to them, they stand up together.

23:48:14.text: “Assemble yourselves, all of you, and hear! Who amongst them has declared these things? He whom the LORD loves will do what he likes to Babylon, and his arm will be against the Chaldeans.

23:48:15.text: I, even I, have spoken. Yes, I have called him. I have brought him and he shall make his way prosperous.

23:48:16.text: “Come near to me and hear this: “From the beginning I have not spoken in secret; from the time that it happened, I was there.” Now the Lord GOD has sent me with his Spirit.

23:48:17.text: The LORD, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel, says: “I am the LORD your God, who teaches you to profit, who leads you by the way that you should go.

23:48:18.text: Oh that you had listened to my commandments! Then your peace would have been like a river and your righteousness like the waves of the sea.

23:48:19.text: Your offspring also would have been as the sand and the descendants of your body like its grains. His name would not be cut off nor destroyed from before me.”

23:48:2.text: for they call themselves citizens of the holy city, and rely on the God of Israel; the LORD of Armies is his name.

23:48:20.text: Leave Babylon! Flee from the Chaldeans! With the sound of joyful shouting announce this, tell it even to the end of the earth; say, “The LORD has redeemed his servant Jacob!”

23:48:21.text: They didn’t thirst when he led them through the deserts. He caused the waters to flow out of the rock for them. He also split the rock and the waters gushed out.

23:48:22.text: “There is no peace”, says the LORD, “for the wicked.”

23:48:3.text: I have declared the former things from of old. Yes, they went out of my mouth, and I revealed them. I did them suddenly, and they happened.

23:48:4.text: Because I knew that you are obstinate, and your neck is an iron sinew, and your brow bronze;

23:48:5.text: therefore I have declared it to you from of old; before it came to pass I showed it to you; lest you should say, ‘ My idol has done them. My engraved image and my molten image has commanded them.’

23:48:6.text: You have heard it. Now see all this. And you, won’t you declare it? “I have shown you new things from this time, even hidden things, which you have not known.

23:48:7.text: They are created now, and not from of old. Before today, you didn’t hear them, lest you should say, ‘ Behold, I knew them.’

23:48:8.text: Yes, you didn’t hear. Yes, you didn’t know. Yes, from of old your ear was not opened, for I knew that you dealt very treacherously, and were called a transgressor from the womb.

23:48:9.text: For my name’s sake, I will defer my anger, and for my praise, I hold it back for you so that I don’t cut you off.

23:49:1.text: Listen, islands, to me. Listen, you peoples, from afar: the LORD has called me from the womb; from the inside of my mother, he has mentioned my name.

23:49:10.text: They shall not hunger nor thirst; neither shall the heat nor sun strike them, for he who has mercy on them will lead them. He will guide them by springs of water.

23:49:11.text: I will make all my mountains a road, and my highways shall be exalted.

23:49:12.text: Behold, these shall come from afar, and behold, these from the north and from the west, and these from the land of Sinim.”

23:49:13.text: Sing, heavens, and be joyful, earth! Break out into singing, mountains! For the LORD has comforted his people, and will have compassion on his afflicted.

23:49:14.text: But Zion said, “The LORD has forsaken me, and the Lord has forgotten me.”

23:49:15.text: “Can a woman forget her nursing child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb? Yes, these may forget, yet I will not forget you!

23:49:16.text: Behold, I have engraved you on the palms of my hands. Your walls are continually before me.

23:49:17.text: Your children hurry. Your destroyers and those who devastated you will leave you.

23:49:18.text: Lift up your eyes all around, and see: all these gather themselves together, and come to you. As I live,” says the LORD, “you shall surely clothe yourself with them all as with an ornament, and dress yourself with them, like a bride.

23:49:19.text: “For, as for your waste and your desolate places, and your land that has been destroyed, surely now that land will be too small for the inhabitants, and those who swallowed you up will be far away.

23:49:2.text: He has made my mouth like a sharp sword. He has hidden me in the shadow of his hand. He has made me a polished shaft. He has kept me close in his quiver.

23:49:20.text: The children of your bereavement will say in your ears, ‘ This place is too small for me. Give me a place to live in.’

23:49:21.text: Then you will say in your heart, ‘ Who has conceived these for me, since I have been bereaved of my children and am alone, an exile, and wandering back and forth? Who has brought these up? Behold, I was left alone. Where were these?’ ”

23:49:22.text: The Lord GOD says, “Behold, I will lift up my hand to the nations, and lift up my banner to the peoples. They shall bring your sons in their bosom, and your daughters shall be carried on their shoulders.

23:49:23.text: Kings shall be your foster fathers, and their queens your nursing mothers. They will bow down to you with their faces to the earth, and lick the dust of your feet. Then you will know that I am the LORD; and those who wait for me won’t be disappointed.”

23:49:24.text: Shall the plunder be taken from the mighty, or the lawful captives be delivered?

23:49:25.text: But the LORD says, “Even the captives of the mighty shall be taken away, and the plunder retrieved from the fierce, for I will contend with him who contends with you and I will save your children.

23:49:26.text: I will feed those who oppress you with their own flesh; and they will be drunk on their own blood, as with sweet wine. Then all flesh shall know that I, the LORD, am your Saviour and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.”

23:49:3.text: He said to me, “You are my servant, Israel, in whom I will be glorified.”

23:49:4.text: But I said, “I have laboured in vain. I have spent my strength in vain for nothing; yet surely the justice due to me is with the LORD, and my reward with my God.”

23:49:5.text: Now the LORD, he who formed me from the womb to be his servant, says to bring Jacob again to him, and to gather Israel to him, for I am honourable in the LORD’s eyes, and my God has become my strength.

23:49:6.text: Indeed, he says, “It is too light a thing that you should be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel. I will also give you as a light to the nations, that you may be my salvation to the end of the earth.”

23:49:7.text: The LORD, the Redeemer of Israel, and his Holy One, says to him whom man despises, to him whom the nation abhors, to a servant of rulers: “Kings shall see and rise up, princes, and they shall worship, because of the LORD who is faithful, even the Holy One of Israel, who has chosen you.”

23:49:8.text: The LORD says, “I have answered you in an acceptable time. I have helped you in a day of salvation. I will preserve you and give you for a covenant of the people, to raise up the land, to make them inherit the desolate heritage,

23:49:9.text: saying to those who are bound, ‘ Come out!’ ; to those who are in darkness, ‘ Show yourselves!’ “They shall feed along the paths, and their pasture shall be on all treeless heights.

23:4:1.text: Seven women shall take hold of one man in that day, saying, “We will eat our own bread, and wear our own clothing. Just let us be called by your name. Take away our reproach.”

23:4:2.text: In that day, the LORD’s branch will be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the land will be the beauty and glory of the survivors of Israel.

23:4:3.text: It will happen that he who is left in Zion and he who remains in Jerusalem shall be called holy, even everyone who is written amongst the living in Jerusalem,

23:4:4.text: when the Lord shall have washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion, and shall have purged the blood of Jerusalem from within it, by the spirit of justice and by the spirit of burning.

23:4:5.text: The LORD will create over the whole habitation of Mount Zion and over her assemblies, a cloud and smoke by day, and the shining of a flaming fire by night, for over all the glory will be a canopy.

23:4:6.text: There will be a pavilion for a shade in the daytime from the heat, and for a refuge and for a shelter from storm and from rain.

23:58:1.text: “Cry aloud! Don’t spare! Lift up your voice like a trumpet! Declare to my people their disobedience, and to the house of Jacob their sins.

23:58:10.text: and if you pour out your soul to the hungry, and satisfy the afflicted soul, then your light will rise in darkness, and your obscurity will be as the noonday;

23:58:11.text: and the LORD will guide you continually, satisfy your soul in dry places, and make your bones strong. You will be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water whose waters don’t fail.

23:58:12.text: Those who will be of you will build the old waste places. You will raise up the foundations of many generations. You will be called Repairer of the Breach, Restorer of Paths with Dwellings.

23:58:13.text: “If you turn away your foot from the Sabbath, from doing your pleasure on my holy day, and call the Sabbath a delight, and the holy of the LORD honourable, and honour it, not doing your own ways, nor finding your own pleasure, nor speaking your own words,

23:58:14.text: then you will delight yourself in the LORD, and I will make you to ride on the high places of the earth, and I will feed you with the heritage of Jacob your father;” for the LORD’s mouth has spoken it.

23:58:2.text: Yet they seek me daily, and delight to know my ways. As a nation that did righteousness, and didn’t forsake the ordinance of their God, they ask of me righteous judgements. They delight to draw near to God.

23:58:3.text: ‘ Why have we fasted,’ they say, ‘ and you don’t see? Why have we afflicted our soul, and you don’t notice?’ “Behold, in the day of your fast you find pleasure, and oppress all your labourers.

23:58:4.text: Behold, you fast for strife and contention, and to strike with the fist of wickedness. You don’t fast today so as to make your voice to be heard on high.

23:58:5.text: Is this the fast that I have chosen? A day for a man to humble his soul? Is it to bow down his head like a reed, and to spread sackcloth and ashes under himself? Will you call this a fast, and an acceptable day to the LORD?

23:58:6.text: “Isn’t this the fast that I have chosen: to release the bonds of wickedness, to undo the straps of the yoke, to let the oppressed go free, and that you break every yoke?

23:58:7.text: Isn’t it to distribute your bread to the hungry, and that you bring the poor who are cast out to your house? When you see the naked, that you cover him; and that you not hide yourself from your own flesh?

23:58:8.text: Then your light will break out as the morning, and your healing will appear quickly; then your righteousness shall go before you, and the LORD’s glory will be your rear guard.

23:58:9.text: Then you will call, and the LORD will answer. You will cry for help, and he will say, ‘ Here I am.’ “If you take away from amongst you the yoke, finger pointing, and speaking wickedly;

23:5:1.text: Let me sing for my well beloved a song of my beloved about his vineyard. My beloved had a vineyard on a very fruitful hill.

23:5:10.text: For ten acres of vineyard shall yield one bath, and a homer of seed shall yield an ephah.”

23:5:11.text: Woe to those who rise up early in the morning, that they may follow strong drink, who stay late into the night, until wine inflames them!

23:5:12.text: The harp, lyre, tambourine, and flute, with wine, are at their feasts; but they don’t respect the work of the LORD, neither have they considered the operation of his hands.

23:5:13.text: Therefore my people go into captivity for lack of knowledge. Their honourable men are famished, and their multitudes are parched with thirst.

23:5:14.text: Therefore Sheol has enlarged its desire, and opened its mouth without measure; and their glory, their multitude, their pomp, and he who rejoices amongst them, descend into it.

23:5:15.text: So man is brought low, mankind is humbled, and the eyes of the arrogant ones are humbled;

23:5:16.text: but the LORD of Armies is exalted in justice, and God the Holy One is sanctified in righteousness.

23:5:17.text: Then the lambs will graze as in their pasture, and strangers will eat the ruins of the rich.

23:5:18.text: Woe to those who draw iniquity with cords of falsehood, and wickedness as with cart rope,

23:5:19.text: who say, “Let him make haste, let him hasten his work, that we may see it; let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel draw near and come, that we may know it!”

23:5:2.text: He dug it up, gathered out its stones, planted it with the choicest vine, built a tower in the middle of it, and also cut out a wine press in it. He looked for it to yield grapes, but it yielded wild grapes.

23:5:20.text: Woe to those who call evil good, and good evil; who put darkness for light, and light for darkness; who put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!

23:5:21.text: Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes, and prudent in their own sight!

23:5:22.text: Woe to those who are mighty to drink wine, and champions at mixing strong drink;

23:5:23.text: who acquit the guilty for a bribe, but deny justice for the innocent!

23:5:24.text: Therefore as the tongue of fire devours the stubble, and as the dry grass sinks down in the flame, so their root shall be as rottenness, and their blossom shall go up as dust, because they have rejected the law of the LORD of Armies, and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.

23:5:25.text: Therefore the LORD’s anger burns against his people, and he has stretched out his hand against them and has struck them. The mountains tremble, and their dead bodies are as refuse in the middle of the streets. For all this, his anger is not turned away, but his hand is still stretched out.

23:5:26.text: He will lift up a banner to the nations from far away, and he will whistle for them from the end of the earth. Behold, they will come speedily and swiftly.

23:5:27.text: No one shall be weary nor stumble amongst them; no one shall slumber nor sleep, neither shall the belt of their waist be untied, nor the strap of their sandals be broken,

23:5:28.text: whose arrows are sharp, and all their bows bent. Their horses’ hoofs will be like flint, and their wheels like a whirlwind.

23:5:29.text: Their roaring will be like a lioness. They will roar like young lions. Yes, they shall roar, and seize their prey and carry it off, and there will be no one to deliver.

23:5:3.text: “Now, inhabitants of Jerusalem and men of Judah, please judge between me and my vineyard.

23:5:30.text: They will roar against them in that day like the roaring of the sea. If one looks to the land, behold, darkness and distress. The light is darkened in its clouds.

23:5:4.text: What could have been done more to my vineyard, that I have not done in it? Why, when I looked for it to yield grapes, did it yield wild grapes?

23:5:5.text: Now I will tell you what I will do to my vineyard. I will take away its hedge, and it will be eaten up. I will break down its wall, and it will be trampled down.

23:5:6.text: I will lay it a wasteland. It won’t be pruned or hoed, but it will grow briers and thorns. I will also command the clouds that they rain no rain on it.”

23:5:7.text: For the vineyard of the LORD of Armies is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah his pleasant plant. He looked for justice, but behold, oppression, for righteousness, but behold, a cry of distress.

23:5:8.text: Woe to those who join house to house, who lay field to field, until there is no room, and you are made to dwell alone in the middle of the land!

23:5:9.text: In my ears, the LORD of Armies says: “Surely many houses will be desolate, even great and beautiful, unoccupied.

23:65:1.text: “I am enquired of by those who didn’t ask. I am found by those who didn’t seek me. I said, ‘ See me, see me,’ to a nation that was not called by my name.

23:65:10.text: Sharon will be a fold of flocks, and the valley of Achor a place for herds to lie down in, for my people who have sought me.

23:65:11.text: “But you who forsake the LORD, who forget my holy mountain, who prepare a table for Fortune, and who fill up mixed wine to Destiny;

23:65:12.text: I will destine you to the sword, and you will all bow down to the slaughter; because when I called, you didn’t answer. When I spoke, you didn’t listen; but you did that which was evil in my eyes, and chose that in which I didn’t delight.”

23:65:13.text: Therefore the Lord GOD says, “Behold, my servants will eat, but you will be hungry; behold, my servants will drink, but you will be thirsty. Behold, my servants will rejoice, but you will be disappointed.

23:65:14.text: Behold, my servants will sing for joy of heart, but you will cry for sorrow of heart, and will wail for anguish of spirit.

23:65:15.text: You will leave your name for a curse to my chosen, and the Lord GOD will kill you. He will call his servants by another name,

23:65:16.text: so that he who blesses himself in the earth will bless himself in the God of truth; and he who swears in the earth will swear by the God of truth; because the former troubles are forgotten, and because they are hidden from my eyes.

23:65:17.text: “For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth; and the former things will not be remembered, nor come into mind.

23:65:18.text: But be glad and rejoice forever in that which I create; for, behold, I create Jerusalem to be a delight, and her people a joy.

23:65:19.text: I will rejoice in Jerusalem, and delight in my people; and the voice of weeping and the voice of crying will be heard in her no more.

23:65:2.text: I have spread out my hands all day to a rebellious people, who walk in a way that is not good, after their own thoughts;

23:65:20.text: “No more will there be an infant who only lives a few days, nor an old man who has not filled his days; for the child will die one hundred years old, and the sinner being one hundred years old will be accursed.

23:65:21.text: They will build houses and inhabit them. They will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.

23:65:22.text: They will not build and another inhabit. They will not plant and another eat; for the days of my people will be like the days of a tree, and my chosen will long enjoy the work of their hands.

23:65:23.text: They will not labour in vain nor give birth for calamity; for they are the offspring of the LORD’s blessed and their descendants with them.

23:65:24.text: It will happen that before they call, I will answer; and while they are yet speaking, I will hear.

23:65:25.text: The wolf and the lamb will feed together. The lion will eat straw like the ox. Dust will be the serpent’s food. They will not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain,” says the LORD.

23:65:3.text: a people who provoke me to my face continually, sacrificing in gardens, and burning incense on bricks;

23:65:4.text: who sit amongst the graves, and spend nights in secret places; who eat pig’s meat, and broth of abominable things is in their vessels;

23:65:5.text: who say, ‘Stay by yourself, don’t come near to me, for I am holier than you.’ These are smoke in my nose, a fire that burns all day.

23:65:6.text: “Behold, it is written before me: I will not keep silence, but will repay, yes, I will repay into their bosom

23:65:7.text: your own iniquities and the iniquities of your fathers together”, says the LORD, “who have burnt incense on the mountains, and blasphemed me on the hills. Therefore I will first measure their work into their bosom.”

23:65:8.text: The LORD says, “As the new wine is found in the cluster, and one says, ‘Don’t destroy it, for a blessing is in it:’so I will do for my servants’ sake, that I may not destroy them all.

23:65:9.text: I will bring offspring out of Jacob, and out of Judah an inheritor of my mountains. My chosen will inherit it, and my servants will dwell there.

23:66:1.text: The LORD says: “Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool. What kind of house will you build to me? Where will I rest?

23:66:10.text: “Rejoice with Jerusalem, and be glad for her, all you who love her. Rejoice for joy with her, all you who mourn over her;

23:66:11.text: that you may nurse and be satisfied at the comforting breasts; that you may drink deeply, and be delighted with the abundance of her glory.”

23:66:12.text: For the LORD says, “Behold, I will extend peace to her like a river, and the glory of the nations like an overflowing stream, and you will nurse. You will be carried on her side, and will be dandled on her knees.

23:66:13.text: As one whom his mother comforts, so I will comfort you. You will be comforted in Jerusalem.”

23:66:14.text: You will see it, and your heart shall rejoice, and your bones will flourish like the tender grass. The LORD’s hand will be known amongst his servants; and he will have indignation against his enemies.

23:66:15.text: For, behold, the LORD will come with fire, and his chariots will be like the whirlwind; to give his anger with fierceness, and his rebuke with flames of fire.

23:66:16.text: For the LORD will execute judgement by fire and by his sword on all flesh; and those slain by the LORD will be many.

23:66:17.text: “Those who sanctify themselves and purify themselves to go to the gardens, following one in the middle, eating pig’s meat, abominable things, and the mouse, they shall come to an end together,” says the LORD.

23:66:18.text: “For I know their works and their thoughts. The time comes that I will gather all nations and languages, and they will come, and will see my glory.

23:66:19.text: “I will set a sign amongst them, and I will send those who escape of them to the nations, to Tarshish, Pul, and Lud, who draw the bow, to Tubal and Javan, to far-away islands, who have not heard my fame, nor have seen my glory; and they shall declare my glory amongst the nations.

23:66:2.text: For my hand has made all these things, and so all these things came to be,” says the LORD: “but I will look to this man, even to he who is poor and of a contrite spirit, and who trembles at my word.

23:66:20.text: They shall bring all your brothers out of all the nations for an offering to the LORD, on horses, in chariots, in litters, on mules, and on camels, to my holy mountain Jerusalem, says the LORD, as the children of Israel bring their offering in a clean vessel into the LORD’s house.

23:66:21.text: Of them I will also select priests and Levites,” says the LORD.

23:66:22.text: “For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, shall remain before me,” says the LORD, “so your offspring and your name shall remain.

23:66:23.text: It shall happen that from one new moon to another, and from one Sabbath to another, all flesh will come to worship before me,” says the LORD.

23:66:24.text: “They will go out, and look at the dead bodies of the men who have transgressed against me; for their worm will not die, nor will their fire be quenched, and they will be loathsome to all mankind.”

23:66:3.text: He who kills an ox is as he who kills a man; he who sacrifices a lamb, as he who breaks a dog’s neck; he who offers an offering, as he who offers pig’s blood; he who burns frankincense, as he who blesses an idol. Yes, they have chosen their own ways, and their soul delights in their abominations.
