23:66:4.text: I also will choose their delusions, and will bring their fears on them, because when I called, no one answered; when I spoke, they didn’t listen, but they did that which was evil in my eyes, and chose that in which I didn’t delight.”

23:66:5.text: Hear the LORD’s word, you who tremble at his word: “Your brothers who hate you, who cast you out for my name’s sake, have said, ‘Let the LORD be glorified, that we may see your joy;’ but it is those who shall be disappointed.

23:66:6.text: A voice of tumult from the city, a voice from the temple, a voice of the LORD that repays his enemies what they deserve.

23:66:7.text: “Before she travailed, she gave birth. Before her pain came, she delivered a son.

23:66:8.text: Who has heard of such a thing? Who has seen such things? Shall a land be born in one day? Shall a nation be born at once? For as soon as Zion travailed, she gave birth to her children.

23:66:9.text: Shall I bring to the birth, and not cause to be delivered?” says the LORD. “Shall I who cause to give birth shut the womb?” says your God.

23:6:1.text: In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up; and his train filled the temple.

23:6:10.text: Make the heart of this people fat. Make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their heart, and turn again, and be healed.”

23:6:11.text: Then I said, “Lord, how long?” He answered, “Until cities are waste without inhabitant, houses without man, the land becomes utterly waste,

23:6:12.text: and the LORD has removed men far away, and the forsaken places are many within the land.

23:6:13.text: If there is a tenth left in it, that also will in turn be consumed, as a terebinth, and as an oak whose stump remains when they are cut down, so the holy seed is its stump.”

23:6:2.text: Above him stood the seraphim. Each one had six wings. With two he covered his face. With two he covered his feet. With two he flew.

23:6:3.text: One called to another, and said, “Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of Armies! The whole earth is full of his glory!”

23:6:4.text: The foundations of the thresholds shook at the voice of him who called, and the house was filled with smoke.

23:6:5.text: Then I said, “Woe is me! For I am undone, because I am a man of unclean lips and I live amongst a people of unclean lips, for my eyes have seen the King, the LORD of Armies!”

23:6:6.text: Then one of the seraphim flew to me, having a live coal in his hand, which he had taken with the tongs from off the altar.

23:6:7.text: He touched my mouth with it, and said, “Behold, this has touched your lips; and your iniquity is taken away, and your sin forgiven.”

23:6:8.text: I heard the Lord’s voice, saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” Then I said, “Here I am. Send me!”

23:6:9.text: He said, “Go, and tell this people, ‘ You hear indeed, but don’t understand. You see indeed, but don’t perceive.’

23:7:1.text: In the days of Ahaz the son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin the king of Syria and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up to Jerusalem to war against it, but could not prevail against it.

23:7:10.text: The LORD spoke again to Ahaz, saying,

23:7:11.text: “Ask a sign of the LORD your God; ask it either in the depth, or in the height above.”

23:7:12.text: But Ahaz said, “I won’t ask. I won’t tempt the LORD.”

23:7:13.text: He said, “Listen now, house of David. Is it not enough for you to try the patience of men, that you will try the patience of my God also?

23:7:14.text: Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign. Behold, the virgin will conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.

23:7:15.text: He shall eat butter and honey when he knows to refuse the evil and choose the good.

23:7:16.text: For before the child knows to refuse the evil and choose the good, the land whose two kings you abhor shall be forsaken.

23:7:17.text: The LORD will bring on you, on your people, and on your father’s house days that have not come, from the day that Ephraim departed from Judah, even the king of Assyria.

23:7:18.text: It will happen in that day that the LORD will whistle for the fly that is in the uttermost part of the rivers of Egypt, and for the bee that is in the land of Assyria.

23:7:19.text: They shall come, and shall all rest in the desolate valleys, in the clefts of the rocks, on all thorn hedges, and on all pastures.

23:7:2.text: David’s house was told, “Syria is allied with Ephraim.” His heart trembled, and the heart of his people, as the trees of the forest tremble with the wind.

23:7:20.text: In that day the Lord will shave with a razor that is hired in the parts beyond the River, even with the king of Assyria, the head and the hair of the feet; and it shall also consume the beard.

23:7:21.text: It shall happen in that day that a man shall keep alive a young cow, and two sheep.

23:7:22.text: It shall happen, that because of the abundance of milk which they shall give he shall eat butter, for everyone will eat butter and honey that is left within the land.

23:7:23.text: It will happen in that day that every place where there were a thousand vines worth a thousand silver shekels, will be for briers and thorns.

23:7:24.text: People will go there with arrows and with bow, because all the land will be briers and thorns.

23:7:25.text: All the hills that were cultivated with the hoe, you shall not come there for fear of briers and thorns; but it shall be for the sending out of oxen, and for sheep to tread on.”

23:7:3.text: Then the LORD said to Isaiah, “Go out now to meet Ahaz, you, and Shearjashub your son, at the end of the conduit of the upper pool, on the highway of the fuller’s field.

23:7:4.text: Tell him, ‘ Be careful, and keep calm. Don’t be afraid, neither let your heart be faint because of these two tails of smoking torches, for the fierce anger of Rezin and Syria, and of the son of Remaliah.

23:7:5.text: Because Syria, Ephraim, and the son of Remaliah, have plotted evil against you, saying,

23:7:6.text: “Let’s go up against Judah, and tear it apart, and let’s divide it amongst ourselves, and set up a king within it, even the son of Tabeel.”

23:7:7.text: This is what the Lord GOD says: “It shall not stand, neither shall it happen.”

23:7:8.text: For the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin. Within sixty-five years Ephraim shall be broken in pieces, so that it shall not be a people.

23:7:9.text: The head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliah’s son. If you will not believe, surely you shall not be established.’ ”

23:8:1.text: The LORD said to me, “Take a large tablet, and write on it with a man’s pen, ‘ For Maher Shalal Hash Baz’ ;

23:8:10.text: Take counsel together, and it will be brought to nothing; speak the word, and it will not stand, for God is with us.”

23:8:11.text: For the LORD spoke this to me with a strong hand, and instructed me not to walk in the way of this people, saying,

23:8:12.text: “Don’t call a conspiracy all that this people call a conspiracy. Don’t fear their threats or be terrorised.

23:8:13.text: The LORD of Armies is who you must respect as holy. He is the one you must fear. He is the one you must dread.

23:8:14.text: He will be a sanctuary, but for both houses of Israel, he will be a stumbling stone and a rock that makes them fall. For the people of Jerusalem, he will be a trap and a snare.

23:8:15.text: Many will stumble over it, fall, be broken, be snared, and be captured.”

23:8:16.text: Wrap up the covenant. Seal the law amongst my disciples.

23:8:17.text: I will wait for the LORD, who hides his face from the house of Jacob, and I will look for him.

23:8:18.text: Behold, I and the children whom the LORD has given me are for signs and for wonders in Israel from the LORD of Armies, who dwells in Mount Zion.

23:8:19.text: When they tell you, “Consult with those who have familiar spirits and with the wizards, who chirp and who mutter,” shouldn’t a people consult with their God? Should they consult the dead on behalf of the living?

23:8:2.text: and I will take for myself faithful witnesses to testify: Uriah the priest, and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah.”

23:8:20.text: Turn to the law and to the covenant! If they don’t speak according to this word, surely there is no morning for them.

23:8:21.text: They will pass through it, very distressed and hungry. It will happen that when they are hungry, they will worry, and curse their king and their God. They will turn their faces upward,

23:8:22.text: then look to the earth and see distress, darkness, and the gloom of anguish. They will be driven into thick darkness.

23:8:3.text: I went to the prophetess, and she conceived, and bore a son. Then the LORD said to me, “Call his name ‘Maher Shalal Hash Baz.’

23:8:4.text: For before the child knows how to say, ‘ My father’ and ‘ My mother,’ the riches of Damascus and the plunder of Samaria will be carried away by the king of Assyria.”

23:8:5.text: The LORD spoke to me yet again, saying,

23:8:6.text: “Because this people has refused the waters of Shiloah that go softly, and rejoice in Rezin and Remaliah’s son;

23:8:7.text: now therefore, behold, the Lord brings upon them the mighty flood waters of the River: the king of Assyria and all his glory. It will come up over all its channels, and go over all its banks.

23:8:8.text: It will sweep onward into Judah. It will overflow and pass through. It will reach even to the neck. The stretching out of its wings will fill the width of your land, O Immanuel.

23:8:9.text: Make an uproar, you peoples, and be broken in pieces! Listen, all you from far countries: dress for battle, and be shattered! Dress for battle, and be shattered!

23:9:1.text: But there shall be no more gloom for her who was in anguish. In the former time, he brought into contempt the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali; but in the latter time he has made it glorious, by the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.

23:9:10.text: “The bricks have fallen, but we will build with cut stone. The sycamore fig trees have been cut down, but we will put cedars in their place.”

23:9:11.text: Therefore the LORD will set up on high against him the adversaries of Rezin, and will stir up his enemies,

23:9:12.text: The Syrians in front, and the Philistines behind; and they will devour Israel with open mouth. For all this, his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.

23:9:13.text: Yet the people have not turned to him who struck them, neither have they sought the LORD of Armies.

23:9:14.text: Therefore the LORD will cut off from Israel head and tail, palm branch and reed, in one day.

23:9:15.text: The elder and the honourable man is the head, and the prophet who teaches lies is the tail.

23:9:16.text: For those who lead this people lead them astray; and those who are led by them are destroyed.

23:9:17.text: Therefore the Lord will not rejoice over their young men, neither will he have compassion on their fatherless and widows; for everyone is profane and an evildoer, and every mouth speaks folly. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.

23:9:18.text: For wickedness burns like a fire. It devours the briers and thorns; yes, it kindles in the thickets of the forest, and they roll upward in a column of smoke.

23:9:19.text: Through the LORD of Armies’ wrath, the land is burnt up; and the people are the fuel for the fire. No one spares his brother.

23:9:2.text: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light. The light has shined on those who lived in the land of the shadow of death.

23:9:20.text: One will devour on the right hand, and be hungry; and he will eat on the left hand, and they will not be satisfied. Everyone will eat the flesh of his own arm:

23:9:21.text: Manasseh eating Ephraim and Ephraim eating Manasseh, and they together will be against Judah. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.

23:9:3.text: You have multiplied the nation. You have increased their joy. They rejoice before you according to the joy in harvest, as men rejoice when they divide the plunder.

23:9:4.text: For the yoke of his burden, and the staff of his shoulder, the rod of his oppressor, you have broken as in the day of Midian.

23:9:5.text: For all the armour of the armed man in the noisy battle, and the garments rolled in blood, will be for burning, fuel for the fire.

23:9:6.text: For a child is born to us. A son is given to us; and the government will be on his shoulders. His name will be called Wonderful Counsellor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

23:9:7.text: Of the increase of his government and of peace there shall be no end, on David’s throne, and on his kingdom, to establish it, and to uphold it with justice and with righteousness from that time on, even forever. The zeal of the LORD of Armies will perform this.

23:9:8.text: The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it falls on Israel.

23:9:9.text: All the people will know, including Ephraim and the inhabitants of Samaria, who say in pride and in arrogance of heart,

29:2:1.text: Blow the trumpet in Zion, and sound an alarm in my holy mountain! Let all the inhabitants of the land tremble, for the day of the LORD comes, for it is close at hand:

29:2:10.text: The earth quakes before them. The heavens tremble. The sun and the moon are darkened, and the stars withdraw their shining.

29:2:11.text: The LORD thunders his voice before his army, for his forces are very great; for he is strong who obeys his command; for the day of the LORD is great and very awesome, and who can endure it?

29:2:12.text: “Yet even now,” says the LORD, “turn to me with all your heart, and with fasting, and with weeping, and with mourning.”

29:2:13.text: Tear your heart and not your garments, and turn to the LORD, your God; for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, and relents from sending calamity.

29:2:14.text: Who knows? He may turn and relent, and leave a blessing behind him, even a meal offering and a drink offering to the LORD, your God.

29:2:15.text: Blow the trumpet in Zion! Sanctify a fast. Call a solemn assembly.

29:2:16.text: Gather the people. Sanctify the assembly. Assemble the elders. Gather the children, and those who nurse from breasts. Let the bridegroom go out of his room, and the bride out of her chamber.

29:2:17.text: Let the priests, the ministers of the LORD, weep between the porch and the altar, and let them say, “Spare your people, LORD, and don’t give your heritage to reproach, that the nations should rule over them. Why should they say amongst the peoples, ‘ Where is their God?’ ”

29:2:18.text: Then the LORD was jealous for his land, and had pity on his people.

29:2:19.text: The LORD answered his people, “Behold, I will send you grain, new wine, and oil, and you will be satisfied with them; and I will no more make you a reproach amongst the nations.

29:2:2.text: A day of darkness and gloominess, a day of clouds and thick darkness. As the dawn spreading on the mountains, a great and strong people; there has never been the like, neither will there be any more after them, even to the years of many generations.

29:2:20.text: But I will remove the northern army far away from you, and will drive it into a barren and desolate land, its front into the eastern sea, and its back into the western sea; and its stench will come up, and its bad smell will rise.” Surely he has done great things.

29:2:21.text: Land, don’t be afraid. Be glad and rejoice, for the LORD has done great things.

29:2:22.text: Don’t be afraid, you animals of the field; for the pastures of the wilderness spring up, for the tree bears its fruit. The fig tree and the vine yield their strength.

29:2:23.text: “Be glad then, you children of Zion, and rejoice in the LORD, your God; for he gives you the early rain in just measure, and he causes the rain to come down for you, the early rain and the latter rain, as before.

29:2:24.text: The threshing floors will be full of wheat, and the vats will overflow with new wine and oil.

29:2:25.text: I will restore to you the years that the swarming locust has eaten, the great locust, the grasshopper, and the caterpillar, my great army, which I sent amongst you.

29:2:26.text: You will have plenty to eat and be satisfied, and will praise the name of the LORD, your God, who has dealt wondrously with you; and my people will never again be disappointed.

29:2:27.text: You will know that I am amongst Israel, and that I am the LORD, your God, and there is no one else; and my people will never again be disappointed.

29:2:28.text: “It will happen afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; and your sons and your daughters will prophesy. Your old men will dream dreams. Your young men will see visions.

29:2:29.text: And also on the servants and on the handmaids in those days, I will pour out my Spirit.

29:2:3.text: A fire devours before them, and behind them, a flame burns. The land is as the garden of Eden before them, and behind them, a desolate wilderness. Yes, and no one has escaped them.

29:2:30.text: I will show wonders in the heavens and in the earth: blood, fire, and pillars of smoke.

29:2:31.text: The sun will be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and terrible day of the LORD comes.

29:2:32.text: It will happen that whoever will call on the LORD’s name shall be saved; for in Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be those who escape, as the LORD has said, and amongst the remnant, those whom the LORD calls.

29:2:4.text: Their appearance is as the appearance of horses, and they run as horsemen.

29:2:5.text: Like the noise of chariots on the tops of the mountains, they leap, like the noise of a flame of fire that devours the stubble, like a strong people set in battle array.

29:2:6.text: At their presence the peoples are in anguish. All faces have grown pale.

29:2:7.text: They run like mighty men. They climb the wall like warriors. They each march in his line, and they don’t swerve off course.

29:2:8.text: One doesn’t jostle another. They each march in their own path. They burst through the defences and don’t break ranks.

29:2:9.text: They rush on the city. They run on the wall. They climb up into the houses. They enter in at the windows like thieves.

29:3:1.text: “For, behold, in those days, and in that time, when I restore the fortunes of Judah and Jerusalem,

29:3:10.text: Beat your ploughshares into swords, and your pruning hooks into spears. Let the weak say, ‘I am strong.’

29:3:11.text: Hurry and come, all you surrounding nations, and gather yourselves together.” Cause your mighty ones to come down there, LORD.

29:3:12.text: “Let the nations arouse themselves, and come up to the valley of Jehoshaphat; for there I will sit to judge all the surrounding nations.

29:3:13.text: Put in the sickle; for the harvest is ripe. Come, tread, for the wine press is full, the vats overflow, for their wickedness is great.”

29:3:14.text: Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision! For the day of the LORD is near in the valley of decision.

29:3:15.text: The sun and the moon are darkened, and the stars withdraw their shining.

29:3:16.text: The LORD will roar from Zion, and thunder from Jerusalem; and the heavens and the earth will shake; but the LORD will be a refuge to his people, and a stronghold to the children of Israel.

29:3:17.text: “So you will know that I am the LORD, your God, dwelling in Zion, my holy mountain. Then Jerusalem will be holy, and no strangers will pass through her any more.

29:3:18.text: It will happen in that day, that the mountains will drop down sweet wine, the hills will flow with milk, all the brooks of Judah will flow with waters; and a fountain will flow out from the LORD’s house, and will water the valley of Shittim.

29:3:19.text: Egypt will be a desolation and Edom will be a desolate wilderness, for the violence done to the children of Judah, because they have shed innocent blood in their land.

29:3:2.text: I will gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat; and I will execute judgement on them there for my people, and for my heritage, Israel, whom they have scattered amongst the nations. They have divided my land,

29:3:20.text: But Judah will be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.

29:3:21.text: I will cleanse their blood that I have not cleansed, for the LORD dwells in Zion.”

29:3:3.text: and have cast lots for my people, and have given a boy for a prostitute, and sold a girl for wine, that they may drink.

29:3:4.text: “Yes, and what are you to me, Tyre and Sidon, and all the regions of Philistia? Will you repay me? And if you repay me, I will swiftly and speedily return your repayment on your own head.

29:3:5.text: Because you have taken my silver and my gold, and have carried my finest treasures into your temples,

29:3:6.text: and have sold the children of Judah and the children of Jerusalem to the sons of the Greeks, that you may remove them far from their border.

29:3:7.text: Behold, I will stir them up out of the place where you have sold them, and will return your repayment on your own head;

29:3:8.text: and I will sell your sons and your daughters into the hands of the children of Judah, and they will sell them to the men of Sheba, to a faraway nation, for the LORD has spoken it.”

29:3:9.text: Proclaim this amongst the nations: “Prepare for war! Stir up the mighty men. Let all the warriors draw near. Let them come up.

38:8:1.text: The word of the LORD of Armies came to me.

38:8:10.text: For before those days there was no wages for man nor any wages for an animal, neither was there any peace to him who went out or came in, because of the adversary. For I set all men everyone against his neighbour.

38:8:11.text: But now I will not be to the remnant of this people as in the former days,” says the LORD of Armies.

38:8:12.text: “For the seed of peace and the vine will yield its fruit, and the ground will give its increase, and the heavens will give their dew. I will cause the remnant of this people to inherit all these things.

38:8:13.text: It shall come to pass that, as you were a curse amongst the nations, house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will save you, and you shall be a blessing. Don’t be afraid. Let your hands be strong.”

38:8:14.text: For the LORD of Armies says: “As I thought to do evil to you when your fathers provoked me to wrath,” says the LORD of Armies, “and I didn’t repent,

38:8:15.text: so again I have thought in these days to do good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah. Don’t be afraid.

38:8:16.text: These are the things that you shall do: speak every man the truth with his neighbour. Execute the judgement of truth and peace in your gates,

38:8:17.text: and let none of you devise evil in your hearts against his neighbour, and love no false oath; for all these are things that I hate,” says the LORD.

38:8:18.text: The word of the LORD of Armies came to me.

38:8:19.text: The LORD of Armies says: “The fasts of the fourth, fifth, seventh, and tenth months shall be for the house of Judah joy, gladness, and cheerful feasts. Therefore love truth and peace.”

38:8:2.text: The LORD of Armies says: “I am jealous for Zion with great jealousy, and I am jealous for her with great wrath.”

38:8:20.text: The LORD of Armies says: “Many peoples and the inhabitants of many cities will yet come.

38:8:21.text: The inhabitants of one will go to another, saying, ‘ Let’s go speedily to entreat the favour of the LORD, and to seek the LORD of Armies. I will go also.’

38:8:22.text: Yes, many peoples and strong nations will come to seek the LORD of Armies in Jerusalem and to entreat the favour of the LORD.”

38:8:23.text: The LORD of Armies says: “In those days, ten men out of all the languages of the nations will take hold of the skirt of him who is a Jew, saying, ‘ We will go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.’ ”

38:8:3.text: The LORD says: “I have returned to Zion, and will dwell in the middle of Jerusalem. Jerusalem shall be called ‘ The City of Truth;’ and the mountain of the LORD of Armies, ‘ The Holy Mountain.’ ”

38:8:4.text: The LORD of Armies says: “Old men and old women will again dwell in the streets of Jerusalem, every man with his staff in his hand because of their old age.

38:8:5.text: The streets of the city will be full of boys and girls playing in its streets.”

38:8:6.text: The LORD of Armies says: “If it is marvellous in the eyes of the remnant of this people in those days, should it also be marvellous in my eyes?” says the LORD of Armies.

38:8:7.text: The LORD of Armies says: “Behold, I will save my people from the east country and from the west country.

38:8:8.text: I will bring them, and they will dwell within Jerusalem. They will be my people, and I will be their God, in truth and in righteousness.”

38:8:9.text: The LORD of Armies says: “Let your hands be strong, you who hear in these days these words from the mouth of the prophets who were in the day that the foundation of the house of the LORD of Armies was laid, even the temple, that it might be built.

40:10:1.text: He called to himself his twelve disciples, and gave them authority over unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal every disease and every sickness.

40:10:10.text: Take no bag for your journey, neither two coats, nor sandals, nor staff: for the labourer is worthy of his food.

40:10:11.text: Into whatever city or village you enter, find out who in it is worthy, and stay there until you go on.

40:10:12.text: As you enter into the household, greet it.

40:10:13.text: If the household is worthy, let your peace come on it, but if it isn’t worthy, let your peace return to you.

40:10:14.text: Whoever doesn’t receive you or hear your words, as you go out of that house or that city, shake the dust off your feet.

40:10:15.text: Most certainly I tell you, it will be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgement than for that city.

40:10:16.text: “Behold, I send you out as sheep amongst wolves. Therefore be wise as serpents and harmless as doves.

40:10:17.text: But beware of men, for they will deliver you up to councils, and in their synagogues they will scourge you.

40:10:18.text: Yes, and you will be brought before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony to them and to the nations.

40:10:19.text: But when they deliver you up, don’t be anxious how or what you will say, for it will be given you in that hour what you will say.

40:10:2.text: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these. The first, Simon, who is called Peter; Andrew, his brother; James the son of Zebedee; John, his brother;

40:10:20.text: For it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father who speaks in you.

40:10:21.text: “Brother will deliver up brother to death, and the father his child. Children will rise up against parents and cause them to be put to death.

40:10:22.text: You will be hated by all men for my name’s sake, but he who endures to the end will be saved.

40:10:23.text: But when they persecute you in this city, flee into the next, for most certainly I tell you, you will not have gone through the cities of Israel until the Son of Man has come.

40:10:24.text: “A disciple is not above his teacher, nor a servant above his lord.

40:10:25.text: It is enough for the disciple that he be like his teacher, and the servant like his lord. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebul, how much more those of his household!

40:10:26.text: Therefore don’t be afraid of them, for there is nothing covered that will not be revealed, or hidden that will not be known.

40:10:27.text: What I tell you in the darkness, speak in the light; and what you hear whispered in the ear, proclaim on the housetops.

40:10:28.text: Don’t be afraid of those who kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul. Rather, fear him who is able to destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.

40:10:29.text: “Aren’t two sparrows sold for an assarion coin? Not one of them falls to the ground apart from your Father’s will.

40:10:3.text: Philip; Bartholomew; Thomas; Matthew the tax collector; James the son of Alphaeus; Lebbaeus, who was also called Thaddaeus;

40:10:30.text: But the very hairs of your head are all numbered.

40:10:31.text: Therefore don’t be afraid. You are of more value than many sparrows.

40:10:32.text: Everyone therefore who confesses me before men, I will also confess him before my Father who is in heaven.

40:10:33.text: But whoever denies me before men, I will also deny him before my Father who is in heaven.

40:10:34.text: “Don’t think that I came to send peace on the earth. I didn’t come to send peace, but a sword.

40:10:35.text: For I came to set a man at odds against his father, and a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.

40:10:36.text: A man’s foes will be those of his own household.

40:10:37.text: He who loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me; and he who loves son or daughter more than me isn’t worthy of me.

40:10:38.text: He who doesn’t take his cross and follow after me isn’t worthy of me.

40:10:39.text: He who seeks his life will lose it; and he who loses his life for my sake will find it.

40:10:4.text: Simon the Zealot; and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.

40:10:40.text: “He who receives you receives me, and he who receives me receives him who sent me.

40:10:41.text: He who receives a prophet in the name of a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward. He who receives a righteous man in the name of a righteous man will receive a righteous man’s reward.

40:10:42.text: Whoever gives one of these little ones just a cup of cold water to drink in the name of a disciple, most certainly I tell you, he will in no way lose his reward.”

40:10:5.text: Jesus sent these twelve out and commanded them, saying, “Don’t go amongst the Gentiles, and don’t enter into any city of the Samaritans.

40:10:6.text: Rather, go to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.

40:10:7.text: As you go, preach, saying, ‘ The Kingdom of Heaven is at hand!’

40:10:8.text: Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, and cast out demons. Freely you received, so freely give.

40:10:9.text: Don’t take any gold, silver, or brass in your money belts.

40:11:1.text: When Jesus had finished directing his twelve disciples, he departed from there to teach and preach in their cities.

40:11:10.text: For this is he, of whom it is written, ‘ Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you.’

40:11:11.text: Most certainly I tell you, amongst those who are born of women there has not arisen anyone greater than John the Baptiser; yet he who is least in the Kingdom of Heaven is greater than he.

40:11:12.text: From the days of John the Baptiser until now, the Kingdom of Heaven suffers violence, and the violent take it by force.

40:11:13.text: For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John.

40:11:14.text: If you are willing to receive it, this is Elijah, who is to come.

40:11:15.text: He who has ears to hear, let him hear.

40:11:16.text: “But to what shall I compare this generation? It is like children sitting in the marketplaces, who call to their companions

40:11:17.text: and say, ‘ We played the flute for you, and you didn’t dance. We mourned for you, and you didn’t lament.’

40:11:18.text: For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, ‘ He has a demon.’

40:11:19.text: The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, ‘ Behold, a gluttonous man and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’ But wisdom is justified by her children.”

40:11:2.text: Now when John heard in the prison the works of Christ, he sent two of his disciples

40:11:20.text: Then he began to denounce the cities in which most of his mighty works had been done, because they didn’t repent.

40:11:21.text: “Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon which were done in you, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.

40:11:22.text: But I tell you, it will be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon on the day of judgement than for you.

40:11:23.text: You, Capernaum, who are exalted to heaven, you will go down to Hades. For if the mighty works had been done in Sodom which were done in you, it would have remained until today.

40:11:24.text: But I tell you that it will be more tolerable for the land of Sodom on the day of judgement, than for you.”

40:11:25.text: At that time, Jesus answered, “I thank you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you hid these things from the wise and understanding, and revealed them to infants.

40:11:26.text: Yes, Father, for so it was well-pleasing in your sight.

40:11:27.text: All things have been delivered to me by my Father. No one knows the Son, except the Father; neither does anyone know the Father, except the Son and he to whom the Son desires to reveal him.

40:11:28.text: “Come to me, all you who labour and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.

40:11:29.text: Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart; and you will find rest for your souls.

40:11:3.text: and said to him, “Are you he who comes, or should we look for another?”

40:11:30.text: For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.”

40:11:4.text: Jesus answered them, “Go and tell John the things which you hear and see:

40:11:5.text: the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have good news preached to them.

40:11:6.text: Blessed is he who finds no occasion for stumbling in me.”

40:11:7.text: As these went their way, Jesus began to say to the multitudes concerning John, “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?

40:11:8.text: But what did you go out to see? A man in soft clothing? Behold, those who wear soft clothing are in kings’ houses.

40:11:9.text: But why did you go out? To see a prophet? Yes, I tell you, and much more than a prophet.

40:12:1.text: At that time, Jesus went on the Sabbath day through the grain fields. His disciples were hungry and began to pluck heads of grain and to eat.

40:12:10.text: And behold, there was a man with a withered hand. They asked him, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath day?” so that they might accuse him.

40:12:11.text: He said to them, “What man is there amongst you who has one sheep, and if this one falls into a pit on the Sabbath day, won’t he grab on to it and lift it out?

40:12:12.text: Of how much more value then is a man than a sheep! Therefore it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath day.”

40:12:13.text: Then he told the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He stretched it out; and it was restored whole, just like the other.

40:12:14.text: But the Pharisees went out and conspired against him, how they might destroy him.

40:12:15.text: Jesus, perceiving that, withdrew from there. Great multitudes followed him; and he healed them all,

40:12:16.text: and commanded them that they should not make him known,

40:12:17.text: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying,

40:12:18.text: “Behold, my servant whom I have chosen, my beloved in whom my soul is well pleased. I will put my Spirit on him. He will proclaim justice to the nations.

40:12:19.text: He will not strive, nor shout, neither will anyone hear his voice in the streets.

40:12:2.text: But the Pharisees, when they saw it, said to him, “Behold, your disciples do what is not lawful to do on the Sabbath.”

40:12:20.text: He won’t break a bruised reed. He won’t quench a smoking flax, until he leads justice to victory.

40:12:21.text: In his name, the nations will hope.”

40:12:22.text: Then one possessed by a demon, blind and mute, was brought to him; and he healed him, so that the blind and mute man both spoke and saw.

40:12:23.text: All the multitudes were amazed, and said, “Can this be the son of David?”

40:12:24.text: But when the Pharisees heard it, they said, “This man does not cast out demons except by Beelzebul, the prince of the demons.”

40:12:25.text: Knowing their thoughts, Jesus said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation, and every city or house divided against itself will not stand.

40:12:26.text: If Satan casts out Satan, he is divided against himself. How then will his kingdom stand?

40:12:27.text: If I by Beelzebul cast out demons, by whom do your children cast them out? Therefore they will be your judges.

40:12:28.text: But if I by the Spirit of God cast out demons, then God’s Kingdom has come upon you.

40:12:29.text: Or how can one enter into the house of the strong man and plunder his goods, unless he first bind the strong man? Then he will plunder his house.

40:12:3.text: But he said to them, “Haven’t you read what David did when he was hungry, and those who were with him:

40:12:30.text: “He who is not with me is against me, and he who doesn’t gather with me, scatters.

40:12:31.text: Therefore I tell you, every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven men, but the blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven men.

40:12:32.text: Whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man, it will be forgiven him; but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit, it will not be forgiven him, either in this age, or in that which is to come.

40:12:33.text: “Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree corrupt and its fruit corrupt; for the tree is known by its fruit.

40:12:34.text: You offspring of vipers, how can you, being evil, speak good things? For out of the abundance of the heart, the mouth speaks.

40:12:35.text: The good man out of his good treasure brings out good things, and the evil man out of his evil treasure brings out evil things.

40:12:36.text: I tell you that every idle word that men speak, they will give account of it in the day of judgement.

40:12:37.text: For by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.”

40:12:38.text: Then certain of the scribes and Pharisees answered, “Teacher, we want to see a sign from you.”

40:12:39.text: But he answered them, “An evil and adulterous generation seeks after a sign, but no sign will be given to it but the sign of Jonah the prophet.

40:12:4.text: how he entered into God’s house and ate the show bread, which was not lawful for him to eat, nor for those who were with him, but only for the priests?

40:12:40.text: For as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the huge fish, so will the Son of Man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.

40:12:41.text: The men of Nineveh will stand up in the judgement with this generation and will condemn it, for they repented at the preaching of Jonah; and behold, someone greater than Jonah is here.

40:12:42.text: The Queen of the South will rise up in the judgement with this generation and will condemn it, for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and behold, someone greater than Solomon is here.

40:12:43.text: “When an unclean spirit has gone out of a man, he passes through waterless places seeking rest, and doesn’t find it.

40:12:44.text: Then he says, ‘ I will return into my house from which I came;’ and when he has come back, he finds it empty, swept, and put in order.

40:12:45.text: Then he goes and takes with himself seven other spirits more evil than he is, and they enter in and dwell there. The last state of that man becomes worse than the first. Even so will it be also to this evil generation.”

40:12:46.text: While he was yet speaking to the multitudes, behold, his mother and his brothers stood outside, seeking to speak to him.

40:12:47.text: One said to him, “Behold, your mother and your brothers stand outside, seeking to speak to you.”

40:12:48.text: But he answered him who spoke to him, “Who is my mother? Who are my brothers?”

40:12:49.text: He stretched out his hand towards his disciples, and said, “Behold, my mother and my brothers!

40:12:5.text: Or have you not read in the law that on the Sabbath day the priests in the temple profane the Sabbath and are guiltless?

40:12:50.text: For whoever does the will of my Father who is in heaven, he is my brother, and sister, and mother.”

40:12:6.text: But I tell you that one greater than the temple is here.

40:12:7.text: But if you had known what this means, ‘ I desire mercy, and not sacrifice,’ you wouldn’t have condemned the guiltless.

40:12:8.text: For the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”

40:12:9.text: He departed from there and went into their synagogue.

40:13:1.text: On that day Jesus went out of the house and sat by the seaside.

40:13:10.text: The disciples came, and said to him, “Why do you speak to them in parables?”

40:13:11.text: He answered them, “To you it is given to know the mysteries of the Kingdom of Heaven, but it is not given to them.

40:13:12.text: For whoever has, to him will be given, and he will have abundance; but whoever doesn’t have, from him will be taken away even that which he has.

40:13:13.text: Therefore I speak to them in parables, because seeing they don’t see, and hearing, they don’t hear, neither do they understand.

40:13:14.text: In them the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled, which says, ‘ By hearing you will hear, and will in no way understand; Seeing you will see, and will in no way perceive;

40:13:15.text: for this people’s heart has grown callous, their ears are dull of hearing, and they have closed their eyes; or else perhaps they might perceive with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their heart, and would turn again, and I would heal them.’

40:13:16.text: “But blessed are your eyes, for they see; and your ears, for they hear.

40:13:17.text: For most certainly I tell you that many prophets and righteous men desired to see the things which you see, and didn’t see them; and to hear the things which you hear, and didn’t hear them.

40:13:18.text: “Hear, then, the parable of the farmer.

40:13:19.text: When anyone hears the word of the Kingdom and doesn’t understand it, the evil one comes and snatches away that which has been sown in his heart. This is what was sown by the roadside.

40:13:2.text: Great multitudes gathered to him, so that he entered into a boat and sat; and all the multitude stood on the beach.

40:13:20.text: What was sown on the rocky places, this is he who hears the word and immediately with joy receives it;

40:13:21.text: yet he has no root in himself, but endures for a while. When oppression or persecution arises because of the word, immediately he stumbles.

40:13:22.text: What was sown amongst the thorns, this is he who hears the word, but the cares of this age and the deceitfulness of riches choke the word, and he becomes unfruitful.

40:13:23.text: What was sown on the good ground, this is he who hears the word and understands it, who most certainly bears fruit and produces, some one hundred times as much, some sixty, and some thirty.”

40:13:24.text: He set another parable before them, saying, “The Kingdom of Heaven is like a man who sowed good seed in his field,

40:13:25.text: but while people slept, his enemy came and sowed darnel weeds also amongst the wheat, and went away.

40:13:26.text: But when the blade sprang up and produced grain, then the darnel weeds appeared also.

40:13:27.text: The servants of the householder came and said to him, ‘ Sir, didn’t you sow good seed in your field? Where did these darnel weeds come from?’

40:13:28.text: “He said to them, ‘ An enemy has done this.’ “The servants asked him, ‘ Do you want us to go and gather them up?’

40:13:29.text: “But he said, ‘ No, lest perhaps while you gather up the darnel weeds, you root up the wheat with them.

40:13:3.text: He spoke to them many things in parables, saying, “Behold, a farmer went out to sow.

40:13:30.text: Let both grow together until the harvest, and in the harvest time I will tell the reapers, “First, gather up the darnel weeds, and bind them in bundles to burn them; but gather the wheat into my barn.”’ ”

40:13:31.text: He set another parable before them, saying, “The Kingdom of Heaven is like a grain of mustard seed which a man took, and sowed in his field,

40:13:32.text: which indeed is smaller than all seeds. But when it is grown, it is greater than the herbs and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in its branches.”

40:13:33.text: He spoke another parable to them. “The Kingdom of Heaven is like yeast which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, until it was all leavened.”

40:13:34.text: Jesus spoke all these things in parables to the multitudes; and without a parable, he didn’t speak to them,

40:13:35.text: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through the prophet, saying, “I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden from the foundation of the world.”

40:13:36.text: Then Jesus sent the multitudes away, and went into the house. His disciples came to him, saying, “Explain to us the parable of the darnel weeds of the field.”

40:13:37.text: He answered them, “He who sows the good seed is the Son of Man,

40:13:38.text: the field is the world, the good seeds are the children of the Kingdom, and the darnel weeds are the children of the evil one.

40:13:39.text: The enemy who sowed them is the devil. The harvest is the end of the age, and the reapers are angels.

40:13:4.text: As he sowed, some seeds fell by the roadside, and the birds came and devoured them.

40:13:40.text: As therefore the darnel weeds are gathered up and burnt with fire; so will it be at the end of this age.

40:13:41.text: The Son of Man will send out his angels, and they will gather out of his Kingdom all things that cause stumbling and those who do iniquity,

40:13:42.text: and will cast them into the furnace of fire. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

40:13:43.text: Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the Kingdom of their Father. He who has ears to hear, let him hear.

40:13:44.text: “Again, the Kingdom of Heaven is like treasure hidden in the field, which a man found and hid. In his joy, he goes and sells all that he has and buys that field.

40:13:45.text: “Again, the Kingdom of Heaven is like a man who is a merchant seeking fine pearls,

40:13:46.text: who having found one pearl of great price, he went and sold all that he had and bought it.

40:13:47.text: “Again, the Kingdom of Heaven is like a dragnet that was cast into the sea and gathered some fish of every kind,

40:13:48.text: which, when it was filled, fishermen drew up on the beach. They sat down and gathered the good into containers, but the bad they threw away.

40:13:49.text: So it will be in the end of the world. The angels will come and separate the wicked from amongst the righteous,

40:13:5.text: Others fell on rocky ground, where they didn’t have much soil, and immediately they sprang up, because they had no depth of earth.

40:13:50.text: and will cast them into the furnace of fire. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.”

40:13:51.text: Jesus said to them, “Have you understood all these things?” They answered him, “Yes, Lord.”

40:13:52.text: He said to them, “Therefore every scribe who has been made a disciple in the Kingdom of Heaven is like a man who is a householder, who brings out of his treasure new and old things.”

40:13:53.text: When Jesus had finished these parables, he departed from there.

40:13:54.text: Coming into his own country, he taught them in their synagogue, so that they were astonished and said, “Where did this man get this wisdom and these mighty works?

40:13:55.text: Isn’t this the carpenter’s son? Isn’t his mother called Mary, and his brothers James, Joses, Simon, and Judas?

40:13:56.text: Aren’t all of his sisters with us? Where then did this man get all of these things?”

40:13:57.text: They were offended by him. But Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honour, except in his own country and in his own house.”

40:13:58.text: He didn’t do many mighty works there because of their unbelief.

40:13:6.text: When the sun had risen, they were scorched. Because they had no root, they withered away.

40:13:7.text: Others fell amongst thorns. The thorns grew up and choked them.

40:13:8.text: Others fell on good soil and yielded fruit: some one hundred times as much, some sixty, and some thirty.

40:13:9.text: He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”

40:14:1.text: At that time, Herod the tetrarch heard the report concerning Jesus,

40:14:10.text: and he sent and beheaded John in the prison.

40:14:11.text: His head was brought on a platter and given to the young lady; and she brought it to her mother.

40:14:12.text: His disciples came, took the body, and buried it. Then they went and told Jesus.

40:14:13.text: Now when Jesus heard this, he withdrew from there in a boat to a deserted place apart. When the multitudes heard it, they followed him on foot from the cities.

40:14:14.text: Jesus went out, and he saw a great multitude. He had compassion on them and healed their sick.

40:14:15.text: When evening had come, his disciples came to him, saying, “This place is deserted, and the hour is already late. Send the multitudes away, that they may go into the villages, and buy themselves food.”

40:14:16.text: But Jesus said to them, “They don’t need to go away. You give them something to eat.”

40:14:17.text: They told him, “We only have here five loaves and two fish.”

40:14:18.text: He said, “Bring them here to me.”

40:14:19.text: He commanded the multitudes to sit down on the grass; and he took the five loaves and the two fish, and looking up to heaven, he blessed, broke and gave the loaves to the disciples; and the disciples gave to the multitudes.

40:14:2.text: and said to his servants, “This is John the Baptiser. He is risen from the dead. That is why these powers work in him.”

40:14:20.text: They all ate and were filled. They took up twelve baskets full of that which remained left over from the broken pieces.

40:14:21.text: Those who ate were about five thousand men, in addition to women and children.

40:14:22.text: Immediately Jesus made the disciples get into the boat and go ahead of him to the other side, while he sent the multitudes away.

40:14:23.text: After he had sent the multitudes away, he went up into the mountain by himself to pray. When evening had come, he was there alone.

40:14:24.text: But the boat was now in the middle of the sea, distressed by the waves, for the wind was contrary.

40:14:25.text: In the fourth watch of the night, Jesus came to them, walking on the sea.

40:14:26.text: When the disciples saw him walking on the sea, they were troubled, saying, “It’s a ghost!” and they cried out for fear.

40:14:27.text: But immediately Jesus spoke to them, saying, “Cheer up! It is I! Don’t be afraid.”

40:14:28.text: Peter answered him and said, “Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you on the waters.”

40:14:29.text: He said, “Come!” Peter stepped down from the boat and walked on the waters to come to Jesus.

40:14:3.text: For Herod had arrested John, bound him, and put him in prison for the sake of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife.

40:14:30.text: But when he saw that the wind was strong, he was afraid, and beginning to sink, he cried out, saying, “Lord, save me!”

40:14:31.text: Immediately Jesus stretched out his hand, took hold of him, and said to him, “You of little faith, why did you doubt?”

40:14:32.text: When they got up into the boat, the wind ceased.

40:14:33.text: Those who were in the boat came and worshipped him, saying, “You are truly the Son of God!”

40:14:34.text: When they had crossed over, they came to the land of Gennesaret.

40:14:35.text: When the people of that place recognised him, they sent into all that surrounding region and brought to him all who were sick;

40:14:36.text: and they begged him that they might just touch the fringe of his garment. As many as touched it were made whole.

40:14:4.text: For John said to him, “It is not lawful for you to have her.”

40:14:5.text: When he would have put him to death, he feared the multitude, because they counted him as a prophet.

40:14:6.text: But when Herod’s birthday came, the daughter of Herodias danced amongst them and pleased Herod.

40:14:7.text: Therefore he promised with an oath to give her whatever she should ask.

40:14:8.text: She, being prompted by her mother, said, “Give me here on a platter the head of John the Baptiser.”

40:14:9.text: The king was grieved, but for the sake of his oaths and of those who sat at the table with him, he commanded it to be given,

40:15:1.text: Then Pharisees and scribes came to Jesus from Jerusalem, saying,

40:15:10.text: He summoned the multitude, and said to them, “Hear, and understand.

40:15:11.text: That which enters into the mouth doesn’t defile the man; but that which proceeds out of the mouth, this defiles the man.”

40:15:12.text: Then the disciples came and said to him, “Do you know that the Pharisees were offended when they heard this saying?”

40:15:13.text: But he answered, “Every plant which my heavenly Father didn’t plant will be uprooted.

40:15:14.text: Leave them alone. They are blind guides of the blind. If the blind guide the blind, both will fall into a pit.”

40:15:15.text: Peter answered him, “Explain the parable to us.”

40:15:16.text: So Jesus said, “Do you also still not understand?

40:15:17.text: Don’t you understand that whatever goes into the mouth passes into the belly and then out of the body?

40:15:18.text: But the things which proceed out of the mouth come out of the heart, and they defile the man.

40:15:19.text: For out of the heart come evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, sexual sins, thefts, false testimony, and blasphemies.

40:15:2.text: “Why do your disciples disobey the tradition of the elders? For they don’t wash their hands when they eat bread.”

40:15:20.text: These are the things which defile the man; but to eat with unwashed hands doesn’t defile the man.”

40:15:21.text: Jesus went out from there and withdrew into the region of Tyre and Sidon.

40:15:22.text: Behold, a Canaanite woman came out from those borders and cried, saying, “Have mercy on me, Lord, you son of David! My daughter is severely possessed by a demon!”

40:15:23.text: But he answered her not a word. His disciples came and begged him, saying, “Send her away; for she cries after us.”

40:15:24.text: But he answered, “I wasn’t sent to anyone but the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”

40:15:25.text: But she came and worshipped him, saying, “Lord, help me.”

40:15:26.text: But he answered, “It is not appropriate to take the children’s bread and throw it to the dogs.”

40:15:27.text: But she said, “Yes, Lord, but even the dogs eat the crumbs which fall from their masters’ table.”

40:15:28.text: Then Jesus answered her, “Woman, great is your faith! Be it done to you even as you desire.” And her daughter was healed from that hour.

40:15:29.text: Jesus departed from there and came near to the sea of Galilee; and he went up on the mountain and sat there.

40:15:3.text: He answered them, “Why do you also disobey the commandment of God because of your tradition?

40:15:30.text: Great multitudes came to him, having with them the lame, blind, mute, maimed, and many others, and they put them down at his feet. He healed them,

40:15:31.text: so that the multitude wondered when they saw the mute speaking, the injured healed, the lame walking, and the blind seeing — and they glorified the God of Israel.

40:15:32.text: Jesus summoned his disciples and said, “I have compassion on the multitude, because they have continued with me now three days and have nothing to eat. I don’t want to send them away fasting, or they might faint on the way.”

40:15:33.text: The disciples said to him, “Where could we get so many loaves in a deserted place as to satisfy so great a multitude?”

40:15:34.text: Jesus said to them, “How many loaves do you have?” They said, “Seven, and a few small fish.”

40:15:35.text: He commanded the multitude to sit down on the ground;

40:15:36.text: and he took the seven loaves and the fish. He gave thanks and broke them, and gave to the disciples, and the disciples to the multitudes.

40:15:37.text: They all ate and were filled. They took up seven baskets full of the broken pieces that were left over.

40:15:38.text: Those who ate were four thousand men, in addition to women and children.

40:15:39.text: Then he sent away the multitudes, got into the boat, and came into the borders of Magdala.

40:15:4.text: For God commanded, ‘ Honour your father and your mother,’ and, ‘ He who speaks evil of father or mother, let him be put to death.’

40:15:5.text: But you say, ‘ Whoever may tell his father or his mother, “Whatever help you might otherwise have gotten from me is a gift devoted to God,”

40:15:6.text: he shall not honour his father or mother.’ You have made the commandment of God void because of your tradition.

40:15:7.text: You hypocrites! Well did Isaiah prophesy of you, saying,

40:15:8.text: ‘ These people draw near to me with their mouth, and honour me with their lips; but their heart is far from me.

40:15:9.text: And they worship me in vain, teaching as doctrine rules made by men.’ ”

40:16:1.text: The Pharisees and Sadducees came, and testing him, asked him to show them a sign from heaven.

40:16:10.text: or the seven loaves for the four thousand, and how many baskets you took up?

40:16:11.text: How is it that you don’t perceive that I didn’t speak to you concerning bread? But beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”

40:16:12.text: Then they understood that he didn’t tell them to beware of the yeast of bread, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.

40:16:13.text: Now when Jesus came into the parts of Caesarea Philippi, he asked his disciples, saying, “Who do men say that I, the Son of Man, am?”

40:16:14.text: They said, “Some say John the Baptiser, some, Elijah, and others, Jeremiah or one of the prophets.”

40:16:15.text: He said to them, “But who do you say that I am?”

40:16:16.text: Simon Peter answered, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”

40:16:17.text: Jesus answered him, “Blessed are you, Simon Bar Jonah, for flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but my Father who is in heaven.

40:16:18.text: I also tell you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my assembly, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it.

40:16:19.text: I will give to you the keys of the Kingdom of Heaven, and whatever you bind on earth will have been bound in heaven; and whatever you release on earth will have been released in heaven.”

40:16:2.text: But he answered them, “When it is evening, you say, ‘ It will be fair weather, for the sky is red.’

40:16:20.text: Then he commanded the disciples that they should tell no one that he was Jesus the Christ.

40:16:21.text: From that time, Jesus began to show his disciples that he must go to Jerusalem and suffer many things from the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and the third day be raised up.

40:16:22.text: Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him, saying, “Far be it from you, Lord! This will never be done to you.”

40:16:23.text: But he turned and said to Peter, “Get behind me, Satan! You are a stumbling block to me, for you are not setting your mind on the things of God, but on the things of men.”

40:16:24.text: Then Jesus said to his disciples, “If anyone desires to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me.

40:16:25.text: For whoever desires to save his life will lose it, and whoever will lose his life for my sake will find it.

40:16:26.text: For what will it profit a man if he gains the whole world and forfeits his life? Or what will a man give in exchange for his life?

40:16:27.text: For the Son of Man will come in the glory of his Father with his angels, and then he will give to everyone according to his deeds.

40:16:28.text: Most certainly I tell you, there are some standing here who will in no way taste of death until they see the Son of Man coming in his Kingdom.”

40:16:3.text: In the morning, ‘ It will be foul weather today, for the sky is red and threatening.’ Hypocrites! You know how to discern the appearance of the sky, but you can’t discern the signs of the times!

40:16:4.text: An evil and adulterous generation seeks after a sign, and there will be no sign given to it, except the sign of the prophet Jonah.” He left them and departed.

40:16:5.text: The disciples came to the other side and had forgotten to take bread.

40:16:6.text: Jesus said to them, “Take heed and beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”

40:16:7.text: They reasoned amongst themselves, saying, “We brought no bread.”

40:16:8.text: Jesus, perceiving it, said, “Why do you reason amongst yourselves, you of little faith, because you have brought no bread?

40:16:9.text: Don’t you yet perceive or remember the five loaves for the five thousand, and how many baskets you took up,

40:17:1.text: After six days, Jesus took with him Peter, James, and John his brother, and brought them up into a high mountain by themselves.

40:17:10.text: His disciples asked him, saying, “Then why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”

40:17:11.text: Jesus answered them, “Elijah indeed comes first, and will restore all things;

40:17:12.text: but I tell you that Elijah has come already, and they didn’t recognise him, but did to him whatever they wanted to. Even so the Son of Man will also suffer by them.”

40:17:13.text: Then the disciples understood that he spoke to them of John the Baptiser.

40:17:14.text: When they came to the multitude, a man came to him, kneeling down to him and saying,

40:17:15.text: “Lord, have mercy on my son, for he is epileptic and suffers grievously; for he often falls into the fire, and often into the water.

40:17:16.text: So I brought him to your disciples, and they could not cure him.”

40:17:17.text: Jesus answered, “Faithless and perverse generation! How long will I be with you? How long will I bear with you? Bring him here to me.”

40:17:18.text: Jesus rebuked the demon, and it went out of him, and the boy was cured from that hour.

40:17:19.text: Then the disciples came to Jesus privately, and said, “Why weren’t we able to cast it out?”

40:17:2.text: He was changed before them. His face shone like the sun, and his garments became as white as the light.

40:17:20.text: He said to them, “Because of your unbelief. For most certainly I tell you, if you have faith as a grain of mustard seed, you will tell this mountain, ‘ Move from here to there,’ and it will move; and nothing will be impossible for you.

40:17:21.text: But this kind doesn’t go out except by prayer and fasting.”

40:17:22.text: While they were staying in Galilee, Jesus said to them, “The Son of Man is about to be delivered up into the hands of men,

40:17:23.text: and they will kill him, and the third day he will be raised up.” They were exceedingly sorry.

40:17:24.text: When they had come to Capernaum, those who collected the didrachma coins came to Peter, and said, “Doesn’t your teacher pay the didrachma?”

40:17:25.text: He said, “Yes.” When he came into the house, Jesus anticipated him, saying, “What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth receive toll or tribute? From their children, or from strangers?”

40:17:26.text: Peter said to him, “From strangers.” Jesus said to him, “Therefore the children are exempt.

40:17:27.text: But, lest we cause them to stumble, go to the sea, cast a hook, and take up the first fish that comes up. When you have opened its mouth, you will find a stater coin. Take that, and give it to them for me and you.”

40:17:3.text: Behold, Moses and Elijah appeared to them talking with him.

40:17:4.text: Peter answered and said to Jesus, “Lord, it is good for us to be here. If you want, let’s make three tents here: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”

40:17:5.text: While he was still speaking, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them. Behold, a voice came out of the cloud, saying, “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Listen to him.”

40:17:6.text: When the disciples heard it, they fell on their faces, and were very afraid.

40:17:7.text: Jesus came and touched them and said, “Get up, and don’t be afraid.”

40:17:8.text: Lifting up their eyes, they saw no one, except Jesus alone.

40:17:9.text: As they were coming down from the mountain, Jesus commanded them, saying, “Don’t tell anyone what you saw, until the Son of Man has risen from the dead.”

40:18:1.text: In that hour the disciples came to Jesus, saying, “Who then is greatest in the Kingdom of Heaven?”

40:18:10.text: See that you don’t despise one of these little ones, for I tell you that in heaven their angels always see the face of my Father who is in heaven.

40:18:11.text: For the Son of Man came to save that which was lost.

40:18:12.text: “What do you think? If a man has one hundred sheep, and one of them goes astray, doesn’t he leave the ninety-nine, go to the mountains, and seek that which has gone astray?

40:18:13.text: If he finds it, most certainly I tell you, he rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine which have not gone astray.

40:18:14.text: Even so it is not the will of your Father who is in heaven that one of these little ones should perish.

40:18:15.text: “If your brother sins against you, go, show him his fault between you and him alone. If he listens to you, you have gained back your brother.

40:18:16.text: But if he doesn’t listen, take one or two more with you, that at the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established.

40:18:17.text: If he refuses to listen to them, tell it to the assembly. If he refuses to hear the assembly also, let him be to you as a Gentile or a tax collector.

40:18:18.text: Most certainly I tell you, whatever things you bind on earth will have been bound in heaven, and whatever things you release on earth will have been released in heaven.

40:18:19.text: Again, assuredly I tell you, that if two of you will agree on earth concerning anything that they will ask, it will be done for them by my Father who is in heaven.

40:18:2.text: Jesus called a little child to himself, and set him in the middle of them

40:18:20.text: For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there I am in the middle of them.”

40:18:21.text: Then Peter came and said to him, “Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? Until seven times?”

40:18:22.text: Jesus said to him, “I don’t tell you until seven times, but, until seventy times seven.

40:18:23.text: Therefore the Kingdom of Heaven is like a certain king who wanted to settle accounts with his servants.

40:18:24.text: When he had begun to settle, one was brought to him who owed him ten thousand talents.

40:18:25.text: But because he couldn’t pay, his lord commanded him to be sold, with his wife, his children, and all that he had, and payment to be made.

40:18:26.text: The servant therefore fell down and knelt before him, saying, ‘ Lord, have patience with me, and I will repay you all!’

40:18:27.text: The lord of that servant, being moved with compassion, released him and forgave him the debt.

40:18:28.text: “But that servant went out and found one of his fellow servants who owed him one hundred denarii, and he grabbed him and took him by the throat, saying, ‘Pay me what you owe!’

40:18:29.text: “So his fellow servant fell down at his feet and begged him, saying, ‘ Have patience with me, and I will repay you!’

40:18:3.text: and said, “Most certainly I tell you, unless you turn and become as little children, you will in no way enter into the Kingdom of Heaven.

40:18:30.text: He would not, but went and cast him into prison until he should pay back that which was due.

40:18:31.text: So when his fellow servants saw what was done, they were exceedingly sorry, and came and told their lord all that was done.

40:18:32.text: Then his lord called him in and said to him, ‘ You wicked servant! I forgave you all that debt because you begged me.

40:18:33.text: Shouldn’t you also have had mercy on your fellow servant, even as I had mercy on you?’

40:18:34.text: His lord was angry, and delivered him to the tormentors until he should pay all that was due to him.

40:18:35.text: So my heavenly Father will also do to you, if you don’t each forgive your brother from your hearts for his misdeeds.”

40:18:4.text: Whoever therefore humbles himself as this little child is the greatest in the Kingdom of Heaven.

40:18:5.text: Whoever receives one such little child in my name receives me,

40:18:6.text: but whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him if a huge millstone were hung around his neck and that he were sunk in the depths of the sea.

40:18:7.text: “Woe to the world because of occasions of stumbling! For it must be that the occasions come, but woe to that person through whom the occasion comes!

40:18:8.text: If your hand or your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off and cast it from you. It is better for you to enter into life maimed or crippled, rather than having two hands or two feet to be cast into the eternal fire.

40:18:9.text: If your eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and cast it from you. It is better for you to enter into life with one eye, rather than having two eyes to be cast into the Gehenna of fire.

40:19:1.text: When Jesus had finished these words, he departed from Galilee and came into the borders of Judea beyond the Jordan.

40:19:10.text: His disciples said to him, “If this is the case of the man with his wife, it is not expedient to marry.”

40:19:11.text: But he said to them, “Not all men can receive this saying, but those to whom it is given.

40:19:12.text: For there are eunuchs who were born that way from their mother’s womb, and there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs by men; and there are eunuchs who made themselves eunuchs for the Kingdom of Heaven’s sake. He who is able to receive it, let him receive it.”

40:19:13.text: Then little children were brought to him that he should lay his hands on them and pray; and the disciples rebuked them.

40:19:14.text: But Jesus said, “Allow the little children, and don’t forbid them to come to me; for the Kingdom of Heaven belongs to ones like these.”

40:19:15.text: He laid his hands on them, and departed from there.

40:19:16.text: Behold, one came to him and said, “Good teacher, what good thing shall I do, that I may have eternal life?”

40:19:17.text: He said to him, “Why do you call me good? No one is good but one, that is, God. But if you want to enter into life, keep the commandments.”

40:19:18.text: He said to him, “Which ones?” Jesus said, “‘ You shall not murder.’ ‘ You shall not commit adultery.’ ‘ You shall not steal.’ ‘ You shall not offer false testimony.’

40:19:19.text: ‘ Honour your father and your mother.’ And, ‘ You shall love your neighbour as yourself.’ ”

40:19:2.text: Great multitudes followed him, and he healed them there.

40:19:20.text: The young man said to him, “All these things I have observed from my youth. What do I still lack?”

40:19:21.text: Jesus said to him, “If you want to be perfect, go, sell what you have, and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me.”

40:19:22.text: But when the young man heard this, he went away sad, for he was one who had great possessions.

40:19:23.text: Jesus said to his disciples, “Most certainly I say to you, a rich man will enter into the Kingdom of Heaven with difficulty.

40:19:24.text: Again I tell you, it is easier for a camel to go through a needle’s eye than for a rich man to enter into God’s Kingdom.”

40:19:25.text: When the disciples heard it, they were exceedingly astonished, saying, “Who then can be saved?”

40:19:26.text: Looking at them, Jesus said, “With men this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.”

40:19:27.text: Then Peter answered, “Behold, we have left everything and followed you. What then will we have?”

40:19:28.text: Jesus said to them, “Most certainly I tell you that you who have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Man will sit on the throne of his glory, you also will sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

40:19:29.text: Everyone who has left houses, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my name’s sake, will receive one hundred times, and will inherit eternal life.

40:19:3.text: Pharisees came to him, testing him and saying, “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any reason?”

40:19:30.text: But many will be last who are first, and first who are last.

40:19:4.text: He answered, “Haven’t you read that he who made them from the beginning made them male and female,

40:19:5.text: and said, ‘ For this cause a man shall leave his father and mother, and shall be joined to his wife; and the two shall become one flesh’ ?

40:19:6.text: So that they are no more two, but one flesh. What therefore God has joined together, don’t let man tear apart.”

40:19:7.text: They asked him, “Why then did Moses command us to give her a certificate of divorce and divorce her?”

40:19:8.text: He said to them, “Moses, because of the hardness of your hearts, allowed you to divorce your wives, but from the beginning it has not been so.

40:19:9.text: I tell you that whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, and marries another, commits adultery; and he who marries her when she is divorced commits adultery.”

40:1:1.text: The book of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham.

40:1:10.text: Hezekiah became the father of Manasseh. Manasseh became the father of Amon. Amon became the father of Josiah.

40:1:11.text: Josiah became the father of Jechoniah and his brothers at the time of the exile to Babylon.

40:1:12.text: After the exile to Babylon, Jechoniah became the father of Shealtiel. Shealtiel became the father of Zerubbabel.

40:1:13.text: Zerubbabel became the father of Abiud. Abiud became the father of Eliakim. Eliakim became the father of Azor.

40:1:14.text: Azor became the father of Zadok. Zadok became the father of Achim. Achim became the father of Eliud.

40:1:15.text: Eliud became the father of Eleazar. Eleazar became the father of Matthan. Matthan became the father of Jacob.

40:1:16.text: Jacob became the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary, from whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.

40:1:17.text: So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations; from David to the exile to Babylon fourteen generations; and from the carrying away to Babylon to the Christ, fourteen generations.

40:1:18.text: Now the birth of Jesus Christ was like this: After his mother, Mary, was engaged to Joseph, before they came together, she was found pregnant by the Holy Spirit.

40:1:19.text: Joseph, her husband, being a righteous man, and not willing to make her a public example, intended to put her away secretly.

40:1:2.text: Abraham became the father of Isaac. Isaac became the father of Jacob. Jacob became the father of Judah and his brothers.

40:1:20.text: But when he thought about these things, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying, “Joseph, son of David, don’t be afraid to take to yourself Mary as your wife, for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Spirit.

40:1:21.text: She shall give birth to a son. You shall name him Jesus, for it is he who shall save his people from their sins.”

40:1:22.text: Now all this has happened that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Lord through the prophet, saying,

40:1:23.text: “Behold, the virgin shall be with child, and shall give birth to a son. They shall call his name Immanuel,” which is, being interpreted, “God with us.”

40:1:24.text: Joseph arose from his sleep, and did as the angel of the Lord commanded him, and took his wife to himself;

40:1:25.text: and didn’t know her sexually until she had given birth to her firstborn son. He named him Jesus.

40:1:3.text: Judah became the father of Perez and Zerah by Tamar. Perez became the father of Hezron. Hezron became the father of Ram.

40:1:4.text: Ram became the father of Amminadab. Amminadab became the father of Nahshon. Nahshon became the father of Salmon.

40:1:5.text: Salmon became the father of Boaz by Rahab. Boaz became the father of Obed by Ruth. Obed became the father of Jesse.

40:1:6.text: Jesse became the father of King David. David the king became the father of Solomon by her who had been Uriah’s wife.

40:1:7.text: Solomon became the father of Rehoboam. Rehoboam became the father of Abijah. Abijah became the father of Asa.

40:1:8.text: Asa became the father of Jehoshaphat. Jehoshaphat became the father of Joram. Joram became the father of Uzziah.

40:1:9.text: Uzziah became the father of Jotham. Jotham became the father of Ahaz. Ahaz became the father of Hezekiah.

40:20:1.text: “For the Kingdom of Heaven is like a man who was the master of a household, who went out early in the morning to hire labourers for his vineyard.

40:20:10.text: When the first came, they supposed that they would receive more; and they likewise each received a denarius.

40:20:11.text: When they received it, they murmured against the master of the household,

40:20:12.text: saying, ‘ These last have spent one hour, and you have made them equal to us who have borne the burden of the day and the scorching heat!’

40:20:13.text: “But he answered one of them, ‘ Friend, I am doing you no wrong. Didn’t you agree with me for a denarius?

40:20:14.text: Take that which is yours, and go your way. It is my desire to give to this last just as much as to you.

40:20:15.text: Isn’t it lawful for me to do what I want to with what I own? Or is your eye evil, because I am good?’

40:20:16.text: So the last will be first, and the first last. For many are called, but few are chosen.”

40:20:17.text: As Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, he took the twelve disciples aside, and on the way he said to them,

40:20:18.text: “Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be delivered to the chief priests and scribes, and they will condemn him to death,

40:20:19.text: and will hand him over to the Gentiles to mock, to scourge, and to crucify; and the third day he will be raised up.”

40:20:2.text: When he had agreed with the labourers for a denarius a day, he sent them into his vineyard.

40:20:20.text: Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee came to him with her sons, kneeling and asking a certain thing of him.

40:20:21.text: He said to her, “What do you want?” She said to him, “Command that these, my two sons, may sit, one on your right hand and one on your left hand, in your Kingdom.”

40:20:22.text: But Jesus answered, “You don’t know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink, and be baptised with the baptism that I am baptised with?” They said to him, “We are able.”
