41:3:34.text: Looking around at those who sat around him, he said, “Behold, my mother and my brothers!

41:3:35.text: For whoever does the will of God is my brother, my sister, and mother.”

41:3:4.text: He said to them, “Is it lawful on the Sabbath day to do good or to do harm? To save a life or to kill?” But they were silent.

41:3:5.text: When he had looked around at them with anger, being grieved at the hardening of their hearts, he said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He stretched it out, and his hand was restored as healthy as the other.

41:3:6.text: The Pharisees went out, and immediately conspired with the Herodians against him, how they might destroy him.

41:3:7.text: Jesus withdrew to the sea with his disciples; and a great multitude followed him from Galilee, from Judea,

41:3:8.text: from Jerusalem, from Idumaea, beyond the Jordan, and those from around Tyre and Sidon. A great multitude, hearing what great things he did, came to him.

41:3:9.text: He spoke to his disciples that a little boat should stay near him because of the crowd, so that they wouldn’t press on him.

41:4:1.text: Again he began to teach by the seaside. A great multitude was gathered to him, so that he entered into a boat in the sea and sat down. All the multitude were on the land by the sea.

41:4:10.text: When he was alone, those who were around him with the twelve asked him about the parables.

41:4:11.text: He said to them, “To you is given the mystery of God’s Kingdom, but to those who are outside, all things are done in parables,

41:4:12.text: that ‘ seeing they may see and not perceive, and hearing they may hear and not understand, lest perhaps they should turn again, and their sins should be forgiven them.’ ”

41:4:13.text: He said to them, “Don’t you understand this parable? How will you understand all of the parables?

41:4:15.text: The ones by the road are the ones where the word is sown; and when they have heard, immediately Satan comes and takes away the word which has been sown in them.

41:4:16.text: These in the same way are those who are sown on the rocky places, who, when they have heard the word, immediately receive it with joy.

41:4:17.text: They have no root in themselves, but are short-lived. When oppression or persecution arises because of the word, immediately they stumble.

41:4:18.text: Others are those who are sown amongst the thorns. These are those who have heard the word,

41:4:19.text: and the cares of this age, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.

41:4:2.text: He taught them many things in parables, and told them in his teaching,

41:4:20.text: Those which were sown on the good ground are those who hear the word, accept it, and bear fruit, some thirty times, some sixty times, and some one hundred times.”

41:4:21.text: He said to them, “Is a lamp brought to be put under a basket or under a bed? Isn’t it put on a stand?

41:4:22.text: For there is nothing hidden except that it should be made known, neither was anything made secret but that it should come to light.

41:4:23.text: If any man has ears to hear, let him hear.”

41:4:24.text: He said to them, “Take heed what you hear. With whatever measure you measure, it will be measured to you; and more will be given to you who hear.

41:4:25.text: For whoever has, to him more will be given; and he who doesn’t have, even that which he has will be taken away from him.”

41:4:26.text: He said, “God’s Kingdom is as if a man should cast seed on the earth,

41:4:27.text: and should sleep and rise night and day, and the seed should spring up and grow, though he doesn’t know how.

41:4:28.text: For the earth bears fruit by itself: first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain in the ear.

41:4:29.text: But when the fruit is ripe, immediately he puts in the sickle, because the harvest has come.”

41:4:3.text: “Listen! Behold, the farmer went out to sow.

41:4:30.text: He said, “How will we liken God’s Kingdom? Or with what parable will we illustrate it?

41:4:31.text: It’s like a grain of mustard seed, which, when it is sown in the earth, though it is less than all the seeds that are on the earth,

41:4:32.text: yet when it is sown, grows up and becomes greater than all the herbs, and puts out great branches, so that the birds of the sky can lodge under its shadow.”

41:4:33.text: With many such parables he spoke the word to them, as they were able to hear it.

41:4:34.text: Without a parable he didn’t speak to them; but privately to his own disciples he explained everything.

41:4:35.text: On that day, when evening had come, he said to them, “Let’s go over to the other side.”

41:4:36.text: Leaving the multitude, they took him with them, even as he was, in the boat. Other small boats were also with him.

41:4:37.text: A big wind storm arose, and the waves beat into the boat, so much that the boat was already filled.

41:4:38.text: He himself was in the stern, asleep on the cushion; and they woke him up and asked him, “Teacher, don’t you care that we are dying?”

41:4:39.text: He awoke and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Peace! Be still!” The wind ceased and there was a great calm.

41:4:4.text: As he sowed, some seed fell by the road, and the birds came and devoured it.

41:4:40.text: He said to them, “Why are you so afraid? How is it that you have no faith?”

41:4:41.text: They were greatly afraid and said to one another, “Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?”

41:4:5.text: Others fell on the rocky ground, where it had little soil, and immediately it sprang up, because it had no depth of soil.

41:4:6.text: When the sun had risen, it was scorched; and because it had no root, it withered away.

41:4:7.text: Others fell amongst the thorns, and the thorns grew up and choked it, and it yielded no fruit.

41:4:8.text: Others fell into the good ground and yielded fruit, growing up and increasing. Some produced thirty times, some sixty times, and some one hundred times as much.”

41:4:9.text: He said, “Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.”

41:5:1.text: They came to the other side of the sea, into the country of the Gadarenes.

41:5:10.text: He begged him much that he would not send them away out of the country.

41:5:11.text: Now on the mountainside there was a great herd of pigs feeding.

41:5:12.text: All the demons begged him, saying, “Send us into the pigs, that we may enter into them.”

41:5:13.text: At once Jesus gave them permission. The unclean spirits came out and entered into the pigs. The herd of about two thousand rushed down the steep bank into the sea, and they were drowned in the sea.

41:5:14.text: Those who fed the pigs fled, and told it in the city and in the country. The people came to see what it was that had happened.

41:5:15.text: They came to Jesus, and saw him who had been possessed by demons sitting, clothed, and in his right mind, even him who had the legion; and they were afraid.

41:5:16.text: Those who saw it declared to them what happened to him who was possessed by demons, and about the pigs.

41:5:17.text: They began to beg him to depart from their region.

41:5:18.text: As he was entering into the boat, he who had been possessed by demons begged him that he might be with him.

41:5:19.text: He didn’t allow him, but said to him, “Go to your house, to your friends, and tell them what great things the Lord has done for you and how he had mercy on you.”

41:5:2.text: When he had come out of the boat, immediately a man with an unclean spirit met him out of the tombs.

41:5:20.text: He went his way, and began to proclaim in Decapolis how Jesus had done great things for him, and everyone marvelled.

41:5:21.text: When Jesus had crossed back over in the boat to the other side, a great multitude was gathered to him; and he was by the sea.

41:5:22.text: Behold, one of the rulers of the synagogue, Jairus by name, came; and seeing him, he fell at his feet

41:5:23.text: and begged him much, saying, “My little daughter is at the point of death. Please come and lay your hands on her, that she may be made healthy, and live.”

41:5:24.text: He went with him, and a great multitude followed him, and they pressed upon him on all sides.

41:5:25.text: A certain woman who had a discharge of blood for twelve years,

41:5:26.text: and had suffered many things by many physicians, and had spent all that she had, and was no better, but rather grew worse,

41:5:27.text: having heard the things concerning Jesus, came up behind him in the crowd and touched his clothes.

41:5:28.text: For she said, “If I just touch his clothes, I will be made well.”

41:5:29.text: Immediately the flow of her blood was dried up, and she felt in her body that she was healed of her affliction.

41:5:3.text: He lived in the tombs. Nobody could bind him any more, not even with chains,

41:5:30.text: Immediately Jesus, perceiving in himself that the power had gone out from him, turned around in the crowd and asked, “Who touched my clothes?”

41:5:31.text: His disciples said to him, “You see the multitude pressing against you, and you say, ‘ Who touched me?’ ”

41:5:32.text: He looked around to see her who had done this thing.

41:5:33.text: But the woman, fearing and trembling, knowing what had been done to her, came and fell down before him, and told him all the truth.

41:5:34.text: He said to her, “Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace, and be cured of your disease.”

41:5:35.text: While he was still speaking, people came from the synagogue ruler’s house, saying, “Your daughter is dead. Why bother the Teacher any more?”

41:5:36.text: But Jesus, when he heard the message spoken, immediately said to the ruler of the synagogue, “Don’t be afraid, only believe.”

41:5:37.text: He allowed no one to follow him except Peter, James, and John the brother of James.

41:5:38.text: He came to the synagogue ruler’s house, and he saw an uproar, weeping, and great wailing.

41:5:39.text: When he had entered in, he said to them, “Why do you make an uproar and weep? The child is not dead, but is asleep.”

41:5:4.text: because he had been often bound with fetters and chains, and the chains had been torn apart by him, and the fetters broken in pieces. Nobody had the strength to tame him.

41:5:40.text: They ridiculed him. But he, having put them all out, took the father of the child, her mother, and those who were with him, and went in where the child was lying.

41:5:41.text: Taking the child by the hand, he said to her, “Talitha cumi!” which means, being interpreted, “Girl, I tell you, get up!”

41:5:42.text: Immediately the girl rose up and walked, for she was twelve years old. They were amazed with great amazement.

41:5:43.text: He strictly ordered them that no one should know this, and commanded that something should be given to her to eat.

41:5:5.text: Always, night and day, in the tombs and in the mountains, he was crying out, and cutting himself with stones.

41:5:6.text: When he saw Jesus from afar, he ran and bowed down to him,

41:5:7.text: and crying out with a loud voice, he said, “What have I to do with you, Jesus, you Son of the Most High God? I adjure you by God, don’t torment me.”

41:5:8.text: For he said to him, “Come out of the man, you unclean spirit!”

41:5:9.text: He asked him, “What is your name?” He said to him, “My name is Legion, for we are many.”

41:6:1.text: He went out from there. He came into his own country, and his disciples followed him.

41:6:10.text: He said to them, “Wherever you enter into a house, stay there until you depart from there.

41:6:11.text: Whoever will not receive you nor hear you, as you depart from there, shake off the dust that is under your feet for a testimony against them. Assuredly, I tell you, it will be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgement than for that city!”

41:6:12.text: They went out and preached that people should repent.

41:6:13.text: They cast out many demons, and anointed many with oil who were sick and healed them.

41:6:14.text: King Herod heard this, for his name had become known, and he said, “John the Baptiser has risen from the dead, and therefore these powers are at work in him.”

41:6:15.text: But others said, “He is Elijah.” Others said, “He is a prophet, or like one of the prophets.”

41:6:16.text: But Herod, when he heard this, said, “This is John, whom I beheaded. He has risen from the dead.”

41:6:17.text: For Herod himself had sent out and arrested John and bound him in prison for the sake of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife, for he had married her.

41:6:18.text: For John had said to Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife.”

41:6:20.text: for Herod feared John, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man, and kept him safe. When he heard him, he did many things, and he heard him gladly.

41:6:24.text: She went out and said to her mother, “What shall I ask?” She said, “The head of John the Baptiser.”

41:6:25.text: She came in immediately with haste to the king and requested, “I want you to give me right now the head of John the Baptiser on a platter.”

41:6:26.text: The king was exceedingly sorry, but for the sake of his oaths and of his dinner guests, he didn’t wish to refuse her.

41:6:27.text: Immediately the king sent out a soldier of his guard and commanded to bring John’s head; and he went and beheaded him in the prison,

41:6:28.text: and brought his head on a platter, and gave it to the young lady; and the young lady gave it to her mother.

41:6:3.text: Isn’t this the carpenter, the son of Mary and brother of James, Joses, Judah, and Simon? Aren’t his sisters here with us?” So they were offended at him.

41:6:30.text: The apostles gathered themselves together to Jesus, and they told him all things, whatever they had done, and whatever they had taught.

41:6:31.text: He said to them, “Come away into a deserted place, and rest awhile.” For there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.

41:6:32.text: They went away in the boat to a deserted place by themselves.

41:6:33.text: They saw them going, and many recognised him and ran there on foot from all the cities. They arrived before them and came together to him.

41:6:34.text: Jesus came out, saw a great multitude, and he had compassion on them because they were like sheep without a shepherd; and he began to teach them many things.

41:6:35.text: When it was late in the day, his disciples came to him and said, “This place is deserted, and it is late in the day.

41:6:36.text: Send them away, that they may go into the surrounding country and villages and buy themselves bread, for they have nothing to eat.”

41:6:37.text: But he answered them, “You give them something to eat.” They asked him, “Shall we go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread and give them something to eat?”

41:6:38.text: He said to them, “How many loaves do you have? Go see.” When they knew, they said, “Five, and two fish.”

41:6:39.text: He commanded them that everyone should sit down in groups on the green grass.

41:6:4.text: Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honour, except in his own country, and amongst his own relatives, and in his own house.”

41:6:40.text: They sat down in ranks, by hundreds and by fifties.

41:6:42.text: They all ate and were filled.

41:6:43.text: They took up twelve baskets full of broken pieces and also of the fish.

41:6:44.text: Those who ate the loaves were five thousand men.

41:6:47.text: When evening had come, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and he was alone on the land.

41:7:23.text: All these evil things come from within and defile the man.”

41:7:24.text: From there he arose and went away into the borders of Tyre and Sidon. He entered into a house and didn’t want anyone to know it, but he couldn’t escape notice.

41:7:25.text: For a woman whose little daughter had an unclean spirit, having heard of him, came and fell down at his feet.

41:7:26.text: Now the woman was a Greek, a Syrophoenician by race. She begged him that he would cast the demon out of her daughter.

41:7:27.text: But Jesus said to her, “Let the children be filled first, for it is not appropriate to take the children’s bread and throw it to the dogs.”

41:7:28.text: But she answered him, “Yes, Lord. Yet even the dogs under the table eat the children’s crumbs.”

41:7:29.text: He said to her, “For this saying, go your way. The demon has gone out of your daughter.”

41:7:35.text: Immediately his ears were opened, and the impediment of his tongue was released, and he spoke clearly.

41:7:36.text: He commanded them that they should tell no one, but the more he commanded them, so much the more widely they proclaimed it.

41:7:8.text: “For you set aside the commandment of God, and hold tightly to the tradition of men — the washing of pitchers and cups, and you do many other such things.”

41:8:12.text: He sighed deeply in his spirit and said, “Why does this generation seek a sign? Most certainly I tell you, no sign will be given to this generation.”

41:8:16.text: They reasoned with one another, saying, “It’s because we have no bread.”

41:8:17.text: Jesus, perceiving it, said to them, “Why do you reason that it’s because you have no bread? Don’t you perceive yet or understand? Is your heart still hardened?

41:8:18.text: Having eyes, don’t you see? Having ears, don’t you hear? Don’t you remember?

41:8:2.text: “I have compassion on the multitude, because they have stayed with me now three days and have nothing to eat.

41:8:20.text: “When the seven loaves fed the four thousand, how many baskets full of broken pieces did you take up?” They told him, “Seven.”

41:8:21.text: He asked them, “Don’t you understand yet?”

41:8:22.text: He came to Bethsaida. They brought a blind man to him and begged him to touch him.

41:9:1.text: He said to them, “Most certainly I tell you, there are some standing here who will in no way taste death until they see God’s Kingdom come with power.”

41:9:11.text: They asked him, saying, “Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”

41:9:12.text: He said to them, “Elijah indeed comes first, and restores all things. How is it written about the Son of Man, that he should suffer many things and be despised?

41:9:13.text: But I tell you that Elijah has come, and they have also done to him whatever they wanted to, even as it is written about him.”

41:9:14.text: Coming to the disciples, he saw a great multitude around them, and scribes questioning them.

41:9:15.text: Immediately all the multitude, when they saw him, were greatly amazed, and running to him, greeted him.

41:9:20.text: They brought him to him, and when he saw him, immediately the spirit convulsed him and he fell on the ground, wallowing and foaming at the mouth.

41:9:21.text: He asked his father, “How long has it been since this has been happening to him?” He said, “From childhood.

41:9:22.text: Often it has cast him both into the fire and into the water to destroy him. But if you can do anything, have compassion on us and help us.”

41:9:23.text: Jesus said to him, “If you can believe, all things are possible to him who believes.”

41:9:24.text: Immediately the father of the child cried out with tears, “I believe. Help my unbelief!”

41:9:25.text: When Jesus saw that a multitude came running together, he rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to him, “You mute and deaf spirit, I command you, come out of him, and never enter him again!”

41:9:27.text: But Jesus took him by the hand and raised him up; and he arose.

41:9:35.text: He sat down and called the twelve; and he said to them, “If any man wants to be first, he shall be last of all, and servant of all.”

42:11:1.text: When he finished praying in a certain place, one of his disciples said to him, “Lord, teach us to pray, just as John also taught his disciples.”

42:11:10.text: For everyone who asks receives. He who seeks finds. To him who knocks it will be opened.

42:11:11.text: “Which of you fathers, if your son asks for bread, will give him a stone? Or if he asks for a fish, he won’t give him a snake instead of a fish, will he?

42:11:12.text: Or if he asks for an egg, he won’t give him a scorpion, will he?

42:11:13.text: If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him?”

42:11:14.text: He was casting out a demon, and it was mute. When the demon had gone out, the mute man spoke; and the multitudes marvelled.

42:11:15.text: But some of them said, “He casts out demons by Beelzebul, the prince of the demons.”

42:11:16.text: Others, testing him, sought from him a sign from heaven.

42:11:17.text: But he, knowing their thoughts, said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation. A house divided against itself falls.

42:11:18.text: If Satan also is divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand? For you say that I cast out demons by Beelzebul.

42:11:19.text: But if I cast out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your children cast them out? Therefore they will be your judges.

42:11:2.text: He said to them, “When you pray, say, ‘ Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy. May your Kingdom come. May your will be done on earth, as it is in heaven.

42:11:20.text: But if I by God’s finger cast out demons, then God’s Kingdom has come to you.

42:11:21.text: “When the strong man, fully armed, guards his own dwelling, his goods are safe.

42:11:22.text: But when someone stronger attacks him and overcomes him, he takes from him his whole armour in which he trusted, and divides his plunder.

42:11:23.text: “He who is not with me is against me. He who doesn’t gather with me scatters.

42:11:24.text: The unclean spirit, when he has gone out of the man, passes through dry places, seeking rest; and finding none, he says, ‘ I will turn back to my house from which I came out.’

42:11:25.text: When he returns, he finds it swept and put in order.

42:11:26.text: Then he goes and takes seven other spirits more evil than himself, and they enter in and dwell there. The last state of that man becomes worse than the first.”

42:11:27.text: It came to pass, as he said these things, a certain woman out of the multitude lifted up her voice and said to him, “Blessed is the womb that bore you, and the breasts which nursed you!”

42:11:28.text: But he said, “On the contrary, blessed are those who hear the word of God, and keep it.”

42:11:29.text: When the multitudes were gathering together to him, he began to say, “This is an evil generation. It seeks after a sign. No sign will be given to it but the sign of Jonah the prophet.

42:11:3.text: Give us day by day our daily bread.

42:11:30.text: For even as Jonah became a sign to the Ninevites, so the Son of Man will also be to this generation.

42:11:31.text: The Queen of the South will rise up in the judgement with the men of this generation and will condemn them, for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and behold, one greater than Solomon is here.

42:11:32.text: The men of Nineveh will stand up in the judgement with this generation, and will condemn it, for they repented at the preaching of Jonah; and behold, one greater than Jonah is here.

42:11:33.text: “No one, when he has lit a lamp, puts it in a cellar or under a basket, but on a stand, that those who come in may see the light.

42:11:34.text: The lamp of the body is the eye. Therefore when your eye is good, your whole body is also full of light; but when it is evil, your body also is full of darkness.

42:11:35.text: Therefore see whether the light that is in you isn’t darkness.

42:11:36.text: If therefore your whole body is full of light, having no part dark, it will be wholly full of light, as when the lamp with its bright shining gives you light.”

42:11:37.text: Now as he spoke, a certain Pharisee asked him to dine with him. He went in and sat at the table.

42:11:38.text: When the Pharisee saw it, he marvelled that he had not first washed himself before dinner.

42:11:39.text: The Lord said to him, “Now you Pharisees cleanse the outside of the cup and of the platter, but your inward part is full of extortion and wickedness.

42:11:4.text: Forgive us our sins, for we ourselves also forgive everyone who is indebted to us. Bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.’ ”

42:11:40.text: You foolish ones, didn’t he who made the outside make the inside also?

42:11:41.text: But give for gifts to the needy those things which are within, and behold, all things will be clean to you.

42:11:42.text: But woe to you Pharisees! For you tithe mint and rue and every herb, but you bypass justice and God’s love. You ought to have done these, and not to have left the other undone.

42:11:43.text: Woe to you Pharisees! For you love the best seats in the synagogues and the greetings in the marketplaces.

42:11:44.text: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like hidden graves, and the men who walk over them don’t know it.”

42:11:45.text: One of the lawyers answered him, “Teacher, in saying this you insult us also.”

42:11:46.text: He said, “Woe to you lawyers also! For you load men with burdens that are difficult to carry, and you yourselves won’t even lift one finger to help carry those burdens.

42:11:47.text: Woe to you! For you build the tombs of the prophets, and your fathers killed them.

42:11:48.text: So you testify and consent to the works of your fathers. For they killed them, and you build their tombs.

42:11:49.text: Therefore also the wisdom of God said, ‘ I will send to them prophets and apostles; and some of them they will kill and persecute,

42:11:5.text: He said to them, “Which of you, if you go to a friend at midnight and tell him, ‘ Friend, lend me three loaves of bread,

42:11:50.text: that the blood of all the prophets, which was shed from the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation,

42:11:51.text: from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zachariah, who perished between the altar and the sanctuary.’ Yes, I tell you, it will be required of this generation.

42:11:52.text: Woe to you lawyers! For you took away the key of knowledge. You didn’t enter in yourselves, and those who were entering in, you hindered.”

42:11:53.text: As he said these things to them, the scribes and the Pharisees began to be terribly angry, and to draw many things out of him,

42:11:54.text: lying in wait for him, and seeking to catch him in something he might say, that they might accuse him.

42:11:6.text: for a friend of mine has come to me from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him,’

42:11:7.text: and he from within will answer and say, ‘Don’t bother me. The door is now shut, and my children are with me in bed. I can’t get up and give it to you’ ?

42:11:8.text: I tell you, although he will not rise and give it to him because he is his friend, yet because of his persistence, he will get up and give him as many as he needs.

42:11:9.text: “I tell you, keep asking, and it will be given you. Keep seeking, and you will find. Keep knocking, and it will be opened to you.

42:12:1.text: Meanwhile, when a multitude of many thousands had gathered together, so much so that they trampled on each other, he began to tell his disciples first of all, “Beware of the yeast of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.

42:12:10.text: Everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but those who blaspheme against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.

42:12:11.text: When they bring you before the synagogues, the rulers, and the authorities, don’t be anxious how or what you will answer or what you will say;

42:12:12.text: for the Holy Spirit will teach you in that same hour what you must say.”

42:12:13.text: One of the multitude said to him, “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.”

42:12:14.text: But he said to him, “Man, who made me a judge or an arbitrator over you?”

42:12:15.text: He said to them, “Beware! Keep yourselves from covetousness, for a man’s life doesn’t consist of the abundance of the things which he possesses.”

42:12:16.text: He spoke a parable to them, saying, “The ground of a certain rich man produced abundantly.

42:12:17.text: He reasoned within himself, saying, ‘ What will I do, because I don’t have room to store my crops?’

42:12:18.text: He said, ‘ This is what I will do. I will pull down my barns, build bigger ones, and there I will store all my grain and my goods.

42:12:19.text: I will tell my soul, “Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years. Take your ease, eat, drink, and be merry.”’

42:12:2.text: But there is nothing covered up that will not be revealed, nor hidden that will not be known.

42:12:20.text: “But God said to him, ‘ You foolish one, tonight your soul is required of you. The things which you have prepared — whose will they be?’

42:12:21.text: So is he who lays up treasure for himself, and is not rich towards God.”

42:12:22.text: He said to his disciples, “Therefore I tell you, don’t be anxious for your life, what you will eat, nor yet for your body, what you will wear.

42:12:23.text: Life is more than food, and the body is more than clothing.

42:12:24.text: Consider the ravens: they don’t sow, they don’t reap, they have no warehouse or barn, and God feeds them. How much more valuable are you than birds!

42:12:25.text: Which of you by being anxious can add a cubit to his height?

42:12:26.text: If then you aren’t able to do even the least things, why are you anxious about the rest?

42:12:27.text: Consider the lilies, how they grow. They don’t toil, neither do they spin; yet I tell you, even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.

42:12:28.text: But if this is how God clothes the grass in the field, which today exists and tomorrow is cast into the oven, how much more will he clothe you, O you of little faith?

42:12:29.text: “Don’t seek what you will eat or what you will drink; neither be anxious.

42:12:3.text: Therefore whatever you have said in the darkness will be heard in the light. What you have spoken in the ear in the inner rooms will be proclaimed on the housetops.

42:12:30.text: For the nations of the world seek after all of these things, but your Father knows that you need these things.

42:12:31.text: But seek God’s Kingdom, and all these things will be added to you.

42:12:32.text: “Don’t be afraid, little flock, for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the Kingdom.

42:12:33.text: Sell what you have and give gifts to the needy. Make for yourselves purses which don’t grow old, a treasure in the heavens that doesn’t fail, where no thief approaches and no moth destroys.

42:12:34.text: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.

42:12:35.text: “Let your waist be dressed and your lamps burning.

42:12:36.text: Be like men watching for their lord when he returns from the wedding feast, that when he comes and knocks, they may immediately open to him.

42:12:37.text: Blessed are those servants whom the lord will find watching when he comes. Most certainly I tell you that he will dress himself, make them recline, and will come and serve them.

42:12:38.text: They will be blessed if he comes in the second or third watch and finds them so.

42:12:39.text: But know this, that if the master of the house had known in what hour the thief was coming, he would have watched and not allowed his house to be broken into.

42:12:4.text: “I tell you, my friends, don’t be afraid of those who kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do.

42:12:40.text: Therefore be ready also, for the Son of Man is coming in an hour that you don’t expect him.”

42:12:41.text: Peter said to him, “Lord, are you telling this parable to us, or to everybody?”

42:12:42.text: The Lord said, “Who then is the faithful and wise steward, whom his lord will set over his household, to give them their portion of food at the right times?

42:12:43.text: Blessed is that servant whom his lord will find doing so when he comes.

42:12:44.text: Truly I tell you that he will set him over all that he has.

42:12:45.text: But if that servant says in his heart, ‘ My lord delays his coming,’ and begins to beat the menservants and the maidservants, and to eat and drink and to be drunken,

42:12:46.text: then the lord of that servant will come in a day when he isn’t expecting him and in an hour that he doesn’t know, and will cut him in two, and place his portion with the unfaithful.

42:12:47.text: That servant who knew his lord’s will, and didn’t prepare nor do what he wanted, will be beaten with many stripes,

42:12:48.text: but he who didn’t know, and did things worthy of stripes, will be beaten with few stripes. To whomever much is given, of him will much be required; and to whom much was entrusted, of him more will be asked.

42:12:49.text: “I came to throw fire on the earth. I wish it were already kindled.

42:12:5.text: But I will warn you whom you should fear. Fear him who after he has killed, has power to cast into Gehenna. Yes, I tell you, fear him.

42:12:50.text: But I have a baptism to be baptised with, and how distressed I am until it is accomplished!

42:12:51.text: Do you think that I have come to give peace in the earth? I tell you, no, but rather division.

42:12:52.text: For from now on, there will be five in one house divided, three against two, and two against three.

42:12:53.text: They will be divided, father against son, and son against father; mother against daughter, and daughter against her mother; mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law, and daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.”

42:12:54.text: He said to the multitudes also, “When you see a cloud rising from the west, immediately you say, ‘ A shower is coming,’ and so it happens.

42:12:55.text: When a south wind blows, you say, ‘ There will be a scorching heat,’ and it happens.

42:12:56.text: You hypocrites! You know how to interpret the appearance of the earth and the sky, but how is it that you don’t interpret this time?

42:12:57.text: “Why don’t you judge for yourselves what is right?

42:12:58.text: For when you are going with your adversary before the magistrate, try diligently on the way to be released from him, lest perhaps he drag you to the judge, and the judge deliver you to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.

42:12:59.text: I tell you, you will by no means get out of there until you have paid the very last penny. ”

42:12:6.text: “Aren’t five sparrows sold for two assaria coins? Not one of them is forgotten by God.

42:12:7.text: But the very hairs of your head are all counted. Therefore don’t be afraid. You are of more value than many sparrows.

42:12:8.text: “I tell you, everyone who confesses me before men, the Son of Man will also confess before the angels of God;

42:12:9.text: but he who denies me in the presence of men will be denied in the presence of God’s angels.

42:13:1.text: Now there were some present at the same time who told him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.

42:13:10.text: He was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath day.

42:13:11.text: Behold, there was a woman who had a spirit of infirmity eighteen years. She was bent over and could in no way straighten herself up.

42:13:12.text: When Jesus saw her, he called her and said to her, “Woman, you are freed from your infirmity.”

42:13:13.text: He laid his hands on her, and immediately she stood up straight and glorified God.

42:13:14.text: The ruler of the synagogue, being indignant because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, said to the multitude, “There are six days in which men ought to work. Therefore come on those days and be healed, and not on the Sabbath day!”

42:13:15.text: Therefore the Lord answered him, “You hypocrites! Doesn’t each one of you free his ox or his donkey from the stall on the Sabbath and lead him away to water?

42:13:16.text: Ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham whom Satan had bound eighteen long years, be freed from this bondage on the Sabbath day?”

42:13:17.text: As he said these things, all his adversaries were disappointed; and all the multitude rejoiced for all the glorious things that were done by him.

42:13:18.text: He said, “What is God’s Kingdom like? To what shall I compare it?

42:13:19.text: It is like a grain of mustard seed which a man took and put in his own garden. It grew and became a large tree, and the birds of the sky live in its branches.”

42:13:2.text: Jesus answered them, “Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans, because they suffered such things?

42:13:20.text: Again he said, “To what shall I compare God’s Kingdom?

42:13:21.text: It is like yeast, which a woman took and hid in three measures of flour, until it was all leavened.”

42:13:22.text: He went on his way through cities and villages, teaching, and travelling on to Jerusalem.

42:13:23.text: One said to him, “Lord, are they few who are saved?” He said to them,

42:13:24.text: “Strive to enter in by the narrow door, for many, I tell you, will seek to enter in and will not be able.

42:13:25.text: When once the master of the house has risen up and has shut the door, and you begin to stand outside and to knock at the door, saying, ‘ Lord, Lord, open to us!’ then he will answer and tell you, ‘ I don’t know you or where you come from.’

42:13:26.text: Then you will begin to say, ‘ We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught in our streets.’

42:13:27.text: He will say, ‘ I tell you, I don’t know where you come from. Depart from me, all you workers of iniquity.’

42:13:28.text: There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in God’s Kingdom, and yourselves being thrown outside.

42:13:29.text: They will come from the east, west, north, and south, and will sit down in God’s Kingdom.

42:13:3.text: I tell you, no, but unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.

42:13:30.text: Behold, there are some who are last who will be first, and there are some who are first who will be last.”

42:13:31.text: On that same day, some Pharisees came, saying to him, “Get out of here and go away, for Herod wants to kill you.”

42:13:32.text: He said to them, “Go and tell that fox, ‘ Behold, I cast out demons and perform cures today and tomorrow, and the third day I complete my mission.

42:13:33.text: Nevertheless I must go on my way today and tomorrow and the next day, for it can’t be that a prophet would perish outside of Jerusalem.’

42:13:34.text: “Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to her! How often I wanted to gather your children together, like a hen gathers her own brood under her wings, and you refused!

42:13:35.text: Behold, your house is left to you desolate. I tell you, you will not see me until you say, ‘ Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!’ ”

42:13:4.text: Or those eighteen on whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them — do you think that they were worse offenders than all the men who dwell in Jerusalem?

42:13:5.text: I tell you, no, but, unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.”

42:13:6.text: He spoke this parable. “A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came seeking fruit on it and found none.

42:13:7.text: He said to the vine dresser, ‘ Behold, these three years I have come looking for fruit on this fig tree, and found none. Cut it down! Why does it waste the soil?’

42:13:8.text: He answered, ‘ Lord, leave it alone this year also, until I dig around it and fertilise it.

42:13:9.text: If it bears fruit, fine; but if not, after that, you can cut it down.’ ”

42:14:1.text: When he went into the house of one of the rulers of the Pharisees on a Sabbath to eat bread, they were watching him.

42:14:10.text: But when you are invited, go and sit in the lowest place, so that when he who invited you comes, he may tell you, ‘ Friend, move up higher.’ Then you will be honoured in the presence of all who sit at the table with you.

42:14:11.text: For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.”

42:14:12.text: He also said to the one who had invited him, “When you make a dinner or a supper, don’t call your friends, nor your brothers, nor your kinsmen, nor rich neighbours, or perhaps they might also return the favour, and pay you back.

42:14:13.text: But when you make a feast, ask the poor, the maimed, the lame, or the blind;

42:14:14.text: and you will be blessed, because they don’t have the resources to repay you. For you will be repaid in the resurrection of the righteous.”

42:14:15.text: When one of those who sat at the table with him heard these things, he said to him, “Blessed is he who will feast in God’s Kingdom!”

42:14:16.text: But he said to him, “A certain man made a great supper, and he invited many people.

42:14:17.text: He sent out his servant at supper time to tell those who were invited, ‘ Come, for everything is ready now.’

42:14:18.text: They all as one began to make excuses. “The first said to him, ‘ I have bought a field, and I must go and see it. Please have me excused.’

42:14:19.text: “Another said, ‘ I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I must go try them out. Please have me excused.’

42:14:2.text: Behold, a certain man who had dropsy was in front of him.

42:14:20.text: “Another said, ‘ I have married a wife, and therefore I can’t come.’

42:14:21.text: “That servant came, and told his lord these things. Then the master of the house, being angry, said to his servant, ‘ Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in the poor, maimed, blind, and lame.’

42:14:22.text: “The servant said, ‘ Lord, it is done as you commanded, and there is still room.’

42:14:23.text: “The lord said to the servant, ‘ Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.

42:14:24.text: For I tell you that none of those men who were invited will taste of my supper. For many are called, but few are chosen.’ ”

42:14:25.text: Now great multitudes were going with him. He turned and said to them,

42:14:26.text: “If anyone comes to me, and doesn’t disregard his own father, mother, wife, children, brothers, and sisters, yes, and his own life also, he can’t be my disciple.

42:14:27.text: Whoever doesn’t bear his own cross and come after me, can’t be my disciple.

42:14:28.text: For which of you, desiring to build a tower, doesn’t first sit down and count the cost, to see if he has enough to complete it?

42:14:29.text: Or perhaps, when he has laid a foundation and isn’t able to finish, everyone who sees begins to mock him,

42:14:3.text: Jesus, answering, spoke to the lawyers and Pharisees, saying, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?”

42:14:30.text: saying, ‘ This man began to build and wasn’t able to finish.’

42:14:31.text: Or what king, as he goes to encounter another king in war, will not sit down first and consider whether he is able with ten thousand to meet him who comes against him with twenty thousand?

42:14:32.text: Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sends an envoy and asks for conditions of peace.

42:14:33.text: So therefore, whoever of you who doesn’t renounce all that he has, he can’t be my disciple.

42:14:34.text: “Salt is good, but if the salt becomes flat and tasteless, with what do you season it?

42:14:35.text: It is fit neither for the soil nor for the manure pile. It is thrown out. He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”

42:14:4.text: But they were silent. He took him, and healed him, and let him go.

42:14:5.text: He answered them, “Which of you, if your son or an ox fell into a well, wouldn’t immediately pull him out on a Sabbath day?”

42:14:6.text: They couldn’t answer him regarding these things.

42:14:7.text: He spoke a parable to those who were invited, when he noticed how they chose the best seats, and said to them,

42:14:8.text: “When you are invited by anyone to a wedding feast, don’t sit in the best seat, since perhaps someone more honourable than you might be invited by him,

42:14:9.text: and he who invited both of you would come and tell you, ‘ Make room for this person.’ Then you would begin, with shame, to take the lowest place.

42:15:1.text: Now all the tax collectors and sinners were coming close to him to hear him.

42:15:10.text: Even so, I tell you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner repenting.”

42:15:11.text: He said, “A certain man had two sons.

42:15:12.text: The younger of them said to his father, ‘ Father, give me my share of your property.’ So he divided his livelihood between them.

42:15:13.text: Not many days after, the younger son gathered all of this together and travelled into a far country. There he wasted his property with riotous living.

42:15:14.text: When he had spent all of it, there arose a severe famine in that country, and he began to be in need.

42:15:15.text: He went and joined himself to one of the citizens of that country, and he sent him into his fields to feed pigs.

42:15:16.text: He wanted to fill his belly with the pods that the pigs ate, but no one gave him any.

42:15:17.text: But when he came to himself, he said, ‘ How many hired servants of my father’s have bread enough to spare, and I’m dying with hunger!

42:15:18.text: I will get up and go to my father, and will tell him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven and in your sight.

42:15:19.text: I am no more worthy to be called your son. Make me as one of your hired servants.”’

42:15:2.text: The Pharisees and the scribes murmured, saying, “This man welcomes sinners, and eats with them.”

42:15:20.text: “He arose and came to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him and was moved with compassion, and ran, fell on his neck, and kissed him.

42:15:21.text: The son said to him, ‘ Father, I have sinned against heaven and in your sight. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’

42:15:22.text: “But the father said to his servants, ‘ Bring out the best robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet.

42:15:23.text: Bring the fattened calf, kill it, and let’s eat and celebrate;

42:15:24.text: for this, my son, was dead and is alive again. He was lost and is found.’ Then they began to celebrate.

42:15:25.text: “Now his elder son was in the field. As he came near to the house, he heard music and dancing.

42:15:26.text: He called one of the servants to him and asked what was going on.

42:15:27.text: He said to him, ‘ Your brother has come, and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has received him back safe and healthy.’

42:15:28.text: But he was angry and would not go in. Therefore his father came out and begged him.

42:15:29.text: But he answered his father, ‘ Behold, these many years I have served you, and I never disobeyed a commandment of yours, but you never gave me a goat, that I might celebrate with my friends.

42:15:30.text: But when this your son came, who has devoured your living with prostitutes, you killed the fattened calf for him.’

42:15:31.text: “He said to him, ‘ Son, you are always with me, and all that is mine is yours.

42:15:32.text: But it was appropriate to celebrate and be glad, for this, your brother, was dead, and is alive again. He was lost, and is found.’ ”

42:15:4.text: “Which of you men, if you had one hundred sheep and lost one of them, wouldn’t leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the one that was lost, until he found it?

42:15:5.text: When he has found it, he carries it on his shoulders, rejoicing.

42:6:11.text: But they were filled with rage, and talked with one another about what they might do to Jesus.

42:6:12.text: In these days, he went out to the mountain to pray, and he continued all night in prayer to God.

42:6:13.text: When it was day, he called his disciples, and from them he chose twelve, whom he also named apostles:

42:6:14.text: Simon, whom he also named Peter; Andrew, his brother; James; John; Philip; Bartholomew;

42:6:15.text: Matthew; Thomas; James the son of Alphaeus; Simon who was called the Zealot;

42:6:16.text: Judas the son of James; and Judas Iscariot, who also became a traitor.

42:6:17.text: He came down with them and stood on a level place, with a crowd of his disciples and a great number of the people from all Judea and Jerusalem and the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon, who came to hear him and to be healed of their diseases,

42:6:18.text: as well as those who were troubled by unclean spirits; and they were being healed.

42:6:19.text: All the multitude sought to touch him, for power came out of him and healed them all.

42:6:2.text: But some of the Pharisees said to them, “Why do you do that which is not lawful to do on the Sabbath day?”

42:6:20.text: He lifted up his eyes to his disciples, and said: “Blessed are you who are poor, for God’s Kingdom is yours.

42:6:21.text: Blessed are you who hunger now, for you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.

42:6:22.text: Blessed are you when men hate you, and when they exclude and mock you, and throw out your name as evil, for the Son of Man’s sake.

42:6:23.text: Rejoice in that day and leap for joy, for behold, your reward is great in heaven, for their fathers did the same thing to the prophets.

42:6:24.text: “But woe to you who are rich! For you have received your consolation.

42:6:25.text: Woe to you, you who are full now, for you will be hungry. Woe to you who laugh now, for you will mourn and weep.

42:6:26.text: Woe, when men speak well of you, for their fathers did the same thing to the false prophets.

42:6:27.text: “But I tell you who hear: love your enemies, do good to those who hate you,

42:6:28.text: bless those who curse you, and pray for those who mistreat you.

42:6:29.text: To him who strikes you on the cheek, offer also the other; and from him who takes away your cloak, don’t withhold your coat also.

42:6:3.text: Jesus, answering them, said, “Haven’t you read what David did when he was hungry, he and those who were with him,

42:6:30.text: Give to everyone who asks you, and don’t ask him who takes away your goods to give them back again.

42:6:31.text: “As you would like people to do to you, do exactly so to them.

42:6:32.text: “If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners love those who love them.

42:6:33.text: If you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners do the same.

42:6:34.text: If you lend to those from whom you hope to receive, what credit is that to you? Even sinners lend to sinners, to receive back as much.

42:6:35.text: But love your enemies, and do good, and lend, expecting nothing back; and your reward will be great, and you will be children of the Most High; for he is kind towards the unthankful and evil.

42:6:36.text: “Therefore be merciful, even as your Father is also merciful.

42:6:37.text: Don’t judge, and you won’t be judged. Don’t condemn, and you won’t be condemned. Set free, and you will be set free.

42:6:38.text: “Give, and it will be given to you: good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and running over, will be given to you. For with the same measure you measure it will be measured back to you.”

42:6:39.text: He spoke a parable to them. “Can the blind guide the blind? Won’t they both fall into a pit?

42:6:4.text: how he entered into God’s house, and took and ate the show bread, and gave also to those who were with him, which is not lawful to eat except for the priests alone?”

42:6:40.text: A disciple is not above his teacher, but everyone when he is fully trained will be like his teacher.

42:6:41.text: Why do you see the speck of chaff that is in your brother’s eye, but don’t consider the beam that is in your own eye?

42:6:42.text: Or how can you tell your brother, ‘Brother, let me remove the speck of chaff that is in your eye,’ when you yourself don’t see the beam that is in your own eye? You hypocrite! First remove the beam from your own eye, and then you can see clearly to remove the speck of chaff that is in your brother’s eye.

42:6:43.text: “For there is no good tree that produces rotten fruit, nor again a rotten tree that produces good fruit.

42:6:44.text: For each tree is known by its own fruit. For people don’t gather figs from thorns, nor do they gather grapes from a bramble bush.

42:6:45.text: The good man out of the good treasure of his heart brings out that which is good, and the evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart brings out that which is evil, for out of the abundance of the heart, his mouth speaks.

42:6:46.text: “Why do you call me, ‘ Lord, Lord,’ and don’t do the things which I say?

42:6:47.text: Everyone who comes to me, and hears my words and does them, I will show you who he is like.

42:6:48.text: He is like a man building a house, who dug and went deep and laid a foundation on the rock. When a flood arose, the stream broke against that house, and could not shake it, because it was founded on the rock.

42:6:49.text: But he who hears and doesn’t do, is like a man who built a house on the earth without a foundation, against which the stream broke, and immediately it fell; and the ruin of that house was great.”

42:6:5.text: He said to them, “The Son of Man is lord of the Sabbath.”

42:6:6.text: It also happened on another Sabbath that he entered into the synagogue and taught. There was a man there, and his right hand was withered.

42:6:7.text: The scribes and the Pharisees watched him, to see whether he would heal on the Sabbath, that they might find an accusation against him.

42:6:8.text: But he knew their thoughts; and he said to the man who had the withered hand, “Rise up and stand in the middle.” He arose and stood.

42:6:9.text: Then Jesus said to them, “I will ask you something: Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good, or to do harm? To save a life, or to kill?”

42:7:1.text: After he had finished speaking in the hearing of the people, he entered into Capernaum.

42:7:10.text: Those who were sent, returning to the house, found that the servant who had been sick was well.

42:7:11.text: Soon afterwards, he went to a city called Nain. Many of his disciples, along with a great multitude, went with him.

42:7:12.text: Now when he came near to the gate of the city, behold, one who was dead was carried out, the only born son of his mother, and she was a widow. Many people of the city were with her.

42:7:13.text: When the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her and said to her, “Don’t cry.”

42:7:14.text: He came near and touched the coffin, and the bearers stood still. He said, “Young man, I tell you, arise!”

42:7:15.text: He who was dead sat up and began to speak. Then he gave him to his mother.

42:7:16.text: Fear took hold of all, and they glorified God, saying, “A great prophet has arisen amongst us!” and, “God has visited his people!”

42:7:17.text: This report went out concerning him in the whole of Judea and in all the surrounding region.

42:7:18.text: The disciples of John told him about all these things.

42:7:19.text: John, calling to himself two of his disciples, sent them to Jesus, saying, “Are you the one who is coming, or should we look for another?”

42:7:2.text: A certain centurion’s servant, who was dear to him, was sick and at the point of death.

42:7:20.text: When the men had come to him, they said, “John the Baptiser has sent us to you, saying, ‘ Are you he who comes, or should we look for another?’ ”

42:7:21.text: In that hour he cured many of diseases and plagues and evil spirits; and to many who were blind he gave sight.

42:7:22.text: Jesus answered them, “Go and tell John the things which you have seen and heard: that the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have good news preached to them.

42:7:23.text: Blessed is he who finds no occasion for stumbling in me.”

42:7:24.text: When John’s messengers had departed, he began to tell the multitudes about John, “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?

42:7:25.text: But what did you go out to see? A man clothed in soft clothing? Behold, those who are gorgeously dressed and live delicately are in kings’ courts.

42:7:26.text: But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and much more than a prophet.

42:7:27.text: This is he of whom it is written, ‘ Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you.’

42:7:28.text: “For I tell you, amongst those who are born of women there is not a greater prophet than John the Baptiser; yet he who is least in God’s Kingdom is greater than he.”

42:7:29.text: When all the people and the tax collectors heard this, they declared God to be just, having been baptised with John’s baptism.

42:7:3.text: When he heard about Jesus, he sent to him elders of the Jews, asking him to come and save his servant.

42:7:30.text: But the Pharisees and the lawyers rejected the counsel of God, not being baptised by him themselves.

42:7:31.text: “To what then should I compare the people of this generation? What are they like?

42:7:32.text: They are like children who sit in the marketplace and call to one another, saying, ‘ We piped to you, and you didn’t dance. We mourned, and you didn’t weep.’

42:7:33.text: For John the Baptiser came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, ‘ He has a demon.’

42:7:34.text: The Son of Man has come eating and drinking, and you say, ‘ Behold, a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’

42:7:35.text: Wisdom is justified by all her children.”

42:7:36.text: One of the Pharisees invited him to eat with him. He entered into the Pharisee’s house and sat at the table.

42:7:37.text: Behold, a woman in the city who was a sinner, when she knew that he was reclining in the Pharisee’s house, brought an alabaster jar of ointment.

42:7:38.text: Standing behind at his feet weeping, she began to wet his feet with her tears, and she wiped them with the hair of her head, kissed his feet, and anointed them with the ointment.

42:7:39.text: Now when the Pharisee who had invited him saw it, he said to himself, “This man, if he were a prophet, would have perceived who and what kind of woman this is who touches him, that she is a sinner.”

42:7:4.text: When they came to Jesus, they begged him earnestly, saying, “He is worthy for you to do this for him,

42:7:40.text: Jesus answered him, “Simon, I have something to tell you.” He said, “Teacher, say on.”

42:7:41.text: “A certain lender had two debtors. The one owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.

42:7:42.text: When they couldn’t pay, he forgave them both. Which of them therefore will love him most?”

42:7:43.text: Simon answered, “He, I suppose, to whom he forgave the most.” He said to him, “You have judged correctly.”

42:7:44.text: Turning to the woman, he said to Simon, “Do you see this woman? I entered into your house, and you gave me no water for my feet, but she has wet my feet with her tears, and wiped them with the hair of her head.

42:7:45.text: You gave me no kiss, but she, since the time I came in, has not ceased to kiss my feet.

42:7:46.text: You didn’t anoint my head with oil, but she has anointed my feet with ointment.

42:7:47.text: Therefore I tell you, her sins, which are many, are forgiven, for she loved much. But one to whom little is forgiven, loves little.”

42:7:48.text: He said to her, “Your sins are forgiven.”

42:7:49.text: Those who sat at the table with him began to say to themselves, “Who is this who even forgives sins?”

42:7:5.text: for he loves our nation, and he built our synagogue for us.”

42:7:50.text: He said to the woman, “Your faith has saved you. Go in peace.”

42:7:6.text: Jesus went with them. When he was now not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to him, saying to him, “Lord, don’t trouble yourself, for I am not worthy for you to come under my roof.

42:7:7.text: Therefore I didn’t even think myself worthy to come to you; but say the word, and my servant will be healed.

42:7:8.text: For I also am a man placed under authority, having under myself soldiers. I tell this one, ‘ Go!’ and he goes; and to another, ‘ Come!’ and he comes; and to my servant, ‘ Do this,’ and he does it.”

42:7:9.text: When Jesus heard these things, he marvelled at him, and turned and said to the multitude who followed him, “I tell you, I have not found such great faith, no, not in Israel.”

42:8:1.text: Soon afterwards, he went about through cities and villages, preaching and bringing the good news of God’s Kingdom. With him were the twelve,

42:8:10.text: He said, “To you it is given to know the mysteries of God’s Kingdom, but to the rest it is given in parables, that ‘seeing they may not see, and hearing they may not understand.’

42:8:11.text: “Now the parable is this: The seed is the word of God.

42:8:12.text: Those along the road are those who hear; then the devil comes and takes away the word from their heart, that they may not believe and be saved.

42:8:13.text: Those on the rock are they who, when they hear, receive the word with joy; but these have no root. They believe for a while, then fall away in time of temptation.

42:8:14.text: What fell amongst the thorns, these are those who have heard, and as they go on their way they are choked with cares, riches, and pleasures of life; and they bring no fruit to maturity.

42:8:15.text: Those in the good ground, these are those who with an honest and good heart, having heard the word, hold it tightly, and produce fruit with perseverance.

42:8:16.text: “No one, when he has lit a lamp, covers it with a container or puts it under a bed; but puts it on a stand, that those who enter in may see the light.

42:8:17.text: For nothing is hidden that will not be revealed, nor anything secret that will not be known and come to light.

42:8:18.text: Be careful therefore how you hear. For whoever has, to him will be given; and whoever doesn’t have, from him will be taken away even that which he thinks he has.”

42:8:19.text: His mother and brothers came to him, and they could not come near him for the crowd.

42:8:2.text: and certain women who had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities: Mary who was called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out;

42:8:20.text: Some people told him, “Your mother and your brothers stand outside, desiring to see you.”

42:8:21.text: But he answered them, “My mother and my brothers are these who hear the word of God and do it.”

42:8:22.text: Now on one of those days, he entered into a boat, himself and his disciples, and he said to them, “Let’s go over to the other side of the lake.” So they launched out.

42:8:23.text: But as they sailed, he fell asleep. A wind storm came down on the lake, and they were taking on dangerous amounts of water.

42:8:24.text: They came to him and awoke him, saying, “Master, Master, we are dying!” He awoke and rebuked the wind and the raging of the water; then they ceased, and it was calm.

42:8:25.text: He said to them, “Where is your faith?” Being afraid, they marvelled, saying to one another, “Who is this then, that he commands even the winds and the water, and they obey him?”

42:8:26.text: Then they arrived at the country of the Gadarenes, which is opposite Galilee.

42:8:27.text: When Jesus stepped ashore, a certain man out of the city who had demons for a long time met him. He wore no clothes, and didn’t live in a house, but in the tombs.

42:8:28.text: When he saw Jesus, he cried out and fell down before him, and with a loud voice said, “What do I have to do with you, Jesus, you Son of the Most High God? I beg you, don’t torment me!”

42:8:29.text: For Jesus was commanding the unclean spirit to come out of the man. For the unclean spirit had often seized the man. He was kept under guard and bound with chains and fetters. Breaking the bonds apart, he was driven by the demon into the desert.

42:8:3.text: and Joanna, the wife of Chuzas, Herod’s steward; Susanna; and many others who served them from their possessions.

42:8:30.text: Jesus asked him, “What is your name?” He said, “Legion,” for many demons had entered into him.

42:8:31.text: They begged him that he would not command them to go into the abyss.

42:8:32.text: Now there was there a herd of many pigs feeding on the mountain, and they begged him that he would allow them to enter into those. Then he allowed them.

42:8:33.text: The demons came out of the man and entered into the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and were drowned.

42:8:34.text: When those who fed them saw what had happened, they fled and told it in the city and in the country.

42:8:35.text: People went out to see what had happened. They came to Jesus and found the man from whom the demons had gone out, sitting at Jesus’ feet, clothed and in his right mind; and they were afraid.

42:8:36.text: Those who saw it told them how he who had been possessed by demons was healed.

42:8:37.text: All the people of the surrounding country of the Gadarenes asked him to depart from them, for they were very much afraid. Then he entered into the boat and returned.

42:8:38.text: But the man from whom the demons had gone out begged him that he might go with him, but Jesus sent him away, saying,

42:8:39.text: “Return to your house, and declare what great things God has done for you.” He went his way, proclaiming throughout the whole city what great things Jesus had done for him.

42:8:4.text: When a great multitude came together and people from every city were coming to him, he spoke by a parable:

42:8:40.text: When Jesus returned, the multitude welcomed him, for they were all waiting for him.

42:8:41.text: Behold, a man named Jairus came. He was a ruler of the synagogue. He fell down at Jesus’ feet and begged him to come into his house,

42:8:42.text: for he had an only born daughter, about twelve years of age, and she was dying. But as he went, the multitudes pressed against him.

42:8:43.text: A woman who had a flow of blood for twelve years, who had spent all her living on physicians and could not be healed by any,

42:8:44.text: came behind him and touched the fringe of his cloak. Immediately the flow of her blood stopped.

42:8:45.text: Jesus said, “Who touched me?” When all denied it, Peter and those with him said, “Master, the multitudes press and jostle you, and you say, ‘ Who touched me?’ ”

42:8:46.text: But Jesus said, “Someone did touch me, for I perceived that power has gone out of me.”

42:8:47.text: When the woman saw that she was not hidden, she came trembling; and falling down before him declared to him in the presence of all the people the reason why she had touched him, and how she was healed immediately.

42:8:48.text: He said to her, “Daughter, cheer up. Your faith has made you well. Go in peace.”

42:8:49.text: While he still spoke, one from the ruler of the synagogue’s house came, saying to him, “Your daughter is dead. Don’t trouble the Teacher.”

42:8:5.text: “The farmer went out to sow his seed. As he sowed, some fell along the road, and it was trampled under foot, and the birds of the sky devoured it.

42:8:50.text: But Jesus hearing it, answered him, “Don’t be afraid. Only believe, and she will be healed.”

42:8:51.text: When he came to the house, he didn’t allow anyone to enter in, except Peter, John, James, the father of the child, and her mother.

42:8:52.text: All were weeping and mourning her, but he said, “Don’t weep. She isn’t dead, but sleeping.”

42:8:53.text: They were ridiculing him, knowing that she was dead.

42:8:54.text: But he put them all outside, and taking her by the hand, he called, saying, “Child, arise!”

42:8:55.text: Her spirit returned, and she rose up immediately. He commanded that something be given to her to eat.

42:8:56.text: Her parents were amazed, but he commanded them to tell no one what had been done.

42:8:6.text: Other seed fell on the rock, and as soon as it grew, it withered away, because it had no moisture.

42:8:7.text: Other fell amid the thorns, and the thorns grew with it and choked it.

42:8:8.text: Other fell into the good ground and grew and produced one hundred times as much fruit.” As he said these things, he called out, “He who has ears to hear, let him hear!”

42:8:9.text: Then his disciples asked him, “What does this parable mean?”

42:9:1.text: He called the twelve together and gave them power and authority over all demons, and to cure diseases.

42:9:10.text: The apostles, when they had returned, told him what things they had done. He took them and withdrew apart to a desert region of a city called Bethsaida.

42:9:11.text: But the multitudes, perceiving it, followed him. He welcomed them, spoke to them of God’s Kingdom, and he cured those who needed healing.

42:9:12.text: The day began to wear away; and the twelve came and said to him, “Send the multitude away, that they may go into the surrounding villages and farms and lodge and get food, for we are here in a deserted place.”

42:9:13.text: But he said to them, “You give them something to eat.” They said, “We have no more than five loaves and two fish, unless we should go and buy food for all these people.”

42:9:14.text: For they were about five thousand men. He said to his disciples, “Make them sit down in groups of about fifty each.”

42:9:15.text: They did so, and made them all sit down.

42:9:16.text: He took the five loaves and the two fish, and looking up to the sky, he blessed them, broke them, and gave them to the disciples to set before the multitude.

42:9:17.text: They ate and were all filled. They gathered up twelve baskets of broken pieces that were left over.

42:9:18.text: As he was praying alone, the disciples were near him, and he asked them, “Who do the multitudes say that I am?”

42:9:19.text: They answered, “‘ John the Baptiser,’ but others say, ‘ Elijah,’ and others, that one of the old prophets has risen again.”

42:9:2.text: He sent them out to preach God’s Kingdom and to heal the sick.

42:9:20.text: He said to them, “But who do you say that I am?” Peter answered, “The Christ of God.”

42:9:21.text: But he warned them and commanded them to tell this to no one,

42:9:22.text: saying, “The Son of Man must suffer many things, and be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and the third day be raised up.”

42:9:23.text: He said to all, “If anyone desires to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me.

42:9:24.text: For whoever desires to save his life will lose it, but whoever will lose his life for my sake will save it.

42:9:25.text: For what does it profit a man if he gains the whole world, and loses or forfeits his own self?

42:9:26.text: For whoever will be ashamed of me and of my words, of him will the Son of Man be ashamed when he comes in his glory, and the glory of the Father, and of the holy angels.

42:9:27.text: But I tell you the truth: There are some of those who stand here who will in no way taste of death until they see God’s Kingdom.”

42:9:28.text: About eight days after these sayings, he took with him Peter, John, and James, and went up onto the mountain to pray.

42:9:29.text: As he was praying, the appearance of his face was altered, and his clothing became white and dazzling.

42:9:3.text: He said to them, “Take nothing for your journey — no staffs, nor wallet, nor bread, nor money. Don’t have two tunics each.

42:9:30.text: Behold, two men were talking with him, who were Moses and Elijah,

42:9:31.text: who appeared in glory and spoke of his departure, which he was about to accomplish at Jerusalem.

42:9:32.text: Now Peter and those who were with him were heavy with sleep, but when they were fully awake, they saw his glory, and the two men who stood with him.

42:9:33.text: As they were parting from him, Peter said to Jesus, “Master, it is good for us to be here. Let’s make three tents: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah,” not knowing what he said.

42:9:34.text: While he said these things, a cloud came and overshadowed them, and they were afraid as they entered into the cloud.

42:9:35.text: A voice came out of the cloud, saying, “This is my beloved Son. Listen to him!”

42:9:36.text: When the voice came, Jesus was found alone. They were silent, and told no one in those days any of the things which they had seen.

42:9:37.text: On the next day, when they had come down from the mountain, a great multitude met him.

42:9:38.text: Behold, a man from the crowd called out, saying, “Teacher, I beg you to look at my son, for he is my only born child.

42:9:39.text: Behold, a spirit takes him, he suddenly cries out, and it convulses him so that he foams; and it hardly departs from him, bruising him severely.

42:9:4.text: Into whatever house you enter, stay there, and depart from there.

42:9:40.text: I begged your disciples to cast it out, and they couldn’t.”

42:9:41.text: Jesus answered, “Faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you and bear with you? Bring your son here.”

42:9:42.text: While he was still coming, the demon threw him down and convulsed him violently. But Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, healed the boy, and gave him back to his father.

42:9:43.text: They were all astonished at the majesty of God. But while all were marvelling at all the things which Jesus did, he said to his disciples,

42:9:44.text: “Let these words sink into your ears, for the Son of Man will be delivered up into the hands of men.”

42:9:45.text: But they didn’t understand this saying. It was concealed from them, that they should not perceive it, and they were afraid to ask him about this saying.

42:9:46.text: An argument arose amongst them about which of them was the greatest.

42:9:47.text: Jesus, perceiving the reasoning of their hearts, took a little child, and set him by his side,

42:9:48.text: and said to them, “Whoever receives this little child in my name receives me. Whoever receives me receives him who sent me. For whoever is least amongst you all, this one will be great.”

42:9:49.text: John answered, “Master, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, and we forbade him, because he doesn’t follow with us.”

42:9:5.text: As many as don’t receive you, when you depart from that city, shake off even the dust from your feet for a testimony against them.”

42:9:50.text: Jesus said to him, “Don’t forbid him, for he who is not against us is for us.”

42:9:51.text: It came to pass, when the days were near that he should be taken up, he intently set his face to go to Jerusalem

42:9:52.text: and sent messengers before his face. They went and entered into a village of the Samaritans, so as to prepare for him.

42:9:53.text: They didn’t receive him, because he was travelling with his face set towards Jerusalem.

42:9:54.text: When his disciples, James and John, saw this, they said, “Lord, do you want us to command fire to come down from the sky and destroy them, just as Elijah did?”

42:9:55.text: But he turned and rebuked them, “You don’t know of what kind of spirit you are.

42:9:56.text: For the Son of Man didn’t come to destroy men’s lives, but to save them.” They went to another village.

42:9:57.text: As they went on the way, a certain man said to him, “I want to follow you wherever you go, Lord.”

42:9:58.text: Jesus said to him, “The foxes have holes and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to lay his head.”

42:9:59.text: He said to another, “Follow me!” But he said, “Lord, allow me first to go and bury my father.”

43:10:1.text: “Most certainly, I tell you, one who doesn’t enter by the door into the sheep fold, but climbs up some other way, is a thief and a robber.
