43:14:7.text: If you had known me, you would have known my Father also. From now on, you know him and have seen him.”

43:14:8.text: Philip said to him, “Lord, show us the Father, and that will be enough for us.”

43:14:9.text: Jesus said to him, “Have I been with you such a long time, and do you not know me, Philip? He who has seen me has seen the Father. How do you say, ‘ Show us the Father’ ?

43:15:1.text: “I am the true vine, and my Father is the farmer.

43:15:10.text: If you keep my commandments, you will remain in my love, even as I have kept my Father’s commandments and remain in his love.

43:15:11.text: I have spoken these things to you, that my joy may remain in you, and that your joy may be made full.

43:15:12.text: “This is my commandment, that you love one another, even as I have loved you.

43:15:13.text: Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends.

43:15:14.text: You are my friends if you do whatever I command you.

43:15:15.text: No longer do I call you servants, for the servant doesn’t know what his lord does. But I have called you friends, for everything that I heard from my Father, I have made known to you.

43:15:16.text: You didn’t choose me, but I chose you and appointed you, that you should go and bear fruit, and that your fruit should remain; that whatever you will ask of the Father in my name, he may give it to you.

43:15:17.text: “I command these things to you, that you may love one another.

43:15:18.text: If the world hates you, you know that it has hated me before it hated you.

43:15:19.text: If you were of the world, the world would love its own. But because you are not of the world, since I chose you out of the world, therefore the world hates you.

43:15:2.text: Every branch in me that doesn’t bear fruit, he takes away. Every branch that bears fruit, he prunes, that it may bear more fruit.

43:15:20.text: Remember the word that I said to you: ‘ A servant is not greater than his lord.’ If they persecuted me, they will also persecute you. If they kept my word, they will also keep yours.

43:15:21.text: But they will do all these things to you for my name’s sake, because they don’t know him who sent me.

43:15:22.text: If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have had sin; but now they have no excuse for their sin.

43:15:23.text: He who hates me, hates my Father also.

43:15:24.text: If I hadn’t done amongst them the works which no one else did, they wouldn’t have had sin. But now they have seen and also hated both me and my Father.

43:15:25.text: But this happened so that the word may be fulfilled which was written in their law, ‘ They hated me without a cause.’

43:15:26.text: “When the Counsellor has come, whom I will send to you from the Father, the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father, he will testify about me.

43:15:27.text: You will also testify, because you have been with me from the beginning.

43:15:3.text: You are already pruned clean because of the word which I have spoken to you.

43:15:4.text: Remain in me, and I in you. As the branch can’t bear fruit by itself unless it remains in the vine, so neither can you, unless you remain in me.

43:15:5.text: I am the vine. You are the branches. He who remains in me and I in him bears much fruit, for apart from me you can do nothing.

43:15:6.text: If a man doesn’t remain in me, he is thrown out as a branch and is withered; and they gather them, throw them into the fire, and they are burnt.

43:15:7.text: If you remain in me, and my words remain in you, you will ask whatever you desire, and it will be done for you.

43:15:8.text: “In this my Father is glorified, that you bear much fruit; and so you will be my disciples.

43:15:9.text: Even as the Father has loved me, I also have loved you. Remain in my love.

43:16:1.text: “I have said these things to you so that you wouldn’t be caused to stumble.

43:16:10.text: about righteousness, because I am going to my Father, and you won’t see me any more;

43:16:11.text: about judgement, because the prince of this world has been judged.

43:16:12.text: “I still have many things to tell you, but you can’t bear them now.

43:16:13.text: However, when he, the Spirit of truth, has come, he will guide you into all truth, for he will not speak from himself; but whatever he hears, he will speak. He will declare to you things that are coming.

43:16:14.text: He will glorify me, for he will take from what is mine and will declare it to you.

43:16:15.text: All things that the Father has are mine; therefore I said that he takes of mine and will declare it to you.

43:16:16.text: “A little while, and you will not see me. Again a little while, and you will see me.”

43:16:17.text: Some of his disciples therefore said to one another, “What is this that he says to us, ‘ A little while, and you won’t see me, and again a little while, and you will see me;’ and, ‘ Because I go to the Father’ ?”

43:16:18.text: They said therefore, “What is this that he says, ‘ A little while’ ? We don’t know what he is saying.”

43:16:19.text: Therefore Jesus perceived that they wanted to ask him, and he said to them, “Do you enquire amongst yourselves concerning this, that I said, ‘ A little while, and you won’t see me, and again a little while, and you will see me’ ?

43:16:2.text: They will put you out of the synagogues. Yes, the time is coming that whoever kills you will think that he offers service to God.

43:16:20.text: Most certainly I tell you that you will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice. You will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will be turned into joy.

43:16:21.text: A woman, when she gives birth, has sorrow because her time has come. But when she has delivered the child, she doesn’t remember the anguish any more, for the joy that a human being is born into the world.

43:16:22.text: Therefore you now have sorrow, but I will see you again, and your heart will rejoice, and no one will take your joy away from you.

43:16:23.text: “In that day you will ask me no questions. Most certainly I tell you, whatever you may ask of the Father in my name, he will give it to you.

43:16:24.text: Until now, you have asked nothing in my name. Ask, and you will receive, that your joy may be made full.

43:16:25.text: “I have spoken these things to you in figures of speech. But the time is coming when I will no more speak to you in figures of speech, but will tell you plainly about the Father.

43:16:26.text: In that day you will ask in my name; and I don’t say to you that I will pray to the Father for you,

43:16:27.text: for the Father himself loves you, because you have loved me, and have believed that I came from God.

43:16:28.text: I came from the Father and have come into the world. Again, I leave the world and go to the Father.”

43:16:29.text: His disciples said to him, “Behold, now you are speaking plainly, and using no figures of speech.

43:16:3.text: They will do these things because they have not known the Father nor me.

43:16:30.text: Now we know that you know all things, and don’t need for anyone to question you. By this we believe that you came from God.”

43:16:31.text: Jesus answered them, “Do you now believe?

43:16:32.text: Behold, the time is coming, yes, and has now come, that you will be scattered, everyone to his own place, and you will leave me alone. Yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me.

43:16:33.text: I have told you these things, that in me you may have peace. In the world you have trouble; but cheer up! I have overcome the world.”

43:16:4.text: But I have told you these things so that when the time comes, you may remember that I told you about them. I didn’t tell you these things from the beginning, because I was with you.

43:16:5.text: But now I am going to him who sent me, and none of you asks me, ‘ Where are you going?’

43:16:6.text: But because I have told you these things, sorrow has filled your heart.

43:16:7.text: Nevertheless I tell you the truth: It is to your advantage that I go away; for if I don’t go away, the Counsellor won’t come to you. But if I go, I will send him to you.

43:16:8.text: When he has come, he will convict the world about sin, about righteousness, and about judgement;

43:16:9.text: about sin, because they don’t believe in me;

43:17:1.text: Jesus said these things, then lifting up his eyes to heaven, he said, “Father, the time has come. Glorify your Son, that your Son may also glorify you;

43:17:10.text: All things that are mine are yours, and yours are mine, and I am glorified in them.

43:17:11.text: I am no more in the world, but these are in the world, and I am coming to you. Holy Father, keep them through your name which you have given me, that they may be one, even as we are.

43:17:12.text: While I was with them in the world, I kept them in your name. I have kept those whom you have given me. None of them is lost except the son of destruction, that the Scripture might be fulfilled.

43:17:13.text: But now I come to you, and I say these things in the world, that they may have my joy made full in themselves.

43:17:14.text: I have given them your word. The world hated them because they are not of the world, even as I am not of the world.

43:17:15.text: I pray not that you would take them from the world, but that you would keep them from the evil one.

43:17:16.text: They are not of the world, even as I am not of the world.

43:17:17.text: Sanctify them in your truth. Your word is truth.

43:17:18.text: As you sent me into the world, even so I have sent them into the world.

43:17:19.text: For their sakes I sanctify myself, that they themselves also may be sanctified in truth.

43:17:2.text: even as you gave him authority over all flesh, so he will give eternal life to all whom you have given him.

43:17:20.text: “Not for these only do I pray, but for those also who will believe in me through their word,

43:17:21.text: that they may all be one; even as you, Father, are in me, and I in you, that they also may be one in us; that the world may believe that you sent me.

43:17:22.text: The glory which you have given me, I have given to them, that they may be one, even as we are one,

43:17:23.text: I in them, and you in me, that they may be perfected into one, that the world may know that you sent me and loved them, even as you loved me.

43:17:24.text: Father, I desire that they also whom you have given me be with me where I am, that they may see my glory which you have given me, for you loved me before the foundation of the world.

43:17:25.text: Righteous Father, the world hasn’t known you, but I knew you; and these knew that you sent me.

43:17:26.text: I made known to them your name, and will make it known; that the love with which you loved me may be in them, and I in them.”

43:17:3.text: This is eternal life, that they should know you, the only true God, and him whom you sent, Jesus Christ.

43:17:4.text: I glorified you on the earth. I have accomplished the work which you have given me to do.

43:17:5.text: Now, Father, glorify me with your own self with the glory which I had with you before the world existed.

43:17:6.text: “I revealed your name to the people whom you have given me out of the world. They were yours, and you have given them to me. They have kept your word.

43:17:7.text: Now they have known that all things whatever you have given me are from you,

43:17:8.text: for the words which you have given me I have given to them; and they received them, and knew for sure that I came from you. They have believed that you sent me.

43:17:9.text: I pray for them. I don’t pray for the world, but for those whom you have given me, for they are yours.

43:19:1.text: So Pilate then took Jesus and flogged him.

43:19:10.text: Pilate therefore said to him, “Aren’t you speaking to me? Don’t you know that I have power to release you and have power to crucify you?”

43:19:11.text: Jesus answered, “You would have no power at all against me, unless it were given to you from above. Therefore he who delivered me to you has greater sin.”

43:19:12.text: At this, Pilate was seeking to release him, but the Jews cried out, saying, “If you release this man, you aren’t Caesar’s friend! Everyone who makes himself a king speaks against Caesar!”

43:19:13.text: When Pilate therefore heard these words, he brought Jesus out and sat down on the judgement seat at a place called “The Pavement”, but in Hebrew, “Gabbatha.”

43:19:14.text: Now it was the Preparation Day of the Passover, at about the sixth hour. He said to the Jews, “Behold, your King!”

43:19:15.text: They cried out, “Away with him! Away with him! Crucify him!” Pilate said to them, “Shall I crucify your King?” The chief priests answered, “We have no king but Caesar!”

43:19:16.text: So then he delivered him to them to be crucified. So they took Jesus and led him away.

43:19:17.text: He went out, bearing his cross, to the place called “The Place of a Skull”, which is called in Hebrew, “Golgotha”,

43:19:18.text: where they crucified him, and with him two others, on either side one, and Jesus in the middle.

43:19:19.text: Pilate wrote a title also, and put it on the cross. There was written, “JESUS OF NAZARETH, THE KING OF THE JEWS.”

43:19:2.text: The soldiers twisted thorns into a crown and put it on his head, and dressed him in a purple garment.

43:19:20.text: Therefore many of the Jews read this title, for the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city; and it was written in Hebrew, in Latin, and in Greek.

43:19:21.text: The chief priests of the Jews therefore said to Pilate, “Don’t write, ‘ The King of the Jews,’ but, ‘ he said, “I am King of the Jews.”’ ”

43:19:22.text: Pilate answered, “What I have written, I have written.”

43:19:23.text: Then the soldiers, when they had crucified Jesus, took his garments and made four parts, to every soldier a part; and also the tunic. Now the tunic was without seam, woven from the top throughout.

43:19:24.text: Then they said to one another, “Let’s not tear it, but cast lots for it to decide whose it will be,” that the Scripture might be fulfilled, which says, “They parted my garments amongst them. They cast lots for my clothing.” Therefore the soldiers did these things.

43:19:25.text: But standing by Jesus’ cross were his mother, his mother’s sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene.

43:19:26.text: Therefore when Jesus saw his mother, and the disciple whom he loved standing there, he said to his mother, “Woman, behold, your son!”

43:19:27.text: Then he said to the disciple, “Behold, your mother!” From that hour, the disciple took her to his own home.

43:19:28.text: After this, Jesus, seeing that all things were now finished, that the Scripture might be fulfilled, said, “I am thirsty!”

43:19:29.text: Now a vessel full of vinegar was set there; so they put a sponge full of the vinegar on hyssop, and held it at his mouth.

43:19:3.text: They kept saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!” and they kept slapping him.

43:19:30.text: When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said, “It is finished!” Then he bowed his head and gave up his spirit.

43:19:31.text: Therefore the Jews, because it was the Preparation Day, so that the bodies wouldn’t remain on the cross on the Sabbath (for that Sabbath was a special one), asked of Pilate that their legs might be broken and that they might be taken away.

43:19:32.text: Therefore the soldiers came and broke the legs of the first and of the other who was crucified with him;

43:19:33.text: but when they came to Jesus and saw that he was already dead, they didn’t break his legs.

43:19:34.text: However, one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and immediately blood and water came out.

43:19:35.text: He who has seen has testified, and his testimony is true. He knows that he tells the truth, that you may believe.

43:19:36.text: For these things happened that the Scripture might be fulfilled, “A bone of him will not be broken.”

43:19:37.text: Again another Scripture says, “They will look on him whom they pierced.”

43:19:38.text: After these things, Joseph of Arimathaea, being a disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jews, asked of Pilate that he might take away Jesus’ body. Pilate gave him permission. He came therefore and took away his body.

43:19:39.text: Nicodemus, who at first came to Jesus by night, also came bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred Roman pounds.

43:19:4.text: Then Pilate went out again, and said to them, “Behold, I bring him out to you, that you may know that I find no basis for a charge against him.”

43:19:40.text: So they took Jesus’ body, and bound it in linen cloths with the spices, as the custom of the Jews is to bury.

43:19:41.text: Now in the place where he was crucified there was a garden. In the garden was a new tomb in which no man had ever yet been laid.

43:19:42.text: Then, because of the Jews’ Preparation Day (for the tomb was near at hand), they laid Jesus there.

43:19:5.text: Jesus therefore came out, wearing the crown of thorns and the purple garment. Pilate said to them, “Behold, the man!”

43:19:6.text: When therefore the chief priests and the officers saw him, they shouted, saying, “Crucify! Crucify!” Pilate said to them, “Take him yourselves and crucify him, for I find no basis for a charge against him.”

43:19:7.text: The Jews answered him, “We have a law, and by our law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of God.”

43:19:8.text: When therefore Pilate heard this saying, he was more afraid.

43:19:9.text: He entered into the Praetorium again, and said to Jesus, “Where are you from?” But Jesus gave him no answer.

43:1:1.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

43:1:10.text: He was in the world, and the world was made through him, and the world didn’t recognise him.

43:1:11.text: He came to his own, and those who were his own didn’t receive him.

43:1:12.text: But as many as received him, to them he gave the right to become God’s children, to those who believe in his name:

43:1:13.text: who were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.

43:1:14.text: The Word became flesh and lived amongst us. We saw his glory, such glory as of the only born Son of the Father, full of grace and truth.

43:1:15.text: John testified about him. He cried out, saying, “This was he of whom I said, ‘ He who comes after me has surpassed me, for he was before me.’ ”

43:1:16.text: From his fullness we all received grace upon grace.

43:1:17.text: For the law was given through Moses. Grace and truth were realised through Jesus Christ.

43:1:18.text: No one has seen God at any time. The only born Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, has declared him.

43:1:19.text: This is John’s testimony, when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him, “Who are you?”

43:1:2.text: The same was in the beginning with God.

43:1:20.text: He declared, and didn’t deny, but he declared, “I am not the Christ.”

43:1:21.text: They asked him, “What then? Are you Elijah?” He said, “I am not.” “Are you the prophet?” He answered, “No.”

43:1:22.text: They said therefore to him, “Who are you? Give us an answer to take back to those who sent us. What do you say about yourself?”

43:1:23.text: He said, “I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘ Make straight the way of the Lord,’ as Isaiah the prophet said.”

43:1:24.text: The ones who had been sent were from the Pharisees.

43:1:25.text: They asked him, “Why then do you baptise if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the prophet?”

43:1:26.text: John answered them, “I baptise in water, but amongst you stands one whom you don’t know.

43:1:27.text: He is the one who comes after me, who is preferred before me, whose sandal strap I’m not worthy to loosen.”

43:1:28.text: These things were done in Bethany beyond the Jordan, where John was baptising.

43:1:29.text: The next day, he saw Jesus coming to him, and said, “Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!

43:1:3.text: All things were made through him. Without him, nothing was made that has been made.

43:1:30.text: This is he of whom I said, ‘ After me comes a man who is preferred before me, for he was before me.’

43:1:31.text: I didn’t know him, but for this reason I came baptising in water, that he would be revealed to Israel.”

43:1:32.text: John testified, saying, “I have seen the Spirit descending like a dove out of heaven, and it remained on him.

43:1:33.text: I didn’t recognise him, but he who sent me to baptise in water said to me, ‘ On whomever you will see the Spirit descending and remaining on him is he who baptises in the Holy Spirit.’

43:1:34.text: I have seen and have testified that this is the Son of God.”

43:1:35.text: Again, the next day, John was standing with two of his disciples,

43:1:36.text: and he looked at Jesus as he walked, and said, “Behold, the Lamb of God!”

43:1:37.text: The two disciples heard him speak, and they followed Jesus.

43:1:38.text: Jesus turned and saw them following, and said to them, “What are you looking for?” They said to him, “Rabbi” (which is to say, being interpreted, Teacher), “where are you staying?”

43:1:39.text: He said to them, “Come and see.” They came and saw where he was staying, and they stayed with him that day. It was about the tenth hour.

43:1:4.text: In him was life, and the life was the light of men.

43:1:40.text: One of the two who heard John and followed him was Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother.

43:1:41.text: He first found his own brother, Simon, and said to him, “We have found the Messiah!” (which is, being interpreted, Christ).

43:1:42.text: He brought him to Jesus. Jesus looked at him and said, “You are Simon the son of Jonah. You shall be called Cephas” (which is by interpretation, Peter).

43:1:43.text: On the next day, he was determined to go out into Galilee, and he found Philip. Jesus said to him, “Follow me.”

43:1:44.text: Now Philip was from Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter.

43:1:45.text: Philip found Nathanael, and said to him, “We have found him of whom Moses in the law and also the prophets, wrote: Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.”

43:1:46.text: Nathanael said to him, “Can any good thing come out of Nazareth?” Philip said to him, “Come and see.”

43:1:47.text: Jesus saw Nathanael coming to him, and said about him, “Behold, an Israelite indeed, in whom is no deceit!”

43:1:48.text: Nathanael said to him, “How do you know me?” Jesus answered him, “Before Philip called you, when you were under the fig tree, I saw you.”

43:1:49.text: Nathanael answered him, “Rabbi, you are the Son of God! You are King of Israel!”

43:1:5.text: The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness hasn’t overcome it.

43:1:50.text: Jesus answered him, “Because I told you, ‘ I saw you underneath the fig tree,’ do you believe? You will see greater things than these!”

43:1:51.text: He said to him, “Most certainly, I tell you all, hereafter you will see heaven opened, and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man.”

43:1:6.text: There came a man sent from God, whose name was John.

43:1:7.text: The same came as a witness, that he might testify about the light, that all might believe through him.

43:1:8.text: He was not the light, but was sent that he might testify about the light.

43:1:9.text: The true light that enlightens everyone was coming into the world.

43:20:1.text: Now on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene went early, while it was still dark, to the tomb, and saw that the stone had been taken away from the tomb.

43:20:10.text: So the disciples went away again to their own homes.

43:20:11.text: But Mary was standing outside at the tomb weeping. So as she wept, she stooped and looked into the tomb,

43:20:12.text: and she saw two angels in white sitting, one at the head and one at the feet, where the body of Jesus had lain.

43:20:13.text: They asked her, “Woman, why are you weeping?” She said to them, “Because they have taken away my Lord, and I don’t know where they have laid him.”

43:20:14.text: When she had said this, she turned around and saw Jesus standing, and didn’t know that it was Jesus.

43:20:15.text: Jesus said to her, “Woman, why are you weeping? Who are you looking for?” She, supposing him to be the gardener, said to him, “Sir, if you have carried him away, tell me where you have laid him, and I will take him away.”

43:20:16.text: Jesus said to her, “Mary.” She turned and said to him, “Rabboni!” which is to say, “Teacher!”

43:20:17.text: Jesus said to her, “Don’t hold me, for I haven’t yet ascended to my Father; but go to my brothers and tell them, ‘ I am ascending to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God.’ ”

43:20:18.text: Mary Magdalene came and told the disciples that she had seen the Lord, and that he had said these things to her.

43:20:19.text: When therefore it was evening on that day, the first day of the week, and when the doors were locked where the disciples were assembled, for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in the middle and said to them, “Peace be to you.”

43:20:2.text: Therefore she ran and came to Simon Peter and to the other disciple whom Jesus loved, and said to them, “They have taken away the Lord out of the tomb, and we don’t know where they have laid him!”

43:20:20.text: When he had said this, he showed them his hands and his side. The disciples therefore were glad when they saw the Lord.

43:20:21.text: Jesus therefore said to them again, “Peace be to you. As the Father has sent me, even so I send you.”

43:20:22.text: When he had said this, he breathed on them, and said to them, “Receive the Holy Spirit!

43:20:23.text: If you forgive anyone’s sins, they have been forgiven them. If you retain anyone’s sins, they have been retained.”

43:20:24.text: But Thomas, one of the twelve, called Didymus, wasn’t with them when Jesus came.

43:20:25.text: The other disciples therefore said to him, “We have seen the Lord!” But he said to them, “Unless I see in his hands the print of the nails, put my finger into the print of the nails, and put my hand into his side, I will not believe.”

43:20:26.text: After eight days, again his disciples were inside and Thomas was with them. Jesus came, the doors being locked, and stood in the middle, and said, “Peace be to you.”

43:20:27.text: Then he said to Thomas, “Reach here your finger, and see my hands. Reach here your hand, and put it into my side. Don’t be unbelieving, but believing.”

43:20:28.text: Thomas answered him, “My Lord and my God!”

43:20:29.text: Jesus said to him, “Because you have seen me, you have believed. Blessed are those who have not seen and have believed.”

43:20:3.text: Therefore Peter and the other disciple went out, and they went towards the tomb.

43:20:30.text: Therefore Jesus did many other signs in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book;

43:20:31.text: but these are written that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that believing you may have life in his name.

43:20:4.text: They both ran together. The other disciple outran Peter and came to the tomb first.

43:20:5.text: Stooping and looking in, he saw the linen cloths lying there; yet he didn’t enter in.

43:20:6.text: Then Simon Peter came, following him, and entered into the tomb. He saw the linen cloths lying,

43:20:7.text: and the cloth that had been on his head, not lying with the linen cloths, but rolled up in a place by itself.

43:20:8.text: So then the other disciple who came first to the tomb also entered in, and he saw and believed.

43:20:9.text: For as yet they didn’t know the Scripture, that he must rise from the dead.

43:21:1.text: After these things, Jesus revealed himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias. He revealed himself this way.

43:21:10.text: Jesus said to them, “Bring some of the fish which you have just caught.”

43:21:11.text: Simon Peter went up, and drew the net to land, full of one hundred and fifty-three great fish. Even though there were so many, the net wasn’t torn.

43:21:12.text: Jesus said to them, “Come and eat breakfast!” None of the disciples dared enquire of him, “Who are you?” knowing that it was the Lord.

43:21:13.text: Then Jesus came and took the bread, gave it to them, and the fish likewise.

43:21:14.text: This is now the third time that Jesus was revealed to his disciples after he had risen from the dead.

43:21:15.text: So when they had eaten their breakfast, Jesus said to Simon Peter, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me more than these?” He said to him, “Yes, Lord; you know that I have affection for you.” He said to him, “Feed my lambs.”

43:21:16.text: He said to him again a second time, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me?” He said to him, “Yes, Lord; you know that I have affection for you.” He said to him, “Tend my sheep.”

43:21:17.text: He said to him the third time, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you have affection for me?” Peter was grieved because he asked him the third time, “Do you have affection for me?” He said to him, “Lord, you know everything. You know that I have affection for you.” Jesus said to him, “Feed my sheep.

43:21:18.text: Most certainly I tell you, when you were young, you dressed yourself and walked where you wanted to. But when you are old, you will stretch out your hands, and another will dress you and carry you where you don’t want to go.”

43:21:19.text: Now he said this, signifying by what kind of death he would glorify God. When he had said this, he said to him, “Follow me.”

43:21:2.text: Simon Peter, Thomas called Didymus, Nathanael of Cana in Galilee, and the sons of Zebedee, and two others of his disciples were together.

43:21:20.text: Then Peter, turning around, saw a disciple following. This was the disciple whom Jesus loved, the one who had also leaned on Jesus’ chest at the supper and asked, “Lord, who is going to betray you?”

43:21:21.text: Peter, seeing him, said to Jesus, “Lord, what about this man?”

43:21:22.text: Jesus said to him, “If I desire that he stay until I come, what is that to you? You follow me.”

43:21:23.text: This saying therefore went out amongst the brothers that this disciple wouldn’t die. Yet Jesus didn’t say to him that he wouldn’t die, but, “If I desire that he stay until I come, what is that to you?”

43:21:24.text: This is the disciple who testifies about these things, and wrote these things. We know that his witness is true.

43:21:25.text: There are also many other things which Jesus did, which if they would all be written, I suppose that even the world itself wouldn’t have room for the books that would be written.

43:21:3.text: Simon Peter said to them, “I’m going fishing.” They told him, “We are also coming with you.” They immediately went out and entered into the boat. That night, they caught nothing.

43:21:4.text: But when day had already come, Jesus stood on the beach; yet the disciples didn’t know that it was Jesus.

43:21:5.text: Jesus therefore said to them, “Children, have you anything to eat?” They answered him, “No.”

43:21:6.text: He said to them, “Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and you will find some.” They cast it therefore, and now they weren’t able to draw it in for the multitude of fish.

43:21:7.text: That disciple therefore whom Jesus loved said to Peter, “It’s the Lord!” So when Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he wrapped his coat around himself (for he was naked), and threw himself into the sea.

43:21:8.text: But the other disciples came in the little boat (for they were not far from the land, but about two hundred cubits away), dragging the net full of fish.

43:21:9.text: So when they got out on the land, they saw a fire of coals there, with fish and bread laid on it.

43:2:1.text: The third day, there was a wedding in Cana of Galilee. Jesus’ mother was there.

43:2:10.text: and said to him, “Everyone serves the good wine first, and when the guests have drunk freely, then that which is worse. You have kept the good wine until now!”

43:2:11.text: This beginning of his signs Jesus did in Cana of Galilee, and revealed his glory; and his disciples believed in him.

43:2:12.text: After this, he went down to Capernaum, he, and his mother, his brothers, and his disciples; and they stayed there a few days.

43:2:13.text: The Passover of the Jews was at hand, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.

43:2:14.text: He found in the temple those who sold oxen, sheep, and doves, and the changers of money sitting.

43:2:15.text: He made a whip of cords and drove all out of the temple, both the sheep and the oxen; and he poured out the changers’ money and overthrew their tables.

43:2:16.text: To those who sold the doves, he said, “Take these things out of here! Don’t make my Father’s house a marketplace!”

43:2:17.text: His disciples remembered that it was written, “Zeal for your house will eat me up.”

43:2:18.text: The Jews therefore answered him, “What sign do you show us, seeing that you do these things?”

43:2:19.text: Jesus answered them, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.”

43:2:2.text: Jesus also was invited, with his disciples, to the wedding.

43:2:20.text: The Jews therefore said, “It took forty-six years to build this temple! Will you raise it up in three days?”

43:2:21.text: But he spoke of the temple of his body.

43:2:22.text: When therefore he was raised from the dead, his disciples remembered that he said this, and they believed the Scripture and the word which Jesus had said.

43:2:23.text: Now when he was in Jerusalem at the Passover, during the feast, many believed in his name, observing his signs which he did.

43:2:24.text: But Jesus didn’t entrust himself to them, because he knew everyone,

43:2:25.text: and because he didn’t need for anyone to testify concerning man; for he himself knew what was in man.

43:2:3.text: When the wine ran out, Jesus’ mother said to him, “They have no wine.”

43:2:4.text: Jesus said to her, “Woman, what does that have to do with you and me? My hour has not yet come.”

43:2:5.text: His mother said to the servants, “Whatever he says to you, do it.”

43:2:6.text: Now there were six water pots of stone set there after the Jews’ way of purifying, containing two or three metretes apiece.

43:2:7.text: Jesus said to them, “Fill the water pots with water.” So they filled them up to the brim.

43:2:8.text: He said to them, “Now draw some out, and take it to the ruler of the feast.” So they took it.

43:2:9.text: When the ruler of the feast tasted the water now become wine, and didn’t know where it came from (but the servants who had drawn the water knew), the ruler of the feast called the bridegroom

43:3:1.text: Now there was a man of the Pharisees named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews.

43:3:10.text: Jesus answered him, “Are you the teacher of Israel, and don’t understand these things?

43:3:11.text: Most certainly I tell you, we speak that which we know and testify of that which we have seen, and you don’t receive our witness.

43:3:12.text: If I told you earthly things and you don’t believe, how will you believe if I tell you heavenly things?

43:3:13.text: No one has ascended into heaven but he who descended out of heaven, the Son of Man, who is in heaven.

43:3:14.text: As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of Man be lifted up,

43:3:15.text: that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.

43:3:16.text: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only born Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.

43:3:17.text: For God didn’t send his Son into the world to judge the world, but that the world should be saved through him.

43:3:18.text: He who believes in him is not judged. He who doesn’t believe has been judged already, because he has not believed in the name of the only born Son of God.

43:3:19.text: This is the judgement, that the light has come into the world, and men loved the darkness rather than the light, for their works were evil.

43:3:2.text: He came to Jesus by night and said to him, “Rabbi, we know that you are a teacher come from God, for no one can do these signs that you do, unless God is with him.”

43:3:20.text: For everyone who does evil hates the light and doesn’t come to the light, lest his works would be exposed.

43:3:21.text: But he who does the truth comes to the light, that his works may be revealed, that they have been done in God.”

43:3:22.text: After these things, Jesus came with his disciples into the land of Judea. He stayed there with them and baptised.

43:3:23.text: John also was baptising in Enon near Salim, because there was much water there. They came and were baptised;

43:3:24.text: for John was not yet thrown into prison.

43:3:25.text: Therefore a dispute arose on the part of John’s disciples with some Jews about purification.

43:3:26.text: They came to John and said to him, “Rabbi, he who was with you beyond the Jordan, to whom you have testified, behold, he baptises, and everyone is coming to him.”

43:3:27.text: John answered, “A man can receive nothing unless it has been given him from heaven.

43:3:28.text: You yourselves testify that I said, ‘ I am not the Christ,’ but, ‘ I have been sent before him.’

43:3:29.text: He who has the bride is the bridegroom; but the friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices greatly because of the bridegroom’s voice. Therefore my joy is made full.

43:3:3.text: Jesus answered him, “Most certainly I tell you, unless one is born anew, he can’t see God’s Kingdom.”

43:3:30.text: He must increase, but I must decrease.

43:3:31.text: “He who comes from above is above all. He who is from the earth belongs to the earth and speaks of the earth. He who comes from heaven is above all.

43:3:32.text: What he has seen and heard, of that he testifies; and no one receives his witness.

43:3:33.text: He who has received his witness has set his seal to this, that God is true.

43:3:34.text: For he whom God has sent speaks the words of God; for God gives the Spirit without measure.

43:3:35.text: The Father loves the Son, and has given all things into his hand.

43:3:36.text: One who believes in the Son has eternal life, but one who disobeys the Son won’t see life, but the wrath of God remains on him.”

43:3:4.text: Nicodemus said to him, “How can a man be born when he is old? Can he enter a second time into his mother’s womb and be born?”

43:3:5.text: Jesus answered, “Most certainly I tell you, unless one is born of water and Spirit, he can’t enter into God’s Kingdom.

43:3:6.text: That which is born of the flesh is flesh. That which is born of the Spirit is spirit.

43:3:7.text: Don’t marvel that I said to you, ‘ You must be born anew.’

43:3:8.text: The wind blows where it wants to, and you hear its sound, but don’t know where it comes from and where it is going. So is everyone who is born of the Spirit.”

43:3:9.text: Nicodemus answered him, “How can these things be?”

43:4:1.text: Therefore when the Lord knew that the Pharisees had heard that Jesus was making and baptising more disciples than John

43:4:10.text: Jesus answered her, “If you knew the gift of God, and who it is who says to you, ‘ Give me a drink,’ you would have asked him, and he would have given you living water.”

43:4:11.text: The woman said to him, “Sir, you have nothing to draw with, and the well is deep. So where do you get that living water?

43:4:12.text: Are you greater than our father Jacob, who gave us the well and drank from it himself, as did his children and his livestock?”

43:4:13.text: Jesus answered her, “Everyone who drinks of this water will thirst again,

43:4:14.text: but whoever drinks of the water that I will give him will never thirst again; but the water that I will give him will become in him a well of water springing up to eternal life.”

43:4:15.text: The woman said to him, “Sir, give me this water, so that I don’t get thirsty, neither come all the way here to draw.”

43:4:16.text: Jesus said to her, “Go, call your husband, and come here.”

43:4:17.text: The woman answered, “I have no husband.” Jesus said to her, “You said well, ‘ I have no husband,’

43:4:18.text: for you have had five husbands; and he whom you now have is not your husband. This you have said truly.”

43:4:19.text: The woman said to him, “Sir, I perceive that you are a prophet.

43:4:2.text: (although Jesus himself didn’t baptise, but his disciples),

43:4:20.text: Our fathers worshipped in this mountain, and you Jews say that in Jerusalem is the place where people ought to worship.”

43:4:21.text: Jesus said to her, “Woman, believe me, the hour is coming when neither in this mountain nor in Jerusalem will you worship the Father.

43:4:22.text: You worship that which you don’t know. We worship that which we know; for salvation is from the Jews.

43:4:23.text: But the hour comes, and now is, when the true worshippers will worship the Father in spirit and truth, for the Father seeks such to be his worshippers.

43:4:24.text: God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth.”

43:4:25.text: The woman said to him, “I know that Messiah is coming, he who is called Christ. When he has come, he will declare to us all things.”

43:4:26.text: Jesus said to her, “I am he, the one who speaks to you.”

43:4:27.text: Just then, his disciples came. They marvelled that he was speaking with a woman; yet no one said, “What are you looking for?” or, “Why do you speak with her?”

43:4:28.text: So the woman left her water pot, went away into the city, and said to the people,

43:4:29.text: “Come, see a man who told me everything that I have done. Can this be the Christ?”

43:4:3.text: he left Judea and departed into Galilee.

43:4:30.text: They went out of the city, and were coming to him.

43:4:31.text: In the meanwhile, the disciples urged him, saying, “Rabbi, eat.”

43:4:32.text: But he said to them, “I have food to eat that you don’t know about.”

43:4:33.text: The disciples therefore said to one another, “Has anyone brought him something to eat?”

43:4:34.text: Jesus said to them, “My food is to do the will of him who sent me and to accomplish his work.

43:4:35.text: Don’t you say, ‘ There are yet four months until the harvest’ ? Behold, I tell you, lift up your eyes and look at the fields, that they are white for harvest already.

43:4:36.text: He who reaps receives wages and gathers fruit to eternal life, that both he who sows and he who reaps may rejoice together.

43:4:37.text: For in this the saying is true, ‘ One sows, and another reaps.’

43:4:38.text: I sent you to reap that for which you haven’t laboured. Others have laboured, and you have entered into their labour.”

43:4:39.text: From that city many of the Samaritans believed in him because of the word of the woman, who testified, “He told me everything that I have done.”

43:4:4.text: He needed to pass through Samaria.

43:4:40.text: So when the Samaritans came to him, they begged him to stay with them. He stayed there two days.

43:4:41.text: Many more believed because of his word.

43:4:42.text: They said to the woman, “Now we believe, not because of your speaking; for we have heard for ourselves, and know that this is indeed the Christ, the Saviour of the world.”

43:4:43.text: After the two days he went out from there and went into Galilee.

43:4:44.text: For Jesus himself testified that a prophet has no honour in his own country.

43:4:45.text: So when he came into Galilee, the Galileans received him, having seen all the things that he did in Jerusalem at the feast, for they also went to the feast.

43:4:46.text: Jesus came therefore again to Cana of Galilee, where he made the water into wine. There was a certain nobleman whose son was sick at Capernaum.

43:4:47.text: When he heard that Jesus had come out of Judea into Galilee, he went to him and begged him that he would come down and heal his son, for he was at the point of death.

43:4:48.text: Jesus therefore said to him, “Unless you see signs and wonders, you will in no way believe.”

43:4:49.text: The nobleman said to him, “Sir, come down before my child dies.”

43:4:5.text: So he came to a city of Samaria called Sychar, near the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph.

43:4:50.text: Jesus said to him, “Go your way. Your son lives.” The man believed the word that Jesus spoke to him, and he went his way.

43:4:51.text: As he was going down, his servants met him and reported, saying “Your child lives!”

43:4:52.text: So he enquired of them the hour when he began to get better. They said therefore to him, “Yesterday at the seventh hour, the fever left him.”

43:4:53.text: So the father knew that it was at that hour in which Jesus said to him, “Your son lives.” He believed, as did his whole house.

43:4:54.text: This is again the second sign that Jesus did, having come out of Judea into Galilee.

43:4:6.text: Jacob’s well was there. Jesus therefore, being tired from his journey, sat down by the well. It was about the sixth hour.

43:4:7.text: A woman of Samaria came to draw water. Jesus said to her, “Give me a drink.”

43:4:8.text: For his disciples had gone away into the city to buy food.

43:4:9.text: The Samaritan woman therefore said to him, “How is it that you, being a Jew, ask for a drink from me, a Samaritan woman?” (For Jews have no dealings with Samaritans.)

43:5:1.text: After these things, there was a feast of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.

43:5:10.text: So the Jews said to him who was cured, “It is the Sabbath. It is not lawful for you to carry the mat.”

43:5:11.text: He answered them, “He who made me well said to me, ‘ Take up your mat and walk.’ ”

43:5:12.text: Then they asked him, “Who is the man who said to you, ‘ Take up your mat and walk’ ?”

43:5:13.text: But he who was healed didn’t know who it was, for Jesus had withdrawn, a crowd being in the place.

43:5:14.text: Afterward Jesus found him in the temple and said to him, “Behold, you are made well. Sin no more, so that nothing worse happens to you.”

43:5:15.text: The man went away, and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had made him well.

43:5:16.text: For this cause the Jews persecuted Jesus and sought to kill him, because he did these things on the Sabbath.

43:5:17.text: But Jesus answered them, “My Father is still working, so I am working, too.”

43:5:18.text: For this cause therefore the Jews sought all the more to kill him, because he not only broke the Sabbath, but also called God his own Father, making himself equal with God.

43:5:19.text: Jesus therefore answered them, “Most certainly, I tell you, the Son can do nothing of himself, but what he sees the Father doing. For whatever things he does, these the Son also does likewise.

43:5:2.text: Now in Jerusalem by the sheep gate, there is a pool, which is called in Hebrew, “Bethesda”, having five porches.

43:5:20.text: For the Father has affection for the Son, and shows him all things that he himself does. He will show him greater works than these, that you may marvel.

43:5:21.text: For as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, even so the Son also gives life to whom he desires.

43:5:22.text: For the Father judges no one, but he has given all judgement to the Son,

43:5:23.text: that all may honour the Son, even as they honour the Father. He who doesn’t honour the Son doesn’t honour the Father who sent him.

43:5:24.text: “Most certainly I tell you, he who hears my word and believes him who sent me has eternal life, and doesn’t come into judgement, but has passed out of death into life.

43:5:25.text: Most certainly I tell you, the hour comes, and now is, when the dead will hear the Son of God’s voice; and those who hear will live.

43:5:26.text: For as the Father has life in himself, even so he gave to the Son also to have life in himself.

43:5:27.text: He also gave him authority to execute judgement, because he is a son of man.

43:5:28.text: Don’t marvel at this, for the hour comes in which all who are in the tombs will hear his voice

43:5:29.text: and will come out; those who have done good, to the resurrection of life; and those who have done evil, to the resurrection of judgement.

43:5:3.text: In these lay a great multitude of those who were sick, blind, lame, or paralysed, waiting for the moving of the water;

43:5:30.text: I can of myself do nothing. As I hear, I judge; and my judgement is righteous, because I don’t seek my own will, but the will of my Father who sent me.

43:5:31.text: “If I testify about myself, my witness is not valid.

43:5:32.text: It is another who testifies about me. I know that the testimony which he testifies about me is true.

43:5:33.text: You have sent to John, and he has testified to the truth.

43:5:34.text: But the testimony which I receive is not from man. However, I say these things that you may be saved.

43:5:35.text: He was the burning and shining lamp, and you were willing to rejoice for a while in his light.

43:5:36.text: But the testimony which I have is greater than that of John; for the works which the Father gave me to accomplish, the very works that I do, testify about me, that the Father has sent me.

43:5:37.text: The Father himself, who sent me, has testified about me. You have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his form.

43:5:38.text: You don’t have his word living in you, because you don’t believe him whom he sent.

43:5:39.text: “You search the Scriptures, because you think that in them you have eternal life; and these are they which testify about me.

43:5:4.text: for an angel went down at certain times into the pool and stirred up the water. Whoever stepped in first after the stirring of the water was healed of whatever disease he had.

43:5:40.text: Yet you will not come to me, that you may have life.

43:5:41.text: I don’t receive glory from men.

43:5:42.text: But I know you, that you don’t have God’s love in yourselves.

43:5:43.text: I have come in my Father’s name, and you don’t receive me. If another comes in his own name, you will receive him.

43:5:44.text: How can you believe, who receive glory from one another, and you don’t seek the glory that comes from the only God?

43:5:45.text: “Don’t think that I will accuse you to the Father. There is one who accuses you, even Moses, on whom you have set your hope.

43:5:46.text: For if you believed Moses, you would believe me; for he wrote about me.

43:5:47.text: But if you don’t believe his writings, how will you believe my words?”

43:5:5.text: A certain man was there who had been sick for thirty-eight years.

43:5:6.text: When Jesus saw him lying there, and knew that he had been sick for a long time, he asked him, “Do you want to be made well?”

43:5:7.text: The sick man answered him, “Sir, I have no one to put me into the pool when the water is stirred up, but while I’m coming, another steps down before me.”

43:5:8.text: Jesus said to him, “Arise, take up your mat, and walk.”

43:5:9.text: Immediately, the man was made well, and took up his mat and walked. Now that day was a Sabbath.

43:6:1.text: After these things, Jesus went away to the other side of the sea of Galilee, which is also called the Sea of Tiberias.

43:6:10.text: Jesus said, “Have the people sit down.” Now there was much grass in that place. So the men sat down, in number about five thousand.

43:6:11.text: Jesus took the loaves, and having given thanks, he distributed to the disciples, and the disciples to those who were sitting down, likewise also of the fish as much as they desired.

43:6:12.text: When they were filled, he said to his disciples, “Gather up the broken pieces which are left over, that nothing be lost.”

43:6:13.text: So they gathered them up, and filled twelve baskets with broken pieces from the five barley loaves, which were left over by those who had eaten.

43:6:14.text: When therefore the people saw the sign which Jesus did, they said, “This is truly the prophet who comes into the world.”

43:6:15.text: Jesus therefore, perceiving that they were about to come and take him by force to make him king, withdrew again to the mountain by himself.

43:6:16.text: When evening came, his disciples went down to the sea.

43:6:17.text: They entered into the boat, and were going over the sea to Capernaum. It was now dark, and Jesus had not come to them.

43:6:18.text: The sea was tossed by a great wind blowing.

43:6:19.text: When therefore they had rowed about twenty-five or thirty stadia, they saw Jesus walking on the sea and drawing near to the boat; and they were afraid.

43:6:2.text: A great multitude followed him, because they saw his signs which he did on those who were sick.

43:6:20.text: But he said to them, “It is I. Don’t be afraid.”

43:6:21.text: They were willing therefore to receive him into the boat. Immediately the boat was at the land where they were going.

43:6:22.text: On the next day, the multitude that stood on the other side of the sea saw that there was no other boat there, except the one in which his disciples had embarked, and that Jesus hadn’t entered with his disciples into the boat, but his disciples had gone away alone.

43:6:23.text: However, boats from Tiberias came near to the place where they ate the bread after the Lord had given thanks.

43:6:24.text: When the multitude therefore saw that Jesus wasn’t there, nor his disciples, they themselves got into the boats and came to Capernaum, seeking Jesus.

43:6:25.text: When they found him on the other side of the sea, they asked him, “Rabbi, when did you come here?”

43:6:26.text: Jesus answered them, “Most certainly I tell you, you seek me, not because you saw signs, but because you ate of the loaves and were filled.

43:6:27.text: Don’t work for the food which perishes, but for the food which remains to eternal life, which the Son of Man will give to you. For God the Father has sealed him.”

43:6:28.text: They said therefore to him, “What must we do, that we may work the works of God?”

43:6:29.text: Jesus answered them, “This is the work of God, that you believe in him whom he has sent.”

43:6:3.text: Jesus went up into the mountain, and he sat there with his disciples.

43:6:30.text: They said therefore to him, “What then do you do for a sign, that we may see and believe you? What work do you do?

43:6:31.text: Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness. As it is written, ‘ He gave them bread out of heaven to eat.’ ”

43:6:32.text: Jesus therefore said to them, “Most certainly, I tell you, it wasn’t Moses who gave you the bread out of heaven, but my Father gives you the true bread out of heaven.

43:6:33.text: For the bread of God is that which comes down out of heaven and gives life to the world.”

43:6:34.text: They said therefore to him, “Lord, always give us this bread.”

43:6:35.text: Jesus said to them, “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will not be hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty.

43:6:36.text: But I told you that you have seen me, and yet you don’t believe.

43:6:37.text: All those whom the Father gives me will come to me. He who comes to me I will in no way throw out.

43:6:38.text: For I have come down from heaven, not to do my own will, but the will of him who sent me.

43:6:39.text: This is the will of my Father who sent me, that of all he has given to me I should lose nothing, but should raise him up at the last day.

43:6:4.text: Now the Passover, the feast of the Jews, was at hand.
