45:14:6.text: He who observes the day, observes it to the Lord; and he who does not observe the day, to the Lord he does not observe it. He who eats, eats to the Lord, for he gives God thanks. He who doesn’t eat, to the Lord he doesn’t eat, and gives God thanks.

45:14:7.text: For none of us lives to himself, and none dies to himself.

45:14:8.text: For if we live, we live to the Lord. Or if we die, we die to the Lord. If therefore we live or die, we are the Lord’s.

45:14:9.text: For to this end Christ died, rose, and lived again, that he might be Lord of both the dead and the living.

45:15:1.text: Now we who are strong ought to bear the weaknesses of the weak, and not to please ourselves.

45:15:10.text: Again he says, “Rejoice, you Gentiles, with his people.”

45:15:11.text: Again, “Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles! Let all the peoples praise him.”

45:15:12.text: Again, Isaiah says, “There will be the root of Jesse, he who arises to rule over the Gentiles; in him the Gentiles will hope.”

45:15:13.text: Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that you may abound in hope in the power of the Holy Spirit.

45:15:14.text: I myself am also persuaded about you, my brothers, that you yourselves are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, able also to admonish others.

45:15:15.text: But I write the more boldly to you in part as reminding you, because of the grace that was given to me by God,

45:15:16.text: that I should be a servant of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles, serving as a priest of the Good News of God, that the offering up of the Gentiles might be made acceptable, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.

45:15:17.text: I have therefore my boasting in Christ Jesus in things pertaining to God.

45:15:18.text: For I will not dare to speak of any things except those which Christ worked through me for the obedience of the Gentiles, by word and deed,

45:15:19.text: in the power of signs and wonders, in the power of God’s Spirit; so that from Jerusalem and around as far as to Illyricum, I have fully preached the Good News of Christ;

45:15:2.text: Let each one of us please his neighbour for that which is good, to be building him up.

45:15:20.text: yes, making it my aim to preach the Good News, not where Christ was already named, that I might not build on another’s foundation.

45:15:21.text: But, as it is written, “They will see, to whom no news of him came. They who haven’t heard will understand.”

45:15:22.text: Therefore also I was hindered these many times from coming to you,

45:15:23.text: but now, no longer having any place in these regions, and having these many years a longing to come to you,

45:15:24.text: whenever I travel to Spain, I will come to you. For I hope to see you on my journey, and to be helped on my way there by you, if first I may enjoy your company for a while.

45:15:25.text: But now, I say, I am going to Jerusalem, serving the saints.

45:15:26.text: For it has been the good pleasure of Macedonia and Achaia to make a certain contribution for the poor amongst the saints who are at Jerusalem.

45:15:27.text: Yes, it has been their good pleasure, and they are their debtors. For if the Gentiles have been made partakers of their spiritual things, they owe it to them also to serve them in material things.

45:15:28.text: When therefore I have accomplished this, and have sealed to them this fruit, I will go on by way of you to Spain.

45:15:29.text: I know that when I come to you, I will come in the fullness of the blessing of the Good News of Christ.

45:15:3.text: For even Christ didn’t please himself. But, as it is written, “The reproaches of those who reproached you fell on me.”

45:15:30.text: Now I beg you, brothers, by our Lord Jesus Christ and by the love of the Spirit, that you strive together with me in your prayers to God for me,

45:15:31.text: that I may be delivered from those who are disobedient in Judea, and that my service which I have for Jerusalem may be acceptable to the saints,

45:15:32.text: that I may come to you in joy through the will of God, and together with you, find rest.

45:15:33.text: Now the God of peace be with you all. Amen.

45:15:4.text: For whatever things were written before were written for our learning, that through perseverance and through encouragement of the Scriptures we might have hope.

45:15:5.text: Now the God of perseverance and of encouragement grant you to be of the same mind with one another according to Christ Jesus,

45:15:6.text: that with one accord you may with one mouth glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.

45:15:7.text: Therefore accept one another, even as Christ also accepted you, to the glory of God.

45:15:8.text: Now I say that Christ has been made a servant of the circumcision for the truth of God, that he might confirm the promises given to the fathers,

45:15:9.text: and that the Gentiles might glorify God for his mercy. As it is written, “Therefore I will give praise to you amongst the Gentiles and sing to your name.”

45:16:1.text: I commend to you Phoebe, our sister, who is a servant of the assembly that is at Cenchreae,

45:16:10.text: Greet Apelles, the approved in Christ. Greet those who are of the household of Aristobulus.

45:16:11.text: Greet Herodion, my kinsman. Greet them of the household of Narcissus, who are in the Lord.

45:16:12.text: Greet Tryphaena and Tryphosa, who labour in the Lord. Greet Persis, the beloved, who laboured much in the Lord.

45:16:13.text: Greet Rufus, the chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine.

45:16:14.text: Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers who are with them.

45:16:15.text: Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints who are with them.

45:16:16.text: Greet one another with a holy kiss. The assemblies of Christ greet you.

45:16:17.text: Now I beg you, brothers, look out for those who are causing the divisions and occasions of stumbling, contrary to the doctrine which you learnt, and turn away from them.

45:16:18.text: For those who are such don’t serve our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly; and by their smooth and flattering speech they deceive the hearts of the innocent.

45:16:19.text: For your obedience has become known to all. I rejoice therefore over you. But I desire to have you wise in that which is good, but innocent in that which is evil.

45:16:2.text: that you receive her in the Lord in a way worthy of the saints, and that you assist her in whatever matter she may need from you, for she herself also has been a helper of many, and of my own self.

45:16:20.text: And the God of peace will quickly crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.

45:16:21.text: Timothy, my fellow worker, greets you, as do Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater, my relatives.

45:16:22.text: I, Tertius, who write the letter, greet you in the Lord.

45:16:23.text: Gaius, my host and host of the whole assembly, greets you. Erastus, the treasurer of the city, greets you, as does Quartus, the brother.

45:16:24.text: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all! Amen.

45:16:3.text: Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus,

45:16:4.text: who risked their own necks for my life, to whom not only I give thanks, but also all the assemblies of the Gentiles.

45:16:5.text: Greet the assembly that is in their house. Greet Epaenetus, my beloved, who is the first fruits of Achaia to Christ.

45:16:6.text: Greet Mary, who laboured much for us.

45:16:7.text: Greet Andronicus and Junia, my relatives and my fellow prisoners, who are notable amongst the apostles, who were also in Christ before me.

45:16:8.text: Greet Amplias, my beloved in the Lord.

45:16:9.text: Greet Urbanus, our fellow worker in Christ, and Stachys, my beloved.

45:1:1.text: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, set apart for the Good News of God,

45:1:10.text: requesting, if by any means now at last I may be prospered by the will of God to come to you.

45:1:11.text: For I long to see you, that I may impart to you some spiritual gift, to the end that you may be established;

45:1:12.text: that is, that I with you may be encouraged in you, each of us by the other’s faith, both yours and mine.

45:1:13.text: Now I don’t desire to have you unaware, brothers, that I often planned to come to you (and was hindered so far), that I might have some fruit amongst you also, even as amongst the rest of the Gentiles.

45:1:14.text: I am debtor both to Greeks and to foreigners, both to the wise and to the foolish.

45:1:15.text: So as much as is in me, I am eager to preach the Good News to you also who are in Rome.

45:1:16.text: For I am not ashamed of the Good News of Christ, because it is the power of God for salvation for everyone who believes, for the Jew first, and also for the Greek.

45:1:17.text: For in it is revealed God’s righteousness from faith to faith. As it is written, “But the righteous shall live by faith.”

45:1:18.text: For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men who suppress the truth in unrighteousness,

45:1:19.text: because that which is known of God is revealed in them, for God revealed it to them.

45:1:2.text: which he promised before through his prophets in the holy Scriptures,

45:1:20.text: For the invisible things of him since the creation of the world are clearly seen, being perceived through the things that are made, even his everlasting power and divinity, that they may be without excuse.

45:1:21.text: Because knowing God, they didn’t glorify him as God, and didn’t give thanks, but became vain in their reasoning, and their senseless heart was darkened.

45:1:22.text: Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,

45:1:23.text: and traded the glory of the incorruptible God for the likeness of an image of corruptible man, and of birds, four-footed animals, and creeping things.

45:1:24.text: Therefore God also gave them up in the lusts of their hearts to uncleanness, that their bodies should be dishonoured amongst themselves;

45:1:25.text: who exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and worshipped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever. Amen.

45:1:26.text: For this reason, God gave them up to vile passions. For their women changed the natural function into that which is against nature.

45:1:27.text: Likewise also the men, leaving the natural function of the woman, burnt in their lust towards one another, men doing what is inappropriate with men, and receiving in themselves the due penalty of their error.

45:1:28.text: Even as they refused to have God in their knowledge, God gave them up to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not fitting;

45:1:29.text: being filled with all unrighteousness, sexual immorality, wickedness, covetousness, malice; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, evil habits, secret slanderers,

45:1:3.text: concerning his Son, who was born of the offspring of David according to the flesh,

45:1:30.text: backbiters, hateful to God, insolent, arrogant, boastful, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents,

45:1:31.text: without understanding, covenant breakers, without natural affection, unforgiving, unmerciful;

45:1:32.text: who, knowing the ordinance of God, that those who practise such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but also approve of those who practise them.

45:1:4.text: who was declared to be the Son of God with power according to the Spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead, Jesus Christ our Lord,

45:1:5.text: through whom we received grace and apostleship for obedience of faith amongst all the nations for his name’s sake;

45:1:6.text: amongst whom you are also called to belong to Jesus Christ;

45:1:7.text: to all who are in Rome, beloved of God, called to be saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

45:1:8.text: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, that your faith is proclaimed throughout the whole world.

45:1:9.text: For God is my witness, whom I serve in my spirit in the Good News of his Son, how unceasingly I make mention of you always in my prayers,

45:2:1.text: Therefore you are without excuse, O man, whoever you are who judge. For in that which you judge another, you condemn yourself. For you who judge practise the same things.

45:2:10.text: But glory, honour, and peace go to every man who does good, to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.

45:2:11.text: For there is no partiality with God.

45:2:12.text: For as many as have sinned without the law will also perish without the law. As many as have sinned under the law will be judged by the law.

45:2:13.text: For it isn’t the hearers of the law who are righteous before God, but the doers of the law will be justified

45:2:14.text: (for when Gentiles who don’t have the law do by nature the things of the law, these, not having the law, are a law to themselves,

45:2:15.text: in that they show the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience testifying with them, and their thoughts amongst themselves accusing or else excusing them)

45:2:16.text: in the day when God will judge the secrets of men, according to my Good News, by Jesus Christ.

45:2:17.text: Indeed you bear the name of a Jew, rest on the law, glory in God,

45:2:18.text: know his will, and approve the things that are excellent, being instructed out of the law,

45:2:19.text: and are confident that you yourself are a guide of the blind, a light to those who are in darkness,

45:2:2.text: We know that the judgement of God is according to truth against those who practise such things.

45:2:20.text: a corrector of the foolish, a teacher of babies, having in the law the form of knowledge and of the truth.

45:2:21.text: You therefore who teach another, don’t you teach yourself? You who preach that a man shouldn’t steal, do you steal?

45:2:22.text: You who say a man shouldn’t commit adultery, do you commit adultery? You who abhor idols, do you rob temples?

45:2:23.text: You who glory in the law, do you dishonour God by disobeying the law?

45:2:24.text: For “the name of God is blasphemed amongst the Gentiles because of you,” just as it is written.

45:2:25.text: For circumcision indeed profits, if you are a doer of the law, but if you are a transgressor of the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.

45:2:26.text: If therefore the uncircumcised keep the ordinances of the law, won’t his uncircumcision be accounted as circumcision?

45:2:27.text: Won’t those who are physically uncircumcised, but fulfil the law, judge you, who with the letter and circumcision are a transgressor of the law?

45:2:28.text: For he is not a Jew who is one outwardly, neither is that circumcision which is outward in the flesh;

45:2:29.text: but he is a Jew who is one inwardly, and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, not in the letter; whose praise is not from men, but from God.

45:2:3.text: Do you think this, O man who judges those who practise such things, and do the same, that you will escape the judgement of God?

45:2:4.text: Or do you despise the riches of his goodness, forbearance, and patience, not knowing that the goodness of God leads you to repentance?

45:2:5.text: But according to your hardness and unrepentant heart you are treasuring up for yourself wrath in the day of wrath, revelation, and of the righteous judgement of God,

45:2:6.text: who “will pay back to everyone according to their works:”

45:2:7.text: to those who by perseverance in well-doing seek for glory, honour, and incorruptibility, eternal life;

45:2:8.text: but to those who are self-seeking and don’t obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness, will be wrath, indignation,

45:2:9.text: oppression, and anguish on every soul of man who does evil, to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.

45:3:1.text: Then what advantage does the Jew have? Or what is the profit of circumcision?

45:3:10.text: As it is written, “There is no one righteous; no, not one.

45:3:11.text: There is no one who understands. There is no one who seeks after God.

45:3:12.text: They have all turned away. They have together become unprofitable. There is no one who does good, no, not so much as one.”

45:3:13.text: “Their throat is an open tomb. With their tongues they have used deceit.” “The poison of vipers is under their lips.”

45:3:14.text: “Their mouth is full of cursing and bitterness.”

45:3:15.text: “Their feet are swift to shed blood.

45:3:16.text: Destruction and misery are in their ways.

45:3:17.text: The way of peace, they haven’t known.”

45:3:18.text: “There is no fear of God before their eyes.”

45:3:19.text: Now we know that whatever things the law says, it speaks to those who are under the law, that every mouth may be closed, and all the world may be brought under the judgement of God.

45:3:2.text: Much in every way! Because first of all, they were entrusted with the revelations of God.

45:3:20.text: Because by the works of the law, no flesh will be justified in his sight; for through the law comes the knowledge of sin.

45:3:21.text: But now apart from the law, a righteousness of God has been revealed, being testified by the law and the prophets;

45:3:22.text: even the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ to all and on all those who believe. For there is no distinction,

45:3:23.text: for all have sinned, and fall short of the glory of God;

45:3:24.text: being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus,

45:3:25.text: whom God sent to be an atoning sacrifice through faith in his blood, for a demonstration of his righteousness through the passing over of prior sins, in God’s forbearance;

45:3:26.text: to demonstrate his righteousness at this present time, that he might himself be just and the justifier of him who has faith in Jesus.

45:3:27.text: Where then is the boasting? It is excluded. By what kind of law? Of works? No, but by a law of faith.

45:3:28.text: We maintain therefore that a man is justified by faith apart from the works of the law.

45:3:29.text: Or is God the God of Jews only? Isn’t he the God of Gentiles also? Yes, of Gentiles also,

45:3:3.text: For what if some were without faith? Will their lack of faith nullify the faithfulness of God?

45:3:30.text: since indeed there is one God who will justify the circumcised by faith and the uncircumcised through faith.

45:3:31.text: Do we then nullify the law through faith? May it never be! No, we establish the law.

45:3:4.text: May it never be! Yes, let God be found true, but every man a liar. As it is written, “that you might be justified in your words, and might prevail when you come into judgement.”

45:3:5.text: But if our unrighteousness commends the righteousness of God, what will we say? Is God unrighteous who inflicts wrath? I speak like men do.

45:3:6.text: May it never be! For then how will God judge the world?

45:3:7.text: For if the truth of God through my lie abounded to his glory, why am I also still judged as a sinner?

45:3:8.text: Why not (as we are slanderously reported, and as some affirm that we say), “Let’s do evil, that good may come?” Those who say so are justly condemned.

45:3:9.text: What then? Are we better than they? No, in no way. For we previously warned both Jews and Greeks that they are all under sin.

45:4:1.text: What then will we say that Abraham, our forefather, has found according to the flesh?

45:4:10.text: How then was it counted? When he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.

45:4:11.text: He received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had while he was in uncircumcision, that he might be the father of all those who believe, though they might be in uncircumcision, that righteousness might also be accounted to them.

45:4:12.text: He is the father of circumcision to those who not only are of the circumcision, but who also walk in the steps of that faith of our father Abraham, which he had in uncircumcision.

45:4:13.text: For the promise to Abraham and to his offspring that he would be heir of the world wasn’t through the law, but through the righteousness of faith.

45:4:14.text: For if those who are of the law are heirs, faith is made void, and the promise is made of no effect.

45:4:15.text: For the law produces wrath; for where there is no law, neither is there disobedience.

45:4:16.text: For this cause it is of faith, that it may be according to grace, to the end that the promise may be sure to all the offspring, not to that only which is of the law, but to that also which is of the faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all.

45:4:17.text: As it is written, “I have made you a father of many nations.” This is in the presence of him whom he believed: God, who gives life to the dead, and calls the things that are not, as though they were.

45:4:18.text: Against hope, Abraham in hope believed, to the end that he might become a father of many nations, according to that which had been spoken, “So will your offspring be.”

45:4:19.text: Without being weakened in faith, he didn’t consider his own body, already having been worn out, (he being about a hundred years old), and the deadness of Sarah’s womb.

45:4:2.text: For if Abraham was justified by works, he has something to boast about, but not towards God.

45:4:20.text: Yet, looking to the promise of God, he didn’t waver through unbelief, but grew strong through faith, giving glory to God,

45:4:21.text: and being fully assured that what he had promised, he was also able to perform.

45:4:22.text: Therefore it also was “credited to him for righteousness.”

45:4:23.text: Now it was not written that it was accounted to him for his sake alone,

45:4:24.text: but for our sake also, to whom it will be accounted, who believe in him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead,

45:4:25.text: who was delivered up for our trespasses, and was raised for our justification.

45:4:3.text: For what does the Scripture say? “Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him for righteousness.”

45:4:4.text: Now to him who works, the reward is not counted as grace, but as something owed.

45:4:5.text: But to him who doesn’t work, but believes in him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is accounted for righteousness.

45:4:6.text: Even as David also pronounces blessing on the man to whom God counts righteousness apart from works:

45:4:7.text: “Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, whose sins are covered.

45:4:8.text: Blessed is the man whom the Lord will by no means charge with sin.”

45:4:9.text: Is this blessing then pronounced only on the circumcised, or on the uncircumcised also? For we say that faith was accounted to Abraham for righteousness.

45:5:1.text: Being therefore justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ;

45:5:10.text: For if while we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we will be saved by his life.

45:5:11.text: Not only so, but we also rejoice in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received the reconciliation.

45:5:12.text: Therefore, as sin entered into the world through one man, and death through sin, so death passed to all men because all sinned.

45:5:13.text: For until the law, sin was in the world; but sin is not charged when there is no law.

45:5:14.text: Nevertheless death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over those whose sins weren’t like Adam’s disobedience, who is a foreshadowing of him who was to come.

45:5:15.text: But the free gift isn’t like the trespass. For if by the trespass of the one the many died, much more did the grace of God and the gift by the grace of the one man, Jesus Christ, abound to the many.

45:5:16.text: The gift is not as through one who sinned; for the judgement came by one to condemnation, but the free gift followed many trespasses to justification.

45:5:17.text: For if by the trespass of the one, death reigned through the one; so much more will those who receive the abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness reign in life through the one, Jesus Christ.

45:5:18.text: So then as through one trespass, all men were condemned; even so through one act of righteousness, all men were justified to life.

45:5:19.text: For as through the one man’s disobedience many were made sinners, even so through the obedience of the one, many will be made righteous.

45:5:2.text: through whom we also have our access by faith into this grace in which we stand. We rejoice in hope of the glory of God.

45:5:20.text: The law came in that the trespass might abound; but where sin abounded, grace abounded more exceedingly,

45:5:21.text: that as sin reigned in death, even so grace might reign through righteousness to eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

45:5:3.text: Not only this, but we also rejoice in our sufferings, knowing that suffering produces perseverance;

45:5:4.text: and perseverance, proven character; and proven character, hope;

45:5:5.text: and hope doesn’t disappoint us, because God’s love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit who was given to us.

45:5:6.text: For while we were yet weak, at the right time Christ died for the ungodly.

45:5:7.text: For one will hardly die for a righteous man. Yet perhaps for a good person someone would even dare to die.

45:5:8.text: But God commends his own love towards us, in that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.

45:5:9.text: Much more then, being now justified by his blood, we will be saved from God’s wrath through him.

45:6:1.text: What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?

45:6:10.text: For the death that he died, he died to sin one time; but the life that he lives, he lives to God.

45:6:11.text: Thus consider yourselves also to be dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus our Lord.

45:6:12.text: Therefore don’t let sin reign in your mortal body, that you should obey it in its lusts.

45:6:13.text: Also, do not present your members to sin as instruments of unrighteousness, but present yourselves to God as alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness to God.

45:6:14.text: For sin will not have dominion over you, for you are not under law, but under grace.

45:6:15.text: What then? Shall we sin because we are not under law but under grace? May it never be!

45:6:16.text: Don’t you know that when you present yourselves as servants and obey someone, you are the servants of whomever you obey, whether of sin to death, or of obedience to righteousness?

45:6:17.text: But thanks be to God that, whereas you were bondservants of sin, you became obedient from the heart to that form of teaching to which you were delivered.

45:6:18.text: Being made free from sin, you became bondservants of righteousness.

45:6:19.text: I speak in human terms because of the weakness of your flesh; for as you presented your members as servants to uncleanness and to wickedness upon wickedness, even so now present your members as servants to righteousness for sanctification.

45:6:2.text: May it never be! We who died to sin, how could we live in it any longer?

45:6:20.text: For when you were servants of sin, you were free from righteousness.

45:6:21.text: What fruit then did you have at that time in the things of which you are now ashamed? For the end of those things is death.

45:6:22.text: But now, being made free from sin and having become servants of God, you have your fruit of sanctification and the result of eternal life.

45:6:23.text: For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.

45:6:3.text: Or don’t you know that all of us who were baptised into Christ Jesus were baptised into his death?

45:6:4.text: We were buried therefore with him through baptism into death, that just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, so we also might walk in newness of life.

45:6:5.text: For if we have become united with him in the likeness of his death, we will also be part of his resurrection;

45:6:6.text: knowing this, that our old man was crucified with him, that the body of sin might be done away with, so that we would no longer be in bondage to sin.

45:6:7.text: For he who has died has been freed from sin.

45:6:8.text: But if we died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with him,

45:6:9.text: knowing that Christ, being raised from the dead, dies no more. Death no longer has dominion over him!

45:7:1.text: Or don’t you know, brothers (for I speak to men who know the law), that the law has dominion over a man for as long as he lives?

45:7:10.text: The commandment which was for life, this I found to be for death;

45:7:11.text: for sin, finding occasion through the commandment, deceived me, and through it killed me.

45:7:12.text: Therefore the law indeed is holy, and the commandment holy, righteous, and good.

45:7:13.text: Did then that which is good become death to me? May it never be! But sin, that it might be shown to be sin, was producing death in me through that which is good; that through the commandment sin might become exceedingly sinful.

45:7:14.text: For we know that the law is spiritual, but I am fleshly, sold under sin.

45:7:15.text: For I don’t understand what I am doing. For I don’t practise what I desire to do; but what I hate, that I do.

45:7:16.text: But if what I don’t desire, that I do, I consent to the law that it is good.

45:7:17.text: So now it is no more I that do it, but sin which dwells in me.

45:7:18.text: For I know that in me, that is, in my flesh, dwells no good thing. For desire is present with me, but I don’t find it doing that which is good.

45:7:19.text: For the good which I desire, I don’t do; but the evil which I don’t desire, that I practise.

45:7:2.text: For the woman that has a husband is bound by law to the husband while he lives, but if the husband dies, she is discharged from the law of the husband.

45:7:20.text: But if what I don’t desire, that I do, it is no more I that do it, but sin which dwells in me.

45:7:21.text: I find then the law that, while I desire to do good, evil is present.

45:7:22.text: For I delight in God’s law after the inward person,

45:7:23.text: but I see a different law in my members, warring against the law of my mind, and bringing me into captivity under the law of sin which is in my members.

45:7:24.text: What a wretched man I am! Who will deliver me out of the body of this death?

45:7:25.text: I thank God through Jesus Christ, our Lord! So then with the mind, I myself serve God’s law, but with the flesh, sin’s law.

45:7:3.text: So then if, while the husband lives, she is joined to another man, she would be called an adulteress. But if the husband dies, she is free from the law, so that she is no adulteress, though she is joined to another man.

45:7:4.text: Therefore, my brothers, you also were made dead to the law through the body of Christ, that you would be joined to another, to him who was raised from the dead, that we might produce fruit to God.

45:7:5.text: For when we were in the flesh, the sinful passions which were through the law worked in our members to bring out fruit to death.

45:7:6.text: But now we have been discharged from the law, having died to that in which we were held; so that we serve in newness of the spirit, and not in oldness of the letter.

45:7:7.text: What shall we say then? Is the law sin? May it never be! However, I wouldn’t have known sin except through the law. For I wouldn’t have known coveting unless the law had said, “You shall not covet.”

45:7:8.text: But sin, finding occasion through the commandment, produced in me all kinds of coveting. For apart from the law, sin is dead.

45:7:9.text: I was alive apart from the law once, but when the commandment came, sin revived and I died.

45:8:1.text: There is therefore now no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus, who don’t walk according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit.

45:8:10.text: If Christ is in you, the body is dead because of sin, but the spirit is alive because of righteousness.

45:8:11.text: But if the Spirit of him who raised up Jesus from the dead dwells in you, he who raised up Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through his Spirit who dwells in you.

45:8:12.text: So then, brothers, we are debtors, not to the flesh, to live after the flesh.

45:8:13.text: For if you live after the flesh, you must die; but if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will live.

45:8:14.text: For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are children of God.

45:8:15.text: For you didn’t receive the spirit of bondage again to fear, but you received the Spirit of adoption, by whom we cry, “Abba! Father!”

45:8:16.text: The Spirit himself testifies with our spirit that we are children of God;

45:8:17.text: and if children, then heirs — heirs of God and joint heirs with Christ, if indeed we suffer with him, that we may also be glorified with him.

45:8:18.text: For I consider that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which will be revealed towards us.

45:8:19.text: For the creation waits with eager expectation for the children of God to be revealed.

45:8:2.text: For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus made me free from the law of sin and of death.

45:8:20.text: For the creation was subjected to vanity, not of its own will, but because of him who subjected it, in hope

45:8:21.text: that the creation itself also will be delivered from the bondage of decay into the liberty of the glory of the children of God.

45:8:22.text: For we know that the whole creation groans and travails in pain together until now.

45:8:23.text: Not only so, but ourselves also, who have the first fruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for adoption, the redemption of our body.

45:8:24.text: For we were saved in hope, but hope that is seen is not hope. For who hopes for that which he sees?

45:8:25.text: But if we hope for that which we don’t see, we wait for it with patience.

45:8:26.text: In the same way, the Spirit also helps our weaknesses, for we don’t know how to pray as we ought. But the Spirit himself makes intercession for us with groanings which can’t be uttered.

45:8:27.text: He who searches the hearts knows what is on the Spirit’s mind, because he makes intercession for the saints according to God.

45:8:28.text: We know that all things work together for good for those who love God, for those who are called according to his purpose.

45:8:29.text: For whom he foreknew, he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn amongst many brothers.

45:8:3.text: For what the law couldn’t do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God did, sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and for sin, he condemned sin in the flesh,

45:8:30.text: Whom he predestined, those he also called. Whom he called, those he also justified. Whom he justified, those he also glorified.

45:8:31.text: What then shall we say about these things? If God is for us, who can be against us?

45:8:32.text: He who didn’t spare his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how would he not also with him freely give us all things?

45:8:33.text: Who could bring a charge against God’s chosen ones? It is God who justifies.

45:8:34.text: Who is he who condemns? It is Christ who died, yes rather, who was raised from the dead, who is at the right hand of God, who also makes intercession for us.

45:8:35.text: Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Could oppression, or anguish, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword?

45:8:36.text: Even as it is written, “For your sake we are killed all day long. We were accounted as sheep for the slaughter.”

45:8:37.text: No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him who loved us.

45:8:38.text: For I am persuaded that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers,

45:8:39.text: nor height, nor depth, nor any other created thing will be able to separate us from God’s love which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

45:8:4.text: that the ordinance of the law might be fulfilled in us who don’t walk according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit.

45:8:5.text: For those who live according to the flesh set their minds on the things of the flesh, but those who live according to the Spirit, the things of the Spirit.

45:8:6.text: For the mind of the flesh is death, but the mind of the Spirit is life and peace;

45:8:7.text: because the mind of the flesh is hostile towards God, for it is not subject to God’s law, neither indeed can it be.

45:8:8.text: Those who are in the flesh can’t please God.

45:8:9.text: But you are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if it is so that the Spirit of God dwells in you. But if any man doesn’t have the Spirit of Christ, he is not his.

45:9:1.text: I tell the truth in Christ. I am not lying, my conscience testifying with me in the Holy Spirit

45:9:10.text: Not only so, but Rebekah also conceived by one, by our father Isaac.

45:9:11.text: For being not yet born, neither having done anything good or bad, that the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him who calls,

45:9:12.text: it was said to her, “The elder will serve the younger.”

45:9:13.text: Even as it is written, “Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated.”

45:9:14.text: What shall we say then? Is there unrighteousness with God? May it never be!

45:9:15.text: For he said to Moses, “I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I have compassion.”

45:9:16.text: So then it is not of him who wills, nor of him who runs, but of God who has mercy.

45:9:17.text: For the Scripture says to Pharaoh, “For this very purpose I caused you to be raised up, that I might show in you my power, and that my name might be proclaimed in all the earth.”

45:9:18.text: So then, he has mercy on whom he desires, and he hardens whom he desires.

45:9:19.text: You will say then to me, “Why does he still find fault? For who withstands his will?”

45:9:2.text: that I have great sorrow and unceasing pain in my heart.

45:9:20.text: But indeed, O man, who are you to reply against God? Will the thing formed ask him who formed it, “Why did you make me like this?”

45:9:21.text: Or hasn’t the potter a right over the clay, from the same lump to make one part a vessel for honour, and another for dishonour?

45:9:22.text: What if God, willing to show his wrath and to make his power known, endured with much patience vessels of wrath prepared for destruction,

45:9:23.text: and that he might make known the riches of his glory on vessels of mercy, which he prepared beforehand for glory —

45:9:24.text: us, whom he also called, not from the Jews only, but also from the Gentiles?

45:9:25.text: As he says also in Hosea, “I will call them ‘ my people,’ which were not my people; and her ‘beloved,’ who was not beloved.”

45:9:26.text: “It will be that in the place where it was said to them, ‘ You are not my people,’there they will be called ‘ children of the living God.’ ”

45:9:27.text: Isaiah cries concerning Israel, “If the number of the children of Israel are as the sand of the sea, it is the remnant who will be saved;

45:9:28.text: for he will finish the work and cut it short in righteousness, because the Lord will make a short work upon the earth.”

45:9:29.text: As Isaiah has said before, “Unless the Lord of Armies had left us a seed, we would have become like Sodom, and would have been made like Gomorrah.”

45:9:3.text: For I could wish that I myself were accursed from Christ for my brothers’ sake, my relatives according to the flesh

45:9:30.text: What shall we say then? That the Gentiles, who didn’t follow after righteousness, attained to righteousness, even the righteousness which is of faith;

45:9:31.text: but Israel, following after a law of righteousness, didn’t arrive at the law of righteousness.

45:9:32.text: Why? Because they didn’t seek it by faith, but as it were by works of the law. They stumbled over the stumbling stone,

45:9:33.text: even as it is written, “Behold, I lay in Zion a stumbling stone and a rock of offence; and no one who believes in him will be disappointed.”

45:9:4.text: who are Israelites; whose is the adoption, the glory, the covenants, the giving of the law, the service, and the promises;

45:9:5.text: of whom are the fathers, and from whom is Christ as concerning the flesh, who is over all, God, blessed forever. Amen.

45:9:6.text: But it is not as though the word of God has come to nothing. For they are not all Israel that are of Israel.

45:9:7.text: Neither, because they are Abraham’s offspring, are they all children. But, “your offspring will be accounted as from Isaac.”

45:9:8.text: That is, it is not the children of the flesh who are children of God, but the children of the promise are counted as heirs.

45:9:9.text: For this is a word of promise: “At the appointed time I will come, and Sarah will have a son.”

46:10:1.text: Now I would not have you ignorant, brothers, that our fathers were all under the cloud, and all passed through the sea;

46:10:10.text: Don’t grumble, as some of them also grumbled, and perished by the destroyer.

46:10:11.text: Now all these things happened to them by way of example, and they were written for our admonition, on whom the ends of the ages have come.

46:10:12.text: Therefore let him who thinks he stands be careful that he doesn’t fall.

46:10:13.text: No temptation has taken you except what is common to man. God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted above what you are able, but will with the temptation also make the way of escape, that you may be able to endure it.

46:10:14.text: Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.

46:10:15.text: I speak as to wise men. Judge what I say.

46:10:16.text: The cup of blessing which we bless, isn’t it a sharing of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, isn’t it a sharing of the body of Christ?

46:10:17.text: Because there is one loaf of bread, we, who are many, are one body; for we all partake of the one loaf of bread.

46:10:18.text: Consider Israel according to the flesh. Don’t those who eat the sacrifices participate in the altar?

46:10:19.text: What am I saying then? That a thing sacrificed to idols is anything, or that an idol is anything?

46:10:2.text: and were all baptised into Moses in the cloud and in the sea;

46:10:20.text: But I say that the things which the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to God, and I don’t desire that you would have fellowship with demons.

46:10:21.text: You can’t both drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons. You can’t both partake of the table of the Lord and of the table of demons.

46:10:22.text: Or do we provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than he?

46:10:23.text: “All things are lawful for me,” but not all things are profitable. “All things are lawful for me,” but not all things build up.

46:10:24.text: Let no one seek his own, but each one his neighbour’s good.

46:10:25.text: Whatever is sold in the butcher shop, eat, asking no question for the sake of conscience,

46:10:26.text: for “the earth is the Lord’s, and its fullness.”

46:10:27.text: But if one of those who don’t believe invites you to a meal, and you are inclined to go, eat whatever is set before you, asking no questions for the sake of conscience.

46:10:28.text: But if anyone says to you, “This was offered to idols,” don’t eat it for the sake of the one who told you, and for the sake of conscience. For “the earth is the Lord’s, with all its fullness.”

46:10:29.text: Conscience, I say, not your own, but the other’s conscience. For why is my liberty judged by another conscience?

46:10:3.text: and all ate the same spiritual food;

46:10:30.text: If I partake with thankfulness, why am I denounced for something I give thanks for?

46:10:31.text: Whether therefore you eat or drink, or whatever you do, do all to the glory of God.

46:10:32.text: Give no occasion for stumbling, whether to Jews, to Greeks, or to the assembly of God;

46:10:33.text: even as I also please all men in all things, not seeking my own profit, but the profit of the many, that they may be saved.

46:10:4.text: and all drank the same spiritual drink. For they drank of a spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ.

46:10:5.text: However with most of them, God was not well pleased, for they were overthrown in the wilderness.

46:10:6.text: Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things as they also lusted.

46:10:7.text: Don’t be idolaters, as some of them were. As it is written, “The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.”

46:10:8.text: Let’s not commit sexual immorality, as some of them committed, and in one day twenty-three thousand fell.

46:10:9.text: Let’s not test Christ, as some of them tested, and perished by the serpents.

46:11:1.text: Be imitators of me, even as I also am of Christ.

46:11:10.text: For this cause the woman ought to have authority over her own head, because of the angels.

46:11:11.text: Nevertheless, neither is the woman independent of the man, nor the man independent of the woman, in the Lord.

46:11:12.text: For as woman came from man, so a man also comes through a woman; but all things are from God.

46:11:13.text: Judge for yourselves. Is it appropriate that a woman pray to God unveiled?

46:11:14.text: Doesn’t even nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair, it is a dishonour to him?

46:11:15.text: But if a woman has long hair, it is a glory to her, for her hair is given to her for a covering.

46:11:16.text: But if any man seems to be contentious, we have no such custom, neither do God’s assemblies.

46:11:17.text: But in giving you this command I don’t praise you, because you come together not for the better but for the worse.

46:11:18.text: For first of all, when you come together in the assembly, I hear that divisions exist amongst you, and I partly believe it.

46:11:19.text: For there also must be factions amongst you, that those who are approved may be revealed amongst you.

46:11:2.text: Now I praise you, brothers, that you remember me in all things, and hold firm the traditions, even as I delivered them to you.

46:11:20.text: When therefore you assemble yourselves together, it is not the Lord’s supper that you eat.

46:11:21.text: For in your eating each one takes his own supper first. One is hungry, and another is drunken.

46:11:22.text: What, don’t you have houses to eat and to drink in? Or do you despise God’s assembly and put them to shame who don’t have enough? What shall I tell you? Shall I praise you? In this I don’t praise you.

46:11:23.text: For I received from the Lord that which also I delivered to you, that the Lord Jesus on the night in which he was betrayed took bread.

46:11:24.text: When he had given thanks, he broke it and said, “Take, eat. This is my body, which is broken for you. Do this in memory of me.”

46:11:25.text: In the same way he also took the cup after supper, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood. Do this, as often as you drink, in memory of me.”

46:11:26.text: For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until he comes.

46:11:27.text: Therefore whoever eats this bread or drinks the Lord’s cup in a way unworthy of the Lord will be guilty of the body and the blood of the Lord.

46:11:28.text: But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of the bread and drink of the cup.

46:11:29.text: For he who eats and drinks in an unworthy way eats and drinks judgement to himself if he doesn’t discern the Lord’s body.

46:11:3.text: But I would have you know that the head of every man is Christ, and the head of the woman is man, and the head of Christ is God.

46:11:30.text: For this cause many amongst you are weak and sickly, and not a few sleep.

46:11:31.text: For if we discerned ourselves, we wouldn’t be judged.

46:11:32.text: But when we are judged, we are disciplined by the Lord, that we may not be condemned with the world.

46:11:33.text: Therefore, my brothers, when you come together to eat, wait for one another.

46:11:34.text: But if anyone is hungry, let him eat at home, lest your coming together be for judgement. The rest I will set in order whenever I come.

46:11:4.text: Every man praying or prophesying, having his head covered, dishonours his head.

46:11:5.text: But every woman praying or prophesying with her head uncovered dishonours her head. For it is one and the same thing as if she were shaved.

46:11:6.text: For if a woman is not covered, let her hair also be cut off. But if it is shameful for a woman to have her hair cut off or be shaved, let her be covered.

46:11:7.text: For a man indeed ought not to have his head covered, because he is the image and glory of God, but the woman is the glory of the man.

46:11:8.text: For man is not from woman, but woman from man;

46:11:9.text: for man wasn’t created for the woman, but woman for the man.

46:12:1.text: Now concerning spiritual things, brothers, I don’t want you to be ignorant.

46:12:10.text: and to another workings of miracles, and to another prophecy, and to another discerning of spirits, to another different kinds of languages, and to another the interpretation of languages.

46:12:11.text: But the one and the same Spirit produces all of these, distributing to each one separately as he desires.

46:12:12.text: For as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of the body, being many, are one body; so also is Christ.

46:12:13.text: For in one Spirit we were all baptised into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, whether bond or free; and were all given to drink into one Spirit.

46:12:14.text: For the body is not one member, but many.

46:12:15.text: If the foot would say, “Because I’m not the hand, I’m not part of the body,” it is not therefore not part of the body.

46:12:16.text: If the ear would say, “Because I’m not the eye, I’m not part of the body,” it’s not therefore not part of the body.

46:12:17.text: If the whole body were an eye, where would the hearing be? If the whole were hearing, where would the smelling be?

46:12:18.text: But now God has set the members, each one of them, in the body, just as he desired.

46:12:19.text: If they were all one member, where would the body be?

46:12:2.text: You know that when you were heathen, you were led away to those mute idols, however you might be led.

46:12:20.text: But now they are many members, but one body.

46:12:21.text: The eye can’t tell the hand, “I have no need for you,” or again the head to the feet, “I have no need for you.”

46:12:22.text: No, much rather, those members of the body which seem to be weaker are necessary.

46:12:23.text: Those parts of the body which we think to be less honourable, on those we bestow more abundant honour; and our unpresentable parts have more abundant modesty,

46:12:24.text: while our presentable parts have no such need. But God composed the body together, giving more abundant honour to the inferior part,

46:12:25.text: that there should be no division in the body, but that the members should have the same care for one another.

46:12:26.text: When one member suffers, all the members suffer with it. When one member is honoured, all the members rejoice with it.

46:12:27.text: Now you are the body of Christ, and members individually.

46:12:28.text: God has set some in the assembly: first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then miracle workers, then gifts of healings, helps, governments, and various kinds of languages.

46:12:29.text: Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Are all miracle workers?

46:12:3.text: Therefore I make known to you that no man speaking by God’s Spirit says, “Jesus is accursed.” No one can say, “Jesus is Lord,” but by the Holy Spirit.

46:12:30.text: Do all have gifts of healings? Do all speak with various languages? Do all interpret?

46:12:31.text: But earnestly desire the best gifts. Moreover, I show a most excellent way to you.

46:12:4.text: Now there are various kinds of gifts, but the same Spirit.

46:12:5.text: There are various kinds of service, and the same Lord.

46:12:6.text: There are various kinds of workings, but the same God who works all things in all.

46:12:7.text: But to each one is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the profit of all.

46:12:8.text: For to one is given through the Spirit the word of wisdom, and to another the word of knowledge according to the same Spirit,

46:12:9.text: to another faith by the same Spirit, and to another gifts of healings by the same Spirit,

46:13:1.text: If I speak with the languages of men and of angels, but don’t have love, I have become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal.

46:13:10.text: but when that which is complete has come, then that which is partial will be done away with.

46:13:11.text: When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I felt as a child, I thought as a child. Now that I have become a man, I have put away childish things.

46:13:12.text: For now we see in a mirror, dimly, but then face to face. Now I know in part, but then I will know fully, even as I was also fully known.

46:13:13.text: But now faith, hope, and love remain — these three. The greatest of these is love.

46:13:2.text: If I have the gift of prophecy, and know all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have all faith, so as to remove mountains, but don’t have love, I am nothing.

46:13:3.text: If I give away all my goods to feed the poor, and if I give my body to be burnt, but don’t have love, it profits me nothing.

46:13:4.text: Love is patient and is kind. Love doesn’t envy. Love doesn’t brag, is not proud,

46:13:5.text: doesn’t behave itself inappropriately, doesn’t seek its own way, is not provoked, takes no account of evil;

46:13:6.text: doesn’t rejoice in unrighteousness, but rejoices with the truth;

46:13:7.text: bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, and endures all things.

46:13:8.text: Love never fails. But where there are prophecies, they will be done away with. Where there are various languages, they will cease. Where there is knowledge, it will be done away with.

46:13:9.text: For we know in part and we prophesy in part;

46:14:1.text: Follow after love and earnestly desire spiritual gifts, but especially that you may prophesy.

46:14:10.text: There are, it may be, so many kinds of languages in the world, and none of them is without meaning.

46:14:11.text: If then I don’t know the meaning of the language, I would be to him who speaks a foreigner, and he who speaks would be a foreigner to me.

46:14:12.text: So also you, since you are zealous for spiritual gifts, seek that you may abound to the building up of the assembly.

46:14:13.text: Therefore let him who speaks in another language pray that he may interpret.

46:14:14.text: For if I pray in another language, my spirit prays, but my understanding is unfruitful.

46:14:15.text: What should I do? I will pray with the spirit, and I will pray with the understanding also. I will sing with the spirit, and I will sing with the understanding also.

46:14:16.text: Otherwise, if you bless with the spirit, how will he who fills the place of the unlearned say the “Amen” at your giving of thanks, seeing he doesn’t know what you say?

46:14:17.text: For you most certainly give thanks well, but the other person is not built up.

46:14:18.text: I thank my God, I speak with other languages more than you all.

46:14:19.text: However, in the assembly I would rather speak five words with my understanding, that I might instruct others also, than ten thousand words in another language.

46:14:2.text: For he who speaks in another language speaks not to men, but to God, for no one understands, but in the Spirit he speaks mysteries.

46:14:20.text: Brothers, don’t be children in thoughts, yet in malice be babies, but in thoughts be mature.

46:14:21.text: In the law it is written, “By men of strange languages and by the lips of strangers I will speak to this people. They won’t even listen to me that way, says the Lord.”

46:14:22.text: Therefore other languages are for a sign, not to those who believe, but to the unbelieving; but prophesying is for a sign, not to the unbelieving, but to those who believe.

46:14:23.text: If therefore the whole assembly is assembled together and all speak with other languages, and unlearned or unbelieving people come in, won’t they say that you are crazy?

46:14:24.text: But if all prophesy, and someone unbelieving or unlearned comes in, he is reproved by all, and he is judged by all.

46:14:25.text: And thus the secrets of his heart are revealed. So he will fall down on his face and worship God, declaring that God is amongst you indeed.

46:14:26.text: What is it then, brothers? When you come together, each one of you has a psalm, has a teaching, has a revelation, has another language, or has an interpretation. Let all things be done to build each other up.

46:14:27.text: If any man speaks in another language, let there be two, or at the most three, and in turn; and let one interpret.

46:14:28.text: But if there is no interpreter, let him keep silent in the assembly, and let him speak to himself and to God.

46:14:29.text: Let two or three of the prophets speak, and let the others discern.

46:14:3.text: But he who prophesies speaks to men for their edification, exhortation, and consolation.

46:14:30.text: But if a revelation is made to another sitting by, let the first keep silent.

46:14:31.text: For you all can prophesy one by one, that all may learn and all may be exhorted.

46:14:32.text: The spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets,

46:14:33.text: for God is not a God of confusion but of peace, as in all the assemblies of the saints.

46:14:34.text: Let the wives be quiet in the assemblies, for it has not been permitted for them to be talking except in submission, as the law also says,

46:14:35.text: if they desire to learn anything. “Let them ask their own husbands at home, for it is shameful for a wife to be talking in the assembly.”

46:14:36.text: What!? Was it from you that the word of God went out? Or did it come to you alone?

46:14:37.text: If any man thinks himself to be a prophet or spiritual, let him recognise the things which I write to you, that they are the commandment of the Lord.

46:14:38.text: But if anyone is ignorant, let him be ignorant.

46:14:39.text: Therefore, brothers, desire earnestly to prophesy, and don’t forbid speaking with other languages.

46:14:4.text: He who speaks in another language edifies himself, but he who prophesies edifies the assembly.

46:14:40.text: Let all things be done decently and in order.

46:14:5.text: Now I desire to have you all speak with other languages, but even more that you would prophesy. For he is greater who prophesies than he who speaks with other languages, unless he interprets, that the assembly may be built up.

46:14:6.text: But now, brothers, if I come to you speaking with other languages, what would I profit you unless I speak to you either by way of revelation, or of knowledge, or of prophesying, or of teaching?

46:14:7.text: Even lifeless things that make a sound, whether pipe or harp, if they didn’t give a distinction in the sounds, how would it be known what is piped or harped?

46:14:8.text: For if the trumpet gave an uncertain sound, who would prepare himself for war?

46:14:9.text: So also you, unless you uttered by the tongue words easy to understand, how would it be known what is spoken? For you would be speaking into the air.

46:15:1.text: Now I declare to you, brothers, the Good News which I preached to you, which also you received, in which you also stand,

46:15:10.text: But by the grace of God I am what I am. His grace which was given to me was not futile, but I worked more than all of them; yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me.

46:15:11.text: Whether then it is I or they, so we preach, and so you believed.

46:15:12.text: Now if Christ is preached, that he has been raised from the dead, how do some amongst you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?

46:15:13.text: But if there is no resurrection of the dead, neither has Christ been raised.

46:15:14.text: If Christ has not been raised, then our preaching is in vain and your faith also is in vain.

46:15:15.text: Yes, we are also found false witnesses of God, because we testified about God that he raised up Christ, whom he didn’t raise up if it is true that the dead are not raised.

46:15:16.text: For if the dead aren’t raised, neither has Christ been raised.

46:15:17.text: If Christ has not been raised, your faith is vain; you are still in your sins.

46:15:18.text: Then they also who are fallen asleep in Christ have perished.

46:15:19.text: If we have only hoped in Christ in this life, we are of all men most pitiable.

46:15:2.text: by which also you are saved, if you hold firmly the word which I preached to you — unless you believed in vain.

46:15:20.text: But now Christ has been raised from the dead. He became the first fruit of those who are asleep.

46:15:21.text: For since death came by man, the resurrection of the dead also came by man.

46:15:22.text: For as in Adam all die, so also in Christ all will be made alive.

46:15:23.text: But each in his own order: Christ the first fruits, then those who are Christ’s at his coming.

46:15:24.text: Then the end comes, when he will deliver up the Kingdom to God the Father, when he will have abolished all rule and all authority and power.

46:15:25.text: For he must reign until he has put all his enemies under his feet.

46:15:26.text: The last enemy that will be abolished is death.

46:15:27.text: For, “He put all things in subjection under his feet.” But when he says, “All things are put in subjection”, it is evident that he is excepted who subjected all things to him.

46:15:28.text: When all things have been subjected to him, then the Son will also himself be subjected to him who subjected all things to him, that God may be all in all.

46:15:29.text: Or else what will they do who are baptised for the dead? If the dead aren’t raised at all, why then are they baptised for the dead?

46:15:3.text: For I delivered to you first of all that which I also received: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures,

46:15:30.text: Why do we also stand in jeopardy every hour?

46:15:31.text: I affirm, by the boasting in you which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, I die daily.

46:15:32.text: If I fought with animals at Ephesus for human purposes, what does it profit me? If the dead are not raised, then “let’s eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.”

46:15:33.text: Don’t be deceived! “Evil companionships corrupt good morals.”

46:15:34.text: Wake up righteously and don’t sin, for some have no knowledge of God. I say this to your shame.

46:15:35.text: But someone will say, “How are the dead raised?” and, “With what kind of body do they come?”

46:15:36.text: You foolish one, that which you yourself sow is not made alive unless it dies.

46:15:37.text: That which you sow, you don’t sow the body that will be, but a bare grain, maybe of wheat, or of some other kind.

46:15:38.text: But God gives it a body even as it pleased him, and to each seed a body of its own.

46:15:39.text: All flesh is not the same flesh, but there is one flesh of men, another flesh of animals, another of fish, and another of birds.

46:15:4.text: that he was buried, that he was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures,

46:15:40.text: There are also celestial bodies and terrestrial bodies; but the glory of the celestial differs from that of the terrestrial.

46:15:41.text: There is one glory of the sun, another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars; for one star differs from another star in glory.

46:15:42.text: So also is the resurrection of the dead. The body is sown perishable; it is raised imperishable.

46:15:43.text: It is sown in dishonour; it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness; it is raised in power.

46:15:44.text: It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body. There is a natural body and there is also a spiritual body.

46:15:45.text: So also it is written, “The first man Adam became a living soul.” The last Adam became a life-giving spirit.

46:15:46.text: However, that which is spiritual isn’t first, but that which is natural, then that which is spiritual.

46:15:47.text: The first man is of the earth, made of dust. The second man is the Lord from heaven.

46:15:48.text: As is the one made of dust, such are those who are also made of dust; and as is the heavenly, such are they also that are heavenly.

46:15:49.text: As we have borne the image of those made of dust, let’s also bear the image of the heavenly.

46:15:5.text: and that he appeared to Cephas, then to the twelve.

46:15:50.text: Now I say this, brothers, that flesh and blood can’t inherit God’s Kingdom; neither does the perishable inherit imperishable.

46:15:51.text: Behold, I tell you a mystery. We will not all sleep, but we will all be changed,

46:15:52.text: in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound and the dead will be raised incorruptible, and we will be changed.

46:15:53.text: For this perishable body must become imperishable, and this mortal must put on immortality.

46:15:54.text: But when this perishable body will have become imperishable, and this mortal will have put on immortality, then what is written will happen: “Death is swallowed up in victory.”

46:15:55.text: “Death, where is your sting? Hades, where is your victory?”

46:15:56.text: The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.

46:15:57.text: But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.

46:15:58.text: Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the Lord’s work, because you know that your labour is not in vain in the Lord.

46:15:6.text: Then he appeared to over five hundred brothers at once, most of whom remain until now, but some have also fallen asleep.

46:15:7.text: Then he appeared to James, then to all the apostles,

46:15:8.text: and last of all, as to the child born at the wrong time, he appeared to me also.

46:15:9.text: For I am the least of the apostles, who is not worthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the assembly of God.

46:16:1.text: Now concerning the collection for the saints: as I commanded the assemblies of Galatia, you do likewise.

46:16:10.text: Now if Timothy comes, see that he is with you without fear, for he does the work of the Lord, as I also do.

46:16:11.text: Therefore let no one despise him. But set him forward on his journey in peace, that he may come to me; for I expect him with the brothers.

46:16:12.text: Now concerning Apollos the brother, I strongly urged him to come to you with the brothers, but it was not at all his desire to come now; but he will come when he has an opportunity.

46:16:13.text: Watch! Stand firm in the faith! Be courageous! Be strong!

46:16:14.text: Let all that you do be done in love.

46:16:15.text: Now I beg you, brothers — you know the house of Stephanas, that it is the first fruits of Achaia, and that they have set themselves to serve the saints —

46:16:16.text: that you also be in subjection to such, and to everyone who helps in the work and labours.

46:16:17.text: I rejoice at the coming of Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus; for that which was lacking on your part, they supplied.

46:16:18.text: For they refreshed my spirit and yours. Therefore acknowledge those who are like that.

46:16:19.text: The assemblies of Asia greet you. Aquila and Priscilla greet you warmly in the Lord, together with the assembly that is in their house.

46:16:2.text: On the first day of every week, let each one of you save as he may prosper, that no collections are made when I come.

46:16:20.text: All the brothers greet you. Greet one another with a holy kiss.

46:16:21.text: This greeting is by me, Paul, with my own hand.

46:16:22.text: If any man doesn’t love the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be cursed. Come, Lord!

46:16:23.text: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with you.

46:16:24.text: My love to all of you in Christ Jesus. Amen.

46:16:3.text: When I arrive, I will send whoever you approve with letters to carry your gracious gift to Jerusalem.

46:16:4.text: If it is appropriate for me to go also, they will go with me.

46:16:5.text: I will come to you when I have passed through Macedonia, for I am passing through Macedonia.

46:16:6.text: But with you it may be that I will stay with you, or even winter with you, that you may send me on my journey wherever I go.

46:16:7.text: For I do not wish to see you now in passing, but I hope to stay a while with you, if the Lord permits.

46:16:8.text: But I will stay at Ephesus until Pentecost,

46:16:9.text: for a great and effective door has opened to me, and there are many adversaries.

46:1:1.text: Paul, called to be an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, and our brother Sosthenes,

46:1:10.text: Now I beg you, brothers, through the name of our Lord, Jesus Christ, that you all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions amongst you, but that you be perfected together in the same mind and in the same judgement.

46:1:11.text: For it has been reported to me concerning you, my brothers, by those who are from Chloe’s household, that there are contentions amongst you.

46:1:12.text: Now I mean this, that each one of you says, “I follow Paul,” “I follow Apollos,” “I follow Cephas,” and, “I follow Christ.”

46:1:13.text: Is Christ divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptised into the name of Paul?

46:1:14.text: I thank God that I baptised none of you except Crispus and Gaius,

46:1:15.text: so that no one should say that I had baptised you into my own name.

46:1:16.text: (I also baptised the household of Stephanas; besides them, I don’t know whether I baptised any other.)

46:1:17.text: For Christ sent me not to baptise, but to preach the Good News — not in wisdom of words, so that the cross of Christ wouldn’t be made void.

46:1:18.text: For the word of the cross is foolishness to those who are dying, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.

46:1:19.text: For it is written, “I will destroy the wisdom of the wise. I will bring the discernment of the discerning to nothing.”

46:1:2.text: to the assembly of God which is at Corinth — those who are sanctified in Christ Jesus, called saints, with all who call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ in every place, both theirs and ours:

46:1:20.text: Where is the wise? Where is the scribe? Where is the debater of this age? Hasn’t God made foolish the wisdom of this world?

46:1:21.text: For seeing that in the wisdom of God, the world through its wisdom didn’t know God, it was God’s good pleasure through the foolishness of the preaching to save those who believe.

46:1:22.text: For Jews ask for signs, Greeks seek after wisdom,

46:1:23.text: but we preach Christ crucified, a stumbling block to Jews and foolishness to Greeks,

46:1:24.text: but to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God;

46:1:25.text: because the foolishness of God is wiser than men, and the weakness of God is stronger than men.

46:1:26.text: For you see your calling, brothers, that not many are wise according to the flesh, not many mighty, and not many noble;

46:1:27.text: but God chose the foolish things of the world that he might put to shame those who are wise. God chose the weak things of the world that he might put to shame the things that are strong.

46:1:28.text: God chose the lowly things of the world, and the things that are despised, and the things that don’t exist, that he might bring to nothing the things that exist,

46:1:29.text: that no flesh should boast before God.

46:1:3.text: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

46:1:30.text: Because of him, you are in Christ Jesus, who was made to us wisdom from God, and righteousness and sanctification, and redemption,

46:1:31.text: that, as it is written, “He who boasts, let him boast in the Lord.”

46:1:4.text: I always thank my God concerning you for the grace of God which was given you in Christ Jesus,

46:1:5.text: that in everything you were enriched in him, in all speech and all knowledge —

46:1:6.text: even as the testimony of Christ was confirmed in you —

46:1:7.text: so that you come behind in no gift, waiting for the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ,

46:1:8.text: who will also confirm you until the end, blameless in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.

46:1:9.text: God is faithful, through whom you were called into the fellowship of his Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.

46:2:1.text: When I came to you, brothers, I didn’t come with excellence of speech or of wisdom, proclaiming to you the testimony of God.

46:2:10.text: But to us, God revealed them through the Spirit. For the Spirit searches all things, yes, the deep things of God.

46:2:11.text: For who amongst men knows the things of a man except the spirit of the man which is in him? Even so, no one knows the things of God except God’s Spirit.

46:2:12.text: But we received not the spirit of the world, but the Spirit which is from God, that we might know the things that were freely given to us by God.

46:2:13.text: We also speak these things, not in words which man’s wisdom teaches but which the Holy Spirit teaches, comparing spiritual things with spiritual things.

46:2:14.text: Now the natural man doesn’t receive the things of God’s Spirit, for they are foolishness to him; and he can’t know them, because they are spiritually discerned.

46:2:15.text: But he who is spiritual discerns all things, and he himself is to be judged by no one.

46:2:16.text: “For who has known the mind of the Lord that he should instruct him?” But we have Christ’s mind.

46:2:2.text: For I determined not to know anything amongst you except Jesus Christ and him crucified.

46:2:3.text: I was with you in weakness, in fear, and in much trembling.

46:2:4.text: My speech and my preaching were not in persuasive words of human wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power,

46:2:5.text: that your faith wouldn’t stand in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God.

46:2:6.text: We speak wisdom, however, amongst those who are full grown, yet a wisdom not of this world nor of the rulers of this world who are coming to nothing.

46:2:7.text: But we speak God’s wisdom in a mystery, the wisdom that has been hidden, which God foreordained before the worlds for our glory,

46:2:8.text: which none of the rulers of this world has known. For had they known it, they wouldn’t have crucified the Lord of glory.

46:2:9.text: But as it is written, “Things which an eye didn’t see, and an ear didn’t hear, which didn’t enter into the heart of man, these God has prepared for those who love him.”

46:3:1.text: Brothers, I couldn’t speak to you as to spiritual, but as to fleshly, as to babies in Christ.

46:3:10.text: According to the grace of God which was given to me, as a wise master builder I laid a foundation, and another builds on it. But let each man be careful how he builds on it.

46:3:11.text: For no one can lay any other foundation than that which has been laid, which is Jesus Christ.

46:3:12.text: But if anyone builds on the foundation with gold, silver, costly stones, wood, hay, or straw,

46:3:13.text: each man’s work will be revealed. For the Day will declare it, because it is revealed in fire; and the fire itself will test what sort of work each man’s work is.

46:3:14.text: If any man’s work remains which he built on it, he will receive a reward.

46:3:15.text: If any man’s work is burnt, he will suffer loss, but he himself will be saved, but as through fire.

46:3:16.text: Don’t you know that you are God’s temple and that God’s Spirit lives in you?

46:3:17.text: If anyone destroys God’s temple, God will destroy him; for God’s temple is holy, which you are.

46:3:18.text: Let no one deceive himself. If anyone thinks that he is wise amongst you in this world, let him become a fool that he may become wise.

46:3:19.text: For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God. For it is written, “He has taken the wise in their craftiness.”

46:3:2.text: I fed you with milk, not with solid food, for you weren’t yet ready. Indeed, you aren’t ready even now,

46:3:20.text: And again, “The Lord knows the reasoning of the wise, that it is worthless.”

46:3:21.text: Therefore let no one boast in men. For all things are yours,

46:3:22.text: whether Paul, or Apollos, or Cephas, or the world, or life, or death, or things present, or things to come. All are yours,

46:3:23.text: and you are Christ’s, and Christ is God’s.

46:3:3.text: for you are still fleshly. For insofar as there is jealousy, strife, and factions amongst you, aren’t you fleshly, and don’t you walk in the ways of men?

46:3:4.text: For when one says, “I follow Paul,” and another, “I follow Apollos,” aren’t you fleshly?

46:3:5.text: Who then is Apollos, and who is Paul, but servants through whom you believed, and each as the Lord gave to him?

46:3:6.text: I planted. Apollos watered. But God gave the increase.

46:3:7.text: So then neither he who plants is anything, nor he who waters, but God who gives the increase.

46:3:8.text: Now he who plants and he who waters are the same, but each will receive his own reward according to his own labour.

46:3:9.text: For we are God’s fellow workers. You are God’s farming, God’s building.

46:4:1.text: So let a man think of us as Christ’s servants and stewards of God’s mysteries.

46:4:10.text: We are fools for Christ’s sake, but you are wise in Christ. We are weak, but you are strong. You have honour, but we have dishonour.

46:4:11.text: Even to this present hour we hunger, thirst, are naked, are beaten, and have no certain dwelling place.

46:4:12.text: We toil, working with our own hands. When people curse us, we bless. Being persecuted, we endure.

46:4:13.text: Being defamed, we entreat. We are made as the filth of the world, the dirt wiped off by all, even until now.

46:4:14.text: I don’t write these things to shame you, but to admonish you as my beloved children.

46:4:15.text: For though you have ten thousand tutors in Christ, you don’t have many fathers. For in Christ Jesus, I became your father through the Good News.

46:4:16.text: I beg you therefore, be imitators of me.

46:4:17.text: Because of this I have sent Timothy to you, who is my beloved and faithful child in the Lord, who will remind you of my ways which are in Christ, even as I teach everywhere in every assembly.

46:4:18.text: Now some are puffed up, as though I were not coming to you.

46:4:19.text: But I will come to you shortly, if the Lord is willing. And I will know, not the word of those who are puffed up, but the power.

46:4:2.text: Here, moreover, it is required of stewards that they be found faithful.
