58:8:13.text: In that he says, “A new covenant”, he has made the first obsolete. But that which is becoming obsolete and grows aged is near to vanishing away.

58:8:2.text: a servant of the sanctuary and of the true tabernacle which the Lord pitched, not man.

58:8:3.text: For every high priest is appointed to offer both gifts and sacrifices. Therefore it is necessary that this high priest also have something to offer.

58:8:4.text: For if he were on earth, he would not be a priest at all, seeing there are priests who offer the gifts according to the law,

58:8:5.text: who serve a copy and shadow of the heavenly things, even as Moses was warned by God when he was about to make the tabernacle, for he said, “See, you shall make everything according to the pattern that was shown to you on the mountain.”

58:8:6.text: But now he has obtained a more excellent ministry, by as much as he is also the mediator of a better covenant, which on better promises has been given as law.

58:8:7.text: For if that first covenant had been faultless, then no place would have been sought for a second.

58:8:8.text: For finding fault with them, he said, “Behold, the days are coming”, says the Lord, “that I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah;

58:8:9.text: not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day that I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; for they didn’t continue in my covenant, and I disregarded them,” says the Lord.

58:9:1.text: Now indeed even the first covenant had ordinances of divine service and an earthly sanctuary.

58:9:10.text: being only (with foods and drinks and various washings) fleshly ordinances, imposed until a time of reformation.

58:9:11.text: But Christ having come as a high priest of the coming good things, through the greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this creation,

58:9:12.text: nor yet through the blood of goats and calves, but through his own blood, entered in once for all into the Holy Place, having obtained eternal redemption.

58:9:13.text: For if the blood of goats and bulls, and the ashes of a heifer sprinkling those who have been defiled, sanctify to the cleanness of the flesh,

58:9:14.text: how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without defect to God, cleanse your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?

58:9:15.text: For this reason he is the mediator of a new covenant, since a death has occurred for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first covenant, that those who have been called may receive the promise of the eternal inheritance.

58:9:16.text: For where a last will and testament is, there must of necessity be the death of him who made it.

58:9:17.text: For a will is in force where there has been death, for it is never in force while he who made it lives.

58:9:18.text: Therefore even the first covenant has not been dedicated without blood.

58:9:19.text: For when every commandment had been spoken by Moses to all the people according to the law, he took the blood of the calves and the goats, with water and scarlet wool and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book itself and all the people,

58:9:2.text: For a tabernacle was prepared. In the first part were the lamp stand, the table, and the show bread, which is called the Holy Place.

58:9:20.text: saying, “This is the blood of the covenant which God has commanded you.”

58:9:21.text: He sprinkled the tabernacle and all the vessels of the ministry in the same way with the blood.

58:9:22.text: According to the law, nearly everything is cleansed with blood, and apart from shedding of blood there is no remission.

58:9:23.text: It was necessary therefore that the copies of the things in the heavens should be cleansed with these, but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.

58:9:24.text: For Christ hasn’t entered into holy places made with hands, which are representations of the true, but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us;

58:9:25.text: nor yet that he should offer himself often, as the high priest enters into the holy place year by year with blood not his own,

58:9:26.text: or else he must have suffered often since the foundation of the world. But now once at the end of the ages, he has been revealed to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself.

58:9:27.text: Inasmuch as it is appointed for men to die once, and after this, judgement,

58:9:28.text: so Christ also, having been offered once to bear the sins of many, will appear a second time, not to deal with sin, but to save those who are eagerly waiting for him.

58:9:3.text: After the second veil was the tabernacle which is called the Holy of Holies,

58:9:4.text: having a golden altar of incense and the ark of the covenant overlaid on all sides with gold, in which was a golden pot holding the manna, Aaron’s rod that budded, and the tablets of the covenant;

58:9:5.text: and above it cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat, of which things we can’t speak now in detail.

58:9:6.text: Now these things having been thus prepared, the priests go in continually into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the services,

58:9:7.text: but into the second the high priest alone, once in the year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the errors of the people.

58:9:8.text: The Holy Spirit is indicating this, that the way into the Holy Place wasn’t yet revealed while the first tabernacle was still standing.

58:9:9.text: This is a symbol of the present age, where gifts and sacrifices are offered that are incapable, concerning the conscience, of making the worshipper perfect,

59:1:1.text: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are in the Dispersion: Greetings.

59:1:10.text: and the rich, in that he is made humble, because like the flower in the grass, he will pass away.

59:1:11.text: For the sun arises with the scorching wind and withers the grass; and the flower in it falls, and the beauty of its appearance perishes. So the rich man will also fade away in his pursuits.

59:1:12.text: Blessed is a person who endures temptation, for when he has been approved, he will receive the crown of life which the Lord promised to those who love him.

59:1:13.text: Let no man say when he is tempted, “I am tempted by God,” for God can’t be tempted by evil, and he himself tempts no one.

59:1:14.text: But each one is tempted when he is drawn away by his own lust and enticed.

59:1:15.text: Then the lust, when it has conceived, bears sin. The sin, when it is full grown, produces death.

59:1:16.text: Don’t be deceived, my beloved brothers.

59:1:17.text: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom can be no variation nor turning shadow.

59:1:18.text: Of his own will he gave birth to us by the word of truth, that we should be a kind of first fruits of his creatures.

59:1:19.text: So, then, my beloved brothers, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger;

59:1:2.text: Count it all joy, my brothers, when you fall into various temptations,

59:1:20.text: for the anger of man doesn’t produce the righteousness of God.

59:1:21.text: Therefore, putting away all filthiness and overflowing of wickedness, receive with humility the implanted word, which is able to save your souls.

59:1:22.text: But be doers of the word, and not only hearers, deluding your own selves.

59:1:23.text: For if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer, he is like a man looking at his natural face in a mirror;

59:1:24.text: for he sees himself, and goes away, and immediately forgets what kind of man he was.

59:1:25.text: But he who looks into the perfect law of freedom and continues, not being a hearer who forgets but a doer of the work, this man will be blessed in what he does.

59:1:26.text: If anyone amongst you thinks himself to be religious while he doesn’t bridle his tongue, but deceives his heart, this man’s religion is worthless.

59:1:27.text: Pure religion and undefiled before our God and Father is this: to visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself unstained by the world.

59:1:3.text: knowing that the testing of your faith produces endurance.

59:1:4.text: Let endurance have its perfect work, that you may be perfect and complete, lacking in nothing.

59:1:5.text: But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all liberally and without reproach, and it will be given to him.

59:1:6.text: But let him ask in faith, without any doubting, for he who doubts is like a wave of the sea, driven by the wind and tossed.

59:1:7.text: For that man shouldn’t think that he will receive anything from the Lord.

59:1:8.text: He is a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways.

59:1:9.text: Let the brother in humble circumstances glory in his high position;

59:2:1.text: My brothers, don’t hold the faith of our glorious Lord Jesus Christ with partiality.

59:2:10.text: For whoever keeps the whole law, and yet stumbles in one point, he has become guilty of all.

59:2:11.text: For he who said, “Do not commit adultery,” also said, “Do not commit murder.” Now if you do not commit adultery but do murder, you have become a transgressor of the law.

59:2:12.text: So speak and so do as men who are to be judged by the law of freedom.

59:2:13.text: For judgement is without mercy to him who has shown no mercy. Mercy triumphs over judgement.

59:2:14.text: What good is it, my brothers, if a man says he has faith, but has no works? Can faith save him?

59:2:15.text: And if a brother or sister is naked and in lack of daily food,

59:2:16.text: and one of you tells them, “Go in peace. Be warmed and filled;” yet you didn’t give them the things the body needs, what good is it?

59:2:17.text: Even so faith, if it has no works, is dead in itself.

59:2:18.text: Yes, a man will say, “You have faith, and I have works.” Show me your faith without works, and I will show you my faith by my works.

59:2:19.text: You believe that God is one. You do well. The demons also believe — and shudder.

59:2:2.text: For if a man with a gold ring, in fine clothing, comes into your synagogue, and a poor man in filthy clothing also comes in,

59:2:20.text: But do you want to know, vain man, that faith apart from works is dead?

59:2:21.text: Wasn’t Abraham our father justified by works, in that he offered up Isaac his son on the altar?

59:2:22.text: You see that faith worked with his works, and by works faith was perfected.

59:2:23.text: So the Scripture was fulfilled which says, “Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him as righteousness,” and he was called the friend of God.

59:2:24.text: You see then that by works a man is justified, and not only by faith.

59:2:25.text: In the same way, wasn’t Rahab the prostitute also justified by works when she received the messengers and sent them out another way?

59:2:26.text: For as the body apart from the spirit is dead, even so faith apart from works is dead.

59:2:3.text: and you pay special attention to him who wears the fine clothing and say, “Sit here in a good place;” and you tell the poor man, “Stand there,” or “Sit by my footstool”

59:2:4.text: haven’t you shown partiality amongst yourselves, and become judges with evil thoughts?

59:2:5.text: Listen, my beloved brothers. Didn’t God choose those who are poor in this world to be rich in faith and heirs of the Kingdom which he promised to those who love him?

59:2:6.text: But you have dishonoured the poor man. Don’t the rich oppress you and personally drag you before the courts?

59:2:7.text: Don’t they blaspheme the honourable name by which you are called?

59:2:8.text: However, if you fulfil the royal law according to the Scripture, “You shall love your neighbour as yourself,” you do well.

59:2:9.text: But if you show partiality, you commit sin, being convicted by the law as transgressors.

59:3:1.text: Let not many of you be teachers, my brothers, knowing that we will receive heavier judgement.

59:3:10.text: Out of the same mouth comes blessing and cursing. My brothers, these things ought not to be so.

59:3:11.text: Does a spring send out from the same opening fresh and bitter water?

59:3:12.text: Can a fig tree, my brothers, yield olives, or a vine figs? Thus no spring yields both salt water and fresh water.

59:3:13.text: Who is wise and understanding amongst you? Let him show by his good conduct that his deeds are done in gentleness of wisdom.

59:3:14.text: But if you have bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your heart, don’t boast and don’t lie against the truth.

59:3:15.text: This wisdom is not that which comes down from above, but is earthly, sensual, and demonic.

59:3:16.text: For where jealousy and selfish ambition are, there is confusion and every evil deed.

59:3:17.text: But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceful, gentle, reasonable, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy.

59:3:18.text: Now the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace.

59:3:2.text: For we all stumble in many things. Anyone who doesn’t stumble in word is a perfect person, able to bridle the whole body also.

59:3:3.text: Indeed, we put bits into the horses’ mouths so that they may obey us, and we guide their whole body.

59:3:4.text: Behold, the ships also, though they are so big and are driven by fierce winds, are yet guided by a very small rudder, wherever the pilot desires.

59:3:5.text: So the tongue is also a little member, and boasts great things. See how a small fire can spread to a large forest!

59:3:6.text: And the tongue is a fire. The world of iniquity amongst our members is the tongue, which defiles the whole body, and sets on fire the course of nature, and is set on fire by Gehenna.

59:3:7.text: For every kind of animal, bird, creeping thing, and sea creature is tamed, and has been tamed by mankind;

59:3:8.text: but nobody can tame the tongue. It is a restless evil, full of deadly poison.

59:3:9.text: With it we bless our God and Father, and with it we curse men who are made in the image of God.

59:4:1.text: Where do wars and fightings amongst you come from? Don’t they come from your pleasures that war in your members?

59:4:10.text: Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he will exalt you.

59:4:11.text: Don’t speak against one another, brothers. He who speaks against a brother and judges his brother, speaks against the law and judges the law. But if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law but a judge.

59:4:12.text: Only one is the lawgiver, who is able to save and to destroy. But who are you to judge another?

59:4:13.text: Come now, you who say, “Today or tomorrow let’s go into this city and spend a year there, trade, and make a profit.”

59:4:14.text: Yet you don’t know what your life will be like tomorrow. For what is your life? For you are a vapour that appears for a little time and then vanishes away.

59:4:15.text: For you ought to say, “If the Lord wills, we will both live, and do this or that.”

59:4:16.text: But now you glory in your boasting. All such boasting is evil.

59:4:17.text: To him therefore who knows to do good and doesn’t do it, to him it is sin.

59:4:2.text: You lust, and don’t have. You murder and covet, and can’t obtain. You fight and make war. You don’t have, because you don’t ask.

59:4:3.text: You ask, and don’t receive, because you ask with wrong motives, so that you may spend it on your pleasures.

59:4:4.text: You adulterers and adulteresses, don’t you know that friendship with the world is hostility towards God? Whoever therefore wants to be a friend of the world makes himself an enemy of God.

59:4:5.text: Or do you think that the Scripture says in vain, “The Spirit who lives in us yearns jealously”?

59:4:6.text: But he gives more grace. Therefore it says, “God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”

59:4:7.text: Be subject therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.

59:4:8.text: Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners. Purify your hearts, you double-minded.

59:4:9.text: Lament, mourn, and weep. Let your laughter be turned to mourning and your joy to gloom.

59:5:1.text: Come now, you rich, weep and howl for your miseries that are coming on you.

59:5:10.text: Take, brothers, for an example of suffering and of perseverance, the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.

59:5:11.text: Behold, we call them blessed who endured. You have heard of the perseverance of Job and have seen the Lord in the outcome, and how the Lord is full of compassion and mercy.

59:5:12.text: But above all things, my brothers, don’t swear — not by heaven, or by the earth, or by any other oath; but let your “yes” be “yes”, and your “no”, “no”, so that you don’t fall into hypocrisy.

59:5:13.text: Is any amongst you suffering? Let him pray. Is any cheerful? Let him sing praises.

59:5:14.text: Is any amongst you sick? Let him call for the elders of the assembly, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord;

59:5:15.text: and the prayer of faith will heal him who is sick, and the Lord will raise him up. If he has committed sins, he will be forgiven.

59:5:16.text: Confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, that you may be healed. The insistent prayer of a righteous person is powerfully effective.

59:5:17.text: Elijah was a man with a nature like ours, and he prayed earnestly that it might not rain, and it didn’t rain on the earth for three years and six months.

59:5:18.text: He prayed again, and the sky gave rain, and the earth produced its fruit.

59:5:19.text: Brothers, if any amongst you wanders from the truth and someone turns him back,

59:5:2.text: Your riches are corrupted and your garments are moth-eaten.

59:5:20.text: let him know that he who turns a sinner from the error of his way will save a soul from death and will cover a multitude of sins.

59:5:3.text: Your gold and your silver are corroded, and their corrosion will be for a testimony against you and will eat your flesh like fire. You have laid up your treasure in the last days.

59:5:4.text: Behold, the wages of the labourers who mowed your fields, which you have kept back by fraud, cry out; and the cries of those who reaped have entered into the ears of the Lord of Armies.

59:5:5.text: You have lived in luxury on the earth, and taken your pleasure. You have nourished your hearts as in a day of slaughter.

59:5:6.text: You have condemned and you have murdered the righteous one. He doesn’t resist you.

59:5:7.text: Be patient therefore, brothers, until the coming of the Lord. Behold, the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth, being patient over it, until it receives the early and late rain.

59:5:8.text: You also be patient. Establish your hearts, for the coming of the Lord is at hand.

59:5:9.text: Don’t grumble, brothers, against one another, so that you won’t be judged. Behold, the judge stands at the door.

60:1:1.text: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the chosen ones who are living as foreigners in the Dispersion in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia,

60:1:10.text: Concerning this salvation, the prophets sought and searched diligently. They prophesied of the grace that would come to you,

60:1:11.text: searching for who or what kind of time the Spirit of Christ which was in them pointed to when he predicted the sufferings of Christ and the glories that would follow them.

60:1:12.text: To them it was revealed that they served not themselves, but you, in these things, which now have been announced to you through those who preached the Good News to you by the Holy Spirit sent out from heaven; which things angels desire to look into.

60:1:13.text: Therefore prepare your minds for action. Be sober, and set your hope fully on the grace that will be brought to you at the revelation of Jesus Christ —

60:1:14.text: as children of obedience, not conforming yourselves according to your former lusts as in your ignorance,

60:1:15.text: but just as he who called you is holy, you yourselves also be holy in all of your behaviour,

60:1:16.text: because it is written, “You shall be holy, for I am holy.”

60:1:17.text: If you call on him as Father, who without respect of persons judges according to each man’s work, pass the time of your living as foreigners here in reverent fear,

60:1:18.text: knowing that you were redeemed, not with corruptible things like silver or gold, from the useless way of life handed down from your fathers,

60:1:19.text: but with precious blood, as of a lamb without blemish or spot, the blood of Christ,

60:1:2.text: according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, in sanctification of the Spirit, that you may obey Jesus Christ and be sprinkled with his blood: Grace to you and peace be multiplied.

60:1:20.text: who was foreknown indeed before the foundation of the world, but was revealed in this last age for your sake,

60:1:21.text: who through him are believers in God, who raised him from the dead and gave him glory, so that your faith and hope might be in God.

60:1:22.text: Seeing you have purified your souls in your obedience to the truth through the Spirit in sincere brotherly affection, love one another from the heart fervently,

60:1:23.text: having been born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, through the word of God, which lives and remains forever.

60:1:24.text: For, “All flesh is like grass, and all of man’s glory like the flower in the grass. The grass withers, and its flower falls;

60:1:25.text: but the Lord’s word endures forever.” This is the word of Good News which was preached to you.

60:1:3.text: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to his great mercy caused us to be born again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,

60:1:4.text: to an incorruptible and undefiled inheritance that doesn’t fade away, reserved in Heaven for you,

60:1:5.text: who by the power of God are guarded through faith for a salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.

60:1:6.text: In this you greatly rejoice, though now for a little while, if need be, you have been grieved in various trials,

60:1:7.text: that the proof of your faith, which is more precious than gold that perishes, even though it is tested by fire, may be found to result in praise, glory, and honour at the revelation of Jesus Christ —

60:1:8.text: whom, not having known, you love. In him, though now you don’t see him, yet believing, you rejoice greatly with joy that is unspeakable and full of glory,

60:1:9.text: receiving the result of your faith, the salvation of your souls.

60:2:1.text: Putting away therefore all wickedness, all deceit, hypocrisies, envies, and all evil speaking,

60:2:10.text: In the past, you were not a people, but now are God’s people, who had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy.

60:2:11.text: Beloved, I beg you as foreigners and pilgrims to abstain from fleshly lusts which war against the soul,

60:2:12.text: having good behaviour amongst the nations, so in that of which they speak against you as evildoers, they may see your good works and glorify God in the day of visitation.

60:2:13.text: Therefore subject yourselves to every ordinance of man for the Lord’s sake: whether to the king, as supreme,

60:2:14.text: or to governors, as sent by him for vengeance on evildoers and for praise to those who do well.

60:2:15.text: For this is the will of God, that by well-doing you should put to silence the ignorance of foolish men.

60:2:16.text: Live as free people, yet not using your freedom for a cloak of wickedness, but as bondservants of God.

60:2:17.text: Honour all men. Love the brotherhood. Fear God. Honour the king.

60:2:18.text: Servants, be in subjection to your masters with all respect, not only to the good and gentle, but also to the wicked.

60:2:19.text: For it is commendable if someone endures pain, suffering unjustly, because of conscience towards God.

60:2:2.text: as newborn babies, long for the pure spiritual milk, that with it you may grow,

60:2:20.text: For what glory is it if, when you sin, you patiently endure beating? But if when you do well, you patiently endure suffering, this is commendable with God.

60:2:21.text: For you were called to this, because Christ also suffered for us, leaving you an example, that you should follow his steps,

60:2:22.text: who didn’t sin, “neither was deceit found in his mouth.”

60:2:23.text: When he was cursed, he didn’t curse back. When he suffered, he didn’t threaten, but committed himself to him who judges righteously.

60:2:24.text: He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree, that we, having died to sins, might live to righteousness. You were healed by his wounds.

60:2:25.text: For you were going astray like sheep; but now you have returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls.

60:2:3.text: if indeed you have tasted that the Lord is gracious.

60:2:4.text: Come to him, a living stone, rejected indeed by men, but chosen by God, precious.

60:2:5.text: You also as living stones are built up as a spiritual house, to be a holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.

60:2:6.text: Because it is contained in Scripture, “Behold, I lay in Zion a chief cornerstone, chosen and precious. He who believes in him will not be disappointed.”

60:2:7.text: For you who believe therefore is the honour, but for those who are disobedient, “The stone which the builders rejected has become the chief cornerstone,”

60:2:8.text: and, “a stumbling stone and a rock of offence.” For they stumble at the word, being disobedient, to which also they were appointed.

60:2:9.text: But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God’s own possession, that you may proclaim the excellence of him who called you out of darkness into his marvellous light.

60:3:1.text: In the same way, wives, be in subjection to your own husbands, so that, even if any don’t obey the Word, they may be won by the behaviour of their wives without a word,

60:3:10.text: For, “He who would love life and see good days, let him keep his tongue from evil and his lips from speaking deceit.

60:3:11.text: Let him turn away from evil and do good. Let him seek peace and pursue it.

60:3:12.text: For the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous, and his ears open to their prayer; but the face of the Lord is against those who do evil.”

60:3:13.text: Now who will harm you if you become imitators of that which is good?

60:3:14.text: But even if you should suffer for righteousness’ sake, you are blessed. “Don’t fear what they fear, neither be troubled.”

60:3:15.text: But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts. Always be ready to give an answer to everyone who asks you a reason concerning the hope that is in you, with humility and fear,

60:3:16.text: having a good conscience. Thus, while you are spoken against as evildoers, they may be disappointed who curse your good way of life in Christ.

60:3:17.text: For it is better, if it is God’s will, that you suffer for doing what is right than for doing evil.

60:3:18.text: Because Christ also suffered for sins once, the righteous for the unrighteous, that he might bring you to God, being put to death in the flesh, but made alive in the Spirit,

60:3:19.text: in whom he also went and preached to the spirits in prison,

60:3:2.text: seeing your pure behaviour in fear.

60:3:20.text: who before were disobedient when God waited patiently in the days of Noah while the ship was being built. In it, few, that is, eight souls, were saved through water.

60:3:21.text: This is a symbol of baptism, which now saves you — not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience towards God — through the resurrection of Jesus Christ,

60:3:22.text: who is at the right hand of God, having gone into heaven, angels and authorities and powers being made subject to him.

60:3:3.text: Let your beauty come not from the outward adorning of braiding your hair, and of wearing gold ornaments or of putting on fine clothing,

60:3:4.text: but from the hidden person of the heart, in the incorruptible adornment of a gentle and quiet spirit, which is very precious in God’s sight.

60:3:5.text: For this is how in the past the holy women who hoped in God also adorned themselves, being in subjection to their own husbands.

60:3:6.text: So Sarah obeyed Abraham, calling him lord, whose children you now are if you do well and are not put in fear by any terror.

60:3:7.text: You husbands, in the same way, live with your wives according to knowledge, giving honour to the woman as to the weaker vessel, as also being joint heirs of the grace of life, that your prayers may not be hindered.

60:3:8.text: Finally, all of you be like-minded, compassionate, loving as brothers, tenderhearted, courteous,

60:3:9.text: not rendering evil for evil or insult for insult; but instead blessing, knowing that you were called to this, that you may inherit a blessing.

60:4:1.text: Therefore, since Christ suffered for us in the flesh, arm yourselves also with the same mind; for he who has suffered in the flesh has ceased from sin,

60:4:10.text: As each has received a gift, employ it in serving one another, as good managers of the grace of God in its various forms.

60:4:11.text: If anyone speaks, let it be as it were the very words of God. If anyone serves, let it be as of the strength which God supplies, that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom belong the glory and the dominion forever and ever. Amen.

60:4:12.text: Beloved, don’t be astonished at the fiery trial which has come upon you to test you, as though a strange thing happened to you.

60:4:13.text: But because you are partakers of Christ’s sufferings, rejoice, that at the revelation of his glory you also may rejoice with exceeding joy.

60:4:14.text: If you are insulted for the name of Christ, you are blessed, because the Spirit of glory and of God rests on you. On their part he is blasphemed, but on your part he is glorified.

60:4:15.text: But let none of you suffer as a murderer, or a thief, or an evil doer, or a meddler in other men’s matters.

60:4:16.text: But if one of you suffers for being a Christian, let him not be ashamed; but let him glorify God in this matter.

60:4:17.text: For the time has come for judgement to begin with the household of God. If it begins first with us, what will happen to those who don’t obey the Good News of God?

60:4:18.text: “If it is hard for the righteous to be saved, what will happen to the ungodly and the sinner?”

60:4:19.text: Therefore let them also who suffer according to the will of God in doing good entrust their souls to him, as to a faithful Creator.

60:4:2.text: that you no longer should live the rest of your time in the flesh for the lusts of men, but for the will of God.

60:4:3.text: For we have spent enough of our past time doing the desire of the Gentiles, and having walked in lewdness, lusts, drunken binges, orgies, carousings, and abominable idolatries.

60:4:4.text: They think it is strange that you don’t run with them into the same excess of riot, speaking evil of you.

60:4:5.text: They will give account to him who is ready to judge the living and the dead.

60:4:6.text: For to this end the Good News was preached even to the dead, that they might be judged indeed as men in the flesh, but live as to God in the spirit.

60:4:7.text: But the end of all things is near. Therefore be of sound mind, self-controlled, and sober in prayer.

60:4:8.text: And above all things be earnest in your love amongst yourselves, for love covers a multitude of sins.

60:4:9.text: Be hospitable to one another without grumbling.

60:5:1.text: Therefore I exhort the elders amongst you, as a fellow elder and a witness of the sufferings of Christ, and who will also share in the glory that will be revealed:

60:5:10.text: But may the God of all grace, who called you to his eternal glory by Christ Jesus, after you have suffered a little while, perfect, establish, strengthen, and settle you.

60:5:11.text: To him be the glory and the power forever and ever. Amen.

60:5:12.text: Through Silvanus, our faithful brother, as I consider him, I have written to you briefly, exhorting and testifying that this is the true grace of God in which you stand.

60:5:13.text: She who is in Babylon, chosen together with you, greets you. So does Mark, my son.

60:5:14.text: Greet one another with a kiss of love. Peace be to all of you who are in Christ Jesus. Amen.

60:5:2.text: shepherd the flock of God which is amongst you, exercising the oversight, not under compulsion, but voluntarily; not for dishonest gain, but willingly;

60:5:3.text: not as lording it over those entrusted to you, but making yourselves examples to the flock.

60:5:4.text: When the chief Shepherd is revealed, you will receive the crown of glory that doesn’t fade away.

60:5:5.text: Likewise, you younger ones, be subject to the elder. Yes, all of you clothe yourselves with humility and subject yourselves to one another; for “God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”

60:5:6.text: Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time,

60:5:7.text: casting all your worries on him, because he cares for you.

60:5:8.text: Be sober and self-controlled. Be watchful. Your adversary, the devil, walks around like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour.

60:5:9.text: Withstand him steadfast in your faith, knowing that your brothers who are in the world are undergoing the same sufferings.

61:1:1.text: Simon Peter, a servant and apostle of Jesus Christ, to those who have obtained a like precious faith with us in the righteousness of our God and Saviour, Jesus Christ:

61:1:10.text: Therefore, brothers, be more diligent to make your calling and election sure. For if you do these things, you will never stumble.

61:1:11.text: For thus you will be richly supplied with the entrance into the eternal Kingdom of our Lord and Saviour, Jesus Christ.

61:1:12.text: Therefore I will not be negligent to remind you of these things, though you know them and are established in the present truth.

61:1:13.text: I think it right, as long as I am in this tent, to stir you up by reminding you,

61:1:14.text: knowing that the putting off of my tent comes swiftly, even as our Lord Jesus Christ made clear to me.

61:1:15.text: Yes, I will make every effort that you may always be able to remember these things even after my departure.

61:1:16.text: For we didn’t follow cunningly devised fables when we made known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, but we were eyewitnesses of his majesty.

61:1:17.text: For he received from God the Father honour and glory when the voice came to him from the Majestic Glory, “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.”

61:1:18.text: We heard this voice come out of heaven when we were with him on the holy mountain.

61:1:19.text: We have the more sure word of prophecy; and you do well that you heed it as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star arises in your hearts,

61:1:2.text: Grace to you and peace be multiplied in the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord,

61:1:20.text: knowing this first, that no prophecy of Scripture is of private interpretation.

61:1:21.text: For no prophecy ever came by the will of man, but holy men of God spoke, being moved by the Holy Spirit.

61:1:3.text: seeing that his divine power has granted to us all things that pertain to life and godliness, through the knowledge of him who called us by his own glory and virtue,

61:1:4.text: by which he has granted to us his precious and exceedingly great promises; that through these you may become partakers of the divine nature, having escaped from the corruption that is in the world by lust.

61:1:5.text: Yes, and for this very cause adding on your part all diligence, in your faith supply moral excellence; and in moral excellence, knowledge;

61:1:6.text: and in knowledge, self-control; and in self-control, perseverance; and in perseverance, godliness;

61:1:7.text: and in godliness, brotherly affection; and in brotherly affection, love.

61:1:8.text: For if these things are yours and abound, they make you to not be idle or unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.

61:1:9.text: For he who lacks these things is blind, seeing only what is near, having forgotten the cleansing from his old sins.

61:2:1.text: But false prophets also arose amongst the people, as false teachers will also be amongst you, who will secretly bring in destructive heresies, denying even the Master who bought them, bringing on themselves swift destruction.

61:2:10.text: but chiefly those who walk after the flesh in the lust of defilement and despise authority. Daring, self-willed, they are not afraid to speak evil of dignitaries,

61:2:11.text: whereas angels, though greater in might and power, don’t bring a slanderous judgement against them before the Lord.

61:2:12.text: But these, as unreasoning creatures, born natural animals to be taken and destroyed, speaking evil in matters about which they are ignorant, will in their destroying surely be destroyed,

61:2:13.text: receiving the wages of unrighteousness; people who count it pleasure to revel in the daytime, spots and defects, revelling in their deceit while they feast with you;

61:2:14.text: having eyes full of adultery, and who can’t cease from sin, enticing unsettled souls, having a heart trained in greed, accursed children!

61:2:15.text: Forsaking the right way, they went astray, having followed the way of Balaam the son of Beor, who loved the wages of wrongdoing;

61:2:16.text: but he was rebuked for his own disobedience. A speechless donkey spoke with a man’s voice and stopped the madness of the prophet.

61:2:17.text: These are wells without water, clouds driven by a storm, for whom the blackness of darkness has been reserved forever.

61:2:18.text: For, uttering great swelling words of emptiness, they entice in the lusts of the flesh, by licentiousness, those who are indeed escaping from those who live in error;

61:2:19.text: promising them liberty, while they themselves are bondservants of corruption; for a man is brought into bondage by whoever overcomes him.

61:2:2.text: Many will follow their immoral ways, and as a result, the way of the truth will be maligned.

61:2:20.text: For if, after they have escaped the defilement of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, they are again entangled in it and overcome, the last state has become worse for them than the first.

61:2:21.text: For it would be better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than after knowing it, to turn back from the holy commandment delivered to them.

61:2:22.text: But it has happened to them according to the true proverb, “The dog turns to his own vomit again,” and “the sow that has washed to wallowing in the mire.”

61:2:3.text: In covetousness they will exploit you with deceptive words: whose sentence now from of old doesn’t linger, and their destruction will not slumber.

61:2:4.text: For if God didn’t spare angels when they sinned, but cast them down to Tartarus, and committed them to pits of darkness to be reserved for judgement;

61:2:5.text: and didn’t spare the ancient world, but preserved Noah with seven others, a preacher of righteousness, when he brought a flood on the world of the ungodly,

61:2:6.text: and turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah into ashes, condemned them to destruction, having made them an example to those who would live in an ungodly way,

61:2:7.text: and delivered righteous Lot, who was very distressed by the lustful life of the wicked

61:2:8.text: (for that righteous man dwelling amongst them was tormented in his righteous soul from day to day with seeing and hearing lawless deeds),

61:2:9.text: then the Lord knows how to deliver the godly out of temptation and to keep the unrighteous under punishment for the day of judgement,

61:3:1.text: This is now, beloved, the second letter that I have written to you; and in both of them I stir up your sincere mind by reminding you

61:3:10.text: But the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night, in which the heavens will pass away with a great noise, and the elements will be dissolved with fervent heat; and the earth and the works that are in it will be burnt up.

61:3:11.text: Therefore, since all these things will be destroyed like this, what kind of people ought you to be in holy living and godliness,

61:3:12.text: looking for and earnestly desiring the coming of the day of God, which will cause the burning heavens to be dissolved, and the elements will melt with fervent heat?

61:3:13.text: But, according to his promise, we look for new heavens and a new earth, in which righteousness dwells.

61:3:14.text: Therefore, beloved, seeing that you look for these things, be diligent to be found in peace, without defect and blameless in his sight.

61:3:15.text: Regard the patience of our Lord as salvation; even as our beloved brother Paul also, according to the wisdom given to him, wrote to you,

61:3:16.text: as also in all of his letters, speaking in them of these things. In those, there are some things that are hard to understand, which the ignorant and unsettled twist, as they also do to the other Scriptures, to their own destruction.

61:3:17.text: You therefore, beloved, knowing these things beforehand, beware, lest being carried away with the error of the wicked, you fall from your own steadfastness.

61:3:18.text: But grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ. To him be the glory both now and forever. Amen.

61:3:2.text: that you should remember the words which were spoken before by the holy prophets and the commandment of us, the apostles of the Lord and Saviour,

61:3:3.text: knowing this first, that in the last days mockers will come, walking after their own lusts

61:3:4.text: and saying, “Where is the promise of his coming? For, from the day that the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation.”

61:3:5.text: For they wilfully forget that there were heavens from of old, and an earth formed out of water and amid water by the word of God,

61:3:6.text: by which means the world that existed then, being overflowed with water, perished.

61:3:7.text: But the heavens that exist now and the earth, by the same word have been stored up for fire, being reserved against the day of judgement and destruction of ungodly men.

61:3:8.text: But don’t forget this one thing, beloved, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.

61:3:9.text: The Lord is not slow concerning his promise, as some count slowness; but he is patient with us, not wishing that anyone should perish, but that all should come to repentance.

62:1:1.text: That which was from the beginning, that which we have heard, that which we have seen with our eyes, that which we saw, and our hands touched, concerning the Word of life

62:1:10.text: If we say that we haven’t sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us.

62:1:2.text: (and the life was revealed, and we have seen, and testify, and declare to you the life, the eternal life, which was with the Father, and was revealed to us);

62:1:3.text: that which we have seen and heard we declare to you, that you also may have fellowship with us. Yes, and our fellowship is with the Father and with his Son, Jesus Christ.

62:1:4.text: And we write these things to you, that our joy may be fulfilled.

62:1:5.text: This is the message which we have heard from him and announce to you, that God is light, and in him is no darkness at all.

62:1:6.text: If we say that we have fellowship with him and walk in the darkness, we lie and don’t tell the truth.

62:1:7.text: But if we walk in the light as he is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son, cleanses us from all sin.

62:1:8.text: If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.

62:1:9.text: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

62:2:1.text: My little children, I write these things to you so that you may not sin. If anyone sins, we have a Counsellor with the Father, Jesus Christ, the righteous.

62:2:10.text: He who loves his brother remains in the light, and there is no occasion for stumbling in him.

62:2:11.text: But he who hates his brother is in the darkness, and walks in the darkness, and doesn’t know where he is going, because the darkness has blinded his eyes.

62:2:12.text: I write to you, little children, because your sins are forgiven you for his name’s sake.

62:2:13.text: I write to you, fathers, because you know him who is from the beginning. I write to you, young men, because you have overcome the evil one. I write to you, little children, because you know the Father.

62:2:14.text: I have written to you, fathers, because you know him who is from the beginning. I have written to you, young men, because you are strong, and the word of God remains in you, and you have overcome the evil one.

62:2:15.text: Don’t love the world or the things that are in the world. If anyone loves the world, the Father’s love isn’t in him.

62:2:16.text: For all that is in the world — the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life — isn’t the Father’s, but is the world’s.

62:2:17.text: The world is passing away with its lusts, but he who does God’s will remains forever.

62:2:18.text: Little children, these are the end times, and as you heard that the Antichrist is coming, even now many antichrists have arisen. By this we know that it is the final hour.

62:2:19.text: They went out from us, but they didn’t belong to us; for if they had belonged to us, they would have continued with us. But they left, that they might be revealed that none of them belong to us.

62:2:2.text: And he is the atoning sacrifice for our sins, and not for ours only, but also for the whole world.

62:2:20.text: You have an anointing from the Holy One, and you all have knowledge.

62:2:21.text: I have not written to you because you don’t know the truth, but because you know it, and because no lie is of the truth.

62:2:22.text: Who is the liar but he who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This is the Antichrist, he who denies the Father and the Son.

62:2:23.text: Whoever denies the Son doesn’t have the Father. He who confesses the Son has the Father also.

62:2:24.text: Therefore, as for you, let that remain in you which you heard from the beginning. If that which you heard from the beginning remains in you, you also will remain in the Son, and in the Father.

62:2:25.text: This is the promise which he promised us, the eternal life.

62:2:26.text: These things I have written to you concerning those who would lead you astray.

62:2:27.text: As for you, the anointing which you received from him remains in you, and you don’t need for anyone to teach you. But as his anointing teaches you concerning all things, and is true, and is no lie, and even as it taught you, you will remain in him.

62:2:28.text: Now, little children, remain in him, that when he appears, we may have boldness and not be ashamed before him at his coming.

62:2:29.text: If you know that he is righteous, you know that everyone who practices righteousness has been born of him.

62:2:3.text: This is how we know that we know him: if we keep his commandments.

62:2:4.text: One who says, “I know him,” and doesn’t keep his commandments, is a liar, and the truth isn’t in him.

62:2:5.text: But God’s love has most certainly been perfected in whoever keeps his word. This is how we know that we are in him:

62:2:6.text: he who says he remains in him ought himself also to walk just like he walked.

62:2:7.text: Brothers, I write no new commandment to you, but an old commandment which you had from the beginning. The old commandment is the word which you heard from the beginning.

62:2:8.text: Again, I write a new commandment to you, which is true in him and in you, because the darkness is passing away and the true light already shines.

62:2:9.text: He who says he is in the light and hates his brother is in the darkness even until now.

62:3:1.text: See how great a love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God! For this cause the world doesn’t know us, because it didn’t know him.

62:3:10.text: In this the children of God are revealed, and the children of the devil. Whoever doesn’t do righteousness is not of God, neither is he who doesn’t love his brother.

62:3:11.text: For this is the message which you heard from the beginning, that we should love one another —

62:3:12.text: unlike Cain, who was of the evil one and killed his brother. Why did he kill him? Because his deeds were evil, and his brother’s righteous.

62:3:13.text: Don’t be surprised, my brothers, if the world hates you.

62:3:14.text: We know that we have passed out of death into life, because we love the brothers. He who doesn’t love his brother remains in death.

62:3:15.text: Whoever hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life remaining in him.

62:3:16.text: By this we know love, because he laid down his life for us. And we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers.

62:3:17.text: But whoever has the world’s goods and sees his brother in need, then closes his heart of compassion against him, how does God’s love remain in him?

62:3:18.text: My little children, let’s not love in word only, or with the tongue only, but in deed and truth.

62:3:19.text: And by this we know that we are of the truth and persuade our hearts before him,

62:3:2.text: Beloved, now we are children of God. It is not yet revealed what we will be; but we know that when he is revealed, we will be like him, for we will see him just as he is.

62:3:20.text: because if our heart condemns us, God is greater than our heart, and knows all things.

62:3:21.text: Beloved, if our hearts don’t condemn us, we have boldness towards God;

62:3:22.text: so whatever we ask, we receive from him, because we keep his commandments and do the things that are pleasing in his sight.

62:3:23.text: This is his commandment, that we should believe in the name of his Son, Jesus Christ, and love one another, even as he commanded.

62:3:24.text: He who keeps his commandments remains in him, and he in him. By this we know that he remains in us, by the Spirit which he gave us.

62:3:3.text: Everyone who has this hope set on him purifies himself, even as he is pure.

62:3:4.text: Everyone who sins also commits lawlessness. Sin is lawlessness.

62:3:5.text: You know that he was revealed to take away our sins, and no sin is in him.

62:3:6.text: Whoever remains in him doesn’t sin. Whoever sins hasn’t seen him and doesn’t know him.

62:3:7.text: Little children, let no one lead you astray. He who does righteousness is righteous, even as he is righteous.

62:3:8.text: He who sins is of the devil, for the devil has been sinning from the beginning. To this end the Son of God was revealed: that he might destroy the works of the devil.

62:3:9.text: Whoever is born of God doesn’t commit sin, because his seed remains in him, and he can’t sin, because he is born of God.

62:4:1.text: Beloved, don’t believe every spirit, but test the spirits, whether they are of God, because many false prophets have gone out into the world.

62:4:10.text: In this is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son as the atoning sacrifice for our sins.

62:4:11.text: Beloved, if God loved us in this way, we also ought to love one another.

62:4:12.text: No one has seen God at any time. If we love one another, God remains in us, and his love has been perfected in us.

62:4:13.text: By this we know that we remain in him and he in us, because he has given us of his Spirit.

62:4:14.text: We have seen and testify that the Father has sent the Son as the Saviour of the world.

62:4:15.text: Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God remains in him, and he in God.

62:4:16.text: We know and have believed the love which God has for us. God is love, and he who remains in love remains in God, and God remains in him.

62:4:17.text: In this, love has been made perfect amongst us, that we may have boldness in the day of judgement, because as he is, even so we are in this world.

62:4:18.text: There is no fear in love; but perfect love casts out fear, because fear has punishment. He who fears is not made perfect in love.

62:4:19.text: We love him, because he first loved us.

62:4:2.text: By this you know the Spirit of God: every spirit who confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is of God,

62:4:20.text: If a man says, “I love God,” and hates his brother, he is a liar; for he who doesn’t love his brother whom he has seen, how can he love God whom he has not seen?

62:4:21.text: This commandment we have from him, that he who loves God should also love his brother.

62:4:3.text: and every spirit who doesn’t confess that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is not of God; and this is the spirit of the Antichrist, of whom you have heard that it comes. Now it is in the world already.

62:4:4.text: You are of God, little children, and have overcome them, because greater is he who is in you than he who is in the world.

62:4:5.text: They are of the world. Therefore they speak of the world, and the world hears them.

62:4:6.text: We are of God. He who knows God listens to us. He who is not of God doesn’t listen to us. By this we know the spirit of truth, and the spirit of error.

62:4:7.text: Beloved, let’s love one another, for love is of God; and everyone who loves has been born of God and knows God.

62:4:8.text: He who doesn’t love doesn’t know God, for God is love.

62:4:9.text: By this God’s love was revealed in us, that God has sent his only born Son into the world that we might live through him.

62:5:1.text: Whoever believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God. Whoever loves the Father also loves the child who is born of him.

62:5:10.text: He who believes in the Son of God has the testimony in himself. He who doesn’t believe God has made him a liar, because he has not believed in the testimony that God has given concerning his Son.

62:5:11.text: The testimony is this: that God gave to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.

62:5:12.text: He who has the Son has the life. He who doesn’t have God’s Son doesn’t have the life.

62:5:13.text: These things I have written to you who believe in the name of the Son of God, that you may know that you have eternal life, and that you may continue to believe in the name of the Son of God.

62:5:14.text: This is the boldness which we have towards him, that if we ask anything according to his will, he listens to us.

62:5:15.text: And if we know that he listens to us, whatever we ask, we know that we have the petitions which we have asked of him.

62:5:16.text: If anyone sees his brother sinning a sin not leading to death, he shall ask, and God will give him life for those who sin not leading to death. There is sin leading to death. I don’t say that he should make a request concerning this.

62:5:17.text: All unrighteousness is sin, and there is sin not leading to death.

62:5:18.text: We know that whoever is born of God doesn’t sin, but he who was born of God keeps himself, and the evil one doesn’t touch him.

62:5:19.text: We know that we are of God, and the whole world lies in the power of the evil one.

62:5:2.text: By this we know that we love the children of God, when we love God and keep his commandments.

62:5:20.text: We know that the Son of God has come and has given us an understanding, that we know him who is true; and we are in him who is true, in his Son Jesus Christ. This is the true God and eternal life.

62:5:21.text: Little children, keep yourselves from idols.

62:5:3.text: For this is loving God, that we keep his commandments. His commandments are not grievous.

62:5:4.text: For whatever is born of God overcomes the world. This is the victory that has overcome the world: your faith.

62:5:5.text: Who is he who overcomes the world, but he who believes that Jesus is the Son of God?

62:5:6.text: This is he who came by water and blood, Jesus Christ; not with the water only, but with the water and the blood. It is the Spirit who testifies, because the Spirit is the truth.

62:5:7.text: For there are three who testify:

62:5:8.text: the Spirit, the water, and the blood; and the three agree as one.

62:5:9.text: If we receive the witness of men, the witness of God is greater; for this is God’s testimony which he has testified concerning his Son.

63:1:1.text: The elder, to the chosen lady and her children, whom I love in truth, and not I only, but also all those who know the truth,

63:1:10.text: If anyone comes to you and doesn’t bring this teaching, don’t receive him into your house, and don’t welcome him,

63:1:11.text: for he who welcomes him participates in his evil deeds.

63:1:12.text: Having many things to write to you, I don’t want to do so with paper and ink, but I hope to come to you and to speak face to face, that our joy may be made full.

63:1:13.text: The children of your chosen sister greet you. Amen.

63:1:2.text: for the truth’s sake, which remains in us, and it will be with us forever:

63:1:3.text: Grace, mercy, and peace will be with us, from God the Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father, in truth and love.

63:1:4.text: I rejoice greatly that I have found some of your children walking in truth, even as we have been commanded by the Father.

63:1:5.text: Now I beg you, dear lady, not as though I wrote to you a new commandment, but that which we had from the beginning, that we love one another.

63:1:6.text: This is love, that we should walk according to his commandments. This is the commandment, even as you heard from the beginning, that you should walk in it.

63:1:7.text: For many deceivers have gone out into the world, those who don’t confess that Jesus Christ came in the flesh. This is the deceiver and the Antichrist.

63:1:8.text: Watch yourselves, that we don’t lose the things which we have accomplished, but that we receive a full reward.

63:1:9.text: Whoever transgresses and doesn’t remain in the teaching of Christ doesn’t have God. He who remains in the teaching has both the Father and the Son.

64:1:1.text: The elder to Gaius the beloved, whom I love in truth.

64:1:10.text: Therefore, if I come, I will call attention to his deeds which he does, unjustly accusing us with wicked words. Not content with this, he doesn’t receive the brothers himself, and those who would, he forbids and throws out of the assembly.

64:1:11.text: Beloved, don’t imitate that which is evil, but that which is good. He who does good is of God. He who does evil hasn’t seen God.

64:1:12.text: Demetrius has the testimony of all, and of the truth itself; yes, we also testify, and you know that our testimony is true.

64:1:13.text: I had many things to write to you, but I am unwilling to write to you with ink and pen;

64:1:14.text: but I hope to see you soon. Then we will speak face to face. Peace be to you. The friends greet you. Greet the friends by name.

64:1:2.text: Beloved, I pray that you may prosper in all things and be healthy, even as your soul prospers.

64:1:3.text: For I rejoiced greatly when brothers came and testified about your truth, even as you walk in truth.

64:1:4.text: I have no greater joy than this: to hear about my children walking in truth.

64:1:5.text: Beloved, you do a faithful work in whatever you accomplish for those who are brothers and strangers.

64:1:6.text: They have testified about your love before the assembly. You will do well to send them forward on their journey in a way worthy of God,

64:1:7.text: because for the sake of the Name they went out, taking nothing from the Gentiles.

64:1:8.text: We therefore ought to receive such, that we may be fellow workers for the truth.

64:1:9.text: I wrote to the assembly, but Diotrephes, who loves to be first amongst them, doesn’t accept what we say.

65:1:1.text: Jude, a servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James, to those who are called, sanctified by God the Father, and kept for Jesus Christ:

65:1:10.text: But these speak evil of whatever things they don’t know. They are destroyed in these things that they understand naturally, like the creatures without reason.

65:1:11.text: Woe to them! For they went in the way of Cain, and ran riotously in the error of Balaam for hire, and perished in Korah’s rebellion.

65:1:12.text: These are hidden rocky reefs in your love feasts when they feast with you, shepherds who without fear feed themselves; clouds without water, carried along by winds; autumn trees without fruit, twice dead, plucked up by the roots;

65:1:13.text: wild waves of the sea, foaming out their own shame; wandering stars, for whom the blackness of darkness has been reserved forever.

65:1:14.text: About these also Enoch, the seventh from Adam, prophesied, saying, “Behold, the Lord came with ten thousands of his holy ones,

65:1:15.text: to execute judgement on all, and to convict all the ungodly of all their works of ungodliness which they have done in an ungodly way, and of all the hard things which ungodly sinners have spoken against him.”

65:1:16.text: These are murmurers and complainers, walking after their lusts — and their mouth speaks proud things — showing respect of persons to gain advantage.

65:1:17.text: But you, beloved, remember the words which have been spoken before by the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ.

65:1:18.text: They said to you, “In the last time there will be mockers, walking after their own ungodly lusts.”

65:1:19.text: These are those who cause divisions and are sensual, not having the Spirit.

65:1:2.text: May mercy, peace, and love be multiplied to you.

65:1:20.text: But you, beloved, keep building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Spirit.

65:1:21.text: Keep yourselves in God’s love, looking for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ to eternal life.

65:1:22.text: On some have compassion, making a distinction,

65:1:23.text: and some save, snatching them out of the fire with fear, hating even the clothing stained by the flesh.

65:1:24.text: Now to him who is able to keep them from stumbling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory in great joy,

65:1:25.text: to God our Saviour, who alone is wise, be glory and majesty, dominion and power, both now and forever. Amen.

65:1:3.text: Beloved, while I was very eager to write to you about our common salvation, I was constrained to write to you exhorting you to contend earnestly for the faith which was once for all delivered to the saints.

65:1:4.text: For there are certain men who crept in secretly, even those who were long ago written about for this condemnation: ungodly men, turning the grace of our God into indecency, and denying our only Master, God, and Lord, Jesus Christ.

65:1:5.text: Now I desire to remind you, though you already know this, that the Lord, having saved a people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed those who didn’t believe.

65:1:6.text: Angels who didn’t keep their first domain, but deserted their own dwelling place, he has kept in everlasting bonds under darkness for the judgement of the great day.

65:1:7.text: Even as Sodom and Gomorrah and the cities around them, having in the same way as these given themselves over to sexual immorality and gone after strange flesh, are shown as an example, suffering the punishment of eternal fire.

65:1:8.text: Yet in the same way, these also in their dreaming defile the flesh, despise authority, and slander celestial beings.

65:1:9.text: But Michael, the archangel, when contending with the devil and arguing about the body of Moses, dared not bring against him an abusive condemnation, but said, “May the Lord rebuke you!”

1:10:1.text: Now this is the history of the generations of the sons of Noah and of Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Sons were born to them after the flood.

1:10:10.text: The beginning of his kingdom was Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.

1:10:11.text: Out of that land he went into Assyria, and built Nineveh, Rehoboth Ir, Calah,

1:10:12.text: and Resen between Nineveh and the great city Calah.

1:10:13.text: Mizraim became the father of Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim,

1:10:14.text: Pathrusim, Casluhim (which the Philistines descended from), and Caphtorim.

1:10:15.text: Canaan became the father of Sidon (his firstborn), Heth,

1:10:16.text: the Jebusites, the Amorites, the Girgashites,

1:10:17.text: the Hivites, the Arkites, the Sinites,

1:10:18.text: the Arvadites, the Zemarites, and the Hamathites. Afterward the families of the Canaanites were spread abroad.

1:10:19.text: The border of the Canaanites was from Sidon — as you go toward Gerar — to Gaza — as you go toward Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim — to Lasha.

1:10:2.text: The sons of Japheth were: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.

1:10:20.text: These are the sons of Ham, after their families, according to their languages, in their lands and their nations.

1:10:21.text: Children were also born to Shem (the elder brother of Japheth), the father of all the children of Eber.

1:10:22.text: The sons of Shem were: Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, and Aram.

1:10:23.text: The sons of Aram were: Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash.

1:10:24.text: Arpachshad became the father of Shelah. Shelah became the father of Eber.

1:10:25.text: To Eber were born two sons. The name of the one was Peleg, for in his days the earth was divided. His brother’s name was Joktan.

1:10:26.text: Joktan became the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,

1:10:29.text: Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these were the sons of Joktan.

1:10:3.text: The sons of Gomer were: Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.

1:10:30.text: Their dwelling extended from Mesha, as you go toward Sephar, the mountain of the east.

1:10:31.text: These are the sons of Shem, by their families, according to their languages, lands, and nations.

1:10:32.text: These are the families of the sons of Noah, by their generations, according to their nations. The nations divided from these in the earth after the flood.

1:10:4.text: The sons of Javan were: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.

1:10:5.text: Of these were the islands of the nations divided in their lands, everyone after his language, after their families, in their nations.

1:10:6.text: The sons of Ham were: Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.

1:10:7.text: The sons of Cush were: Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. The sons of Raamah were: Sheba and Dedan.

1:10:8.text: Cush became the father of Nimrod. He began to be a mighty one in the earth.

1:10:9.text: He was a mighty hunter before Yahweh. Therefore it is said, “like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before Yahweh”.

1:11:1.text: The whole earth was of one language and of one speech.

1:11:10.text: This is the history of the generations of Shem: Shem was one hundred years old when he became the father of Arpachshad two years after the flood.

1:11:11.text: Shem lived five hundred years after he became the father of Arpachshad, and became the father of more sons and daughters.

1:11:12.text: Arpachshad lived thirty-five years and became the father of Shelah.

1:11:13.text: Arpachshad lived four hundred three years after he became the father of Shelah, and became the father of more sons and daughters.

1:11:14.text: Shelah lived thirty years, and became the father of Eber.

1:11:15.text: Shelah lived four hundred three years after he became the father of Eber, and became the father of more sons and daughters.

1:11:16.text: Eber lived thirty-four years, and became the father of Peleg.

1:11:17.text: Eber lived four hundred thirty years after he became the father of Peleg, and became the father of more sons and daughters.

1:11:18.text: Peleg lived thirty years, and became the father of Reu.

1:11:19.text: Peleg lived two hundred nine years after he became the father of Reu, and became the father of more sons and daughters.

1:11:2.text: As they traveled east, they found a plain in the land of Shinar, and they lived there.

1:11:20.text: Reu lived thirty-two years, and became the father of Serug.

1:11:21.text: Reu lived two hundred seven years after he became the father of Serug, and became the father of more sons and daughters.

1:11:22.text: Serug lived thirty years, and became the father of Nahor.

1:11:23.text: Serug lived two hundred years after he became the father of Nahor, and became the father of more sons and daughters.

1:11:24.text: Nahor lived twenty-nine years, and became the father of Terah.

1:11:25.text: Nahor lived one hundred nineteen years after he became the father of Terah, and became the father of more sons and daughters.

1:11:26.text: Terah lived seventy years, and became the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran.

1:11:27.text: Now this is the history of the generations of Terah. Terah became the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran. Haran became the father of Lot.

1:11:28.text: Haran died in the land of his birth, in Ur of the Chaldees, while his father Terah was still alive.

1:11:29.text: Abram and Nahor married wives. The name of Abram’s wife was Sarai, and the name of Nahor’s wife was Milcah, the daughter of Haran, who was also the father of Iscah.

1:11:3.text: They said to one another, “Come, let’s make bricks, and burn them thoroughly.” They had brick for stone, and they used tar for mortar.

1:11:30.text: Sarai was barren. She had no child.

1:11:31.text: Terah took Abram his son, Lot the son of Haran, his son’s son, and Sarai his daughter-in-law, his son Abram’s wife. They went from Ur of the Chaldees, to go into the land of Canaan. They came to Haran and lived there.

1:11:32.text: The days of Terah were two hundred five years. Terah died in Haran.

1:11:4.text: They said, “Come, let’s build ourselves a city, and a tower whose top reaches to the sky, and let’s make a name for ourselves, lest we be scattered abroad on the surface of the whole earth.”

1:11:5.text: Yahweh came down to see the city and the tower, which the children of men built.

1:11:6.text: Yahweh said, “Behold, they are one people, and they all have one language, and this is what they begin to do. Now nothing will be withheld from them, which they intend to do.

1:11:7.text: Come, let’s go down, and there confuse their language, that they may not understand one another’s speech.”

1:11:8.text: So Yahweh scattered them abroad from there on the surface of all the earth. They stopped building the city.

1:11:9.text: Therefore its name was called Babel, because there Yahweh confused the language of all the earth. From there, Yahweh scattered them abroad on the surface of all the earth.

1:12:1.text: Now Yahweh said to Abram, “Leave your country, and your relatives, and your father’s house, and go to the land that I will show you.

1:12:10.text: There was a famine in the land. Abram went down into Egypt to live as a foreigner there, for the famine was severe in the land.

1:12:11.text: When he had come near to enter Egypt, he said to Sarai his wife, “See now, I know that you are a beautiful woman to look at.

1:12:12.text: It will happen that when the Egyptians see you, they will say, ‘This is his wife.’ They will kill me, but they will save you alive.

1:12:13.text: Please say that you are my sister, that it may be well with me for your sake, and that my soul may live because of you.”

1:12:14.text: When Abram had come into Egypt, some Egyptians saw that the woman was very beautiful.

1:12:15.text: The princes of Pharaoh saw her, and praised her to Pharaoh; and the woman was taken into Pharaoh’s house.

1:12:16.text: He dealt well with Abram for her sake. He had sheep, cattle, male donkeys, male servants, female servants, female donkeys, and camels.

1:12:17.text: Yahweh afflicted Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai, Abram’s wife.

1:12:18.text: Pharaoh called Abram and said, “What is this that you have done to me? Why didn’t you tell me that she was your wife?

1:12:19.text: Why did you say, ‘She is my sister,’ so that I took her to be my wife? Now therefore, see your wife, take her, and go your way.”

1:12:2.text: I will make of you a great nation. I will bless you and make your name great. You will be a blessing.

1:12:20.text: Pharaoh commanded men concerning him, and they escorted him away with his wife and all that he had.

1:12:3.text: I will bless those who bless you, and I will curse him who treats you with contempt. All the families of the earth will be blessed through you.”

1:12:4.text: So Abram went, as Yahweh had told him. Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he departed from Haran.

1:12:5.text: Abram took Sarai his wife, Lot his brother’s son, all their possessions that they had gathered, and the people whom they had acquired in Haran, and they went to go into the land of Canaan. They entered into the land of Canaan.

1:12:6.text: Abram passed through the land to the place of Shechem, to the oak of Moreh. At that time, Canaanites were in the land.

1:12:7.text: Yahweh appeared to Abram and said, “I will give this land to your offspring.” He built an altar there to Yahweh, who had appeared to him.

1:12:8.text: He left from there to go to the mountain on the east of Bethel and pitched his tent, having Bethel on the west, and Ai on the east. There he built an altar to Yahweh and called on Yahweh’s name.

1:12:9.text: Abram traveled, still going on toward the South.

1:13:1.text: Abram went up out of Egypt — he, his wife, all that he had, and Lot with him — into the South.

1:13:10.text: Lot lifted up his eyes, and saw all the plain of the Jordan, that it was well-watered everywhere, before Yahweh destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah, like the garden of Yahweh, like the land of Egypt, as you go to Zoar.

1:13:11.text: So Lot chose the Plain of the Jordan for himself. Lot traveled east, and they separated themselves from one another.

1:13:12.text: Abram lived in the land of Canaan, and Lot lived in the cities of the plain, and moved his tent as far as Sodom.

1:13:13.text: Now the men of Sodom were exceedingly wicked and sinners against Yahweh.

1:13:14.text: Yahweh said to Abram, after Lot was separated from him, “Now, lift up your eyes, and look from the place where you are, northward and southward and eastward and westward,

1:13:15.text: for I will give all the land which you see to you and to your offspring forever.

1:13:16.text: I will make your offspring as the dust of the earth, so that if a man can count the dust of the earth, then your offspring may also be counted.

1:13:17.text: Arise, walk through the land in its length and in its width; for I will give it to you.”

1:13:18.text: Abram moved his tent, and came and lived by the oaks of Mamre, which are in Hebron, and built an altar there to Yahweh.

1:13:2.text: Abram was very rich in livestock, in silver, and in gold.

1:13:3.text: He went on his journeys from the South as far as Bethel, to the place where his tent had been at the beginning, between Bethel and Ai,

1:13:4.text: to the place of the altar, which he had made there at the first. There Abram called on Yahweh’s name.

1:13:5.text: Lot also, who went with Abram, had flocks, herds, and tents.

1:13:6.text: The land was not able to bear them, that they might live together; for their possessions were so great that they couldn’t live together.

1:13:7.text: There was strife between the herdsmen of Abram’s livestock and the herdsmen of Lot’s livestock. The Canaanites and the Perizzites lived in the land at that time.

1:13:8.text: Abram said to Lot, “Please, let there be no strife between you and me, and between your herdsmen and my herdsmen; for we are relatives.

1:13:9.text: Isn’t the whole land before you? Please separate yourself from me. If you go to the left hand, then I will go to the right. Or if you go to the right hand, then I will go to the left.”

1:15:1.text: After these things Yahweh’s word came to Abram in a vision, saying, “Don’t be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your exceedingly great reward.”

1:15:10.text: He brought him all these, and divided them in the middle, and laid each half opposite the other; but he didn’t divide the birds.

1:15:11.text: The birds of prey came down on the carcasses, and Abram drove them away.

1:15:12.text: When the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell on Abram. Now terror and great darkness fell on him.

1:15:13.text: He said to Abram, “Know for sure that your offspring will live as foreigners in a land that is not theirs, and will serve them. They will afflict them four hundred years.

1:15:14.text: I will also judge that nation, whom they will serve. Afterward they will come out with great wealth;

1:15:15.text: but you will go to your fathers in peace. You will be buried at a good old age.

1:15:16.text: In the fourth generation they will come here again, for the iniquity of the Amorite is not yet full.”

1:15:17.text: It came to pass that, when the sun went down, and it was dark, behold, a smoking furnace and a flaming torch passed between these pieces.

1:15:18.text: In that day Yahweh made a covenant with Abram, saying, “I have given this land to your offspring, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Euphrates:

1:15:19.text: the land of the Kenites, the Kenizzites, the Kadmonites,

1:15:2.text: Abram said, “Lord Yahweh, what will you give me, since I go childless, and he who will inherit my estate is Eliezer of Damascus?”

1:15:20.text: the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Rephaim,

1:15:21.text: the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Girgashites, and the Jebusites.”

1:15:3.text: Abram said, “Behold, you have given no children to me: and, behold, one born in my house is my heir.”

1:15:4.text: Behold, Yahweh’s word came to him, saying, “This man will not be your heir, but he who will come out of your own body will be your heir.”

1:15:5.text: Yahweh brought him outside, and said, “Look now toward the sky, and count the stars, if you are able to count them.” He said to Abram, “So your offspring will be.”

1:15:6.text: He believed in Yahweh, who credited it to him for righteousness.

1:15:7.text: He said to Abram, “I am Yahweh who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldees, to give you this land to inherit it.”

1:15:8.text: He said, “Lord Yahweh, how will I know that I will inherit it?”

1:15:9.text: He said to him, “Bring me a heifer three years old, a female goat three years old, a ram three years old, a turtledove, and a young pigeon.”

1:17:1.text: When Abram was ninety-nine years old, Yahweh appeared to Abram and said to him, “I am God Almighty. Walk before me and be blameless.

1:17:10.text: This is my covenant, which you shall keep, between me and you and your offspring after you. Every male among you shall be circumcised.
