40:17:1.text: After six days, Jesus took with him Peter, James, and John his brother, and brought them up into a high mountain by themselves.

40:17:10.text: His disciples asked him, saying, “Then why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”

40:17:11.text: Jesus answered them, “Elijah indeed comes first, and will restore all things;

40:17:12.text: but I tell you that Elijah has come already, and they didn’t recognize him, but did to him whatever they wanted to. Even so the Son of Man will also suffer by them.”

40:17:13.text: Then the disciples understood that he spoke to them of John the Baptizer.

40:17:14.text: When they came to the multitude, a man came to him, kneeling down to him and saying,

40:17:15.text: “Lord, have mercy on my son, for he is epileptic and suffers grievously; for he often falls into the fire, and often into the water.

40:17:16.text: So I brought him to your disciples, and they could not cure him.”

40:17:17.text: Jesus answered, “Faithless and perverse generation! How long will I be with you? How long will I bear with you? Bring him here to me.”

40:17:18.text: Jesus rebuked the demon, and it went out of him, and the boy was cured from that hour.

40:17:19.text: Then the disciples came to Jesus privately, and said, “Why weren’t we able to cast it out?”

40:17:2.text: He was changed before them. His face shone like the sun, and his garments became as white as the light.

40:17:20.text: He said to them, “Because of your unbelief. For most certainly I tell you, if you have faith as a grain of mustard seed, you will tell this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move; and nothing will be impossible for you.

40:17:21.text: But this kind doesn’t go out except by prayer and fasting.”

40:17:22.text: While they were staying in Galilee, Jesus said to them, “The Son of Man is about to be delivered up into the hands of men,

40:17:23.text: and they will kill him, and the third day he will be raised up.” They were exceedingly sorry.

40:17:24.text: When they had come to Capernaum, those who collected the didrachma coins came to Peter, and said, “Doesn’t your teacher pay the didrachma?”

40:17:25.text: He said, “Yes.” When he came into the house, Jesus anticipated him, saying, “What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth receive toll or tribute? From their children, or from strangers?”

40:17:26.text: Peter said to him, “From strangers.” Jesus said to him, “Therefore the children are exempt.

40:17:27.text: But, lest we cause them to stumble, go to the sea, cast a hook, and take up the first fish that comes up. When you have opened its mouth, you will find a stater coin. Take that, and give it to them for me and you.”

40:17:3.text: Behold, Moses and Elijah appeared to them talking with him.

40:17:4.text: Peter answered and said to Jesus, “Lord, it is good for us to be here. If you want, let’s make three tents here: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”

40:17:5.text: While he was still speaking, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them. Behold, a voice came out of the cloud, saying, “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Listen to him.”

40:17:6.text: When the disciples heard it, they fell on their faces, and were very afraid.

40:17:7.text: Jesus came and touched them and said, “Get up, and don’t be afraid.”

40:17:8.text: Lifting up their eyes, they saw no one, except Jesus alone.

40:17:9.text: As they were coming down from the mountain, Jesus commanded them, saying, “Don’t tell anyone what you saw, until the Son of Man has risen from the dead.”

40:18:1.text: In that hour the disciples came to Jesus, saying, “Who then is greatest in the Kingdom of Heaven?”

40:18:10.text: See that you don’t despise one of these little ones, for I tell you that in heaven their angels always see the face of my Father who is in heaven.

40:18:11.text: For the Son of Man came to save that which was lost.

40:18:12.text: “What do you think? If a man has one hundred sheep, and one of them goes astray, doesn’t he leave the ninety-nine, go to the mountains, and seek that which has gone astray?

40:18:13.text: If he finds it, most certainly I tell you, he rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine which have not gone astray.

40:18:14.text: Even so it is not the will of your Father who is in heaven that one of these little ones should perish.

40:18:15.text: “If your brother sins against you, go, show him his fault between you and him alone. If he listens to you, you have gained back your brother.

40:18:16.text: But if he doesn’t listen, take one or two more with you, that at the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established.

40:18:17.text: If he refuses to listen to them, tell it to the assembly. If he refuses to hear the assembly also, let him be to you as a Gentile or a tax collector.

40:18:18.text: Most certainly I tell you, whatever things you bind on earth will have been bound in heaven, and whatever things you release on earth will have been released in heaven.

40:18:19.text: Again, assuredly I tell you, that if two of you will agree on earth concerning anything that they will ask, it will be done for them by my Father who is in heaven.

40:18:2.text: Jesus called a little child to himself, and set him in the middle of them

40:18:20.text: For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there I am in the middle of them.”

40:18:21.text: Then Peter came and said to him, “Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? Until seven times?”

40:18:22.text: Jesus said to him, “I don’t tell you until seven times, but, until seventy times seven.

40:18:23.text: Therefore the Kingdom of Heaven is like a certain king who wanted to settle accounts with his servants.

40:18:24.text: When he had begun to settle, one was brought to him who owed him ten thousand talents.

40:18:25.text: But because he couldn’t pay, his lord commanded him to be sold, with his wife, his children, and all that he had, and payment to be made.

40:18:26.text: The servant therefore fell down and knelt before him, saying, ‘Lord, have patience with me, and I will repay you all!’

40:18:27.text: The lord of that servant, being moved with compassion, released him and forgave him the debt.

40:18:28.text: “But that servant went out and found one of his fellow servants who owed him one hundred denarii, and he grabbed him and took him by the throat, saying, ‘Pay me what you owe!’

40:18:29.text: “So his fellow servant fell down at his feet and begged him, saying, ‘Have patience with me, and I will repay you!’

40:18:3.text: and said, “Most certainly I tell you, unless you turn and become as little children, you will in no way enter into the Kingdom of Heaven.

40:18:30.text: He would not, but went and cast him into prison until he should pay back that which was due.

40:18:31.text: So when his fellow servants saw what was done, they were exceedingly sorry, and came and told their lord all that was done.

40:18:32.text: Then his lord called him in and said to him, ‘You wicked servant! I forgave you all that debt because you begged me.

40:18:33.text: Shouldn’t you also have had mercy on your fellow servant, even as I had mercy on you?’

40:18:34.text: His lord was angry, and delivered him to the tormentors until he should pay all that was due to him.

40:18:35.text: So my heavenly Father will also do to you, if you don’t each forgive your brother from your hearts for his misdeeds.”

40:18:4.text: Whoever therefore humbles himself as this little child is the greatest in the Kingdom of Heaven.

40:18:5.text: Whoever receives one such little child in my name receives me,

40:18:6.text: but whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him if a huge millstone were hung around his neck and that he were sunk in the depths of the sea.

40:18:7.text: “Woe to the world because of occasions of stumbling! For it must be that the occasions come, but woe to that person through whom the occasion comes!

40:18:8.text: If your hand or your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off and cast it from you. It is better for you to enter into life maimed or crippled, rather than having two hands or two feet to be cast into the eternal fire.

40:18:9.text: If your eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and cast it from you. It is better for you to enter into life with one eye, rather than having two eyes to be cast into the Gehenna of fire.

40:19:1.text: When Jesus had finished these words, he departed from Galilee and came into the borders of Judea beyond the Jordan.

40:19:10.text: His disciples said to him, “If this is the case of the man with his wife, it is not expedient to marry.”

40:19:11.text: But he said to them, “Not all men can receive this saying, but those to whom it is given.

40:19:12.text: For there are eunuchs who were born that way from their mother’s womb, and there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs by men; and there are eunuchs who made themselves eunuchs for the Kingdom of Heaven’s sake. He who is able to receive it, let him receive it.”

40:19:13.text: Then little children were brought to him that he should lay his hands on them and pray; and the disciples rebuked them.

40:19:14.text: But Jesus said, “Allow the little children, and don’t forbid them to come to me; for the Kingdom of Heaven belongs to ones like these.”

40:19:15.text: He laid his hands on them, and departed from there.

40:19:16.text: Behold, one came to him and said, “Good teacher, what good thing shall I do, that I may have eternal life?”

40:19:17.text: He said to him, “Why do you call me good? No one is good but one, that is, God. But if you want to enter into life, keep the commandments.”

40:19:18.text: He said to him, “Which ones?” Jesus said, “‘You shall not murder.’ ‘You shall not commit adultery.’ ‘You shall not steal.’ ‘You shall not offer false testimony.’

40:19:19.text: ‘Honor your father and your mother.’ And, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ ”

40:19:2.text: Great multitudes followed him, and he healed them there.

40:19:20.text: The young man said to him, “All these things I have observed from my youth. What do I still lack?”

40:19:21.text: Jesus said to him, “If you want to be perfect, go, sell what you have, and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me.”

40:19:22.text: But when the young man heard this, he went away sad, for he was one who had great possessions.

40:19:23.text: Jesus said to his disciples, “Most certainly I say to you, a rich man will enter into the Kingdom of Heaven with difficulty.

40:19:24.text: Again I tell you, it is easier for a camel to go through a needle’s eye than for a rich man to enter into God’s Kingdom.”

40:19:25.text: When the disciples heard it, they were exceedingly astonished, saying, “Who then can be saved?”

40:19:26.text: Looking at them, Jesus said, “With men this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.”

40:19:27.text: Then Peter answered, “Behold, we have left everything and followed you. What then will we have?”

40:19:28.text: Jesus said to them, “Most certainly I tell you that you who have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Man will sit on the throne of his glory, you also will sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

40:19:29.text: Everyone who has left houses, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my name’s sake, will receive one hundred times, and will inherit eternal life.

40:19:3.text: Pharisees came to him, testing him and saying, “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any reason?”

40:19:30.text: But many will be last who are first, and first who are last.

40:19:4.text: He answered, “Haven’t you read that he who made them from the beginning made them male and female,

40:19:5.text: and said, ‘For this cause a man shall leave his father and mother, and shall be joined to his wife; and the two shall become one flesh’ ?

40:19:6.text: So that they are no more two, but one flesh. What therefore God has joined together, don’t let man tear apart.”

40:19:7.text: They asked him, “Why then did Moses command us to give her a certificate of divorce and divorce her?”

40:19:8.text: He said to them, “Moses, because of the hardness of your hearts, allowed you to divorce your wives, but from the beginning it has not been so.

40:19:9.text: I tell you that whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, and marries another, commits adultery; and he who marries her when she is divorced commits adultery.”

40:1:1.text: The book of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham.

40:1:10.text: Hezekiah became the father of Manasseh. Manasseh became the father of Amon. Amon became the father of Josiah.

40:1:11.text: Josiah became the father of Jechoniah and his brothers at the time of the exile to Babylon.

40:1:12.text: After the exile to Babylon, Jechoniah became the father of Shealtiel. Shealtiel became the father of Zerubbabel.

40:1:13.text: Zerubbabel became the father of Abiud. Abiud became the father of Eliakim. Eliakim became the father of Azor.

40:1:14.text: Azor became the father of Zadok. Zadok became the father of Achim. Achim became the father of Eliud.

40:1:15.text: Eliud became the father of Eleazar. Eleazar became the father of Matthan. Matthan became the father of Jacob.

40:1:16.text: Jacob became the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary, from whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.

40:1:17.text: So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations; from David to the exile to Babylon fourteen generations; and from the carrying away to Babylon to the Christ, fourteen generations.

40:1:18.text: Now the birth of Jesus Christ was like this: After his mother, Mary, was engaged to Joseph, before they came together, she was found pregnant by the Holy Spirit.

40:1:19.text: Joseph, her husband, being a righteous man, and not willing to make her a public example, intended to put her away secretly.

40:1:2.text: Abraham became the father of Isaac. Isaac became the father of Jacob. Jacob became the father of Judah and his brothers.

40:1:20.text: But when he thought about these things, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying, “Joseph, son of David, don’t be afraid to take to yourself Mary as your wife, for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Spirit.

40:1:21.text: She shall give birth to a son. You shall name him Jesus, for it is he who shall save his people from their sins.”

40:1:22.text: Now all this has happened that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Lord through the prophet, saying,

40:1:23.text: “Behold, the virgin shall be with child, and shall give birth to a son. They shall call his name Immanuel,” which is, being interpreted, “God with us.”

40:1:24.text: Joseph arose from his sleep, and did as the angel of the Lord commanded him, and took his wife to himself;

40:1:25.text: and didn’t know her sexually until she had given birth to her firstborn son. He named him Jesus.

40:1:3.text: Judah became the father of Perez and Zerah by Tamar. Perez became the father of Hezron. Hezron became the father of Ram.

40:1:4.text: Ram became the father of Amminadab. Amminadab became the father of Nahshon. Nahshon became the father of Salmon.

40:1:5.text: Salmon became the father of Boaz by Rahab. Boaz became the father of Obed by Ruth. Obed became the father of Jesse.

40:1:6.text: Jesse became the father of King David. David the king became the father of Solomon by her who had been Uriah’s wife.

40:1:7.text: Solomon became the father of Rehoboam. Rehoboam became the father of Abijah. Abijah became the father of Asa.

40:1:8.text: Asa became the father of Jehoshaphat. Jehoshaphat became the father of Joram. Joram became the father of Uzziah.

40:1:9.text: Uzziah became the father of Jotham. Jotham became the father of Ahaz. Ahaz became the father of Hezekiah.

40:20:1.text: “For the Kingdom of Heaven is like a man who was the master of a household, who went out early in the morning to hire laborers for his vineyard.

40:20:10.text: When the first came, they supposed that they would receive more; and they likewise each received a denarius.

40:20:11.text: When they received it, they murmured against the master of the household,

40:20:12.text: saying, ‘These last have spent one hour, and you have made them equal to us who have borne the burden of the day and the scorching heat!’

40:20:13.text: “But he answered one of them, ‘Friend, I am doing you no wrong. Didn’t you agree with me for a denarius?

40:20:14.text: Take that which is yours, and go your way. It is my desire to give to this last just as much as to you.

40:20:15.text: Isn’t it lawful for me to do what I want to with what I own? Or is your eye evil, because I am good?’

40:20:16.text: So the last will be first, and the first last. For many are called, but few are chosen.”

40:20:17.text: As Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, he took the twelve disciples aside, and on the way he said to them,

40:20:18.text: “Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be delivered to the chief priests and scribes, and they will condemn him to death,

40:20:19.text: and will hand him over to the Gentiles to mock, to scourge, and to crucify; and the third day he will be raised up.”

40:20:2.text: When he had agreed with the laborers for a denarius a day, he sent them into his vineyard.

40:20:20.text: Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee came to him with her sons, kneeling and asking a certain thing of him.

40:20:21.text: He said to her, “What do you want?” She said to him, “Command that these, my two sons, may sit, one on your right hand and one on your left hand, in your Kingdom.”

40:20:22.text: But Jesus answered, “You don’t know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with?” They said to him, “We are able.”

40:20:23.text: He said to them, “You will indeed drink my cup, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with; but to sit on my right hand and on my left hand is not mine to give, but it is for whom it has been prepared by my Father.”

40:20:24.text: When the ten heard it, they were indignant with the two brothers.

40:21:32.text: For John came to you in the way of righteousness, and you didn’t believe him; but the tax collectors and the prostitutes believed him. When you saw it, you didn’t even repent afterward, that you might believe him.

40:21:33.text: “Hear another parable. There was a man who was a master of a household who planted a vineyard, set a hedge about it, dug a wine press in it, built a tower, leased it out to farmers, and went into another country.

40:21:34.text: When the season for the fruit came near, he sent his servants to the farmers to receive his fruit.

40:21:35.text: The farmers took his servants, beat one, killed another, and stoned another.

40:21:36.text: Again, he sent other servants more than the first; and they treated them the same way.

40:21:37.text: But afterward he sent to them his son, saying, ‘They will respect my son.’

40:21:38.text: But the farmers, when they saw the son, said among themselves, ‘This is the heir. Come, let’s kill him and seize his inheritance.’

40:21:39.text: So they took him and threw him out of the vineyard, then killed him.

40:21:4.text: All this was done that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through the prophet, saying,

40:21:41.text: They told him, “He will miserably destroy those miserable men, and will lease out the vineyard to other farmers who will give him the fruit in its season.”

40:21:42.text: Jesus said to them, “Did you never read in the Scriptures, ‘The stone which the builders rejected was made the head of the corner. This was from the Lord. It is marvelous in our eyes’ ?

40:21:43.text: “Therefore I tell you, God’s Kingdom will be taken away from you and will be given to a nation producing its fruit.

40:21:44.text: He who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces, but on whomever it will fall, it will scatter him as dust.”

40:22:23.text: On that day Sadducees (those who say that there is no resurrection) came to him. They asked him,

40:22:25.text: Now there were with us seven brothers. The first married and died, and having no offspring left his wife to his brother.

40:22:26.text: In the same way, the second also, and the third, to the seventh.

40:22:27.text: After them all, the woman died.

40:22:28.text: In the resurrection therefore, whose wife will she be of the seven? For they all had her.”

40:22:29.text: But Jesus answered them, “You are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures, nor the power of God.

40:22:3.text: and sent out his servants to call those who were invited to the wedding feast, but they would not come.

40:22:41.text: Now while the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus asked them a question,

40:23:13.text: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you devour widows’ houses, and as a pretense you make long prayers. Therefore you will receive greater condemnation.

40:23:14.text: “But woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! Because you shut up the Kingdom of Heaven against men; for you don’t enter in yourselves, neither do you allow those who are entering in to enter.

40:23:15.text: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you travel around by sea and land to make one proselyte; and when he becomes one, you make him twice as much a son of Gehenna as yourselves.

40:23:16.text: “Woe to you, you blind guides, who say, ‘Whoever swears by the temple, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gold of the temple, he is obligated.’

40:23:17.text: You blind fools! For which is greater, the gold or the temple that sanctifies the gold?

40:23:18.text: And, ‘Whoever swears by the altar, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gift that is on it, he is obligated.’

40:23:19.text: You blind fools! For which is greater, the gift, or the altar that sanctifies the gift?

40:23:2.text: saying, “The scribes and the Pharisees sit on Moses’ seat.

40:23:20.text: He therefore who swears by the altar, swears by it and by everything on it.

40:23:21.text: He who swears by the temple, swears by it and by him who has been living in it.

40:23:22.text: He who swears by heaven, swears by the throne of God and by him who sits on it.

40:23:23.text: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you tithe mint, dill, and cumin, and have left undone the weightier matters of the law: justice, mercy, and faith. But you ought to have done these, and not to have left the other undone.

40:23:24.text: You blind guides, who strain out a gnat, and swallow a camel!

40:23:25.text: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and unrighteousness.

40:23:26.text: You blind Pharisee, first clean the inside of the cup and of the platter, that its outside may become clean also.

40:23:27.text: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like whitened tombs, which outwardly appear beautiful, but inwardly are full of dead men’s bones and of all uncleanness.

40:23:28.text: Even so you also outwardly appear righteous to men, but inwardly you are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.

40:25:21.text: “His lord said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant. You have been faithful over a few things, I will set you over many things. Enter into the joy of your lord.’

40:25:22.text: “He also who got the two talents came and said, ‘Lord, you delivered to me two talents. Behold, I have gained another two talents in addition to them.’

40:25:23.text: “His lord said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant. You have been faithful over a few things. I will set you over many things. Enter into the joy of your lord.’

40:25:24.text: “He also who had received the one talent came and said, ‘Lord, I knew you that you are a hard man, reaping where you didn’t sow, and gathering where you didn’t scatter.

40:3:16.text: Jesus, when he was baptized, went up directly from the water: and behold, the heavens were opened to him. He saw the Spirit of God descending as a dove, and coming on him.

40:3:17.text: Behold, a voice out of the heavens said, “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.”

40:3:2.text: “Repent, for the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand!”

40:3:3.text: For this is he who was spoken of by Isaiah the prophet, saying, “The voice of one crying in the wilderness, make the way of the Lord ready! Make his paths straight!”

40:3:4.text: Now John himself wore clothing made of camel’s hair with a leather belt around his waist. His food was locusts and wild honey.

40:3:5.text: Then people from Jerusalem, all of Judea, and all the region around the Jordan went out to him.

40:3:6.text: They were baptized by him in the Jordan, confessing their sins.

40:3:7.text: But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming for his baptism, he said to them, “You offspring of vipers, who warned you to flee from the wrath to come?

40:3:8.text: Therefore produce fruit worthy of repentance!

40:3:9.text: Don’t think to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham for our father,’ for I tell you that God is able to raise up children to Abraham from these stones.

40:4:1.text: Then Jesus was led up by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil.

40:4:10.text: Then Jesus said to him, “Get behind me, Satan! For it is written, ‘You shall worship the Lord your God, and you shall serve him only.’ ”

40:4:11.text: Then the devil left him, and behold, angels came and served him.

40:4:12.text: Now when Jesus heard that John was delivered up, he withdrew into Galilee.

40:4:13.text: Leaving Nazareth, he came and lived in Capernaum, which is by the sea, in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali,

40:4:14.text: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying,

40:4:15.text: “The land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, toward the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles,

40:4:16.text: the people who sat in darkness saw a great light; to those who sat in the region and shadow of death, to them light has dawned.”

40:4:17.text: From that time, Jesus began to preach, and to say, “Repent! For the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand.”

40:4:18.text: Walking by the sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers: Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew, his brother, casting a net into the sea; for they were fishermen.

40:4:19.text: He said to them, “Come after me, and I will make you fishers for men.”

40:4:2.text: When he had fasted forty days and forty nights, he was hungry afterward.

40:4:20.text: They immediately left their nets and followed him.

40:4:21.text: Going on from there, he saw two other brothers, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in the boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets. He called them.

40:4:22.text: They immediately left the boat and their father, and followed him.

40:4:23.text: Jesus went about in all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, preaching the Good News of the Kingdom, and healing every disease and every sickness among the people.

40:4:24.text: The report about him went out into all Syria. They brought to him all who were sick, afflicted with various diseases and torments, possessed with demons, epileptics, and paralytics; and he healed them.

40:4:25.text: Great multitudes from Galilee, Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and from beyond the Jordan followed him.

40:4:3.text: The tempter came and said to him, “If you are the Son of God, command that these stones become bread.”

40:4:4.text: But he answered, “It is written, ‘Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of God’s mouth.’ ”

40:4:5.text: Then the devil took him into the holy city. He set him on the pinnacle of the temple,

40:4:6.text: and said to him, “If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down, for it is written, ‘He will command his angels concerning you,’ and, ‘On their hands they will bear you up, so that you don’t dash your foot against a stone.’ ”

40:4:7.text: Jesus said to him, “Again, it is written, ‘You shall not test the Lord, your God.’ ”

40:4:8.text: Again, the devil took him to an exceedingly high mountain, and showed him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory.

40:4:9.text: He said to him, “I will give you all of these things, if you will fall down and worship me.”

40:5:1.text: Seeing the multitudes, he went up onto the mountain. When he had sat down, his disciples came to him.

40:5:10.text: Blessed are those who have been persecuted for righteousness’ sake, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.

40:5:11.text: “Blessed are you when people reproach you, persecute you, and say all kinds of evil against you falsely, for my sake.

40:5:12.text: Rejoice, and be exceedingly glad, for great is your reward in heaven. For that is how they persecuted the prophets who were before you.

40:5:13.text: “You are the salt of the earth, but if the salt has lost its flavor, with what will it be salted? It is then good for nothing, but to be cast out and trodden under the feet of men.

40:5:14.text: “You are the light of the world. A city located on a hill can’t be hidden.

40:5:15.text: Neither do you light a lamp and put it under a measuring basket, but on a stand; and it shines to all who are in the house.

40:5:16.text: Even so, let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven.

40:5:17.text: “Don’t think that I came to destroy the law or the prophets. I didn’t come to destroy, but to fulfill.

40:5:18.text: For most certainly, I tell you, until heaven and earth pass away, not even one smallest letter or one tiny pen stroke shall in any way pass away from the law, until all things are accomplished.

40:5:19.text: Therefore, whoever shall break one of these least commandments and teach others to do so, shall be called least in the Kingdom of Heaven; but whoever shall do and teach them shall be called great in the Kingdom of Heaven.

40:5:2.text: He opened his mouth and taught them, saying,

40:5:20.text: For I tell you that unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, there is no way you will enter into the Kingdom of Heaven.

40:5:21.text: “You have heard that it was said to the ancient ones, ‘You shall not murder;’ and ‘Whoever murders will be in danger of the judgment.’

40:5:22.text: But I tell you that everyone who is angry with his brother without a cause will be in danger of the judgment. Whoever says to his brother, ‘Raca!’ will be in danger of the council. Whoever says, ‘You fool!’ will be in danger of the fire of Gehenna.

40:5:23.text: “If therefore you are offering your gift at the altar, and there remember that your brother has anything against you,

40:5:24.text: leave your gift there before the altar, and go your way. First be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift.

40:5:25.text: Agree with your adversary quickly while you are with him on the way; lest perhaps the prosecutor deliver you to the judge, and the judge deliver you to the officer, and you be cast into prison.

40:5:26.text: Most certainly I tell you, you shall by no means get out of there until you have paid the last penny.

40:5:27.text: “You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall not commit adultery;’

40:5:28.text: but I tell you that everyone who gazes at a woman to lust after her has committed adultery with her already in his heart.

40:5:29.text: If your right eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and throw it away from you. For it is more profitable for you that one of your members should perish than for your whole body to be cast into Gehenna.

40:5:3.text: “Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.

40:5:30.text: If your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off, and throw it away from you. For it is more profitable for you that one of your members should perish, than for your whole body to be cast into Gehenna.

40:5:31.text: “It was also said, ‘Whoever shall put away his wife, let him give her a writing of divorce,’

40:5:32.text: but I tell you that whoever puts away his wife, except for the cause of sexual immorality, makes her an adulteress; and whoever marries her when she is put away commits adultery.

40:5:33.text: “Again you have heard that it was said to the ancient ones, ‘You shall not make false vows, but shall perform to the Lord your vows,’

40:5:34.text: but I tell you, don’t swear at all: neither by heaven, for it is the throne of God;

40:5:35.text: nor by the earth, for it is the footstool of his feet; nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.

40:5:36.text: Neither shall you swear by your head, for you can’t make one hair white or black.

40:5:37.text: But let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes’ and your ‘No’ be ‘No.’ Whatever is more than these is of the evil one.

40:5:38.text: “You have heard that it was said, ‘An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth.’

40:5:39.text: But I tell you, don’t resist him who is evil; but whoever strikes you on your right cheek, turn to him the other also.

40:5:4.text: Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted.

40:5:40.text: If anyone sues you to take away your coat, let him have your cloak also.

40:5:41.text: Whoever compels you to go one mile, go with him two.

40:5:42.text: Give to him who asks you, and don’t turn away him who desires to borrow from you.

40:5:43.text: “You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’

40:5:44.text: But I tell you, love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who mistreat you and persecute you,

40:5:45.text: that you may be children of your Father who is in heaven. For he makes his sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the just and the unjust.

40:5:46.text: For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Don’t even the tax collectors do the same?

40:5:47.text: If you only greet your friends, what more do you do than others? Don’t even the tax collectors do the same?

40:5:48.text: Therefore you shall be perfect, just as your Father in heaven is perfect.

40:5:5.text: Blessed are the gentle, for they shall inherit the earth.

40:5:6.text: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be filled.

40:5:7.text: Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy.

40:5:8.text: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.

40:5:9.text: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God.

40:6:1.text: “Be careful that you don’t do your charitable giving before men, to be seen by them, or else you have no reward from your Father who is in heaven.

40:6:10.text: Let your Kingdom come. Let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven.

40:6:11.text: Give us today our daily bread.

40:6:12.text: Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors.

40:6:13.text: Bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. For yours is the Kingdom, the power, and the glory forever. Amen.’

40:6:14.text: “For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.

40:6:15.text: But if you don’t forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.

40:6:16.text: “Moreover when you fast, don’t be like the hypocrites, with sad faces. For they disfigure their faces that they may be seen by men to be fasting. Most certainly I tell you, they have received their reward.

40:6:17.text: But you, when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face,

40:6:18.text: so that you are not seen by men to be fasting, but by your Father who is in secret; and your Father, who sees in secret, will reward you.

40:6:19.text: “Don’t lay up treasures for yourselves on the earth, where moth and rust consume, and where thieves break through and steal;

40:6:2.text: Therefore, when you do merciful deeds, don’t sound a trumpet before yourself, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, that they may get glory from men. Most certainly I tell you, they have received their reward.

40:6:20.text: but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust consume, and where thieves don’t break through and steal;

40:6:21.text: for where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.

40:6:22.text: “The lamp of the body is the eye. If therefore your eye is sound, your whole body will be full of light.

40:6:23.text: But if your eye is evil, your whole body will be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in you is darkness, how great is the darkness!

40:6:24.text: “No one can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one and love the other, or else he will be devoted to one and despise the other. You can’t serve both God and Mammon.

40:6:25.text: Therefore I tell you, don’t be anxious for your life: what you will eat, or what you will drink; nor yet for your body, what you will wear. Isn’t life more than food, and the body more than clothing?

40:6:26.text: See the birds of the sky, that they don’t sow, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns. Your heavenly Father feeds them. Aren’t you of much more value than they?

40:6:27.text: “Which of you by being anxious, can add one moment to his lifespan?

40:6:28.text: Why are you anxious about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow. They don’t toil, neither do they spin,

40:6:29.text: yet I tell you that even Solomon in all his glory was not dressed like one of these.

40:6:3.text: But when you do merciful deeds, don’t let your left hand know what your right hand does,

40:6:30.text: But if God so clothes the grass of the field, which today exists and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, won’t he much more clothe you, you of little faith?

40:6:31.text: “Therefore don’t be anxious, saying, ‘What will we eat?’ , ‘What will we drink?’ or, ‘With what will we be clothed?’

40:6:32.text: For the Gentiles seek after all these things; for your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things.

40:6:33.text: But seek first God’s Kingdom and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.

40:6:34.text: Therefore don’t be anxious for tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Each day’s own evil is sufficient.

40:6:4.text: so that your merciful deeds may be in secret, then your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.

40:6:5.text: “When you pray, you shall not be as the hypocrites, for they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen by men. Most certainly, I tell you, they have received their reward.

40:6:6.text: But you, when you pray, enter into your inner room, and having shut your door, pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.

40:6:7.text: In praying, don’t use vain repetitions as the Gentiles do; for they think that they will be heard for their much speaking.

40:6:8.text: Therefore don’t be like them, for your Father knows what things you need before you ask him.

40:6:9.text: Pray like this: “‘Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy.

40:7:1.text: “Don’t judge, so that you won’t be judged.

40:7:10.text: Or if he asks for a fish, who will give him a serpent?

40:7:11.text: If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father who is in heaven give good things to those who ask him!

40:7:12.text: Therefore, whatever you desire for men to do to you, you shall also do to them; for this is the law and the prophets.

40:7:13.text: “Enter in by the narrow gate; for the gate is wide and the way is broad that leads to destruction, and there are many who enter in by it.

40:7:14.text: How narrow is the gate and the way is restricted that leads to life! There are few who find it.

40:7:15.text: “Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly are ravening wolves.

40:7:16.text: By their fruits you will know them. Do you gather grapes from thorns or figs from thistles?

40:7:17.text: Even so, every good tree produces good fruit, but the corrupt tree produces evil fruit.

40:7:18.text: A good tree can’t produce evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree produce good fruit.

40:7:19.text: Every tree that doesn’t grow good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.

40:7:2.text: For with whatever judgment you judge, you will be judged; and with whatever measure you measure, it will be measured to you.

40:7:20.text: Therefore by their fruits you will know them.

40:7:21.text: “Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter into the Kingdom of Heaven, but he who does the will of my Father who is in heaven.

40:7:22.text: Many will tell me in that day, ‘Lord, Lord, didn’t we prophesy in your name, in your name cast out demons, and in your name do many mighty works?’

40:7:23.text: Then I will tell them, ‘I never knew you. Depart from me, you who work iniquity.’

40:7:24.text: “Everyone therefore who hears these words of mine and does them, I will liken him to a wise man who built his house on the rock.

40:7:25.text: The rain came down, the floods came, and the winds blew and beat on that house; and it didn’t fall, for it was founded on the rock.

40:7:26.text: Everyone who hears these words of mine and doesn’t do them will be like a foolish man who built his house on the sand.

40:7:27.text: The rain came down, the floods came, and the winds blew and beat on that house; and it fell — and its fall was great.”

40:7:28.text: When Jesus had finished saying these things, the multitudes were astonished at his teaching,

40:7:29.text: for he taught them with authority, and not like the scribes.

40:7:3.text: Why do you see the speck that is in your brother’s eye, but don’t consider the beam that is in your own eye?

40:7:4.text: Or how will you tell your brother, ‘Let me remove the speck from your eye,’ and behold, the beam is in your own eye?

40:7:5.text: You hypocrite! First remove the beam out of your own eye, and then you can see clearly to remove the speck out of your brother’s eye.

40:7:6.text: “Don’t give that which is holy to the dogs, neither throw your pearls before the pigs, lest perhaps they trample them under their feet, and turn and tear you to pieces.

40:7:7.text: “Ask, and it will be given you. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and it will be opened for you.

40:7:8.text: For everyone who asks receives. He who seeks finds. To him who knocks it will be opened.

40:7:9.text: Or who is there among you who, if his son asks him for bread, will give him a stone?

40:8:1.text: When he came down from the mountain, great multitudes followed him.

40:8:10.text: When Jesus heard it, he marveled and said to those who followed, “Most certainly I tell you, I haven’t found so great a faith, not even in Israel.

40:8:11.text: I tell you that many will come from the east and the west, and will sit down with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the Kingdom of Heaven,

40:8:12.text: but the children of the Kingdom will be thrown out into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.”

40:8:13.text: Jesus said to the centurion, “Go your way. Let it be done for you as you have believed.” His servant was healed in that hour.

40:8:14.text: When Jesus came into Peter’s house, he saw his wife’s mother lying sick with a fever.

40:8:15.text: He touched her hand, and the fever left her. So she got up and served him.

40:8:16.text: When evening came, they brought to him many possessed with demons. He cast out the spirits with a word, and healed all who were sick,

40:8:17.text: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying, “He took our infirmities and bore our diseases.”

40:8:18.text: Now when Jesus saw great multitudes around him, he gave the order to depart to the other side.

40:8:19.text: A scribe came and said to him, “Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go.”

40:8:2.text: Behold, a leper came to him and worshiped him, saying, “Lord, if you want to, you can make me clean.”

40:8:20.text: Jesus said to him, “The foxes have holes and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.”

40:8:21.text: Another of his disciples said to him, “Lord, allow me first to go and bury my father.”

40:8:22.text: But Jesus said to him, “Follow me, and leave the dead to bury their own dead.”

40:8:23.text: When he got into a boat, his disciples followed him.

40:8:24.text: Behold, a violent storm came up on the sea, so much that the boat was covered with the waves; but he was asleep.

40:8:25.text: The disciples came to him and woke him up, saying, “Save us, Lord! We are dying!”

40:8:26.text: He said to them, “Why are you fearful, O you of little faith?” Then he got up, rebuked the wind and the sea, and there was a great calm.

40:8:27.text: The men marveled, saying, “What kind of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?”

40:8:28.text: When he came to the other side, into the country of the Gergesenes, two people possessed by demons met him there, coming out of the tombs, exceedingly fierce, so that nobody could pass that way.

40:8:29.text: Behold, they cried out, saying, “What do we have to do with you, Jesus, Son of God? Have you come here to torment us before the time?”

40:8:3.text: Jesus stretched out his hand and touched him, saying, “I want to. Be made clean.” Immediately his leprosy was cleansed.

40:8:30.text: Now there was a herd of many pigs feeding far away from them.

40:8:31.text: The demons begged him, saying, “If you cast us out, permit us to go away into the herd of pigs.”

40:8:32.text: He said to them, “Go!” They came out and went into the herd of pigs; and behold, the whole herd of pigs rushed down the cliff into the sea and died in the water.

40:8:33.text: Those who fed them fled and went away into the city and told everything, including what happened to those who were possessed with demons.

40:8:34.text: Behold, all the city came out to meet Jesus. When they saw him, they begged that he would depart from their borders.

40:8:4.text: Jesus said to him, “See that you tell nobody; but go, show yourself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.”

40:8:5.text: When he came into Capernaum, a centurion came to him, asking him for help,

40:8:6.text: saying, “Lord, my servant lies in the house paralyzed, grievously tormented.”

40:8:7.text: Jesus said to him, “I will come and heal him.”

40:8:8.text: The centurion answered, “Lord, I’m not worthy for you to come under my roof. Just say the word, and my servant will be healed.

40:8:9.text: For I am also a man under authority, having under myself soldiers. I tell this one, ‘Go,’ and he goes; and tell another, ‘Come,’ and he comes; and tell my servant, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”

40:9:1.text: He entered into a boat and crossed over, and came into his own city.

40:9:10.text: As he sat in the house, behold, many tax collectors and sinners came and sat down with Jesus and his disciples.

40:9:11.text: When the Pharisees saw it, they said to his disciples, “Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?”

40:9:12.text: When Jesus heard it, he said to them, “Those who are healthy have no need for a physician, but those who are sick do.

40:9:13.text: But you go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy, and not sacrifice,’ for I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”

40:9:14.text: Then John’s disciples came to him, saying, “Why do we and the Pharisees fast often, but your disciples don’t fast?”

40:9:15.text: Jesus said to them, “Can the friends of the bridegroom mourn as long as the bridegroom is with them? But the days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them, and then they will fast.

40:9:16.text: No one puts a piece of unshrunk cloth on an old garment; for the patch would tear away from the garment, and a worse hole is made.

40:9:17.text: Neither do people put new wine into old wineskins, or else the skins would burst, and the wine be spilled, and the skins ruined. No, they put new wine into fresh wineskins, and both are preserved.”

40:9:18.text: While he told these things to them, behold, a ruler came and worshiped him, saying, “My daughter has just died, but come and lay your hand on her, and she will live.”

40:9:19.text: Jesus got up and followed him, as did his disciples.

40:9:2.text: Behold, they brought to him a man who was paralyzed, lying on a bed. Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the paralytic, “Son, cheer up! Your sins are forgiven you.”

40:9:20.text: Behold, a woman who had a discharge of blood for twelve years came behind him, and touched the fringe of his garment;

40:9:21.text: for she said within herself, “If I just touch his garment, I will be made well.”

40:9:22.text: But Jesus, turning around and seeing her, said, “Daughter, cheer up! Your faith has made you well.” And the woman was made well from that hour.

40:9:23.text: When Jesus came into the ruler’s house and saw the flute players and the crowd in noisy disorder,

40:9:24.text: he said to them, “Make room, because the girl isn’t dead, but sleeping.” They were ridiculing him.

40:9:25.text: But when the crowd was sent out, he entered in, took her by the hand, and the girl arose.

40:9:26.text: The report of this went out into all that land.

40:9:27.text: As Jesus passed by from there, two blind men followed him, calling out and saying, “Have mercy on us, son of David!”

40:9:28.text: When he had come into the house, the blind men came to him. Jesus said to them, “Do you believe that I am able to do this?” They told him, “Yes, Lord.”

40:9:29.text: Then he touched their eyes, saying, “According to your faith be it done to you.”

40:9:3.text: Behold, some of the scribes said to themselves, “This man blasphemes.”

40:9:30.text: Then their eyes were opened. Jesus strictly commanded them, saying, “See that no one knows about this.”

40:9:31.text: But they went out and spread abroad his fame in all that land.

40:9:32.text: As they went out, behold, a mute man who was demon possessed was brought to him.

40:9:33.text: When the demon was cast out, the mute man spoke. The multitudes marveled, saying, “Nothing like this has ever been seen in Israel!”

40:9:34.text: But the Pharisees said, “By the prince of the demons, he casts out demons.”

40:9:35.text: Jesus went about all the cities and the villages, teaching in their synagogues and preaching the Good News of the Kingdom, and healing every disease and every sickness among the people.

40:9:36.text: But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion for them because they were harassed and scattered, like sheep without a shepherd.

40:9:37.text: Then he said to his disciples, “The harvest indeed is plentiful, but the laborers are few.

40:9:38.text: Pray therefore that the Lord of the harvest will send out laborers into his harvest.”

40:9:4.text: Jesus, knowing their thoughts, said, “Why do you think evil in your hearts?

40:9:5.text: For which is easier, to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven;’ or to say, ‘Get up, and walk’ ?

40:9:6.text: But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins — ” (then he said to the paralytic), “Get up, and take up your mat, and go to your house.”

40:9:7.text: He arose and departed to his house.

40:9:8.text: But when the multitudes saw it, they marveled and glorified God, who had given such authority to men.

40:9:9.text: As Jesus passed by from there, he saw a man called Matthew sitting at the tax collection office. He said to him, “Follow me.” He got up and followed him.

41:10:1.text: He arose from there and came into the borders of Judea and beyond the Jordan. Multitudes came together to him again. As he usually did, he was again teaching them.

41:10:10.text: In the house, his disciples asked him again about the same matter.

41:10:11.text: He said to them, “Whoever divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery against her.

41:10:12.text: If a woman herself divorces her husband and marries another, she commits adultery.”

41:10:13.text: They were bringing to him little children, that he should touch them, but the disciples rebuked those who were bringing them.

41:10:14.text: But when Jesus saw it, he was moved with indignation and said to them, “Allow the little children to come to me! Don’t forbid them, for God’s Kingdom belongs to such as these.

41:10:15.text: Most certainly I tell you, whoever will not receive God’s Kingdom like a little child, he will in no way enter into it.”

41:10:16.text: He took them in his arms and blessed them, laying his hands on them.

41:10:17.text: As he was going out into the way, one ran to him, knelt before him, and asked him, “Good Teacher, what shall I do that I may inherit eternal life?”

41:10:18.text: Jesus said to him, “Why do you call me good? No one is good except one — God.

41:10:19.text: You know the commandments: ‘Do not murder,’ ‘Do not commit adultery,’ ‘Do not steal,’ ‘Do not give false testimony,’ ‘Do not defraud,’ ‘Honor your father and mother.’ ”

41:10:2.text: Pharisees came to him testing him, and asked him, “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?”

41:10:20.text: He said to him, “Teacher, I have observed all these things from my youth.”

41:10:21.text: Jesus looking at him loved him, and said to him, “One thing you lack. Go, sell whatever you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me, taking up the cross.”

41:10:22.text: But his face fell at that saying, and he went away sorrowful, for he was one who had great possessions.

41:10:23.text: Jesus looked around and said to his disciples, “How difficult it is for those who have riches to enter into God’s Kingdom!”

41:10:24.text: The disciples were amazed at his words. But Jesus answered again, “Children, how hard it is for those who trust in riches to enter into God’s Kingdom!

41:10:25.text: It is easier for a camel to go through a needle’s eye than for a rich man to enter into God’s Kingdom.”

41:10:26.text: They were exceedingly astonished, saying to him, “Then who can be saved?”

41:10:27.text: Jesus, looking at them, said, “With men it is impossible, but not with God, for all things are possible with God.”

41:10:28.text: Peter began to tell him, “Behold, we have left all and have followed you.”

41:10:29.text: Jesus said, “Most certainly I tell you, there is no one who has left house, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or land, for my sake, and for the sake of the Good News,

41:10:3.text: He answered, “What did Moses command you?”

41:10:30.text: but he will receive one hundred times more now in this time: houses, brothers, sisters, mothers, children, and land, with persecutions; and in the age to come eternal life.

41:10:31.text: But many who are first will be last, and the last first.”

41:10:32.text: They were on the way, going up to Jerusalem; and Jesus was going in front of them, and they were amazed; and those who followed were afraid. He again took the twelve, and began to tell them the things that were going to happen to him.

41:10:33.text: “Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem. The Son of Man will be delivered to the chief priests and the scribes. They will condemn him to death, and will deliver him to the Gentiles.

41:10:34.text: They will mock him, spit on him, scourge him, and kill him. On the third day he will rise again.”

41:10:35.text: James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came near to him, saying, “Teacher, we want you to do for us whatever we will ask.”

41:10:36.text: He said to them, “What do you want me to do for you?”

41:10:37.text: They said to him, “Grant to us that we may sit, one at your right hand and one at your left hand, in your glory.”

41:10:38.text: But Jesus said to them, “You don’t know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I drink, and to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with?”

41:10:39.text: They said to him, “We are able.” Jesus said to them, “You shall indeed drink the cup that I drink, and you shall be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with;

41:10:4.text: They said, “Moses allowed a certificate of divorce to be written, and to divorce her.”

41:10:40.text: but to sit at my right hand and at my left hand is not mine to give, but for whom it has been prepared.”

41:10:41.text: When the ten heard it, they began to be indignant toward James and John.

41:10:42.text: Jesus summoned them and said to them, “You know that they who are recognized as rulers over the nations lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.

41:10:43.text: But it shall not be so among you, but whoever wants to become great among you shall be your servant.

41:10:44.text: Whoever of you wants to become first among you shall be bondservant of all.

41:10:45.text: For the Son of Man also came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”

41:10:46.text: They came to Jericho. As he went out from Jericho with his disciples and a great multitude, the son of Timaeus, Bartimaeus, a blind beggar, was sitting by the road.

41:10:47.text: When he heard that it was Jesus the Nazarene, he began to cry out and say, “Jesus, you son of David, have mercy on me!”

41:10:48.text: Many rebuked him, that he should be quiet, but he cried out much more, “You son of David, have mercy on me!”

41:10:49.text: Jesus stood still and said, “Call him.” They called the blind man, saying to him, “Cheer up! Get up. He is calling you!”

41:10:5.text: But Jesus said to them, “For your hardness of heart, he wrote you this commandment.

41:10:50.text: He, casting away his cloak, sprang up, and came to Jesus.

41:10:51.text: Jesus asked him, “What do you want me to do for you?” The blind man said to him, “Rabboni, that I may see again.”

41:10:52.text: Jesus said to him, “Go your way. Your faith has made you well.” Immediately he received his sight and followed Jesus on the way.

41:10:6.text: But from the beginning of the creation, God made them male and female.

41:10:7.text: For this cause a man will leave his father and mother, and will join to his wife,

41:10:8.text: and the two will become one flesh, so that they are no longer two, but one flesh.

41:10:9.text: What therefore God has joined together, let no man separate.”

41:11:1.text: When they came near to Jerusalem, to Bethsphage and Bethany, at the Mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples

41:11:10.text: Blessed is the kingdom of our father David that is coming in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!”

41:11:11.text: Jesus entered into the temple in Jerusalem. When he had looked around at everything, it being now evening, he went out to Bethany with the twelve.

41:11:12.text: The next day, when they had come out from Bethany, he was hungry.

41:11:13.text: Seeing a fig tree afar off having leaves, he came to see if perhaps he might find anything on it. When he came to it, he found nothing but leaves, for it was not the season for figs.

41:11:14.text: Jesus told it, “May no one ever eat fruit from you again!” and his disciples heard it.

41:11:15.text: They came to Jerusalem, and Jesus entered into the temple and began to throw out those who sold and those who bought in the temple, and overthrew the money changers’ tables and the seats of those who sold the doves.

41:11:16.text: He would not allow anyone to carry a container through the temple.

41:11:17.text: He taught, saying to them, “Isn’t it written, ‘My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations’ ? But you have made it a den of robbers!”

41:11:18.text: The chief priests and the scribes heard it, and sought how they might destroy him. For they feared him, because all the multitude was astonished at his teaching.

41:11:19.text: When evening came, he went out of the city.

41:11:2.text: and said to them, “Go your way into the village that is opposite you. Immediately as you enter into it, you will find a young donkey tied, on which no one has sat. Untie him and bring him.

41:11:20.text: As they passed by in the morning, they saw the fig tree withered away from the roots.

41:11:21.text: Peter, remembering, said to him, “Rabbi, look! The fig tree which you cursed has withered away.”

41:11:22.text: Jesus answered them, “Have faith in God.

41:11:23.text: For most certainly I tell you, whoever may tell this mountain, ‘Be taken up and cast into the sea,’ and doesn’t doubt in his heart, but believes that what he says is happening, he shall have whatever he says.

41:11:24.text: Therefore I tell you, all things whatever you pray and ask for, believe that you have received them, and you shall have them.

41:11:25.text: Whenever you stand praying, forgive, if you have anything against anyone; so that your Father, who is in heaven, may also forgive you your transgressions.

41:11:26.text: But if you do not forgive, neither will your Father in heaven forgive your transgressions.”

41:11:27.text: They came again to Jerusalem, and as he was walking in the temple, the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders came to him,

41:11:28.text: and they began saying to him, “By what authority do you do these things? Or who gave you this authority to do these things?”

41:11:29.text: Jesus said to them, “I will ask you one question. Answer me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.

41:11:3.text: If anyone asks you, ‘Why are you doing this?’ say, ‘The Lord needs him;’ and immediately he will send him back here.”

41:11:30.text: The baptism of John — was it from heaven, or from men? Answer me.”

41:11:31.text: They reasoned with themselves, saying, “If we should say, ‘From heaven;’ he will say, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’

41:11:32.text: If we should say, ‘From men’ ” — they feared the people, for all held John to really be a prophet.

41:11:33.text: They answered Jesus, “We don’t know.” Jesus said to them, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.”

41:11:4.text: They went away, and found a young donkey tied at the door outside in the open street, and they untied him.

41:11:5.text: Some of those who stood there asked them, “What are you doing, untying the young donkey?”

41:11:6.text: They said to them just as Jesus had said, and they let them go.

41:11:7.text: They brought the young donkey to Jesus and threw their garments on it, and Jesus sat on it.

41:11:8.text: Many spread their garments on the way, and others were cutting down branches from the trees and spreading them on the road.

41:11:9.text: Those who went in front and those who followed cried out, “Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!

41:12:1.text: He began to speak to them in parables. “A man planted a vineyard, put a hedge around it, dug a pit for the wine press, built a tower, rented it out to a farmer, and went into another country.

41:12:10.text: Haven’t you even read this Scripture: ‘The stone which the builders rejected was made the head of the corner.

41:12:11.text: This was from the Lord. It is marvelous in our eyes’ ?”

41:12:12.text: They tried to seize him, but they feared the multitude; for they perceived that he spoke the parable against them. They left him and went away.

41:12:13.text: They sent some of the Pharisees and the Herodians to him, that they might trap him with words.

41:12:14.text: When they had come, they asked him, “Teacher, we know that you are honest, and don’t defer to anyone; for you aren’t partial to anyone, but truly teach the way of God. Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar, or not?

41:12:15.text: Shall we give, or shall we not give?” But he, knowing their hypocrisy, said to them, “Why do you test me? Bring me a denarius, that I may see it.”

41:12:16.text: They brought it. He said to them, “Whose is this image and inscription?” They said to him, “Caesar’s.”

41:12:17.text: Jesus answered them, “Give to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.” They marveled greatly at him.

41:12:18.text: Some Sadducees, who say that there is no resurrection, came to him. They asked him, saying,

41:12:19.text: “Teacher, Moses wrote to us, ‘If a man’s brother dies and leaves a wife behind him, and leaves no children, that his brother should take his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.’

41:12:2.text: When it was time, he sent a servant to the farmer to get from the farmer his share of the fruit of the vineyard.

41:12:20.text: There were seven brothers. The first took a wife, and dying left no offspring.

41:12:21.text: The second took her, and died, leaving no children behind him. The third likewise;

41:12:22.text: and the seven took her and left no children. Last of all the woman also died.

41:12:23.text: In the resurrection, when they rise, whose wife will she be of them? For the seven had her as a wife.”

41:12:24.text: Jesus answered them, “Isn’t this because you are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures nor the power of God?

41:12:25.text: For when they will rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven.

41:12:26.text: But about the dead, that they are raised, haven’t you read in the book of Moses about the Bush, how God spoke to him, saying, ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’ ?

41:12:27.text: He is not the God of the dead, but of the living. You are therefore badly mistaken.”

41:12:28.text: One of the scribes came and heard them questioning together, and knowing that he had answered them well, asked him, “Which commandment is the greatest of all?”

41:12:29.text: Jesus answered, “The greatest is: ‘Hear, Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one.

41:12:3.text: They took him, beat him, and sent him away empty.

41:12:30.text: You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your mind, and with all your strength.’ This is the first commandment.

41:12:31.text: The second is like this: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ There is no other commandment greater than these.”

41:12:32.text: The scribe said to him, “Truly, teacher, you have said well that he is one, and there is none other but he;

41:12:33.text: and to love him with all the heart, with all the understanding, all the soul, and with all the strength, and to love his neighbor as himself, is more important than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.”

41:12:34.text: When Jesus saw that he answered wisely, he said to him, “You are not far from God’s Kingdom.” No one dared ask him any question after that.

41:12:35.text: Jesus responded, as he taught in the temple, “How is it that the scribes say that the Christ is the son of David?

41:12:36.text: For David himself said in the Holy Spirit, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies the footstool of your feet.”’

41:12:37.text: Therefore David himself calls him Lord, so how can he be his son?” The common people heard him gladly.

41:12:38.text: In his teaching he said to them, “Beware of the scribes, who like to walk in long robes, and to get greetings in the marketplaces,

41:12:39.text: and to get the best seats in the synagogues and the best places at feasts,

41:12:4.text: Again, he sent another servant to them; and they threw stones at him, wounded him in the head, and sent him away shamefully treated.

41:12:40.text: those who devour widows’ houses, and for a pretense make long prayers. These will receive greater condemnation.”

41:12:41.text: Jesus sat down opposite the treasury and saw how the multitude cast money into the treasury. Many who were rich cast in much.

41:12:42.text: A poor widow came and she cast in two small brass coins, which equal a quadrans coin.

41:12:43.text: He called his disciples to himself and said to them, “Most certainly I tell you, this poor widow gave more than all those who are giving into the treasury,

41:12:44.text: for they all gave out of their abundance, but she, out of her poverty, gave all that she had to live on.”

41:12:5.text: Again he sent another, and they killed him, and many others, beating some, and killing some.

41:12:6.text: Therefore still having one, his beloved son, he sent him last to them, saying, ‘They will respect my son.’

41:12:7.text: But those farmers said among themselves, ‘This is the heir. Come, let’s kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’

41:12:8.text: They took him, killed him, and cast him out of the vineyard.

41:12:9.text: What therefore will the lord of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy the farmers, and will give the vineyard to others.

41:13:1.text: As he went out of the temple, one of his disciples said to him, “Teacher, see what kind of stones and what kind of buildings!”

41:13:10.text: The Good News must first be preached to all the nations.

41:13:11.text: When they lead you away and deliver you up, don’t be anxious beforehand or premeditate what you will say, but say whatever will be given you in that hour. For it is not you who speak, but the Holy Spirit.

41:13:12.text: “Brother will deliver up brother to death, and the father his child. Children will rise up against parents and cause them to be put to death.

41:13:13.text: You will be hated by all men for my name’s sake, but he who endures to the end will be saved.

41:13:14.text: “But when you see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing where it ought not” (let the reader understand), “then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains,

41:13:15.text: and let him who is on the housetop not go down, nor enter in, to take anything out of his house.

41:13:16.text: Let him who is in the field not return back to take his cloak.

41:13:17.text: But woe to those who are with child and to those who nurse babies in those days!

41:13:18.text: Pray that your flight won’t be in the winter.

41:13:19.text: For in those days there will be oppression, such as there has not been the like from the beginning of the creation which God created until now, and never will be.

41:13:2.text: Jesus said to him, “Do you see these great buildings? There will not be left here one stone on another, which will not be thrown down.”

41:13:20.text: Unless the Lord had shortened the days, no flesh would have been saved; but for the sake of the chosen ones, whom he picked out, he shortened the days.

41:13:21.text: Then if anyone tells you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or, ‘Look, there!’ don’t believe it.

41:13:22.text: For false christs and false prophets will arise and will show signs and wonders, that they may lead astray, if possible, even the chosen ones.

41:13:23.text: But you watch. “Behold, I have told you all things beforehand.

41:13:24.text: But in those days, after that oppression, the sun will be darkened, the moon will not give its light,

41:13:25.text: the stars will be falling from the sky, and the powers that are in the heavens will be shaken.

41:13:26.text: Then they will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with great power and glory.

41:13:27.text: Then he will send out his angels, and will gather together his chosen ones from the four winds, from the ends of the earth to the ends of the sky.

41:13:28.text: “Now from the fig tree, learn this parable. When the branch has now become tender and produces its leaves, you know that the summer is near;

41:13:29.text: even so you also, when you see these things coming to pass, know that it is near, at the doors.

41:13:3.text: As he sat on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew asked him privately,

41:13:30.text: Most certainly I say to you, this generation will not pass away until all these things happen.

41:13:31.text: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.

41:13:32.text: “But of that day or that hour no one knows — not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.

41:13:33.text: Watch, keep alert, and pray; for you don’t know when the time is.

41:13:34.text: “It is like a man traveling to another country, having left his house and given authority to his servants, and to each one his work, and also commanded the doorkeeper to keep watch.

41:13:35.text: Watch therefore, for you don’t know when the lord of the house is coming — whether at evening, or at midnight, or when the rooster crows, or in the morning;

41:13:36.text: lest, coming suddenly, he might find you sleeping.

41:13:37.text: What I tell you, I tell all: Watch!”

41:13:4.text: “Tell us, when will these things be? What is the sign that these things are all about to be fulfilled?”

41:13:5.text: Jesus, answering, began to tell them, “Be careful that no one leads you astray.

41:13:6.text: For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am he!’ and will lead many astray.

41:13:7.text: “When you hear of wars and rumors of wars, don’t be troubled. For those must happen, but the end is not yet.

41:13:8.text: For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be earthquakes in various places. There will be famines and troubles. These things are the beginning of birth pains.

41:13:9.text: “But watch yourselves, for they will deliver you up to councils. You will be beaten in synagogues. You will stand before rulers and kings for my sake, for a testimony to them.

41:14:1.text: It was now two days before the Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread, and the chief priests and the scribes sought how they might seize him by deception and kill him.

41:14:10.text: Judas Iscariot, who was one of the twelve, went away to the chief priests, that he might deliver him to them.

41:14:11.text: They, when they heard it, were glad, and promised to give him money. He sought how he might conveniently deliver him.

41:14:12.text: On the first day of unleavened bread, when they sacrificed the Passover, his disciples asked him, “Where do you want us to go and prepare that you may eat the Passover?”

41:14:13.text: He sent two of his disciples and said to them, “Go into the city, and there a man carrying a pitcher of water will meet you. Follow him,

41:14:14.text: and wherever he enters in, tell the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says, “Where is the guest room, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?”’

41:14:15.text: He will himself show you a large upper room furnished and ready. Get ready for us there.”

41:14:16.text: His disciples went out, and came into the city, and found things as he had said to them, and they prepared the Passover.

41:14:17.text: When it was evening he came with the twelve.

41:14:18.text: As they sat and were eating, Jesus said, “Most certainly I tell you, one of you will betray me — he who eats with me.”

41:14:19.text: They began to be sorrowful, and to ask him one by one, “Surely not I?” And another said, “Surely not I?”

41:14:2.text: For they said, “Not during the feast, because there might be a riot among the people.”

41:14:20.text: He answered them, “It is one of the twelve, he who dips with me in the dish.

41:14:21.text: For the Son of Man goes as it is written about him, but woe to that man by whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would be better for that man if he had not been born.”

41:14:22.text: As they were eating, Jesus took bread, and when he had blessed it, he broke it and gave to them, and said, “Take, eat. This is my body.”

41:14:23.text: He took the cup, and when he had given thanks, he gave to them. They all drank of it.

41:14:24.text: He said to them, “This is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many.

41:14:25.text: Most certainly I tell you, I will no more drink of the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it anew in God’s Kingdom.”

41:14:26.text: When they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.

41:14:27.text: Jesus said to them, “All of you will be made to stumble because of me tonight, for it is written, ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.’

41:14:28.text: However, after I am raised up, I will go before you into Galilee.”

41:14:29.text: But Peter said to him, “Although all will be offended, yet I will not.”

41:14:3.text: While he was at Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper, as he sat at the table, a woman came having an alabaster jar of ointment of pure nard — very costly. She broke the jar and poured it over his head.

41:14:30.text: Jesus said to him, “Most certainly I tell you that you today, even this night, before the rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times.”

41:14:31.text: But he spoke all the more, “If I must die with you, I will not deny you.” They all said the same thing.

41:14:32.text: They came to a place which was named Gethsemane. He said to his disciples, “Sit here while I pray.”

41:14:33.text: He took with him Peter, James, and John, and began to be greatly troubled and distressed.

41:14:34.text: He said to them, “My soul is exceedingly sorrowful, even to death. Stay here and watch.”

41:14:35.text: He went forward a little, and fell on the ground, and prayed that if it were possible, the hour might pass away from him.

41:14:36.text: He said, “Abba, Father, all things are possible to you. Please remove this cup from me. However, not what I desire, but what you desire.”

41:14:37.text: He came and found them sleeping, and said to Peter, “Simon, are you sleeping? Couldn’t you watch one hour?

41:14:38.text: Watch and pray, that you may not enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.”

41:14:39.text: Again he went away and prayed, saying the same words.

41:14:4.text: But there were some who were indignant among themselves, saying, “Why has this ointment been wasted?

41:14:40.text: Again he returned and found them sleeping, for their eyes were very heavy; and they didn’t know what to answer him.

41:14:41.text: He came the third time and said to them, “Sleep on now, and take your rest. It is enough. The hour has come. Behold, the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.

41:14:42.text: Arise! Let’s get going. Behold, he who betrays me is at hand.”

41:14:43.text: Immediately, while he was still speaking, Judas, one of the twelve, came — and with him a multitude with swords and clubs, from the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders.

41:14:44.text: Now he who betrayed him had given them a sign, saying, “Whomever I will kiss, that is he. Seize him, and lead him away safely.”

41:14:45.text: When he had come, immediately he came to him and said, “Rabbi! Rabbi!” and kissed him.

41:14:46.text: They laid their hands on him and seized him.

41:14:47.text: But a certain one of those who stood by drew his sword and struck the servant of the high priest, and cut off his ear.

41:14:48.text: Jesus answered them, “Have you come out, as against a robber, with swords and clubs to seize me?

41:14:49.text: I was daily with you in the temple teaching, and you didn’t arrest me. But this is so that the Scriptures might be fulfilled.”

41:14:5.text: For this might have been sold for more than three hundred denarii and given to the poor.” So they grumbled against her.

41:14:50.text: They all left him, and fled.

41:14:51.text: A certain young man followed him, having a linen cloth thrown around himself over his naked body. The young men grabbed him,

41:14:52.text: but he left the linen cloth and fled from them naked.
