43:9:20.text: His parents answered them, “We know that this is our son, and that he was born blind;

43:9:21.text: but how he now sees, we don’t know; or who opened his eyes, we don’t know. He is of age. Ask him. He will speak for himself.”

43:9:22.text: His parents said these things because they feared the Jews; for the Jews had already agreed that if any man would confess him as Christ, he would be put out of the synagogue.

43:9:23.text: Therefore his parents said, “He is of age. Ask him.”

43:9:24.text: So they called the man who was blind a second time, and said to him, “Give glory to God. We know that this man is a sinner.”

43:9:25.text: He therefore answered, “I don’t know if he is a sinner. One thing I do know: that though I was blind, now I see.”

43:9:26.text: They said to him again, “What did he do to you? How did he open your eyes?”

43:9:27.text: He answered them, “I told you already, and you didn’t listen. Why do you want to hear it again? You don’t also want to become his disciples, do you?”

43:9:28.text: They insulted him and said, “You are his disciple, but we are disciples of Moses.

43:9:29.text: We know that God has spoken to Moses. But as for this man, we don’t know where he comes from.”

43:9:3.text: Jesus answered, “This man didn’t sin, nor did his parents, but that the works of God might be revealed in him.

43:9:30.text: The man answered them, “How amazing! You don’t know where he comes from, yet he opened my eyes.

43:9:31.text: We know that God doesn’t listen to sinners, but if anyone is a worshiper of God and does his will, he listens to him.

43:9:32.text: Since the world began it has never been heard of that anyone opened the eyes of someone born blind.

43:9:33.text: If this man were not from God, he could do nothing.”

43:9:34.text: They answered him, “You were altogether born in sins, and do you teach us?” Then they threw him out.

43:9:35.text: Jesus heard that they had thrown him out, and finding him, he said, “Do you believe in the Son of God?”

43:9:36.text: He answered, “Who is he, Lord, that I may believe in him?”

43:9:37.text: Jesus said to him, “You have both seen him, and it is he who speaks with you.”

43:9:38.text: He said, “Lord, I believe!” and he worshiped him.

43:9:39.text: Jesus said, “I came into this world for judgment, that those who don’t see may see; and that those who see may become blind.”

43:9:4.text: I must work the works of him who sent me while it is day. The night is coming, when no one can work.

43:9:40.text: Those of the Pharisees who were with him heard these things, and said to him, “Are we also blind?”

43:9:41.text: Jesus said to them, “If you were blind, you would have no sin; but now you say, ‘We see.’ Therefore your sin remains.

43:9:5.text: While I am in the world, I am the light of the world.”

43:9:6.text: When he had said this, he spat on the ground, made mud with the saliva, anointed the blind man’s eyes with the mud,

43:9:7.text: and said to him, “Go, wash in the pool of Siloam” (which means “Sent”). So he went away, washed, and came back seeing.

43:9:8.text: Therefore the neighbors and those who saw that he was blind before said, “Isn’t this he who sat and begged?”

43:9:9.text: Others were saying, “It is he.” Still others were saying, “He looks like him.” He said, “I am he.”

44:10:1.text: Now there was a certain man in Caesarea, Cornelius by name, a centurion of what was called the Italian Regiment,

44:10:10.text: He became hungry and desired to eat, but while they were preparing, he fell into a trance.

44:10:11.text: He saw heaven opened and a certain container descending to him, like a great sheet let down by four corners on the earth,

44:10:12.text: in which were all kinds of four-footed animals of the earth, wild animals, reptiles, and birds of the sky.

44:10:13.text: A voice came to him, “Rise, Peter, kill and eat!”

44:10:14.text: But Peter said, “Not so, Lord; for I have never eaten anything that is common or unclean.”

44:10:15.text: A voice came to him again the second time, “What God has cleansed, you must not call unclean.”

44:10:16.text: This was done three times, and immediately the thing was received up into heaven.

44:10:17.text: Now while Peter was very perplexed in himself what the vision which he had seen might mean, behold, the men who were sent by Cornelius, having made inquiry for Simon’s house, stood before the gate,

44:10:18.text: and called and asked whether Simon, who was also called Peter, was lodging there.

44:10:19.text: While Peter was pondering the vision, the Spirit said to him, “Behold, three men seek you.

44:10:2.text: a devout man, and one who feared God with all his house, who gave gifts for the needy generously to the people, and always prayed to God.

44:10:20.text: But arise, get down, and go with them, doubting nothing; for I have sent them.”

44:10:21.text: Peter went down to the men, and said, “Behold, I am he whom you seek. Why have you come?”

44:10:22.text: They said, “Cornelius, a centurion, a righteous man and one who fears God, and well spoken of by all the nation of the Jews, was directed by a holy angel to invite you to his house, and to listen to what you say.”

44:10:23.text: So he called them in and provided a place to stay. On the next day Peter arose and went out with them, and some of the brothers from Joppa accompanied him.

44:10:24.text: On the next day they entered into Caesarea. Cornelius was waiting for them, having called together his relatives and his near friends.

44:10:25.text: When Peter entered, Cornelius met him, fell down at his feet, and worshiped him.

44:10:26.text: But Peter raised him up, saying, “Stand up! I myself am also a man.”

44:10:27.text: As he talked with him, he went in and found many gathered together.

44:10:28.text: He said to them, “You yourselves know how it is an unlawful thing for a man who is a Jew to join himself or come to one of another nation, but God has shown me that I shouldn’t call any man unholy or unclean.

44:10:29.text: Therefore I also came without complaint when I was sent for. I ask therefore, why did you send for me?”

44:10:3.text: At about the ninth hour of the day, he clearly saw in a vision an angel of God coming to him and saying to him, “Cornelius!”

44:10:30.text: Cornelius said, “Four days ago, I was fasting until this hour; and at the ninth hour, I prayed in my house, and behold, a man stood before me in bright clothing

44:10:31.text: and said, ‘Cornelius, your prayer is heard, and your gifts to the needy are remembered in the sight of God.

44:10:32.text: Send therefore to Joppa and summon Simon, who is also called Peter. He is staying in the house of a tanner named Simon, by the seaside. When he comes, he will speak to you.’

44:10:33.text: Therefore I sent to you at once, and it was good of you to come. Now therefore we are all here present in the sight of God to hear all things that have been commanded you by God.”

44:10:34.text: Peter opened his mouth and said, “Truly I perceive that God doesn’t show favoritism;

44:10:35.text: but in every nation he who fears him and works righteousness is acceptable to him.

44:10:36.text: The word which he sent to the children of Israel, preaching good news of peace by Jesus Christ — he is Lord of all —

44:10:37.text: you yourselves know what happened, which was proclaimed throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee, after the baptism which John preached;

44:10:38.text: how God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and with power, who went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, for God was with him.

44:10:39.text: We are witnesses of everything he did both in the country of the Jews and in Jerusalem; whom they also killed, hanging him on a tree.

44:10:4.text: He, fastening his eyes on him and being frightened, said, “What is it, Lord?” He said to him, “Your prayers and your gifts to the needy have gone up for a memorial before God.

44:10:40.text: God raised him up the third day and gave him to be revealed,

44:10:41.text: not to all the people, but to witnesses who were chosen before by God, to us, who ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead.

44:10:42.text: He commanded us to preach to the people and to testify that this is he who is appointed by God as the Judge of the living and the dead.

44:10:43.text: All the prophets testify about him, that through his name everyone who believes in him will receive remission of sins.”

44:10:44.text: While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell on all those who heard the word.

44:10:45.text: They of the circumcision who believed were amazed, as many as came with Peter, because the gift of the Holy Spirit was also poured out on the Gentiles.

44:10:46.text: For they heard them speaking in other languages and magnifying God. Then Peter answered,

44:10:47.text: “Can anyone forbid these people from being baptized with water? They have received the Holy Spirit just like us.”

44:10:48.text: He commanded them to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they asked him to stay some days.

44:10:5.text: Now send men to Joppa, and get Simon, who is also called Peter.

44:10:6.text: He is staying with a tanner named Simon, whose house is by the seaside.

44:10:7.text: When the angel who spoke to him had departed, Cornelius called two of his household servants and a devout soldier of those who waited on him continually.

44:10:8.text: Having explained everything to them, he sent them to Joppa.

44:10:9.text: Now on the next day as they were on their journey and got close to the city, Peter went up on the housetop to pray at about noon.

44:11:1.text: Now the apostles and the brothers who were in Judea heard that the Gentiles had also received the word of God.

44:11:10.text: This was done three times, and all were drawn up again into heaven.

44:11:11.text: Behold, immediately three men stood before the house where I was, having been sent from Caesarea to me.

44:11:12.text: The Spirit told me to go with them without discriminating. These six brothers also accompanied me, and we entered into the man’s house.

44:11:13.text: He told us how he had seen the angel standing in his house and saying to him, ‘Send to Joppa and get Simon, who is called Peter,

44:11:14.text: who will speak to you words by which you will be saved, you and all your house.’

44:11:15.text: As I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell on them, even as on us at the beginning.

44:11:16.text: I remembered the word of the Lord, how he said, ‘John indeed baptized in water, but you will be baptized in the Holy Spirit.’

44:11:17.text: If then God gave to them the same gift as us when we believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I, that I could withstand God?”

44:11:18.text: When they heard these things, they held their peace and glorified God, saying, “Then God has also granted to the Gentiles repentance to life!”

44:11:19.text: They therefore who were scattered abroad by the oppression that arose about Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch, speaking the word to no one except to Jews only.

44:11:2.text: When Peter had come up to Jerusalem, those who were of the circumcision contended with him,

44:11:20.text: But there were some of them, men of Cyprus and Cyrene, who, when they had come to Antioch, spoke to the Hellenists, preaching the Lord Jesus.

44:11:21.text: The hand of the Lord was with them, and a great number believed and turned to the Lord.

44:11:22.text: The report concerning them came to the ears of the assembly which was in Jerusalem. They sent out Barnabas to go as far as Antioch,

44:11:23.text: who, when he had come, and had seen the grace of God, was glad. He exhorted them all, that with purpose of heart they should remain near to the Lord.

44:11:24.text: For he was a good man, and full of the Holy Spirit and of faith, and many people were added to the Lord.

44:11:25.text: Barnabas went out to Tarsus to look for Saul.

44:11:26.text: When he had found him, he brought him to Antioch. For a whole year they were gathered together with the assembly, and taught many people. The disciples were first called Christians in Antioch.

44:11:27.text: Now in these days, prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.

44:11:28.text: One of them named Agabus stood up and indicated by the Spirit that there should be a great famine all over the world, which also happened in the days of Claudius.

44:11:29.text: As any of the disciples had plenty, each determined to send relief to the brothers who lived in Judea;

44:11:3.text: saying, “You went in to uncircumcised men and ate with them!”

44:11:30.text: which they also did, sending it to the elders by the hands of Barnabas and Saul.

44:11:4.text: But Peter began, and explained to them in order, saying,

44:11:5.text: “I was in the city of Joppa praying, and in a trance I saw a vision: a certain container descending, like it was a great sheet let down from heaven by four corners. It came as far as me.

44:11:6.text: When I had looked intently at it, I considered, and saw the four-footed animals of the earth, wild animals, creeping things, and birds of the sky.

44:11:7.text: I also heard a voice saying to me, ‘Rise, Peter, kill and eat!’

44:11:8.text: But I said, ‘Not so, Lord, for nothing unholy or unclean has ever entered into my mouth.’

44:11:9.text: But a voice answered me the second time out of heaven, ‘What God has cleansed, don’t you call unclean.’

44:12:1.text: Now about that time, King Herod stretched out his hands to oppress some of the assembly.

44:12:10.text: When they were past the first and the second guard, they came to the iron gate that leads into the city, which opened to them by itself. They went out and went down one street, and immediately the angel departed from him.

44:12:11.text: When Peter had come to himself, he said, “Now I truly know that the Lord has sent out his angel and delivered me out of the hand of Herod, and from everything the Jewish people were expecting.”

44:12:12.text: Thinking about that, he came to the house of Mary, the mother of John who was called Mark, where many were gathered together and were praying.

44:12:13.text: When Peter knocked at the door of the gate, a servant girl named Rhoda came to answer.

44:12:14.text: When she recognized Peter’s voice, she didn’t open the gate for joy, but ran in and reported that Peter was standing in front of the gate.

44:12:15.text: They said to her, “You are crazy!” But she insisted that it was so. They said, “It is his angel.”

44:12:16.text: But Peter continued knocking. When they had opened, they saw him and were amazed.

44:12:17.text: But he, beckoning to them with his hand to be silent, declared to them how the Lord had brought him out of the prison. He said, “Tell these things to James and to the brothers.” Then he departed and went to another place.

44:12:18.text: Now as soon as it was day, there was no small stir among the soldiers about what had become of Peter.

44:12:19.text: When Herod had sought for him and didn’t find him, he examined the guards, then commanded that they should be put to death. He went down from Judea to Caesarea, and stayed there.

44:12:2.text: He killed James, the brother of John, with the sword.

44:12:20.text: Now Herod was very angry with the people of Tyre and Sidon. They came with one accord to him and, having made Blastus, the king’s personal aide, their friend, they asked for peace, because their country depended on the king’s country for food.

44:12:21.text: On an appointed day, Herod dressed himself in royal clothing, sat on the throne, and gave a speech to them.

44:12:22.text: The people shouted, “The voice of a god, and not of a man!”

44:12:23.text: Immediately an angel of the Lord struck him, because he didn’t give God the glory. Then he was eaten by worms and died.

44:12:24.text: But the word of God grew and multiplied.

44:12:25.text: Barnabas and Saul returned to Jerusalem when they had fulfilled their service, also taking with them John who was called Mark.

44:12:3.text: When he saw that it pleased the Jews, he proceeded to seize Peter also. This was during the days of unleavened bread.

44:12:4.text: When he had arrested him, he put him in prison and delivered him to four squads of four soldiers each to guard him, intending to bring him out to the people after the Passover.

44:12:5.text: Peter therefore was kept in the prison, but constant prayer was made by the assembly to God for him.

44:12:6.text: The same night when Herod was about to bring him out, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains. Guards in front of the door kept the prison.

44:12:7.text: And behold, an angel of the Lord stood by him, and a light shone in the cell. He struck Peter on the side and woke him up, saying, “Stand up quickly!” His chains fell off his hands.

44:12:8.text: The angel said to him, “Get dressed and put on your sandals.” He did so. He said to him, “Put on your cloak and follow me.”

44:12:9.text: And he went out and followed him. He didn’t know that what was being done by the angel was real, but thought he saw a vision.

44:13:1.text: Now in the assembly that was at Antioch there were some prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon who was called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen the foster brother of Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.

44:13:10.text: and said, “You son of the devil, full of all deceit and all cunning, you enemy of all righteousness, will you not cease to pervert the right ways of the Lord?

44:13:11.text: Now, behold, the hand of the Lord is on you, and you will be blind, not seeing the sun for a season!” Immediately a mist and darkness fell on him. He went around seeking someone to lead him by the hand.

44:13:12.text: Then the proconsul, when he saw what was done, believed, being astonished at the teaching of the Lord.

44:13:13.text: Now Paul and his company set sail from Paphos and came to Perga in Pamphylia. John departed from them and returned to Jerusalem.

44:13:14.text: But they, passing on from Perga, came to Antioch of Pisidia. They went into the synagogue on the Sabbath day and sat down.

44:13:15.text: After the reading of the law and the prophets, the rulers of the synagogue sent to them, saying, “Brothers, if you have any word of exhortation for the people, speak.”

44:13:16.text: Paul stood up, and gesturing with his hand said, “Men of Israel, and you who fear God, listen.

44:13:17.text: The God of this people chose our fathers, and exalted the people when they stayed as aliens in the land of Egypt, and with an uplifted arm, he led them out of it.

44:13:18.text: For a period of about forty years he put up with them in the wilderness.

44:13:19.text: When he had destroyed seven nations in the land of Canaan, he gave them their land for an inheritance for about four hundred fifty years.

44:13:2.text: As they served the Lord and fasted, the Holy Spirit said, “Separate Barnabas and Saul for me, for the work to which I have called them.”

44:13:20.text: After these things, he gave them judges until Samuel the prophet.

44:13:21.text: Afterward they asked for a king, and God gave to them Saul the son of Kish, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, for forty years.

44:13:22.text: When he had removed him, he raised up David to be their king, to whom he also testified, ‘I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after my heart, who will do all my will.’

44:13:23.text: From this man’s offspring, God has brought salvation to Israel according to his promise,

44:13:24.text: before his coming, when John had first preached the baptism of repentance to Israel.

44:13:25.text: As John was fulfilling his course, he said, ‘What do you suppose that I am? I am not he. But behold, one comes after me, the sandals of whose feet I am not worthy to untie.’

44:13:26.text: “Brothers, children of the stock of Abraham, and those among you who fear God, the word of this salvation is sent out to you.

44:13:27.text: For those who dwell in Jerusalem, and their rulers, because they didn’t know him, nor the voices of the prophets which are read every Sabbath, fulfilled them by condemning him.

44:13:28.text: Though they found no cause for death, they still asked Pilate to have him killed.

44:13:29.text: When they had fulfilled all things that were written about him, they took him down from the tree and laid him in a tomb.

44:13:3.text: Then, when they had fasted and prayed and laid their hands on them, they sent them away.

44:13:30.text: But God raised him from the dead,

44:13:31.text: and he was seen for many days by those who came up with him from Galilee to Jerusalem, who are his witnesses to the people.

44:13:32.text: We bring you good news of the promise made to the fathers,

44:13:33.text: that God has fulfilled this to us, their children, in that he raised up Jesus. As it is also written in the second psalm, ‘You are my Son. Today I have become your father.’

44:13:34.text: “Concerning that he raised him up from the dead, now no more to return to corruption, he has spoken thus: ‘I will give you the holy and sure blessings of David.’

44:13:35.text: Therefore he says also in another psalm, ‘You will not allow your Holy One to see decay.’

44:13:36.text: For David, after he had in his own generation served the counsel of God, fell asleep, was laid with his fathers, and saw decay.

44:13:37.text: But he whom God raised up saw no decay.

44:13:38.text: Be it known to you therefore, brothers, that through this man is proclaimed to you remission of sins;

44:13:39.text: and by him everyone who believes is justified from all things, from which you could not be justified by the law of Moses.

44:13:4.text: So, being sent out by the Holy Spirit, they went down to Seleucia. From there they sailed to Cyprus.

44:13:40.text: Beware therefore, lest that come on you which is spoken in the prophets:

44:13:41.text: ‘Behold, you scoffers! Wonder and perish, for I work a work in your days, a work which you will in no way believe, if one declares it to you.’ ”

44:13:42.text: So when the Jews went out of the synagogue, the Gentiles begged that these words might be preached to them the next Sabbath.

44:13:43.text: Now when the synagogue broke up, many of the Jews and of the devout proselytes followed Paul and Barnabas; who, speaking to them, urged them to continue in the grace of God.

44:13:44.text: The next Sabbath, almost the whole city was gathered together to hear the word of God.

44:13:45.text: But when the Jews saw the multitudes, they were filled with jealousy, and contradicted the things which were spoken by Paul, and blasphemed.

44:13:46.text: Paul and Barnabas spoke out boldly, and said, “It was necessary that God’s word should be spoken to you first. Since indeed you thrust it from yourselves, and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, behold, we turn to the Gentiles.

44:13:47.text: For so has the Lord commanded us, saying, ‘I have set you as a light for the Gentiles, that you should bring salvation to the uttermost parts of the earth.’ ”

44:13:48.text: As the Gentiles heard this, they were glad and glorified the word of God. As many as were appointed to eternal life believed.

44:13:49.text: The Lord’s word was spread abroad throughout all the region.

44:13:5.text: When they were at Salamis, they proclaimed God’s word in the Jewish synagogues. They also had John as their attendant.

44:13:50.text: But the Jews stirred up the devout and prominent women and the chief men of the city, and stirred up a persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and threw them out of their borders.

44:13:51.text: But they shook off the dust of their feet against them, and came to Iconium.

44:13:52.text: The disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.

44:13:6.text: When they had gone through the island to Paphos, they found a certain sorcerer, a false prophet, a Jew whose name was Bar Jesus,

44:13:7.text: who was with the proconsul, Sergius Paulus, a man of understanding. This man summoned Barnabas and Saul, and sought to hear the word of God.

44:13:8.text: But Elymas the sorcerer (for so is his name by interpretation) withstood them, seeking to turn the proconsul away from the faith.

44:13:9.text: But Saul, who is also called Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, fastened his eyes on him

44:14:1.text: In Iconium, they entered together into the synagogue of the Jews, and so spoke that a great multitude both of Jews and of Greeks believed.

44:14:10.text: said with a loud voice, “Stand upright on your feet!” He leaped up and walked.

44:14:11.text: When the multitude saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voice, saying in the language of Lycaonia, “The gods have come down to us in the likeness of men!”

44:14:12.text: They called Barnabas “Jupiter”, and Paul “Mercury”, because he was the chief speaker.

44:14:13.text: The priest of Jupiter, whose temple was in front of their city, brought oxen and garlands to the gates, and would have made a sacrifice along with the multitudes.

44:14:14.text: But when the apostles, Barnabas and Paul, heard of it, they tore their clothes and sprang into the multitude, crying out,

44:14:15.text: “Men, why are you doing these things? We also are men of the same nature as you, and bring you good news, that you should turn from these vain things to the living God, who made the sky, the earth, the sea, and all that is in them;

44:14:16.text: who in the generations gone by allowed all the nations to walk in their own ways.

44:14:17.text: Yet he didn’t leave himself without witness, in that he did good and gave you rains from the sky and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness.”

44:14:18.text: Even saying these things, they hardly stopped the multitudes from making a sacrifice to them.

44:14:19.text: But some Jews from Antioch and Iconium came there, and having persuaded the multitudes, they stoned Paul and dragged him out of the city, supposing that he was dead.

44:14:2.text: But the disbelieving Jews stirred up and embittered the souls of the Gentiles against the brothers.

44:14:20.text: But as the disciples stood around him, he rose up, and entered into the city. On the next day he went out with Barnabas to Derbe.

44:14:21.text: When they had preached the Good News to that city and had made many disciples, they returned to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch,

44:14:22.text: strengthening the souls of the disciples, exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that through many afflictions we must enter into God’s Kingdom.

44:14:23.text: When they had appointed elders for them in every assembly, and had prayed with fasting, they commended them to the Lord on whom they had believed.

44:14:24.text: They passed through Pisidia and came to Pamphylia.

44:14:25.text: When they had spoken the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia.

44:14:26.text: From there they sailed to Antioch, from where they had been committed to the grace of God for the work which they had fulfilled.

44:14:27.text: When they had arrived and had gathered the assembly together, they reported all the things that God had done with them, and that he had opened a door of faith to the nations.

44:14:28.text: They stayed there with the disciples for a long time.

44:14:3.text: Therefore they stayed there a long time, speaking boldly in the Lord, who testified to the word of his grace, granting signs and wonders to be done by their hands.

44:14:4.text: But the multitude of the city was divided. Part sided with the Jews and part with the apostles.

44:14:5.text: When some of both the Gentiles and the Jews, with their rulers, made a violent attempt to mistreat and stone them,

44:14:6.text: they became aware of it and fled to the cities of Lycaonia, Lystra, Derbe, and the surrounding region.

44:14:7.text: There they preached the Good News.

44:14:8.text: At Lystra a certain man sat, impotent in his feet, a cripple from his mother’s womb, who never had walked.

44:14:9.text: He was listening to Paul speaking, who, fastening eyes on him and seeing that he had faith to be made whole,

44:15:1.text: Some men came down from Judea and taught the brothers, “Unless you are circumcised after the custom of Moses, you can’t be saved.”

44:15:10.text: Now therefore why do you tempt God, that you should put a yoke on the neck of the disciples which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?

44:20:11.text: When he had gone up, had broken bread and eaten, and had talked with them a long while, even until break of day, he departed.

44:20:12.text: They brought the boy in alive, and were greatly comforted.

44:20:13.text: But we, going ahead to the ship, set sail for Assos, intending to take Paul aboard there; for he had so arranged, intending himself to go by land.

44:20:14.text: When he met us at Assos, we took him aboard and came to Mitylene.

44:20:15.text: Sailing from there, we came the following day opposite Chios. The next day we touched at Samos and stayed at Trogyllium, and the day after we came to Miletus.

44:20:16.text: For Paul had determined to sail past Ephesus, that he might not have to spend time in Asia; for he was hastening, if it were possible for him, to be in Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost.

44:20:17.text: From Miletus he sent to Ephesus and called to himself the elders of the assembly.

44:20:18.text: When they had come to him, he said to them, “You yourselves know, from the first day that I set foot in Asia, how I was with you all the time,

44:20:19.text: serving the Lord with all humility, with many tears, and with trials which happened to me by the plots of the Jews;

44:20:2.text: When he had gone through those parts and had encouraged them with many words, he came into Greece.

44:20:20.text: how I didn’t shrink from declaring to you anything that was profitable, teaching you publicly and from house to house,

44:20:21.text: testifying both to Jews and to Greeks repentance toward God and faith toward our Lord Jesus.

44:20:22.text: Now, behold, I go bound by the Spirit to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to me there;

44:20:23.text: except that the Holy Spirit testifies in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions wait for me.

44:20:24.text: But these things don’t count; nor do I hold my life dear to myself, so that I may finish my race with joy, and the ministry which I received from the Lord Jesus, to fully testify to the Good News of the grace of God.

44:20:25.text: “Now, behold, I know that you all, among whom I went about preaching God’s Kingdom, will see my face no more.

44:20:26.text: Therefore I testify to you today that I am clean from the blood of all men,

44:20:27.text: for I didn’t shrink from declaring to you the whole counsel of God.

44:20:28.text: Take heed, therefore, to yourselves and to all the flock, in which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers, to shepherd the assembly of the Lord and God which he purchased with his own blood.

44:20:29.text: For I know that after my departure, vicious wolves will enter in among you, not sparing the flock.

44:20:3.text: When he had spent three months there, and a plot was made against him by Jews as he was about to set sail for Syria, he determined to return through Macedonia.

44:20:30.text: Men will arise from among your own selves, speaking perverse things, to draw away the disciples after them.

44:20:31.text: Therefore watch, remembering that for a period of three years I didn’t cease to admonish everyone night and day with tears.

44:20:32.text: Now, brothers, I entrust you to God and to the word of his grace, which is able to build up and to give you the inheritance among all those who are sanctified.

44:20:33.text: I coveted no one’s silver, gold, or clothing.

44:20:34.text: You yourselves know that these hands served my necessities, and those who were with me.

44:20:35.text: In all things I gave you an example, that so laboring you ought to help the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that he himself said, ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’ ”

44:20:36.text: When he had spoken these things, he knelt down and prayed with them all.

44:20:37.text: They all wept freely, and fell on Paul’s neck and kissed him,

44:20:38.text: sorrowing most of all because of the word which he had spoken, that they should see his face no more. Then they accompanied him to the ship.

44:20:4.text: These accompanied him as far as Asia: Sopater of Beroea, Aristarchus and Secundus of the Thessalonians, Gaius of Derbe, Timothy, and Tychicus and Trophimus of Asia.

44:20:5.text: But these had gone ahead, and were waiting for us at Troas.

44:20:6.text: We sailed away from Philippi after the days of Unleavened Bread, and came to them at Troas in five days, where we stayed seven days.

44:20:7.text: On the first day of the week, when the disciples were gathered together to break bread, Paul talked with them, intending to depart on the next day; and continued his speech until midnight.

44:20:8.text: There were many lights in the upper room where we were gathered together.

44:20:9.text: A certain young man named Eutychus sat in the window, weighed down with deep sleep. As Paul spoke still longer, being weighed down by his sleep, he fell down from the third floor and was taken up dead.

44:21:1.text: When we had departed from them and had set sail, we came with a straight course to Cos, and the next day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.

44:21:10.text: As we stayed there some days, a certain prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.

44:21:11.text: Coming to us and taking Paul’s belt, he bound his own feet and hands, and said, “The Holy Spirit says: ‘So the Jews at Jerusalem will bind the man who owns this belt, and will deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.’ ”

44:21:12.text: When we heard these things, both we and the people of that place begged him not to go up to Jerusalem.

44:21:13.text: Then Paul answered, “What are you doing, weeping and breaking my heart? For I am ready not only to be bound, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.”

44:21:14.text: When he would not be persuaded, we ceased, saying, “The Lord’s will be done.”

44:21:15.text: After these days we took up our baggage and went up to Jerusalem.

44:21:16.text: Some of the disciples from Caesarea also went with us, bringing one Mnason of Cyprus, an early disciple, with whom we would stay.

44:21:17.text: When we had come to Jerusalem, the brothers received us gladly.

44:21:18.text: The day following, Paul went in with us to James; and all the elders were present.

44:21:19.text: When he had greeted them, he reported one by one the things which God had worked among the Gentiles through his ministry.

44:21:2.text: Having found a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, we went aboard and set sail.

44:21:20.text: They, when they heard it, glorified God. They said to him, “You see, brother, how many thousands there are among the Jews of those who have believed, and they are all zealous for the law.

44:21:21.text: They have been informed about you, that you teach all the Jews who are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children and not to walk after the customs.

44:21:22.text: What then? The assembly must certainly meet, for they will hear that you have come.

44:21:23.text: Therefore do what we tell you. We have four men who have taken a vow.

44:21:24.text: Take them and purify yourself with them, and pay their expenses for them, that they may shave their heads. Then all will know that there is no truth in the things that they have been informed about you, but that you yourself also walk keeping the law.

44:21:25.text: But concerning the Gentiles who believe, we have written our decision that they should observe no such thing, except that they should keep themselves from food offered to idols, from blood, from strangled things, and from sexual immorality.”

44:21:26.text: Then Paul took the men, and the next day purified himself and went with them into the temple, declaring the fulfillment of the days of purification, until the offering was offered for every one of them.

44:21:27.text: When the seven days were almost completed, the Jews from Asia, when they saw him in the temple, stirred up all the multitude and laid hands on him,

44:21:28.text: crying out, “Men of Israel, help! This is the man who teaches all men everywhere against the people, and the law, and this place. Moreover, he also brought Greeks into the temple and has defiled this holy place!”

44:21:29.text: For they had seen Trophimus the Ephesian with him in the city, and they supposed that Paul had brought him into the temple.

44:21:3.text: When we had come in sight of Cyprus, leaving it on the left hand, we sailed to Syria and landed at Tyre, for the ship was there to unload her cargo.

44:21:30.text: All the city was moved and the people ran together. They seized Paul and dragged him out of the temple. Immediately the doors were shut.

44:21:31.text: As they were trying to kill him, news came up to the commanding officer of the regiment that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.

44:21:32.text: Immediately he took soldiers and centurions and ran down to them. They, when they saw the chief captain and the soldiers, stopped beating Paul.

44:21:33.text: Then the commanding officer came near, arrested him, commanded him to be bound with two chains, and inquired who he was and what he had done.

44:21:34.text: Some shouted one thing and some another, among the crowd. When he couldn’t find out the truth because of the noise, he commanded him to be brought into the barracks.

44:21:35.text: When he came to the stairs, he was carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the crowd;

44:21:36.text: for the multitude of the people followed after, crying out, “Away with him!”

44:21:37.text: As Paul was about to be brought into the barracks, he asked the commanding officer, “May I speak to you?” He said, “Do you know Greek?

44:21:38.text: Aren’t you then the Egyptian who before these days stirred up to sedition and led out into the wilderness the four thousand men of the Assassins?”

44:21:39.text: But Paul said, “I am a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no insignificant city. I beg you, allow me to speak to the people.”

44:21:4.text: Having found disciples, we stayed there seven days. These said to Paul through the Spirit that he should not go up to Jerusalem.

44:21:40.text: When he had given him permission, Paul, standing on the stairs, beckoned with his hand to the people. When there was a great silence, he spoke to them in the Hebrew language, saying,

44:21:5.text: When those days were over, we departed and went on our journey. They all, with wives and children, brought us on our way until we were out of the city. Kneeling down on the beach, we prayed.

44:21:6.text: After saying goodbye to each other, we went on board the ship, and they returned home again.

44:21:7.text: When we had finished the voyage from Tyre, we arrived at Ptolemais. We greeted the brothers and stayed with them one day.

44:21:8.text: On the next day, we who were Paul’s companions departed and came to Caesarea. We entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the seven, and stayed with him.

44:21:9.text: Now this man had four virgin daughters who prophesied.

44:23:1.text: Paul, looking steadfastly at the council, said, “Brothers, I have lived before God in all good conscience until today.”

44:23:10.text: When a great argument arose, the commanding officer, fearing that Paul would be torn in pieces by them, commanded the soldiers to go down and take him by force from among them and bring him into the barracks.

44:23:11.text: The following night, the Lord stood by him and said, “Cheer up, Paul, for as you have testified about me at Jerusalem, so you must testify also at Rome.”

44:23:12.text: When it was day, some of the Jews banded together and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink until they had killed Paul.

44:23:13.text: There were more than forty people who had made this conspiracy.

44:23:14.text: They came to the chief priests and the elders, and said, “We have bound ourselves under a great curse to taste nothing until we have killed Paul.

44:23:15.text: Now therefore, you with the council inform the commanding officer that he should bring him down to you tomorrow, as though you were going to judge his case more exactly. We are ready to kill him before he comes near.”

44:23:16.text: But Paul’s sister’s son heard they were lying in wait, and he came and entered into the barracks and told Paul.

44:23:17.text: Paul summoned one of the centurions and said, “Bring this young man to the commanding officer, for he has something to tell him.”

44:23:18.text: So he took him and brought him to the commanding officer and said, “Paul, the prisoner, summoned me and asked me to bring this young man to you. He has something to tell you.”

44:23:19.text: The commanding officer took him by the hand, and going aside, asked him privately, “What is it that you have to tell me?”

44:23:2.text: The high priest, Ananias, commanded those who stood by him to strike him on the mouth.

44:23:20.text: He said, “The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul down to the council tomorrow, as though intending to inquire somewhat more accurately concerning him.

44:23:21.text: Therefore don’t yield to them, for more than forty men lie in wait for him, who have bound themselves under a curse to neither eat nor drink until they have killed him. Now they are ready, looking for the promise from you.”

44:23:22.text: So the commanding officer let the young man go, charging him, “Tell no one that you have revealed these things to me.”

44:23:23.text: He called to himself two of the centurions, and said, “Prepare two hundred soldiers to go as far as Caesarea, with seventy horsemen and two hundred men armed with spears, at the third hour of the night.”

44:23:24.text: He asked them to provide mounts, that they might set Paul on one, and bring him safely to Felix the governor.

44:23:25.text: He wrote a letter like this:

44:23:26.text: “Claudius Lysias to the most excellent governor Felix: Greetings.

44:23:27.text: “This man was seized by the Jews, and was about to be killed by them when I came with the soldiers and rescued him, having learned that he was a Roman.

44:23:28.text: Desiring to know the cause why they accused him, I brought him down to their council.

44:23:29.text: I found him to be accused about questions of their law, but not to be charged with anything worthy of death or of imprisonment.

44:23:3.text: Then Paul said to him, “God will strike you, you whitewashed wall! Do you sit to judge me according to the law, and command me to be struck contrary to the law?”

44:23:30.text: When I was told that the Jews lay in wait for the man, I sent him to you immediately, charging his accusers also to bring their accusations against him before you. Farewell.”

44:23:31.text: So the soldiers, carrying out their orders, took Paul and brought him by night to Antipatris.

44:23:32.text: But on the next day they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the barracks.

44:23:33.text: When they came to Caesarea and delivered the letter to the governor, they also presented Paul to him.

44:23:34.text: When the governor had read it, he asked what province he was from. When he understood that he was from Cilicia, he said,

44:23:35.text: “I will hear you fully when your accusers also arrive.” He commanded that he be kept in Herod’s palace.

44:23:4.text: Those who stood by said, “Do you malign God’s high priest?”

44:23:5.text: Paul said, “I didn’t know, brothers, that he was high priest. For it is written, ‘You shall not speak evil of a ruler of your people.’ ”

44:23:6.text: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, “Men and brothers, I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees. Concerning the hope and resurrection of the dead I am being judged!”

44:23:7.text: When he had said this, an argument arose between the Pharisees and Sadducees, and the crowd was divided.

44:23:8.text: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, nor angel, nor spirit; but the Pharisees confess all of these.

44:23:9.text: A great clamor arose, and some of the scribes of the Pharisees’ part stood up, and contended, saying, “We find no evil in this man. But if a spirit or angel has spoken to him, let’s not fight against God!”

44:25:1.text: Festus therefore, having come into the province, after three days went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea.

44:25:10.text: But Paul said, “I am standing before Caesar’s judgment seat, where I ought to be tried. I have done no wrong to the Jews, as you also know very well.

44:25:11.text: For if I have done wrong and have committed anything worthy of death, I don’t refuse to die; but if none of those things is true that they accuse me of, no one can give me up to them. I appeal to Caesar!”

44:25:12.text: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, “You have appealed to Caesar. To Caesar you shall go.”

44:25:13.text: Now when some days had passed, King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea and greeted Festus.

44:25:14.text: As he stayed there many days, Festus laid Paul’s case before the king, saying, “There is a certain man left a prisoner by Felix;

44:25:15.text: about whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews informed me, asking for a sentence against him.

44:25:16.text: I answered them that it is not the custom of the Romans to give up any man to destruction before the accused has met the accusers face to face and has had opportunity to make his defense concerning the matter laid against him.

44:25:17.text: When therefore they had come together here, I didn’t delay, but on the next day sat on the judgment seat and commanded the man to be brought.

44:25:18.text: When the accusers stood up, they brought no charges against him of such things as I supposed;

44:25:19.text: but had certain questions against him about their own religion and about one Jesus, who was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.

44:25:2.text: Then the high priest and the principal men of the Jews informed him against Paul, and they begged him,

44:25:20.text: Being perplexed how to inquire concerning these things, I asked whether he was willing to go to Jerusalem and there be judged concerning these matters.

44:25:21.text: But when Paul had appealed to be kept for the decision of the emperor, I commanded him to be kept until I could send him to Caesar.”

44:25:22.text: Agrippa said to Festus, “I also would like to hear the man myself.” “Tomorrow,” he said, “you shall hear him.”

44:25:23.text: So on the next day, when Agrippa and Bernice had come with great pomp, and they had entered into the place of hearing with the commanding officers and the principal men of the city, at the command of Festus, Paul was brought in.

44:25:24.text: Festus said, “King Agrippa, and all men who are here present with us, you see this man about whom all the multitude of the Jews petitioned me, both at Jerusalem and here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.

44:25:25.text: But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and as he himself appealed to the emperor, I determined to send him,

44:25:26.text: of whom I have no certain thing to write to my lord. Therefore I have brought him out before you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, that, after examination I may have something to write.

44:25:27.text: For it seems to me unreasonable, in sending a prisoner, not to also specify the charges against him.”

44:25:3.text: asking a favor against him, that he would summon him to Jerusalem, plotting to kill him on the way.

44:25:4.text: However Festus answered that Paul should be kept in custody at Caesarea, and that he himself was about to depart shortly.

44:25:5.text: “Let them therefore”, he said, “that are in power among you go down with me, and if there is anything wrong in the man, let them accuse him.”

44:25:6.text: When he had stayed among them more than ten days, he went down to Caesarea, and on the next day he sat on the judgment seat, and commanded Paul to be brought.

44:25:7.text: When he had come, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him, bringing against him many and grievous charges which they could not prove,

44:25:8.text: while he said in his defense, “Neither against the law of the Jews, nor against the temple, nor against Caesar, have I sinned at all.”

44:25:9.text: But Festus, desiring to gain favor with the Jews, answered Paul and said, “Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem and be judged by me there concerning these things?”

44:27:1.text: When it was determined that we should sail for Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan band.

44:27:10.text: and said to them, “Sirs, I perceive that the voyage will be with injury and much loss, not only of the cargo and the ship, but also of our lives.”

44:27:11.text: But the centurion gave more heed to the master and to the owner of the ship than to those things which were spoken by Paul.

44:27:12.text: Because the haven was not suitable to winter in, the majority advised going to sea from there, if by any means they could reach Phoenix and winter there, which is a port of Crete, looking southwest and northwest.

44:27:13.text: When the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, they weighed anchor and sailed along Crete, close to shore.

44:27:14.text: But before long, a stormy wind beat down from shore, which is called Euroclydon.

44:27:15.text: When the ship was caught and couldn’t face the wind, we gave way to it and were driven along.

44:27:16.text: Running under the lee of a small island called Clauda, we were able, with difficulty, to secure the boat.

44:27:17.text: After they had hoisted it up, they used cables to help reinforce the ship. Fearing that they would run aground on the Syrtis sand bars, they lowered the sea anchor, and so were driven along.

44:27:18.text: As we labored exceedingly with the storm, the next day they began to throw things overboard.

44:27:19.text: On the third day, they threw out the ship’s tackle with their own hands.

44:27:2.text: Embarking in a ship of Adramyttium, which was about to sail to places on the coast of Asia, we put to sea, Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica being with us.

44:27:20.text: When neither sun nor stars shone on us for many days, and no small storm pressed on us, all hope that we would be saved was now taken away.

44:27:21.text: When they had been long without food, Paul stood up in the middle of them and said, “Sirs, you should have listened to me, and not have set sail from Crete and have gotten this injury and loss.

44:27:22.text: Now I exhort you to cheer up, for there will be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.

44:27:23.text: For there stood by me this night an angel, belonging to the God whose I am and whom I serve,

44:27:24.text: saying, ‘Don’t be afraid, Paul. You must stand before Caesar. Behold, God has granted you all those who sail with you.’

44:27:25.text: Therefore, sirs, cheer up! For I believe God, that it will be just as it has been spoken to me.

44:27:26.text: But we must run aground on a certain island.”

44:27:27.text: But when the fourteenth night had come, as we were driven back and forth in the Adriatic Sea, about midnight the sailors surmised that they were drawing near to some land.

44:27:28.text: They took soundings and found twenty fathoms. After a little while, they took soundings again, and found fifteen fathoms.

44:27:29.text: Fearing that we would run aground on rocky ground, they let go four anchors from the stern, and wished for daylight.

44:27:3.text: The next day, we touched at Sidon. Julius treated Paul kindly and gave him permission to go to his friends and refresh himself.

44:27:30.text: As the sailors were trying to flee out of the ship and had lowered the boat into the sea, pretending that they would lay out anchors from the bow,

44:27:31.text: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, “Unless these stay in the ship, you can’t be saved.”

44:27:32.text: Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the boat and let it fall off.

44:27:33.text: While the day was coming on, Paul begged them all to take some food, saying, “Today is the fourteenth day that you wait and continue fasting, having taken nothing.

44:27:34.text: Therefore I beg you to take some food, for this is for your safety; for not a hair will perish from any of your heads.”

44:27:35.text: When he had said this and had taken bread, he gave thanks to God in the presence of all; then he broke it and began to eat.

44:27:36.text: Then they all cheered up, and they also took food.

44:27:37.text: In all, we were two hundred seventy-six souls on the ship.

44:27:38.text: When they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, throwing out the wheat into the sea.

44:27:39.text: When it was day, they didn’t recognize the land, but they noticed a certain bay with a beach, and they decided to try to drive the ship onto it.

44:27:4.text: Putting to sea from there, we sailed under the lee of Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.

44:27:40.text: Casting off the anchors, they left them in the sea, at the same time untying the rudder ropes. Hoisting up the foresail to the wind, they made for the beach.

44:27:41.text: But coming to a place where two seas met, they ran the vessel aground. The bow struck and remained immovable, but the stern began to break up by the violence of the waves.

44:27:42.text: The soldiers’ counsel was to kill the prisoners, so that none of them would swim out and escape.

44:27:43.text: But the centurion, desiring to save Paul, stopped them from their purpose, and commanded that those who could swim should throw themselves overboard first to go toward the land;

44:27:44.text: and the rest should follow, some on planks and some on other things from the ship. So they all escaped safely to the land.

44:27:5.text: When we had sailed across the sea which is off Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.

44:27:6.text: There the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing for Italy, and he put us on board.

44:27:7.text: When we had sailed slowly many days, and had come with difficulty opposite Cnidus, the wind not allowing us further, we sailed under the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.

44:27:8.text: With difficulty sailing along it we came to a certain place called Fair Havens, near the city of Lasea.

44:27:9.text: When much time had passed and the voyage was now dangerous because the Fast had now already gone by, Paul admonished them

44:28:1.text: When we had escaped, then they learned that the island was called Malta.

44:28:10.text: They also honored us with many honors; and when we sailed, they put on board the things that we needed.

44:28:11.text: After three months, we set sail in a ship of Alexandria which had wintered in the island, whose figurehead was “The Twin Brothers.”

44:28:12.text: Touching at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.

44:28:13.text: From there we circled around and arrived at Rhegium. After one day, a south wind sprang up, and on the second day we came to Puteoli,

44:28:14.text: where we found brothers, and were entreated to stay with them for seven days. So we came to Rome.

44:28:15.text: From there the brothers, when they heard of us, came to meet us as far as The Market of Appius and The Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and took courage.

44:28:16.text: When we entered into Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard, but Paul was allowed to stay by himself with the soldier who guarded him.

44:28:17.text: After three days Paul called together those who were the leaders of the Jews. When they had come together, he said to them, “I, brothers, though I had done nothing against the people or the customs of our fathers, still was delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans,

44:28:18.text: who, when they had examined me, desired to set me free, because there was no cause of death in me.

44:28:19.text: But when the Jews spoke against it, I was constrained to appeal to Caesar, not that I had anything about which to accuse my nation.

44:28:2.text: The natives showed us uncommon kindness; for they kindled a fire and received us all, because of the present rain and because of the cold.

44:28:20.text: For this cause therefore I asked to see you and to speak with you. For because of the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.”

44:28:21.text: They said to him, “We neither received letters from Judea concerning you, nor did any of the brothers come here and report or speak any evil of you.

44:28:22.text: But we desire to hear from you what you think. For, as concerning this sect, it is known to us that everywhere it is spoken against.”

44:28:23.text: When they had appointed him a day, many people came to him at his lodging. He explained to them, testifying about God’s Kingdom, and persuading them concerning Jesus, both from the law of Moses and from the prophets, from morning until evening.

44:28:24.text: Some believed the things which were spoken, and some disbelieved.

44:28:25.text: When they didn’t agree among themselves, they departed after Paul had spoken one message: “The Holy Spirit spoke rightly through Isaiah the prophet to our fathers,

44:28:26.text: saying, ‘Go to this people and say, in hearing, you will hear, but will in no way understand. In seeing, you will see, but will in no way perceive.

44:7:42.text: But God turned away and gave them up to serve the army of the sky, as it is written in the book of the prophets, ‘Did you offer to me slain animals and sacrifices forty years in the wilderness, O house of Israel?

44:7:43.text: You took up the tabernacle of Moloch, the star of your god Rephan, the figures which you made to worship, so I will carry you away beyond Babylon.’

44:7:44.text: “Our fathers had the tabernacle of the testimony in the wilderness, even as he who spoke to Moses commanded him to make it according to the pattern that he had seen;

44:7:45.text: which also our fathers, in their turn, brought in with Joshua when they entered into the possession of the nations whom God drove out before the face of our fathers to the days of David,

44:7:46.text: who found favor in the sight of God, and asked to find a habitation for the God of Jacob.

44:7:47.text: But Solomon built him a house.

44:7:48.text: However, the Most High doesn’t dwell in temples made with hands, as the prophet says,

44:7:49.text: ‘heaven is my throne, and the earth a footstool for my feet. What kind of house will you build me?’ says the Lord. ‘Or what is the place of my rest?

44:7:5.text: He gave him no inheritance in it, no, not so much as to set his foot on. He promised that he would give it to him for a possession, and to his offspring after him, when he still had no child.

44:7:50.text: Didn’t my hand make all these things?’

44:7:51.text: “You stiff-necked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, you always resist the Holy Spirit! As your fathers did, so you do.

44:7:52.text: Which of the prophets didn’t your fathers persecute? They killed those who foretold the coming of the Righteous One, of whom you have now become betrayers and murderers.

44:7:53.text: You received the law as it was ordained by angels, and didn’t keep it!”

44:7:54.text: Now when they heard these things, they were cut to the heart, and they gnashed at him with their teeth.

44:7:55.text: But he, being full of the Holy Spirit, looked up steadfastly into heaven and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing on the right hand of God,

44:7:56.text: and said, “Behold, I see the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God!”

44:7:57.text: But they cried out with a loud voice and stopped their ears, then rushed at him with one accord.

44:7:58.text: They threw him out of the city and stoned him. The witnesses placed their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul.

44:7:59.text: They stoned Stephen as he called out, saying, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit!”

44:7:6.text: God spoke in this way: that his offspring would live as aliens in a strange land, and that they would be enslaved and mistreated for four hundred years.

44:7:60.text: He kneeled down and cried with a loud voice, “Lord, don’t hold this sin against them!” When he had said this, he fell asleep.

44:7:7.text: ‘I will judge the nation to which they will be in bondage,’ said God, ‘and after that they will come out and serve me in this place.’

44:7:8.text: He gave him the covenant of circumcision. So Abraham became the father of Isaac, and circumcised him the eighth day. Isaac became the father of Jacob, and Jacob became the father of the twelve patriarchs.

44:7:9.text: “The patriarchs, moved with jealousy against Joseph, sold him into Egypt. God was with him

44:8:1.text: Saul was consenting to his death. A great persecution arose against the assembly which was in Jerusalem in that day. They were all scattered abroad throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, except for the apostles.

44:8:10.text: to whom they all listened, from the least to the greatest, saying, “This man is that great power of God.”

44:8:11.text: They listened to him because for a long time he had amazed them with his sorceries.

44:8:12.text: But when they believed Philip preaching good news concerning God’s Kingdom and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women.

44:8:13.text: Simon himself also believed. Being baptized, he continued with Philip. Seeing signs and great miracles occurring, he was amazed.

44:8:14.text: Now when the apostles who were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them,

44:8:15.text: who, when they had come down, prayed for them, that they might receive the Holy Spirit;

44:8:16.text: for as yet he had fallen on none of them. They had only been baptized in the name of Christ Jesus.

44:8:17.text: Then they laid their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.

44:8:18.text: Now when Simon saw that the Holy Spirit was given through the laying on of the apostles’ hands, he offered them money,

44:8:19.text: saying, “Give me also this power, that whomever I lay my hands on may receive the Holy Spirit.”

44:8:2.text: Devout men buried Stephen and lamented greatly over him.

44:8:20.text: But Peter said to him, “May your silver perish with you, because you thought you could obtain the gift of God with money!

44:8:21.text: You have neither part nor lot in this matter, for your heart isn’t right before God.

44:8:22.text: Repent therefore of this, your wickedness, and ask God if perhaps the thought of your heart may be forgiven you.

44:8:23.text: For I see that you are in the poison of bitterness and in the bondage of iniquity.”

44:8:24.text: Simon answered, “Pray for me to the Lord, that none of the things which you have spoken happen to me.”

44:8:25.text: They therefore, when they had testified and spoken the word of the Lord, returned to Jerusalem, and preached the Good News to many villages of the Samaritans.

44:8:26.text: Then an angel of the Lord spoke to Philip, saying, “Arise, and go toward the south to the way that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza. This is a desert.”

44:8:27.text: He arose and went; and behold, there was a man of Ethiopia, a eunuch of great authority under Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, who was over all her treasure, who had come to Jerusalem to worship.

44:8:28.text: He was returning and sitting in his chariot, and was reading the prophet Isaiah.

44:8:29.text: The Spirit said to Philip, “Go near, and join yourself to this chariot.”

44:8:3.text: But Saul ravaged the assembly, entering into every house and dragged both men and women off to prison.

44:8:30.text: Philip ran to him, and heard him reading Isaiah the prophet, and said, “Do you understand what you are reading?”

44:8:31.text: He said, “How can I, unless someone explains it to me?” He begged Philip to come up and sit with him.

44:8:32.text: Now the passage of the Scripture which he was reading was this, “He was led as a sheep to the slaughter. As a lamb before his shearer is silent, so he doesn’t open his mouth.

44:8:33.text: In his humiliation, his judgment was taken away. Who will declare His generation? For his life is taken from the earth.”

44:8:34.text: The eunuch answered Philip, “Who is the prophet talking about? About himself, or about someone else?”

44:8:35.text: Philip opened his mouth, and beginning from this Scripture, preached to him about Jesus.

44:8:36.text: As they went on the way, they came to some water; and the eunuch said, “Behold, here is water. What is keeping me from being baptized?”

44:8:38.text: He commanded the chariot to stand still, and they both went down into the water, both Philip and the eunuch, and he baptized him.

44:8:39.text: When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught Philip away, and the eunuch didn’t see him any more, for he went on his way rejoicing.

44:8:4.text: Therefore those who were scattered abroad went around preaching the word.

44:8:40.text: But Philip was found at Azotus. Passing through, he preached the Good News to all the cities until he came to Caesarea.

44:8:5.text: Philip went down to the city of Samaria and proclaimed to them the Christ.

44:8:6.text: The multitudes listened with one accord to the things that were spoken by Philip when they heard and saw the signs which he did.

44:8:7.text: For unclean spirits came out of many of those who had them. They came out, crying with a loud voice. Many who had been paralyzed and lame were healed.

44:8:8.text: There was great joy in that city.

44:8:9.text: But there was a certain man, Simon by name, who used to practice sorcery in the city and amazed the people of Samaria, making himself out to be some great one,

44:9:1.text: But Saul, still breathing threats and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord, went to the high priest

44:9:10.text: Now there was a certain disciple at Damascus named Ananias. The Lord said to him in a vision, “Ananias!” He said, “Behold, it’s me, Lord.”

44:9:11.text: The Lord said to him, “Arise and go to the street which is called Straight, and inquire in the house of Judah for one named Saul, a man of Tarsus. For behold, he is praying,

44:9:12.text: and in a vision he has seen a man named Ananias coming in and laying his hands on him, that he might receive his sight.”

44:9:13.text: But Ananias answered, “Lord, I have heard from many about this man, how much evil he did to your saints at Jerusalem.

44:9:14.text: Here he has authority from the chief priests to bind all who call on your name.”

44:9:15.text: But the Lord said to him, “Go your way, for he is my chosen vessel to bear my name before the nations and kings, and the children of Israel.

44:9:16.text: For I will show him how many things he must suffer for my name’s sake.”

44:9:17.text: Ananias departed and entered into the house. Laying his hands on him, he said, “Brother Saul, the Lord, who appeared to you on the road by which you came, has sent me that you may receive your sight and be filled with the Holy Spirit.”

44:9:18.text: Immediately something like scales fell from his eyes, and he received his sight. He arose and was baptized.

44:9:19.text: He took food and was strengthened. Saul stayed several days with the disciples who were at Damascus.

44:9:2.text: and asked for letters from him to the synagogues of Damascus, that if he found any who were of the Way, whether men or women, he might bring them bound to Jerusalem.

44:9:20.text: Immediately in the synagogues he proclaimed the Christ, that he is the Son of God.

44:9:21.text: All who heard him were amazed, and said, “Isn’t this he who in Jerusalem made havoc of those who called on this name? And he had come here intending to bring them bound before the chief priests!”

44:9:22.text: But Saul increased more in strength, and confounded the Jews who lived at Damascus, proving that this is the Christ.

44:9:23.text: When many days were fulfilled, the Jews conspired together to kill him,

44:9:24.text: but their plot became known to Saul. They watched the gates both day and night that they might kill him,

44:9:25.text: but his disciples took him by night and let him down through the wall, lowering him in a basket.

44:9:26.text: When Saul had come to Jerusalem, he tried to join himself to the disciples; but they were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple.

44:9:27.text: But Barnabas took him and brought him to the apostles, and declared to them how he had seen the Lord on the way, and that he had spoken to him, and how at Damascus he had preached boldly in the name of Jesus.

44:9:28.text: He was with them entering into Jerusalem,

44:9:29.text: preaching boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus. He spoke and disputed against the Hellenists, but they were seeking to kill him.

44:9:3.text: As he traveled, he got close to Damascus, and suddenly a light from the sky shone around him.

44:9:30.text: When the brothers knew it, they brought him down to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus.

44:9:31.text: So the assemblies throughout all Judea, Galilee, and Samaria had peace and were built up. They were multiplied, walking in the fear of the Lord and in the comfort of the Holy Spirit.

44:9:32.text: As Peter went throughout all those parts, he came down also to the saints who lived at Lydda.

44:9:33.text: There he found a certain man named Aeneas, who had been bedridden for eight years because he was paralyzed.

44:9:34.text: Peter said to him, “Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you. Get up and make your bed!” Immediately he arose.

44:9:35.text: All who lived at Lydda and in Sharon saw him, and they turned to the Lord.

44:9:36.text: Now there was at Joppa a certain disciple named Tabitha, which when translated means Dorcas. This woman was full of good works and acts of mercy which she did.

44:9:37.text: In those days, she became sick and died. When they had washed her, they laid her in an upper room.

44:9:38.text: As Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples, hearing that Peter was there, sent two men to him, imploring him not to delay in coming to them.

44:9:39.text: Peter got up and went with them. When he had come, they brought him into the upper room. All the widows stood by him weeping, and showing the tunics and other garments which Dorcas had made while she was with them.

44:9:4.text: He fell on the earth, and heard a voice saying to him, “Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?”

44:9:40.text: Peter sent them all out, and knelt down and prayed. Turning to the body, he said, “Tabitha, get up!” She opened her eyes, and when she saw Peter, she sat up.

44:9:41.text: He gave her his hand and raised her up. Calling the saints and widows, he presented her alive.

44:9:42.text: This became known throughout all Joppa, and many believed in the Lord.

44:9:43.text: He stayed many days in Joppa with a tanner named Simon.

44:9:5.text: He said, “Who are you, Lord?” The Lord said, “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.

44:9:6.text: But rise up and enter into the city, then you will be told what you must do.”

44:9:7.text: The men who traveled with him stood speechless, hearing the sound, but seeing no one.

44:9:8.text: Saul arose from the ground, and when his eyes were opened, he saw no one. They led him by the hand and brought him into Damascus.

44:9:9.text: He was without sight for three days, and neither ate nor drank.

45:10:1.text: Brothers, my heart’s desire and my prayer to God is for Israel, that they may be saved.

45:10:10.text: For with the heart one believes resulting in righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made resulting in salvation.

45:10:11.text: For the Scripture says, “Whoever believes in him will not be disappointed.”

45:10:12.text: For there is no distinction between Jew and Greek; for the same Lord is Lord of all, and is rich to all who call on him.

45:10:13.text: For, “Whoever will call on the name of the Lord will be saved.”

45:10:14.text: How then will they call on him in whom they have not believed? How will they believe in him whom they have not heard? How will they hear without a preacher?

45:10:15.text: And how will they preach unless they are sent? As it is written: “How beautiful are the feet of those who preach the Good News of peace, who bring glad tidings of good things!”

45:10:16.text: But they didn’t all listen to the glad news. For Isaiah says, “Lord, who has believed our report?”

45:10:17.text: So faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.

45:10:18.text: But I say, didn’t they hear? Yes, most certainly, “Their sound went out into all the earth, their words to the ends of the world.”

45:10:19.text: But I ask, didn’t Israel know? First Moses says, “I will provoke you to jealousy with that which is no nation. I will make you angry with a nation void of understanding.”

45:10:2.text: For I testify about them that they have a zeal for God, but not according to knowledge.

45:10:20.text: Isaiah is very bold and says, “I was found by those who didn’t seek me. I was revealed to those who didn’t ask for me.”

45:10:21.text: But about Israel he says, “All day long I stretched out my hands to a disobedient and contrary people.”

45:10:3.text: For being ignorant of God’s righteousness, and seeking to establish their own righteousness, they didn’t subject themselves to the righteousness of God.

45:10:4.text: For Christ is the fulfillment of the law for righteousness to everyone who believes.

45:10:5.text: For Moses writes about the righteousness of the law, “The one who does them will live by them.”

45:10:6.text: But the righteousness which is of faith says this, “Don’t say in your heart, ‘Who will ascend into heaven?’ (that is, to bring Christ down);

45:10:7.text: or, ‘Who will descend into the abyss?’ (that is, to bring Christ up from the dead.)”

45:10:8.text: But what does it say? “The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart;” that is, the word of faith which we preach:

45:10:9.text: that if you will confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.

45:11:1.text: I ask then, did God reject his people? May it never be! For I also am an Israelite, a descendant of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.

45:11:10.text: Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see. Always keep their backs bent.”

45:11:11.text: I ask then, did they stumble that they might fall? May it never be! But by their fall salvation has come to the Gentiles, to provoke them to jealousy.

45:11:12.text: Now if their fall is the riches of the world, and their loss the riches of the Gentiles, how much more their fullness!

45:11:13.text: For I speak to you who are Gentiles. Since then as I am an apostle to Gentiles, I glorify my ministry,

45:11:14.text: if by any means I may provoke to jealousy those who are my flesh, and may save some of them.

45:11:15.text: For if the rejection of them is the reconciling of the world, what would their acceptance be, but life from the dead?

45:11:16.text: If the first fruit is holy, so is the lump. If the root is holy, so are the branches.

45:11:17.text: But if some of the branches were broken off, and you, being a wild olive, were grafted in among them and became partaker with them of the root and of the richness of the olive tree,

45:11:18.text: don’t boast over the branches. But if you boast, remember that it is not you who support the root, but the root supports you.

45:11:19.text: You will say then, “Branches were broken off, that I might be grafted in.”

45:11:2.text: God didn’t reject his people, whom he foreknew. Or don’t you know what the Scripture says about Elijah? How he pleads with God against Israel:

45:11:20.text: True; by their unbelief they were broken off, and you stand by your faith. Don’t be conceited, but fear;

45:11:21.text: for if God didn’t spare the natural branches, neither will he spare you.

45:11:22.text: See then the goodness and severity of God. Toward those who fell, severity; but toward you, goodness, if you continue in his goodness; otherwise you also will be cut off.

45:11:23.text: They also, if they don’t continue in their unbelief, will be grafted in, for God is able to graft them in again.

45:11:24.text: For if you were cut out of that which is by nature a wild olive tree, and were grafted contrary to nature into a good olive tree, how much more will these, which are the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree?

45:11:25.text: For I don’t desire you to be ignorant, brothers, of this mystery, so that you won’t be wise in your own conceits, that a partial hardening has happened to Israel, until the fullness of the Gentiles has come in,

45:11:26.text: and so all Israel will be saved. Even as it is written, “There will come out of Zion the Deliverer, and he will turn away ungodliness from Jacob.

45:11:27.text: This is my covenant with them, when I will take away their sins.”

45:11:28.text: Concerning the Good News, they are enemies for your sake. But concerning the election, they are beloved for the fathers’ sake.

45:11:29.text: For the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable.

45:11:3.text: “Lord, they have killed your prophets. They have broken down your altars. I am left alone, and they seek my life.”

45:11:30.text: For as you in time past were disobedient to God, but now have obtained mercy by their disobedience,

45:11:31.text: even so these also have now been disobedient, that by the mercy shown to you they may also obtain mercy.

45:11:32.text: For God has bound all to disobedience, that he might have mercy on all.

45:11:33.text: Oh the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and the knowledge of God! How unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past tracing out!

45:11:34.text: “For who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who has been his counselor?”

45:11:35.text: “Or who has first given to him, and it will be repaid to him again?”

45:11:36.text: For of him and through him and to him are all things. To him be the glory for ever! Amen.

45:11:4.text: But how does God answer him? “I have reserved for myself seven thousand men who have not bowed the knee to Baal.”

45:11:5.text: Even so too at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace.

45:11:6.text: And if by grace, then it is no longer of works; otherwise grace is no longer grace. But if it is of works, it is no longer grace; otherwise work is no longer work.

45:11:7.text: What then? That which Israel seeks for, that he didn’t obtain, but the chosen ones obtained it, and the rest were hardened.

45:11:8.text: According as it is written, “God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that they should not see, and ears that they should not hear, to this very day.”

45:11:9.text: David says, “Let their table be made a snare, a trap, a stumbling block, and a retribution to them.

45:12:1.text: Therefore I urge you, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is your spiritual service.

45:12:10.text: In love of the brothers be tenderly affectionate to one another; in honor prefer one another,

45:12:11.text: not lagging in diligence, fervent in spirit, serving the Lord,
