46:1:3.text: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

46:1:30.text: Because of him, you are in Christ Jesus, who was made to us wisdom from God, and righteousness and sanctification, and redemption,

46:1:31.text: that, as it is written, “He who boasts, let him boast in the Lord.”

46:1:4.text: I always thank my God concerning you for the grace of God which was given you in Christ Jesus,

46:1:5.text: that in everything you were enriched in him, in all speech and all knowledge —

46:1:6.text: even as the testimony of Christ was confirmed in you —

46:1:7.text: so that you come behind in no gift, waiting for the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ,

46:1:8.text: who will also confirm you until the end, blameless in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.

46:1:9.text: God is faithful, through whom you were called into the fellowship of his Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.

46:2:1.text: When I came to you, brothers, I didn’t come with excellence of speech or of wisdom, proclaiming to you the testimony of God.

46:2:10.text: But to us, God revealed them through the Spirit. For the Spirit searches all things, yes, the deep things of God.

46:2:11.text: For who among men knows the things of a man except the spirit of the man which is in him? Even so, no one knows the things of God except God’s Spirit.

46:2:12.text: But we received not the spirit of the world, but the Spirit which is from God, that we might know the things that were freely given to us by God.

46:2:13.text: We also speak these things, not in words which man’s wisdom teaches but which the Holy Spirit teaches, comparing spiritual things with spiritual things.

46:2:14.text: Now the natural man doesn’t receive the things of God’s Spirit, for they are foolishness to him; and he can’t know them, because they are spiritually discerned.

46:2:15.text: But he who is spiritual discerns all things, and he himself is to be judged by no one.

46:2:16.text: “For who has known the mind of the Lord that he should instruct him?” But we have Christ’s mind.

46:2:2.text: For I determined not to know anything among you except Jesus Christ and him crucified.

46:2:3.text: I was with you in weakness, in fear, and in much trembling.

46:2:4.text: My speech and my preaching were not in persuasive words of human wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power,

46:2:5.text: that your faith wouldn’t stand in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God.

46:2:6.text: We speak wisdom, however, among those who are full grown, yet a wisdom not of this world nor of the rulers of this world who are coming to nothing.

46:2:7.text: But we speak God’s wisdom in a mystery, the wisdom that has been hidden, which God foreordained before the worlds for our glory,

46:2:8.text: which none of the rulers of this world has known. For had they known it, they wouldn’t have crucified the Lord of glory.

46:2:9.text: But as it is written, “Things which an eye didn’t see, and an ear didn’t hear, which didn’t enter into the heart of man, these God has prepared for those who love him.”

46:3:1.text: Brothers, I couldn’t speak to you as to spiritual, but as to fleshly, as to babies in Christ.

46:3:10.text: According to the grace of God which was given to me, as a wise master builder I laid a foundation, and another builds on it. But let each man be careful how he builds on it.

46:3:11.text: For no one can lay any other foundation than that which has been laid, which is Jesus Christ.

46:3:12.text: But if anyone builds on the foundation with gold, silver, costly stones, wood, hay, or straw,

46:3:13.text: each man’s work will be revealed. For the Day will declare it, because it is revealed in fire; and the fire itself will test what sort of work each man’s work is.

46:3:14.text: If any man’s work remains which he built on it, he will receive a reward.

46:3:15.text: If any man’s work is burned, he will suffer loss, but he himself will be saved, but as through fire.

46:3:16.text: Don’t you know that you are God’s temple and that God’s Spirit lives in you?

46:3:17.text: If anyone destroys God’s temple, God will destroy him; for God’s temple is holy, which you are.

46:3:18.text: Let no one deceive himself. If anyone thinks that he is wise among you in this world, let him become a fool that he may become wise.

46:3:19.text: For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God. For it is written, “He has taken the wise in their craftiness.”

46:3:2.text: I fed you with milk, not with solid food, for you weren’t yet ready. Indeed, you aren’t ready even now,

46:3:20.text: And again, “The Lord knows the reasoning of the wise, that it is worthless.”

46:3:21.text: Therefore let no one boast in men. For all things are yours,

46:3:22.text: whether Paul, or Apollos, or Cephas, or the world, or life, or death, or things present, or things to come. All are yours,

46:3:23.text: and you are Christ’s, and Christ is God’s.

46:3:3.text: for you are still fleshly. For insofar as there is jealousy, strife, and factions among you, aren’t you fleshly, and don’t you walk in the ways of men?

46:3:4.text: For when one says, “I follow Paul,” and another, “I follow Apollos,” aren’t you fleshly?

46:3:5.text: Who then is Apollos, and who is Paul, but servants through whom you believed, and each as the Lord gave to him?

46:3:6.text: I planted. Apollos watered. But God gave the increase.

46:3:7.text: So then neither he who plants is anything, nor he who waters, but God who gives the increase.

46:3:8.text: Now he who plants and he who waters are the same, but each will receive his own reward according to his own labor.

46:3:9.text: For we are God’s fellow workers. You are God’s farming, God’s building.

46:4:1.text: So let a man think of us as Christ’s servants and stewards of God’s mysteries.

46:4:10.text: We are fools for Christ’s sake, but you are wise in Christ. We are weak, but you are strong. You have honor, but we have dishonor.

46:4:11.text: Even to this present hour we hunger, thirst, are naked, are beaten, and have no certain dwelling place.

46:4:12.text: We toil, working with our own hands. When people curse us, we bless. Being persecuted, we endure.

46:4:13.text: Being defamed, we entreat. We are made as the filth of the world, the dirt wiped off by all, even until now.

46:4:14.text: I don’t write these things to shame you, but to admonish you as my beloved children.

46:4:15.text: For though you have ten thousand tutors in Christ, you don’t have many fathers. For in Christ Jesus, I became your father through the Good News.

46:4:16.text: I beg you therefore, be imitators of me.

46:4:17.text: Because of this I have sent Timothy to you, who is my beloved and faithful child in the Lord, who will remind you of my ways which are in Christ, even as I teach everywhere in every assembly.

46:4:18.text: Now some are puffed up, as though I were not coming to you.

46:4:19.text: But I will come to you shortly, if the Lord is willing. And I will know, not the word of those who are puffed up, but the power.

46:4:2.text: Here, moreover, it is required of stewards that they be found faithful.

46:4:20.text: For God’s Kingdom is not in word, but in power.

46:4:21.text: What do you want? Shall I come to you with a rod, or in love and a spirit of gentleness?

46:4:3.text: But with me it is a very small thing that I should be judged by you, or by a human court. Yes, I don’t even judge my own self.

46:4:4.text: For I know nothing against myself. Yet I am not justified by this, but he who judges me is the Lord.

46:4:5.text: Therefore judge nothing before the time, until the Lord comes, who will both bring to light the hidden things of darkness and reveal the counsels of the hearts. Then each man will get his praise from God.

46:4:6.text: Now these things, brothers, I have in a figure transferred to myself and Apollos for your sakes, that in us you might learn not to think beyond the things which are written, that none of you be puffed up against one another.

46:4:7.text: For who makes you different? And what do you have that you didn’t receive? But if you did receive it, why do you boast as if you had not received it?

46:4:8.text: You are already filled. You have already become rich. You have come to reign without us. Yes, and I wish that you did reign, that we also might reign with you!

46:4:9.text: For I think that God has displayed us, the apostles, last of all, like men sentenced to death. For we are made a spectacle to the world, both to angels and men.

46:5:1.text: It is actually reported that there is sexual immorality among you, and such sexual immorality as is not even named among the Gentiles, that one has his father’s wife.

46:5:10.text: yet not at all meaning with the sexual sinners of this world, or with the covetous and extortionists, or with idolaters, for then you would have to leave the world.

46:5:11.text: But as it is, I wrote to you not to associate with anyone who is called a brother who is a sexual sinner, or covetous, or an idolater, or a slanderer, or a drunkard, or an extortionist. Don’t even eat with such a person.

46:5:12.text: For what do I have to do with also judging those who are outside? Don’t you judge those who are within?

46:5:13.text: But those who are outside, God judges. “Put away the wicked man from among yourselves.”

46:5:2.text: You are arrogant, and didn’t mourn instead, that he who had done this deed might be removed from among you.

46:5:3.text: For I most certainly, as being absent in body but present in spirit, have already, as though I were present, judged him who has done this thing.

46:5:4.text: In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, when you are gathered together with my spirit with the power of our Lord Jesus Christ,

46:5:5.text: you are to deliver such a one to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus.

46:5:6.text: Your boasting is not good. Don’t you know that a little yeast leavens the whole lump?

46:5:7.text: Purge out the old yeast, that you may be a new lump, even as you are unleavened. For indeed Christ, our Passover, has been sacrificed in our place.

46:5:8.text: Therefore let’s keep the feast, not with old yeast, neither with the yeast of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.

46:5:9.text: I wrote to you in my letter to have no company with sexual sinners;

46:6:1.text: Dare any of you, having a matter against his neighbor, go to law before the unrighteous, and not before the saints?

46:6:10.text: nor thieves, nor covetous, nor drunkards, nor slanderers, nor extortionists, will inherit God’s Kingdom.

46:6:11.text: Some of you were such, but you were washed. You were sanctified. You were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus, and in the Spirit of our God.

46:6:12.text: “All things are lawful for me,” but not all things are expedient. “All things are lawful for me,” but I will not be brought under the power of anything.

46:6:13.text: “Foods for the belly, and the belly for foods,” but God will bring to nothing both it and them. But the body is not for sexual immorality, but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.

46:6:14.text: Now God raised up the Lord, and will also raise us up by his power.

46:6:15.text: Don’t you know that your bodies are members of Christ? Shall I then take the members of Christ and make them members of a prostitute? May it never be!

46:6:16.text: Or don’t you know that he who is joined to a prostitute is one body? For, “The two”, he says, “will become one flesh.”

46:6:17.text: But he who is joined to the Lord is one spirit.

46:6:18.text: Flee sexual immorality! “Every sin that a man does is outside the body,” but he who commits sexual immorality sins against his own body.

46:6:19.text: Or don’t you know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have from God? You are not your own,

46:6:2.text: Don’t you know that the saints will judge the world? And if the world is judged by you, are you unworthy to judge the smallest matters?

46:6:20.text: for you were bought with a price. Therefore glorify God in your body and in your spirit, which are God’s.

46:6:3.text: Don’t you know that we will judge angels? How much more, things that pertain to this life?

46:6:4.text: If then you have to judge things pertaining to this life, do you set them to judge who are of no account in the assembly?

46:6:5.text: I say this to move you to shame. Isn’t there even one wise man among you who would be able to decide between his brothers?

46:6:6.text: But brother goes to law with brother, and that before unbelievers!

46:6:7.text: Therefore it is already altogether a defect in you that you have lawsuits one with another. Why not rather be wronged? Why not rather be defrauded?

46:6:8.text: No, but you yourselves do wrong and defraud, and that against your brothers.

46:6:9.text: Or don’t you know that the unrighteous will not inherit God’s Kingdom? Don’t be deceived. Neither the sexually immoral, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor male prostitutes, nor homosexuals,

46:7:1.text: Now concerning the things about which you wrote to me: it is good for a man not to touch a woman.

46:7:10.text: But to the married I command — not I, but the Lord — that the wife not leave her husband

46:7:11.text: (but if she departs, let her remain unmarried, or else be reconciled to her husband), and that the husband not leave his wife.

46:7:12.text: But to the rest I — not the Lord — say, if any brother has an unbelieving wife, and she is content to live with him, let him not leave her.

46:7:13.text: The woman who has an unbelieving husband, and he is content to live with her, let her not leave her husband.

46:7:14.text: For the unbelieving husband is sanctified in the wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified in the husband. Otherwise your children would be unclean, but now they are holy.

46:7:15.text: Yet if the unbeliever departs, let there be separation. The brother or the sister is not under bondage in such cases, but God has called us in peace.

46:7:16.text: For how do you know, wife, whether you will save your husband? Or how do you know, husband, whether you will save your wife?

46:7:17.text: Only, as the Lord has distributed to each man, as God has called each, so let him walk. So I command in all the assemblies.

46:7:18.text: Was anyone called having been circumcised? Let him not become uncircumcised. Has anyone been called in uncircumcision? Let him not be circumcised.

46:7:19.text: Circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing, but what matters is keeping God’s commandments.

46:7:2.text: But, because of sexual immoralities, let each man have his own wife, and let each woman have her own husband.

46:7:20.text: Let each man stay in that calling in which he was called.

46:7:21.text: Were you called being a bondservant? Don’t let that bother you, but if you get an opportunity to become free, use it.

46:7:22.text: For he who was called in the Lord being a bondservant is the Lord’s free man. Likewise he who was called being free is Christ’s bondservant.

46:7:23.text: You were bought with a price. Don’t become bondservants of men.

46:7:24.text: Brothers, let each man, in whatever condition he was called, stay in that condition with God.

46:7:25.text: Now concerning virgins, I have no commandment from the Lord, but I give my judgment as one who has obtained mercy from the Lord to be trustworthy.

46:7:26.text: Therefore I think that because of the distress that is on us, it’s good for a man to remain as he is.

46:7:27.text: Are you bound to a wife? Don’t seek to be freed. Are you free from a wife? Don’t seek a wife.

46:7:28.text: But if you marry, you have not sinned. If a virgin marries, she has not sinned. Yet such will have oppression in the flesh, and I want to spare you.

46:7:29.text: But I say this, brothers: the time is short. From now on, both those who have wives may be as though they had none;

46:7:3.text: Let the husband give his wife the affection owed her, and likewise also the wife her husband.

46:7:30.text: and those who weep, as though they didn’t weep; and those who rejoice, as though they didn’t rejoice; and those who buy, as though they didn’t possess;

46:7:31.text: and those who use the world, as not using it to the fullest. For the mode of this world passes away.

46:7:32.text: But I desire to have you to be free from cares. He who is unmarried is concerned for the things of the Lord, how he may please the Lord;

46:7:33.text: but he who is married is concerned about the things of the world, how he may please his wife.

46:7:34.text: There is also a difference between a wife and a virgin. The unmarried woman cares about the things of the Lord, that she may be holy both in body and in spirit. But she who is married cares about the things of the world — how she may please her husband.

46:7:35.text: This I say for your own benefit, not that I may ensnare you, but for that which is appropriate, and that you may attend to the Lord without distraction.

46:7:36.text: But if any man thinks that he is behaving inappropriately toward his virgin, if she is past the flower of her age, and if need so requires, let him do what he desires. He doesn’t sin. Let them marry.

46:7:37.text: But he who stands steadfast in his heart, having no urgency, but has power over his own will, and has determined in his own heart to keep his own virgin, does well.

46:7:38.text: So then both he who gives his own virgin in marriage does well, and he who doesn’t give her in marriage does better.

46:7:39.text: A wife is bound by law for as long as her husband lives; but if the husband is dead, she is free to be married to whomever she desires, only in the Lord.

46:7:4.text: The wife doesn’t have authority over her own body, but the husband does. Likewise also the husband doesn’t have authority over his own body, but the wife does.

46:7:40.text: But she is happier if she stays as she is, in my judgment, and I think that I also have God’s Spirit.

46:7:5.text: Don’t deprive one another, unless it is by consent for a season, that you may give yourselves to fasting and prayer, and may be together again, that Satan doesn’t tempt you because of your lack of self-control.

46:7:6.text: But this I say by way of concession, not of commandment.

46:7:7.text: Yet I wish that all men were like me. However, each man has his own gift from God, one of this kind, and another of that kind.

46:7:8.text: But I say to the unmarried and to widows, it is good for them if they remain even as I am.

46:7:9.text: But if they don’t have self-control, let them marry. For it’s better to marry than to burn with passion.

46:8:1.text: Now concerning things sacrificed to idols: We know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.

46:8:10.text: For if a man sees you who have knowledge sitting in an idol’s temple, won’t his conscience, if he is weak, be emboldened to eat things sacrificed to idols?

46:8:11.text: And through your knowledge, he who is weak perishes, the brother for whose sake Christ died.

46:8:12.text: Thus, sinning against the brothers, and wounding their conscience when it is weak, you sin against Christ.

46:8:13.text: Therefore, if food causes my brother to stumble, I will eat no meat forever more, that I don’t cause my brother to stumble.

46:8:2.text: But if anyone thinks that he knows anything, he doesn’t yet know as he ought to know.

46:8:3.text: But anyone who loves God is known by him.

46:8:4.text: Therefore concerning the eating of things sacrificed to idols, we know that no idol is anything in the world, and that there is no other God but one.

46:8:5.text: For though there are things that are called “gods”, whether in the heavens or on earth — as there are many “gods” and many “lords” —

46:8:6.text: yet to us there is one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we for him; and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things, and we live through him.

46:8:7.text: However, that knowledge isn’t in all men. But some, with consciousness of an idol until now, eat as of a thing sacrificed to an idol, and their conscience, being weak, is defiled.

46:8:8.text: But food will not commend us to God. For neither, if we don’t eat are we the worse, nor if we eat are we the better.

46:8:9.text: But be careful that by no means does this liberty of yours become a stumbling block to the weak.

46:9:1.text: Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Haven’t I seen Jesus Christ, our Lord? Aren’t you my work in the Lord?

46:9:10.text: or does he say it assuredly for our sake? Yes, it was written for our sake, because he who plows ought to plow in hope, and he who threshes in hope should partake of his hope.

46:9:11.text: If we sowed to you spiritual things, is it a great thing if we reap your fleshly things?

46:9:12.text: If others partake of this right over you, don’t we yet more? Nevertheless we didn’t use this right, but we bear all things, that we may cause no hindrance to the Good News of Christ.

46:9:13.text: Don’t you know that those who serve around sacred things eat from the things of the temple, and those who wait on the altar have their portion with the altar?

46:9:14.text: Even so the Lord ordained that those who proclaim the Good News should live from the Good News.

46:9:15.text: But I have used none of these things, and I don’t write these things that it may be done so in my case; for I would rather die, than that anyone should make my boasting void.

46:9:16.text: For if I preach the Good News, I have nothing to boast about, for necessity is laid on me; but woe is to me if I don’t preach the Good News.

46:9:17.text: For if I do this of my own will, I have a reward. But if not of my own will, I have a stewardship entrusted to me.

46:9:18.text: What then is my reward? That when I preach the Good News, I may present the Good News of Christ without charge, so as not to abuse my authority in the Good News.

46:9:19.text: For though I was free from all, I brought myself under bondage to all, that I might gain the more.

46:9:2.text: If to others I am not an apostle, yet at least I am to you; for you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.

46:9:20.text: To the Jews I became as a Jew, that I might gain Jews; to those who are under the law, as under the law, that I might gain those who are under the law;

46:9:21.text: to those who are without law, as without law (not being without law toward God, but under law toward Christ), that I might win those who are without law.

46:9:22.text: To the weak I became as weak, that I might gain the weak. I have become all things to all men, that I may by all means save some.

46:9:23.text: Now I do this for the sake of the Good News, that I may be a joint partaker of it.

46:9:24.text: Don’t you know that those who run in a race all run, but one receives the prize? Run like that, so that you may win.

46:9:25.text: Every man who strives in the games exercises self-control in all things. Now they do it to receive a corruptible crown, but we an incorruptible.

46:9:26.text: I therefore run like that, not aimlessly. I fight like that, not beating the air,

46:9:27.text: but I beat my body and bring it into submission, lest by any means, after I have preached to others, I myself should be disqualified.

46:9:3.text: My defense to those who examine me is this:

46:9:4.text: Have we no right to eat and to drink?

46:9:5.text: Have we no right to take along a wife who is a believer, even as the rest of the apostles, and the brothers of the Lord, and Cephas?

46:9:6.text: Or have only Barnabas and I no right to not work?

46:9:7.text: What soldier ever serves at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard, and doesn’t eat of its fruit? Or who feeds a flock, and doesn’t drink from the flock’s milk?

46:9:8.text: Do I speak these things according to the ways of men? Or doesn’t the law also say the same thing?

46:9:9.text: For it is written in the law of Moses, “You shall not muzzle an ox while it treads out the grain.” Is it for the oxen that God cares,

47:10:1.text: Now I Paul, myself, entreat you by the humility and gentleness of Christ, I who in your presence am lowly among you, but being absent am bold toward you.

47:10:10.text: For, “His letters”, they say, “are weighty and strong, but his bodily presence is weak, and his speech is despised.”

47:10:11.text: Let such a person consider this, that what we are in word by letters when we are absent, such are we also in deed when we are present.

47:10:12.text: For we are not bold to number or compare ourselves with some of those who commend themselves. But they themselves, measuring themselves by themselves, and comparing themselves with themselves, are without understanding.

47:10:13.text: But we will not boast beyond proper limits, but within the boundaries with which God appointed to us, which reach even to you.

47:10:14.text: For we don’t stretch ourselves too much, as though we didn’t reach to you. For we came even as far as to you with the Good News of Christ,

47:10:15.text: not boasting beyond proper limits in other men’s labors, but having hope that as your faith grows, we will be abundantly enlarged by you in our sphere of influence,

47:10:16.text: so as to preach the Good News even to the parts beyond you, not to boast in what someone else has already done.

47:10:17.text: But “he who boasts, let him boast in the Lord.”

47:10:18.text: For it isn’t he who commends himself who is approved, but whom the Lord commends.

47:10:2.text: Yes, I beg you that I may not, when present, show courage with the confidence with which I intend to be bold against some, who consider us to be walking according to the flesh.

47:10:3.text: For though we walk in the flesh, we don’t wage war according to the flesh;

47:10:4.text: for the weapons of our warfare are not of the flesh, but mighty before God to the throwing down of strongholds,

47:10:5.text: throwing down imaginations and every high thing that is exalted against the knowledge of God and bringing every thought into captivity to the obedience of Christ,

47:10:6.text: and being in readiness to avenge all disobedience when your obedience is made full.

47:10:7.text: Do you look at things only as they appear in front of your face? If anyone trusts in himself that he is Christ’s, let him consider this again with himself, that even as he is Christ’s, so we also are Christ’s.

47:10:8.text: For even if I boast somewhat abundantly concerning our authority, which the Lord gave for building you up and not for casting you down, I will not be ashamed,

47:10:9.text: that I may not seem as if I desire to terrify you by my letters.

47:11:1.text: I wish that you would bear with me in a little foolishness, but indeed you do bear with me.

47:11:10.text: As the truth of Christ is in me, no one will stop me from this boasting in the regions of Achaia.

47:11:11.text: Why? Because I don’t love you? God knows.

47:11:12.text: But what I do, that I will continue to do, that I may cut off opportunity from those who desire an opportunity, that in which they boast, they may be recognized just like us.

47:11:13.text: For such men are false apostles, deceitful workers, masquerading as Christ’s apostles.

47:11:14.text: And no wonder, for even Satan masquerades as an angel of light.

47:11:15.text: It is no great thing therefore if his servants also masquerade as servants of righteousness, whose end will be according to their works.

47:11:16.text: I say again, let no one think me foolish. But if so, yet receive me as foolish, that I also may boast a little.

47:11:17.text: That which I speak, I don’t speak according to the Lord, but as in foolishness, in this confidence of boasting.

47:11:18.text: Seeing that many boast after the flesh, I will also boast.

47:11:19.text: For you bear with the foolish gladly, being wise.

47:11:2.text: For I am jealous over you with a godly jealousy. For I promised you in marriage to one husband, that I might present you as a pure virgin to Christ.

47:11:20.text: For you bear with a man if he brings you into bondage, if he devours you, if he takes you captive, if he exalts himself, or if he strikes you on the face.

47:11:21.text: To my shame, I speak as though we had been weak. Yet in whatever way anyone is bold (I speak in foolishness), I am bold also.

47:11:22.text: Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they the offspring of Abraham? So am I.

47:11:23.text: Are they servants of Christ? (I speak as one beside himself.) I am more so: in labors more abundantly, in prisons more abundantly, in stripes above measure, and in deaths often.

47:11:24.text: Five times I received forty stripes minus one from the Jews.

47:11:25.text: Three times I was beaten with rods. Once I was stoned. Three times I suffered shipwreck. I have been a night and a day in the deep.

47:11:26.text: I have been in travels often, perils of rivers, perils of robbers, perils from my countrymen, perils from the Gentiles, perils in the city, perils in the wilderness, perils in the sea, perils among false brothers;

47:11:27.text: in labor and travail, in watchings often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, and in cold and nakedness.

47:11:28.text: Besides those things that are outside, there is that which presses on me daily: anxiety for all the assemblies.

47:11:29.text: Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is caused to stumble, and I don’t burn with indignation?

47:11:3.text: But I am afraid that somehow, as the serpent deceived Eve in his craftiness, so your minds might be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Christ.

47:11:30.text: If I must boast, I will boast of the things that concern my weakness.

47:11:31.text: The God and Father of the Lord Jesus Christ, he who is blessed forever more, knows that I don’t lie.

47:11:32.text: In Damascus the governor under King Aretas guarded the Damascenes’ city, desiring to arrest me.

47:11:33.text: I was let down in a basket through a window by the wall, and escaped his hands.

47:11:4.text: For if he who comes preaches another Jesus whom we didn’t preach, or if you receive a different spirit which you didn’t receive, or a different “good news” which you didn’t accept, you put up with that well enough.

47:11:5.text: For I reckon that I am not at all behind the very best apostles.

47:11:6.text: But though I am unskilled in speech, yet I am not unskilled in knowledge. No, in every way we have been revealed to you in all things.

47:11:7.text: Or did I commit a sin in humbling myself that you might be exalted, because I preached to you God’s Good News free of charge?

47:11:8.text: I robbed other assemblies, taking wages from them that I might serve you.

47:11:9.text: When I was present with you and was in need, I wasn’t a burden on anyone, for the brothers, when they came from Macedonia, supplied the measure of my need. In everything I kept myself from being burdensome to you, and I will continue to do so.

47:12:1.text: It is doubtless not profitable for me to boast, but I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord.

47:12:10.text: Therefore I take pleasure in weaknesses, in injuries, in necessities, in persecutions, and in distresses, for Christ’s sake. For when I am weak, then am I strong.

47:12:11.text: I have become foolish in boasting. You compelled me, for I ought to have been commended by you, for I am in no way inferior to the very best apostles, though I am nothing.

47:12:12.text: Truly the signs of an apostle were worked among you in all perseverance, in signs and wonders and mighty works.

47:12:13.text: For what is there in which you were made inferior to the rest of the assemblies, unless it is that I myself was not a burden to you? Forgive me this wrong!

47:12:14.text: Behold, this is the third time I am ready to come to you, and I will not be a burden to you; for I seek not your possessions, but you. For the children ought not to save up for the parents, but the parents for the children.

47:12:15.text: I will most gladly spend and be spent for your souls. If I love you more abundantly, am I loved the less?

47:12:16.text: Even so, I myself didn’t burden you. But you might say that being crafty, I caught you with deception.

47:12:17.text: Did I take advantage of you by anyone of those whom I have sent to you?

47:12:18.text: I exhorted Titus, and I sent the brother with him. Did Titus take any advantage of you? Didn’t we walk in the same spirit? Didn’t we walk in the same steps?

47:12:19.text: Again, do you think that we are excusing ourselves to you? In the sight of God we speak in Christ. But all things, beloved, are for your edifying.

47:12:2.text: I know a man in Christ who was caught up into the third heaven fourteen years ago — whether in the body, I don’t know, or whether out of the body, I don’t know; God knows.

47:12:20.text: For I am afraid that perhaps when I come, I might find you not the way I want to, and that I might be found by you as you don’t desire, that perhaps there would be strife, jealousy, outbursts of anger, factions, slander, whisperings, proud thoughts, or riots,

47:12:21.text: that again when I come my God would humble me before you, and I would mourn for many of those who have sinned before now, and not repented of the uncleanness, sexual immorality, and lustfulness which they committed.

47:12:3.text: I know such a man (whether in the body, or outside of the body, I don’t know; God knows),

47:12:4.text: how he was caught up into Paradise and heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter.

47:12:5.text: On behalf of such a one I will boast, but on my own behalf I will not boast, except in my weaknesses.

47:12:6.text: For if I would desire to boast, I will not be foolish; for I will speak the truth. But I refrain, so that no man may think more of me than that which he sees in me or hears from me.

47:12:7.text: By reason of the exceeding greatness of the revelations, that I should not be exalted excessively, a thorn in the flesh was given to me: a messenger of Satan to torment me, that I should not be exalted excessively.

47:12:8.text: Concerning this thing, I begged the Lord three times that it might depart from me.

47:12:9.text: He has said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.” Most gladly therefore I will rather glory in my weaknesses, that the power of Christ may rest on me.

47:13:1.text: This is the third time I am coming to you. “At the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every word be established.”

47:13:10.text: For this cause I write these things while absent, that I may not deal sharply when present, according to the authority which the Lord gave me for building up and not for tearing down.

47:13:11.text: Finally, brothers, rejoice! Be perfected. Be comforted. Be of the same mind. Live in peace, and the God of love and peace will be with you.

47:13:12.text: Greet one another with a holy kiss.

47:13:14.text: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, God’s love, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all. Amen.

47:13:2.text: I have warned previously, and I warn again, as when I was present the second time, so now, being absent, I write to those who have sinned before now and to all the rest that if I come again, I will not spare,

47:13:3.text: seeing that you seek a proof of Christ who speaks in me who is not weak, but is powerful in you.

47:13:4.text: For he was crucified through weakness, yet he lives through the power of God. For we also are weak in him, but we will live with him through the power of God toward you.

47:13:5.text: Examine your own selves, whether you are in the faith. Test your own selves. Or don’t you know about your own selves, that Jesus Christ is in you? — unless indeed you are disqualified.

47:13:6.text: But I hope that you will know that we aren’t disqualified.

47:13:7.text: Now I pray to God that you do no evil; not that we may appear approved, but that you may do that which is honorable, though we may seem to have failed.

47:13:8.text: For we can do nothing against the truth, but for the truth.

47:13:9.text: For we rejoice when we are weak and you are strong. We also pray for this: your becoming perfect.

47:1:1.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, and Timothy our brother, to the assembly of God which is at Corinth, with all the saints who are in the whole of Achaia:

47:1:10.text: who delivered us out of so great a death, and does deliver, on whom we have set our hope that he will also still deliver us,

47:1:11.text: you also helping together on our behalf by your supplication; that, for the gift given to us by means of many, thanks may be given by many persons on your behalf.

47:1:12.text: For our boasting is this: the testimony of our conscience that in holiness and sincerity of God, not in fleshly wisdom but in the grace of God, we behaved ourselves in the world, and more abundantly toward you.

47:1:13.text: For we write no other things to you than what you read or even acknowledge, and I hope you will acknowledge to the end —

47:1:14.text: as also you acknowledged us in part — that we are your boasting, even as you also are ours, in the day of our Lord Jesus.

47:1:15.text: In this confidence, I was determined to come first to you, that you might have a second benefit,

47:1:16.text: and by you to pass into Macedonia, and again from Macedonia to come to you, and to be sent forward by you on my journey to Judea.

47:1:17.text: When I therefore planned this, did I show fickleness? Or the things that I plan, do I plan according to the flesh, that with me there should be the “Yes, yes” and the “No, no?”

47:1:18.text: But as God is faithful, our word toward you was not “Yes and no.”

47:1:19.text: For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you by us — by me, Silvanus, and Timothy — was not “Yes and no,” but in him is “Yes.”

47:1:2.text: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

47:1:20.text: For however many are the promises of God, in him is the “Yes.” Therefore also through him is the “Amen”, to the glory of God through us.

47:1:21.text: Now he who establishes us with you in Christ and anointed us is God,

47:1:22.text: who also sealed us and gave us the down payment of the Spirit in our hearts.

47:1:23.text: But I call God for a witness to my soul, that to spare you, I didn’t come to Corinth.

47:1:24.text: We don’t control your faith, but are fellow workers with you for your joy. For you stand firm in faith.

47:1:3.text: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and God of all comfort,

47:1:4.text: who comforts us in all our affliction, that we may be able to comfort those who are in any affliction, through the comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by God.

47:1:5.text: For as the sufferings of Christ abound to us, even so our comfort also abounds through Christ.

47:1:6.text: But if we are afflicted, it is for your comfort and salvation. If we are comforted, it is for your comfort, which produces in you the patient enduring of the same sufferings which we also suffer.

47:1:7.text: Our hope for you is steadfast, knowing that, since you are partakers of the sufferings, so you are also of the comfort.

47:1:8.text: For we don’t desire to have you uninformed, brothers, concerning our affliction which happened to us in Asia: that we were weighed down exceedingly, beyond our power, so much that we despaired even of life.

47:1:9.text: Yes, we ourselves have had the sentence of death within ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God who raises the dead,

47:2:1.text: But I determined this for myself, that I would not come to you again in sorrow.

47:2:10.text: Now I also forgive whomever you forgive anything. For if indeed I have forgiven anything, I have forgiven that one for your sakes in the presence of Christ,

47:2:11.text: that no advantage may be gained over us by Satan, for we are not ignorant of his schemes.

47:2:12.text: Now when I came to Troas for the Good News of Christ, and when a door was opened to me in the Lord,

47:2:13.text: I had no relief for my spirit, because I didn’t find Titus my brother, but taking my leave of them, I went out into Macedonia.

47:2:14.text: Now thanks be to God who always leads us in triumph in Christ, and reveals through us the sweet aroma of his knowledge in every place.

47:2:15.text: For we are a sweet aroma of Christ to God in those who are saved and in those who perish:

47:2:16.text: to the one a stench from death to death, to the other a sweet aroma from life to life. Who is sufficient for these things?

47:2:17.text: For we are not as so many, peddling the word of God. But as of sincerity, but as of God, in the sight of God, we speak in Christ.

47:2:2.text: For if I make you grieve, then who will make me glad but he who is made to grieve by me?

47:2:3.text: And I wrote this very thing to you, so that when I came, I wouldn’t have sorrow from them of whom I ought to rejoice; having confidence in you all that my joy would be shared by all of you.

47:2:4.text: For out of much affliction and anguish of heart I wrote to you with many tears, not that you should be made to grieve, but that you might know the love that I have so abundantly for you.

47:2:5.text: But if any has caused sorrow, he has caused sorrow not to me, but in part (that I not press too heavily) to you all.

47:2:6.text: This punishment which was inflicted by the many is sufficient for such a one;

47:2:7.text: so that, on the contrary, you should rather forgive him and comfort him, lest by any means such a one should be swallowed up with his excessive sorrow.

47:2:8.text: Therefore I beg you to confirm your love toward him.

47:2:9.text: For to this end I also wrote, that I might know the proof of you, whether you are obedient in all things.

47:3:1.text: Are we beginning again to commend ourselves? Or do we need, as do some, letters of commendation to you or from you?

47:3:10.text: For most certainly that which has been made glorious has not been made glorious in this respect, by reason of the glory that surpasses.

47:3:11.text: For if that which passes away was with glory, much more that which remains is in glory.

47:3:12.text: Having therefore such a hope, we use great boldness of speech,

47:3:13.text: and not as Moses, who put a veil on his face so that the children of Israel wouldn’t look steadfastly on the end of that which was passing away.

47:3:14.text: But their minds were hardened, for until this very day at the reading of the old covenant the same veil remains, because in Christ it passes away.

47:3:15.text: But to this day, when Moses is read, a veil lies on their heart.

47:3:16.text: But whenever someone turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.

47:3:17.text: Now the Lord is the Spirit; and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.

47:3:18.text: But we all, with unveiled face seeing the glory of the Lord as in a mirror, are transformed into the same image from glory to glory, even as from the Lord, the Spirit.

47:3:2.text: You are our letter, written in our hearts, known and read by all men,

47:3:3.text: being revealed that you are a letter of Christ, served by us, written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God; not in tablets of stone, but in tablets that are hearts of flesh.

47:3:4.text: Such confidence we have through Christ toward God,

47:3:5.text: not that we are sufficient of ourselves to account anything as from ourselves; but our sufficiency is from God,

47:3:6.text: who also made us sufficient as servants of a new covenant, not of the letter but of the Spirit. For the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.

47:3:7.text: But if the service of death, written engraved on stones, came with glory, so that the children of Israel could not look steadfastly on the face of Moses for the glory of his face, which was passing away,

47:3:8.text: won’t service of the Spirit be with much more glory?

47:3:9.text: For if the service of condemnation has glory, the service of righteousness exceeds much more in glory.

47:4:1.text: Therefore, seeing we have this ministry, even as we obtained mercy, we don’t faint.

47:4:10.text: always carrying in the body the putting to death of the Lord Jesus, that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our body.

47:4:11.text: For we who live are always delivered to death for Jesus’ sake, that the life also of Jesus may be revealed in our mortal flesh.

47:4:12.text: So then death works in us, but life in you.

47:4:13.text: But having the same spirit of faith, according to that which is written, “I believed, and therefore I spoke.” We also believe, and therefore we also speak,

47:4:14.text: knowing that he who raised the Lord Jesus will raise us also with Jesus, and will present us with you.

47:4:15.text: For all things are for your sakes, that the grace, being multiplied through the many, may cause the thanksgiving to abound to the glory of God.

47:4:16.text: Therefore we don’t faint, but though our outward person is decaying, yet our inward person is renewed day by day.

47:4:17.text: For our light affliction, which is for the moment, works for us more and more exceedingly an eternal weight of glory,

47:4:18.text: while we don’t look at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen. For the things which are seen are temporal, but the things which are not seen are eternal.

47:4:2.text: But we have renounced the hidden things of shame, not walking in craftiness nor handling the word of God deceitfully, but by the manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man’s conscience in the sight of God.

47:4:3.text: Even if our Good News is veiled, it is veiled in those who are dying,

47:4:4.text: in whom the god of this world has blinded the minds of the unbelieving, that the light of the Good News of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God, should not dawn on them.

47:4:5.text: For we don’t preach ourselves, but Christ Jesus as Lord, and ourselves as your servants for Jesus’ sake,

47:4:6.text: seeing it is God who said, “Light will shine out of darkness,” who has shone in our hearts to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.

47:4:7.text: But we have this treasure in clay vessels, that the exceeding greatness of the power may be of God and not from ourselves.

47:4:8.text: We are pressed on every side, yet not crushed; perplexed, yet not to despair;

47:4:9.text: pursued, yet not forsaken; struck down, yet not destroyed;

47:5:1.text: For we know that if the earthly house of our tent is dissolved, we have a building from God, a house not made with hands, eternal, in the heavens.

47:5:10.text: For we must all be revealed before the judgment seat of Christ that each one may receive the things in the body according to what he has done, whether good or bad.

47:5:11.text: Knowing therefore the fear of the Lord, we persuade men, but we are revealed to God, and I hope that we are revealed also in your consciences.

47:5:12.text: For we are not commending ourselves to you again, but speak as giving you occasion of boasting on our behalf, that you may have something to answer those who boast in appearance and not in heart.

47:5:13.text: For if we are beside ourselves, it is for God. Or if we are of sober mind, it is for you.

47:5:14.text: For the love of Christ compels us; because we judge thus: that one died for all, therefore all died.

47:5:15.text: He died for all, that those who live should no longer live to themselves, but to him who for their sakes died and rose again.

47:5:16.text: Therefore we know no one according to the flesh from now on. Even though we have known Christ according to the flesh, yet now we know him so no more.

47:5:17.text: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.

47:5:18.text: But all things are of God, who reconciled us to himself through Jesus Christ, and gave to us the ministry of reconciliation;

47:5:19.text: namely, that God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, not reckoning to them their trespasses, and having committed to us the word of reconciliation.

47:5:2.text: For most certainly in this we groan, longing to be clothed with our habitation which is from heaven,

47:5:20.text: We are therefore ambassadors on behalf of Christ, as though God were entreating by us: we beg you on behalf of Christ, be reconciled to God.

47:5:21.text: For him who knew no sin he made to be sin on our behalf, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.

47:5:3.text: if indeed being clothed, we will not be found naked.

47:5:4.text: For indeed we who are in this tent do groan, being burdened, not that we desire to be unclothed, but that we desire to be clothed, that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life.

47:5:5.text: Now he who made us for this very thing is God, who also gave to us the down payment of the Spirit.

47:5:6.text: Therefore we are always confident and know that while we are at home in the body, we are absent from the Lord;

47:5:7.text: for we walk by faith, not by sight.

47:5:8.text: We are courageous, I say, and are willing rather to be absent from the body and to be at home with the Lord.

47:5:9.text: Therefore also we make it our aim, whether at home or absent, to be well pleasing to him.

47:6:1.text: Working together, we entreat also that you do not receive the grace of God in vain.

47:6:10.text: as sorrowful yet always rejoicing, as poor yet making many rich, as having nothing and yet possessing all things.

47:6:11.text: Our mouth is open to you, Corinthians. Our heart is enlarged.

47:6:12.text: You are not restricted by us, but you are restricted by your own affections.

47:6:13.text: Now in return — I speak as to my children — you also open your hearts.

47:6:14.text: Don’t be unequally yoked with unbelievers, for what fellowship do righteousness and iniquity have? Or what fellowship does light have with darkness?

47:6:15.text: What agreement does Christ have with Belial? Or what portion does a believer have with an unbeliever?

47:6:16.text: What agreement does a temple of God have with idols? For you are a temple of the living God. Even as God said, “I will dwell in them and walk in them. I will be their God and they will be my people.”

47:6:17.text: Therefore“‘Come out from among them, and be separate,’ says the Lord. ‘Touch no unclean thing. I will receive you.

47:6:18.text: I will be to you a Father. You will be to me sons and daughters,’ says the Lord Almighty.”

47:6:2.text: For he says, “At an acceptable time I listened to you. In a day of salvation I helped you.” Behold, now is the acceptable time. Behold, now is the day of salvation.

47:6:3.text: We give no occasion of stumbling in anything, that our service may not be blamed,

47:6:4.text: but in everything commending ourselves as servants of God: in great endurance, in afflictions, in hardships, in distresses,

47:6:5.text: in beatings, in imprisonments, in riots, in labors, in watchings, in fastings,

47:6:6.text: in pureness, in knowledge, in perseverance, in kindness, in the Holy Spirit, in sincere love,

47:6:7.text: in the word of truth, in the power of God, by the armor of righteousness on the right hand and on the left,

47:6:8.text: by glory and dishonor, by evil report and good report, as deceivers and yet true,

47:6:9.text: as unknown and yet well known, as dying and behold — we live, as punished and not killed,

47:7:1.text: Having therefore these promises, beloved, let’s cleanse ourselves from all defilement of flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.

47:7:10.text: For godly sorrow produces repentance leading to salvation, which brings no regret. But the sorrow of the world produces death.

47:7:11.text: For behold, this same thing, that you were grieved in a godly way, what earnest care it worked in you. Yes, what defense, indignation, fear, longing, zeal, and vindication! In everything you demonstrated yourselves to be pure in the matter.

47:7:12.text: So although I wrote to you, I wrote not for his cause that did the wrong, nor for his cause that suffered the wrong, but that your earnest care for us might be revealed in you in the sight of God.

47:7:13.text: Therefore we have been comforted. In our comfort we rejoiced the more exceedingly for the joy of Titus, because his spirit has been refreshed by you all.

47:7:14.text: For if in anything I have boasted to him on your behalf, I was not disappointed. But as we spoke all things to you in truth, so our glorying also which I made before Titus was found to be truth.

47:7:15.text: His affection is more abundantly toward you, while he remembers all of your obedience, how with fear and trembling you received him.

47:7:16.text: I rejoice that in everything I am confident concerning you.

47:7:2.text: Open your hearts to us. We wronged no one. We corrupted no one. We took advantage of no one.

47:7:3.text: I say this not to condemn you, for I have said before that you are in our hearts to die together and live together.

47:7:4.text: Great is my boldness of speech toward you. Great is my boasting on your behalf. I am filled with comfort. I overflow with joy in all our affliction.

47:7:5.text: For even when we had come into Macedonia, our flesh had no relief, but we were afflicted on every side. Fightings were outside. Fear was inside.

47:7:6.text: Nevertheless, he who comforts the lowly, God, comforted us by the coming of Titus,

47:7:7.text: and not by his coming only, but also by the comfort with which he was comforted in you while he told us of your longing, your mourning, and your zeal for me, so that I rejoiced still more.

47:7:8.text: For though I grieved you with my letter, I do not regret it, though I did regret it. For I see that my letter made you grieve, though just for a while.

47:7:9.text: I now rejoice, not that you were grieved, but that you were grieved to repentance. For you were grieved in a godly way, that you might suffer loss by us in nothing.

47:8:1.text: Moreover, brothers, we make known to you the grace of God which has been given in the assemblies of Macedonia,

47:8:10.text: I give advice in this: it is expedient for you who were the first to start a year ago, not only to do, but also to be willing.

47:8:11.text: But now complete the doing also, that as there was the readiness to be willing, so there may be the completion also out of your ability.

47:8:12.text: For if the readiness is there, it is acceptable according to what you have, not according to what you don’t have.

47:8:13.text: For this is not that others may be eased and you distressed,

47:8:14.text: but for equality. Your abundance at this present time supplies their lack, that their abundance also may become a supply for your lack, that there may be equality.

47:8:15.text: As it is written, “He who gathered much had nothing left over, and he who gathered little had no lack.”

47:8:16.text: But thanks be to God, who puts the same earnest care for you into the heart of Titus.

47:8:17.text: For he indeed accepted our exhortation, but being himself very earnest, he went out to you of his own accord.

47:8:18.text: We have sent together with him the brother whose praise in the Good News is known throughout all the assemblies.

47:8:19.text: Not only so, but he was also appointed by the assemblies to travel with us in this grace, which is served by us to the glory of the Lord himself, and to show our readiness.

47:8:2.text: how in a severe ordeal of affliction, the abundance of their joy and their deep poverty abounded to the riches of their generosity.

47:8:20.text: We are avoiding this, that any man should blame us concerning this abundance which is administered by us.

47:8:21.text: Having regard for honorable things, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men.

47:8:22.text: We have sent with them our brother whom we have many times proved earnest in many things, but now much more earnest, by reason of the great confidence which he has in you.

47:8:23.text: As for Titus, he is my partner and fellow worker for you. As for our brothers, they are the apostles of the assemblies, the glory of Christ.

47:8:24.text: Therefore show the proof of your love to them before the assemblies, and of our boasting on your behalf.

47:8:3.text: For according to their power, I testify, yes and beyond their power, they gave of their own accord,

47:8:4.text: begging us with much entreaty to receive this grace and the fellowship in the service to the saints.

47:8:5.text: This was not as we had expected, but first they gave their own selves to the Lord, and to us through the will of God.

47:8:6.text: So we urged Titus, that as he had made a beginning before, so he would also complete in you this grace.

47:8:7.text: But as you abound in everything — in faith, utterance, knowledge, all earnestness, and in your love to us — see that you also abound in this grace.

47:8:8.text: I speak not by way of commandment, but as proving through the earnestness of others the sincerity also of your love.

47:8:9.text: For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, that you through his poverty might become rich.

47:9:1.text: It is indeed unnecessary for me to write to you concerning the service to the saints,

47:9:10.text: Now may he who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food, supply and multiply your seed for sowing, and increase the fruits of your righteousness,

47:9:11.text: you being enriched in everything for all generosity, which produces thanksgiving to God through us.

47:9:12.text: For this service of giving that you perform not only makes up for lack among the saints, but abounds also through much giving of thanks to God,

47:9:13.text: seeing that through the proof given by this service, they glorify God for the obedience of your confession to the Good News of Christ and for the generosity of your contribution to them and to all,

47:9:14.text: while they themselves also, with supplication on your behalf, yearn for you by reason of the exceeding grace of God in you.

47:9:15.text: Now thanks be to God for his unspeakable gift!

47:9:2.text: for I know your readiness, of which I boast on your behalf to those of Macedonia, that Achaia has been prepared for the past year. Your zeal has stirred up very many of them.

47:9:3.text: But I have sent the brothers so that our boasting on your behalf may not be in vain in this respect, that, just as I said, you may be prepared,

47:9:4.text: lest by any means, if anyone from Macedonia comes there with me and finds you unprepared, we (to say nothing of you) would be disappointed in this confident boasting.

47:9:5.text: I thought it necessary therefore to entreat the brothers that they would go before to you and arrange ahead of time the generous gift that you promised before, that the same might be ready as a matter of generosity, and not of greediness.

47:9:6.text: Remember this: he who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly. He who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully.

47:9:7.text: Let each man give according as he has determined in his heart, not grudgingly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver.

47:9:8.text: And God is able to make all grace abound to you, that you, always having all sufficiency in everything, may abound to every good work.

47:9:9.text: As it is written, “He has scattered abroad. He has given to the poor. His righteousness remains forever.”

48:1:1.text: Paul, an apostle — not from men, nor through man, but through Jesus Christ, and God the Father, who raised him from the dead —

48:1:10.text: For am I now seeking the favor of men, or of God? Or am I striving to please men? For if I were still pleasing men, I wouldn’t be a servant of Christ.

48:1:11.text: But I make known to you, brothers, concerning the Good News which was preached by me, that it is not according to man.

48:1:12.text: For I didn’t receive it from man, nor was I taught it, but it came to me through revelation of Jesus Christ.

48:1:13.text: For you have heard of my way of living in time past in the Jews’ religion, how that beyond measure I persecuted the assembly of God and ravaged it.

48:1:14.text: I advanced in the Jews’ religion beyond many of my own age among my countrymen, being more exceedingly zealous for the traditions of my fathers.

48:1:15.text: But when it was the good pleasure of God, who separated me from my mother’s womb and called me through his grace,

48:1:16.text: to reveal his Son in me, that I might preach him among the Gentiles, I didn’t immediately confer with flesh and blood,

48:1:17.text: nor did I go up to Jerusalem to those who were apostles before me, but I went away into Arabia. Then I returned to Damascus.

48:1:18.text: Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to visit Peter, and stayed with him fifteen days.

48:1:19.text: But of the other apostles I saw no one except James, the Lord’s brother.

48:1:2.text: and all the brothers who are with me, to the assemblies of Galatia:

48:1:20.text: Now about the things which I write to you, behold, before God, I’m not lying.

48:1:21.text: Then I came to the regions of Syria and Cilicia.

48:1:22.text: I was still unknown by face to the assemblies of Judea which were in Christ,

48:1:23.text: but they only heard, “He who once persecuted us now preaches the faith that he once tried to destroy.”

48:1:24.text: So they glorified God in me.

48:1:3.text: Grace to you and peace from God the Father and our Lord Jesus Christ,

48:1:4.text: who gave himself for our sins, that he might deliver us out of this present evil age, according to the will of our God and Father —

48:1:5.text: to whom be the glory forever and ever. Amen.

48:1:6.text: I marvel that you are so quickly deserting him who called you in the grace of Christ to a different “good news”,

48:1:7.text: but there isn’t another “good news.” Only there are some who trouble you and want to pervert the Good News of Christ.

48:1:8.text: But even though we, or an angel from heaven, should preach to you any “good news” other than that which we preached to you, let him be cursed.

48:1:9.text: As we have said before, so I now say again: if any man preaches to you any “good news” other than that which you received, let him be cursed.

48:2:1.text: Then after a period of fourteen years I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, taking Titus also with me.

48:2:10.text: They only asked us to remember the poor — which very thing I was also zealous to do.

48:2:11.text: But when Peter came to Antioch, I resisted him to his face, because he stood condemned.

48:2:12.text: For before some people came from James, he ate with the Gentiles. But when they came, he drew back and separated himself, fearing those who were of the circumcision.

48:2:13.text: And the rest of the Jews joined him in his hypocrisy, so that even Barnabas was carried away with their hypocrisy.

48:2:14.text: But when I saw that they didn’t walk uprightly according to the truth of the Good News, I said to Peter before them all, “If you, being a Jew, live as the Gentiles do, and not as the Jews do, why do you compel the Gentiles to live as the Jews do?

48:2:15.text: “We, being Jews by nature and not Gentile sinners,

48:2:16.text: yet knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law but through faith in Jesus Christ, even we believed in Christ Jesus, that we might be justified by faith in Christ and not by the works of the law, because no flesh will be justified by the works of the law.

48:2:17.text: But if while we sought to be justified in Christ, we ourselves also were found sinners, is Christ a servant of sin? Certainly not!

48:2:18.text: For if I build up again those things which I destroyed, I prove myself a law-breaker.

48:2:19.text: For I through the law died to the law, that I might live to God.

48:2:2.text: I went up by revelation, and I laid before them the Good News which I preach among the Gentiles, but privately before those who were respected, for fear that I might be running, or had run, in vain.

48:2:20.text: I have been crucified with Christ, and it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me. That life which I now live in the flesh, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself up for me.

48:2:21.text: I don’t reject the grace of God. For if righteousness is through the law, then Christ died for nothing!”

48:2:3.text: But not even Titus, who was with me, being a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised.

48:2:4.text: This was because of the false brothers secretly brought in, who stole in to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage,

48:2:5.text: to whom we gave no place in the way of subjection, not for an hour, that the truth of the Good News might continue with you.

48:2:6.text: But from those who were reputed to be important — whatever they were, it makes no difference to me; God doesn’t show partiality to man — they, I say, who were respected imparted nothing to me,

48:2:7.text: but to the contrary, when they saw that I had been entrusted with the Good News for the uncircumcised, even as Peter with the Good News for the circumcised —

48:2:8.text: for he who worked through Peter in the apostleship with the circumcised also worked through me with the Gentiles —

48:2:9.text: and when they perceived the grace that was given to me, James and Cephas and John, those who were reputed to be pillars, gave to Barnabas and me the right hand of fellowship, that we should go to the Gentiles, and they to the circumcision.

48:3:1.text: Foolish Galatians, who has bewitched you not to obey the truth, before whose eyes Jesus Christ was openly portrayed among you as crucified?

48:3:10.text: For as many as are of the works of the law are under a curse. For it is written, “Cursed is everyone who doesn’t continue in all things that are written in the book of the law, to do them.”

48:3:11.text: Now that no man is justified by the law before God is evident, for, “The righteous will live by faith.”

48:3:12.text: The law is not of faith, but, “The man who does them will live by them.”

48:3:13.text: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, having become a curse for us. For it is written, “Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree,”

48:3:14.text: that the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Christ Jesus, that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.

48:3:15.text: Brothers, speaking of human terms, though it is only a man’s covenant, yet when it has been confirmed, no one makes it void or adds to it.

48:3:16.text: Now the promises were spoken to Abraham and to his offspring. He doesn’t say, “To descendants”, as of many, but as of one, “To your offspring”, which is Christ.

48:3:17.text: Now I say this: A covenant confirmed beforehand by God in Christ, the law, which came four hundred thirty years after, does not annul, so as to make the promise of no effect.

48:3:18.text: For if the inheritance is of the law, it is no more of promise; but God has granted it to Abraham by promise.

48:3:19.text: Then why is there the law? It was added because of transgressions, until the offspring should come to whom the promise has been made. It was ordained through angels by the hand of a mediator.

48:3:2.text: I just want to learn this from you: Did you receive the Spirit by the works of the law, or by hearing of faith?

48:3:20.text: Now a mediator is not between one, but God is one.

48:3:21.text: Is the law then against the promises of God? Certainly not! For if there had been a law given which could make alive, most certainly righteousness would have been of the law.

48:3:22.text: But the Scripture imprisoned all things under sin, that the promise by faith in Jesus Christ might be given to those who believe.

48:3:23.text: But before faith came, we were kept in custody under the law, confined for the faith which should afterwards be revealed.

48:3:24.text: So that the law has become our tutor to bring us to Christ, that we might be justified by faith.

48:3:25.text: But now that faith has come, we are no longer under a tutor.

48:3:26.text: For you are all children of God, through faith in Christ Jesus.

48:3:27.text: For as many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ.

48:3:28.text: There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither slave nor free man, there is neither male nor female; for you are all one in Christ Jesus.

48:3:29.text: If you are Christ’s, then you are Abraham’s offspring and heirs according to promise.

48:3:3.text: Are you so foolish? Having begun in the Spirit, are you now completed in the flesh?

48:3:4.text: Did you suffer so many things in vain, if it is indeed in vain?

48:3:5.text: He therefore who supplies the Spirit to you and does miracles among you, does he do it by the works of the law, or by hearing of faith?

48:3:6.text: Even so, Abraham “believed God, and it was counted to him for righteousness.”

48:3:7.text: Know therefore that those who are of faith are children of Abraham.

48:3:8.text: The Scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, preached the Good News beforehand to Abraham, saying, “In you all the nations will be blessed.”

48:3:9.text: So then, those who are of faith are blessed with the faithful Abraham.

48:4:1.text: But I say that so long as the heir is a child, he is no different from a bondservant, though he is lord of all,

48:4:10.text: You observe days, months, seasons, and years.

48:4:11.text: I am afraid for you, that I might have wasted my labor for you.

48:4:12.text: I beg you, brothers, become as I am, for I also have become as you are. You did me no wrong,

48:4:13.text: but you know that because of weakness in the flesh I preached the Good News to you the first time.

48:4:14.text: That which was a temptation to you in my flesh, you didn’t despise nor reject; but you received me as an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus.

48:4:15.text: What was the blessing you enjoyed? For I testify to you that, if possible, you would have plucked out your eyes and given them to me.

48:4:16.text: So then, have I become your enemy by telling you the truth?

48:4:17.text: They zealously seek you in no good way. No, they desire to alienate you, that you may seek them.

48:4:18.text: But it is always good to be zealous in a good cause, and not only when I am present with you.

48:4:21.text: Tell me, you that desire to be under the law, don’t you listen to the law?

48:4:22.text: For it is written that Abraham had two sons, one by the servant, and one by the free woman.

48:4:23.text: However, the son by the servant was born according to the flesh, but the son by the free woman was born through promise.

48:4:24.text: These things contain an allegory, for these are two covenants. One is from Mount Sinai, bearing children to bondage, which is Hagar.

48:4:25.text: For this Hagar is Mount Sinai in Arabia, and answers to the Jerusalem that exists now, for she is in bondage with her children.

48:4:26.text: But the Jerusalem that is above is free, which is the mother of us all.

48:4:27.text: For it is written, “Rejoice, you barren who don’t bear. Break out and shout, you who don’t travail. For the desolate women have more children than her who has a husband.”

48:4:28.text: Now we, brothers, as Isaac was, are children of promise.

48:4:29.text: But as then, he who was born according to the flesh persecuted him who was born according to the Spirit, so also it is now.

48:4:3.text: So we also, when we were children, were held in bondage under the elemental principles of the world.

48:4:30.text: However, what does the Scripture say? “Throw out the servant and her son, for the son of the servant will not inherit with the son of the free woman.”

48:4:31.text: So then, brothers, we are not children of a servant, but of the free woman.

48:4:4.text: But when the fullness of the time came, God sent out his Son, born to a woman, born under the law,

48:4:5.text: that he might redeem those who were under the law, that we might receive the adoption as children.

48:4:6.text: And because you are children, God sent out the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, “Abba, Father!”

48:4:7.text: So you are no longer a bondservant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ.

48:4:8.text: However at that time, not knowing God, you were in bondage to those who by nature are not gods.

48:4:9.text: But now that you have come to know God, or rather to be known by God, why do you turn back again to the weak and miserable elemental principles, to which you desire to be in bondage all over again?

48:5:1.text: Stand firm therefore in the liberty by which Christ has made us free, and don’t be entangled again with a yoke of bondage.

48:5:10.text: I have confidence toward you in the Lord that you will think no other way. But he who troubles you will bear his judgment, whoever he is.

48:5:11.text: But I, brothers, if I still preach circumcision, why am I still persecuted? Then the stumbling block of the cross has been removed.

48:5:12.text: I wish that those who disturb you would cut themselves off.

48:5:13.text: For you, brothers, were called for freedom. Only don’t use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh, but through love be servants to one another.

48:5:14.text: For the whole law is fulfilled in one word, in this: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”

48:5:15.text: But if you bite and devour one another, be careful that you don’t consume one another.

48:5:16.text: But I say, walk by the Spirit, and you won’t fulfill the lust of the flesh.

48:5:17.text: For the flesh lusts against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh; and these are contrary to one another, that you may not do the things that you desire.

48:5:18.text: But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the law.

48:5:19.text: Now the deeds of the flesh are obvious, which are: adultery, sexual immorality, uncleanness, lustfulness,

48:5:2.text: Behold, I, Paul, tell you that if you receive circumcision, Christ will profit you nothing.

48:5:20.text: idolatry, sorcery, hatred, strife, jealousies, outbursts of anger, rivalries, divisions, heresies,

48:5:22.text: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith,

48:5:23.text: gentleness, and self-control. Against such things there is no law.

48:5:25.text: If we live by the Spirit, let’s also walk by the Spirit.

48:5:26.text: Let’s not become conceited, provoking one another, and envying one another.

48:5:3.text: Yes, I testify again to every man who receives circumcision that he is a debtor to do the whole law.

48:5:4.text: You are alienated from Christ, you who desire to be justified by the law. You have fallen away from grace.

48:5:5.text: For we through the Spirit, by faith wait for the hope of righteousness.

48:5:6.text: For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision amounts to anything, but faith working through love.

48:5:7.text: You were running well! Who interfered with you that you should not obey the truth?

48:5:8.text: This persuasion is not from him who calls you.

48:5:9.text: A little yeast grows through the whole lump.

48:6:1.text: Brothers, even if a man is caught in some fault, you who are spiritual must restore such a one in a spirit of gentleness, looking to yourself so that you also aren’t tempted.

48:6:10.text: So then, as we have opportunity, let’s do what is good toward all men, and especially toward those who are of the household of the faith.

48:6:11.text: See with what large letters I write to you with my own hand.

48:6:12.text: As many as desire to make a good impression in the flesh compel you to be circumcised, just so they may not be persecuted for the cross of Christ.

48:6:13.text: For even they who receive circumcision don’t keep the law themselves, but they desire to have you circumcised, so that they may boast in your flesh.

48:6:14.text: But far be it from me to boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.

48:6:15.text: For in Christ Jesus neither is circumcision anything, nor uncircumcision, but a new creation.

48:6:16.text: As many as walk by this rule, peace and mercy be on them, and on God’s Israel.

48:6:17.text: From now on, let no one cause me any trouble, for I bear the marks of the Lord Jesus branded on my body.

48:6:18.text: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers. Amen.

48:6:2.text: Bear one another’s burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ.

48:6:3.text: For if a man thinks himself to be something when he is nothing, he deceives himself.

48:6:4.text: But let each man examine his own work, and then he will have reason to boast in himself, and not in someone else.

48:6:5.text: For each man will bear his own burden.

48:6:6.text: But let him who is taught in the word share all good things with him who teaches.

48:6:7.text: Don’t be deceived. God is not mocked, for whatever a man sows, that he will also reap.

48:6:8.text: For he who sows to his own flesh will from the flesh reap corruption. But he who sows to the Spirit will from the Spirit reap eternal life.

48:6:9.text: Let’s not be weary in doing good, for we will reap in due season if we don’t give up.
